gate: Entries are filtered AT BUILD TIME on live_type_matched, which I1 established by probing each documented type against the running catalogue. A phantom is not filtered at read time - it is never written here. INGEST-01 required a gate before wiring; this is it.

entries.label: Attribute Sample with Adjacency
entries.summary: Creates a texture map of an attribute sampled from geometry.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the attrib input accepts and the node outputs. Use Select Automatically for most workflows. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Attribute
parameters.description: The name of the geometry attribute to sample. For example, P provides a world space position map.

parameters.label: Class
parameters.description: The type of attribute class to sample. Primitive: Sample a geometry's primitive attribute. Point: Sample a geometry's point attribute. Vertex: Sample a geometry's vertex attribute.

entries.label: Distort with Adjacency
entries.summary: Distorts a layer over texture seams using adjacency.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Border
parameters.description: The sampling behavior outside of the incoming layer's boundaries. Automatically uses the layer's border property. See Border types for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. A value of 1 means this node uses only the new value. The default value is 1. See Mask for more information.

parameters.label: Direction
parameters.description: The world space direction in which you want to distort. This parameter doesn't apply when you wire in a dir input, which instead distorts the layer in a texture space direction.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: The strength of distortion. Negative values follow the directions backwards when tracing. This parameter distorts along the Direction parameter's values. When you wire in a dir input, this parameter then distorts in that texture space direction.

parameters.label: Scale by Timestep
parameters.description: Adjusts the distortion's overall strength by the current timestep. The timestep is usually 1/$FPS, but in a sub-stepped simulation it represents the current step size.

parameters.label: Streak
parameters.description: The method used to combine the pixel values along the direction of distortion. Off: Don't smear the image. Blur: Average the samples together. This smears the image along the distortion direction. Min: Accept the smallest value encountered along the trajectory. This is useful when eroding an input shape. Max: Accept the largest value encountered along the trajectory. This is useful when adding edge roughness on an input shape.

parameters.label: Use Streak Weight Ramp
parameters.description: When Streak is Blur, Min, or Max , weight the samples encountered along the path. Use Streak Weight to weaken the values over the trajectory.

parameters.label: Streak Weight
parameters.description: When Use Streak Weight Ramp is on, this ramp acts as a multiplier on the pixel values when streaking. The left side of the ramp corresponds to the start of the trajectory. For example, when the Streak is Blur, the default linear ramp fades the pixels over their path. This makes the pixels more faint near the start. For more information about using ramps, see Ramp parameters.

parameters.label: Pixels per Step
parameters.description: Controls the tracing quality to increase the accuracy of tracing curved trajectories. Higher values let the node take larger steps, which runs faster, but can miss intermediate variations in the distortion directions and texture island transitions. When off, the node takes a single step for each pixel to determine the source location. This is fast, but causes inconsistencies at texture seams and inaccuracies when the direction or scale vary.

parameters.label: Maximum Steps
parameters.description: Clamps the number of steps taken when Pixels per Step is on. You can raise this parameter (and lower Pixels per Step) if the distortion doesn't faithfully follow the directions. This can be especially noticeable when Streak is turned on.

entries.label: Extrapolate with Adjacency
entries.summary: Fills areas of a texture outside the UV islands with information from their island neighbors.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Transform Vectors between Islands
parameters.description: Treats pixel data as vectors and orients those vectors to match the boundary rotation between islands.

entries.label: Space Transform with Adjacency
entries.summary: Transforms a vector from world space into tangent space.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source outputs. RGB outputs the full vector and UV outputs only the X and Y components of the vector. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Transformation
parameters.description: The space to which you transform the vector. World to Tangent: Transforms the vector from world space to tangent space.

entries.label: Align
entries.summary: Transforms a layer to align with another layer.

parameters.label: Source
parameters.description: The definition of the source rectangle to use for alignment. See Data and display windows for more information. Data Window: The data window is where pixels are actually present in the image. A cropped image or overscan image may not match the display window. Display Window: The display window is the idealized location of the real screen and is independent of any overscan or cropping effects.

parameters.label: Justify with
parameters.description: The target to which the source is aligned. Reference Data Window: The reference data window is the actual pixels of the reference. If you're trying to line up two crops, usually the data windows of each are used. Reference Display Window: The display window is the idealized location of the real screen in the reference. Use this option to align to a position of the reference screen. Target Point: Specify a specific point in the space of the reference layer.

parameters.label: Units
parameters.description: The space in which to specify the target. This applies to the size_ref input, which is the reference layer. Image: Use image coordinates that range from -1 to 1 on the display window of the layer. Texture: Use texture coordinates that range from 0 to 1 on the data window of the layer. Pixels: Use absolute pixel locations in the layer. World: Use coordinates in world space that project through the layer's implicit camera.
parameters.heading: Target

parameters.label: Target Point
parameters.description: The target point. The Units parameter determines if this is in image, texture, pixel, or world space.
parameters.heading: Target

parameters.label: Target Size
parameters.description: The target size. The Units parameter determines if this is in image, texture, pixel, or world space.
parameters.heading: Target

parameters.label: Justify X
parameters.description: The side of the source rectangle to use. None: No movement on this axis. Min: Align the minimum of the source rectangle. Center: Align the center of the source rectangle. Max: Align the maximum of the source rectangle.
parameters.heading: Matching

parameters.label: Justify Y
parameters.description: The side of the source rectangle to use. None: No movement on this axis. Min: Align the minimum of the source rectangle. Center: Align the center of the source rectangle. Max: Align the maximum of the source rectangle.
parameters.heading: Matching

parameters.label: Goal X/Y
parameters.description: The target side of the alignment. Same: Align to the same side of the target that the source used, so minimum to minimum and center to center. Min: The minimum of the target rectangle is the goal. Center: The center of the target rectangle is the goal. Max: The maximum of the target rectangle is the goal.
parameters.heading: Matching

parameters.label: Offset by
parameters.description: An additional offset (in image space) from the computed alignment position.
parameters.heading: Matching

parameters.label: Scale to Fit
parameters.description: Scales the layer so the source rectangle fits inside the target rectangle.
parameters.heading: Matching

parameters.label: Uniform Scale
parameters.description: Scales uniformly in all axes.
parameters.heading: Matching

parameters.label: Scale Axis
parameters.description: The axis to use to fit.
parameters.heading: Matching

parameters.label: Scale X
parameters.description: Scales the x-axis to fit.
parameters.heading: Matching

parameters.label: Scale Y
parameters.description: Scales the y-axis to fit.
parameters.heading: Matching

entries.label: Align Pixels
entries.summary: Shifts a layer to align pixelwise with another layer.

parameters.label: Snapping
parameters.description: The initial snapping needs to pick a point on the source layer to snap. This point will be mapped as closely as possible, but if there are scales or rotations, other points may end up increasingly distant from their own snapped location. This is also used as the source window for alignment. Data Window: The snapping point is picked from the data window of the source. This is where pixels actually are; so usually includes effects of cropping or overscan. Display Window: The snapping point is picked from the display window of the source. This is the idealized screen location in pixels, so is independent of cropping or overscan.

parameters.label: Side
parameters.description: Which side to locate the snapping point on the snapwindow, in Y.

parameters.label: Side
parameters.description: Which side to locate the snapping point on the snapwindow, in X.

parameters.label: Justify with
parameters.description: The alignment works by aligning a source rectangle with a target rectangle. Reference Data Window: Use the data window of the reference as the target rectangle. Reference Display Window: Use the display window of the reference as the target rectangle. Original Data Window: Use the data window of the source as the target rectangle. Original Display Window: Use the display window of the source as the target rectangle. Target Point: Use a specific point for the target. Since resizing isn't possible, this is just a single point.

parameters.label: Units
parameters.description: The space in which to specify the target. This applies to the size_ref input, which is the reference layer. Image: Use image coordinates that range from -1 to 1 on the display window of the layer. Texture: Use texture coordinates that range from 0 to 1 on the data window of the layer. Pixels: Use absolute pixel locations in the layer. World: Use coordinates in world space that project through the layer's implicit camera.

parameters.label: Target Point
parameters.description: The target point. The Units parameter determines if this is in image, texture, pixel, or world space.

parameters.label: Justify X/Y
parameters.description: Controls which side of the source rectangle is used. None: No movement on this axis Min: The minimum of the source rectangle is aligned. Center: The center of the source rectangle is aligned. Max: The maximum of the source rectangle is aligned.

parameters.label: Goal X/Y
parameters.description: Controls the target side of the alignment. Same: Aligned to the same side of the target that the source used, so minimum to minimum and center to center. Min: The minimum of the target rectangle is the goal. Center: The center of the target rectangle is the goal. Max: The maximum of the target rectangle is the goal.

parameters.label: Offset by
parameters.description: An additional nudge from the computed alignment position. This is in pixels.

entries.label: Attribute Extract
entries.summary: Extracts a detached attribute from a geometry.

parameters.label: Class
parameters.description: What class of attribute to extract. The attribute will store a property of its source class to make it easier to re-insert, but this is just advisory.
parameters.heading: Outputs

parameters.label: Attribute Name
parameters.description: The name of the attribute to extract.
parameters.heading: Outputs

parameters.label: Output Type
parameters.description: The type of attribute to extract. The attribute on the geometry must match this size and type.
parameters.heading: Outputs

parameters.label: Optional
parameters.description: If the geometry doesn't have the attribute, rather than erroring a constant attribute will be created of the default value.
parameters.heading: Outputs

parameters.label: Default Value
parameters.description: The default value for Float attributes.
parameters.heading: Outputs

parameters.label: Default Value
parameters.description: The default value for Vector 2 attributes.
parameters.heading: Outputs

parameters.label: Default Value
parameters.description: The default value for Vector attributes.
parameters.heading: Outputs

parameters.label: Default Value
parameters.description: The default value for Vector 4 attributes.
parameters.heading: Outputs

parameters.label: Default Value
parameters.description: The default value for Integer attributes.
parameters.heading: Outputs

entries.label: Attribute from Layer
entries.summary: Extracts a detached attribute from a layer.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Data Ordering
parameters.description: The canonical ordering in Copernicus is for the first pixel to be the bottom left, then to read left to right and bottom to top. Instead, the top left can be the first pixel and read left to right and top to bottom.

entries.label: Attribute Insert
entries.summary: Inserts a detached attribute into a geometry.

parameters.label: Class
parameters.description: What class to insert the attribute as. One of the attribute properties is the source class, so in Input mode this will be used if present. Note the attribute must match in length with the elements of the chosen class.
parameters.heading: Inputs

parameters.label: Attribute Name
parameters.description: The name of the attribute after it has been inserted. Existing attributes will be replaced.
parameters.heading: Inputs

parameters.label: Input Type
parameters.description: Usually the input type is Input to store an attribute of the same type as the wire; but an explicit type can be picked to ensure proper promotion of Float to Vector is performed where needed.
parameters.heading: Inputs

parameters.label: Do Nothing If Unwired
parameters.description: If the attribute wire is un-wired, rather than error, do not do anything.
parameters.heading: Inputs

entries.label: Attribute
entries.summary: Creates a detached attribute.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The attribute type generated. This does not have to match the input. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Class
parameters.description: Detached attributes possess a property providing a hint for what class they should be considered. This can be copied from the input, set to a specific class, or set to None. None will prevent auto-deduction on insertion.

parameters.label: Value
parameters.description: The value to initialize the Float attribute to.

parameters.label: Value
parameters.description: The value to initialize the Vector 2 attribute to.

parameters.label: Color
parameters.description: The color to initialize the Vector attribute to.

parameters.label: Color
parameters.description: The color and alpha to initialize the Vector 4 attribute to.

parameters.label: Value
parameters.description: The integer to initialize the Integer attribute to.

parameters.label: Sizing Method
parameters.description: How to compute the attribute's size. The base size will be the input's size. If there is no input, the base size is 0. Set: Use the size, ignoring any input size. Add: Add the input size with the parameter size. Multiply: Multiply the input size with the multiply size parameter.

parameters.label: Size
parameters.description: The size of the attribute, used to either set or extend it.

parameters.label: Multiply Size
parameters.description: A scale factor to resize the attribute.

parameters.label: Type Info
parameters.description: A property providing a hint as to how the attribute should be interpreted. None: No special treatment. Position: This attribute is a geometric point. Houdini will transform the attribute as a position. Vector: Houdini will transform the attribute as a vector. Normal: Houdini will transform the attribute as a normal. Color: This attribute is a color. Quaternion: Houdini will transform the attribute as a quaternion. Transform Matrix: Houdini will transform the attribute as a transformation matrix. Texture Coordinate: This attribute represents texture coordinates, like uv.

entries.label: Layer Merge
entries.summary: Combines all inputs.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Space
parameters.description: The method used to determine which pixels in the foreground and background match. See /copernicus/spaces for more information. Image: Match layers by image coordinates. Pixels remain square and match based on the 2D canvas in which the images are embedded, but ignore 3D transformations. Texture: Match the data windows of the two layers. This stretches the layers so they overlap exactly. Pixel: Match the display windows in pixel space. This ensures pixels are the same size, and uses the data window offset to offset the coordinates. World: Use the background layer's camera to project the foreground onto the background. This matches what you expect to see in the 3D viewport.

parameters.label: Border
parameters.description: The sampling behavior outside of the incoming layer's boundaries. Automatically uses the layer's border property. See Border types for more information.

parameters.label: Filter
parameters.description: The method used to sample the image. See Filters for more information.

parameters.label: Operation
parameters.description: The method used to combine the pixel values of the layers. Add: Add the input layers' pixel values together. Average: Use the average pixel value of the combined input layers. Multiply: Multiply the input layers' pixel values together. Min: Use the minimum pixel value of the combined input layers. Max: Use the maximum pixel value of the combined input layers. Over: Place the preceeding RGBA values over the following RGBA values. Non-RGBA layers copy the final layer's pixels.

parameters.label: Clip by Data Window
parameters.description: Adds an implied mask that matches the data window of the fg input. This prevents the image from extending into the destination. NOTE: The clipping is sharp.

parameters.label: Crop to Content
parameters.description: Crops the output layer to the size of the source layers' transformed data windows.

entries.label: Bake Geometry Textures
entries.summary: Generates textures by baking between a low-resolution and high-resolution mesh at interactive speeds.

parameters.label: Tracer
parameters.description: The tracer to use. This is an automatic menu that shows only available options based on your hardware. NOTE: OptiX is only available on NVIDIA hardware.
parameters.heading: Tracer

parameters.label: Tracing Mode
parameters.description: The tracing mode that the baker utilizes. Surface Normal: Traditional baking by firing rays bidirectionally from the normals of the low-resolution geometry. Requires a low and high input. Cage Mesh: Use a cage mesh to help improve the texture maps. It's sometimes problematic to determine the direction of the rays from the low-resolution mesh to the high-resolution mesh. When you specify a cage mesh, rays are sent from the position on the cage mesh towards the corresponding position on the low-resolution mesh. When you bake with a cage, the cage must be entirely outside of the high-resolution mesh. NOTE: The low-resolution and cage mesh must have the same topology. Cage meshes are used only when the Tracing Mode is Cage Mesh. Single Mesh (low): Bakes the data of a single mesh, and uses the same mesh for the low-resolution and high-resolution mesh. Requires a low input.
parameters.heading: Tracer

parameters.label: UDIM Override
parameters.description: Select a UDIM to bake, which overrides the UDIM context option.
parameters.heading: Tracer

parameters.label: Sample Multiplier
parameters.description: The amount to multiply against the Sample parameters, such as Occlusion Samples and Thickness Samples. This acts as a general quality scale. For example, a Sample Multiplier of 0.5 and Occlusion Samples of 256 bakes occlusion at 128.
parameters.heading: Tracer

parameters.label: Face Culling
parameters.description: Specifies which polygons to ignore when Ray Tracing primary rays. No Culling: Don't ignore any faces. Back Faces: Ignore Primary Rays that hit the back faces of the bake mesh. Front Faces: Ignore Primary Rays that hit the front faces of the bake mesh.
parameters.heading: Ray Setup

parameters.label: Visibility Culling
parameters.description: The method used to handle secondary rays that interact with the geometry. This can allow floaters on the geometry to be projected onto the low-resolution map without casting a shadow. No Culling: Don't ignore any secondary rays. Back Faces: Ignore any secondary rays that hit the back faces of the geometry. Front Faces: Ignore any secondary rays that hit the front faces of the geometry.
parameters.heading: Ray Setup

parameters.label: Ray Start (Point)
parameters.description: The point attribute that lives on the cage input, which stores the Ray Start Positions.
parameters.heading: Cage Attributes

parameters.label: Ray Direction (Vertex)
parameters.description: The vertex attribute that lives on the cage input, which stores the Ray Directions.
parameters.heading: Cage Attributes

parameters.label: Ray Length (Point)
parameters.description: The point attribute that lives on the cage input, which stores the Ray Lengths. Rays Are Endless: Rays travel infinitely until they hit something. Custom Ray Length: Set a custom ray length.
parameters.heading: Cage Attributes

parameters.label: Custom Ray Length
parameters.description: The length of the rays in world units.
parameters.heading: Cage Attributes

parameters.label: Ray Bias
parameters.description: The amount to offset a ray's origin from the surface of the low-resolution mesh when rays are sent from the low-resolution mesh to the scene. You can use this parameter to arbitrarily offset the low-resolution mesh along its normal without having to define a cage mesh.
parameters.heading: Cage Attributes

parameters.label: Normals
parameters.description: How the node deals with low-resolution geometry that's missing normals. For texture baking to work, the low-resolution mesh should have normals. Error if Low Res Mesh Missing Normals: Produces an error if no normal attribute is present. Warning if Low Res Mesh Missing Normals: Produces a warning if no normal attribute is present, but adds point normals weighted by vertex angle internally. Silently Create Missing Normals: Silently adds point normals weighted by vertex angle internally.
parameters.heading: Geometry Setup

parameters.label: Tangents
parameters.description: How the node deals with low-resolution geometry that's missing tangent attributes. For texture baking to work, the low-resolution mesh should have tangent attributes. Add MikkT Tangents if Needed: Adds MikkT tangents using a Polyframe SOP internally. Add Texture UV Tangents if Needed: Adds texture UV tangents using a Polyframe SOP internally. Error if No Tangent Attributes Present: Produces an error if tangent attributes are missing.
parameters.heading: Geometry Setup

parameters.label: UV Attribute
parameters.description: The attribute to use for UV unwrapping and rasterization. This can be a vertex or point.
parameters.heading: Geometry Setup

parameters.label: Remove UV Z values
parameters.description: Flattens the Z component of float3 UV attributes to 0. Some UV nodes output float3 values by default, which can lead to unexpected results when rasterizing in UV mode.
parameters.heading: Geometry Setup

parameters.label: Match Pieces by Name
parameters.description: Lets you control which primitives are visible when computing ray tracing effects like occlusion and curvature. This matches primitives between the low-resolution and high-resolution geometry and isolates them in their own pocket dimension, which can be used to prevent intersection errors. If a ray hits an object that doesn't belong to the current matched piece, it's ignored. This causes a rebake and changes the bake results. NOTE: This parameter is internally known as Trace Sets.
parameters.heading: Match Pieces by Name

parameters.label: Piece Attribute
parameters.description: The primitive piece attribute to use to identify the different pieces across the low-resolution, high-resolution, and cage.
parameters.heading: Match Pieces by Name

parameters.label: Include Pieces
parameters.description: The sets to always include in the bake. This uses standard Houdini pattern matching.
parameters.heading: Match Pieces by Name

parameters.label: Exclude Pieces
parameters.description: The sets to always exclude from the bake. This happens after the include pieces are gathered. This uses standard Houdini pattern matching. For example, if your include is * but your exclude is hat, the baker bakes every set available except hat.
parameters.heading: Match Pieces by Name

parameters.label: Enable UV Boundary Filling
parameters.description: Fills empty areas of the image using colors at the edges of non-empty areas. This is a post-process that fixes darker pixel values at the edges of UV seams, and can produce better results when MIP-mapping the textures. NOTE: This process can be time consuming. For faster iterations, turn this feature on only for the final baking.
parameters.heading: Enable UV Boundary Filling

parameters.label: Exterior
parameters.description: The method used to set the pixels beyond the edge padding. Unchanged: Leave the pixels unchanged. Black: Set the pixels to black (0). Diffuse Fill: Run a Smooth Fill COP over the region, which smoothly interpolates the pixel values.
parameters.heading: Enable UV Boundary Filling

parameters.label: Edge Padding
parameters.description: The distance (in image coordinates) to directly copy pixel values into the exterior.
parameters.heading: Enable UV Boundary Filling

parameters.label: Edge Offset
parameters.description: When reading the original value to copy outwards for edge padding, the value exactly at the edge padding may already have exterior color incorporated. This is the distance (in image coordinates) to backtrack and read clean values for extrapolation.
parameters.heading: Enable UV Boundary Filling

parameters.label: Exclude Alpha from UV Fill
parameters.description: Turns off UV filling on the alpha map. Adding UV filling to alpha often results in a fully white output.
parameters.heading: Enable UV Boundary Filling

parameters.label: Normal Y Direction
parameters.description: Determines the direction of the Y value of the tangent space normal (or rounded normal) AOVs.
parameters.heading: Alignment

parameters.label: Tangent Normal
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the Tangent Normal map. When off, the normal output is a Null layer.
parameters.heading: Tangent Normal

parameters.label: Normal Space
parameters.description: The normal type the layer outputs as. The natural way to represent normals and how they're represented in geometry is to use signed normals. The red, green, and blue channel can store the x, y, and z components of the normal and range from -1 to 1. However, historically GPUs and photoediting software don't support negative ranges, so normal maps in image files are usually stored in an offset format where they have values from 0 to 1. Signed (-1 to 1): Signed normals where the x, y, and z components range from -1 to 1. Offset (0 to 1): Offset normals where the x, y, and z components range from 0 to 1.
parameters.heading: Tangent Normal

parameters.label: Rounded Edge Normal
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the Rounded Edge Normal map. When off, the edgenormal output is a Null layer.
parameters.heading: Rounded Edge Normal

parameters.label: Rounded Normal Space
parameters.description: The normal type the layer outputs as. The natural way to represent normals and how they're represented in geometry is to use signed normals. The red, green, and blue channel can store the x, y, and z components of the normal and range from -1 to 1. However, historically GPUs and photoediting software don't support negative ranges, so normal maps in image files are usually stored in an offset format where they have values from 0 to 1. Signed (-1 to 1): Signed normals where the x, y, and z components range from -1 to 1. Offset (0 to 1): Offset normals where the x, y, and z components range from 0 to 1.
parameters.heading: Rounded Edge Normal

parameters.label: Rounded Samples
parameters.description: The number of indirect rays used when computing Rounded Edge Normal. If the resulting AOV is noisy, increase Rounded Samples to reduce noise.
parameters.heading: Rounded Edge Normal

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: Whether to capture concave or convex edges in the rounded edge normal map.
parameters.heading: Rounded Edge Normal

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: The radius for the rounded normals.
parameters.heading: Rounded Edge Normal

parameters.label: Cusp Angle
parameters.description: Polygons that have an angle less than this threshold are assumed to be a smooth surface and not appear in the rounded normal map.
parameters.heading: Rounded Edge Normal

parameters.label: World Space
parameters.description: Whether to record the world space position in left or right handed space with Y or Z as the up axis.
parameters.heading: Alignment

parameters.label: World Normal
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the World Normal map. When off, the worldnormal output is a Null layer.
parameters.heading: World Normal

parameters.label: World Normal Space
parameters.description: How to represent the normal map. Signed (-1 to 1): Signed normals where the x, y, and z components range from -1 to 1. Offset (0 to 1): Offset normals where the x, y, and z components range from 0 to 1.
parameters.heading: World Normal

parameters.label: Position
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the Position map. When off, the position output is a Null layer.
parameters.heading: Position

parameters.label: Position Space
parameters.description: How to represent the position map. Absolute ( Use Actual Position Values ): The position isn't normalized and dependent on object size and world position. Relative ( Use Position Within Bounding Box): The position is normalized relative to its bounding box.
parameters.heading: Position

parameters.label: Bounding Box
parameters.description: When the Position is stored, this is how the position is represented. Fit to Bounding Box: The shading position is fit to the bounding box of the low-resolution mesh. Fit to Uniform Box (No Stretching): The shading position is fit to a uniform bounding box of the low-resolution mesh. In this mode, all three axes of the bounding box have the same length.
parameters.heading: Position

parameters.label: Ambient Occlusion
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the Ambient Occlusion map. When off, the occlusion output is a Null layer.
parameters.heading: Ambient Occlusion

parameters.label: Occlusion Samples
parameters.description: The number of indirect rays used when computing Occlusion. If the resulting AOV is noisy, increase Occlusion Samples to reduce noise.
parameters.heading: Ambient Occlusion

parameters.label: Max Distance
parameters.description: The maximum distance to consider when computing Occlusion. A small distance can speed up occlusion shading at the cost of accuracy.
parameters.heading: Ambient Occlusion

parameters.label: Curvature
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the Curvature map. When off, the curvature output is a Null layer.
parameters.heading: Curvature

parameters.label: Curvature Samples
parameters.description: The number of indirect rays used when computing Curvature. If the resulting AOV is noisy, increase Curvature Samples to reduce noise.
parameters.heading: Curvature

parameters.label: Curvature Scale
parameters.description: Controls the overall intensity or contrast of the curvature by amplifying the difference between convex and concave responses.
parameters.heading: Curvature

parameters.label: Max Distance
parameters.description: Smaller values (which create smaller distance) emphasize the concavity. Larger values (which represent greater distance) reveal more curvature and improve the visibility of the convex features.
parameters.heading: Curvature

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.description: Controls whether the map looks more concave or more convex. Smaller values emphasize concavity, higher values enhance convexity.
parameters.heading: Curvature

parameters.label: Edge
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the Edge map. When off, the edge output is a Null layer.
parameters.heading: Edge

parameters.label: Edge Samples
parameters.description: The number of indirect rays used when computing Edge. If the resulting AOV is noisy, increase Edge Samples to reduce noise.
parameters.heading: Edge

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: The types of edges (concave or convex) to smooth.
parameters.heading: Edge

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: The radius of the rounded edge.
parameters.heading: Edge

parameters.label: Cusp Angle
parameters.description: Polygons with an angle below this threshold are considered smooth and don't appear in the Edge map.
parameters.heading: Edge

parameters.label: Cavity
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the Cavity map. When off, the cavity output is a Null layer.
parameters.heading: Cavity

parameters.label: Cavity Samples
parameters.description: The number of indirect rays used when computing Cavity. If the resulting AOV is noisy, increase Cavity Samples to reduce noise.
parameters.heading: Cavity

parameters.label: Max Distance
parameters.description: Limits how far rays can detect nearby geometry. Smaller values (smaller distance) emphasize concavity.
parameters.heading: Cavity

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.description: Blends between a full cavity contrast (0) and a flat result (1).
parameters.heading: Cavity

parameters.label: Thickness
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the Thickness map. When off, the thickness output is a Null layer.
parameters.heading: Thickness

parameters.label: Thickness Samples
parameters.description: The number of indirect rays used when computing Thickness. If the resulting AOV is noisy, increase Thickness Samples to reduce noise.
parameters.heading: Thickness

parameters.label: Invert Thickness Map
parameters.description: Inverts the Thickness map so that thinner areas create darker values and thicker areas create brighter values.
parameters.heading: Thickness

parameters.label: Height
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the Height map. When off, the height output is a Null layer.
parameters.heading: Height

parameters.label: Height Space
parameters.description: Height bakes the true displacement between the low-resolution and high-resolution. This distance may be miniscule so the output image can appear nearly entirely black, which may not be useful when used in masking or shaders so may require manual remapping later. Set this to Custom to remap the height map. True Displacement: True displacement values. These may be visually unfriendly results, and for some bake meshes appear completely black if the geometric difference between the low-resolution and high-resolution is small. Custom: Remap the height layer according to inner and outer distance parameters.
parameters.heading: Height

parameters.label: Inner Distance
parameters.description: Remaps the data within the height map from the inner distance to 0.0.
parameters.heading: Height

parameters.label: Outer Distance
parameters.description: Remaps the data within the height map from the outer distance to 1.0.
parameters.heading: Height

parameters.label: Alpha
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the Alpha map. When off, the alpha output is a Null layer.
parameters.heading: Alpha

parameters.label: Mask Out High Resolution Mesh
parameters.description: Checks for any valid hits on the high-resolution mesh and creates an alpha mask from this, rather than the low-resolution UV map.
parameters.heading: Alpha

parameters.label: Quick Setups
parameters.description: Add a geometry attribute to bake.
parameters.heading: Custom Attributes

parameters.label: Custom Attributes
parameters.description: The number of custom attributes to rasterize.
parameters.heading: Custom Attributes

parameters.label: Attribute Name
parameters.description: Turns on the Position map's baking, which bakes the world position values to the RGB components of the layer. When off, the position output is a Null layer.
parameters.heading: Custom Attributes

parameters.label: Attribute Name
parameters.description: The name of the attribute to rasterize. This must match the attribute present on the geometry. This can be a Point, Vertex, or Primitive.
parameters.heading: Custom Attributes

parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: The output type for the rasterized attribute. To be rasterized, an attribute must either be an integer or a float of four or less components. Mono: Mono layer for single float attributes. UV: UV layer for float2 attributes. RGB: RGB layer for float3 attributes. RGBA: RGBA layer for float4 attributes. ID: ID layer for integer attributes.
parameters.heading: Custom Attributes

entries.label: Bake Pre-Process
entries.summary: Sets up rays for baking, with a visualization state.

parameters.label: Normal Mode
parameters.description: The mode of the normals. Geometric Normal: Sets the normals to the incoming existing geometric normals. Smooth Normals: Promotes the normals to averaged point normals, then back to vertex again.
parameters.heading: Normals

parameters.label: Override
parameters.description: Overrides any existing normals.
parameters.heading: Normals

parameters.label: Missing Normals
parameters.description: How the node deals with low-resolution geometry that's missing normals. For texture baking to work, the low-resolution mesh should have normals. Message and Create Missing Normals: Produces a message if no normal attribute is present, but adds vertex normals weighted by vertex angle internally. Error if Low Res Mesh Missing Normals: Produces an error if no normal attribute is present. Warning if Low Res Mesh Missing Normals: Produces a warning if no normal attribute is present, but adds vertex normals weighted by vertex angle internally. Silently Create Missing Normals: Silently adds vertex normals weighted by vertex angle internally.
parameters.heading: Normals

parameters.label: Cusp Angle
parameters.description: Cusp Angle: When computing vertex normals, if normals of vertices around a single point are less than or equal to this angle (in degrees) apart from each other, they will be averaged together, weighted by the vertex angle in each polygon.
parameters.heading: Advanced Normal Creation Options

parameters.label: Weighting Method
parameters.description: Weighting Method: When set to By Vertex Angle, care is taken when computing normals to try to avoid issues introduced by sliver polygons and to weight contributions to normals by angle, so that triangulation won't change normals significantly. When set to Each Vertex Equally, a faster, but less accurate, approach similar to the approach used by the Facet SOP, is used to compute normals, where each vertex is given equal weight around a point, and less checks are done for ensuring stability. When set to By Face Area, the behavior is similar to Each Vertex Equally_, except that vertices on faces with more area will be given more weight when computing point normals. This is often used to fake the appearance of a smooth bevel for geometry with only a simple chamfer.
parameters.heading: Advanced Normal Creation Options

parameters.label: Soften Cage Group
parameters.description: The point or primitive group to which you apply softening.
parameters.heading: Advanced Normal Creation Options

parameters.label: Soften Cage
parameters.description: Facets the geometry in certain ways before applying the cage offset (Ray Start Offset). A soft cage isn't faceted and ensures a seamless result across sharp edges, but can cause projection errors and skewed detail as the normals are averaged. An unsoftened cage (which is faceted) can fix this projection skewing, but can cause missing detail capture on sharp edges.
parameters.heading: Advanced Normal Creation Options

parameters.label: Soften Mode
parameters.description: The method used to cut up the geometry. By Faces: Split the geometry across faces. By UV Seams: Split the geometry across UV Seams. Requires a UV attribute. By Edge Group: Split the geometry by a custom edge group.
parameters.heading: Advanced Normal Creation Options

parameters.label: Edge Group
parameters.description: The edge group by which to split the geometry.
parameters.heading: Advanced Normal Creation Options

parameters.label: Ray Start Offset
parameters.description: How far the duplicate mesh peaks out from the normals of the original low-resolution mesh. This is the ray start position or the 'Cage'.
parameters.heading: Ray Start

parameters.label: Ray Start Mode
parameters.description: Uniform: No variable offset. Scale by Attribute: Scale the ray start offset by an attribute value, multiplied against the Ray Start Offset.
parameters.heading: Ray Start

parameters.label: Attribute
parameters.description: The attribute value by which to scale the Ray Start Offset.
parameters.heading: Ray Start

parameters.label: Ray End Offset
parameters.description: How far the duplicate mesh peaks in from the normals of the original low-resolution mesh. This is the ray end position. This is turned into the raylength output attribute by calculating the distance difference between the Ray Start Offset and the Ray End Offset.
parameters.heading: Ray End

parameters.label: Ray End Mode
parameters.description: Uniform: No variable offset. Scale by Attribute: Scale the ray end offset by an attribute value, multiplied against the Ray End Offset. No End: Endless rays. Sets the raylength attribute to a value of -1, which the Bake Geometry Textures COP can recognize as endless rays.
parameters.heading: Ray End

parameters.label: Attribute
parameters.description: The attribute value by which to scale the Ray End Offset.
parameters.heading: Ray End

parameters.label: Ray Start (Point)
parameters.description: The point attribute that lives on the cage output, which stores the Ray Start Positions.
parameters.heading: Cage Output Attributes

parameters.label: Ray Direction (Vertex)
parameters.description: The vertex attribute that lives on the cage output, which stores the Ray Directions.
parameters.heading: Cage Output Attributes

parameters.label: Ray Length (Point)
parameters.description: The point attribute that lives on the cage output, which stores the Ray Lengths.
parameters.heading: Cage Output Attributes

parameters.description: The length in image space of the Capture Direction's vector. Higher values result in a larger region of space that receives the partial transforms. NOTE: This value shouldn't be 0 because then there's nothing to bend.
