entries.label: Blend
entries.summary: Blends two layers, VDBs, or attributes together.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Space
parameters.description: The method used to determine which pixels in the foreground and background match. See /copernicus/spaces for more information. Image: Match layers by image coordinates. Pixels remain square and match based on the 2D canvas in which the images are embedded, but ignore 3D transformations. Texture: Match the data windows of the two layers. This stretches the layers so they overlap exactly. Pixel: Match the display windows in pixel space. This ensures pixels are the same size, and uses the data window offset to offset the coordinates. World: Use the background layer's camera to project the foreground onto the background. This matches what you expect to see in the 3D viewport.

parameters.label: Border
parameters.description: The sampling behavior outside of the incoming layer's boundaries. Automatically uses the layer's border property. See Border types for more information.

parameters.label: Filter
parameters.description: The method used to sample the image. See Filters for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. You can also set the RGBA channels to which you apply the effects of this node. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information. Toggle RGB: Turns the Red, Green, and Blue channels on and off. Red: Applies this node's effects to the Red channel. Green: Applies this node's effects to the Green channel. Blue: Applies this node's effects to the Blue channel. Alpha: Applies this node's effects to the Alpha channel.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: Specifies the global compositing operation. Blend: Replaces the background with the foreground. Over: Places the foreground over the background. Under: Places the foreground under the background's alpha. Add: Adds the foreground to the background. Subtract: Subtracts the foreground from the background. Multiply: Multiplies the background by the foreground. Divide: Divides the background by the foreground. Screen: Acts as a saturating add, much like adding photographs. Hypot: Channel-wise, takes the length of the vector formed by the foreground and background channels. Difference: Takes the absolute difference between the foreground and the background. Exclusion: Takes the sum of the foreground and background and subtracts twice the product of the two. This results in a lower contrast version of difference. Blending with 1.0 will invert the source, and 0.0 will leave it unchanged. Sharpen: Increases the contrast of the background using the foreground as the mid-point contrast value. Maximum: Takes the maximum of the foreground and background. This is done component-wise unless the Compare Lengths parameter is set. Minimum: Takes the minimum of the foreground and background. This is done component-wise unless the Compare Lengths parameter is set. Overlay: Switches between applying a Multiply and Screen based on the value of the background. Areas below 0.5 multiply and areas above 0.5 screen. SoftLight: Applies a smooth contrast to the background according to the value of the foreground. The foreground is clamped to 0 to 1. HardLight: Switches between applying a Multiply and Screen based on the value of the foreground. Areas below 0.5 multiply and areas above 0.5 screen. Dodge: Lightens an image according to the foreground value. Burn: Darkens an image according to the foreground value. Hue: Replaces the background's hue with the foreground's. Saturation: Replaces the background's saturation with the foreground's. Luminosity: Replaces the background's luminosity with the foreground's. Color: Replaces the background's color with the foreground's.

parameters.label: Alpha Compositing
parameters.description: For RGBA layers, you can process the blending operation per-component or by using Alpha Compositing rules. When on, this extends monochrome layers with 1 in the alpha so they act like opaque layers. When off, each component (including alpha) is processed independently. This allows a multiply with mono layer to multiply all channels the same.

parameters.label: Swap FG and BG
parameters.description: Swaps the values of the foreground and background. This is useful for non-commutative operators. This has no effect with commutative operators, as this does not affect the masking operation.

parameters.label: Compare Lengths
parameters.description: In maximum and minimum mode, choose the output based on the length of the two values; rather than working component-wise. This allows one to mix vector fields where the highest or lowest magnitude vector is kept.

parameters.label: Clip by Data Window
parameters.description: Adds an implied mask that matches the data window of the fg input. This prevents the image from extending into the destination. NOTE: The clipping is sharp.

parameters.label: Crop to Content
parameters.description: Crop the new layer to the union of the foreground layer's transformed data window and the background layer's data window.

entries.label: Block Begin
entries.summary: Start of a block, containing its inputs.

parameters.label: Block Path
parameters.description: The path to the Block End COP that's the final and closing node of this block. The Block End node must be at the same network level as this Block Begin node.

parameters.label: Rename Wires Using Output Labels
parameters.description: When this toggle is enabled, name of each output wire is set based on its respective port label. Otherwise, wire names are propagated from inputs. Turn this option on if you'd like to discard incoming wire names and harden new ones for the downstream network to use.

parameters.label: Block Inputs
parameters.description: The number of inputs to this block.

parameters.label: Input Name
parameters.description: The name of the input. This string identifies the input when using the Invoke Block COP to execute the block, or when binding inputs for slap comp.

parameters.label: Input Type
parameters.description: The type of the input. This controls what kind of data can be fed into the corresponding port (or bound to the input), as well as what the input can be plugged into. See Data types for more information.

entries.label: Block End
entries.summary: End of a block, declaring its outputs.

parameters.label: Simulate
parameters.description: Turns on simulation so block outputs feed directly back into the inputs, which creates a feedback loop. This is useful for complex motion and simulations.

parameters.label: Reset Simulation
parameters.description: When Simulate is on, this clears the entire simulation cache.

parameters.label: Live Simulation
parameters.description: When Simulate is on, this turns on live simulation to provide an interactive, non-deterministic simulation mode. It simulates independent of the playbar and isn't associated with any keyframes or caching. This parameter (and its associated parameters) is intended as a sandbox mode where you don't have to rely on the playbar. TIP: Live Simulation doesn't save the results like other simulation types in Houdini, so use a Stash COP to save results.

parameters.label: Time Scale
parameters.description: When Simulate is on, this is the amount to scale the time inside the block. A value of 1 maintains the normal speed, a value greater than 1 speeds up the simulation, and a value less than 1 slows down the simulation.

parameters.label: Start Frame
parameters.description: When Simulate is on, this is the frame on the Houdini playbar where the simulation starts.

parameters.label: Cache Simulation
parameters.description: When Simulate is on, this enables the caching of the simulation. If the simulation is uncached, it will always have to cook from the start frame on any new frame.

parameters.label: Cached Frames
parameters.description: When Simulate is on, this is how many frames behind the current frame to keep cached.

parameters.label: Checkpoint Rate
parameters.description: When Simulate is on, this is the rate at which the node continually caches a single frame. For example, set this to 24 to cache frames 24, 48, 72, and such. This allows random-scrubbing to be faster as it only has to re-cook from the checkpoint frame. Set to 0 to disable checkpointing.

parameters.label: Toggle Live Simulation
parameters.description: When Live Simulation is on, this lets you pause and resume the live simulation. TIP: You can also use the Icon:BUTTONS/live_disable Live Simulation button to pause and resume live simulation. See Cooking controls for more information.

parameters.label: Live Tick
parameters.description: When Live Simulation is on, this is the current tick (frame) within the live simulation.

parameters.label: Iterations
parameters.description: How many iterations of the block to run per frame. For example, if you set this to 40 it runs the internals of the block 40 times for each generated frame. This means that by frame 10 it's run 400 iterations but only produced 10 frames.

parameters.label: Iteration Variable
parameters.description: The name of the context option that stores the current iteration, which starts at 0 and counts up to one less than the Iterations amount. Use the Exp:contextoption expression function to access this value inside the block.

parameters.label: Total Iterations Variable
parameters.description: The name of the context option that stores the total number of iterations this block is set to run for, which is equal to the Iterations amount. Use the Exp:contextoption expression function to access this value inside the block.

parameters.label: First Pass Variable
parameters.description: The name of the context option that identifies the first pass in the block. This is equal to 1 on the first iteration of a simple loop or the first substep of a simulation, otherwise it evaluates to 0. Use the Exp:contextoption expression function to read this variable's value.

parameters.label: Enable Compiling
parameters.description: Compiles the block when its outputs need to be cooked. This is more efficient, but doesn't save out any of the intermediate results within the block. NOTE: Compiled COP networks don't support simulation.

parameters.label: Register as Slap Comp Block
parameters.description: Makes this block available to use for slap comp in the Solaris viewport.

parameters.label: Import Cameras with Slap Comp Inputs
parameters.label_norm: import cameras with slap comp inputs
parameters.description: When Register as Slap Comp Block is on, this controls where the incoming layers are placed. When Import Cameras with Slap Comp Inputs is on, the layers come in with the view transform of the camera. When Import Cameras with Slap Comp Inputs is off, this places all layers at the origin, facing the Z axis. Turn this parameter on if you plan to combine the render results with other objects in 3D space.

parameters.label: Add AOVs from Last Render
parameters.description: When Register as Slap Comp Block is on, this populates the block's output list with AOVs from the last Solaris viewport render. The Slap Comp Import COP also has this parameter to fill that node with the render's AOVs and any Block Begin nodes plugged into it.

parameters.label: Rename Wires Using Output Labels
parameters.description: When this toggle is enabled, name of each output wire is set based on its respective port label. Otherwise, wire names are propagated from inputs. Turn this option on if you'd like to discard incoming wire names and harden new ones for the downstream network to use.

parameters.label: Block Outputs
parameters.description: The number of outputs for this block.

parameters.label: Output Name
parameters.description: The name of the output. This string identifies the output when using the Invoke Block COP to execute the block, or when the block is used for slap comp.

parameters.label: Output Type
parameters.description: The type of the output and the corresponding ports on the node. See Data types for more information.

entries.label: Blur
entries.summary: Applies a blur to a layer.

parameters.label: Filter
parameters.description: The filter to blur the image with. See Filters for more information. Box: Creates a box around the pixel of which to take an average of. Gaussian (default): Take a weighted average of the pixels according to a Gaussian distribution.

parameters.label: Read Pixels outside Image
parameters.description: Adds contributions from pixels outside of the image. This depends on the border type, which determines what pixels to read as outside of the image.

parameters.label: Units
parameters.description: The unit of measurement used to determine the size of the blur effect's radius. Image (default): Sets the blur radius to use units of the Image Space. Pixels: Sets the blur radius to use units of the number of pixels. Local: Sets the blur radius to use units of the Local Space.

parameters.label: Size
parameters.description: The size of the blur effect's radius in image, pixels, or local units, which the Units parameter determines.

parameters.label: Scale Size
parameters.description: Scales the blur radius for a specific axis.

parameters.label: Scale by Timestep
parameters.description: Adjusts the blur's overall strength by the current timestep. The timestep is usually 1/$FPS, but in a sub-stepped simulation it represents the current step size.

entries.label: Bubble Noise
entries.summary: Generates bubble noise.

parameters.label: Type Info
parameters.description: The type information for the resulting layer. See Type info for more information.

parameters.label: Amplitude
parameters.description: The amount by which to multiply the noise, which the node applies before the Center adjustment. For example, a value of 0.5 makes a pixel value of 0.5 become 0.25. NOTE: Layers can store negative numbers and values above 1, so this may result in out-of-bounds values. Use the Post Processing options to clamp the output.
parameters.heading: Bubble Noise

parameters.label: Center
parameters.description: The center of the output noise range, which offsets the pixel values. For example, a value of 0.5 makes a pixel value of 0.5 become 1.
parameters.heading: Bubble Noise

parameters.label: Element Size
parameters.description: The size (in image coordinates) of the basic element of the noise. You can turn on the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button to adjust this further using the Element Scale parameter.
parameters.heading: Bubble Noise

parameters.label: Element Scale
parameters.description: When the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button is on, this is the per-axis scaling of the element size for anistropic noise.
parameters.heading: Bubble Noise

parameters.label: Phase
parameters.description: The location of the noise in four-dimensional space, which lets you smoothly pick different seeds. Torus noise works by sampling a flat torus in a four-dimensional space.
parameters.heading: Bubble Noise

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.description: The amount to offset the entire noise function in image coordinates.
parameters.heading: Bubble Noise

parameters.label: Tile Size
parameters.description: The size of a single tile of noise. The noise periodically repeats in this size. The size is in image coordinates, so the default is for the entire default canoncial image. If you have a non-square image, this should match the aspect ratio.
parameters.heading: Bubble Noise

parameters.label: Noise Type
parameters.description: The underlying noise function that's iteratively sampled to generate the fractal noise. Simplex: Create Perlin noise on a simplex grid. Curl: Create a divergence-free curl function on Perlin noise.
parameters.heading: Fractal

parameters.label: Max Octaves
parameters.description: The amount of times to scale add together the noise.
parameters.heading: Fractal

parameters.label: Lacunarity
parameters.description: The amount to scale the noise for each iteration, which is rounded to an integer value for periodic noise.
parameters.heading: Fractal

parameters.label: Roughness
parameters.description: The amount to scale the amplitude of each successive noise.
parameters.heading: Fractal

parameters.label: Distortion
parameters.description: The amount to distort the noise in the direction of decreasing noise values (when greater than 1) or increasing noise values (when less than 1).
parameters.heading: Warping

parameters.label: Stretch
parameters.description: The amount to stretch the noise in each direction in image coordinates. NOTE: Use this parameter instead of Element Size to preserve some details unstretched, which makes the stretched noise pattern look more natural.
parameters.heading: Warping

parameters.label: Droop
parameters.description: The amount to warp the generated noise pattern so it bends or hangs towards the Droop Direction.
parameters.heading: Warping

parameters.label: Droop Direction
parameters.description: When Droop is on, this is the direction in image coordinates in which to warp the noise.
parameters.heading: Warping

parameters.label: Fold each Octave
parameters.description: Remaps the values between -1 and 1 and flips values below 0 to the positive range. For example, a pixel value of -2 becomes 2. This makes all valleys become peaks. NOTE: The node remaps the values during the noise evaluation. This is different from applying an absolute function afterwards like some other noise nodes (Fractal Noise for example).
parameters.heading: Warping

parameters.label: NOTE
parameters.description: The node applies the post-processing operations in the order they're listed.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Fold
parameters.description: Sets the noise values to the absolute value. For example, a pixel value of -2 becomes 2. NOTE: This parameter doesn't impact the output when there's only positive values.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Complement
parameters.description: Sets the pixel value x to 1 - x. NOTE: This method works for values in the 0 to 1 range. For images outside of this range, using Complement results in negative or out of range values.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.description: The amount to pull the medium grey values (around 0.5) towards zero (if Bias is less than 1) or one (if Bias is greater than 1). A bias value of 0.5 doesn't affect the values. Image:/images/nodes/cop/postprocessing_bias.jpg
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Gain
parameters.description: The amount to pull the medium grey values (around 0.5) together, while values around 0 and 1 are pulled apart. A gain value of 0.5 doesn't affect the noise values. Image:/images/nodes/cop/postprocessing_gain.jpg
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Gamma
parameters.description: The overall gamma of the generated noise. Values greater than 1 increase the range of values in originally bright areas, which darkens the noise. Values less than 1 stretch out the range of values for originally dark areas, which increases the overall brightness of the noise.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Contrast
parameters.description: The amount to expand or shrink the overall range of tonal values. Each noise value is pushed towards (if Contrast is less than 1) or away from (if Contrast is greater than 1) medium grey values (around 0.5). NOTE: This is not the same as Noise Contrast, which appears in some noise nodes and applies contrast during the noise function.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Clamp Minimum
parameters.description: Clamps values below the specified threshold.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Clamp Maximum
parameters.description: Clamps values exceeding the specified threshold.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

entries.label: Camera
entries.summary: Creates a camera.

parameters.label: Set Parameters from Input
parameters.description: Autofills the camera's parameters with the settings from the connected camera_ref.

parameters.label: Transform
parameters.description: Transforms the camera.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Transform Order
parameters.description: The order in which transformations and rotations occur.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Translate
parameters.description: The amount of translation along xyz axes.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.description: The amount of rotation about the xyz axes.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Pivot Translate
parameters.description: The local pivot space's translation value for transformations.
parameters.heading: Pivot Transform

parameters.label: Pivot Rotate
parameters.description: The local pivot space's rotation value for transformations.
parameters.heading: Pivot Transform

parameters.label: Look At
parameters.description: Sets the look at target.
parameters.heading: Look At

parameters.label: Look At Position
parameters.description: The target position for the camera to look at.
parameters.heading: Look At

parameters.label: Up Vector Method
parameters.description: Determines the up vector of the look at. Y Axis: Use the Y axis as the up vector. X Axis: Use the X axis as the up vector. Custom: Set a custom position (Up Vector) to use as the up vector.
parameters.heading: Look At

parameters.label: Up Vector
parameters.description: A custom position to use as the up vector of the look at.
parameters.heading: Look At

parameters.label: Twist
parameters.description: Rotates the camera in degrees about the look at axis.
parameters.heading: Look At

parameters.label: View
parameters.description: Sets the view of the camera.
parameters.heading: View

parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.description: Sets the camera resolution in pixels.
parameters.heading: View

parameters.label: Projection
parameters.description: Sets the camera projection type.
parameters.heading: View

parameters.label: Focal Length
parameters.description: Sets the camera's focal length (zoom) in millimeters.
parameters.heading: View

parameters.label: Aperture
parameters.description: Sets the camera's horizontal aperture in millimeters, which is the width of the visible field. The ratio of Focal Length and Aperture determines the offset of the camera. The absolute values are not relevant, so they can be in any unit as long as they're consistent.
parameters.heading: View

parameters.label: Ortho Width
parameters.description: Sets the width of the orthographic view's volume when the Projection is Orthographic.
parameters.heading: View

parameters.label: Near Clipping
parameters.description: Sets the position of the camera's near clipping plane.
parameters.heading: View

parameters.label: Far Clipping
parameters.description: Sets the position of the camera's far clipping plane.
parameters.heading: View

parameters.label: Screen Window X/Y
parameters.description: Defines the center of the window during the rendering process.
parameters.heading: View

parameters.label: Screen Window Size
parameters.description: Expands the cropped area that the Crop parameters specify.
parameters.heading: View

parameters.label: Left Crop
parameters.description: Sets the left cropping margin for the camera's view area.
parameters.heading: View

parameters.label: Right Crop
parameters.description: Sets the right cropping margin for the camera's view area.
parameters.heading: View

parameters.label: Bottom Crop
parameters.description: Sets the bottom cropping margin for the camera's view area.
parameters.heading: View

parameters.label: Top Crop
parameters.description: Sets the top cropping margin for the camera's view area.
parameters.heading: View

parameters.label: Imaging Distance
parameters.description: Sets how far the layer is (in Houdini units) from the eye of the camera.
parameters.heading: View

parameters.label: Guide Scale
parameters.description: Specifies the scale of the camera that's displayed when the layer is metadata.
parameters.heading: View

parameters.label: Sampling
parameters.description: Sets how the camera samples the layer.
parameters.heading: Sampling

parameters.label: Shutter Open
parameters.description: Sets when the camera starts receiving light (open). This is relative to the frame rate.
parameters.heading: Sampling

parameters.label: Shutter Close
parameters.description: Sets when the camera stops receiving light (closed). This is relative to the frame rate.
parameters.heading: Sampling

parameters.label: Focus Distance
parameters.description: Sets the distance from the camera at which objects are in focus, relative to the layer's origin.
parameters.heading: Sampling

parameters.label: F-Stop
parameters.description: Sets the camera's F-stop. Higher values decrease how blurry objects are outside of the Focus Distance.
parameters.heading: Sampling

parameters.label: Metadata
parameters.description: Modifies the metadata dictionary.
parameters.heading: Metadata

parameters.label: Entries
parameters.description: Specifies the number of key and value pairs to add or edit in the metadata dictionary. This option can be useful for adding metadata items with simple data types, such as strings or integers.
parameters.heading: Metadata

parameters.label: Key
parameters.description: The string key to insert or modify the value for.
parameters.heading: Metadata

parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: The data type of the dictionary value.
parameters.heading: Metadata

parameters.label: Value
parameters.description: The value to insert into the dictionary for the Key.
parameters.heading: Metadata

entries.label: Camera Blend
entries.summary: Blends two cameras.

parameters.label: Blend
parameters.description: The weight of the blend between the source and background cameras. A value of 0 displays just the fg camera and a value of 1 displays just the bg camera.

entries.label: Camera Properties
entries.summary: Adjusts the camera properties of a layer.

parameters.label: Projection
parameters.description: The basic projection type. Perspective: A perspective transform where rays converge on the camera position. This is offset back by the focal length from the origin of the layer. Orthographic: An orthographic transform where all rays are parallel.

parameters.label: Imaging Distance
parameters.description: The layer is placed a certain distance away from the eye of the layer's camera. This controls how far this is. The distance can be set explicitly or adjusted from the current distance. It can also be set to automatically set the distance at which the layer will go through a particular point.

parameters.label: Imaging Point
parameters.description: The point in worldspace the imaging layer should go through. The imaging distance will be adjusted so the imaging plane will intersect this point. This makes it straightforward to stick the imaging layers on a focus object despite camera motion.

parameters.label: Near/Far
parameters.description: The near and far clipping of the camera, measured from the distance from the camera origin (rather than from the layer's origin).

parameters.label: Focal Length
parameters.description: The distance, in the same units as Aperture, to set the camera's origin back from the layer's origin.

parameters.label: Aperture (mm)
parameters.description: The width of the camera's aperture. This can be viewed as the width of the layer. The ratio of focal length and aperture is what determines the offset of the camera. The absolute values are not relevant, so they can be in any unit as long as they're consistent.

parameters.label: Aperture Offset
parameters.description: The horizontal adjustment of the aperture, allowing offseting of the imaging point.

parameters.label: Shutter Open/Close
parameters.description: The metadata that controls when the camera should start receiving light and stop receiving light. This is relative to the frame rate. When you have a source layer this parameter isn't used.

parameters.label: Focus Distance
parameters.description: The distance that should be in focus, relative to the layer's origin. By default the layer is at the focus plane. When you have a source layer this parameter isn't used.

parameters.label: F-Stop
parameters.description: Metadata specifying the f-stop for the camera. When you have a source layer this parameter isn't used.

parameters.label: Guide Scale
parameters.description: The metadata that specifies the scale of the camera that's displayed when the layer is metadata.

entries.label: Cell Pattern
entries.summary: Generates cellular patterns.

parameters.label: Type Info
parameters.description: The type information for the resulting layer. See Type info for more information.

parameters.label: Amplitude
parameters.description: A factor controlling the noise's strength or intensity. Higher values increase the contrast between pattern elements; lower values reduce it.
parameters.heading: Range

parameters.label: Shift
parameters.description: The amount to increase or decrease the layer's pixel value. Higher values increase the pixel value and overall brightness. Lower values decrease the pixel value and overall brightness.
parameters.heading: Range

parameters.label: Element Size
parameters.description: The size (in image coordinates) of the basic element of the noise. You can turn on the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls option to adjust this further using the Element Scale parameter.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Element Scale
parameters.description: When you turn on the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls option, this parameter scales the element size per axis to create anisotropic noise.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Jitter
parameters.description: The amount of random noise to add to each point's position on a grid. The random noise is added before the Worley noise measures the distance to the points. You can turn on the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls option to adjust this further using the Jitter Scale parameter. NOTE: Values greater than 1 may produce artifacts because they jitter past the search radius.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Jitter Scale
parameters.description: When you turn on Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls option, this is the per-axis scaling of the jitter.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Density
parameters.description: Values above this threshold randomly cull the cells.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Density Seed
parameters.description: The seed used to randomly cull the cells.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Lattice Type
parameters.description: The grid to define Worley noise on and determine the cell shape. Grid: Define Worley noise on a rectangular grid to create square base shapes. This is the common option. Hexagonal: Define Worley noise on a so-called simplicial grid to create hexagonal base shapes. For higher computational efficiency, simplicial grids are made of triangles or tetrahedrons instead of regular cubes or squares.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Metric
parameters.description: The metric for computing the distance to a point. Euclidean: Use the length of the line segment between the two axial points to define their distance. This can result in circular shapes. See Euclidean distance for more information. Manhattan: Use the sum of the differences between the two axial points to define their distance. This can result in diamond shapes. See Taxicab geometry for more information. Chebyshev: Use the maximum difference between the two axial points to define their distance. This can result in square shapes. See Chebyshev distance for more information.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Smooth Edge
parameters.description: When Metric is set to Euclidean, you can control the roundness of the cells.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.description: Shifts the entire noise function in image coordinates.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Tile Size
parameters.description: The size of a single tile of noise. The noise periodically repeats in this size. The size is in image coordinates, so the default covers the entire standard image space ("canonical image"). If you have a non-square image, the values should match the aspect ratio. NOTE: If on, values for parameters like Element Size are rounded or clamped to make them valid. This is because these types of parameters must meet certain conditions for the noise to be tileable.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: Determines whether the shape parameters work as absolute values in image Space, or as relative values in the 0 to 1 range. Absolute: Shape the cells using absolute values in image space. Relative: Shape the cells using normalized values that are 0 at the cell border and 1 at the cell center. When Jitter is applied, a value of 1 corresponds to the most elongated cell that is possible.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Gap
parameters.description: The amount of space between each cell. Higher values increase the spacing between cells, and the cells will shrink until they're not visible.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Random Height
parameters.description: The scale factor for an additional random noise value that is added to each cell.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Height Seed
parameters.description: The random seed used to control the Random Height.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Bevel
parameters.description: The amount of bevel to add to the outer edges of each cell. Higher values taper the cells inwards to create a pointy top. Lower values decrease the slope to create a flat top with hard edges. TIP: When Metric is set to Euclidean, you can use this parameter together with Smooth Edge to create pebble-like shapes.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Bevel Ramp
parameters.description: A ramp to adjust the shape of the bevel. The left side of the ramp corresponds to each cell's border, and the right side corresponds to the inset length given by the Bevel parameter.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Orient
parameters.description: Tilt cell's noise value by a fixed amount of Steepness. TIP: The orientation of cells can be visualized by setting the resulting Type Info to Height.
parameters.heading: Orient

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.description: Rotates the tilt direction of all cells. Higher values rotate the cells in a counterclockwise direction.
parameters.heading: Orient

parameters.label: Steepness
parameters.description: The slope of each cell's noise value. Higher values create inclined cells. Lower values create flat cells.
parameters.heading: Orient

parameters.label: Random Rotation
parameters.description: The maximum amount to randomly vary the tilt direction of each cell.
parameters.heading: Orient

parameters.label: Tilt Seed
parameters.description: The seed used to randomize the tilt direction of each cell.
parameters.heading: Orient

parameters.label: Distort
parameters.description: Applies distortion to the footprint of the cells.
parameters.heading: Distort

parameters.label: Amplitude
parameters.description: The amplitude of noise to drive the distortion.
parameters.heading: Distort

parameters.label: Element Size
parameters.description: The size (in image coordinates) of the basic element noise that drives the distortion.
parameters.heading: Distort

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: The strength of distortion.
parameters.heading: Distort

parameters.label: Global Seed
parameters.description: The global seed used to randomize the cells.
parameters.heading: Advanced

parameters.label: NOTE
parameters.description: The node applies the post-processing operations in the order they're listed.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Fold
parameters.description: Sets the noise values to the absolute value. For example, a pixel value of -2 becomes 2. NOTE: This parameter doesn't impact the output when there's only positive values.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Complement
parameters.description: Sets the pixel value x to 1 - x. NOTE: This method works for values in the 0 to 1 range. For images outside of this range, using Complement results in negative or out of range values.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.description: The amount to pull the medium grey values (around 0.5) towards zero (if Bias is less than 1) or one (if Bias is greater than 1). A bias value of 0.5 doesn't affect the values. Image:/images/nodes/cop/postprocessing_bias.jpg
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Gain
parameters.description: The amount to pull the medium grey values (around 0.5) together, while values around 0 and 1 are pulled apart. A gain value of 0.5 doesn't affect the noise values. Image:/images/nodes/cop/postprocessing_gain.jpg
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Gamma
parameters.description: The overall gamma of the generated noise. Values greater than 1 increase the range of values in originally bright areas, which darkens the noise. Values less than 1 stretch out the range of values for originally dark areas, which increases the overall brightness of the noise.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Contrast
parameters.description: The amount to expand or shrink the overall range of tonal values. Each noise value is pushed towards (if Contrast is less than 1) or away from (if Contrast is greater than 1) medium grey values (around 0.5). NOTE: This is not the same as Noise Contrast, which appears in some noise nodes and applies contrast during the noise function.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Clamp Minimum
parameters.description: Clamps values below the specified threshold.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Clamp Maximum
parameters.description: Clamps values exceeding the specified threshold.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the input accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. A value of 1 means this node uses only the new value. The default value is 1. See Mask for more information.

parameters.label: Source for Red
parameters.description: The source channel to use for the output red channel. Use the dropdown menu to set whether the source is from the First Input or the Second Input. Red (x): The source red, or first, channel. This is the default value. Green (y): The source green, or second, channel. Blue (z): The source blue, or third, channel. Alpha (w): The source alpha, or fourth, channel. Zero: A constant value of zero. Applies an implicit source zero channel. One: A constant value of one. Applies an implicit source one channel. Value: A constant value determined by the Value for Red parameter.

parameters.label: Value for Red
parameters.description: The constant value to use as the source channel for the output red channel.

parameters.description: Whether to use the legacy Chromakey or the channel separation key.

parameters.label: Invert
parameters.description: Inverts the resulting matte. This is equivalent to appending an Invert COP to the Matte output of this node.

parameters.label: Hue/Saturation
parameters.description: The hue and saturation ranges. TIP: Click Smallicon:BUTTONS/layer_sample and then click on the layer to set the Hue/Saturation.
parameters.heading: Key

parameters.label: Luminance Range
parameters.description: The luminance range.
parameters.heading: Key

parameters.label: Screen Color
parameters.description: When using Channel Separation, the color to key out.
parameters.heading: Key

parameters.label: Threshold
parameters.description: When using Channel Separation, this thresholds the resulting matte. The threshold is equal to the midpoint. Any values above 0.5 become 1 and any values below 0.5 become 0 if Threshold When is Greater, Threshold is 0.5, Width is 0, and the output is (0,1).
parameters.heading: Key

parameters.label: Width
parameters.description: When using Channel Separation, this is the range on both sides of the threshold that determines the input minimum and maximum. A Threshold of 0.5 with a Width of 0.2 represents an input range of (0.4,0.6).
parameters.heading: Key

parameters.label: Hue
parameters.description: Extends the hue range on either side by the rolloff size. Values within the rolloff threshold are interpolated by the Interpolation value.
parameters.heading: Rolloff

parameters.label: Saturation
parameters.description: Extends the saturation range on either side by the rolloff size. Values within the rolloff threshold are interpolated by the Interpolation value.
parameters.heading: Rolloff

parameters.label: Luminance
parameters.description: Extends the luminance range on either side by the rolloff size. Values within the rolloff threshold are interpolated by the Interpolation value.
parameters.heading: Rolloff

parameters.label: Interpolation
parameters.description: The rolloff function to use.
parameters.heading: Rolloff

parameters.label: Preview
parameters.description: Colors the result of the keying operation with Preview Color. The pixels being colored aren't keyed out.
parameters.heading: Visualize

parameters.label: Preview Color
parameters.description: When Preview is turned on, this is the color to apply to the preview.
parameters.heading: Visualize

parameters.label: Premultiply
parameters.description: Multiplies the input image by the matte that this node generates. This discards the parts of the image being keyed out.
parameters.heading: Visualize

entries.label: Chromatic Aberration
entries.summary: Adds chromatic aberration to your image.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Filter
parameters.description: The method used to sample the image. The default value is Box. See Filters for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. A value of 1 means this node uses only the new value. The default value is 1. See Mask for more information.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: Controls how the chromatic aberration result is computed. RGB: Separates and recombines the red, green, and blue channels directly. Spectrum: Converts the image through a spectral approximation, samples multiple wavelengths between the blue, green, and red channel offsets, and converts the result back to RGB. This can create smoother, more physically plausible color fringing.

parameters.label: Pivot
parameters.description: The pivot point (in image space) to scale and rotate the channels around. The default value is (0,0), which corresponds to the center of the image. TIP: Click Icon:BUTTONS/layer_position_sample and then click a location in the image to set the Pivot.
parameters.heading: Distortion

parameters.label: Number of Colors
parameters.description: The number of spectral wavelength samples to use when Mode is Spectrum. Higher values produce a smoother spectral result, but are more expensive to compute.
parameters.heading: Distortion

parameters.label: Red
parameters.description: The amount (in image space) to scale the red channel. Higher values increase the offset between the channels, making the red channel expand outwards and become more apparent. The default value is -0.15.
parameters.heading: Distortion

parameters.label: Green
parameters.description: The amount (in image space) to scale the green channel. Higher values increase the offset between the channels, making the green channel expand outwards and become more apparent. The default value is 0.
parameters.heading: Distortion

parameters.label: Blue
parameters.description: The amount (in image space) to scale the blue channel. Higher values increase the offset between the channels, making the blue channel expand outwards and become more apparent. The default value is 0.15.
parameters.heading: Distortion

parameters.label: Global Distortion Scale
parameters.description: The amount (in image space) to scale all three channels. This applies a zoom-like effect to the image based on the Distortion Scale Mask parameter and the effect input. The default value is 0.15.
parameters.heading: Distortion

parameters.label: Distortion Scale Mask
parameters.description: Scales the distortion based on the pixel's coordinates. By default, the ramp is set up so that the corners of the image are distorted while the center stays the same. For more information about using ramps, see Ramp parameters.
parameters.heading: Distortion

parameters.label: Red
parameters.description: The amount (in degrees) to rotate the red channel by this angle. Higher values rotate the channel in a counterclockwise direction, which makes the offset between the channels more apparent. Lower values rotate the channel in a clockwise direction. The default value is 0.
parameters.heading: Rotation

parameters.label: Green
parameters.description: The amount (in degrees) to rotate the green channel by this angle. Higher values rotate the channel in a counterclockwise direction, which makes the offset between the channels more apparent. Lower values rotate the channel in a clockwise direction. The default value is 0.
parameters.heading: Rotation

parameters.label: Blue
parameters.description: The amount (in degrees) to rotate the blue channel by this angle. Higher values rotate the channel in a counterclockwise direction, which makes the offset between the channels more apparent. Lower values rotate the channel in a clockwise direction. The default value is 0.
parameters.heading: Rotation

parameters.label: Rotation Scale
parameters.description: The amount (in degrees) to rotate all three channels by this angle. This applies a curve-like effect to the image based on the Rotate Scale Mask parameter. The default value is 1.
parameters.heading: Rotation

parameters.label: Rotate Scale Mask
parameters.description: Scales the rotation based on the pixel's coordinates. By default, the ramp is set up so that the corners of the image are rotated while the center stays the same. For more information about using ramps, see Ramp parameters.
parameters.heading: Rotation

parameters.label: Red
parameters.description: The amount in image space to translate the red channel.
parameters.heading: Translation

parameters.label: Green
parameters.description: The amount in image space to translate the green channel.
parameters.heading: Translation

parameters.label: Blue
parameters.description: The amount in image space to translate the blue channel.
parameters.heading: Translation

parameters.label: Translation Scale
parameters.description: The amount to scale all three channel translations.
parameters.heading: Translation

parameters.label: Translation Scale Mask
parameters.description: Scales the translation based on the pixel's distance from the pivot.
parameters.heading: Translation

entries.label: Clamp
entries.summary: Clamps an input layer, VDB, or attribute.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. You can also set the RGBA channels to which you apply the effects of this node. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information. Toggle RGB: Turns the Red, Green, and Blue channels on and off. Red: Applies this node's effects to the Red channel. Green: Applies this node's effects to the Green channel. Blue: Applies this node's effects to the Blue channel. Alpha: Applies this node's effects to the Alpha channel.

parameters.label: Compute Range
parameters.description: Sets the Lower Limit and Upper Limit parameters to the minimum and maximum values of the source input.

parameters.label: Lower Limit
parameters.description: Clamps values below the specified threshold. TIP: Click Smallicon:BUTTONS/layer_sample and then click on the layer to set the Lower Limit.

parameters.label: Upper Limit
parameters.description: Clamps values exceeding the specified threshold. TIP: Click Smallicon:BUTTONS/layer_sample and then click on the layer to set the Upper Limit.

parameters.label: Clamped Values
parameters.description: The value that replaces the clamped values. Replace with Limit Value: Clamped values are replaced by the value they went over or under. When clamping between 0 and 1, -1 becomes 0 and 2 becomes 1. Replace with Black: Clamped values are replaced with 0. Soft Clip: Clamped values smoothly transition across a range.

parameters.label: Soft Clip Direction
parameters.description: The direction in which to smoothly transition the clamped values. Soft Clip Inside Range: Transition the clamped values above the Lower Limit and below the Upper Limit, which narrows the effects of clamping. Soft Clip Outside Range: Transition the clamped values below the Lower Limit and above the Upper Limit, which extends the effects of clamping.

parameters.label: Soft Clip Range
parameters.description: The range over which to transition from the limit values to the original values.

entries.label: Cloud Noise 3D
entries.summary: Generates a billowy cloud noise.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Type Info
parameters.description: The type information for the resulting layer. See Type info for more information.

parameters.label: Amplitude
parameters.description: The amount by which to multiply the noise, which the node applies before the Center adjustment. For example, a value of 0.5 makes a pixel value of 0.5 become 0.25. NOTE: Layers can store negative numbers and values above 1, so this may result in out-of-bounds values. Use the Post Processing options to clamp the output.
parameters.heading: Cloud Noise

parameters.label: Center
parameters.description: The center of the output noise range, which offsets the pixel values. For example, a value of 0.5 makes a pixel value of 0.5 become 1.
parameters.heading: Cloud Noise

parameters.label: Element Size
parameters.description: The size (in world coordinates) of the basic element of the noise. You can turn on the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button to adjust this further using the Element Scale parameter.
parameters.heading: Cloud Noise

parameters.label: Element Scale
parameters.description: When the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button is on, this is the per-axis scaling of the element size for anistropic noise.
parameters.heading: Cloud Noise

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.description: The amount to offset the entire noise function in world coordinates.
parameters.heading: Cloud Noise

parameters.label: Noise Type
parameters.description: The underlying noise function that's iteratively sampled to generate the fractal noise. Simplex: Create Perlin noise on a simplex grid. Curl: Create a divergence-free curl function on Perlin noise.
parameters.heading: Fractal

parameters.label: Max Octaves
parameters.description: The amount of times to scale add together the noise.
parameters.heading: Fractal

parameters.label: Lacunarity
parameters.description: The amount to scale the noise for each iteration.
parameters.heading: Fractal

parameters.label: Roughness
parameters.description: The amount to scale the amplitude of each successive noise.
parameters.heading: Fractal

parameters.label: Distortion
parameters.description: The amount to distort the noise in the direction of decreasing noise values (when greater than 1) or increasing noise values (when less than 1).
parameters.heading: Warping

parameters.label: Stretch
parameters.description: The amount to stretch the noise in each direction in world coordinates. NOTE: Use this parameter instead of Element Size to preserve some details unstretched, which makes the stretched noise pattern look more natural.
parameters.heading: Warping

parameters.label: Droop
parameters.description: The amount to warp the generated noise pattern so it bends or hangs towards the Droop Direction.
parameters.heading: Warping

parameters.label: Droop Direction
parameters.description: When Droop is on, this is the direction in world coordinates in which to warp the noise.
parameters.heading: Warping

parameters.label: Fold Each Octave
parameters.description: Remaps the values between -1 and 1 and flips values below 0 to the positive range. For example, a pixel value of -2 becomes 2. This makes all valleys become peaks. NOTE: The node remaps the values during the noise evaluation. This is different from applying an absolute function afterwards like some other noise nodes (Fractal Noise for example).
parameters.heading: Warping

parameters.label: NOTE
parameters.description: The node applies the post-processing operations in the order they're listed.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Fold
parameters.description: Sets the noise values to the absolute value. For example, a pixel value of -2 becomes 2. NOTE: This parameter doesn't impact the output when there's only positive values.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Complement
parameters.description: Sets the pixel value x to 1 - x. NOTE: This method works for values in the 0 to 1 range. For images outside of this range, using Complement results in negative or out of range values.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.description: The amount to pull the medium grey values (around 0.5) towards zero (if Bias is less than 1) or one (if Bias is greater than 1). A bias value of 0.5 doesn't affect the values. Image:/images/nodes/cop/postprocessing_bias.jpg
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Gain
parameters.description: The amount to pull the medium grey values (around 0.5) together, while values around 0 and 1 are pulled apart. A gain value of 0.5 doesn't affect the noise values. Image:/images/nodes/cop/postprocessing_gain.jpg
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Gamma
parameters.description: The overall gamma of the generated noise. Values greater than 1 increase the range of values in originally bright areas, which darkens the noise. Values less than 1 stretch out the range of values for originally dark areas, which increases the overall brightness of the noise.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Contrast
parameters.description: The amount to expand or shrink the overall range of tonal values. Each noise value is pushed towards (if Contrast is less than 1) or away from (if Contrast is greater than 1) medium grey values (around 0.5). NOTE: This is not the same as Noise Contrast, which appears in some noise nodes and applies contrast during the noise function.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Clamp Minimum
parameters.description: Clamps values below the specified threshold.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Clamp Maximum
parameters.description: Clamps values exceeding the specified threshold.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

entries.label: Compare and Blend
entries.summary: Compares two pixel values on a layer, VDB, or attribute and outputs either a true or false input for that pixel.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: True If
parameters.description: The condition for which a pixel will be selected from either true or false inputs. Equal to each other (==): If the two pixels have the same value. Not equal to each other (!=): If the two pixels have different values. A greater than B (>): If the first input is strictly greater than the second. A greater than or equal to B (>=): If the first input is greater than or equal to the second. B greater than A (<): If the first input is strictly less than the second. B greater than or equal to A (<=): If the first input is less than or equal to the second.

parameters.label: B Value
parameters.description: The value to compare with if the B input is not wired.

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.description: Adds bias towards true or false inputs.

parameters.label: Tolerance
parameters.description: Tolerance: Tolerance for the comparison. This tolerance will be applied two-sided for the equal comparisons, and one-sided for the strict inequality comparisions. Pixels within the tolerance will gain a soft mask value according to the fall off.

parameters.label: Falloff
parameters.description: Falloff: For values that do not pass the test, but are within the tolerance, this controls how they fall off. None: No fall off is performed, a hard cutoff is done. Linear: A linear fall off from 1 to 0. Elendt: An S-shaped smooth fall off that is smooth at the start and end.

entries.label: Configure Stamps
entries.summary: Creates stamp/sprite attributes on points with randomization controls and inputs.

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.description: The initial seed that determines how to generate each random value, such as random Scale, Angle or Color. Changing this value causes each parameter to generate a new random value, which results in a new pattern.

parameters.label: Jitter Layer Mask
parameters.description: Jitter Layer Mask: The amount of the jitter input's UV value to mix in with the Jitter value, which impacts the random position offset. Higher values mix in more of the input's value. Lower values mix in less of the input's value.
parameters.heading: Jitter

parameters.label: Jitter
parameters.description: Jitter: The amount of random position offset to add to each point's position on the grid.
parameters.heading: Jitter

parameters.label: Jitter Scale
parameters.description: When the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button is on, this is the per-axis scaling of the random position offset for the created stamps.
parameters.heading: Jitter

parameters.label: Scale Layer Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the scale input's mono value to mix in with the Scale value, which impacts the stamps' scale. Higher values mix in more of the input's value. Lower values mix in less of the input's value.
parameters.heading: Scale

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: The stamp scale in image space.
parameters.heading: Scale

parameters.label: Scale Mode
parameters.description: The method of post-processing to apply to the scale of stamps. Uniform: No post-processing. Percent Variance: Apply random variance to the scale. Min/Max: The minimum and maximum range of values that each stamp randomly picks from, and then multiplies against the original Scale.
parameters.heading: Scale

parameters.label: Scale Variance
parameters.description: The amount of random variance to apply to the scale. This is applied as a post-process.
parameters.heading: Scale

parameters.label: Min Value
parameters.description: The minimum value that the stamps can randomly select, and then multiply against the original Scale. This is applied as a post-process.
parameters.heading: Scale

parameters.label: Max Value
parameters.description: The maximum value that the stamps can randomly select, and then multiply against the original Scale. This is applied as a post-process.
parameters.heading: Scale

parameters.label: Stretch Layer Mask
parameters.description: Stretch Layer Mask: The amount of the stretch input's UV value to mix in with the Stretch X and Stretch Y values, which impacts the XY scale. Higher values mix in more of the input's value. Lower values mix in less of the input's value.
parameters.heading: Stretch

parameters.label: Stretch Mode
parameters.description: Stretch Mode: The method of post-processing to apply to the non-uniform scale (stretch) of stamps. Uniform: No post-processing. Variance: Apply random variance to the scale of the X and Y-axes. Min/Max: The minimum and maximum range of values that each stamp randomly picks from, and then multiplies against the original Stretch X and Stretch Y.
parameters.heading: Stretch

parameters.label: Stretch X
parameters.description: Stretch X: The scale of the stamps along the X-axis that multiplies to the uniform scale.
parameters.heading: Stretch

parameters.label: Stretch Y
parameters.description: Stretch Y: The scale of the stamps along the Y-axis that multiplies to the uniform scale.
parameters.heading: Stretch

parameters.label: Stretch Variance
parameters.description: The amount of random variance to apply to the scale of the X and Y-axes. This is applied as a post-process. If Stretch X is 1 and Percent Variance is 1, 0 for example, this represents a 100% range in sizes. This means the output stamps have a random scale from 0.5 * Stretch X to 2.0 * Stretch X.
parameters.heading: Stretch

parameters.label: Min Value
parameters.description: The minimum value that the stamps can randomly select, and then multiply against the original Stretch X and Stretch Y. This is applied as a post-process.
parameters.heading: Stretch

parameters.label: Max Value
parameters.description: The maximum value that the stamps can randomly select, and then multiply against the original Stretch X and Stretch Y. This is applied as a post-process.
parameters.heading: Stretch

parameters.label: Angle Layer Mask
parameters.description: Angle Layer Mask: The amount of the angle input's mono value to mix in with the Angle value, which impacts the degree of the stamps' angles. Higher values mix in more of the input's value. Lower values mix in less of the input's value.
parameters.heading: Angle

parameters.label: Direction Layer Mask
parameters.description: Direction Layer Mask: The amount of the direction input's UV value to mix in with the Angle value, which impacts the direction of the stamps' angles. Higher values mix in more of the input's value. Lower values mix in less of the input's value.
parameters.heading: Angle

parameters.label: Angle
parameters.description: Angle: The angle in degrees to rotate each stamp. Use the dropdown menu to set the method of post-processing that applies to the angle of the stamps. Uniform: No post-processing. Variance: Apply random variance to the angles. Min/Max: The minimum and maximum range of values in degrees that each stamp randomly picks from, and then multiplies against the original angle.
parameters.heading: Angle

parameters.label: Angle Variance
parameters.description: Angle Variance: The amount of random variance to apply to the angles. This is applied as a post-process. For example, a value of 30 makes each stamp have a random offset between -30 degrees and 30 degrees.
parameters.heading: Angle

parameters.label: Min Value
parameters.description: Min Value: The minimum degree that the stamps can randomly select, and then multiply against the original Angle. This is applied as a post-process.
parameters.heading: Angle

parameters.label: Max Value
parameters.description: Max Value: The maximum degree that the stamps can randomly select, and then multiply against the original Angle. This is applied as a post-process.
parameters.heading: Angle

parameters.label: Round To
parameters.description: Snaps all stamps to a specified angle. This is applied as a post-process.
parameters.heading: Angle

parameters.label: Use Sort Layer
parameters.description: Enables the usage of the sort input which adds very small position offsets in the Z axis to control Depth Sorting on Stamp Points.
parameters.heading: Color and Blending

parameters.label: Color Seed
parameters.description: Color Seed: The seed value for randomization that deals with stamp color and alpha.
parameters.heading: Color

parameters.label: Color Layer Mask
parameters.description: Color Layer Mask: The amount of the color input's RGB value to mix in with the Stamp Color value, which impacts the stamps' tint. Higher values mix in more of the input's value. Lower values mix in less of the input's value.
parameters.heading: Color

parameters.label: Stamp Color
parameters.description: A tint for the stamp. Use the dropdown menu to set how the color applies to the stamps. Uniform: Apply the same color to each stamp. Variance: Apply random variance to the hue, saturation, and value of the stamps. Random from Ramp: Pick randomly from a color ramp. See Ramp parameters for more information.
parameters.heading: Color

parameters.label: Hue
parameters.description: Hue: The amount of random variance to apply to the hue. This is applied as a post-process. If set to 30 for example, the stamps randomly pick a hue offset from the range of 0 to 30.
parameters.heading: Color

parameters.label: Saturation
parameters.description: Saturation: The amount of random variance to apply to the saturation. This is applied as a post-process. If set to 0.5 for example, the stamps randomly pick a saturation from the range of 0 to 0.5.
parameters.heading: Color

parameters.label: Value
parameters.description: Value: The amount of random variance to apply to the value. This is applied as a post-process. If set to 0.5 for example, the stamps randomly pick a value from the range of 0 to 0.5.
parameters.heading: Color

parameters.label: Alpha Layer Mask
parameters.description: Alpha Layer Mask: The amount of the alpha input's mono value to mix in with the Stamp Alpha value, which impacts the stamps' alpha. Higher values mix in more of the input's value. Lower values mix in less of the input's value.
parameters.heading: Alpha

parameters.label: Stamp Alpha
parameters.description: Stamp Alpha: The amount of black (0) and white (1) by which to multiply the stamp's alpha. Use the dropdown menu to set how the alpha applies to the stamps. Uniform: Apply the same amount of alpha to each stamp. Variance: Apply random variance to the alpha of the stamps. Random from Ramp: Pick randomly from a mono ramp. See Ramp parameters for more information.
parameters.heading: Alpha

parameters.label: Alpha Variance
parameters.description: Alpha Variance: The amount of random variance to apply to the alpha. This is applied as a post-process.
parameters.heading: Alpha

parameters.label: Stamp Count
parameters.description: In order for the node to properly do stamp selection via the select input, it needs to know how many stamps there are in total. Placing down the Stamp Sprites recipe will link this parameter automatically to the attached Stamp Points Stamps
parameters.heading: Stamp Selection

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: Mode: The stamps to place in the image. When no stamps input is wired in, this parameter applies to the default star pattern. Cycle: Loop through all stamps in a repetitive cycle. Random: Randomly choose stamps based on the Select Seed. Layer Select: Use the select input to choose stamps. The parameter uses the first stamp when a pixel value is 0.0 and the last stamp when a pixel value is 1.0.
parameters.heading: Stamp Selection

parameters.label: Select Seed
parameters.description: Select Seed: The seed value for random stamp selection.
parameters.heading: Stamp Selection

entries.label: Convolve Filter
entries.summary: Convolves an image with an arbitrary kernel image using an FFT.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that this node convolves. The input and kernel images are both interpreted with this type. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Normalize Kernel
parameters.description: Divides the kernel by the sum of all its values before convolving, so the values total 1. This keeps the operation from brightening or darkening the image. Turn this off when the kernel is already normalized or when you want the kernel's absolute magnitude to scale the result.

parameters.label: Centered Kernel
parameters.description: Treats the center of the kernel image as its origin, so the convolution does not shift the result. When off, the origin is taken at the corner of the kernel image, which translates the output by half the kernel's size (the raw behavior of a frequency-space convolution).

parameters.label: Padding
parameters.description: When on, extends the image with a border of extra pixels before the transform and crops it back afterward; the value sets the fraction of the image size to add on each side. Because the FFT convolution is cyclic, the kernel otherwise wraps from one edge of the image to the opposite edge, and padding pushes those wrap-around artifacts outside the cropped region. Larger values suppress more wrap-around at the cost of a larger transform.
parameters.heading: Padding

parameters.label: Border
parameters.description: How the padded region added around the image is filled. See Border types for more information. Unchanged: Use the filter's incoming border type. Constant: Fill the padded region with a constant value of 0. This is probably the option you want to use if the intent is to avoid tiling of the input kernel. Clamp: Repeat the edge pixels of the image outward. Mirror: Reflect the image across its edges into the padded region. Wrap: Tile the image into the padded region.
parameters.heading: Padding

entries.label: Corner Detect
entries.summary: Detects corners in an input layer.

parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: The type of algorythm to use when determining what a corner is.

parameters.label: Neighbors
parameters.description: The number of adjacent pixels to consider when computing corner detection.

parameters.label: Threshold
parameters.description: Only values above this threshold will be considered when determining corners.

parameters.label: K
parameters.description: When using the Harris Stephens (fast) 1988 method, large values will be less sensitive to corners. Valid values are between 0.04 and 0.06.

entries.label: Crop
entries.summary: Crops a layer to a new size.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: Cropping can be seen as cutting out part of an image, throwing out the extra, but leaving it in the same location of your work space. But it can also be seen as a pan & zoom to reframe the desired region to now fit the center of your workspace. Discard Cropped: The cropped region is discarded and the pixels remain unchanged in their location in image space. Discard and Reframe to Crop: The cropped region is discarded, but the pixels that remain are reframed to fill image spaces. Reframe to Crop: The data is unaffected by the crop. Instead, the image is reframed so the cropped range fits the display window. This will appear to have no effect in the 2D viewport.

parameters.label: Border
parameters.description: Override the border values used when un-cropping an image. Unchanged: Use the input border type. Constant: Treat the border as zero, with the boundary interpolating to black. Clamp: Clamp boundary values, streaking them outwards. Mirror: Reflect along the boundaries. Wrap: Wrap to the opposite boundary. Clip: Define an implicit cut off at the boundary without any bleeding of black values.

parameters.label: Units
parameters.description: Controls how to specify the crop. This controls the range of the values and if they are in respect to the input's display or data window. Image: The cropping region is specified in terms of the display window, with -1 to 1 being the range. A square size will result in a square crop. Texture: The cropping region is specified in terms of the data window, with 0 to 1 being the range. A square size is not necessarily a square crop because the source may not be square. Pixels: The cropping region is specified in pixels directly. NOTE: The cropping is always done in pixels, which may result in rounding if they do not correspond to buffer elements due to the use of pixel scale.

parameters.label: Geometry Units
parameters.description: If a geometry input is used to drive the crop, this controls what the units of the geometry are. Image: The geometry specifies image coordinates, ranging -1 to 1, that are relative to the display window. Texture: The geometry specifies texture coordinates, ranging 0 to 1, that are relative to the data window. Pixels: The geometry specifies pixel coordinates, ranging 0 to resolution. World: The geometry specifies world coordinates. The resulting crop region will respect the 3D transform that the input layer has.

parameters.label: Method
parameters.description: The method used to specify the crop region. Lower Left and Upper Right: Specify the lower-left and upper-right corners of the crop. Lower Left and Size: Specify the lower-left corner and size of the crop.

parameters.label: Lower Left
parameters.description: The lower-left of the crop in image, texture, or pixel space, which the Units parameter determines.

parameters.label: Upper Right
parameters.description: The upper-right of the crop in image, texture, or pixel space, which the Units parameter determines.

parameters.label: Size
parameters.description: The size of the crop in image, texture, or pixel space, which the Units parameter determines.

parameters.label: Aspect Ratio
parameters.description: Adjust the final crop values to have this aspect ratio.

parameters.label: Extract Tile

parameters.label: Tile Number

parameters.label: Minimum Resolution

parameters.label: Limit Resolution

parameters.label: Maximum Resolution
parameters.description: The cropped region will be clamped to at most this size. This is useful for dynamic cropping to avoid unexpected input from creating overly large textures.

parameters.label: Reset Pixel Origin

parameters.label: Left/Right

parameters.label: Top/Bottom

entries.label: Crystal Noise

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source outputs. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Type Info
parameters.description: The type information for the resulting layer. See Type info for more information.

parameters.label: Amplitude
parameters.description: The amount by which to multiply the noise, which the node applies before the Center adjustment. For example, a value of 0.5 makes a pixel value of 0.5 become 0.25. NOTE: Layers can store negative numbers and values above 1, so this may result in out-of-bounds values. You can use a Clamp COP to enforce the range afterwards.
parameters.heading: Range

parameters.label: Center
parameters.description: The center of the output noise range, which offsets the pixel values. For example, a value of 0.5 makes a pixel value of 0.5 become 1.
parameters.heading: Range

parameters.label: Noise Contrast
parameters.description: The amount of contrast to apply to the noise before the Amplitude and Center parameters. You can use this parameter to make the noise more extreme without exceeding the 0 to 1 range.
parameters.heading: Range

parameters.label: Primary Metric
parameters.description: The distance metric of the internal Worley noises. When Secondary is on, this controls only the first Worley noise. Euclidean: Use the length of the line segment between the two axial points to define the distance between the two points. This can result in jagged shapes. See Euclidean distance for more information. Manhattan: Use the sum of the differences between the two axial points to define the distance between the two points. This can result in jagged diamond shapes. See Taxicab geometry for more information. Chebyshev: Use the maximum difference between the two axial points to define the distance between the two points. This can result in jagged square shapes. See Chebyshev distance for more information.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Jitter
parameters.description: The amount of random noise to add to each point's position on a grid. The random noise is added before the Worley noise measures the distance to the points. NOTE: Values greater than 1 may produce artifacts because they jitter past the search radius.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Element Size
parameters.description: The size (in image coordinates) of the basic element of the noise. You can turn on the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button to adjust this further using the Element Scale parameter.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Element Scale
parameters.description: When the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button is on, this is the per-axis scaling of the element size for anistropic noise.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Secondary
parameters.description: Makes the primary parameters control the first Worley noise while these secondary parameters control the second Worley noise.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Secondary Metric
parameters.description: The distance metric of the secondary internal Worley noise. Euclidean: Use the length of the line segment between the two axial points to define the distance between the two points. This can result in jagged shapes. This can result in jagged diamond shapes. See Taxicab geometry for more information. Chebyshev: Use the maximum difference between the two axial points to define the distance between the two points. parameters.description: The amount to offset the entire noise function in image coordinates.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.description: The size of a single tile of noise. The noise periodically repeats in this size. The size is in image coordinates, so the default is for the entire default canoncial image. parameters.label: Fold

parameters.description: Sets the pixel value x to 1 - x. NOTE: This method works for values in the 0 to 1 range. For images outside of this range, using Complement results in negative or out of range values.
