entries.label: Curl
entries.summary: Computes the curl of a vector field.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Space
parameters.description: The space to compute the curl in. This affects the magnitude of the result. The result may also be affected by anisotropic scaling in the selected space. Image: Compute the curl in Image Space, by normalizing the change in values by the image-space pixel size. Pixel: Compute the curl in Pixel Space, by normalizing the change in values by the pixel size. Local: Compute the curl in Local Space, by normalizing the change in values by the world-space pixel size.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: Multiplies the computed curl by this amount.

parameters.label: Kernel Size
parameters.description: The distance (in buffer elements) to compute the derivatives used for the curl. A derivative is often computed with adjacent pixels or voxels, but if the values are slowly varying there may not be enough bit-depth to get smooth derivatives. Increasing this value may remove stepping artifacts from the result.

parameters.label: Read Pixels outside Image
parameters.description: Determines if derivatives at the boundary should read outside the image or restrict to the image range. Turning this parameter on is useful when building seamless textures with a wrap border type. Turn this off if you want to avoid artificial flattening of the derivative at the boundary in a clamp border type, as it acts like an extrapolation.

entries.label: Curvature
entries.summary: Computes the curvature of a layer.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Space
parameters.description: The space used to measure the layer's curvature.

parameters.label: Method
parameters.description: The method used to calculate the layer's curvature. Finite Difference: Compute the difference between the current pixel value and its neighboring values. This uses classic definitions of curvature based on derivative values. This method is more stable than Angle Deficit for smooth inputs, such as a parameterization of hemisphere. Angle Deficit: Treat each pixel as a vertex in a polygonal height field. This calculates the sum of the angles formed at each pixel by its neighboring vertices. The angle sum equals 2𝜋 in flat regions, but the sum is less in curved areas and results in an angle deficit that's used to estimate local curvature. This method performs more robustly when the input includes complex or non-uniform variations.

parameters.label: Curvature Type
parameters.description: The curvature type from the input layer to compute. Gaussian: This curvature is positive in both convex and concave regions. It becomes negative at saddle points, where the surface curves in opposite directions (concave in one direction and convex in the other). Gaussian curvature is useful for distinguishing simple convex and concave shapes from regions with saddle-like geometry. Mean: This curvature is positive in convex regions and negative in concave regions. Mean curvature is useful for distinguishing convex, concave, and flat regions. Principal (max): The maximal principal curvature represents the largest normal curvature at a point. Although it's not a direct measure of convexity, it often emphasizes geometrically prominent, outward-curving features. Principal (min): The minimal principal curvature represents the smallest normal curvature at a point. Although it's not a direct measure of concavity, it often emphasizes geometrically recessed, inward-curving features.

parameters.label: Output Type
parameters.description: The values from the layer's computed Curvature Type to output. Curvature: Outputs the entire computed curvature. Convexity: Outputs the convex regions based on the selected curvature. Concavity: Outputs the concave regions based on the selected curvature.

parameters.label: Normal Type
parameters.description: When a normal vector field is generated by the Height to Normal COP, its type must be set to match that node. See /copernicus/normals for more information. Signed: Output signed normals, compatible with geometry attributes. Offset: Output offset normals, compatible with normal maps.
parameters.heading: Pre-process

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: Adjusts the scale of the input's pixel values.
parameters.heading: Pre-process

parameters.label: Read Pixels outside Image
parameters.description: Adds contributions from pixels outside of the image to compute curvature at the image boundaries. This depends on the border type, which determines what pixels to read as outside of the image. If the boundary uses wrapping, the result is correct. If the boundary is constant, turn this parameter off to produce correct values near the edges.
parameters.heading: Pre-process

parameters.label: Kernel Size
parameters.description: The scale of the neighborhood that the node considers for curvature computation at each pixel. A larger neighborhood often yields smoother curvature results.
parameters.heading: Pre-process

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: Adjusts the scale of the output's pixel values.
parameters.heading: Post-process

parameters.label: Normalize
parameters.description: Normalizes the output result, which makes the output values stay in the 0 to 1 range. Since minor variations between neighboring pixels can result in unexpectedly high curvature values, this improves visualization by revealing the full curvature structure.
parameters.heading: Post-process

parameters.label: Minimum
parameters.description: The minimum value to clamp the curvature value to.
parameters.heading: Post-process

parameters.label: Maximum
parameters.description: The maximum value to clamp the curvature value to.
parameters.heading: Post-process

parameters.label: Synchronize Keys per Curve
parameters.description: Whether to keep keys synchronized across all points on each curve. This will create new keyframes on any channel belonging to points on that curve if another channel on that curve has an existing keyframe at that time.
parameters.heading: State Settings

parameters.label: Approximate Bezier Shape after Delete
parameters.description: When deleting points on bezier curves, whether to move the tangents of the resulting segment to best approximate the overall shape from before the deletion.
parameters.heading: State Settings

parameters.label: Match Polygon Shape when Converting
parameters.description: When converting from Polygon to Bezier or NURBs, whether to keep the over all polygon shape by inserting new control vertices, or to instead reinterpret the polygon as the Bezier or NURBs curve hull.
parameters.heading: State Settings

parameters.label: Resample Divs
parameters.description: The number of divisions per span when resampling from Bezier or NURBs to polygon.
parameters.heading: State Settings

parameters.label: Enable Soft Transform
parameters.description: Whether to use soft transform when transforming points in edit mode.
parameters.heading: State Settings

parameters.label: Soft Transform Radius
parameters.description: The soft transform radius applied when transforming points in edit mode.
parameters.heading: State Settings

parameters.label: Show Orient Guide
parameters.description: When to show the orientation and scale guide.
parameters.heading: State Settings

parameters.label: Orient Guide Components
parameters.description: Which components of the orientation and scale guide to show.
parameters.heading: State Settings

parameters.label: Orient Guide Scale
parameters.description: The scale applied to the orientation and scale guide geometry.
parameters.heading: State Settings

entries.label: Derivative
entries.summary: Computes the derivative of the source layer along its width (x-axis) and height (y-axis).

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Space
parameters.description: The space in which to compute the derivative. Image: Compute the derivative in image space, which normalizes the change in values by the image-space pixel size. Pixel: Compute the derivative in pixel space, which normalizes the change in values by the pixel size. Local: Compute the derivative in local space, which normalizes the change in values by the world-space pixel size.

parameters.label: Angle
parameters.description: Rotates the position at which the pixels are sampled by this angle. An angle of 90 degrees would mean that the x derivative would be equal to the y derivative of an angle 0.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: Multiplies the output value by this amount.

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.description: Adds this amount to the output value.

parameters.label: Read Pixels outside Image
parameters.description: Determines if derivatives at the boundary should read outside the image or restrict to the image range. Reading outside is useful for building seamless textures with wrap-mode. But restricting to the image range avoids artificial flattening of the derivative at the boundary in clamp modes, as it acts more like an extrapolation.

parameters.label: Kernel Size
parameters.description: Usually a derivative is computed with adjacent pixels, but if the values are slowly varying there may not be enough bit-depth to get smooth derivatives. This will expand the distance (in buffer elements) to compute the derivative, possibly removing stepping artifacts from the derivative.

parameters.label: Difference Mode
parameters.description: The finite difference used to compute the derivatives. See What are screen space derivatives for more information and an image example. Central: Compare values on both sides of the pixel. Forward: Compare the value of a pixel with a subsequent pixel (which is either above or to the right of the original pixel). Diagonal: Compare values on both sides of the pixel. This method has the smoothest results.

entries.label: Despill
entries.summary: Removes color spill from an input layer.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information.

parameters.label: Spill Color
parameters.description: The color to remove. Set this to the color of the blue or green screen. TIP: Click Smallicon:BUTTONS/layer_sample and then click on the layer to set the Spill Color.

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.description: The channel towards which to bias the result. When despilling green for example, bias the result towards blue (1) or red (0). NOTE: You won't see change in the output when the color is pure.

parameters.label: Luminance
parameters.description: The amount to brighten the despilled area. The luminance may decrease when you remove a layer's green component, so use this parameter to re-add luminance. This ensures that the output layer has the same brightness as the original input layer.

entries.label: Dilate Erode
entries.summary: Dilates or erodes a layer.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. A value of 1 means this node uses only the new value. The default value is 1. See Mask for more information.

parameters.label: Units
parameters.description: The unit of measurement used to determine the size of the dilation effect's radius. Image: Sets the dilation radius to use units of the image space. Pixels: Sets the dilation radius to use units of the number of pixels. Local: Sets the dilation radius to use units of the local space.

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: Dilates or erodes the layer by this amount. Positive numbers dilate, negative numbers erode. This radius is clamped by Maximum Radius.

parameters.label: Soft Edge
parameters.description: Adds a gradient to the erosion or dilation. This creates a softer edge around the dilated or eroded areas.

parameters.label: Fill Holes / Remove Specks
parameters.description: Dilates the layer inward. For example, if you have a circle with some holes inside, you can use this option to patch those and end up with a fully filled circle.

parameters.label: Maximum Pixel Radius
parameters.description: Clamps Radius to this value. Increasing the Radius past a certain point has a performance hit so this parameter attempts to mitigate that.

entries.label: Drop Shadow
entries.summary: Composites a copy of a layer under the original to create a shadow.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information.

parameters.label: Border
parameters.description: The sampling behavior outside of the incoming layer's boundaries. Automatically uses the layer's border property. See Border types for more information.

parameters.label: Units
parameters.description: The unit of measurement used to determine the size of the Offset, Distance, Expansion, and Blur parameters. Image: Sets the parameters to use units of the image space. Pixels: Sets the parameters to use units of the number of pixels.

parameters.label: Output Drop Shadow Only
parameters.description: Outputs only the drop shadow effect, which displays a preview of the effect. Turn this on if you want to make the shadow a separate AOV or configure the shadow further before you composite it on top of the source layer. TIP: Turn this parameter on and use the Blend COP to put the shadow back over the original layer.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: The direction in which to offset the shadow. Offset: A two-component vector that represents the X and Y directions to offset the shadow. Angle and Distance: An angle in degrees and distance.
parameters.heading: Drop Shadow

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.description: The amount (based on the Units parameter) to offset the shadow to give the effect of directional lighting. TIP: When Units is Image, click Icon:BUTTONS/layer_position_sample and then click a location in the image to set the Offset.
parameters.heading: Drop Shadow

parameters.label: Angle
parameters.description: The angle by which to offset the shadow.
parameters.heading: Drop Shadow

parameters.label: Distance
parameters.description: The distance (based on the Units parameter) along the angle by which to offset the shadow from the original input.
parameters.heading: Drop Shadow

parameters.label: Color
parameters.description: The color of the drop shadow. TIP: Click Smallicon:BUTTONS/layer_sample and then click on the layer to set the Color.
parameters.heading: Drop Shadow

parameters.label: Multiply with Original
parameters.description: Multiplies the drop shadow's Color with the original input's color before offsetting. When off, the drop shadow's Color replaces the original input's color.
parameters.heading: Drop Shadow

parameters.label: Expansion
parameters.description: The amount (based on the Units parameter) to expand the shadow. Higher values spread the shadow outwards while lower values contract the shadow inwards. Adding some expansion can ensure a strong shadow that blurring would otherwise wash out, especially for thin text.
parameters.heading: Shaping

parameters.label: Maximum Radius
parameters.description: Clamps Expansion to this value. When you increase Expansion past a certain value it slows performance, so this parameter attempts to mitigate this hit.
parameters.heading: Shaping

parameters.label: Streak
parameters.description: Streaks multiple copies in between the original input and the final offset copy. This smears the image along the distortion trajectory set by Streak Weight. When off, the node outputs only a single offset copy of the original input.
parameters.heading: Shaping

parameters.label: Streak Weight
parameters.description: When Streak is on, this ramp acts as a multiplier on the pixel values when streaking. The left side of the ramp corresponds to the start of the trajectory. For more information about using ramps, see Ramp parameters.
parameters.heading: Shaping

parameters.label: Blurring
parameters.description: Blurs the output shadow.
parameters.heading: Blurring

parameters.label: Filter
parameters.description: Filter: The filter to blur the image with. See Filters for more information. Box: Creates a box around the pixel of which to take an average of. Gaussian (default): Take a weighted average of the pixels according to a Gaussian distribution.
parameters.heading: Blurring

parameters.label: Blur
parameters.description: Size: The size of the blur effect's radius in image, pixels, or local units, which the Units parameter determines.
parameters.heading: Blurring

parameters.label: Scale Size
parameters.description: Scale Size: Scales the blur radius for a specific axis.
parameters.heading: Blurring

entries.label: Extrapolate Boundaries
entries.summary: Fills empty areas of an image using colors at the edges of non-empty areas.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Exterior
parameters.description: The method used to set the pixels beyond the edge padding. Unchanged: Leave the pixels unchanged. Black: Set the pixels to black (0). Diffuse Fill: Run a Smooth Fill COP over the region, which smoothly interpolates the pixel values.

parameters.label: Inner Side
parameters.description: The side of the fillarea input to consider the inside. Below Threshold: Values below this threshold are the inside of the source. This fills the white regions of the fillarea. Above Threshold: Values above this threshold are the inside of the soruce. This fills the black regions of the fillarea.

parameters.label: Threshold
parameters.description: The value to switch between the inside and outside in the fillarea input. TIP: Click Smallicon:BUTTONS/layer_sample and then click on the layer to set the Threshold.

parameters.label: Edge Padding
parameters.description: The distance (in image coordinates) to directly copy pixel values into the exterior.

parameters.label: Edge Offset
parameters.description: When reading the original value to copy outwards for edge padding, the value exactly at the edge padding may already have exterior color incorporated. This is the distance (in image coordinates) to backtrack to read clean values for extrapolation.

parameters.label: Sample Only Present
parameters.description: Considers original values only if they're in the source area, which means they pass the Threshold value. This parameter prevents black leaking in from uninitialized areas and is useful when the data in the fillarea is invalid. In most cases, this means you can set Edge Offset to 0 when this parameter is on. If the fillarea contains valid data, turn this parameter off to interpolate a proper smooth edge value.

parameters.label: Diffuse Iterations
parameters.description: Used in Diffuse Fill mode, this is number of iterations to relax the extrapolated values to smooth them.

entries.label: Fast Fourier Transform
entries.summary: Computes the Fourier transform of an image.

parameters.label: FFT Direction
parameters.description: Selects whether to perform the forward or the inverse transform. Forward FFT converts an image into frequency space, while Inverse FFT reconstructs an image from its frequencies. To perform the Forward FFT of an image, you can plug it into the real input.

parameters.label: Center DC
parameters.description: When enabled, the low-frequency components of the spectrum are shifted to be at the center of the image. If Center DC is disabled, center of the image contains the high frequencies, and the low frequencies are at the corners.

parameters.label: Normalize on Forward Pass
parameters.description: When this checkbox is turned on, normalization is applied during the forward transform. When disabled, normalization happens during the inverse pass. Turning this option on allows for easier visualization of the power in the spectrum. Value of this parameter must match on nodes that perform forward and inverse passes for faithful reconsturction.

parameters.label: Target Sum
parameters.description: When enabled, rescales the spectrum such that the sum of all pixel values after the inverse pass will work out to Target Sum.

entries.label: File
entries.summary: Loads an image or video from disk.

parameters.label: Source
parameters.description: The method used to load your image or video. File: Load a file from disk. Clone: Load a clone from the Clone Control Panel. Live Render: Load a live render from a Live Render LOP.

parameters.label: File Name
parameters.description: When Source is File, this is the path to the image, image sequence, or video file to load. You can load individual images by providing the path to the image on disk. For image sequences, you can use either $F as a placeholder for the frame number or <F> to use the Video Timing parameter. Use the <UDIM> token to load a specific UDIM. The context option UDIM is used unless you override it with the UDIM parameter. Use the <LAYER> token to load from multiple files at once. Instead of the AOV names referring to specific AOVs in one input file, the AOV name replaces the <LAYER> token in the filename and the loaded C AOV (or the first AOV if C isn't present).

parameters.label: Clone Name
parameters.description: When Source is Clone, this is the name of the clone to load in the Clone Control Panel.

parameters.label: Live Render LOP
parameters.description: When Source is Live Render, this is the path to the Live Render LOP you want to grab data from. The File COP is dirtied whenever the live render updates, so recook when you view something dependent on it. See Live rendering in Solaris for information about how to start and stop a live render session.

parameters.label: Reload Image
parameters.description: Reloads the image.

parameters.label: Video Timing
parameters.description: Defines how to generate the frame number for either image sequences that use the <F> notation or video files. Start Frame: Start playing back an image sequence or video at a specific frame. Frame Number: Display the image sequence or video at a specific frame.

parameters.label: Video Start Frame
parameters.description: When Video Timing is Start Frame, this is the frame when the image sequence or video starts playing back.

parameters.label: Video Frame
parameters.description: When Video Timing is Frame Number, this is the frame when the image sequence or video displays. You can use this parameter to write custom frame number expressions.

parameters.label: UDIM
parameters.description: Overrides the current UDIM with a specific one. This is the value that replaces any <UDIM> token in the filename. Otherwise, the current context UDIM value is used.

parameters.label: Border
parameters.description: The method used to handle the border of the raster when the Tile Visualization parameter is on in the enclosing COP Network node or COP Network SOP. See Border types for more information. Default: If the Default Border parameter is off in the enclosing COP Network node or SOP, this repeats the raster. If the Default Border parameter is on in the enclosing COP Network node or SOP, this uses the network-level default value. Constant: Pad the raster by a constant transparent value. Clamp: Extend the edges of the raster. Mirror: Alternatively mirror the raster. Wrap: Repeat the raster.

parameters.label: Missing Data
parameters.description: The method used to handle missing data, such as missing AOVs and missing frames in a sequence. Report Message: Raise an error for missing frames and a warning for missing AOVs. Use Color: Replace the missing data with a constant color. For missing frames, the size of the raster is the default context resolution. For missing AOVs, the size of the raster is the size of the image.

parameters.label: Missing Color
parameters.description: When Missing Data is Use Color, this is the constant color that replaces the missing data.

parameters.label: Incoming Colorspace
parameters.description: The method used to interpret AOV color data. OpenColorIO: Use OpenColorIO rules to determine how to interpret AOV color data. Raw: Interpret all AOVs as raw color data. This is equivalent to turning on the Raw parameter for each AOV.

parameters.label: Pre-Multiply if Necessary
parameters.description: Pre-multiplies color with alpha for formats that store data un-premultiplied (PNG, TGA). This doesn't effect other formats.

parameters.label: Load Camera
parameters.description: Loads the camera information from the file metadata and appropriately sets the transform and camera of the layers. This looks for the worldToCamera and worldToNDC metadata, and prefers the _d suffixed versions because those are usually double versions. NOTE: Houdini recovers other camera settings (such as focal length) from the projection matrix.

parameters.label: Display Window from Input
parameters.description: Makes the file use the input's display window. When unwired, this uses the default context option for Copernicus and causes all files to have equal-sized pixels. Turn this on when you want pixel-to-pixel correspondences. For example, this makes a 2k texture twice the size of a 1k texture. When off, files normally generate a new display window from the file's own data. This frames all files to the same size in image space regardless of the resolution of the file, which is useful for switching between 1k and 2k textures without changing locations.

parameters.label: Add AOVs from File
parameters.description: Imports each AOV from the specified file or video and sets their properties in the Number of AOVs parameters. If the file has a <LAYER> token, this finds all files that match that pattern and creates an AOV for each. ((Ctrl + LMB)) to reset the AOV list, otherwise this adds only newly detected AOVs.

parameters.label: Number of AOVs
parameters.description: The AOVs to load from the Source image or video.

parameters.label: File AOV
parameters.description: The name of the AOV to load from the specified file or video. For images, if C is specified and it doesn't exist in the file, the first AOV in the file is loaded instead. Video files only support C.

parameters.label: Channel Type
parameters.description: The channel type to use for this AOV. See Data types for more information. Mono: Load the AOV as a grayscale (single-component) floating-point raster. UV: Load the AOV as a UV (two-component) floating-point raster. RGB: Load the AOV as an RGB (three-component) floating-point raster. RGBA: Load the AOV as an RGBA (four-component) floating-point raster. ID: Load the AOV as a single-channel integer raster.

parameters.label: Precision
parameters.description: The precision to use for this AOV, which controls how many bits the channel uses. Default: Load the AOV with the default precision (32-bit). If the Default Precision parameter is on in the enclosing COP Network node or SOP, this uses the network-level default value. File: Load the AOV with the same precision that's used in the specified file. 8-bit: Load the AOV with 8-bit precision. 16-bit: Load the AOV with 16-bit precision. 32-bit: Load the AOV with 32-bit precision.

parameters.label: Raw
parameters.description: Converts pixel values into the working scene linear color space (from the file's color space based on the OCIO settings of the loaded file's type). When off, pixel values are loaded from the file without modifications.

entries.label: Filter Frequencies
entries.summary: Boosts or suppresses spatial frequencies in an image.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type this node filters. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: Multiplies the filtered result. Use values above 1 to boost the kept band or below 1 to attenuate it. The default of 1 passes the band through unchanged.

parameters.label: Frequency
parameters.description: The center of the kept band, as a normalized radial frequency from 0 to 1. A value of 0 is the lowest frequency (the broad, slowly varying content at the center of the transform) and 1 is the highest frequency the image can represent (the finest detail). The default of 0 keeps the lowest frequencies.
parameters.heading: Frequency

parameters.label: Width
parameters.description: The full width of the kept band around Frequency, so the band spans Frequency - Width/2 to Frequency + Width/2. Wider values keep more of the spectrum; a narrow width isolates a single, tightly defined frequency.
parameters.heading: Frequency

parameters.label: Smooth
parameters.description: Gives the band a soft falloff at its edges instead of a hard cutoff. A hard cutoff in frequency space can produce ringing artifacts in the result, so smoothing the band usually gives a cleaner image.
parameters.heading: Frequency

parameters.label: Angle
parameters.description: The center direction of the wedge, in degrees from 0 to 360. Frequencies oriented along this direction are kept.
parameters.heading: Anisotropy

parameters.label: Width
parameters.description: The angular extent of the wedge, in degrees. The default of 360 keeps all directions, leaving the filter isotropic. Smaller values narrow the wedge so only frequencies near Angle survive.
parameters.heading: Anisotropy

parameters.label: Smooth
parameters.description: Gives the wedge a soft falloff at its angular edges instead of a hard cutoff.
parameters.heading: Anisotropy

parameters.label: Reflect
parameters.description: Mirrors the wedge to the opposite direction, so a wedge at Angle also covers Angle + 180. Because the frequency spectrum of a real image is symmetric about its center, you usually want this on so the filter treats a direction and its opposite alike.
parameters.heading: Anisotropy

entries.label: Fractal Noise
entries.summary: Generates fractal noise.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Type Info
parameters.description: The type information for the resulting layer. See Type info for more information.

parameters.label: Amplitude
parameters.description: The amount by which to multiply the noise, which the node applies before the Center adjustment. For example, a value of 0.5 makes a pixel value of 0.5 become 0.25. NOTE: Layers can store negative numbers and values above 1, so this may result in out-of-bounds values. Use the Post Processing options to clamp the output.
parameters.heading: Range

parameters.label: Center
parameters.description: The center of the output noise range, which offsets the pixel values. For example, a value of 0.5 makes a pixel value of 0.5 become 1.
parameters.heading: Range

parameters.label: Noise Contrast
parameters.description: The amount of contrast to apply to the noise before the Amplitude and Center parameters. You can use this parameter to make the noise more extreme without exceeding the 0 to 1 range.
parameters.heading: Range

parameters.label: Noise Type
parameters.description: The underlying noise function that's iteratively sampled to generate the fractal noise. Torus: Create 4D simplex noise evaluated on a flat torus. This generates noise that's periodic by construction, which means it doesn't clamp or round settings to enforce periodic behavior (unlike other noise types). Perlin: Create Perlin noise on a regular grid. This type of noise generates more natural results. Worley Cellular F1: Create Worley noise using its primary distance value, which is the distance to the closest worley point. This generates a cell-like noise. Worley Cellular F2-F1: Create Worley noise using the difference between its second closest and closest points. This generates a cell border-like noise. White (Random): Create white noise where each noise element is given a constant but random value. Alligator: Create alligator noise to produce a bumpy output. This pattern resembles alligator skin. Sparse Convolution: Create a type of Value noise that smoothly blends values on a regular grid. This type of noise generates natural results that are smoother than Perlin noise.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Per Component
parameters.description: Computes a separate noise for each channel of the output. If off, the output is grayscale for mono and non-mono layers.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Metric
parameters.description: When Noise Type is Worley Cellular F1 or Worley Cellular F2-F1, this is how to define different metrics for computing the distance to a point. Euclidean: Use the length of the line segment between the two axial points to define the distance between the two points. This can result in circular shapes. See Euclidean distance for more information. Manhattan: Use the sum of the differences between the two axial points to define the distance between the two points. This can result in diamond shapes. See Taxicab geometry for more information. Chebyshev: Use the maximum difference between the two axial points to define the distance between the two points. This can result in square shapes. See Chebyshev distance for more information.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Jitter
parameters.description: When Noise Type is Worley Cellular F1 or Worley Cellular F2-F1, this is the amount of random noise to add to each point's position on a grid. The random noise is added before the Worley noise measures the distance to the points. NOTE: Values greater than 1 may produce artifacts because they jitter past the search radius.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Element Size
parameters.description: The size (in image coordinates) of the basic element of the noise. You can turn on the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button to adjust this further using the Element Scale parameter.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Element Scale
parameters.description: When the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button is on, this is the per-axis scaling of the element size for anistropic noise.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.description: The amount to offset the entire noise function in image coordinates.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Tile Size
parameters.description: The size of a single tile of noise. The noise periodically repeats in this size. The size is in image coordinates, so the default is for the entire default canoncial image. If you have a non-square image, this should match the aspect ratio. NOTE: If on, values for parameters like Element Size and Lacunarity are rounded or clamped to make them valid. This is because these types of parameters must meet certain conditions for the noise to be tileable.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: 3D Noise
parameters.description: Evaluates the noise in a 3D space. Use these parameters to control the third dimension, while the first two dimensions are the location in the image.
parameters.heading: 3D Noise

parameters.label: Animate
parameters.description: Implicitly adds time to the third coordinate.
parameters.heading: 3D Noise

parameters.label: Pulse Length
parameters.description: The interval length (in seconds) of the noise's pulse in the third dimension. Lower values increase the rate at which the noise switches its appearance, while higher values decrease this rate.
parameters.heading: 3D Noise

parameters.label: Time Offset
parameters.description: The amount of time (in seconds) that's added to the start frame.
parameters.heading: 3D Noise

parameters.label: Time Scale
parameters.description: The amount of time (in seconds) by which to multiply the start frame. Higher values increase the rate at which the noise switches its appearance, while lower values decrease this rate.
parameters.heading: 3D Noise

parameters.label: Loop Length (sec)
parameters.description: This is the time (in seconds) at which to repeat the noise. This clamps other options to enforce periodic behavior. Turn this on to generate animations that seamlessly loop. When off, the animation generally doesn't repeat after any amount of time.
parameters.heading: 3D Noise

parameters.label: Fractal Type
parameters.description: How to add successive layers of noise to create finer-scale details. None: Don't add any additional layers of noise. Sharp: Add sharp layers of noise. Dampened: Add dampened layers of noise. Terrain: Add smoother layers of noise, which resembles terrain. Hybrid Terrain: Add smooth layers of noise that are sharpened at the peaks, which resembles rocky terrain.
parameters.heading: Fractal

parameters.label: Max Octaves
parameters.description: The amount of times to scale add together the noise.
parameters.heading: Fractal

parameters.label: Lacunarity
parameters.description: The amount to scale the noise for each iteration, which is rounded to an integer value for periodic noise.
parameters.heading: Fractal

parameters.label: Octave Offset
parameters.description: The amount to offset the noise for each iteration.
parameters.heading: Fractal

parameters.label: Roughness
parameters.description: The amount to scale the amplitude of each successive noise.
parameters.heading: Fractal

parameters.label: NOTE
parameters.description: The node applies the post-processing operations in the order they're listed.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Fold
parameters.description: Sets the noise values to the absolute value. For example, a pixel value of -2 becomes 2. NOTE: This parameter doesn't impact the output when there's only positive values.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Complement
parameters.description: Sets the pixel value x to 1 - x. NOTE: This method works for values in the 0 to 1 range. For images outside of this range, using Complement results in negative or out of range values.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.description: The amount to pull the medium grey values (around 0.5) towards zero (if Bias is less than 1) or one (if Bias is greater than 1). A bias value of 0.5 doesn't affect the values. Image:/images/nodes/cop/postprocessing_bias.jpg
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Gain
parameters.description: The amount to pull the medium grey values (around 0.5) together, while values around 0 and 1 are pulled apart. A gain value of 0.5 doesn't affect the noise values. Image:/images/nodes/cop/postprocessing_gain.jpg
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Gamma
parameters.description: The overall gamma of the generated noise. Values greater than 1 increase the range of values in originally bright areas, which darkens the noise. Values less than 1 stretch out the range of values for originally dark areas, which increases the overall brightness of the noise.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Contrast
parameters.description: The amount to expand or shrink the overall range of tonal values. Each noise value is pushed towards (if Contrast is less than 1) or away from (if Contrast is greater than 1) medium grey values (around 0.5). NOTE: This is not the same as Noise Contrast, which appears in some noise nodes and applies contrast during the noise function.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Clamp Minimum
parameters.description: Clamps values below the specified threshold.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Clamp Maximum
parameters.description: Clamps values exceeding the specified threshold.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

entries.label: Fractal Noise 3D
entries.summary: Generates fractal noise from 3D locations.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Type Info
parameters.description: The type information for the resulting layer. See Type info for more information.

parameters.label: Amplitude
parameters.description: The amount by which to multiply the noise, which the node applies before the Center adjustment. For example, a value of 0.5 makes a pixel value of 0.5 become 0.25. NOTE: Layers can store negative numbers and values above 1, so this may result in out-of-bounds values. You can use a Clamp COP to enforce the range afterwards.
parameters.heading: Range

parameters.label: Center
parameters.description: The center of the output noise range, which offsets the pixel values. For example, a value of 0.5 makes a pixel value of 0.5 become 1.
parameters.heading: Range

parameters.label: Noise Contrast
parameters.description: The amount of contrast to apply to the noise before the Amplitude and Center parameters. You can use this parameter to make the noise more extreme without exceeding the 0 to 1 range.
parameters.heading: Range

parameters.label: Noise Type
parameters.description: The underlying noise function that's iteratively sampled to generate the fractal noise. Simplex: Create Perlin noise on a simplex grid. Perlin: Create Perlin noise on a regular grid. This type of noise generates more natural results. Worley Cellular F1: Create Worley noise using its distance to the closest Worley point. This generates a cell-like pattern. Worley Cellular F2-F1: Create Worley noise using the difference between its second closest and closest points. This generates a cell border-like noise. White (Random): Create white noise where each noise element is given a constant, but random value. Alligator: Create Alligator noise to produce a bumpy output. This pattern resembles alligator skin. Sparse Convolution: Create a type of value noise that smoothly blends values on a regular grid. This type of noise generates natural results that are smoother than Perlin noise.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Per Component
parameters.description: Computes a separate noise for each channel of the output. If off, the output is grayscale for mono and non-mono layers.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Metric
parameters.description: When Noise Type is Worley Cellular F1 or Worley Cellular F2-F1, you can define different metrics for computing the distance to a point. Euclidean: Use the length of the line segment between the two axial points to define the distance between the two points. This can result in circular shapes. See Euclidean distance for more information. Manhattan: Use the sum of the differences between the two axial points to define the distance between the two points. This can result in diamond shapes. See Taxicab geometry for more information. Chebyshev: Use the maximum difference between the two axial points to define the distance between the two points. This can result in square shapes. See Chebyshev distance for more information.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Worley Jitter
parameters.description: When Noise Type is Worley Cellular F1 or Worley Cellular F2-F1, this is the amount of random noise to add to each point's position on a grid. The random noise is added before the Worley noise measures the distance to the points. NOTE: Values greater than 1 may produce artifacts because they jitter past the search radius.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Element Size
parameters.description: The size (in world coordinates) of the basic element of the noise. You can turn on the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button to adjust this further using the Element Scale parameter.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Element Scale
parameters.description: When the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button is on, this is the per-axis scaling of the element size for anistropic noise.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.description: The amount to offset the entire noise function in world coordinates.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Fractal Type
parameters.description: How to accumulate successive layers of noise to create finer-scale details. None: Don't add any additional layers of noise. Sharp: Add sharp layers of noise. Dampened: Add dampened layers of noise. Terrain: Add smoother layers of noise resembling terrain. Hybrid Terrain: Add smooth layers of noise that are sharpened at the peaks resembling rocky terrain.
parameters.heading: Fractal

parameters.label: Max Octaves
parameters.description: The number of times the noise is scaled and layered on top of itself.
parameters.heading: Fractal

parameters.label: Lacunarity
parameters.description: The amount to scale the noise for each iteration.
parameters.heading: Fractal

parameters.label: Octave Offset
parameters.description: The amount to offset the noise for each iteration.
parameters.heading: Fractal

parameters.label: Roughness
parameters.description: The amount to scale the amplitude of each successive noise.
parameters.heading: Fractal

parameters.label: NOTE
parameters.description: The node applies the post-processing operations in the order they're listed.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Fold
parameters.description: Sets the noise values to the absolute value. For example, a pixel value of -2 becomes 2. NOTE: This parameter doesn't impact the output when there's only positive values.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Complement
parameters.description: Sets the pixel value x to 1 - x. NOTE: This method works for values in the 0 to 1 range. For images outside of this range, using Complement results in negative or out of range values.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.description: The amount to pull the medium grey values (around 0.5) towards zero (if Bias is less than 1) or one (if Bias is greater than 1). A bias value of 0.5 doesn't affect the values. Image:/images/nodes/cop/postprocessing_bias.jpg
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Gain
parameters.description: The amount to pull the medium grey values (around 0.5) together, while values around 0 and 1 are pulled apart. A gain value of 0.5 doesn't affect the noise values. Image:/images/nodes/cop/postprocessing_gain.jpg
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Gamma
parameters.description: The overall gamma of the generated noise. Values greater than 1 increase the range of values in originally bright areas, which darkens the noise. Values less than 1 stretch out the range of values for originally dark areas, which increases the overall brightness of the noise.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Contrast
parameters.description: The amount to expand or shrink the overall range of tonal values. Each noise value is pushed towards (if Contrast is less than 1) or away from (if Contrast is greater than 1) medium grey values (around 0.5). NOTE: This is not the same as Noise Contrast, which appears in some noise nodes and applies contrast during the noise function.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Clamp Minimum
parameters.description: Clamps values below the specified threshold.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Clamp Maximum
parameters.description: Clamps values exceeding the specified threshold.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

entries.label: Fractal Sample
entries.summary: Generates a fractal of the source input that you can randomize.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Type Info
parameters.description: The type information for the resulting layer. See Type info for more information.

parameters.label: Maintain Tileable
parameters.description: Clamps or rounds certain parameter values so they maintain tileability. For example, Lacunarity clamps to integers and Angle rounds to 90 degrees. NOTE: This parameter doesn't create tileability. The original source input must tile in order for this option to maintain tileability.

parameters.label: Max Octaves
parameters.description: The amount of times to scale add together the octaves.

parameters.label: Lacunarity
parameters.description: The amount to scale the octave for each iteration, which is rounded to an integer value if Maintain Tileable is enabled.

parameters.label: Roughness
parameters.description: The amount to scale the amplitude of each successive octave.

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.description: In order to keep results 0 centered, this parameter can be used to select your midpoint which will be subtracted from each sample inside the fractal loop.

parameters.label: Offset with Bias
parameters.description: After the main sample is done and adjusted internally by weight and gain, you can then offset the output value by the same bias value, which will offset your output range. This is especially useful in Maximum blend mode, where your base value is very high up.

parameters.label: Blend Mode
parameters.description: The method used to combine the octaves. Max Octaves determines the amount of octaves. Add: Adds each octave onto the next. Subtract: Subtracts each octave from the next. Maximum: Takes the maximum of the preceeding octave and the following octave. Over: Places the preceeding octave over the following octave. This mode is only valid when the input is RGBA.

parameters.label: Border
parameters.description: The sampling behavior outside of the incoming layer's boundaries. Automatically uses the layer's border property. See Border types for more information.

parameters.label: Filter
parameters.description: The filtering method used for sampling the source layer. Consider using one of the area filters (Box and later) if the distortion shrinks large regions and you notice noise. See Filters for more information.

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.description: The initial seed that determines how to generate each Jitter, Angle (when Random), and Random Flip X/Y. Changing this value causes each parameter to generate a new random value, which results in a new pattern.
parameters.heading: Randomization

parameters.label: Jitter
parameters.description: The amount in image space of random position offset to add to each octave.
parameters.heading: Randomization

parameters.label: Angle
parameters.description: The angle in degrees to rotate each octave. Use the dropdown menu to set how the angle applies to the octaves. Per Octave: Each octave gets an increment of the Angle. If Angle is set to 30 degrees for example, the third octave has 90 degrees applied. Random: Each octave has a random angle chosen from within the range of the Angle. If Angle is set to 30 degrees for example, each octave has a random rotation between -30 and 30 degrees.
parameters.heading: Randomization

parameters.label: Random Flip X
parameters.description: Randomly flips each octave on the X-axis.
parameters.heading: Randomization

parameters.label: Random Flip Y
parameters.description: Randomly flips each octave on the Y-axis.
parameters.heading: Randomization

entries.label: Geometry Attribute from Layer
entries.summary: Samples layers with a geometry's attribute to create attributes from those layers.

parameters.label: Class
parameters.description: The class of the Position Attribute and Attributes. Primitive: A unit of geometry. See /model/primitives for more information. Point: A point in space as defined by four numbers (X, Y, Z, W). See /model/points for more information. Vertex: A point where lines meet. See /model/points for more information.

parameters.label: Space
parameters.description: The space that the Position Attribute uses to sample the layers. Texture: Use texture space, which is 0 to 1 in the data window of the input. This provides normalized coordinates that're independent of the source's aspect ratio. For example, use this space when looking up into a latitude and longitude map. Image: Use image space, which is -1 to 1 in the display window of the input. This preserves square pixels for non-square aspect ratios. This space is invariant to cropping or overscanning. World: Use world space, which is a 3D location in the modelling space.

parameters.label: Position Attribute
parameters.description: The attribute that samples the layers relative to the geometry. Use a float3 attribute for world space. You can use a float2 attribute for texture and image space, though the node takes the xy component if you use a float3 attribute.

parameters.label: Attributes
parameters.description: The number of attributes to insert onto the geometry.

parameters.label: Attribute Name
parameters.description: The name to use for the attribute created from the sampled layer. Use the dropdown menu to choose which data type to sample, which determines the new attribute's type. Input: Automatically determines the type of attribute to create from the current attrib# input. ID: Takes an ID layer and creates an int attribute. Mono: Takes a mono layer and creates a float attribute. UV: Takes a UV layer and creates a float2 attribute. RGB: Takes an RGB layer and creates a float3 attribute. RGBA: Takes an RGBA layer and creates a float4 attribute.

parameters.label: Do Nothing if Unwired
parameters.description: The node doesn't sample this attribute and insert it onto the geometry when the input is a null or unwired.

entries.label: Geometry to Adjacency
entries.summary: Rasterizes geometry to generate an adjacency cable.

parameters.label: UV Attribute
parameters.description: The name of the vertex UV attribute to rasterize.

Values in the generated layer cover the range from C-A to C+A, where C is Center and A is Amplitude. NOTE: Layers can store negative numbers and values above 1, so this may result in out-of-bounds values. Use Post Processing options to clamp the output.
parameters.heading: Range

parameters.label: Center
parameters.description: The center of the output pixel values, applied as an offset. Values in the generated layer cover the range from C-A to C+A, where C is Center and A is Amplitude. NOTE: Layers can store negative numbers and values above 1, so this may result in out-of-bounds values. Use Post Processing options to clamp the output.
parameters.heading: Range

parameters.label: Mask Contrast
parameters.description: The amount of contrast to apply to the pixel values before the Amplitude and Center parameters. You can use this parameter to make the values more extreme without exceeding the 0 to 1 range.
parameters.heading: Range

parameters.label: Element Size
parameters.description: The size (in image coordinates) of the basic element of the generated pattern. You can turn on the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button to adjust this further using the Element Scale parameter.

parameters.description: When the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button is on, this is the per-axis scaling of the element size.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.description: The amount to offset the entire pattern in image coordinates.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Tile Size
parameters.description: The size of a single tile of the pattern. The pattern periodically repeats in this size. The size is in image coordinates, so the default is for the entire default canonical image. If you have a non-square image, this should match the aspect ratio.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Distortion Strength
parameters.description: The amount of vertical distortion to apply to each pixel along the X-axis. Higher values vertically reshape the straight input lines into irregular contours.
parameters.heading: Aurora

parameters.label: Distortion Size
parameters.description: The roughness of the distortion for pixels along the X-axis. Higher values result in smoother, more coherent edges with less waves. Lower values result in rougher edges with more waves.
parameters.heading: Aurora

parameters.label: Streak Weight
parameters.description: The weight of samples along the trajectory, which are averaged as each pixel is distorted. This ramp acts as a multiplier on the pixel values when streaking, which affects the vertical profiles. For example, moving Point 1 from its default left position (evaluating to 0) to the right increases the separation between the streaks. For more information about using ramps, see Ramp parameters.
parameters.heading: Aurora

parameters.label: Maximum Steps
parameters.description: The maximum number of steps that are allowed when applying distortion. Increase this value if you notice stepping artifacts in the result.
parameters.heading: Advanced

parameters.label: Strips Inflate
parameters.description: The width of the strips. Higher values expand the width of the strips to increase bulges, while lower values contract the width of the strips inwards.

parameters.label: Primary Edge Breakup
parameters.description: The amount of horizontal distortion and edge wear to apply to the strips. Higher values add and increase the severity of jagged edges along the strips.

parameters.label: Secondary Mask
parameters.description: The visibility of the secondary layer (horizontal lines) on top of the base bark layer. Higher values darken and expand the lines to add cuts and grooves on the bark. Lower values fade and compress the lines until they disappear.
parameters.heading: Bark Strips

parameters.label: Secondary Size
parameters.description: The size (in image coordinates) of the secondary layer on top of the base bark layer. Higher values zoom in on the lines so each line covers more of the pattern, which decreases the overall amount of cuts. Lower values zoom out on the lines so each line covers less of the pattern, which increases the overall amount of cuts.
parameters.heading: Bark Strips

parameters.label: Tertiary Mask
parameters.description: The visibility of the tertiary layer (elongated vertical cells) on top of the base bark layer. Higher values darken and expand the cells to add swirls on the bark. Lower values fade and compress the cells until they disappear.
parameters.heading: Bark Strips

parameters.label: Tertiary Size
parameters.description: The size (in image coordinates) of the tertiary layer on top of the base bark layer. Higher values zoom in on the cells so each cell covers more of the pattern, which decreases the overall amount of swirls. Lower values zoom out on the cells so each cell covers less of the pattern, which increases the overall amount of swirls.
parameters.heading: Bark Strips

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.description: Seed: The seed value that randomizes the values used in the generator. Changing this value results in a different output, but retains the same concept and look.
parameters.heading: Bark Strips
