entries.label: Height to Ambient Occlusion
entries.summary: Imagines a sphere for each pixel and determines how occluded that sphere is based on its surroundings.

parameters.label: Height Scale
parameters.description: The scale applied to input height values before computing ambient occlusion. Increasing the scale exaggerates the amount of occlusion, which enables small variations in height to appear more pronounced.
parameters.heading: Height

parameters.label: Space
parameters.description: The space used to interpret the height's steepness.
parameters.heading: Quality

parameters.label: View Radius
parameters.description: The distance (in the given Space) to send rays to determine if a pixel's occluded. Higher values increase the distance you send the rays and provide more accurate measurements, but may slow cooking. Lower values decrease the distance you send the rays.
parameters.heading: Quality

parameters.label: Step Scale
parameters.description: How many steps (in buffer space) to take along the rays to determine if a pixel's occluded. Higher values create less steps and therefore cook faster, but may miss thin features since the steps are more spread out. Lower values create more steps, which are closer together.
parameters.heading: Quality

parameters.label: Sample Count
parameters.description: The amount of rays to send to determine if a pixel's occluded. Higher values increase the amount of rays sent and provide more accurate measurements, but may slow cooking. Lower values decrease the amount of rays sent.
parameters.heading: Quality

parameters.label: Sample from Hemisphere
parameters.description: Divides the point's calculated angle by 90 degrees instead of 180 degrees.
parameters.heading: Quality

parameters.label: Remap Ramp
parameters.description: Remaps the output ambient occlusion values. For more information about using ramps, see Ramp parameters.
parameters.heading: Quality

entries.label: Height to Caustics
entries.summary: Creates caustic patterns on the ground from a refractive height layer.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The output layer type to generate. RGB enables the Dispersion parameters. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Space
parameters.description: Local: Use the height layer's local space for the light direction or position. World: Use world space for the light direction or position.

parameters.label: Enable Tile
parameters.description: Wrap ray hit positions back into the output image when they land outside the image bounds.

parameters.label: Directional
parameters.description: Use a directional light. When this is off, the node uses a point light.

parameters.label: Light Azimuth
parameters.description: The horizontal angle of the directional light.

parameters.label: Light Altitude
parameters.description: The vertical angle of the directional light above the horizon.

parameters.label: Light Position
parameters.description: The position of the point light in the selected space.

parameters.label: Exposure
parameters.description: Multiplies the final caustic intensity.

parameters.label: Index of Refraction
parameters.description: The index of refraction of the medium. The default value of 1.33 approximates water.
parameters.heading: Height

parameters.label: Height Offset
parameters.description: The value to add to the input height before tracing rays.
parameters.heading: Height

parameters.label: Height Scale
parameters.description: The value to multiply the input height by before tracing rays.
parameters.heading: Height

parameters.label: Compute Derivative outside Image
parameters.description: Allows the internal derivative calculation for the height surface to read outside the image bounds. This affects the surface normals used for refraction.
parameters.heading: Height

parameters.label: Kernel Size
parameters.description: The kernel size for the internal derivative calculation on the height surface.
parameters.heading: Height

parameters.label: Ground Center
parameters.description: The base height of the ground. When no ground input is wired, this is the height of the flat ground plane.
parameters.heading: Ground

parameters.label: Ground Offset
parameters.description: The value to multiply the wired ground height by before adding Ground Center.
parameters.heading: Ground

parameters.label: Ray Trace Iterations
parameters.description: The number of Newton iterations used to approximate where refracted rays intersect the ground height layer.
parameters.heading: Ground

parameters.label: Compute Derivative outside Image
parameters.description: Allows the internal derivative calculation for the ground layer to read outside the image bounds. This affects the ray-ground intersection solve.
parameters.heading: Ground

parameters.label: Kernel Size
parameters.description: The kernel size for the internal derivative calculation on the ground layer.
parameters.heading: Ground

parameters.label: Photon Jitter Radius
parameters.description: The radius used to jitter photon samples during accumulation. Larger values create softer caustics with fewer grid artifacts. This has no effect when Photon Iterations is 1.
parameters.heading: Quality

parameters.label: Photon Iterations
parameters.description: The number of photon accumulation passes to run for each pixel. Higher values reduce noise and improve denoising quality, but take longer to cook.
parameters.heading: Quality

parameters.label: Denoise Iterations
parameters.description: The number of denoising iterations to apply after photon accumulation.
parameters.heading: Quality

parameters.label: Denoise Mask
parameters.description: Controls where denoising is applied based on the caustic intensity mask. Higher ramp values apply stronger denoising in the corresponding intensity range.
parameters.heading: Quality

parameters.label: Method
parameters.description: Perturbation: Uses a fast approximation that perturbs the refractive result into color bands. This is faster than Spectrum, but is less physically accurate. Spectrum: Samples wavelengths using the selected material's dispersion model. This can create more vivid dispersion, but is slower.
parameters.heading: Dispersion

parameters.label: Material
parameters.description: The transparent material used for spectral dispersion. This is available when Method is Spectrum. Water: Uses water-like dispersion. Glass: Uses glass-like dispersion, which is stronger than water. Diamond: Uses diamond-like dispersion, which produces the strongest color separation.
parameters.heading: Dispersion

parameters.label: Background Color
parameters.description: The background color composited behind the RGB caustics.
parameters.heading: Dispersion

parameters.label: Strength
parameters.description: The amount of color dispersion. Higher values increase the separation between wavelengths.
parameters.heading: Dispersion

parameters.label: Number of Colors
parameters.description: When Method is Perturbation, this controls the number of color bands used for photon distribution. When Method is Spectrum, this controls the number of wavelength samples per photon iteration. Higher values create smoother spectral dispersion, but take longer to cook.
parameters.heading: Dispersion

entries.label: Height to Shadow
entries.summary: Creates shadows using a virtual light source.

parameters.label: Space
parameters.description: The space in which to interpret light position, direction, and normal parameters. Local: Uses the image's local space. World: Uses world space.

parameters.label: Height Map Scale
parameters.description: The scale to apply to height values before computing shadow occlusion.
parameters.heading: Height

parameters.label: View Radius
parameters.description: The distance (in the given Space) to send rays to determine if a pixel's occluded. Higher values increase the distance you send the rays and provide more accurate measurements, but may slow cooking. Lower values decrease the distance you send the rays.
parameters.heading: Quality

parameters.label: Step Scale
parameters.description: How many steps (in buffer space) to take along the rays to determine if a pixel's occluded. Higher values create less steps and therefore cook faster, but may miss thin features since the steps are more spread out. Lower values create more steps, which are closer together.
parameters.heading: Quality

parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: The light source profile to use. Disk: Sets the virtual light source as a disk, which distributes lights over the area of a disk. This corresponds to an area light as used in rendering engines. Sphere: Sets the virtual light source as a sphere, which distributes lights along the outside surface of a sphere. This corresponds to a sphere light as used in rendering engines. Directional: Sets the virtual light source as a directional light, which emits a point light source at infinity. This corresponds to a directional light as used in rendering engines.
parameters.heading: Light Source

parameters.label: Single Sided
parameters.description: When the light source is Disk, ignores light from the back side of the disk.
parameters.heading: Light Source

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: The radius in image space of the light source. This parameter is available for Disk and Sphere light sources.
parameters.heading: Light Source

parameters.label: Angular Size
parameters.description: The angular radius in degrees of the Directional light source.
parameters.heading: Light Source

parameters.label: Use
parameters.description: The coordinates to use to control the position of Disk and Sphere light sources. Spherical: Use spherical coordinates, which use distance and two angles to define a point. Cartesian: Use Cartesian coordinates, which are the X, Y, and Z locations along the axes.
parameters.heading: Disk and Sphere

parameters.label: Distance
parameters.description: When Use is Azimuth/Altitude/Distance, this is the distance in image space between the origin and the light source.
parameters.heading: Disk and Sphere

parameters.label: Altitude
parameters.description: When Use is Azimuth/Altitude/Distance, this is the angle in degrees of the light source relative to the XY-plane.
parameters.heading: Disk and Sphere

parameters.label: Azimuth
parameters.description: When Use is Azimuth/Altitude/Distance, this is the angle in degrees of the light source relative to the X-axis on the XY-plane.
parameters.heading: Disk and Sphere

parameters.label: Position
parameters.description: When Use is Position, this is the 3D position of the light source.
parameters.heading: Disk and Sphere

parameters.label: Light Normal
parameters.description: The normal direction of the Disk light source.
parameters.heading: Disk and Sphere

parameters.label: Use
parameters.description: The coordinates to use to control the direction of a Directional light source. Azimuth/Altitude: Uses two angles to define the light direction. Direction Vector: Uses a 3D direction vector.
parameters.heading: Directional

parameters.label: Azimuth
parameters.description: When the directional Use parameter is Azimuth/Altitude, this is the angle in degrees of the light direction relative to the X-axis on the XY-plane.
parameters.heading: Directional

parameters.label: Altitude
parameters.description: When the directional Use parameter is Azimuth/Altitude, this is the angle in degrees of the light direction relative to the XY-plane.
parameters.heading: Directional

parameters.label: Direction
parameters.description: When the directional Use parameter is Direction Vector, this is the 3D light direction.
parameters.heading: Directional

entries.label: ID to Mono
entries.summary: Converts an ID layer, VDB, or attribute into a float.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Conversion
parameters.description: The method used to convert the integer into a float value. Cast: Cast the integer into a float. Integers that are too big to be represented by a float are not represented correctly. Safe Pack: Reversibly pack an integer into a float. For many input integers, this produces the equivalent float value. See the pack_inttosafefloat VEX function for more information. Bitwise: Reinterpret the integer as a float. Although this is reversible, the resulting float value doesn't reflect the incoming integer.

entries.label: Invoke Block
entries.summary: Runs a block using inputs plugged into this node.

parameters.label: Block End Node
parameters.description: The path to the Block End COP node that's the final node of the block you want to invoke. This block's Block Begin and Block End nodes determine the Inputs and Outputs multiparameters.

parameters.label: Iterations
parameters.description: The number of times to run the block, with outputs feeding back as inputs into the subsequent iteration. NOTE: This node can repeatedly run the block only when its outputs can be converted into the respective inputs (matched by index). Otherwise, this node performs a single iteration and sends a warning.

parameters.label: Iterations Variable
parameters.description: The name of the context option that stores the current iteration, which starts at 0 and counts up to one less than the Iterations amount. Use Exp:contextoption expression function to access this value inside the target block to vary parameter values per iteration.

parameters.label: Total Iterations Variable
parameters.description: The name of the context option that stores the total number of iterations this block is set to run for, which is equal to the Iterations amount. Use the Exp:contextoption expression function to access this value inside the target block to vary logic based on the total number of iterations.

parameters.label: Set Inputs and Outputs from Selected Block
parameters.label_norm: set inputs and outputs from selected block
parameters.description: Sets up this node's input and output ports to match the selected block. This populates the Inputs and Outputs multiparameters using the block's signature.

parameters.label: Inputs
parameters.description: The number of this node's input ports, which are based on the Block Inputs of the Block Begin COP for the selected block.

parameters.label: Input Label
parameters.description: The name of the block input to bind the respective incoming layer to. This is matched against the Input Name values on the Block Begin COP for the selected block.

parameters.label: Input Type
parameters.description: The data type of the input and the corresponding port on this node.

parameters.label: Outputs
parameters.description: The number of this node's output ports, which are based on the Block Outputs of the selected Block End Node.

parameters.label: Output Label
parameters.description: The name of the block output that comes out of the respective port. This is matched against the Output Name values on the selected Block End Node.

parameters.label: Output Type
parameters.description: The data type of the output and the corresponding port on this node.

entries.label: Knit
entries.summary: Generates a grid of knitted fabric stitches.

parameters.label: Preset
parameters.description: Loads a predefined collection of settings for a particular style of knit. Choosing a preset overwrites the parameters below. Image:/images/nodes/cop/knit_presets.jpg

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.description: The initial seed for all of the node's randomization, including Jitter and the Variance and Min/Max modes of Scale, Stretch, and Angle. Changing it produces a new random arrangement.

parameters.label: Rows
parameters.description: The number of rows of stitches in the grid.
parameters.heading: Point Generation

parameters.label: Columns
parameters.description: The number of columns of stitches in the grid.
parameters.heading: Point Generation

parameters.label: Row Offset
parameters.description: Staggers each successive row sideways by this amount, in image space. Use a small offset to break up the regular grid.
parameters.heading: Point Generation

parameters.label: Column Offset
parameters.description: Staggers each successive column by this amount, in image space.
parameters.heading: Point Generation

parameters.label: Jitter Layer Mask
parameters.description: Scales how much the jitter input layer affects the result. Disabled when nothing is connected to the jitter input.
parameters.heading: Jitter

parameters.label: Jitter
parameters.description: The amount of random positional offset added to each stitch, in image space. Higher values scatter the stitches off their grid positions.
parameters.heading: Jitter

parameters.label: Jitter Type
parameters.description: Toggles per-component jitter controls. Per-Component Controls: Reveals Jitter Scale so you can scale the jitter independently along each axis instead of uniformly.
parameters.heading: Jitter

parameters.label: Jitter Scale
parameters.description: Per-axis multipliers for the Jitter amount, biasing the random offset more along X or Y. Visible when Jitter Type has per-component controls enabled.
parameters.heading: Jitter

parameters.label: Scale Layer Mask
parameters.description: Controls how much the scale input layer affects each stitch's size. Disabled when nothing is connected to the scale input.
parameters.heading: Scale

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: The base size of each stitch, in image space. Lower values leave gaps between stitches; higher values pack them closer together.
parameters.heading: Scale

parameters.label: Scale Mode
parameters.description: How each stitch's scale is chosen. Uniform: Every stitch uses the same Scale. Variance: Randomly varies each stitch's scale around Scale by up to Scale Variance. Min/Max: Randomly picks each stitch's scale between Min Value and Max Value.
parameters.heading: Scale

parameters.label: Scale Variance
parameters.description: The maximum random deviation from Scale when Scale Mode is Variance.
parameters.heading: Scale

parameters.label: Min Value
parameters.description: The smallest random scale when Scale Mode is Min/Max.
parameters.heading: Scale

parameters.label: Max Value
parameters.description: The largest random scale when Scale Mode is Min/Max.
parameters.heading: Scale

parameters.label: Stretch Layer Mask
parameters.description: Scales how much the stretch input layer affects the per-stitch stretch. Disabled when nothing is connected to the stretch input.
parameters.heading: Stretch

parameters.label: Stretch Mode
parameters.description: How each stitch's stretch is chosen. Uniform: Every stitch uses the same Stretch X and Stretch Y. Variance: Randomly varies each stitch's stretch around Stretch X/Stretch Y by up to Stretch Variance. Min/Max: Randomly picks each stitch's stretch between Min Value and Max Value.
parameters.heading: Stretch

parameters.label: Stretch X
parameters.description: The horizontal stretch factor for each stitch. Values above 1 widen stitches; below 1 narrow them.
parameters.heading: Stretch

parameters.label: Stretch Y
parameters.description: The vertical stretch factor for each stitch. Values above 1 lengthen stitches; below 1 shorten them.
parameters.heading: Stretch

parameters.label: Stretch Variance
parameters.description: The maximum random X and Y deviation from Stretch X/Stretch Y when Stretch Mode is Variance.
parameters.heading: Stretch

parameters.label: Min Value
parameters.description: The smallest random X and Y stretch when Stretch Mode is Min/Max.
parameters.heading: Stretch

parameters.label: Max Value
parameters.description: The largest random X and Y stretch when Stretch Mode is Min/Max.
parameters.heading: Stretch

parameters.label: Angle Layer Mask
parameters.description: Scales how much the angle input layer rotates each stitch. Disabled when nothing is connected to the angle input.
parameters.heading: Angle

parameters.label: Direction Layer Mask
parameters.description: Scales how much the direction input layer orients each stitch. Disabled when nothing is connected to the direction input.
parameters.heading: Angle

parameters.label: Angle
parameters.description: The base rotation applied to every stitch, in degrees.
parameters.heading: Angle

parameters.label: Angle Mode
parameters.description: How each stitch's rotation is chosen. Uniform: Every stitch uses the same Angle. Variance: Randomly varies each stitch's angle around Angle by up to Angle Variance. Min/Max: Randomly picks each stitch's angle between Min Value and Max Value.
parameters.heading: Angle

parameters.label: Angle Variance
parameters.description: The maximum random deviation, in degrees, from Angle when Angle Mode is Variance.
parameters.heading: Angle

parameters.label: Min Value
parameters.description: The smallest random angle, in degrees, when Angle Mode is Min/Max.
parameters.heading: Angle

parameters.label: Max Value
parameters.description: The largest random angle, in degrees, when Angle Mode is Min/Max.
parameters.heading: Angle

parameters.label: Round to Multiples
parameters.description: When the toggle is on, snaps each stitch's final angle to the nearest multiple of this value, in degrees. Applied as a post-process.
parameters.heading: Angle

parameters.label: Knit Shape Type
parameters.description: The style of stitch the node generates. Purl: A bumpy purl stitch, shaped by the bulge and wrinkle controls below. Knit: A V-shaped knit stitch built from interlocking fibers, shaped by the weave and fiber controls below.
parameters.heading: Knit Shape

parameters.label: Width
parameters.description: The width of each purl stitch. Larger values round out the shape, while smaller values make it more compact and pinched at the ends.
parameters.heading: Knit Shape

parameters.label: Bulge Scale
parameters.description: How far the purl stitch bulges outward in height.
parameters.heading: Knit Shape

parameters.label: Softness
parameters.description: Softens the edges of the stitch, blurring the transition between the stitch and the gaps around it.
parameters.heading: Knit Shape

parameters.label: Wrinkles
parameters.description: The strength of the fine wrinkles added across the stitch surface.
parameters.heading: Knit Shape

parameters.label: Wrinkle Size
parameters.description: The size of the wrinkle detail. Smaller values produce finer wrinkles.
parameters.heading: Knit Shape

parameters.label: Edge Bend
parameters.description: How much the stitch bends along its edges. Negative values bend it the opposite way.
parameters.heading: Knit Shape

parameters.label: Edge Bend Bias
parameters.description: Shifts the balance of the Edge Bend across the stitch, weighting the bend more toward one end than the other. At 0 the bend stays concentrated on one side; higher values push it toward the opposite side, distributing the curvature more evenly.
parameters.heading: Knit Shape

parameters.label: Bulge Ramp
parameters.description: Remaps the cross-sectional bulge profile of the stitch, controlling how its height falls off from the center toward the edges.
parameters.heading: Knit Shape

parameters.label: Height Ramp
parameters.description: Remaps the height profile of the stitch along its length.
parameters.heading: Knit Shape

parameters.label: Double Knit
parameters.description: Generates a second interlocking strand for each stitch, producing a denser double-knit weave.
parameters.heading: Knit Shape

parameters.label: Invert Knit
parameters.description: Flips the over/under direction of the knit stitch.
parameters.heading: Knit Shape

parameters.label: Weave Width
parameters.description: The width of each knit stitch.
parameters.heading: Knit Shape

parameters.label: Weave Height
parameters.description: The height of each knit stitch. This is the in-plane vertical extent of the stitch shape, not its out-of-plane depth.
parameters.heading: Knit Shape

parameters.label: Weave Radius
parameters.description: The thickness of the yarn that forms each knit stitch.
parameters.heading: Knit Shape

parameters.label: Fiber Strength
parameters.description: The strength of the fine fiber detail added along each strand.
parameters.heading: Knit Shape

parameters.label: Fiber Cycles
parameters.description: The number of fiber twist cycles along each strand.
parameters.heading: Knit Shape

parameters.label: Fiber Twist
parameters.description: The direction and amount of twist in the fiber detail. Negative values twist the opposite way.
parameters.heading: Knit Shape

entries.label: Laplacian
entries.summary: Computes the Laplacian of the source layer.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Space
parameters.description: The space to compute the Laplacian in. This affects the magnitude of the result. Image: Compute the Laplacian in Image Space, by normalizing the change in values by the image-space pixel size. Pixel: Compute the Laplacian in Pixel Space, by normalizing the change in values by the pixel size. Local: Compute the Laplacian in Local Space, by normalizing the change in values by the world-space pixel size.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: Multiplies the source values before computing the Laplacian.

parameters.label: Read Pixels outside Image
parameters.description: Determines if derivatives at the boundary should read outside the image or restrict to the image range. Turning this parameter on is useful when building seamless textures with a wrap border type. Turn this off if you want to avoid artificial flattening of the derivative at the boundary in a clamp border type, as it acts like an extrapolation.

parameters.label: Kernel Size
parameters.description: The distance (in buffer elements) to compute the derivatives used for the Laplacian. A derivative is often computed with adjacent pixels, but if the values are slowly varying there may not be enough bit-depth to get smooth derivatives. Increasing this value may remove stepping artifacts from the result.

entries.label: Lattice Deform
entries.summary: Applies grid-based deformation to a layer.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Filter
parameters.description: The method used to sample the image. See Filters for more information.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: The interpolation method to use between the grid and image. Linear: The deformation follows the grid exactly. Smooth: Use non-uniform rational b-spline (NURBS) interpolation to produce fluid deformation across the grid.
parameters.heading: Image Mesh

parameters.label: U
parameters.description: The point density in the U-direction when NURBS curves convert into polygons.
parameters.heading: Image Mesh

parameters.label: V
parameters.description: The point density in the V-direction when NURBS curves convert into polygons.
parameters.heading: Image Mesh

parameters.label: Cells per Column
parameters.description: The number of grid cells in each column. This value is always one less than the Columns value.
parameters.heading: Lattice

parameters.label: Columns
parameters.description: The number of columns in the grid, which are represented by vertical lines. This value is always one more than the Cells per Column value.
parameters.heading: Lattice

parameters.label: Row 0
parameters.description: The number of grid points in the row. The leftmost points correspond to Point #_0. Use the tab menu to configure the grid points for a row. For example, click the 0 tab to configure the row along the bottom of the image.
parameters.heading: Lattice

parameters.label: Point 0_0
parameters.description: The position in image space of the grid point. This represents a handle in the viewport.
parameters.heading: Lattice

entries.label: Layer
entries.summary: Generates a layer.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type to generate. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Value
parameters.description: The value to initialize mono layers.

parameters.label: Value
parameters.description: The value to initialize UV layers.

parameters.label: Color
parameters.description: The value to initialize RGB layers.

parameters.label: Color
parameters.description: The value to initialize RGBA layers.

parameters.label: Value
parameters.description: The value to initialize ID layers.

parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.description: The number of pixels to make the layer. The actual number of buffer elements may be higher or lower depending on the Pixel scale.

parameters.label: Pixel Aspect Ratio
parameters.description: Overrides the pixel aspect ratio, which is usually a square shape in display windows. This can create anisotropic pixels. See Spaces for more information.

parameters.label: Pixel Padding
parameters.description: The provided resolution fits the display window. This further expands or erodes the data window to allow overscanning or cropping effects.
parameters.heading: Pixel Padding

parameters.label: Left/Right
parameters.description: The amount to adjust the left and right of the data window.
parameters.heading: Pixel Padding

parameters.label: Top/Bottom
parameters.description: The amount to adjust the top and bottom of the data window.
parameters.heading: Pixel Padding

parameters.label: Precision
parameters.description: The precision of the layer. NOTE: 16-bit floats lack enough precision for nice derivatives, so you may want to use 32-bit for height workflows. 8-bit: The layer uses 8-bit precision. This is supported only for ID layers. 16-bit: The layer uses 16-bit precision, which uses twice the amount of memory as 8-bit. 32-bit: The layer uses 32-bit precision, which uses twice the amount of memory as 16-bit.
parameters.heading: Pixel Padding

parameters.label: Use Fixed Point Storage
parameters.description: Stores 8-bit unsigned and 16-bit signed floating point values as fixed point values. This clamps 8-bit fixed point values to the 0 to 1 range and 16-bit fixed point values to the -1 to 1 range. This parameter applies to only non-ID layers. Storage types are propagated through the network, so nodes often use the same storage type as their inputs. Fixed point storage offers more consistent precision for the same amount of storage compared to floating point, but can only represent values in a limited range. TIP: Hold ((MMB)) on the node to use the node info window to check the storage type of each layer.
parameters.heading: Pixel Padding

parameters.label: Border
parameters.description: The behavior of the layer when operations read outside of its data window. See Border types for more information. Constant: Treat the border as zero, with the boundary interpolating to black. Clamp: Clamp boundary values, which streaks them outwards. Mirror: Reflect along the boundaries. Wrap: Wrap to the opposite boundary.
parameters.heading: Pixel Padding

parameters.label: Type Info
parameters.description: The layer's type information. This controls the visualization of the layer in the 3D viewport. See Type info for more information.
parameters.heading: Pixel Padding

parameters.label: Pixel Scale
parameters.description: The number of pixels that fit across one buffer element. This allows for fast proxy cooking without changing measurements specified in pixels. For example, a value of 2 means a 640x480 image has only 320x240 buffer elements to store the data.
parameters.heading: Pixel Padding

parameters.label: Identity Transform
parameters.description: Resets the layer to the canonical space. This moves the layer to the origin, aligns it with the XY plane, and resets its camera properties to the canonical orthographic projection.
parameters.heading: Pixel Padding

entries.label: Layer Property Create
entries.summary: Adds or edits user-defined properties on a layer.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Number of Properties
parameters.description: The number of properties.

parameters.label: Name #
parameters.description: The name of the property. If blank no property is created.

parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: The type of property to create.

parameters.label: Value #
parameters.description: The property's string, float, or integer value (which the Type parameter determines).

entries.label: Layer Property Delete
entries.summary: Removes user-defined properties from a layer.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Delete Property
parameters.description: The property pattern to delete. The node deletes any layer property that matches this pattern.

parameters.label: Keep Property
parameters.description: The property pattern to keep. The node deletes any layer property that doesn't match this pattern.

entries.label: Layer from Attribute
entries.summary: Fills a layer from a detached attribute.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The attribute type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Data Ordering
parameters.description: The canonical ordering in Copernicus is for the first pixel to be the bottom left, then to read left to right and bottom to top. Instead, the top left can be the first pixel and read left to right and top to bottom.

parameters.label: Resize Layer
parameters.description: Usually the size_ref will control the size of the resulting layer. Instead, it can be automatically sized by using the length of the attribute. This is useful for visualization or for extracting ramps.

parameters.label: Resize Shape
parameters.description: How to resize the layer to fit the attribute. Power of 2 Square: The smallest square which fits the attribute and is a power of two on each side is used. Square: The smallest square that fits the attribute is used. Single Row: A single row with columns set to the attribute size. Single Column: A single column with rows set to the attribute size.

entries.label: Layer Property Copy
entries.summary: Transfers layer properties from one layer, VDB, or attribute to another.

parameters.label: Transfer Properties
parameters.description: The list of properties to transfer from the source to the destination.

parameters.label: Transfer Border
parameters.description: Transfers the border from the source to the destination. See Border types for more information.

parameters.label: Transfer Type Info
parameters.description: Transfers the type info from the source to the destination. See Type info for more information.

parameters.label: Transfer Precision
parameters.description: Transfers the precision from the source to the destination. This controls how many bytes of storage each channel of the layer requires. More bytes allow for larger integer values or more accuracy for floating point values, but require more memory.

entries.label: Light
entries.summary: Lights a layer given a light direction and normals.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. You can also set the RGBA channels to which you apply the effects of this node. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information. Toggle RGB: Turns the Red, Green, and Blue channels on and off. Red: Applies this node's effects to the Red channel. Green: Applies this node's effects to the Green channel. Blue: Applies this node's effects to the Blue channel. Alpha: Applies this node's effects to the Alpha channel.

parameters.label: Normal Type
parameters.description: The type of the input normal. Signed (-1 to 1): The input normal layer ranges from -1 to 1 and likely comes from geometry. Offset (0 to 1): The input nomral layer ranges from 0 to 1 and likely comes from a normal map.

parameters.label: Directional
parameters.description: Directional lights are considered at infinity. All the light rays will be parallel. When points are used as a source, the direction from the points to the origin is the direction of the light. Non-directional lights are point lights emanating from the 3d location.
parameters.heading: Light

parameters.label: Light Direction
parameters.description: When no point geometry is provided, this is the direction pointing to the source light. The magnitude doesn't matter. The default value is 0, 0, 1.
parameters.heading: Light

parameters.label: Light Position
parameters.description: When no point geometry is provided, this is the center of the light when not directional.
parameters.heading: Light

parameters.label: Light Radius
parameters.description: Point lights have a singularity at their location, so if a point light is inside a volume it will become infinitely bright at that location. This regularizes the falloff by treating the light to be approximately a sphere of this radius. This will be multiplied by the pscale attribute on points.
parameters.heading: Light

parameters.label: Light Color
parameters.description: The color of the light. The default value is 1, 1, 1.
parameters.heading: Light

parameters.label: Intensity
parameters.description: The linear brightness of the light.
parameters.heading: Light

parameters.label: Exposure
parameters.description: An exponential brightness of the light. Each 1 value higher is 2 times the brightness.
parameters.heading: Light

parameters.label: Environment Map Offset
parameters.description: Angle to rotate the environment map around the Y-axis.
parameters.heading: Light

parameters.label: Diffuse
parameters.description: A tint for the diffuse colour of the material. The incoming source layer will be multiplied by this to determine the diffuse contribution. Setting to zero can allow the extraction of the pure reflective or specular components.
parameters.heading: Material

parameters.label: Specular
parameters.description: A specular color for the material. This will be multiplied by the light color to form the specular color in light models that have specular, such as Phong.
parameters.heading: Material

parameters.label: Metallic
parameters.description: The amount of metallicity of the material. Increasing metallicity will lower the diffuse value and replace it with a reflected color.
parameters.heading: Material

parameters.label: Model
parameters.description: The lighting model to shade with. Lambertian: An ideal matte surface. Wrapped Diffuse: An extension of the Lambertian model, but allowing the specification of the terminator position. This allows the light to "wrap" around the surface and light the back half - this is useful for non-physical effects, especially for toon-shading pipelines where the light is further processed. Phong: The Phong Reflection model, developed by Bui Tuong Phong, is a simple breakdown of light into a specular and diffuse component. The exponent controls how sharp the specular effect is.
parameters.heading: Material

parameters.label: Terminator
parameters.description: Where the terminator of the Wrapped Diffuse should lie. -1 will make it entirely black, 0 will be at the half way part and so match Lambertian shading, and 1 will wrap all the way to the far side of the object.
parameters.heading: Material

parameters.label: Exponent
parameters.description: The tightness of the specular lobe in the Phong model.
parameters.heading: Material

entries.label: Logic
entries.summary: Applies logic operations to ID layers.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: For ID layers, if the final mask is greater than 0.5, the new value is used. Otherwise the original value is used. The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information.

parameters.label: Function Class
parameters.description: Selects the high-level category of logic functions to perform. Logic: Expose boolean logic operators. Comparison: Expose comparison operators. Bit Shift: Expose bit shifting operators. Bit Twiddle: Expose bit-twiddling operators that enable low-level control of individual bits.

parameters.label: Logic
parameters.description: Boolean logical functions. In logical mode, 0 is false and any other value is true. In bitwise mode, the individual bits are processed independently. A: Output the A input. B: Output the B input. And: True if A and B are both true. Or: True either A or B are true. Exclusive Or: True only if A or B are true, but not both.

parameters.label: True If
parameters.description: Equal to each other (==): True if the A and B are equal. Not equal to each other (!=): True if the A and B are unequal. A greater than B (>): True if A is greater than B. A greater than or equal to B (>=): True if A is greater than or equal to B. B greater than A (<): True if B is greater than A. B greater than or equal to A (<=): True if B is greater than or equal to A.

parameters.label: Bit Shift
parameters.description: This shifts the bits of the A input. Shift Right Arithmetic: Shift the bits right by the B value. The sign of the number will be preserved. Shift Right Logical: Shift the bits right by the B value. Zeros will be shifted in from the left, so the number will be treated as unsigned. Shift Left: Shift the bits left by the B value. Rotate Right: Rotate the bits right by the B value. Bits that fall off the right side will be moved to the left. Rotate Left: Rotate the bits left by the B value. Bits that fall off the left side will be moved to the right.

parameters.label: Bit Twiddle
parameters.description: Specific operations to manipulate individual bits. Is Bit Set: True if the Bth bit in A is set. Set Bit: Outputs A with the Bth bit set. Clear Bit: Outputs A with the Bth bit cleared. Toggle Bit: Outputs A with the Bth bit toggled. Count Set Bits: Output the number of set bits in A. Leading Zeros: Output the number of leading zeros in A. (A * B) >> 32: Multiply A and B together and shift right by 32. This returns the high component of the multiplication that normally is lost due to overflow.

parameters.label: Operate Bitwise
parameters.description: Boolean operations will operate per-bit rather than logically.

parameters.label: All Bits Set for True
parameters.description: A true result normally is 1, and a false 0. This instead will have the true value have all the 1s set, which usually is -1. This is useful for masking operations.

parameters.label: Not A
parameters.description: Complement the value of A before doing the operation.

parameters.label: Not B
parameters.description: Complement the value of B before doing the operation.

parameters.label: Not Result
parameters.description: Complement the result of the operation.

parameters.label: Default B Value
parameters.description: If B is unwired, this is the value used for B.

entries.label: Mask Combine
entries.summary: Combines several mask layers from an input cable into a single mask.

parameters.label: Starting Value
parameters.description: The starting mask value that the first layer blends onto. The layers in Mask Layers are combined onto this value in order.

parameters.label: Mask Layers
parameters.description: Each entry in this list combines one wire from the input cable onto the running mask. The layers are processed from top to bottom.

parameters.label: Wire Name
parameters.description: Turns the layer on or off. When off, the layer is skipped and doesn't contribute to the combined mask.

parameters.label: Wire Name
parameters.description: The name of the wire in the input cable to combine. A valid layer must be either Mono, UV, RGB, or RGBA type.

parameters.label: Blend Mode
parameters.description: How this layer is combined with the running result. See the Blend COP for full descriptions of each mode (the running mask and the current layer are the background and foreground blend inputs, respectively). Blend: Replaces the running result with this layer. Add: Adds this layer to the running result. Subtract: Subtracts this layer from the running result. Multiply: Multiplies the running result by this layer. Divide: Divides the running result by this layer. Screen: Acts as a saturating add, much like adding photographs. Hypot: Takes the length of the vector formed by this layer and the running result. Difference: Takes the absolute difference between this layer and the running result. Exclusion: A lower contrast version of Difference. Sharpen: Increases the contrast of the running result using this layer as the mid-point contrast value. Maximum: Takes the maximum of this layer and the running result. Minimum: Takes the minimum of this layer and the running result. Overlay: Switches between Multiply and Screen based on the value of the running result. Areas below 0.5 multiply and areas above 0.5 screen. SoftLight: Applies a smooth contrast to the running result according to the value of this layer. HardLight: Switches between Multiply and Screen based on the value of this layer. Areas below 0.5 multiply and areas above 0.5 screen. Dodge: Lightens the running result according to this layer's value. Burn: Darkens the running result according to this layer's value.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of this layer to mix into the running result. Higher values mix in more of the layer. A value of 1 applies the blend fully.

parameters.label: Conversion
parameters.description: How a multi-channel wire (such as UV, RGB, or RGBA) is reduced to a mono value before blending. Channel Extract: Uses a single channel of the wire as the mask. Channel Mix: Combines the channels using a weighted sum. Light Direction: Treats the wire as a normal map and computes the mask from how much each normal faces a given light direction.

parameters.label: Channel to Extract
parameters.description: The channel to use as the mask when Conversion is Channel Extract.

parameters.label: X Weight
parameters.description: The weight of the Red (x) channel when Conversion is Channel Mix.

parameters.label: Y Weight
parameters.description: The weight of the Green (y) channel when Conversion is Channel Mix.

parameters.label: Z Weight
parameters.description: The weight of the Blue (z) channel when Conversion is Channel Mix.

parameters.label: W Weight
parameters.description: The weight of the Alpha (w) channel when Conversion is Channel Mix.

parameters.label: Normalize Weights
parameters.description: Divides the channel mix by the sum of the weights so the result keeps the same overall range. Turn this off to use the weights as raw multipliers.

parameters.label: Normal Type
parameters.description: How the normal values are encoded when Conversion is Light Direction. Signed (-1 to 1): The channels store normal components directly in the -1 to 1 range. Offset (0 to 1): The channels store normal components remapped into the 0 to 1 range, as is common for normal maps.

parameters.label: Light Direction
parameters.description: The direction the light comes from when Conversion is Light Direction. Normals facing this direction produce higher mask values.

parameters.label: Terminator
parameters.description: Shifts the boundary between the lit and unlit sides of the surface when Conversion is Light Direction.

parameters.label: Blur
parameters.description: Blurs the layer before it's blended in, softening its edges.

parameters.label: Layer Remap
parameters.description: Remaps this layer's values through a ramp before blending, letting you reshape its contrast or invert it.

parameters.label: NOTE
parameters.description: The node applies the post-processing operations in the order they're listed.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Combined Mask Remap
parameters.description: Remaps the combined mask through a ramp, letting you reshape the final result after all layers are blended.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: NOTE
parameters.description: The node applies the post-processing operations in the order they're listed.
parameters.heading: Range

parameters.label: Fold
parameters.description: Sets the noise values to the absolute value. For example, a pixel value of -2 becomes 2. NOTE: This parameter doesn't impact the output when there's only positive values.
parameters.heading: Range

parameters.label: Complement
parameters.description: Sets the pixel value x to 1 - x. NOTE: This method works for values in the 0 to 1 range. For images outside of this range, using Complement results in negative or out of range values.
parameters.heading: Range

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.description: The amount to pull the medium grey values (around 0.5) towards zero (if Bias is less than 1) or one (if Bias is greater than 1). A bias value of 0.5 doesn't affect the values. Image:/images/nodes/cop/postprocessing_bias.jpg
parameters.heading: Range

parameters.label: Gain
parameters.description: The amount to pull the medium grey values (around 0.5) together, while values around 0 and 1 are pulled apart. A gain value of 0.5 doesn't affect the noise values. Image:/images/nodes/cop/postprocessing_gain.jpg
parameters.heading: Range

parameters.label: Gamma
parameters.description: The overall gamma of the generated noise. Values greater than 1 increase the range of values in originally bright areas, which darkens the noise. Values less than 1 stretch out the range of values for originally dark areas, which increases the overall brightness of the noise.
parameters.heading: Range

parameters.label: Contrast
parameters.description: The amount to expand or shrink the overall range of tonal values. Each noise value is pushed towards (if Contrast is less than 1) or away from (if Contrast is greater than 1) medium grey values (around 0.5). NOTE: This is not the same as Noise Contrast, which appears in some noise nodes and applies contrast during the noise function.
parameters.heading: Range

parameters.label: Clamp Minimum
parameters.description: Clamps values below the specified threshold.
parameters.heading: Range

parameters.label: Clamp Maximum
parameters.description: Clamps values exceeding the specified threshold.
parameters.heading: Range

entries.label: Mask from Curves
entries.summary: Creates a mask from 2D curves.

parameters.label: Output Type
parameters.description: The output type. Mask: Output a mask with white inside the curves and black outside the curves. SDF: Output the distance from the closed curves as a signed distance field (SDF).

parameters.label: Invert
parameters.description: Inverts the outgoing mask or SDF, which reverses the inside sense of the curves. This does not affect the id values.

parameters.label: Blur
parameters.description: Applies a postprocess blur to the mask output that softens the edges.

parameters.label: Units
parameters.description: The units to use for blurring the mask. Image: Specify the blur in image space. Pixels: Specify the blur in absolute pixels.

parameters.label: Size
parameters.description: The size of the mask blur in image space or pixels, which the Units parameter determines.

parameters.label: Conversion Quality
parameters.description: How well to convert NURBs and Bezier into polygons. Higher values result in smoother conversions but require more time.

parameters.label: Resample
parameters.description: Resamples the incoming polygons so they have equal-spaced points. This can reduce dense geometry or add smoothness to low resolution curves.

parameters.label: Segment Length
parameters.description: The size in world space to resample each edge of the input curves.

parameters.label: Treat Polygons As
parameters.description: Set the new points along an implicit curve. Refining a polygon normally has little effect on the smoothness of the curve since the new points lie on the edges. Straight Edges: New points lie along the original curve's edges. Subdivision Curves: New points treat the original curves as control points of a B-spline. Interpolating Curves: New points follow a B-spline that interpolates the original points. This helps keep the size of the curve, but might introduce overshoots and oscillations.

entries.label: Match Camera
entries.summary: Transforms a layer to match a reference camera.

parameters.label: Identity Transform
parameters.description: Resets the layer to the canonical space. This moves the layer to the origin, aligns it with the XY plane, and resets its camera properties to the canonical orthographic projection.

entries.label: Mono to ID
entries.summary: Converts a mono layer, VDB, or attribute into an integer.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Conversion
parameters.description: The method used to convert the float value into an integer. Cast: Cast the float into an integer. Safe Unpack: Reverse the packing of Safe Pack in the ID to Mono COP to get back the original integer. See the unpack_intfromsafefloat VEX function for more information. Bitwise: Reinterpret the float as an integer. Although this is reversible, the resulting integer doesn't reflect the incoming floating point value.

entries.label: Mono to RGB
entries.summary: Converts a mono layer, VDB, or attribute into an RGB layer, VDB, or attribute.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Compute Range
parameters.description: Sets the Input Min and Input Max parameters to the minimum and maximum values of the source input.

parameters.label: Input Min
parameters.description: This value in the input corresponds with the start of the ramp.

parameters.label: Input Max
parameters.description: This value of the input corresponds with the end of the ramp.

parameters.label: Output Min
parameters.description: The ramp is shifted & scaled so black (0) in the ramp has this intensity before being applied.

parameters.label: Output Max
parameters.description: The ramp is shifted & scaled so white (1) in the ramp has this intensity before being applied.

parameters.label: Scale by Value
parameters.description: After the ramp color is computed, it is scaled by the input's value after normalization to the input min/max range. This allows a ramp to continue to brighten outside of the ramped range.

parameters.label: Outside Range
parameters.description: The method used to control how the ramp affects input values that're outside of the input range. Clamp at End: Values below the minimum are clamped to the start of the ramp. Values above the maximum are clamped to the end of the ramp. Repeat: Repeat the ramp, cycling the resulting colors for out-of-range inputs.

parameters.label: Ramp
parameters.description: An RGB ramp that defines how to map the input pixels. The left side corresponds to the input minimum and the right side corresponds to the input maximum. See Ramp parameters for more information.

entries.label: Neural Cellular Automata Core
entries.summary: Runs a neural cellular automata model to evolve cell states.

parameters.label: Model
parameters.description: The NCA model preset to use. This sets the model file path and any other parameters stored in the recipe simultaneously.

parameters.label: Initialize Cells
parameters.description: Outputs an initialized cell state without running the NCA model. Use this to create the starting state for a cellular automata simulation. NOTE: This parameter helps provide the correct input cable when running the model in a block.

parameters.label: NCA Model File
parameters.description: The path to an ONNX model file for the NCA.

parameters.label: Reload Model
parameters.description: Forces a reload of the ONNX model file.

parameters.label: Model Iterations
parameters.description: The number of times the NCA model is applied per cook. Higher values evolve the cell state further but take longer to compute. TIP: When growing textures on meshes with adjacency information, use the Neural Cellular Automata Block recipe with this parameter set to a low value. Make use of the block's own iterations or simulate over time to make sure the adjacency information is used frequently to update the solve between model iterations.

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.description: A seed value that controls the stochastic update mask.

parameters.label: Update Rate
parameters.description: The fraction of cells to update each iteration, in the range 0.1 to 0.9. Lower values update fewer cells per step, producing a more gradual evolution. Use the seed to change the random number generation, affecting which cells get updated. This can be used to generate variations of the overall pattern.

parameters.label: Update Mask Type
parameters.description: Controls how the update mask is applied to each cell. Amplitude-Weighted: The update is scaled by the incoming 0-1 mask, but the likelihood of an update is still only controlled by the seed. This produces smoother gradual evolution. Probabilistic: The update is always applied fully, but the 0-1 mask drives the probability of an update occurring in the first place. This creates noisier evolution, but pronounces the cell-based underlying structure.

parameters.label: Cell Rotation
parameters.description: Applies a rotation in turns to the cell perception kernel, where a value of 1 is a full rotation (360°). This is added on top of the per-cell rotation coming from the rotation input.

parameters.label: Cell Scale
parameters.description: Applies a scale to the cell perception gradient. This is multiplied with the per-cell scale coming from the scale input. The final scale is clamped to the range 0.2 to 1 to avoid exploding gradients. You can use values above 1 to multiply a small input scale mask up towards the upper bound of the valid range, but the values are limited by the internal clamping.

parameters.label: World Space Direction
parameters.description: When an adjacency cable is connected, this is the world space direction vector used as an up vector when computing the cell rotation adjacency information. With the default value of (0,1,0), the pattern on the geometry matches the pattern on a 2D layer in the origin when looking along the Z axis.
parameters.heading: Adjacency

parameters.label: Size Ref Scale
parameters.description: A scale factor applied to the size_ref input resolution to determine the working resolution of the NCA. Lower fractions reduce memory usage and computation time. 1/1: Full resolution. 1/2: Half resolution. 1/4: Quarter resolution. 1/8: Eighth resolution.
parameters.heading: Advanced

entries.label: Neural Cellular Automata Decode
entries.summary: Decodes a cell state from the Neural Cellular Automata Core into a visible pattern.

parameters.label: Model
parameters.description: Controls where the decoder model comes from. From Metadata: Uses the decoder model referenced in the layer metadata of the incoming cell state. This automatically matches the decoder to the model used by the upstream Node:cop/neural_cellularautomatacore. NOTE: This is the default setting. In this mode, the node looks for the decodemodel string layer property to know from where it should load the decoder ONNX model file. The node won't know which model to load if this layer property is removed. You can always set the model file path explicitly. Custom: Use a custom decoder ONNX file.

parameters.label: Decoder Model File
parameters.description: The path to a custom decoder ONNX model file.

parameters.label: Reload Model
parameters.description: Forces a reload of the ONNX model file.

parameters.label: Upres Factor
parameters.description: The factor by which to upsample the cell states before decoding. 1x: No upressing, just decoding 2x: 2 times the input resolution. 4x: 4 times the input resolution. 8x: 8 times the input resolution.

parameters.label: Filter
parameters.description: The filter used when upsampling the incoming cell states. See Filters for more information. Point: Sets the pixel value to the pixel value of the nearest neighbor. Bilinear: Sets the pixel value through bilinear interpolation. Box: Sets the pixel value through a box filter, done by sampling all pixels within a box on the original image's matching pixel. Bartlett: Sets the pixel value through interpolating according to a triangular window or a Bartlett window, taking each pixel as a sample of this signal. Catmull-Rom: Sets the pixel value through a bicubic spline known as the Catmull-Rom spline. This is a special case of the Mitchell-Netravali filter. Mitchell: Sets the pixel value through a bicubic spline known as the Mitchell-Netravali filter. B-spline: Sets the pixel value through a bicubic spline known as the B-spline. This is a special case of the Mitchell-Netravali filter.

parameters.label: Color Transform
parameters.description: The color transformation to apply to the input image before processing. OCIO: Use OpenColorIO to transform colors to the target space (Output Space). See /solaris/ocio for more information. None (Raw): Don't apply any color transformation. The default NCA output colorspace is Linear rec709.
