parameters.label: Apply Sky Mask
parameters.description: Masks out regions classified as sky in the skymask output. This prevents unstable point estimations in areas of the image that lack reconstructible surfaces.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Sky Depth Shift
parameters.description: Applies a depth offset (in meters) to sky regions when Apply Sky Mask is on.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Remove Edges
parameters.description: Removes points that are near depth discontinuities, which are sudden changes in depth disparity. Configure Max Depth Change to set the maximum depth change that the points can surround until they're removed.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Max Depth Change
parameters.description: The maximum change in depth disparity (in meters) the node allows until it removes points around the depth discontinuities. Lower values remove more points while higher values preserve more detail (but may retain noisy points).
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Normal Type
parameters.description: The method used to store the normals (see Normals for more information). Signed (-1 to 1): Output signed normals, compatible with geometry attributes. Offset (0 to 1): Output offset normals, compatible with normal maps.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Create GSplat Points
parameters.description: Visualizes the 3D point cloud as a Gaussian splat.
parameters.heading: GSplat

parameters.label: GSplat Scale
parameters.description: The size (in meters) of the Gaussian splat points.
parameters.heading: GSplat

parameters.label: Use Solved Camera
parameters.description: Matches output layers to a camera solved with pixel-GSplat point correspondences.
parameters.heading: Camera

parameters.label: RANSAC Seed
parameters.description: The seed used to randomly select candidate point correspondences used to solve for a camera.
parameters.heading: Camera

parameters.label: RANSAC Iterations
parameters.description: The number of RANSAC loop iterations executed to solve for a camera. Increasing this can improve the accuracy of the solution.
parameters.heading: Camera

parameters.label: RANSAC Tolerance
parameters.description: The reprojection error tolerance used to determine if a camera solution is acceptable.
parameters.heading: Camera

parameters.label: Execution Provider
parameters.description: Determines which ONNX execution provider to use for inference. By default, the node attempts to pick the best available provider and prefers to use GPU acceleration. Automatic CPU CUDA DirectML CoreML
parameters.heading: Advanced

parameters.label: Device ID
parameters.description: This parameter can be used to specify which GPU to use for inference when multiple GPUs are available. It has no effect when using CPU inference.
parameters.heading: Advanced

entries.label: Neural Layer to Mask (SAM2)
entries.summary: Creates a mask based on coordinates set through prompts.

parameters.label: Model
parameters.description: The SAM 2 model variant to use for segmentation. SAM2 Large: The most accurate model, but slower and with a larger memory footprint. SAM2 Tiny: A fast, but less accurate model. Custom: Use custom encoder and decoder ONNX files.

parameters.label: Download Models
parameters.description: Downloads the pre-trained SAM 2 model files to the SHFS model location.

parameters.label: Encoder ONNX File
parameters.description: The path to a custom encoder ONNX file.

parameters.label: Decoder ONNX File
parameters.description: The path to a custom decoder ONNX file.

parameters.label: Reload Model
parameters.description: Forces a reload of the .onnx file.

parameters.label: Units
parameters.description: The coordinate system that specifies the point and bounding box positions. This controls the range of the values and whether they're in respect to the input's display or data window. Image: Specify coordinates in terms of the display window, with a range of -1 to 1. Texture: Specify coordinates in terms of the data window, with a range of 0 to 1. Pixels: Specify coordinates in pixels as integers.

parameters.label: Points
parameters.description: The number of point prompts, which are positive or negative. These tell the model which areas you want to mask in the original image. NOTE: A prompt identifies an object, and the model predicts a mask that covers all pixels belonging to that object. TIP: Click the Icon:TOOLS/handles Handles tool to set points directly in the Scene Viewer. See Set points in the Scene Viewer for more information.

parameters.label: Point Coords #
parameters.description: Coordinates for the prompt point. The Units parameter determines if this is in image space, texture space, or pixels.

parameters.label: Negative
parameters.description: Makes the point indicate an area to exclude from the mask.

parameters.label: Bounding Box
parameters.description: Defines a bounding box prompt.

parameters.label: BBox Lower Left
parameters.description: The lower-left corner coordinates of the bounding box. The Units parameter determines if this is in image space, texture space, or pixels.

parameters.label: BBox Upper Right
parameters.description: The upper-right corner coordinates of the bounding box. The Units parameter determines if this is in image space, texture space, or pixels.

parameters.label: Resample Behavior
parameters.description: The method used to handle images that don't match the model's expected input size of 1024x1024. Stretch to Fit: Stretch the image to fit the model's input size (1024 x 1024). Fit Minimally: Fit the image within the model's input size (1024 x 1024) with minimal distortion. The node pads the image as needed.
parameters.heading: Pre Processing

parameters.label: Color Transform
parameters.description: The color transformation to apply to the input image before processing. OCIO: Use OpenColorIO to transform colors from the Original Space to the target space (To Space). See /solaris/ocio for more information. None (raw): Don't apply any color transformation.
parameters.heading: Pre Processing

parameters.label: Original Space
parameters.description: The space that the input color is in.
parameters.heading: Pre Processing

parameters.label: To Space
parameters.description: The output color space to which the input color transforms.
parameters.heading: Pre Processing

parameters.label: Clean Up
parameters.description: Refines the output masks using Total Variation Denoising (TVD). These are post-processing cleanup operations.
parameters.heading: Output

parameters.label: TVD Iterations
parameters.description: The number of denoising rounds that the node performs on the mask. More iterations increase the smoothing of the mask but lose more fine detail. The run time of this operation is proportional to the number of rounds.
parameters.heading: Output

parameters.label: TVD Speed
parameters.description: The amount by which to multiply the TVD Iterations value. The result determines the total amount of diffusion to apply in each round of iteration. NOTE: If the total amount of diffusion is too large, the process can be unstable and not converge to a good result. A total amount higher than 0.75 can cause significant artifacts.
parameters.heading: Output

parameters.label: Upsampling Filter
parameters.description: The filter to use when upsampling masks to the original image resolution. See Filters for more information. Point: Sets the pixel value to the pixel value of the nearest neighbor. Bilinear: Sets the pixel value through bilinear interpolation. Box: Sets the pixel value through a box filter, done by sampling all pixels within a box on the original image's matching pixel. Bartlett: Sets the pixel value through interpolating according to a triangular window or a Bartlett window, taking each pixel as a sample of this signal. Catmull-Rom: Sets the pixel value through a bicubic spline known as the Catmull-Rom spline. This is a special case of the Mitchell-Netravali filter. Mitchell: Sets the pixel value through a bicubic spline known as the Mitchell-Netravali filter. B-spline: Sets the pixel value through a bicubic spline known as the B-spline. This is a special case of the Mitchell-Netravali filter.
parameters.heading: Output

parameters.label: Mask Threshold
parameters.description: The threshold value at which the node converts soft masks to binary masks. The node makes pixels above this value white (1.0) and pixels below this value black (0.0). When off, the node outputs the raw, soft mask values.
parameters.heading: Output

parameters.label: Preview Color
parameters.description: The color that overlays the mask in the viewer state to preview the final mask output. TIP: Click the Icon:TOOLS/handles Handles tool and then press ((O)) in the Scene Viewer to turn the mask preview on or off.
parameters.heading: Visualization

parameters.label: Execution Provider
parameters.description: Determines which ONNX execution provider to use for inference. By default, the node attempts to pick the best available provider and prefers to use GPU acceleration. Automatic CPU CUDA DirectML CoreML
parameters.heading: Advanced

parameters.label: Device ID
parameters.description: This parameter can be used to specify which GPU to use for inference when multiple GPUs are available. It has no effect when using CPU inference.
parameters.heading: Advanced

entries.label: Normal to Height
entries.summary: Reconstructs a height layer from a normal layer.

parameters.label: Solver
parameters.description: The method used to integrate the normals into a height field. FFT: Solves Poisson's equation in the frequency domain in a single pass. This is fast, but implicitly treats the layer as tiling, so the borders are always periodic and there are no boundary controls. Poisson: Solves Poisson's equation with an iterative geometric multigrid solver (see Solve Poisson Multigrid). This offers more control over the borders, but may need to be iterated for accuracy.

parameters.label: Normal Type
parameters.description: How the incoming normals are stored (see Normals for more information). Signed (-1 to 1): Read signed normals, as stored in geometry attributes. Offset (0 to 1): Read offset normals, as stored in normal maps.

parameters.label: Height Scale
parameters.description: A global multiplier applied to the reconstructed height as a post-process. Higher values make the result steeper.

parameters.label: Center
parameters.description: The value about which the reconstructed height is centered. The solve fixes the height only up to an additive constant, so the result is shifted to have this mean value.

parameters.label: Iterations
parameters.description: Number of multigrid V-cycle iterations to perform. The solution is more accurate with a higher number of iterations, but also takes longer to produce. Only used by the Poisson Solver.
parameters.heading: Poisson

parameters.label: Smoothing Method
parameters.description: The method used for relaxation on the up- and down-strokes of the multigrid solve. Gauss-Seidel offers better asymptotic convergence and requires less memory, as the red-black partitioning of cells allows for in-place smoothing. Jacobi works on all pixels at once, which avoids systemic checkerboard patterns in the residuals but requires an extra copy of the layer. Disabled when either border is set to Periodic. Gauss-Seidel: Relax cells in red-black order, smoothing in place. Jacobi: Relax all cells at once into a separate copy.
parameters.heading: Poisson

parameters.label: X Borders
parameters.description: State of the borders on the left and right sides of the layer, set independently. When the left side is Periodic, the right side is connected to it and its own setting is ignored. Open: Prescribe a height of 0 along that side. Closed: Force the height to flatten out toward that side. Periodic: Wrap the left and right sides of the layer together.
parameters.heading: Poisson

parameters.label: Y Borders
parameters.description: State of the borders on the bottom and top sides of the layer, set independently. When the bottom side is Periodic, the top side is connected to it and its own setting is ignored. Open: Prescribe a height of 0 along that side. Closed: Force the height to flatten out toward that side. Periodic: Wrap the bottom and top sides of the layer together.
parameters.heading: Poisson

entries.label: Ocean Evaluate
entries.summary: Converts the layers of an ocean spectrum into an animated ocean surface.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: An overall multiplier applied to the amplitude of the evaluated waves. Higher values produce taller waves.

parameters.label: Chop
parameters.description: The amount of sharp cusps the waves will have. This horizontally displaces the surface towards the wave peaks, sharpening the crests and flattening the troughs.

parameters.label: Time
parameters.description: The time at which to evaluate the ocean surface.

parameters.label: Ocean Size
parameters.description: The world space size of the input ocean spectrum. This should match the Ocean Size used on the Ocean Spectrum COP that generated the input layers so that the horizontal displacement is scaled correctly.

entries.label: Ocean Spectrum
entries.summary: Generates layers containing information for simulating ocean waves.

parameters.label: Ocean Size
parameters.description: The world space size of the generated ocean spectrum. Increasing this value will fit more wave peaks and crests into a single ocean tile, and the waves will appear to move slower through it. For proper visualization of the height field generated by Ocean Evaluate from this spectrum, it should be uniformly scaled (transformed) by this amount.

parameters.label: Depth
parameters.description: The depth of the ocean. The waves in deep oceans have a strong dispersion relationship, meaning the large, low-frequency waves move faster than the smaller waves. Decreasing this parameter reduces the amount of dispersion and causes more uniformity in wave speed.

parameters.label: Gravity
parameters.description: Acceleration due of gravity. Waves have a shorter wavelength and move faster under stronger gravity.

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.description: Seed for random generation of the spectrum. Changing the seed will modify the spectrum without affecting the wave dynamics.

parameters.label: Spectrum Type
parameters.description: The algorithm used to generate wave amplitudes given various parameters such as water depth, wind direction and speed. Phillips: The classic spectrum that provides control over wind direction in a fully developed ocean. This spectrum type is also known as _Tessendorf_. TMA: An enhanced spectrum that adds additional parameters for how long wind has acted upon the ocean and performs better at lower Depth settings. The implementation of the TMA (Texel-Marsen-Arsloe) spectrum is also known as _Encino_ waves.
parameters.heading: Wind

parameters.label: Wind Direction
parameters.description: Wind direction in degrees, with zero being along the local X axis. This parameter controls the overall directionality of the spectrum.
parameters.heading: Wind

parameters.label: Wind Speed
parameters.description: The wind speed. Higher wind speeds create larger low-frequency waves and generally increase the dynamic range of the ocean spectrum.
parameters.heading: Wind

parameters.label: Swell
parameters.description: Enhances the directionality of the waves in the TMA spectrum when set to values greater than zero. Negative values remove directionality and adds more waves in directions opposing the wind.
parameters.heading: Wind

parameters.label: Fetch (km)
parameters.description: The distance in kilometers that the wind has been acting upon the ocean in the TMA spectrum, often thought of as the distance from shore.
parameters.heading: Wind

parameters.label: Wind Direction Bias
parameters.description: The amount that the waves in the Phillips spectrum will align with the wind direction. As this parameter increases, waves that don't align with the wind will be dampened.
parameters.heading: Wind

parameters.label: Directional Movement
parameters.description: The amount that waves in the Phillips spectrum will move in the same direction as the wind. When this value is low, the ocean will contain waves that are aligned with the wind, but moving in the opposite direction from the wind. Increasing this value will dampen those waves, leaving only those moving in the same direction.
parameters.heading: Wind

parameters.label: Distribution
parameters.description: The random distribution used to scale the wave amplitudes after the shaping parameters have been applied. None: No random values are applied to the amplitudes. This setting is useful for post-multiplying the amplitude volume with custom values before they are evaluated with Ocean Evaluate. Uniform: Use a uniform random distribution, which gives amplitude to many wave frequencies across the spectrum. Gaussian: Use a Gaussian random distribution, which tends to be the best match to experimental models of ocean spectra. Log Normal: Use a Log Normal distribution, which gives higher amplitudes to fewer wave frequencies.
parameters.heading: Amplitude

parameters.label: Normalize
parameters.description: The ocean spectrum is shaped by reducing the amplitude of waves traveling in unwatned directions, which causes the overall height of the ocean to change as the waves are shaped. Normalizing maintains consistent wave heights as the various shaping parameters are modified. When this parameter is enabled, the only parameters that affect wave height are the Wind Speed, which affects dynamic range, and Scale, which affects overall amplitude gain.
parameters.heading: Amplitude

parameters.label: Reference Wind
parameters.description: The reference wind used for normalizing the overall wave height. Should only be changed if the units of your scene are changing.
parameters.heading: Amplitude

parameters.label: Min Wavelength
parameters.description: Dampen any waves with a smaller wavelength than this value, which can help with aliasing of very small waves at very high resolution.
parameters.heading: Amplitude

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: A constant gain by which to scale all the wave amplitudes.
parameters.heading: Amplitude

parameters.label: Loop Period
parameters.description: Length of the looping animation in seconds when looping is enabled.
parameters.heading: Time

entries.label: ONNX Inference
entries.summary: Applies inference from an ONNX Machine Learning model.

parameters.label: Execution Provider
parameters.description: Determines which ONNX execution provider to use for inference. By default, the node will attempt to pick the best available provider and will prefer to use GPU acceleration if possible. Automatic CPU CUDA DirectML CoreML
parameters.heading: Model

parameters.label: Device ID
parameters.description: The GPU to use for inference when multiple GPUs are available. This parameter is off when you use CPU inference.
parameters.heading: Model

parameters.label: Model File
parameters.description: The name of the .onnx file to load. The model inputs and outputs must match the settings of the ONNX file. NOTE: An error message appears when you set the Model File parameter but the input and output information in the Model tab is empty. Setting the other Model parameters resolves this error.
parameters.heading: Model

parameters.label: Reload Model
parameters.description: Forces a reload of the .onnx file.
parameters.heading: Model

parameters.label: Setup Shapes from Model
parameters.description: Reads the .onnx file to determine the number of inputs and outputs and their shapes. See Setup Shapes from Model for more information.
parameters.heading: Model

parameters.label: Number of Inputs
parameters.description: The number of inputs to the model. NOTE: The order of the inputs must match the order of the inputs in the ONNX model, as the node doesn't match the model based on names.
parameters.heading: Model

parameters.label: Name
parameters.description: The name of the input to the model. The Setup Shapes from Model button populates this with the input name from the model, but you can rename it.
parameters.heading: Model

parameters.label: Data
parameters.description: The node input(s) that provide the data for this model input. You can enter a space- or comma-separated list of node input names to link multiple inputs together in a chain, such as separate R, G, and B layers.
parameters.heading: Model

parameters.label: Input Tensor Element Data Type
parameters.description: The tensor element data type. There is a choice between Float32, Float16, Int32, Int8, UInt8, Int64, Float64 and Bool.
parameters.heading: Model

parameters.label: Input Tensor Shape
parameters.description: The shape of the input that the model requires. The total shape must match the number of elements (the total size of the data) in the input. A warning appears if the input image's size doesn't match the model's expected input size. Use the Resample Size parameter to resize the input image. See Tensor shapes for more information.
parameters.heading: Model

parameters.label: Tensor Order
parameters.description: Specifies how to convert the input image into the data layout that the model expects, which is a 1D tensor. YX: Unpack pixels horizontally (neighboring samples along X are placed together). XY: Unpack pixels vertically (neighboring samples along Y are placed together).
parameters.heading: Model

parameters.label: Collate Channels Separately
parameters.description: When converting an image with multiple channels per pixel into a 1D tensor, this stores the RGB image as rrrgggbbb (separate RGB sets) and the shape's first dimension is the number of channels. If this parameter is off when converting an image with multiple channels per pixel into a 1D tensor, this stores the RGB image as rgbrgbrgb and the shape's final dimension is the number of channels. See Tensor shapes for more information.
parameters.heading: Model

parameters.label: Channel Size
parameters.description: The value that overrides the input image's number of channels so it matches the channel size that the model expects.
parameters.heading: Model

parameters.label: Number of Outputs
parameters.description: The number of outputs to the model. NOTE: The order of the outputs must match the order of the outputs in the ONNX model, as the node doesn't match the model based on names.
parameters.heading: Model

parameters.label: Name
parameters.description: The name of the output of the model. The Setup Shapes from Model button populates this with the output name from the model, but you can rename it. In the Input & Output tab, enter this name in a node output's Data parameter so it uses this model output's data.

parameters.label: Output Tensor Element Data Type
parameters.description: The tensor element data type. There is a choice between Float32, Float16, Int32, Int8, UInt8, Int64, Float64 and Bool.

parameters.label: Output Tensor Shape
parameters.description: The shape of the output that the model requires. The total shape must match the number of elements (the total size of the data) that the model generates. See Tensor shapes for more information.

parameters.label: Tensor Order
parameters.description: Specifies how to convert the output image into the data layout that the model expects, which is a 1D tensor. YX: Unpack pixels horizontally (neighboring samples along X are placed together). XY: Unpack pixels vertically (neighboring samples along Y are placed together).

parameters.label: Collate Channels Separately
parameters.description: When converting an image with multiple channels per pixel into a 1D tensor, this stores the RGB image as rrrgggbbb (separate RGB sets) and the shape's first dimension is the number of channels. If this parameter is off when converting an image with multiple channels per pixel into a 1D tensor, this stores the RGB image as rgbrgbrgb and the shape's final dimension is the number of channels. See Tensor shapes for more information.
parameters.heading: Model

parameters.label: Channel Size
parameters.description: The value that overrides the output image's number of channels so it matches the channel size that the model expects.
parameters.heading: Model

parameters.label: Max Batch Size
parameters.description: Determines how many multiples of the input you want to evaluate together and process at once. If you have multiple input instances, set this parameter to split the inputs into batches so the model runs them in succession to reduce peak memory usage. This parameter doesn't correspond to the amount of pixels in the image, but instead depends on what size the rest of the input is. For example, if you had a model that only accepts an image as a single input, this parameter value is how many images you batch together at once. NOTE: This parameter applies to only the first dynamic dimension.
parameters.heading: Model

parameters.label: Number of Inputs
parameters.description: The number of inputs for the node. The Setup Shapes from Model button creates a node input for each model input and associates them using the model's Data parameter.
parameters.heading: Input & Output

parameters.label: Name
parameters.description: The name of the node input. The Setup Shapes from Model button populates this, but you can rename it. In the Model tab, enter this name in a model input's Data parameter so it uses this node input's data.
parameters.heading: Input & Output

parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: The data type for the node input.
parameters.heading: Input & Output

parameters.label: RGBA Treatment
parameters.description: How RGBA is treated: There is a choice between Preserve R, G, B and A and Discard Component A.
parameters.heading: Input & Output

parameters.label: Tensor Order
parameters.description: Specifies how to convert the input image into the data layout that the model expects, which is a 1D tensor. This value applies only when you enter multiple input names in a Data parameter in the Model tab, as it changes this input's layout before combining it with the other inputs. YX: Unpack pixels horizontally (neighboring samples along X are placed together). XY: Unpack pixels vertically (neighboring samples along Y are placed together).
parameters.heading: Input & Output

parameters.label: Flip Input Vertically
parameters.description: Flips the input image vertically. You can use this for models (2D images) that expect the origin to be at the top left corner of the image instead of at the bottom left corner. See Tensor shapes for more information.
parameters.heading: Input & Output

parameters.label: Collate Channels Separately
parameters.description: Stores an RGB image as rrrgggbbb and the shape's first dimension is the number of channels. When off, this stores an RGB image as rgbrgbrgb and the shape's final dimension is the number of channels. This parameter applies only when you enter multiple input names in a Data parameter in the Model tab, as it separates this input's channels before combining it with the other inputs. When converting an image with multiple channels per pixel into a 1D tensor, the channel values can either be interleaved or placed one after another. See Tensor shapes for more information.
parameters.heading: Input & Output

parameters.label: Resample Size
parameters.description: Resamples the input image to the specified dimensions (width by height). Use this parameter to match the model's expected size for an input image, which is based on the Input Tensor Shape. Set the width or height to -1 and the other cell to a specific value when you want the node to preserve the aspect ratio based on the specified dimension. For example, if you set the width to 224 and the height to -1, the node resizes the image's height to a dimension that maintains the aspect ratio.

parameters.label: Filter

parameters.label: Brightness Multiplier
parameters.description: Adjusts the brightness of the input image. This is useful for models that expect colors to be represented by integers between 0 and 255, rather than floating-point values between 0 and 1. These models require scaling up of the input image's brightness and scaling down the output image's brightness. 1: Maintains the brightness as the input's default amount. 255: Scales the brightness up by 255. 1/255: Scales the brightness down by 1/255.

parameters.label: Deduce Output Shapes from Data String

This parameter is useful if you want to calculate the tensor shape and channel size when merging multiple model outputs. The Setup Shapes from Model parameter automatically triggers this parameter. NOTE: This parameter uses the input and output data from the Model tab, so you must populate those Model parameters before using this parameter.

When converting an image with multiple channels per pixel into a 1D tensor, the channel values can either be interleaved or placed one after another. See Tensor shapes for more information.

This is useful for models that expect colors to be represented by integers between 0 and 255, rather than floating-point values between 0 and 1. entries.label: OpenCL
entries.summary: Executes an OpenCL kernel on layers, attributes, volumes, and VDBs.

parameters.label: Kernel Code
parameters.description: OpenCL kernel to execute. This is usually a series of #bind commands to describe what the bindings to the kernel will be, along with an @KERNEL which contains the actual kernel function. Within the kernel function @ references can be used to refer to the bindings.
parameters.heading: Kernel

parameters.label: Run Over
parameters.description: What to run the OpenCL kernels on. First Writeable Layer: Run the OpenCL kernels on the first writeable layer. First Writeable Attribute: Run the OpenCL kernels on the first writeable attribute. First Writeable Volume: Run the OpenCL kernels on the first writeable volume. First Writeable VDB: Run the OpenCL kernels on the first writeable VDB.
parameters.heading: Options

parameters.label: Kernel Name
parameters.description: The name of the OpenCL kernel to run with the loaded program.
parameters.heading: Options

parameters.label: Write Back Kernel Name
parameters.description: The name of the kernel to use in the write back operation. It has the same function signature as the main operation.
parameters.heading: Options

parameters.label: Compiler Options
parameters.description: Specify any desired compile flags for the kernel. The most common is to use -D to provide #define directives for the pre-processor. NOTE: The Apple OSX OpenCL compiler requires only a single space between kernel options. Houdini defines additional flags while compiling kernels depending on the OpenCL device. The flags H_GPU or H_CPU distinguish between GPU and CPU devices, and H_NVIDIA, H_AMD, H_INTEL, or H_APPLE_ signify the hardware vendor. You can set the environment variable HOUDINI_OCL_REPORT_BUILD_LOGS to 1 before running Houdini to get a dump of all kernels compiled along with their preprocessor flags.
parameters.heading: Options

parameters.label: Layer Tile Size
parameters.description: When Run Over is First Writeable Layer, the kernel runs once for every NxM block of buffer elements, where this gives the size of blocks. This means the edge blocks might go past the edges of the buffer. The default behavior is to run the kernel for every buffer element in the source layer. If a tilesize is zero, the corresponding block size is set to the width or height of the image. This can be used for per-row or per-column operations. @ixy will give the start of the current tile, and @tilesize the configured tile size. min(@ixy+@tilesize, @res) can be used as the end point of a loop that stays within the buffer.
parameters.heading: Options

parameters.label: VDB Tile Size
parameters.description: When Run Over is First Writeable VDB, the kernel runs once for every block of voxels this size.
parameters.heading: Options

parameters.label: Kernel Iterations
parameters.description: The kernel can be re-executed a variable number of times. This avoids having to use more nodes to create a loop, and ensures all data remains on the video card during the successive evaluations.
parameters.heading: Options

parameters.label: Kernel Include Iteration
parameters.description: Binds an @Iteration integer containing the current kernel iteration.
parameters.heading: Options

parameters.label: Use Write Back Kernel
parameters.description: After the kernel is executed, a second kernel may be immediately executed with the same set of parameters bound to it. You can avoid race conditions where multiple threads want to write to the same data by breaking it into a two-pass operation. The second kernel is configured with @WRITEBACK.
parameters.heading: Options

parameters.label: Include Time
parameters.description: Binds @Time to the current evaluation time in seconds. The node becomes time-dependent once it cooks.
parameters.heading: Options

parameters.label: Use Timestep
parameters.description: Respects the timescale specified on the Block End COP or the current Frame Rate. If not set, the time increment will be 1.0 scaled by the time scale. Turning this off stops the @TimeInc from varying with frame rate, substeps, or the containing block's time scale. This lets you set the time increment to an absolute value.
parameters.heading: Options

parameters.label: Include Timestep
parameters.description: Binds @TimeInc containing the timestep.
parameters.heading: Options

parameters.label: Time Scale
parameters.description: When Include Timestep is on, this is a constant multiplier on the timestep. You can also set the method used to determine the value of the current timestep. Timestep: The current timestep value is the linear timestep. e ^ Timestep: The current timestep value is the exponential evaluated at the timestep. This is useful for multiplicative or exponential dynamic processes where you must raise a power to the timestep.
parameters.heading: Options

parameters.label: Use #import for Prequel Code
parameters.description: Several common headers are always included. These can be brought in with either a #include or #import directive, this option will pick the latter. #import results in messier results in the Generate Code output, but can speed up caching of kernels on Windows.
parameters.heading: Options

parameters.label: Timing Messages
parameters.description: Sychronize the kernel when complete to ensure timing is accurate. Otherwise each kernel will run asynchronously, making it hard to tell which operation slowed things down.
parameters.heading: Options

parameters.label: Rename Wires Using Output Labels
parameters.description: When this toggle is enabled, name of each output wire is set based on its respective port label. Otherwise, wire names are propagated from inputs. Turn this option on if you'd like to discard incoming wire names and harden new ones for the downstream network to use.
parameters.heading: Options

parameters.label: Area Sampling Filter
parameters.description: The filtering method used for sampling the source layer. Consider using one of the area filters (Box and later) if the distortion shrinks large regions and you notice noise. See Filters for more information.
parameters.heading: Options

parameters.label: Precision
parameters.description: Controls the precision of this node. The fpreal and exint types will be defined in the generated code to correspond with this specified precision. The vector variants will also be defined, ie, fpreal3, fpreal4, etc. Additionally the FPREAL_PREC symbol is defined as 16 for half, 32 for float, or 64 for double. Auto will use the preferred precision of the incoming geometry, as set by the Attribute Cast SOP. NOTE: 16-bit cannot be used for computation in most drivers.
parameters.heading: Options

parameters.label: NOTE
parameters.description: This tab is often not configured explicitly, but set up with the "Create inputs and spare parameters" button.
parameters.heading: Signature

parameters.label: Inputs
parameters.description: The number of inputs for the node.
parameters.heading: Signature

parameters.label: Input #
parameters.description: The name of the input. This is what is bound to in the #bind command.
parameters.heading: Signature

parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: Varying: Accepts Mono, UV, RGB, or RGBA. All inputs of varying type will be set to the same type. ID: Accepts ID layers. Mono: Accepts Mono layers. UV: Accepts UV layers. RGB: Accepts RGB layers. RGBA: Accepts RGBA layers. Geometry: A geometry input. These must be referred to by name in an attribute or volume binding. Metadata: This input is only used for size and meta data information and will not be read. Integer VDB: Accepts integer VDBs. Float VDB: Accepts float VDBs. Vector VDB: Accepts vector VDBs. Varying VDB: Accepts float or vector VDBs.
parameters.heading: Signature

parameters.label: Optional
parameters.description: Marks if the input is mandatory. The corresponding binding should be marked optional.
parameters.heading: Signature

parameters.label: Outputs
parameters.description: The number of outputs for the node.
parameters.heading: Signature

parameters.label: Output #
parameters.description: The name of the output. This is the target of the #bind.
parameters.heading: Signature

parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: Varying: A Mono, UV, RGB, or RGBA layer matching the corresponding varying input layers. ID: An ID layer. Mono: A Mono layer. UV: A UV layer. RGB: An RGB layer. RGBA: An RGBA layer. Geometry: Geometry output. As geometry can't be created by OpenCL, this must match a geometry input. Integer VDB: An integer VDB. Float VDB: A float VDB. Vector VDB: A vector VDB. Varying VDB: A float or vector VDB.
parameters.heading: Signature

parameters.label: Metadata
parameters.description: Controls where the metadata of the layer will come from. This is where the size, display window, camera transforms, etc, will come from. First Input: The first input of a COP is often the size reference, so is a good choice to use for the metadata. Matching Name: The input whose name matches this output's name will be used. Input Name: A specific input of the provided name will be used.
parameters.heading: Signature

parameters.label: Precision
parameters.description: Layers can be stored in 16-bit and 32-bit formats for floating point layers, and in 8, 16, and 32-bit formats for integer. Input Precision: Maintain the precision of the input layer. 16-bit: Force 16-bit precision. 32-bit: Force 32-bit precision.
parameters.heading: Signature

parameters.label: Type Info
parameters.description: The type info for the resulting layer. Choosing Input will use whatever the metadata's type info was. See the Copernicus glossary for a description of type infos.
parameters.heading: Signature

parameters.label: Input for Metaada
parameters.description: The name of the input to use metadata from.
parameters.heading: Signature

parameters.label: Bindings
parameters.description: The number of this node's bound parameters. Expand a Bind# parameter's dropdown menu to configure its Name, Type, and other values.
parameters.heading: Bindings

parameters.label: Name
parameters.description: The name of the parameter. This is used in the Generate Kernel button and by the @ bindings. The actual OpenCL kernel function is defined by parameter order, not by the name, but if using @KERNEL this is hidden from you.
parameters.heading: Bindings

parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: The type of parameter to create and bind. Integer Float Vector2 Vector Vector4 Ramp: A scalar or color ramp. Because evaluating a spline-based ramp inside of an OpenCL kernel is complex, the ramp is instead sampled into a uniform array of floats. The Ramp Size parameter controls the number of samples used. Layer: A 2D image layer corresponding to a wire in Copernicus. Geometry: Bind a geometry attribute. Volume: Bind a volume. VDB: Bind a VDB. Context Option: Bind a Context Option. This directly binds block-iteration parameters to the kernel without needing parameter bindings.
parameters.heading: Bindings

parameters.label: Input Type
parameters.description: How the ramp is presented. Ramp Parameter: Exposes the Ramp parameter for ramp configuration. Raw Ramp: Set the ramp from its raw string representation (use the Exp:chrampraw expression function to serialize a ramp parameter into a string). This makes it easier to reference other ramps.
parameters.heading: Bindings

parameters.label: Ramp Size
parameters.description: The number of floating point values to evaluate the ramp in.
parameters.heading: Bindings

parameters.label: Data Type
parameters.description: The type of ramp to bind Float: A scalar ramp. Vector: A color ramp.
parameters.heading: Bindings

parameters.label: Ramp
parameters.description: The scalar ramp values.
parameters.heading: Bindings

parameters.label: Ramp
parameters.description: The color ramp values.
parameters.heading: Bindings

parameters.label: Raw Ramp
parameters.description: The string representation of the ramp. Use the Exp:chrampraw expression function to construct this string from a ramp parameter.
parameters.heading: Bindings

parameters.label: Data Type
parameters.description: What type of layer to bind. This refers to the OpenCL type system, not the COP system. Integer: An ID layer. Float: A Mono layer. Float2: A UV layer. Float3: An RGB layer. Float4: An RGBA layer. Float?: A Mono, UV, RGB, or RGBA layer.
parameters.heading: Bindings

parameters.label: Border
parameters.description: You can override the incoming layer's border rules without having to edit its metadata directly. Input: Use the input's border values unchanged. Constant: Force a constant, zero, value for out of bounds. Clamp: Clamp or streak out of bounds. Mirror: Reflect out of bounds on the boundary. Wrap: Wrap out of bounds to the other side.
parameters.heading: Bindings

parameters.label: Port
parameters.description: When binding geometry there may be more than one geoemtry input. This is the name of the input, as specified in the signature, to bind to.
parameters.heading: Bindings

parameters.label: Volume
parameters.description: The name or number of the volume or VDB primitive to bind.
parameters.heading: Bindings

parameters.label: Force Alignment
parameters.description: To simplify kernels one may often assume all volumes are aligned in resolution and transform. If Force Alignment is set, this is enforced and volumes that are misaligned generate errors.
parameters.heading: Bindings

parameters.label: Voxel Resolution
parameters.description: Add the resolution of the volume as a parameter.
parameters.heading: Bindings

parameters.label: Voxel Size
parameters.description: Add the size of the volume as a parameter, in SOP space.
parameters.heading: Bindings

parameters.label: Transform to World
parameters.description: Add a matrix transform that converts from the volume's voxel coordinates to the SOP coordinates.
parameters.heading: Bindings

parameters.label: Transform to Voxel
parameters.description: Add a matrix transform that converts from SOP coordinates to the volume's voxel coordinates.
parameters.heading: Bindings

parameters.label: Data Type
parameters.description: The types of VDBs to accept for the binding. Any: Any type of VDB can be bound, the kernel will have to do introspection to validate the type. Float: Floating point VDBs. Vector: Vector VDBs.
parameters.heading: Bindings

parameters.label: Attribute
parameters.description: Which attribute to bind. It is an error if it is missing, unless the optional flag is set. Present for Attributes.
parameters.heading: Bindings

parameters.label: Class
parameters.description: The type of the attribute. Not all bound attributes need to be the same type, or even come from the same geometry data. Present for Attributes.
parameters.heading: Bindings

parameters.label: Data Type
parameters.description: What sort of attribute to bind. Float and integer attributes are bound as single arrays containing all element values in order. Tuples are interleaved, ie, P will be bound as xyzxyzxyz. Array attributes are bound as two arrays. One array contains the offsets of each element's array data. Thus, the difference of a pair of offsets provides the elements array length. The second array is the data of all elements' arrays concatenated into a single array. Present for Attributes.
parameters.heading: Bindings

parameters.label: Tuple Size
parameters.description: Tuple size of the attribute to bind. If greater than zero, the attribute must be able to provide this tuple size. If zero, it will bind automatically and an extra parameter will be generated storing the tuplesize. Present for Attributes.
parameters.heading: Bindings

parameters.label: Precision
parameters.description: Controls the precision the data of this parameter is bound with. The Node option uses the node's precision, so will vary depending on its setting and the corresponding kernel code should use the fpreal or exint defines. This is the precision the data is stored on the video card so using lower precision can save GPU memory. 16-bit, which corresponds to half, often cannot be used for computation. The vload_half can be used to promote it to float for computation. If the same attribute ends up bound with different precisions it will fail the binding. Currently volumes only bind with 32bit data precision.
parameters.heading: Bindings

parameters.label: Read
parameters.description: Determines if the OpenCL kernel will read from this attribute or volume. If not set, the attributes values will not be copied onto the GPU. This is useful for write-only attributes as it avoids an unnecessary copy, but requires care as uninitialized data will be present.
parameters.heading: Bindings

parameters.label: Write
parameters.description: Determines if the OpenCL kernel will write back to this attribute or volume. Causes the CPU version of the attribute or volume to be marked out of date so the next time it is needed it will be copied back from the GPU.
parameters.heading: Bindings

parameters.label: Optional
parameters.description: Marks the attribute or volume as not necessary. If the attribute or volume isn't present in the geometry, rather than erroring, a #define is set in the kernel options to disable the attribute. This also changes the parameter signature, so the Generate Code button should be used to verify the syntax. NOTE: The parameter name is used in the #define, so changing the parameter name requires changing the code.
parameters.heading: Bindings

parameters.label: Default Value
parameters.description: Marks that if an optional attribute or volume is missing that a parameter value should still be bound to the kernel. A #define is set in the kernel options to disable the attribute and switch to the single value. This also changes the parameter signature, so the Generate Code button should be used to verify the syntax. The value of the bound parameter will be taken from the integer or float value of this parameter.
parameters.heading: Bindings

parameters.label: Value
parameters.description: The integer value used for integer parameters or default values.
parameters.heading: Bindings

parameters.label: Value
parameters.description: The float value used for float parameters or default values.
parameters.heading: Bindings

parameters.label: Value
parameters.description: The float2 value used for float2 parameters or default values.
parameters.heading: Bindings

parameters.label: Value
parameters.description: The float3 value used for float3 parameters or default values.
parameters.heading: Bindings

parameters.label: Value
parameters.description: The float4 value used for float4 parameters or default values.
parameters.heading: Bindings

parameters.label: Build BVH
parameters.description: Builds a bounding volume hierarchy around a triangle mesh with positions given by values of the bound attribute. You can use certain geometric proximity queries when this parameter is on (such as xyzdist and closest_idx functions). This is only available for 3D point or vertex attributes of a triangle mesh. Parts of the mesh that don't have triangle connectivity aren't visible to the geometric proximity functions.
parameters.heading: Bindings

parameters.label: Build Point BVH
parameters.description: Builds a bounding volume hierarchy over the points of the geometry, using positions given by values of the bound attribute. You can use nearest-point queries when this parameter is on (such as the nearpoint, nearpoints, and minpos functions). Unlike Build BVH, this needs no triangle connectivity, so it works on raw point clouds. This is only available for a 3D point attribute, and cannot be combined with Build BVH on the same binding.
parameters.heading: Bindings

parameters.label: Point BVH Mask Attr
parameters.description: An optional integer point attribute that restricts which points are added to the point BVH. Only points whose mask value is non-zero are included in the nearest-point queries. When left blank, every point is included.
parameters.heading: Bindings

parameters.label: Time Scale
parameters.description: How to scale the provided float value by the timestep. Because timeinc may not be known at time of parameter evaluation, it can be computed as a constant prior to evaluating the kernel and applied to the float value.
parameters.heading: Bindings

parameters.label: Context Option
parameters.description: The context option to bind, which directly binds block-iteration parameters to the kernel.
parameters.heading: Bindings

parameters.label: Data Type
parameters.description: The type of context option to bind. Integer: An ID context option. Float: A mono context option.
parameters.heading: Bindings

parameters.label: Display Code
parameters.description: Produces the fully expanded code that is sent to the actual compiler. This can resolve line numbers for errors when compilers do not respect the #line directive, and also help understand how the @-macros work. The exact expansion of @-macros should not be relied upon.
parameters.heading: Generated Code

parameters.label: Generated Code
parameters.description: The code snippet with all @-bindings expanded. NOTE: This parameter is not used but is purely informational.
parameters.heading: Generated Code

entries.label: Paint 3D
entries.summary: Paint on a COP layer or UV-mapped geometry.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The canvas type. For a metadata or RGBA signature the type of the paint output is RGBA. For a metadata canvas, RGBA (0,0,0,0) is used as the canvas color. Otherwise, for the Mono, UV, and RGB signatures the type of the paint output is the same as that of the canvas input, and 1 is used as the input alpha value.

parameters.label: Group
parameters.description: A group expression selecting surface primitives to paint on. Only this region of uvgeo is paintable, as texels outside this group remain unmodified.

parameters.label: Hide Rest
parameters.description: Shows only the region of uvgeo in the specified group. When off, visualize the entire uvgeo, regardless of what "Group" is set to.

parameters.label: FG Color
parameters.description: The color currently used for writing to a PaintLayer's color.

parameters.label: BG Color
parameters.description: An extra color that can be swapped with the foreground color in the viewer state. Swapping is bound to X by default in the viewer state.

parameters.label: FG Mask
parameters.description: The value currently used for writing to a PaintLayer's mask.

parameters.label: BG Mask
parameters.description: An extra value that can be swapped with the foreground mask value in the viewer state. Swapping is bound to X by default in the viewer state.

parameters.label: 2D Paint Mode
parameters.description: Whether to ignore the input geometry for visualization purposes. This is a way to switch from painting directly on the input 3D geometry to the 2D texturemap. By default, it's bound to F in the viewer state.
parameters.heading: Preferences

parameters.label: Stroke Alignment
parameters.description: How the stroke is positioned and oriented in 3D space while painting. Surface: A ray is repeatedly cast from the mouse position to the input geometry. Where it hits, a local coordinate system is constructed for each stamp, with the surface normal as Z, either the stroke direction or tangent vector most closely directed toward Up Direction as Y, and the cross product of these as X. Each stamp can thus be thought of as a rectangular prism centred on this local coordinate system, whose depth (along the Z axis) is determined by the Depth Falloff. Screen: Stamps are positioned along the screen-space stroke. For each stamp, a local coordinate system is constructed, with either the stroke direction or screenspace "up" as Y, the screen-space orthogonal direction as X, and the direction from the viewport camera toward the mouse's screenspace position as Z. Because there is no notion of depth, Depth Falloff doesn't apply in this mode and each stamp can be thought of as a rectangular pyramid extending to infinity.
parameters.heading: Preferences

parameters.label: Only Write to Visible
parameters.description: When on and stroke alignment is set to Surface, only texels visible by the viewport camera can be affected by viewer state paint operations.
parameters.heading: Preferences

parameters.label: Only Write to Visible
parameters.description: When on and stroke alignment is set to Screen, only texels visible by the viewport camera can be affected by viewer state paint operations.
parameters.heading: Preferences

parameters.label: Use Lazy Mouse
parameters.description: Whether to use the viewer state's lazy mouse feature. When on, instead of the brush cursor following the operating system pointer directly, it trails behind as if dragged by a string with a fixed length.
parameters.heading: Preferences

parameters.label: Lazy Mouse Radius
parameters.description: How far the brush cursor trails behind the OS pointer. This can be thought of as the length of the string attaching the brush cursor to the OS pointer, measured in viewport widths.
parameters.heading: Preferences

parameters.label: Write to Mask
parameters.description: Whether to write to the mask of the currently selected PaintLayer. This is typically toggled by clicking on either the color or mask thumbnail of a PaintLayer in the blend stack widget, in the Python panel.
parameters.heading: Preferences

parameters.label: Visualize Mask
parameters.description: Whether to visualize the mask of the writing layer. This shows the mask as a tinted overlay on top of the final blended texture. In the viewer state, this is bound to G by default.
parameters.heading: Preferences

parameters.label: Mask Tint
parameters.description: The color of the mask overlay used when Visualize Mask is on.
parameters.heading: Preferences

parameters.label: Mask Visibility
parameters.description: How visible the mask overlay is when Visualize Mask is on. To see only the mask, set this to 1. When set to 1, you may also want to set Mask Tint to white (1,1,1).
parameters.heading: Preferences

parameters.label: Up Direction
parameters.description: When stroke alignment is Surface and Orient to is set to Up Direction, this is the direction toward which to orient the Y (up) axis of each stamp before any rotation (static or dynamic) is applied.
parameters.heading: Preferences

parameters.label: Tile Symmetry
parameters.description: When painting a COP layer, whether to make paint applied near the edges of the canvas wrap around to the other side.
parameters.heading: Symmetry

parameters.label: Visualize Tile Symmetry
parameters.description: When painting a COP layer, whether to replace the canvas with a 3-by-3 grid for the purpose of visualizing how painted features wrap around the border of the canvas.
parameters.heading: Tile Symmetry

parameters.label: Reflection
parameters.description: Turns on 3D reflection symmetry.
parameters.heading: Tile Symmetry

parameters.label: Origin
parameters.description: The origin of the reflection plane.
parameters.heading: Reflection

parameters.label: Direction
parameters.description: The direction of the reflection plane.
parameters.heading: Reflection

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.description: The additional amount by which Origin is shifted along Direction.
parameters.heading: Reflection

parameters.label: Save Brush as Recipe
parameters.description: Save the current paint brush as a partial node preset recipe. The recipe becomes accessible as an entry in the Brush Catalog, which can be opened by clicking on the brush preview image in the Python panel.
parameters.heading: Paint

parameters.label: Brush Radius
parameters.description: When stroke alignment is Surface, this is the current size of the paint brush cursor. This can be adjusted in the viewer state by ((Ctrl + Shift + LMB)) drag or mouse wheel.
parameters.heading: Paint

parameters.label: Brush Radius
parameters.description: When stroke alignment is Screen, this is the current size of the paint brush cursor. This can be adjusted in the viewer state by ((Ctrl + Shift + LMB)) drag or mouse wheel.
parameters.heading: Paint

parameters.label: Opacity
parameters.description: A final opacity multiplier for each independent paint stroke. A paint stroke, regardless of dynamics, can't surpass this amount of alpha being added to the writing Paintlayer.
parameters.heading: Paint

parameters.label: Flow
parameters.description: A multiplier for the amount flow used by the paint brush. Flow is the rate at which alpha is added to the writing PaintLayer.
parameters.heading: Paint

parameters.label: Stroke Spacing
parameters.description: The space between adjacent stamps, measured in stroke widths. A value of 1 means stamps are touching end-to-end. A value of 0.5 means the left half of a stamp is completely overlapped by its left neighbor and its right half is completely overlapped by its right neighbor.
parameters.heading: Paint

parameters.label: Adjust Flow to Compensate for Spacing
parameters.label_norm: adjust flow to compensate for spacing
parameters.description: Adjusts the amount of flow to compensate for variable stroke spacing. When on, changing stroke spacing results in the overall alpha-applied-per-distance to remain constant, modulo quantisation due the starts and ends of stroke stamps.
parameters.heading: Paint

parameters.label: Rotation
parameters.description: A constant amount of rotation to apply to every stamp transform, after its local coordinate system is constructed according to the current stroke alignment.
parameters.heading: Paint

parameters.label: Orient to
parameters.description: When stroke alignment is Screen, this indicates whether to orient the stamp's Y (up) axis along the stroke direction or to match the screen space "up" direction.
parameters.heading: Paint

parameters.label: Orient to
parameters.description: When stroke alignment is Surface, this indicates whether to orient the stamp's Y (up) axis along the stroke direction or toward the specified Up Direction parameter as closely as possible. With surface alignment, stamps are always placed tangent to the surface at the brush cursor, so in most cases the world space up direction can't exactly be aligned to the stamp's up direction. However, there is typically a surface tangent direction most closely aligned with the worldspace up direction, which is what we use as the stamp up direction.
parameters.heading: Paint

parameters.label: Save Alpha as Recipe
parameters.description: Save the current brush alpha as a node partial node preset recipe. If a raster image is being used as the current alpha, the saved partial node preset recipe HDA contains the raster image embedded as an HDA section to avoid the possibility of a brush recipe becoming unlinked from the image used to create it. If the current alpha is procedural (circle or square), a low resolution image is still saved as part of the preset recipe and is used as a thumbnail to display the recipe in the Alpha Catalogue.
parameters.heading: Alpha

parameters.label: Shape
parameters.description: What kind of alpha image to use.
parameters.heading: Alpha

parameters.label: File
parameters.description: The file in which the alpha image is stored.
parameters.heading: Alpha

parameters.label: Catalog File (hidden)
parameters.description: The HDA section in which an alpha image is stored, when a recipe is loaded from the asset catalogue.
parameters.heading: Alpha

parameters.label: Soft Edge
parameters.description: When using the Circle or Square alpha shapes, this is the amount of feathering around the edges of each stamp. This parameter is forwarded to Stamp Point's Shape Falloff parameter.
parameters.heading: Alpha

parameters.label: Depth Falloff
parameters.description: When alignment is Surface, this is the amount by which each brush stamp extends in 3D space along its normal axis. When using Surface stroke alignment, for each brush stamp we construct a local coordinate system on the input geometry surface at the location of the brush cursor, using two surface tangents and the surface normal. Because the painted surface is typically not completely flat, we need a way to describe how much paint to apply to texels that don't lie directly on the stamp plane. Thus we compute a "Z alpha", a multiplier for the stamp's alpha based on its distance to the stamp plane. This multiplier is computed as smoothstep(-z_falloff, 0, -abs(z_distance)). This parameter is forwarded to Stamp Point's Z Falloff parameter.
parameters.heading: Alpha

parameters.label: Squish
parameters.description: The amount by which to shrink the alpha image along its horizontal axis. 0 means to leave unchanged. 1 means fully collapsed into a line with no area.
parameters.heading: Alpha

parameters.label: Use Flow Dynamics
parameters.description: Whether flow is a dynamics output (driven by dynamics).
parameters.heading: Flow Dynamics

parameters.label: Use Distance
parameters.description: Whether to multiply the flow by a value based on the screen-space accumulated stroke distance.
parameters.heading: Distance Input

parameters.label: Max Distance
parameters.description: The accumulated screen-space stroke distance (measured in viewport widths) at which this flow dynamics input multiplier reaches its final value. If Increase with Distance is on, that final value is 1. Otherwise, it is Min Flow Scale. Even when stroke alignment is Surface, the node measures the screen-space distance for this dynamics input.
parameters.heading: Distance Input

parameters.label: Min Flow Scale
parameters.description: The minimum value of this flow dynamics input multiplier.
parameters.heading: Distance Input

parameters.label: Increase with Distance
parameters.description: Whether this flow dynamics input multiplier increases or decreases as accumulated screens-space stroke distance increases. Min Flow Scale to 1, or 1 to Min Flow Scale.
parameters.heading: Distance Input

parameters.label: Use Pressure
parameters.description: Whether to multiply the flow by a value-based pen pressure.
parameters.heading: Pressure Input

parameters.label: Min Flow Scale
parameters.description: The minimum value of this flow dynamics input multiplier.
parameters.heading: Pressure Input

parameters.label: Increase with Pressure
parameters.description: Whether this flow dynamics input multiplier increases or decreases as pen pressure increases. Min Flow Scale to 1, or 1 to Min Flow Scale.
parameters.heading: Pressure Input

parameters.label: Use Random
parameters.description: Whether to scale the flow of each brush stamp by a random amount.
parameters.heading: Random Input

parameters.label: Random Scale
parameters.description: The amount by which each brush stamp's flow is randomised. 0 means no randomisation. A value of x means that each stamp's flow is multiplied by a number uniformly randomly selected between 1-x and 1+x. If the final flow surpasses 1, a flow of 1 is used instead.
parameters.heading: Random Input

parameters.label: Use Speed
parameters.description: Whether to scale the flow by a value based on the current stroke speed.
parameters.heading: Speed Input

parameters.label: Max Speed
parameters.description: The speed (measured in viewport widths/second) at which this flow dynamics input multiplier reaches its final value. If Increase with Speed is on, that final value is 1. Otherwise, it is Min Flow Scale. Even when stroke alignment is Surface, the node measures screen-space distance for this dynamics input.
parameters.heading: Speed Input

parameters.label: Min Flow Scale
parameters.description: The minimum value of this flow dynamics input multiplier.
parameters.heading: Speed Input

parameters.label: Increase with Speed
parameters.description: Whether this flow dynamics input multiplier increases or decreases as speed increases. Min Flow Scale to 1, or 1 to Min Flow Scale.
parameters.heading: Speed Input

parameters.label: Use Radius Dynamics
parameters.description: Whether brush radius is a dynamics output (driven by dynamics).
parameters.heading: Radius Dynamics

parameters.label: Use Distance
parameters.description: Whether to multiply the radius by a value based on the screen-space accumulated stroke distance.
parameters.heading: Distance Input

parameters.label: Max Distance
parameters.description: The accumulated screen-space stroke distance (measured in viewport widths) at which this radius dynamics input multiplier reaches its final value. If Increase with Distance is on, that final value is 1. Otherwise, it is Min Radius Scale. Even when stroke alignment is Surface, the node measures screen-space distance for this dynamics input.
parameters.heading: Distance Input

parameters.label: Min Radius Scale
parameters.description: The minimum value of this radius dynamics input multiplier.
parameters.heading: Distance Input

parameters.label: Increase with Distance

parameters.description: When on, the Sample tool samples the result of evaluating the full blend stack, to store as the new foreground color. When off, only the writing layer is sampled.
parameters.heading: Sample

parameters.label: Sample All Visible Layers
parameters.description: When on, the Fill tool uses the result of evaluating the full blend stack to determine which texels to floodfill based on the provided Threshold. When off, only the writing layer is used to determine the floodfilled area.
parameters.heading: Fill

parameters.label: Opacity
parameters.description: The fill operation applies a color to a group of flooded texels. It applies this color by performing an "over" blend, with this parameter's value as the opacity.
parameters.heading: Fill

parameters.label: Threshold
parameters.description: The maximum distance in Euclidean RGB-space at which floodfill proceeds from the color of the texel clicked on in the viewer state to every texel traversed while flood filling. Because the maximum distance between colors in an RGB cube is sqrt(3), this parameter is multiplied by this value to normalize the parameter to a 0,1 range. For example, if in the viewer state a red (1,0,0) texel is clicked and this parameter is set to x, floodfill proceeds so long as it can traverse texels whose color satisfies |(1,0,0) - (r,g,b)|_2 <= x/sqrt(3). This parameter is forwarded to Segment by Connectivity's Threshold parameter. To fill the entire writing layer with a single color, set this to 1 to ensure all texels get flooded.
parameters.heading: Fill

entries.label: Phasor Noise
entries.summary: Generates phasor noise, which resembles a wave pattern.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source outputs. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Type Info
parameters.description: The type information for the resulting layer. See Type info for more information.

parameters.label: Rotate Channel
parameters.description: When Signature is any channel except Mono, this is the amount to rotate the noise in the additional channels. Each layer is rotated by a different angle offset. When set to 0, the output image is equivalent to when the Signature is Mono. For example, when Signature is RGBA, the node generates four separate phasor noises that each have a unique rotation.

parameters.label: Amplitude
parameters.description: The amount by which to multiply the noise, which the node applies before the Center adjustment. For example, a value of 0.5 makes a pixel value of 0.5 become 0.25. NOTE: Layers can store negative numbers and values above 1, so this may result in out-of-bounds values. You can use a Clamp COP to enforce the range afterwards.
parameters.heading: Range

parameters.label: Center
parameters.description: The center of the output noise range, which offsets the pixel values. For example, a value of 0.5 makes a pixel value of 0.5 become 1.
parameters.heading: Range

parameters.label: Noise Contrast
parameters.description: The amount of contrast to apply to the noise before the Amplitude and Center parameters. You can use this parameter to make the noise more extreme without exceeding the 0 to 1 range.
parameters.heading: Range

parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: Sets the type of noise and, when set to Phasor Wave, the periodic function (wave type). Phasor Wave: Consists of the Sine, Rectangle, and Saw profiles. These provide consistent wave patterns across the entire surface. Phasor Noise: Defined by the Gabor Noise. It has a sharper shape than the Gabor Noise. Gabor Noise: The result of summing the phasor kernel values. This means overlapping kernel regions either amplify or cancel each other out. These overlapping areas create softened gray, ripple patterns. Intensity Field: The set of intensity values that define the Phasor Wave and Gabor Noise, which outputs soft ripple patterns with varying wave widths. This type can create more organic, natural-looking forms than the other noise types. When set to Phasor Wave, you can choose one of the following periodic functions Sine: Sets the periodic function as the sine function. This creates smooth contrast transitions between the top and bottom peaks. Rectangle: Sets the periodic function as a rectangular function. This creates distinct black-and-white regions, resulting in vivid, cartoon-like wave patterns. Saw: Sets the periodic function as a sawtooth function. This creates a linear contrast transition from the top to bottom peak, sharply emphasizing both extremes.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Element Size
parameters.description: The size of the wave's width in the noise. You can turn on the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button to adjust this further using the Element Scale parameter. WARNING: This parameter can output undesired results if you use values outside the 0 to 1 range.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Element Scale
parameters.description: When the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button is on, this is the per-axis scaling of the element size.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.description: The amount to offset the entire noise function in image coordinates.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Tile Size
parameters.description: The size of a single tile of noise. The noise periodically repeats in this size. The size is in image coordinates, so the default is for the entire default canoncial image. If you have a non-square image, this should match the aspect ratio. NOTE: If on, values for parameters like Element Size are rounded or clamped to make them valid. This is because these types of parameters must meet certain conditions for the noise to be tileable.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Wave Bias
parameters.description: When Type is Phasor Wave, this is the peak position of each periodic function. When a bias input is wired in, that value is used instead of the Wave Bias.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Blending Radius
parameters.description: The radius of the phasor kernels. Higher values increase the radius of the phasor kernels so they overlap more, while lower values decrease their radius so there is more space between each kernel.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.description: The seed that the random number generator uses. Change this parameter to generate a new position for the kernels.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Kernels
parameters.description: The number of disk-shaped local regions where the primary sine and cosine waves are defined.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Blur
parameters.description: The amount to blur the input image. Blurring results in a softened bias boundary.
parameters.heading: Bias

parameters.label: Strength
parameters.description: The strength of bias blending. When set to 0, this displays the original noise and doesn't apply bias blending.
parameters.heading: Bias

parameters.label: Blur
parameters.description: The amount to blur the input image. Blurring results in a softened scale boundary.
parameters.heading: Scale

parameters.label: Strength
parameters.description: The strength of scale blending. When set to 0, this displays the original noise and doesn't apply scale blending.
parameters.heading: Scale

parameters.label: 3D Noise
parameters.description: Evaluates the noise in a 3D space. Use these parameters to control the third dimension, while the first two dimensions are the location in the image.
parameters.heading: 3D Noise

parameters.label: Animate
parameters.description: Implicitly adds time to the third coordinate.
parameters.heading: 3D Noise

parameters.label: Pulse Length
parameters.description: The interval length (in seconds) of the noise's pulse in the third dimension. Lower values increase the rate at which the noise switches its appearance, while higher values decrease this rate.
parameters.heading: 3D Noise

parameters.label: Time Offset
parameters.description: The amount of time (in seconds) that's added to the start frame.
parameters.heading: 3D Noise

parameters.label: Time Scale
parameters.description: The amount of time (in seconds) by which to multiply the start frame. Higher values increase the rate at which the noise switches its appearance, while lower values decrease this rate.
parameters.heading: 3D Noise

parameters.label: Loop Length (sec)
parameters.description: This is the time (in seconds) at which to repeat the noise. This clamps other options to enforce periodic behavior. Turn this on to generate animations that seamlessly loop. When off, the animation generally doesn't repeat after any amount of time.
parameters.heading: 3D Noise

parameters.label: Rotate Pattern
parameters.description: The amount to rotate the phasor kernels. When Uniform, this sets a uniform initial angle for each phasor kernel. When Set Varying, this lets you set Rotation Varying to randomize the initial angle of each phasor kernel. NOTE: Each phasor kernel has a certain angle. As kernels are rotated, the noise pattern is rotated. Since kernel intersections change depending on the rotation, it behaves differently from a standard image rotation.
parameters.heading: Rotate

parameters.label: Rotation Varying
parameters.description: When Rotate Pattern is Set Varying, this is the randomized initial angle of phasor kernels. When set to 0, the value displays uniformed initial angles.
parameters.heading: Rotate

parameters.label: Use Secondary Rotation
parameters.description: Sets secondary phasor kernels at the same location of the initial phasor kernels.
parameters.heading: Rotate

parameters.label: Rotate Pattern
parameters.description: The amount to rotate the additional phasor kernels. When Uniform, this sets a uniform initial angle for each secondary phasor kernel. When Set Varying, this lets you set Rotation Varying to randomize the initial angle of each secondary phasor kernel.
parameters.heading: Rotate

parameters.label: Rotation Varying
parameters.description: When Rotate Pattern is Set Varying, this is the randomized initial angle of the secondary phasor kernels. When set to 0, the value displays uniformed initial angles.
parameters.heading: Rotate

parameters.label: NOTE
parameters.description: The node applies the post-processing operations in the order they're listed.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Fold
parameters.description: Sets the noise values to the absolute value. For example, a pixel value of -2 becomes 2. NOTE: This parameter doesn't impact the output when there's only positive values.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Complement
parameters.description: Sets the pixel value x to 1 - x. NOTE: This method works for values in the 0 to 1 range. For images outside of this range, using Complement results in negative or out of range values.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.description: The amount to pull the medium grey values (around 0.5) towards zero (if Bias is less than 1) or one (if Bias is greater than 1). A bias value of 0.5 doesn't affect the values. Image:/images/nodes/cop/postprocessing_bias.jpg
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Gain
parameters.description: The amount to pull the medium grey values (around 0.5) together, while values around 0 and 1 are pulled apart. A gain value of 0.5 doesn't affect the noise values. Image:/images/nodes/cop/postprocessing_gain.jpg
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Gamma
parameters.description: The overall gamma of the generated noise. Values greater than 1 increase the range of values in originally bright areas, which darkens the noise. Values less than 1 stretch out the range of values for originally dark areas, which increases the overall brightness of the noise.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Contrast
parameters.description: The amount to expand or shrink the overall range of tonal values. Each noise value is pushed towards (if Contrast is less than 1) or away from (if Contrast is greater than 1) medium grey values (around 0.5). NOTE: This is not the same as Noise Contrast, which appears in some noise nodes and applies contrast during the noise function.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Clamp Minimum
parameters.description: Clamps values below the specified threshold.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Clamp Maximum
parameters.description: Clamps values exceeding the specified threshold.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

entries.label: Planar Inflate
entries.summary: Inflates a 2D SDF into a height layer.

parameters.label: Height Scale
parameters.description: Controls the final height profile of the inflated region. Higher positive values create a fuller, more raised shape. Negative values invert the height direction.

parameters.label: Pre Scale
parameters.description: The base inflation amount before the height is solved. Higher values increase the strength of the inflation source.
parameters.heading: Inflate Features

parameters.label: Noise Scale
parameters.description: The amount of wrinkle and mound noise to add to the inflation source.
parameters.heading: Inflate Features

parameters.label: Use Wrinkle
parameters.description: Adds fine phasor-noise wrinkle detail to the inflated surface.
parameters.heading: Inflate Features

parameters.label: Size
