parameters.label: Remove Opaque Alpha Channels
parameters.description: Detects and removes opaque alpha channels when saving textures.
parameters.heading: Optimization

parameters.label: JPEG quality
parameters.description: JPEG Quality, integer from 10 to 100.
parameters.heading: Optimization

parameters.label: TIFF compression
parameters.description: Type of image compression to use in TIFF files. Possible values are "None", "LZW", "AdobeDeflate", "Deflate", "PackBits", "JPEG", "PixarLog", "SGILog", "SGILog24", "LZMA", "Zstd".
parameters.heading: Optimization

parameters.label: EXR Compression
parameters.description: Compression type for EXR format images. Possible values are "none", "rle", "zips", "zip", "piz", "pix", "b44", "b44a", "dwaa", "dwab".
parameters.heading: Optimization

parameters.label: DWA Compression Level
parameters.description: DWA compression level, integer from 1 to 500.
parameters.heading: Optimization

parameters.label: PNG/TGA Premultiplication
parameters.description: When R, G, and B are the pure color values of a pixel and A is its alpha, this determines whether the values are premultiplied or unpremultiplied. Premultiplied: Stores RGBA as RA,GA,BA,A. This option makes certain compositing operations easier and is how Copernicus interprets the values in RGBA layers by default. Unpremultiplied: Stores RGBA as R,G,B,A. If saving in PNG or TGA format, the RGB channels in an RGBA layer are first divided by A before writing out. Since these formats expect un-premultiplied pixel data, this makes them load correctly in other software.
parameters.heading: Optimization

parameters.label: Pre-Render Script
parameters.description: Run this script before any rendering.
parameters.heading: Optimization

parameters.label: Pre-Frame Script
parameters.description: Run this script before each frame.
parameters.heading: Optimization

parameters.label: Post-Frame Script
parameters.description: Run this script after each frame.
parameters.heading: Optimization

parameters.label: Post-Write Script
parameters.description: Run this script after each frame's data finishes writing to disk.
parameters.heading: Optimization

parameters.label: Post-Render Script
parameters.description: Run this script after all rendering.
parameters.heading: Optimization

entries.label: Sequence
entries.summary: Sequences parts of one or more inputs temporally.

parameters.label: Start Frame
parameters.description: Frame number to take from the input.
parameters.heading: Clips

parameters.label: Length in Frames
parameters.description: Length in frames to take from the input.
parameters.heading: Clips

parameters.label: Output Start Frame
parameters.description: The frame number to output the first clip starting at.
parameters.heading: Clips

entries.label: Scatter Shapes
entries.summary: Scatters input stamps across the image using randomization controls.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the node outputs. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Link Stamps
parameters.description: Makes the Stamps X and Stamps Y values equal.

parameters.label: Stamps X
parameters.description: The amount of stamps to scatter along the X-axis of the image.

parameters.label: Stamps Y
parameters.description: The amount of stamps to scatter along the Y-axis of the image.

parameters.label: Stamps
parameters.description: The amount of stamps to scatter along both the X and Y-axes of the image.

parameters.label: Scatter Seed
parameters.description: The seed value for all randomization that deals with stamp placement. This includes jitter, density, angle and direction, scale, and stretch.
parameters.heading: Scattering

parameters.label: Stamp Scaling
parameters.description: The way that the stamps scale in respect to the tile. Image: Makes all stamps conform to their original size relative to the image. Stretch to Tile: Makes all stamps squish or stretch to fit the tile.
parameters.heading: Scale

parameters.label: Scale Layer Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the scale input's mono value to mix in with the Image Scale or Tile Scale value, which impacts the stamps' scale. Higher values mix in more of the input's value. Lower values mix in less of the input's value.
parameters.heading: Scale

parameters.label: Scale Mode
parameters.description: The method of post-processing to apply to the scale of stamps. Uniform: No post-processing. Variance: Apply random variance to the scale. Min/Max: The minimum and maximum range of values that each stamp randomly picks from, and then multiplies against the original Image Scale or Tile Scale.
parameters.heading: Scale

parameters.label: Image Scale
parameters.description: Sets the scale of the stamps in image space.
parameters.heading: Scale

parameters.label: Tile Scale
parameters.description: Sets the scale of the stamps in tile space, where a value of 1 is one tile space and a value of 2 is two times a tile space.
parameters.heading: Scale

parameters.label: Scale Variance
parameters.description: The amount of random variance to apply to the scale. This is applied as a post-process. If Tile Scale is 1 and Scale Variance 1 for example, this represents a 100% range in sizes. This means the output stamps have a random scale from 0.5 * Scale to 2.0 * Scale.
parameters.heading: Scale

parameters.label: Min Value
parameters.description: The minimum value that the stamps can randomly select, and then multiply against the original Image Scale or Tile Scale. This is applied as a post-process.
parameters.heading: Scale

parameters.label: Max Value
parameters.description: The maximum value that the stamps can randomly select, and then multiply against the original Image Scale or Tile Scale. This is applied as a post-process.
parameters.heading: Scale

parameters.label: Jitter Layer Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the jitter input's UV value to mix in with the Jitter value, which impacts the random position offset. Higher values mix in more of the input's value. Lower values mix in less of the input's value.
parameters.heading: Jitter

parameters.label: Jitter Layer Strength
parameters.description: The amount by which to multiply the jitter input's UV value.
parameters.heading: Jitter

parameters.label: Post-Jitter
parameters.description: Sample the input layers such as scale, angle, using the stamps' position post-jitter.
parameters.heading: Jitter

parameters.label: Jitter
parameters.description: The amount of random position offset to add to each point's position on the grid.
parameters.heading: Jitter

parameters.label: Jitter Scale
parameters.description: When the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button is on, this is the per-axis scaling of the random position offset for the created stamps.
parameters.heading: Jitter

parameters.label: Angle Layer Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the angle input's mono value to mix in with the Angle value, which impacts the degree of the stamps' angles. Higher values mix in more of the input's value. Lower values mix in less of the input's value.
parameters.heading: Angle

parameters.label: Direction Layer Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the direction input's UV value to mix in with the Angle value, which impacts the direction of the stamps' angles. Higher values mix in more of the input's value. Lower values mix in less of the input's value.
parameters.heading: Angle

parameters.label: Angle
parameters.description: The angle in degrees to rotate each stamp. Use the dropdown menu to set the method of post-processing that applies to the angle of the stamps. Uniform: No post-processing. Variance: Apply random variance to the angles. Min/Max: The minimum and maximum range of values in degrees that each stamp randomly picks from, and then multiplies against the original angle.
parameters.heading: Angle

parameters.label: Angle Variance
parameters.description: The amount of random variance to apply to the angles. This is applied as a post-process. For example, a value of 30 makes each stamp have a random offset between -30 degrees and 30 degrees.
parameters.heading: Angle

parameters.label: Min Value
parameters.description: The minimum degree that the stamps can randomly select, and then multiply against the original Angle. This is applied as a post-process.
parameters.heading: Angle

parameters.label: Max Value
parameters.description: The maximum degree that the stamps can randomly select, and then multiply against the original Angle. This is applied as a post-process.
parameters.heading: Angle

parameters.label: Round to Multiples
parameters.description: Snaps all stamps to a specified angle. This is applied as a post-process.
parameters.heading: Angle

parameters.label: Stretch Layer Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the stretch input's UV value to mix in with the Stretch X and Stretch Y values, which impacts the XY scale. Higher values mix in more of the input's value. Lower values mix in less of the input's value.
parameters.heading: Stretch

parameters.label: Stretch Mode
parameters.description: The method of post-processing to apply to the non-uniform scale (stretch) of stamps. Uniform: No post-processing. Variance: Apply random variance to the scale of the X and Y-axes. Min/Max: The minimum and maximum range of values that each stamp randomly picks from, and then multiplies against the original Stretch X and Stretch Y.
parameters.heading: Stretch

parameters.label: Random per Component
parameters.description: Randomizes the Stretch Variance and Min/Max Value differently for each X or Y component.
parameters.heading: Stretch

parameters.label: Stretch X
parameters.description: The scale of the stamps along the X-axis that multiplies to the uniform scale.
parameters.heading: Stretch

parameters.label: Stretch Y
parameters.description: The scale of the stamps along the Y-axis that multiplies to the uniform scale.
parameters.heading: Stretch

parameters.label: Stretch Variance
parameters.description: The amount of random variance to apply to the scale of the X and Y-axes. This is applied as a post-process. If Stretch X is 1 and Stretch Variance is 1, 0 for example, this represents a 100% range in sizes. This means the output stamps have a random scale from 0.5 * Stretch X to 2.0 * Stretch X.
parameters.heading: Stretch

parameters.label: Min Value
parameters.description: The minimum value that the stamps can randomly select, and then multiply against the original Stretch X and Stretch Y. This is applied as a post-process.
parameters.heading: Stretch

parameters.label: Max Value
parameters.description: The maximum value that the stamps can randomly select, and then multiply against the original Stretch X and Stretch Y. This is applied as a post-process.
parameters.heading: Stretch

parameters.label: Density Layer Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the density input's mono value to mix in with the Density value, which impacts the rejection sampling. Higher values mix in more of the input's value. Lower values mix in less of the input's value.
parameters.heading: Density

parameters.label: Density
parameters.description: The amount of rejection sampling to apply to the created stamps. For example, a value of 0.8 means that each stamp has a 20% chance to disappear.
parameters.heading: Density

parameters.label: Blend Method
parameters.description: When mulitple stamps overlap, this controls how they blend together. Depth-Sorted Over: Post-sort the points by their depth. The farthest points are rendered first, so closer points paint over them. Since this has expensive internal operations, there's a performance loss. This is also unforgiving to partially transparent stamps. NOTE: When you wire in a sort input, that value is used instead. Unsorted Depth-Weighted Over: Apply a non-linear weighting that approximates depth-sorting without the need for sorting. NOTE: When you wire in a sort input, that value is used instead. Add: Add the overlapping pixel values of the stamps together. Subtract: Subtract the original pixel value from the new overlapping stamp's pixel value. This method works better when you're not subtracting from zero. Multiply: Multiply the overlapping pixel values of the stamps together. This method works better when the background starts at a non-zero value. Maximum: Compare the stamps along with the background color and use the maximum value. Minimum: Compare the stamps along with the background color and use the minimum value.
parameters.heading: Color and Blending

parameters.label: Use Sort Layer
parameters.description: Multiplies the Depth-Sorted Over or Unsorted Depth-Weighted Over sort values by the sort input's value.
parameters.heading: Color and Blending

parameters.label: Treat Mono as Alpha
parameters.description: Makes the expansion from mono to RGBA occur as GGGG, which means that a mono input as a stamp expanded to RGBA produces a darker than usual looking stamp. When off, the default for this node is to expand with GGG1, which means the resulting stamp doesn't look different.
parameters.heading: Color and Blending

parameters.label: Color Seed
parameters.description: The seed value for randomization that deals with stamp color and alpha.
parameters.heading: Color

parameters.label: Color Layer Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the color input's RGB value to mix in with the Stamp Color value, which impacts the stamps' tint. Higher values mix in more of the input's value. Lower values mix in less of the input's value.
parameters.heading: Color

parameters.label: Stamp Color
parameters.description: A tint for the stamp. Use the dropdown menu to set how the color applies to the stamps. Uniform: Apply the same color to each stamp. Variance: Apply random variance to the hue, saturation, and value of the stamps. Random from Ramp: Pick randomly from a color ramp. See Ramp parameters for more information.
parameters.heading: Color

parameters.label: Hue
parameters.description: The amount of random variance to apply to the hue. This is applied as a post-process. If set to 30 for example, the stamps randomly pick a hue offset from the range of 0 to 30.
parameters.heading: Color

parameters.label: Saturation
parameters.description: The amount of random variance to apply to the saturation. This is applied as a post-process. If set to 0.5 for example, the stamps randomly pick a saturation from the range of 0 to 0.5.
parameters.heading: Color

parameters.label: Value
parameters.description: The amount of random variance to apply to the value. This is applied as a post-process. If set to 0.5 for example, the stamps randomly pick a value from the range of 0 to 0.5.
parameters.heading: Color

parameters.label: Alpha Layer Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the alpha input's mono value to mix in with the Stamp Alpha value, which impacts the stamps' alpha. Higher values mix in more of the input's value. Lower values mix in less of the input's value.
parameters.heading: Alpha

parameters.label: Stamp Alpha
parameters.description: The amount of black (0) and white (1) by which to multiply the stamp's alpha. Use the dropdown menu to set how the alpha applies to the stamps. Uniform: Apply the same amount of alpha to each stamp. Variance: Apply random variance to the alpha of the stamps. Random from Ramp: Pick randomly from a mono ramp. See Ramp parameters for more information.
parameters.heading: Alpha

parameters.label: Alpha Variance
parameters.description: The amount of random variance to apply to the alpha. This is applied as a post-process.
parameters.heading: Alpha

parameters.label: Background Color
parameters.description: The initial background color of the space around the stamps.
parameters.heading: Background

parameters.label: Background Alpha
parameters.description: The initial background alpha of the space around the stamps.
parameters.heading: Background

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: The stamps to place in the image. When no stamps input is wired in, this parameter applies to the default star pattern. Cycle: Loop through all stamps in a repetitive cycle. Random: Randomly choose stamps based on the Select Seed. Layer Select: Use the select input to choose stamps. The parameter uses the first stamp when a pixel value is 0.0 and the last stamp when a pixel value is 1.0.
parameters.heading: Stamp Selection

parameters.label: Limit Selection
parameters.description: Limits the maximum number of stamps that the node uses.
parameters.heading: Stamp Selection

parameters.label: Select Seed
parameters.description: The seed value for random stamp selection.
parameters.heading: Stamp Selection

parameters.label: Grid Type
parameters.description: Grid: Regular Grid. Hexagonal: Offsets rows to make a hexagonal grid.
parameters.heading: Grid

parameters.label: Do Tiled
parameters.description: When enabled, the Grid Angle gets clamped to 90 degrees, and the Grid Offset and Scale are snapped to a divisor of the Stamps X or Y. For example, if your Stamps X was 10, your Grid Offset will snap to increments of 0.1, in order to not have a stamp cut off on the edge of an image.
parameters.heading: Grid

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: Grid Scale in image space.
parameters.heading: Grid

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.description: Grid Offset in image space.
parameters.heading: Grid

parameters.label: Angle
parameters.description: Grid Rotation in Degrees.
parameters.heading: Grid

entries.label: Sharpen
entries.summary: Sharpens an input layer to increase the definition of its edges.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information.

parameters.label: Units
parameters.description: The unit of measurement that the Blur COP in the node's subnetwork uses to determine the size of the sharpen effect's radius. Image: Use image space to configure the size of the sharpen effect's radius. Pixels: Use pixels to configure the size of the sharpen effect's radius.

parameters.label: Read Pixels outside Image
parameters.description: Adds contributions from pixels outside of the image. This depends on the border type, which determines what pixels to read as outside of the image.

parameters.label: Size
parameters.description: The size of the sharpen effect's radius in image space or pixels, which the Units parameter determines. Higher values expand the circumference of the radius to enhance the crispness of the sharpen effect. Lower values contract the circumference of the radius to add softness and remove the sharpen effect.

parameters.label: Scale Size
parameters.description: The amount to scale the sharpen effect's radius.

parameters.label: Amplitude
parameters.description: The amount by which to multiply the original layer's pixels by the unsharp mask. Higher values increase the sharpen effect, while lower values remove the sharpen effect.

parameters.label: Gain
parameters.description: The amount by which to multiply the brightness of the original layer's pixels. Set this parameter to 0 and Amplitude to a positive value to generate a high-pass filter.

parameters.label: Threshold
parameters.description: The difference in pixel value between the original layer and its unsharp mask that's required for the node to sharpen the layer. Higher values help remove high frequency noise that you might not want to sharpen.

entries.label: Slope Direction
entries.summary: Converts a height layer into a direction layer.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Space
parameters.description: The space in which to compute the slope. This affects the magnitude of the directions. This may also affect the directions themselves if pixels are anisotropically scaled in the provided space. Image: Compute the slope in image space, which normalizes the change in values by the image-space pixel size. Pixel: Compute the slope in pixel space, which normalizes the change in values by the pixel size. Local: Compute the slope in local space, which normalizes the change in values by the world-space pixel size.

parameters.label: Angle
parameters.description: After computing the slope direction, rotate it by this amount. By setting to 90 you will get directions that avoid going up slope and instead circumnavigate hills.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: Heights are often not to scale, so this adjusts the direction's magnitude globally to get into a useful value.

parameters.label: Read Pixels outside Image
parameters.description: Determine if derivatives at the boundary should read outside the image or restrict to the image range. Reading outside is useful for building seamless textures with wrap-mode. But restricting to the image range avoids artificial flattening of the derivative at the boundary in clamp modes, as it acts more like an extrapolation.

parameters.label: Kernel Size
parameters.description: Usually a derivative is computed with adjacent pixels, but if the values are slowly varying there may not be enough bit-detph to get smooth derivatives. This will expand the distance, in buffer elements, to compute the derivative, possibly removing stepping artifacts from the derivative.

entries.label: Solve Poisson
entries.summary: Solves Poisson's equation inside a 2D boundary.

parameters.label: Iterations
parameters.description: The number of solver iterations to perform. Higher values produce a more converged solution, but take longer to compute.

parameters.label: Boundary Blend
parameters.description: Blends between the Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions. A value of 0 uses Dirichlet boundary values, and a value of 1 uses Neumann boundary values. When the blend input is wired, that input overrides this parameter.

parameters.label: Iterations
parameters.description: The number of pre-conditioner iterations to perform during the solve. Higher values can improve convergence, but increase cook time.
parameters.heading: Pre-conditioner

parameters.label: Smoothing Iterations
parameters.description: The number of smoothing iterations to perform in the pre-conditioner. Higher values can improve the pre-conditioned approximation.
parameters.heading: Pre-conditioner

parameters.label: Coarsest Smoothing Iterations
parameters.description: The number of smoothing iterations to perform at the coarsest level of the pre-conditioner, in place of an exact coarse solve.
parameters.heading: Pre-conditioner

entries.label: Sphere Sample
entries.summary: Samples a layer onto a sphere.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Filter
parameters.description: The method used to sample the source layer. Point: Use the nearest pixel with no interpolation. Bilinear: Linearly interpolate between neighboring pixels. Box: Average pixels within a box filter. Bartlett: Use a triangular filter. Catmull-Rom: Use a sharper cubic filter. Mitchell: Use a smooth cubic filter with reduced ringing. B-spline: Use a smooth cubic B-spline filter.

parameters.label: Transform Order
parameters.description: The order in which the transform components are applied when Celestial Sphere is off. Scale Rot Trans: Apply scale, then rotation, then translation. Scale Trans Rot: Apply scale, then translation, then rotation. Rot Scale Trans: Apply rotation, then scale, then translation. Rot Trans Scale: Apply rotation, then translation, then scale. Trans Scale Rot: Apply translation, then scale, then rotation. Trans Rot Scale: Apply translation, then rotation, then scale.

parameters.label: Rotation Order
parameters.description: The order in which rotations around the X, Y, and Z axes are applied. Rx Ry Rz: Rotate around X, then Y, then Z. Rx Rz Ry: Rotate around X, then Z, then Y. Ry Rx Rz: Rotate around Y, then X, then Z. Ry Rz Rx: Rotate around Y, then Z, then X. Rz Rx Ry: Rotate around Z, then X, then Y. Rz Ry Rx: Rotate around Z, then Y, then X.

parameters.label: Celestial Sphere
parameters.description: Samples the source as a sphere at infinity. When on, only Rotate affects the sampled direction, and the mask is 1 everywhere.

parameters.label: Projection
parameters.description: The projection used to sample the transformable sphere when Celestial Sphere is off. Perspective: Cast rays from the camera through the output pixels. Orthographic: Cast parallel rays using the view direction.

parameters.label: Translate
parameters.description: Moves the sampled sphere in 3D space when Celestial Sphere is off.

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.description: Rotates the sampled sphere, in degrees.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: Scales the sampled sphere independently along each axis when Celestial Sphere is off.

parameters.label: Uniform Scale
parameters.description: Uniformly scales the sampled sphere when Celestial Sphere is off.

entries.label: Stamp Points
entries.summary: Stamps layers from point positions.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Background Color
parameters.description: The initial background color.
parameters.heading: Color

parameters.label: Background Alpha
parameters.description: The initial background alpha.
parameters.heading: Color

parameters.label: Stamp Color
parameters.description: A tint for the stamp.
parameters.heading: Color

parameters.label: Stamp Alpha
parameters.description: A scale for the stamped alpha. This is multiplied by both an Alpha and a blend attribute.
parameters.heading: Color

parameters.label: Shape
parameters.description: If a clipshape is not provided, this determines the shape of the stamp. If it is provided, it is treated as an SDF and the zero contour will determine the cut out shape. Square: A square. Circle: A perfect circle.
parameters.heading: Clipping

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: A uniform scale for the stamped values. This is multiplied by a pscale attribute.
parameters.heading: Clipping

parameters.label: Angle
parameters.description: An angle in degrees to rotate the stamps by. This is added to a spriterot for the final angle.
parameters.heading: Clipping

parameters.label: Shape Edge Filter
parameters.description: A filter-scale to apply for filtering the edge of the cutout of a stamped shape. Zero will make it all or nothing but result in aliasing, 1 will do the expected level of aliasing for the current resolution.
parameters.heading: Clipping

parameters.label: Shape Falloff
parameters.description: How much into the shape the falloff region should extend.
parameters.heading: Clipping

parameters.label: Space
parameters.description: The mode in which the transform attributes on the points input are interpreted: 2D or 3D. Image Space: Standard instancing attributes or sprite attributes on the pos input are used to position and orient sprites image space. This is a 2D operation and the resulting stamps are always of camera-facing textures with no perspective transform. World Space: Standard instancing attributes on the pos input are used to specify a 4x4 matrix describing a stamp-space to world-space projective coordinate transformation matrix (where the W component acts as a divisor), for each stamp. This matrix is inverted to derive a world-to-stamp matrix for each stamp. At every output pixel, we take the pixel's position (or use the position at the same image-space location in the pos position map for that pixel, if pos is wired) and transform that world-space position using each stamp's world-to-stamp matrix to get a 3D position coordinate in stamp-space. We sample the stamp at the (x,y) components of this coordinate.
parameters.heading: Options

parameters.label: Instancing Attributes
parameters.description: Attributes in Houdini can specify instancing either through sprite attributes, such as with the Sprite SOP, or through the standard copy and transform attributes. Automatic: Detect which attributes to use by what are present. If orient, transform, up and N, or up and v are present, the standard attributes will be used. Standard Instancing: Use the standard instancing attributes. These use the standard attributes such as orient and up to construct a transform for the point. This is then used to compute the proper spriterot and spritescale to match it. Sprite: Use the standard sprite attributes. This uses spriterot, spritescale, and spriteuv.
parameters.heading: Options

parameters.label: Up Axis
parameters.description: When converting standard instancing attributes, you must know which axis maps to "up" on the stamp.
parameters.heading: Options

parameters.label: Rotation from
parameters.description: Which axis is read out to determine the effective rotation, as they may not be consistent in the case of shears, etc.
parameters.heading: Options

parameters.label: Z Falloff
parameters.description: When Space is set to World Space, this is the Z-falloff for the stamp-space's depth (the Z coordinate). As the absolute value of this parameter approaches the Z-falloff, the alpha is multilplied by a factor that tends to 0. When 0, this effect is off (the Z-falloff becomes infinite).
parameters.heading: Options

parameters.label: Number of Stamps
parameters.description: The number of possible stamps to use. These are indexed from zero with the stamp attribute.
parameters.heading: Options

parameters.label: Filter Scale
parameters.description: The amount by which to multiply the pos input. Higher values indicate that the target pixels take up more world space. This means that when a stamp is applied on top of those target pixels, more pixels in the stamp have to be sampled to cover the footprint of every target pixel in stamp space.
parameters.heading: Options

parameters.label: Filter
parameters.description: The method used to sample the image. The default value is Box. See Filters for more information.
parameters.heading: Options

parameters.label: Blend Method
parameters.description: When mulitple stamps overlap, this controls how they blend together. Depth-Sorted Over: The points are pre-sorted by their depth. The farthest ones are rendered first, so closer points paint over them. Because this needs to sort this can be expensive. Unsorted Depth-Weighted Over: A non-linear weighting is applied that roughly approximates depth-sorting without the need for sorting. Add: The stamps add together. Subtract: Each stamp subtracts its value, likely requiring background to start non-zero. Multiply: Each stamp multiplies its value, likely requiring background to start non-zero. Maximum: The maximum of each stamp with the current background is used. Minimum: The minimum of each stamp with the current background is used.
parameters.heading: Options

parameters.label: Sort Stamps by Depth
parameters.description: Sorts the stamps based on their depth.
parameters.heading: Options

parameters.label: Wrap Mode
parameters.description: The wrapping behavior of the stamps. Auto: Wrap points outside of the main tile (whose size is controlled by Tile Size) back into the tile when the size_ref input image's Border type is Wrap. Off: Don't wrap the stamps. On: Wrap points outside of the main tile (whose size is controlled by Tile Size) back into the tile. This makes the main tile seamlessly repeat.
parameters.heading: Options

parameters.label: Tile Size
parameters.description: When Wrap Mode is Auto or On, this is the size (in image space) of the region to wrap into. The resultant image periodically repeats in this size.
parameters.heading: Options

entries.label: Star Glow
entries.summary: Streaks the layer multiple times in different directions to create a star effect.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information.

parameters.label: Threshold
parameters.description: Any pixel with a luminance value above this threshold has the star glow effect. This lets you apply star glow to only high luminance parts of your source layer. You can also use the effect input with this parameter to select where the effect happens. TIP: Click Smallicon:BUTTONS/layer_sample and then click on the layer to set the Threshold.

parameters.label: Width
parameters.description: The range (in image space) on both sides of the Threshold that determines the input minimum and maximum.

parameters.label: Border
parameters.description: The sampling behavior outside of the incoming layer's boundaries. Automatically uses the layer's border property. See Border types for more information.

parameters.label: Output Star Glow Only
parameters.description: Outputs only the star glow effect, which displays a preview of the effect. Turn this on if you want to make the star glow a separate AOV or configure the star glow further before you composite it on top of the source layer. TIP: Turn this parameter on and use the Blend COP to put the star glow effect back over the original image.

parameters.label: Streaks
parameters.description: The amount of streaks in the layer. Each new streak takes up a space in 360 degrees. A value of 2 means each streak is 180 degrees offset from each other. A value of 6 means each streak is 60 degrees offset from each other.
parameters.heading: Star Glow

parameters.label: Streak Length
parameters.description: The overall strength (in image space) of the streaks. Negative values follow the directions backwards when tracing.
parameters.heading: Star Glow

parameters.label: Brightness
parameters.description: The amount of brightness to apply to the star glow effect. Higher values increase the brightness to lighten and expand the star glow effect. Lower values decrease the brightness to dim and shrink the star glow effect.
parameters.heading: Star Glow

parameters.label: Angle
parameters.description: The degree by which to offset the direction of all streaks.
parameters.heading: Star Glow

parameters.label: Streak
parameters.description: The method used to combine the pixel values along the direction of distortion. Blur: Average the samples together. This smears the layer along the distortion direction. Max: Accept the largest value encountered along the trajectory. This is useful when adding edge roughness on an input shape.
parameters.heading: Star Glow

parameters.label: Streak Weight
parameters.description: This ramp acts as a multiplier on the pixel values when streaking. The left side of the ramp corresponds to the start of the trajectory. For example, when the Streak is Blur, the default linear ramp fades the pixels over their path. This makes the pixels more faint near the start. For more information about using ramps, see Ramp parameters.
parameters.heading: Star Glow

parameters.label: Combine Streaks with
parameters.description: The blending operation used to combine the streaks before they're added onto the original layer. The node doesn't add the combined streaks onto the original layer when Output Star Glow Only is on. Add: Adds the streaks together. Screen: Saturation adds the streaks together, similar to adding photographs. Hypot: Uses the length of the vector formed by the streaks' channels. Maximum: Uses the maximum of the streaks, per component. Difference: Uses the absolute difference between the streaks.
parameters.heading: Color

parameters.label: Color Mode
parameters.description: The method used to color the streaks. Uniform: Apply a singular color to all streaks. Ramp: Apply a ramp across each streak. When Streaks is set to 4 for example, the first streak takes position 0.0 and the final streak takes position 1.0 on the ramp.
parameters.heading: Color

parameters.label: Multiply with Original
parameters.description: Multiplies the selected color with the color of the pixels in the original layer. When off, the selected color replaces the original layer's color.
parameters.heading: Color

parameters.label: Color
parameters.description: The color to apply to all streaks.
parameters.heading: Color

parameters.label: Azimuth
parameters.description: The direction in degrees to cycle the ramp across each streak.
parameters.heading: Color

parameters.label: Color Ramp
parameters.description: The ramp to apply across each streak. See Ramp parameters for more information.
parameters.heading: Color

parameters.label: Aberration
parameters.description: Splits each streak into separate RGB streaks and composites them together. Each channel streak contributes to the final alpha when in RGBA mode.
parameters.heading: Aberration

parameters.label: Red
parameters.description: The amount (in degrees) to rotate the red channel by this angle. Higher values rotate the channel in a counterclockwise direction, which makes the offset between the channels more apparent. Lower values rotate the channel in a clockwise direction.
parameters.heading: Aberration

parameters.label: Green
parameters.description: The amount (in degrees) to rotate the green channel by this angle. Higher values rotate the channel in a counterclockwise direction, which makes the offset between the channels more apparent. Lower values rotate the channel in a clockwise direction.
parameters.heading: Aberration

parameters.label: Blue
parameters.description: The amount (in degrees) to rotate the blue channel by this angle. Higher values rotate the channel in a counterclockwise direction, which makes the offset between the channels more apparent. Lower values rotate the channel in a clockwise direction.
parameters.heading: Aberration

parameters.label: Glimmer
parameters.description: Applies noise to the streak lengths, which can create a subtle glimmering and shimmering effect.
parameters.heading: Glimmer

parameters.label: Glimmer Strength
parameters.description: The amount that the noise affects (multiplies against) the streak lengths.
parameters.heading: Glimmer

parameters.label: Glimmer Size
parameters.description: The size (in image space) of the basic element of the noise.
parameters.heading: Glimmer

parameters.label: Animate
parameters.description: Animate: Implicitly adds time to the third coordinate.
parameters.heading: Glimmer

parameters.label: Pulse Length
parameters.description: Pulse Length: The interval length (in seconds) of the noise's pulse in the third dimension. Lower values increase the rate at which the noise switches its appearance, while higher values decrease this rate.
parameters.heading: Glimmer

parameters.label: Time Scale
parameters.description: Time Scale: The amount of time (in seconds) by which to multiply the start frame. Higher values increase the rate at which the noise switches its appearance, while lower values decrease this rate.
parameters.heading: Glimmer

parameters.label: Loop Length (sec)
parameters.description: Loop Length (sec): This is the time (in seconds) at which to repeat the noise. This clamps other options to enforce periodic behavior. Turn this on to generate animations that seamlessly loop. When off, the animation generally doesn't repeat after any amount of time.
parameters.heading: Glimmer

parameters.label: Maximum Steps
parameters.description: The maximum number of steps taken in the streak. Higher streak lengths can cause gaps, so increase this parameter to fill these gaps.
parameters.heading: Advanced

entries.label: Streak Blur
entries.summary: Streaks an image, adding a motion blur effect.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. A value of 1 means this node uses only the new value. The default value is 1. See Mask for more information.

parameters.label: Border
parameters.description: The sampling behavior outside of the incoming layer's boundaries. Automatically uses the layer's border property. See Border types for more information.

parameters.label: Direction Type
parameters.description: Whether the streak angle is specified directly as an angle or through polar coordinates.

parameters.label: Angle
parameters.description: Specifies the streak direction (0 is horizontal, 90 vertical).

parameters.label: Direction
parameters.description: Specifies the streak direction in polar coordinates (1 0 is rightwards, 0 1 is upwards). If normalize direction is off, these will be multipled by the length to provide the effective length.

parameters.label: Normalise Direction
parameters.description: Whether to multiply the length by the magnitude of the direction vector to provide the effective length.

parameters.label: Units
parameters.description: Sets the effect's area units. Image: Sets the length to use units of the Image Space. Pixels: Sets the blur radius to use units of the number of pixels.

parameters.label: Length
parameters.description: Sets the length of the streaks according to the units set.

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.description: Determines how the streak is centered on the pixel creating the streak. To center the streak around the pixel, use 0. To make the streak end at the pixel, use -1 (the streak comes before the pixel that generates it). To make the streak begin at the pixel, use 1.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: The method used to combine the pixel values along the line. Blur: Average the samples together. This smears the image along the distortion direction. Min: Accept the smallest value encountered along the trajectory. This is useful when eroding an input shape. Max: Accept the largest value encountered along the trajectory. This is useful when adding edge roughness on an input shape.

parameters.label: Use Streak Weight
parameters.description: Weight the samples encountered along the path. Use Streak Weight to weaken the values over the trajectory.

parameters.label: Streak Weight
parameters.description: When Use Streak Weight is on, this ramp acts as a multiplier on the pixel values when streaking. The left side of the ramp corresponds to the start of the trajectory. For example, when the Mode is Blur, the default linear ramp fades the pixels over their path. This makes the pixels more faint near the start. For more information about using ramps, see Ramp parameters.

entries.label: Subnetwork
entries.summary: Used to organize a collection of COPs into one node.

parameters.label: Rename Wires Using Output Labels
parameters.description: When this toggle is enabled, name of each output wire is set based on its respective port label. Otherwise, wire names are propagated from inputs. Turn this option on if you'd like to discard incoming wire names and harden new ones for the downstream network to use.

parameters.label: Inputs
parameters.description: Controls the number of inputs exposed on this subnetwork node.

parameters.label: Input Label
parameters.description: Label of the respective input port.

parameters.label: Input Type
parameters.description: Type of the respective port. This parameter affects the subnetwork's signature and thus the types of data that can be plugged into it.

parameters.label: Outputs
parameters.description: Controls the number of outputs exposed on this subnetwork node.

parameters.label: Output Label
parameters.description: Label of the respective output port.

parameters.label: Output Type
parameters.description: Type of the respective port. This parameter affects the subnetwork's signature and the type of data that flows out of this port.

entries.label: Swirl
entries.summary: Twists an image layer into a spiral shape.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Wrap Mode
parameters.description: The wrapping behavior of the deformation at the boundary. Auto: Inherits the wrap mode setting from the input layer. Off: Clamps deformation at the boundary. On: Wraps deformation at the boundary.

parameters.label: Filter
parameters.description: The filter used to sample the source layer when the swirl deformation reads between pixels. See Filters for more information.

parameters.label: Tile Size
parameters.description: The size of the base deformation region.

parameters.label: Parameter Mode
parameters.description: Set whether to use the uniform or random parameters. Uniform: Use the uniform parameter controls. Random: Activate random variation for parameters, which the standard deviation controls. This adds natural variation when applying the effect to multiple swirl centers.

parameters.label: Translation
parameters.description: The amount in image space to translate the deformation regions.
parameters.heading: Uniform controls

parameters.label: Strength
parameters.description: The strength with which to apply the spiral deformation. Positive values create a counterclockwise spiral and negative values create a clockwise spiral.
parameters.heading: Uniform controls

parameters.label: Bulge
parameters.description: The amount of deformation to apply along radial directions from the center. This produces lens distortion deformation.
parameters.heading: Uniform controls

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: The radius of the deformation, which defines the actual distance from each swirl's center in image space.
parameters.heading: Uniform controls

parameters.label: Blend Region
parameters.description: The radius of the blended region between the deformed area and the background. This specifies the distance (in image space) from the boundary that the Radius parameter defines.
parameters.heading: Uniform controls

parameters.label: Inner Radius
parameters.description: The radius of the undeformed center region inside each swirl.
parameters.heading: Uniform controls

parameters.label: Inner Blend Region
parameters.description: The size of the blended region between the undeformed center and the swirled area.
parameters.heading: Uniform controls

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.description: The amount in degrees to rotate the areas that the Bulge and Strength parameters deform. This parameter allows for full control over the ellipses orientation.
parameters.heading: Uniform controls

parameters.label: Roundness
parameters.description: The elliptical shape of the deformation. A value of 1 produces a circular (disk-shaped) deformation. Values less than 1 create elliptical shapes, where the Y-axis is the semi-major axis and the X-axis is the semi-minor axis.
parameters.heading: Uniform controls

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.description: The seed used to generate the random numbers.
parameters.heading: Randomize

parameters.label: Activate Position Random
parameters.description: Enables random offsets for swirl center positions.
parameters.heading: Randomize

parameters.label: Central Position
parameters.description: The center point (mean) of the random position offsets.
parameters.heading: Randomize

parameters.label: Central Value
parameters.description: The center point (mean) of the randomized swirl parameters.
parameters.heading: Randomize

parameters.label: Scatter
parameters.description: The standard deviation of randomized parameter offsets.
parameters.heading: Randomize

parameters.label: Number of Points
parameters.description: The number of swirl centers, and therefore swirls.
parameters.heading: Swirl

parameters.label: Position #
parameters.description: The position of an individual swirl's center.
parameters.heading: Swirl

parameters.label: Strength Scale #
parameters.description: The amount to scale the strength of an individual swirl's center.
parameters.heading: Swirl

parameters.label: Bulge Scale #
parameters.description: The amount to scale the bulge of an individual swirl's center.
parameters.heading: Swirl

parameters.label: Radius Scale #
parameters.description: The amount to scale the radius of an individual swirl's center.
parameters.heading: Swirl

parameters.label: Blend Region Scale #
parameters.description: The amount to scale the blend region of an individual swirl's center.
parameters.heading: Swirl

parameters.label: Inner Radius Scale #
parameters.description: The amount to scale the inner radius of an individual swirl's center.
parameters.heading: Swirl

parameters.label: Inner Blend Region Scale #
parameters.description: The amount to scale the inner blend region of an individual swirl's center.
parameters.heading: Swirl

parameters.label: Rotate Scale #
parameters.description: The amount to scale the rotation of an individual swirl's center.
parameters.heading: Swirl

parameters.label: Roundness Scale #
parameters.description: The amount to scale the roundness of an individual swirl's center.
parameters.heading: Swirl

parameters.label: Strength
parameters.description: The attribute name to use for the strength scale.
parameters.heading: Match Attributes Names

parameters.label: Bulge
parameters.description: The attribute name to use for the bulge scale.
parameters.heading: Match Attributes Names

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: The attribute name to use for the radius scale.
parameters.heading: Match Attributes Names

parameters.label: Blend Region
parameters.description: The attribute name to use for the blend scale.
