entries.label: Tile Pattern
entries.summary: Generates rectangular tiles for texture patterns.

parameters.label: Pattern Size
parameters.description: Controls the size of the pattern that tiles must cover. Usually this should be the size of the image.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Clip to Size
parameters.description: When Pattern Size is smaller than the image size, use this to control the tiles that have a centroid outside the given area.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Pattern Type
parameters.description: Sets various pre-defined pattern types. Choose Custom Pattern to create a new pattern. Use the menu to the right side of this parameter to control the amount of tiles in the selected pattern. Stack Bond: The tiles are laid directly on top of one another with all joints aligned Header Bond: The pattern is laid with the header course sitting halfway over the joints of the courses in the row below. Stretcher Bond: The pattern is laid with the stretcher course sitting halfway over the joints of the courses in the row below. Flemish Bond: Flemish bond is another traditional pattern where stretchers and headers are laid alternately in a single course. American Bond: American Bond also referred to as Common Bond is a variation of the running bond patterns with a course of full headers at regular intervals. Monk Bond: The monk bond is a variant of the Flemish bond and involves two stretchers between the headers in each course. The headers are centered over the joint between the two stretchers in the course below. English Bond: A course of stretchers alternates with a course of headers. The stretcher course is each time started with a three-quarter brick. Double English Bond: The pattern is made up of two alternating courses between headers and stretchers. Windmill: Windmill Pattern requires a square tile enclosed by four rectangular tiles that are double the size of the square. The repetition results in a grid-like look. Cross Hatch: In each tile lines are placed at an angle to one another. Basketwave: Groups of warp and weft threads are interfaced so that they form a simple criss-cross pattern. Hopscotch: Hopscotch is a modular tile pattern that is laid in a specific arrangement with two sizes of square tiles. French Pattern: French Pattern or Versailles Pattern is a modular interlocking pattern that is reminiscent of a stone floor from the historic European palaces. Custom Pattern: Provides controls to create a custom pattern. The overall pattern is generated by defining tiles for the first row, which is located at the bottom of the pattern. The defined tiles repeat horizontally until they fill the row. You can also define multiple rows, and each row also repeats vertically until they fill the pattern.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: Controls the mode by which to define the number of tiles in the pattern. Seamless: Using the Divisions parameter the generated pattern is always tileable. A pattern that can be repeated seamlessly along a surface, creating the illusion of a larger and more detailed material. Tile Count: In this mode, the size of the tiles are calculated based on the Rows and Columns parameters. Tile Size: In this mode, Tile Width and Tile Height provide direct control over the size of the tiles.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Divisions
parameters.description: When Seamless mode is selected, it controls the size of the tiles making up the pattern.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Rows
parameters.description: When Tile Count mode is selected, it controls the number of rows in the pattern.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Columns
parameters.description: When Tile Count mode is selected, it controls the number of columns in the pattern.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Tile Width
parameters.description: When Tile Size mode is selected, it controls the horizontal size of the tiles.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Tile Height
parameters.description: When Tile Size mode is selected, it controls the vertical size of the tiles.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Iris
parameters.description: When Windmill is set, this controls the ratio between the central square and the four surrounding tiles. Increase this value to make the central tile larger.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Row Divisions
parameters.description: When Cross Hatch is set, this controls the number of tile divisions where the tile is divided horizontally.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Column Divisions
parameters.description: When Cross Hatch is set, this controls the number of tile divisions where the tile is divided vertically.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Row Thickness
parameters.description: When Basketwave is set, this controls the thickness of the tiles oriented horizontally.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Column Thickness
parameters.description: When Basketwave is set, this controls the thickness of the tiles oriented vertically.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Draw Square Bonds
parameters.description: When Basketwave is set, this controls whenever to draw the square tiles between the waves.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Tile Count
parameters.description: When Herringbone N:1 or Herringbone 3:2 and Tile Count mode are selected, it controls the number of tiles in the pattern.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Tile Size
parameters.description: When Herringbone N:1 or Herringbone 3:2 and Tile Size mode are selected, it controls the size of the tiles.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: N
parameters.description: When Herringbone N:1 is set, this is the ratio that controls the thickness of the tile relative to the length. Increase this value to make the tiles thinner and elongated.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Flip Pattern
parameters.description: Flips the pattern 90 degrees.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Use Epxression
parameters.description: When this is off, the tile pattern is given by a nested multi-parameters. Turn this off to create the tile pattern using a custom tile expression.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Pattern Expression
parameters.description: Uses a special expression to define and repeat rows and columns until the pattern size is fully tiled. Each row is defined in a new line using the following format For Example Use the additional flags followed by a value for advanced pattern creation
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Visible
parameters.description: Sets the visibility of the row. Turn this off to hide the row.
parameters.heading: Number of Rows

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.description: Sets the vertical offset of the columns in the row.
parameters.heading: Row #

parameters.label: Reflect Block
parameters.description: When columns in the row need to be repeated, always start from the first entry or from the last.
parameters.heading: Row #

parameters.label: Slide Offset
parameters.description: Continuous offset for each row that is multiplied by the row number.
parameters.heading: Row #

parameters.label: Height
parameters.description: The vertical height of the columns in the row.
parameters.heading: Row #

parameters.label: Visible
parameters.description: Sets the visibility of the column. Turn this off to hide the column.
parameters.heading: Number of Columns

parameters.label: Width
parameters.description: The horizontal width of the column.
parameters.heading: Column #.#

parameters.label: Height
parameters.description: This will overwrite the height of the column in the row, ignoring Height.
parameters.heading: Column #.#

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.description: This will overwrite the vertical offset of the column in the row.
parameters.heading: Column #.#

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.description: The rotation of the column in the row.
parameters.heading: Column #.#

parameters.label: Shape Class
parameters.description: Shapes are organized into various groups. Basic shapes are consist of elementary algebraic shapes, while Marker and Compound contain shapes of various complexities.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Stretch Shape
parameters.description: Stretches the shape according to the tile ratio. Turn this off to not stretch the shape.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Basic Shapes
parameters.description: The list of available elementary algebraic shapes when Shape Class is set to Basic. See Basic Shapes for more information.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Markers
parameters.description: The list of available marker shapes when Shape Class is set to Marker. See Markers for more information.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Compound Shapes
parameters.description: The list of available complex shapes when Shape Class is set to Compound. See Compound Shapes for more information.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: The radius of the circle. Use this parameter to control the size of the circle.
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes

parameters.label: Arc
parameters.description: When turned on, and the value is less than 1, the circle becomes an open arc, which can be used to create shapes of a sliced pie.
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes

parameters.label: Thickness
parameters.description: When turned on, and the value is less than 1, the circle becomes hollowed, which can be used to create ring-like shapes.
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes

parameters.label: Round Ends
parameters.description: When both Arc and Thickness are turned on, use this to make the end of the ring shape rounded.
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes

parameters.label: Quadratic Circle
parameters.description: When turned on, the circle changes into a quadratic circle shape.
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes

parameters.label: Size
parameters.description: Controls the horizontal and vertical size of the diamond shape.
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes

parameters.label: Length
parameters.description: Sets the length of the line, which is oriented horizontally at the center. Turn on Use Points next to this parameter if you need to control the exact positions for the start and end points of the line.
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes

parameters.label: Start Point
parameters.description: Sets the horizontal and vertical position for the start point of the line.
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes

parameters.label: End Point
parameters.description: Sets the horizontal and vertical position for the end point of the line.
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes

parameters.label: Add Thickness
parameters.description: When turned on, the start and end thickness of the lines can be controlled by Start Thickness and End Thickness.
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes

parameters.label: Start Thickness
parameters.description: The thickness of the line at the start point.
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes

parameters.label: End Thickness
parameters.description: The thickness of the line at the end point.
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes

parameters.label: Bulge
parameters.description: When turned on, controls the thickness at the center of the line. A value of 0 means no bulging. In this mode, only Start Thickness is on to control the same thickness at both ends of the line.
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes

parameters.label: Size
parameters.description: Controls the horizontal and vertical size of the rectangle shape.
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes

parameters.label: Round Corners
parameters.description: When turned on, controls the roundness of the corners. With a value of 1 and both horizontal and vertical size is equal, the shape becomes a circle. When this is set to 0, the rectangle is not rounded. Use Separate Controls next to this parameter to control the roundness for each corner separately.
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes

parameters.label: Separate Controls
parameters.description: When turned on, the roundness of each corner can be controlled separately.
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes

parameters.label: Top Left
parameters.description: Controls the roundness for the top left corner of the rectangle. Value of 1 means the corner is rounded to the maximum, and the value of 0 means that the corner is not rounded.
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes

parameters.label: Top Right
parameters.description: Controls the roundness for the top right corner of the rectangle. Value of 1 means the corner is rounded to the maximum, and the value of 0 means that the corner is not rounded.
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes

parameters.label: Bottom Left
parameters.description: Controls the roundness for the bottom left corner of the rectangle. Value of 1 means the corner is rounded to the maximum, and the value of 0 means that the corner is not rounded.
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes

parameters.label: Bottom Right
parameters.description: Controls the roundness for the bottom right corner of the rectangle. Value of 1 means the corner is rounded to the maximum, and the value of 0 means that the corner is not rounded.
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: The size of the radius for the polygon shape.
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes

parameters.label: Number of Sides
parameters.description: Controls the number of sides for the polygon. The larger the number the more the shape will resemble a circle.
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: The size of the radius for the spiral shape.
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes

parameters.label: Arc Bend
parameters.description: Controls how much each arc length segment should bend towards the center. When this value is set to 0 and the Number of Arcs is set to 4, the arc is a perfect circle.
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes

parameters.label: Number of Arcs
parameters.description: Controls the number of components the spiral is made of. When Arc Bend is set to 0, a value of 4 creates a perfect circle.
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: The size of the radius for a squircle, which is a shape intermediate between a square and a circle.
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes

parameters.label: Blend
parameters.description: Controls the shape of the squircle. The value of 2 creates a perfect circle. Values above this will blend the shape more into a square. A value of 1 creates a diamond shape.
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: The size of the radius for the star shape.
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes

parameters.label: Number of Sides
parameters.description: Controls the number of sides for the star. The larger the number, the more the shape will resemble a circle.
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes

parameters.label: Angle Factor
parameters.description: Controls how much the center of the sides push towards the center of the shape. The angle factor of 2 will create a regular polygon shape instead of a star.
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes

parameters.label: Height
parameters.description: Controls the vertical height of the trapezoid.
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes

parameters.label: Bottom Length
parameters.description: Controls the horizontal length at the bottom of the trapezoid.
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes

parameters.label: Top Length
parameters.description: Controls the horizontal length at the top of the trapezoid.
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes

parameters.label: Width
parameters.description: Controls the horizontal length at the bottom of the triangle.
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes

parameters.label: Height
parameters.description: Controls the vertical height of the triangle.
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes

parameters.label: Use Points
parameters.description: When this is turned on, the three corners of the triangle are controlled by Point0, Point1 and Point2 parameters.
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes

parameters.label: Point 0
parameters.description: Controls the bottom left corner position of the triangle.
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes

parameters.label: Point 1
parameters.description: Controls the top corner position of the triangle.
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes

parameters.label: Point 2
parameters.description: Controls the bottom right corner position of the triangle.
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes

parameters.label: Arc
parameters.description: Controls the amount of distortion applied to the wave. Values closer to 0 will make the wave look like a flat line. The value of 0.5 closer resembles a sine wave, while a value of 1 will fold the wave pattern onto each other.
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes

parameters.label: Element Size
parameters.description: Controls the size of the wave pattern. Lower values will make smaller patterns.
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes

parameters.label: Size
parameters.description: The radius of the marker. Use this parameter to control the size of the shape.
parameters.heading: Markers

parameters.label: Width
parameters.description: Controls the horizontal width of the arch. Increase this value to make the shape wider.
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes

parameters.label: Height
parameters.description: Controls the vertical height of the arch. The value of 0 creates a half-circle.
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes

parameters.label: Length
parameters.description: Controls the overall length of the arrow, both shaft and head. After adjusting the length, use the Head Ratio to control the size of the head relative to the new arrow length.
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes

parameters.label: Use Points
parameters.description: When this is turned on, the start and end points of the arrow can be controlled by Start Point and End Point parameters.
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes

parameters.label: Start Point
parameters.description: Sets the horizontal and vertical position for the start point of the arrow.
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes

parameters.label: End Point
parameters.description: Sets the horizontal and vertical position for the end point of the arrow.
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes

parameters.label: Shaft Thickness
parameters.description: Sets the vertical thickness of the shaft of the arrow. Increase this parameter to make the shaft thicker.
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes

parameters.label: Head Thickness
parameters.description: Sets the vertical thickness of the head of the arrow. Increase this parameter to make the head thicker.
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes

parameters.label: Head Ratio
parameters.description: Sets the horizontal ratio between the head and the shaft of the arrow.
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes

parameters.label: Cross Size
parameters.description: Controls the overall size of the cross shape.
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes

parameters.label: Cross Inset
parameters.description: Controls the amount to chip away from the corners of a square. When this value is set to 0, the result is a perfect square. Increasing this value will chip away the shape starting from the corners of the square.
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes

parameters.label: Cross Bevel
parameters.description: Controls the amount of rounding at the inner corner of the cross.
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: The size of the radius for the egg.
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes

parameters.label: Roundness
parameters.description: Controls the roundness of the top edge of the egg. A value of 0 creates an egg shape with a sharp top edge, and increasing this value smooths the top edge. The value of 1 will create a perfect circle shape.
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes

parameters.label: Thickness
parameters.description: Controls the thickness of the fishscale shape. This shape is generally used for fishscale-like tile patterns.
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes

parameters.label: Size
parameters.description: The overall size of the horseshoe.
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes

parameters.label: Separation
parameters.description: Controls the arc length of the horseshoe. The value of 0 creates a perfect round shape, closing both ends of the horseshoe.
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes

parameters.label: Length
parameters.description: Controls the extent of each end of the horseshoe.
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes

parameters.label: Thickness
parameters.description: Controls the thickness of the horseshoe.
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes

parameters.label: Outter Radius
parameters.description: Controls the overall radius of the moon. For a generic moon shape, this parameter should be larger than Inner Radius.
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes

parameters.label: Inner Radius
parameters.description: Controls the radius of the shape that will be cut out from the body of the moon given by Outter Radius.
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes

parameters.label: Inner Offset
parameters.description: The horizontal position of the inner shape given by Inner Radius to control where to cut into the moon.
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes

parameters.label: Thickness
parameters.description: Controls the thickness of the octagon-dot shape. This shape is generally used for octagon-dot-like tile patterns.
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes

parameters.label: Size
parameters.description: Controls the overall size of the cross. The value of 0 creates a perfect circle.
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes

parameters.label: Thickness
parameters.description: Controls the thickness of the cross.
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: The size of the radius for the vesica.
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes

parameters.label: Roundness
parameters.description: Controls the vertical thickness of the vesica shape. Increasing this value makes the shape more rounded.
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes

parameters.label: Draw As
parameters.description: Controls how to draw the shape into the tile. Filled: The tile will be filled with a single value based on Tile Value. Distance: The shape will fade from the center towards the edges. The fading can be controlled using Fade Distance. Gradient: The shape will be drawn as a gradient ramp. Outline: Only the edges of the shape will be drawn as outlines.
parameters.heading: Drawing

parameters.label: Shape Edge Filter
parameters.description: A filter-scale to apply for filtering the edge of the cutout of a stamped shape. Zero will make it all or nothing but result in aliasing, 1 will do the expected level of aliasing for the current resolution.
parameters.heading: Drawing

parameters.label: Anti-Aliasing
parameters.description: When turned on, it reduces the jagged edges by smoothing the drawn shapes and outlines.
parameters.heading: Drawing

parameters.label: Fade Distance
parameters.description: When Draw As is set to Distance, this controls the distance from the edge, from which the zero edge value fades into the Tile Value towards the center.
parameters.heading: Drawing

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.description: When Type is set to Horizontal or Vertical, this is the rotation (in degrees) of the linear ramp.
parameters.heading: Drawing

parameters.label: Ramp Type
parameters.description: The type of ramp to generate. Horizontal: Ramp is linear type with points horizontally. Vertical: Ramp is linear type with points vertically. Radial: Ramp is circular with points extending radially. Concentric: Ramp is circular with points at varying distances from the center.
parameters.heading: Drawing

parameters.label: Gradient Ramp
parameters.description: Draws the shape as a gradient ramp. For more information about using ramps, see Ramp parameters.
parameters.heading: Drawing

parameters.label: Outline Width
parameters.description: Controls the thickness of the outline. Increase this value to create a thicker outline.
parameters.heading: Drawing

parameters.label: Filter
parameters.description: The method used to sample the image. The default value is Box. See Filters for more information.
parameters.heading: Stamping

parameters.label: Blend Method
parameters.description: When mulitple stamps overlap, this controls how they blend together. Depth-Sorted Over: The points are pre-sorted by their depth. The farthest ones are rendered first, so closer points paint over them. Because this needs to sort this can be expensive. Unsorted Depth-Weighted Over: A non-linear weighting is applied that roughly approximates depth-sorting without the need for sorting. Add: The stamps add together. Subtract: Each stamp subtracts its value, likely requiring background to start non-zero. Multiply: Each stamp multiplies its value, likely requiring background to start non-zero. Maximum: The maximum of each stamp with the current background is used. Minimum: The minimum of each stamp with the current background is used.
parameters.heading: Stamping

parameters.label: Randomize Stamp Order
parameters.description: Randomly varies the point order by which the points are stamped into the image. Change the value if the current variation is undesirable.
parameters.heading: Stamping

parameters.label: Tile Value
parameters.description: Controls the value of the shape inside the tile. Set Uniform to Set Varying on the right side of this parameter to randomize the value per tile.
parameters.heading: Value

parameters.label: Variation
parameters.description: The maximum allowed variation for the tiles. The value of 0 means no variation from Tile Value.
parameters.heading: Value

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.description: Controls random selection for variation. Change the value of the Seed if the current variation is undesirable.
parameters.heading: Value

parameters.label: Background Value
parameters.description: Controls the value outside of the shape.
parameters.heading: Value

parameters.label: Row Offset
parameters.description: Offsets the horizontal position of each tile with this amount.
parameters.heading: Position

parameters.label: Column Offset
parameters.description: Offsets the vertical position of each tile with this amount.
parameters.heading: Position

parameters.label: Row Slide Offset
parameters.description: Offsets each row horizontally with increasing amount based on the row number. This is used to create brick wall like patterns. To add further offset randomness to each row, change the menu on the right side of this parameter from Uniform to Set Varying.
parameters.heading: Position

parameters.label: Variation
parameters.description: Sets the maximum allowed row offset variation.
parameters.heading: Position

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.description: Controls random selection for variation. Change the value of the Seed if the current variation is undesirable.
parameters.heading: Position

parameters.label: Uniform Jitter
parameters.description: Controls the offset to move the points along the plane of grid. This is used to create positional randomness both horizontally and vertically for each tile.
parameters.heading: Position

parameters.label: Horizontal Jitter
parameters.description: Controls the offset to move the points horizontally along the plane of grid.
parameters.heading: Position

parameters.label: Vertical Jitter
parameters.description: Controls the offset to move the points vertically along the plane of grid.
parameters.heading: Position

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.description: Controls random selection for variation for Uniform Jitter, Horizontal Jitter and Vertical Jitter.
parameters.heading: Position

parameters.label: Rotate Pattern
parameters.description: Rotates the pattern based on the value in degrees.
parameters.heading: Rotate

parameters.label: Rotate Tile
parameters.description: Rotates each tile from its center in degrees.
parameters.heading: Rotate

parameters.label: Rotate Variation
parameters.description: Sets the maximum allowed variation in degrees. Rotated angles will be between Rotate Tile - Rotate Variation and Rotate Tile + Rotate Variation.
parameters.heading: Rotate

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.description: Controls random selection for variation. Change the value of the Seed if the current variation is undesirable.
parameters.heading: Rotate

parameters.label: Checkerboard Rotate
parameters.description: Rotates the tiles that the rotation alternates between 0 and 90 degrees.
parameters.heading: Rotate

parameters.label: Orient Tiles
parameters.description: Sets the orientation attribute for the tiles. This ensures that using Horizontal Scale and Vertical Scale always scale the right edge of the tiles. Especially when the pattern consists of tiles that are both longer than wider and wider than longer.
parameters.heading: Rotate

parameters.label: Uniform Scale
parameters.description: Sets the scale for the tiles. Set Uniform to Set Varying on the right side of this parameter to randomize the scale per tile. The amount of scale depends on the size of each tile. If you need to dilate the tiles with equal amounts use Inset instead.
parameters.heading: Size

parameters.label: Variation
parameters.description: Sets the maximum allowed variation. The value of 0 means that there is no variation from Uniform Scale.
parameters.heading: Size

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.description: Controls random selection for variation. Change the value of the Seed if the current variation is undesirable.
parameters.heading: Size

parameters.label: Horizontal Scale
parameters.description: Sets the horizontal scale for the tiles. Set Uniform to Set Varying on the right side of this parameter to randomize the scale per tile.
parameters.heading: Size

parameters.label: Variation
parameters.description: Sets the maximum allowed variation. The value of 0 means that there is no variation from Horizontal Scale.
parameters.heading: Size

parameters.label: Vertical Scale
parameters.description: Sets the vertical scale for the tiles. Set Uniform to Set Varying on the right side of this parameter to randomize the scale per tile.
parameters.heading: Size

parameters.label: Variation
parameters.description: Sets the maximum allowed variation. The value of 0 means that there is no variation from Vertical Scale.
parameters.heading: Size

parameters.label: Inset
parameters.description: Dilates the edges of the tiles regardless of the height or width of each tile. Set Uniform to Set Varying on the right side of this parameter to randomize the inset per tile.
parameters.heading: Size

parameters.label: Variation
parameters.description: Sets the maximum allowed variation. The value of 0 means that there is no variation from Inset.
parameters.heading: Size

parameters.label: By Tile Order
parameters.description: This menu controls the order by which the tiles are removed. If you turned on Row Offset or Column Offset or if you use a custom pattern, the first tile might not be the tile at the bottom left position. Default: The ordering of the tiles is unchanged. As Threshold increases more and more tiles are removed starting from the bottom left corner of the pattern. Reverse: The ordering of the tiles are reversed. As Threshold increases more and more tiles are removed starting from the top right corner of the pattern. Random: The tiles are randomized. Shift: The ordering of the tiles is unchanged. However, this method provides a control to shift the tile order.
parameters.heading: Tile Selection

parameters.label: Threshold
parameters.description: Controls the number of tiles to be removed. This is a normalized value, 0 does not remove any tiles, while the value of 1 removes all tiles in the pattern. Turn on Negate Selection on the right side of this parameter to reverse the selection.
parameters.heading: Tile Selection

parameters.label: Negate Selection
parameters.description: When turned on, instead of deleting anything selected, it will delete anything not selected.
parameters.heading: Tile Selection

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.description: When Random tile order is selected, controls random selection for variation. Change the value of the Seed if the current variation is undesirable.
parameters.heading: Tile Selection

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.description: When Shift tile order is selected, offsets the tiles that are removed.
parameters.heading: Tile Selection

parameters.label: Every Nth Tile
parameters.description: When this is turned on, deletes every (number of the parameter) tile. Turn on Negate Selection on the right side of this parameter to reverse the selection.
parameters.heading: Tile Selection

parameters.label: Every Nth Row
parameters.description: When this is turned on, deletes every (number of the parameter) row. Turn on Negate Selection on the right side of this parameter to reverse the selection.
parameters.heading: Tile Selection

parameters.label: Every Nth Column
parameters.description: When this is turned on, deletes every (number of the parameter) column. Turn on Negate Selection on the right side of this parameter to reverse the selection.
parameters.heading: Tile Selection

parameters.label: Checkerboard
parameters.description: The removal alternates across the pattern.
parameters.heading: Tile Selection

parameters.label: Split Tiles
parameters.description: When this is turned on, tiles can be split according to various rules.
parameters.heading: Split Tiles

parameters.label: Iterations
parameters.description: When this is turned on, tiles that already split have a chance to split again iteratively. This number controls the maximum number of times a tile can be split.
parameters.heading: Split Tiles

parameters.label: Area Threshold
parameters.description: When this is turned on, any tile that has an area smaller than this value will not be split. Use this parameter to limit splitting small tiles.
parameters.heading: Split Tiles

parameters.label: Split Treshold
parameters.description: Controls the number of tiles to be split. This is a normalized value, 0 does not split any tiles, while the value of 1 splits all tiles in the pattern.
parameters.heading: Split Tiles

parameters.label: Number of Splits
parameters.description: When a tile is selected for split, this controls the number of splits for a tile. Set Uniform to Set Varying on the right side of this parameter to randomize the number of splits per tile.
parameters.heading: Split Tiles

parameters.label: Variation
parameters.description: Sets the maximum allowed variation. The value of 0 means that there is no variation from Number of Splits. While the value of 1 means that a tile can split 1 or Number of Splits-1 times.
parameters.heading: Split Tiles

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.description: Controls random selection for variation. Change the value of the Seed if the current variation is undesirable.
parameters.heading: Split Tiles

parameters.label: Jitter Scale
parameters.description: Controls the split position of the tiles. Set Uniform to Set Varying on the right side of this parameter to further randomize the number of splits per tile.
parameters.heading: Split Tiles

parameters.label: Variation
parameters.description: Sets the maximum allowed variation. The value of 0 means that there is no variation from Jitter Scale.
parameters.heading: Split Tiles

parameters.label: Orient Ratio
parameters.description: Controls whenever the tiles should be split horizontally or vertically. The value of 0 means that all tiles are split horizontally, and the value of 1 means that all tiles are split 'vertically'. The value of 0.5 will split tiles both horizontally and vertically in equal ratio.
parameters.heading: Split Tiles

entries.label: Time Blend
entries.summary: Blends intraframe values for layers and VDBs.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Hold First Frame
parameters.description: Determines if the first frame should be clamped. If so, any evaluations before this frame value will instead evaluate at this frame value.

parameters.label: Hold Last Frame
parameters.description: Determines if the last frame should be clamped. If so, any evaluations after this frame value will instead evaluate at this frame value.

entries.label: Time Loop
entries.summary: Repeats input frame range to form a looping animation.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Frame Start
parameters.description: The frame to start the looping sequence at. Note in the output this frame number will be unchanged. Ie, if the loop starts at frame 10, then the output frame 10 will match the input frame 10; if you want the output sequence to start at frame 1 use a Time Shift COP.

parameters.label: Frame Length
parameters.description: The length of the sequence to loop, in frames.

parameters.label: Loop Type
parameters.description: How to loop the sequence. Cycle: When the frame length is reached, jump immediately back to the start frame. This is useful for extending already seamless sequences. Zig-Zag: When the frame length is reached, play backwards, creating a zig-zag play pattern. This will be technically seamless, but the direction of time will clearly reverse. Blend: A copy of the sequence is offset by half the length and blended in to hide the transition point.

parameters.label: Blend Shape
parameters.description: How to blend in the offset sequence. Linear: A harsh saw-tooth pattern is used for blending. Cosine: A smooth cosine curve is used for blending.

entries.label: Time Pack
entries.summary: Combines its input at multiple times into a cable.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: Relative: Uses a window that is relative to the requested frame (for example, you can bundle the previous, current, and next frames together). Absolute: Specify a start and end directly.

parameters.label: Method
parameters.description: When Method is set to By Frame, this is the frame number to cook the input on.

parameters.label: Range
parameters.description: The range to obtain from the input, relative, and specified in frames.

parameters.label: Range
parameters.description: The range to obtain from the input, absolute, and specified in frames.

parameters.label: Range
parameters.description: The range to obtain from the input, relative, and specified in seconds.

parameters.label: Range
parameters.description: The range to obtain from the input, absolute, and specified in seconds.

parameters.label: Step
parameters.description: The increment between samples, in frames.

parameters.label: Step
parameters.description: The increment between samples, in seconds.

parameters.label: Add Time As
parameters.description: Whether to add an indication of the sample number to the name as a Prefix or a Suffix.

entries.label: Time Shift
entries.summary: Cooks its input at a different time.

parameters.label: Method
parameters.description: Determines if the input should be cooked at a given frame number or time. Time is measured in seconds.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: Determines what mode the shift should operate in. In Absolute Shift you specify an 'origin' and a 'destination' frame (or time); in Relative Shift, you provide an offset in frames (or seconds), and in Custom you provide a value in frames (or seconds) that is designed to be driven directly by an expression.

parameters.label: Frame
parameters.description: When Mode is set to Custom, specifies the frame to pull from the input.

parameters.label: Frame
parameters.description: When Mode is set to Relative Shift, specifies the offset to apply to the clip. This offset is added to the requested frame to get the frame pulled from the input, so a negative offset will make the input be moved forward in time.

parameters.label: Shift from
parameters.description: When Mode is set to Absolute Shift, specifies an anchor for a frame that will be moved.

parameters.label: to
parameters.description: When Mode is set to Absolute Shift, specifies a new frame that the anchored frame will be moved to.

parameters.label: Integer Frames
parameters.description: Whether to round frame numbers back down to integers after other calculations are done.

parameters.label: Time
parameters.description: When Mode is set to Custom, specifies the time to pull from the input.

parameters.label: Time
parameters.description: When Mode is set to Relative Shift, specifies the offset to apply to the clip. This offset is added to the requested frame to get the frame pulled from the input, so a negative offset will make the input be moved forward in time.

parameters.label: Shift from
parameters.description: When Mode is set to Absolute Shift, specifies an anchor for a time that will be moved.

parameters.label: to
parameters.description: When Mode is set to Absolute Shift, specifies a new time that the anchored time will be moved to.

parameters.label: Clamp
parameters.description: Optional clamping of the Frame/Time value to retrieve. The choices are: None, Clamp to First (uses only the start frame/time value), Clamp to Last (uses only the end frame/time value), or Clamp to Both.

parameters.label: Start/End Frame
parameters.description: The frame values used to perform clamping. This parameter is available when Method is set to By Frame, and Clamp is not None.

parameters.label: Start/End Time
parameters.description: The time values used to perform clamping. This parameter is available when Method is set to By Time, and Clamp is not None.

entries.label: Triplanar
entries.summary: Generates a texture by projecting X, Y, and Z textures onto the position layer.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Normal Type
parameters.description: The type of the input normal. Signed (-1 to 1): The input normal layer ranges from -1 to 1 and likely comes from geometry. Offset (0 to 1): The input normal layer ranges from 0 to 1 and likely comes from a normal map.

parameters.label: Texture Source
parameters.description: The source of the output texture. Uniform Texture: Uses the texture input to generate the output texture. Texture Per Axis: Uses the X, Y, and Z texture inputs independently to compute the output texture.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: Adjusts the texture scale for the X, Y, and Z projections. A smaller scale value results in a larger tiling of the input texture, since the scale is applied directly to the texture coordinates.

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.description: Rotates the texture in the X, Y, and Z projection directions.

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.description: Adjusts the given texture offset in the X, Y, and Z projection directions.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: Adjusts the given texture scale in the X projection direction.

parameters.description: Rotates the given texture in the X projection direction.

parameters.label: Scale

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.description: Rotates the given texture in the Y projection direction.
parameters.heading: Per-axis Controls

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.description: Adjusts the given texture offset in the Y projection direction.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: Adjusts the given texture scale in the Z projection direction.

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.description: Rotates the given texture in the Z projection direction.

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.description: Adjusts the given texture offset in the Z projection direction.

parameters.label: Blend
parameters.description: Adjusts the blending between the X, Y, and Z coordinate projections. If each projection ramp isn't properly interpolated, visible seams may appear between the projected textures.

parameters.label: X-Z Blending
parameters.description: Adjusts blending between the X and Z projection directions. See Ramp parameters for more information.

parameters.label: Y Blend
parameters.description: Adjusts blending between the Y projection direction and the other projection directions. See Ramp parameters for more information.

parameters.label: Filter Scale
parameters.description: The amount to filter the input to avoid aliasing for non-identity UV maps. This value defaults to the size of the voxels. Increase or decrease the value to reflect the nature of the UV map.
parameters.heading: Sampling

parameters.label: Filter
parameters.description: The method used to sample the image. See Filters for more information.
parameters.heading: Sampling

entries.label: Triplanar Hex Tile
entries.summary: Seamless texturing and normal mapping of triplanar projections without visible repetitions.

parameters.label: Normal Type

parameters.label: Size

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: The global scale of hex tiles.

parameters.label: Scale Random

parameters.label: Rotate

parameters.label: Random Seed

parameters.label: Contrast

parameters.label: Falloff

parameters.label: Weight Exp

parameters.description: The offset texture in Y-projection.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: The scale texture in Z-projection.
parameters.heading: Per Axis Triplanar Controls

parameters.label: Rotate

parameters.label: Offset

parameters.heading: Per Axis Triplanar Controls

parameters.label: Blend

parameters.heading: Triplanar Blending

parameters.label: XZ Blend
parameters.description: Remaps triplanar blending in X and Z projections. See Ramp parameters for more information.

entries.label: Triplanar UV
entries.summary: Generates UVs in three orthogonal projections.

parameters.label: Normal Type
parameters.description: The type of the input normal. Signed (-1 to 1): The input normal layer ranges from -1 to 1 and likely comes from geometry. Offset (0 to 1): The input normal layer ranges from 0 to 1 and likely comes from a normal map.

parameters.label: Blend
parameters.description: The amount to smooth the projections' weights.

entries.label: Turing Patterns
entries.summary: Applies a filter to create Turing patterns.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. You can also set the RGBA channels to which you apply the effects of this node. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information. Toggle RGB: Turns the Red, Green, and Blue channels on and off. Red: Applies this node's effects to the Red channel. Green: Applies this node's effects to the Green channel. Blue: Applies this node's effects to the Blue channel. Alpha: Applies this node's effects to the Alpha channel.

parameters.label: Filter
parameters.description: Filter: The filter to blur the image with. See Filters for more information. Box: Creates a box around the pixel of which to take an average of. Gaussian (default): Take a weighted average of the pixels according to a Gaussian distribution.

parameters.label: Read Pixels outside Image
parameters.description: Read Pixels outside Image: Adds contributions from pixels outside of the image. This depends on the border type, which determines what pixels to read as outside of the image.

parameters.label: Units
parameters.description: Sets the units used for the parameters. Image: Sets the radius to use units of the image space. Pixels: Sets the radius to use units of the number of pixels.

parameters.label: Iterations
parameters.description: The amount of times to blur and sharpen the image.

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: The size of the blur effect's radius in image space or pixels.

parameters.label: Power
parameters.description: The amplitude of the sharpening. This is the brightness done between each iteration. Higher values expand and solidify the pattern.

parameters.label: Gain
parameters.description: The amount by which to multiply the brightness of the original layer's pixels.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: Scale Size: Scales the blur radius for a specific axis.

entries.label: UDIM Pack
entries.summary: Combines its input at multiple UDIMs into a cable.

parameters.label: UDIMs
parameters.description: The list of UDIMs to sample the input at. This list is comma-separated and you can use hyphens to specify a range of UDIMs. If this list is not activated it will use the default UDIM list from the COP Network.

parameters.label: Add UDIM As
parameters.description: Whether to add an indication of the UDIM to the name as a Prefix or a Suffix.

entries.label: UV Inverse
entries.summary: Computes the inverse of a UV distortion map.

parameters.label: Space
parameters.description: The space the distortion map is in. A Texture distortion map is stretched to 0..1 range. An Image distortion map is fit to the -1..1 range.

parameters.label: Polish Iterations
parameters.description: Each valid pixel on the uv map is used as a seed by mapping it into the image space. Polish iterations improve the quality of this mapping by iterating the forward/backward maps.

parameters.label: Diffuse Iterations
parameters.description: Often many pixels in texture space have no equivalent in image space; a smooth fill is used to fill the gaps. This controls the number of iterations used, increasing will improve the quality of intermediate mapping values.

entries.label: UV Shape
entries.summary: Generates UV coordinates for common 2D shapes.

parameters.label: Shapes
parameters.description: The shape used to generate the UV coordinates and mask. Disk: Generate UV coordinates inside a disk. Square: Generate UV coordinates for a folded square tile. Horseshoe: Generate UV coordinates for a horseshoe shape with a circular bend and straight arms. Spiral: Generate UV coordinates along a spiral band. Annulus: Generate UV coordinates inside a ring. Fishscale: Generate UV coordinates for repeating fishscale-shaped tiles.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: The mapping method to use for the disk shape. Linear: Stretch the disk to fit the square UV range. This is inexpensive, but creates more distortion along diagonals. Polar: Use the disk angle for U and radius for V. Equal Area: Preserve relative area while mapping the disk into the square UV range. Squircle: Use a squircle-based disk-to-square mapping with stable distortion near the axes. Elliptic Arc: Use an elliptic-arc grid to map the disk into the square UV range. Conformal: Preserve local angles as much as possible while mapping the disk into the square UV range.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: The mapping method to use for the square shape. Linear: Linearly map the folded square region into UV space. Conformal: Use an angle-preserving mapping for the folded square region.

parameters.label: Fold
parameters.description: How many symmetric folds to use for the square tile. 2-fold: Use a two-way diagonal fold. 4-fold: Use four symmetric folded regions around the center.

parameters.label: Vertex
parameters.description: The orientation of the central top vertex of the image to use for the linear square mapping. Top: Place the mapped vertex at the top. Left: Place the mapped vertex on the left. Right: Place the mapped vertex on the right.

parameters.label: Flip Tile Orientation
parameters.description: Flips the orientation of the folded square tile.

parameters.label: Spiral Type
parameters.description: The type of spiral curve to use. Archimedean: Use an Archimedean spiral, where the radius changes linearly with angle. Log: Use a logarithmic spiral, where the radius changes exponentially with angle. Loxodrome: Use a loxodrome-style spiral produced from a transformed logarithmic spiral by a Möbius transformation.

parameters.label: U Mode
parameters.description: How to compute the U coordinate along the spiral. Angle: Base U on the angle parameter of the closest point on the spiral. Arc Length: Base U on the arc length along the spiral.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: The mapping method to use for the annulus. Polar: Use angle for U and linear radius for V. Log: Use angle for U and logarithmic radius for V.

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: The radius of the disk shape.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: The method used to generate the fishscale pattern. Offset: Generate fishscales from offset disk tiles on a grid. Fill: Fill each fishscale cell by deforming a disk mapping into the fishscale shape.
parameters.heading: Fishscale

parameters.label: Disk Mode
parameters.description: The disk mapping method to use inside each fishscale cell. Linear: Stretch the disk to fit the square UV range. Polar: Use disk angle and radius. Eqaul-area: Preserve relative area while mapping the disk. Squircle: Use a squircle-based disk-to-square mapping. Elliptic Arc: Use an elliptic-arc grid mapping. Conformal: Preserve local angles as much as possible.
parameters.heading: Fishscale

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: The radius of the disk used to build the fishscale cells.
parameters.heading: Fishscale

parameters.label: Center Blend
parameters.description: In Fill mode, the width of the blend region near the center singularity.
parameters.heading: Fishscale

parameters.label: Center Blend Exponent
parameters.description: In Fill mode, shapes the blend near the center singularity.
parameters.heading: Fishscale

parameters.label: Do Tiled
parameters.description: In Offset mode, rounds the grid scale so the fishscale pattern tiles cleanly.
parameters.heading: Fishscale

parameters.label: Grid Scale
parameters.description: In Offset mode, the overall scale of the fishscale grid.
parameters.heading: Fishscale

parameters.label: Grid Size Type
parameters.description: Controls whether the grid scale uses a single uniform value or separate per-axis scaling. Per-Component Controls: Allows Grid Scale to scale the fishscale grid independently in each axis.
parameters.heading: Fishscale

parameters.label: Grid Scale
parameters.description: When Per-Component Controls is on, this is the per-axis scale of the fishscale grid.
parameters.heading: Fishscale

parameters.label: Size

parameters.label: Separation

entries.label: Wipe
entries.summary: Performs a wipe transition between two images.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. A value of 1 means this node uses only the new value. The default value is 1. See Mask for more information.

parameters.label: Amount
parameters.description: The amount of the Operation to apply. Higher values apply more of the b input to the Operation. Lower values apply less of the b input to the Operation. The default value is 0.5.

parameters.label: Operation
parameters.description: The transition operation that the node performs. Cross Dissolve: Blend each pixel from the a input into the b input. Per-Pixel Flip: Randomly switch pixels from the a input to the b input. Wipe (default): Use a moving or evolving shape to replace one image (a input) with the other (b input).

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.description: When Operation is set to Per-Pixel Flip, this is the random number seed to adjust the per-pixel flip behavior. This parameter lets you select the randomness for variation. The default value is 0.

parameters.label: Shape
parameters.description: When Operation is set to Wipe, these are shapes you can apply to the b input. If you wire in a shape input, that shape is used instead of this parameter. Line (default): A line moves across the overall image to switch between the two images. Higher Amount values increase how much of the b input's image covers the a input image. Lower Amount values decrease how much of the b input's image covers the a input image. Rectangle: The b input is a rectangle that grows out of the center of the overlapping images. Higher Amount values expand the image outwards in a rectangular shape to cover more of the a input image. Lower Amount values contract the image towards the center to cover less of the a input image. Circle: The b input is a circle that grows out of the center of the overlapping images. Higher Amount values expand the circumference of the image's radius to cover more of the a input image. Lower Amount values contract the circumference of the image's radius to cover less of the a input image. 4 Corner Shrink: The four corners of the b input are squares that grow out of the border towards the center of the overlapping images. Higher Amount values expand the image corners towards the center to cover more of the a input image. Lower Amount values shrink the image corners outwards from the center to cover less of the a input image.

parameters.label: Direction
parameters.description: When Operation is set to Wipe and Shape is set to Line, this is the orientation (in degrees) of the line shape. The default value is 0.

parameters.label: Filter Scale
parameters.description: The amount to scale the blended boundary between the two images (the boundary is blended to anti-alias the terminator). This is scaled to the image resolution, but you can lower this value for a sharper transition.

parameters.label: Line Width
parameters.description: When Operation is set to Wipe, this is the thickness (in image units) of the line drawn between the two inputs. The default value is 0.001.

parameters.label: Line Color
parameters.description: When Operation is set to Wipe, this is the color (including alpha) of the line drawn between the two inputs. The default value is 1, 1, 1, 1.

entries.summary: Generates Worley noise.

parameters.label: Type Info
parameters.description: The type information for the resulting layer. See Type info for more information.

parameters.label: Element Size
parameters.description: The size (in image coordinates) of the basic element of the noise. You can turn on the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button to adjust this further using the Element Scale parameter.

parameters.label: Element Scale
parameters.description: When the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button is on, this is the per-axis scaling of the element size for anistropic noise.

parameters.label: Jitter
parameters.description: The amount of random noise to add to each point's position on a grid. The random noise is added before the Worley noise measures the distance to the points. You can turn on the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button to adjust this further using the Jitter Scale parameter. NOTE: Values greater than 1 may produce artifacts because they jitter past the search radius.

parameters.label: Jitter Scale
parameters.description: When the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button is on, this is the per-axis scaling of the jitter.

parameters.label: Lattice Type
parameters.description: Worley noise is normally defined on a rectangular grid, forming square patterns. But it can be specified on a simplical grid, resulting in hexagonal base shapes.

parameters.label: Metric
parameters.description: The metric for computing the distance to a point. Euclidean: Use the length of the line segment between the two axial points to define the distance between the two points. This can result in circular shapes. See Euclidean distance for more information. Manhattan: Use the sum of the differences between the two axial points to define the distance between the two points. This can result in diamond shapes. See Taxicab geometry for more information. Chebyshev: Use the maximum difference between the two axial points to define the distance between the two points. This can result in square shapes. See Chebyshev distance for more information.

parameters.label: Round Border
parameters.description: The amount of smoothing to apply when computing the exact border distance for Euclidean Worley cells. Higher values round the border between neighboring cells. This parameter is only available when Metric is set to Euclidean.

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.description: The amount to offset the entire noise function in image coordinates.

parameters.label: Tile Size
parameters.description: The size of a single tile of noise. The noise periodically repeats in this size. The size is in image coordinates, so the default is for the entire default canoncial image. If you have a non-square image, this should match the aspect ratio. NOTE: If on, values for parameters like Element Size are rounded or clamped to make them valid. This is because these types of parameters must meet certain conditions for the noise to be tileable.

parameters.label: NOTE
parameters.description: The node applies the post-processing operations in the order they're listed.

parameters.label: Complement
parameters.description: Complement: Sets the pixel value x to 1 - x. NOTE: This method works for values in the 0 to 1 range. For images outside of this range, using Complement results in negative or out of range values.

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.description: Bias: The amount to pull the medium grey values (around 0.5) towards zero (if Bias is less than 1) or one (if Bias is greater than 1). A bias value of 0.5 doesn't affect the values. Image:/images/nodes/cop/postprocessing_bias.jpg

parameters.label: Gain
parameters.description: Gain: The amount to pull the medium grey values (around 0.5) together, while values around 0 and 1 are pulled apart. A gain value of 0.5 doesn't affect the noise values. Image:/images/nodes/cop/postprocessing_gain.jpg

parameters.label: Gamma
parameters.description: Gamma: The overall gamma of the generated noise. Values greater than 1 increase the range of values in originally bright areas, which darkens the noise. Values less than 1 stretch out the range of values for originally dark areas, which increases the overall brightness of the noise.

parameters.label: Contrast
parameters.description: Contrast: The amount to expand or shrink the overall range of tonal values. Each noise value is pushed towards (if Contrast is less than 1) or away from (if Contrast is greater than 1) medium grey values (around 0.5). NOTE: This is not the same as Noise Contrast, which appears in some noise nodes and applies contrast during the noise function.

parameters.label: Clamp Minimum
parameters.description: Clamp Minimum: Clamps values below the specified threshold.

parameters.label: Clamp Maximum
parameters.description: Clamp Maximum: Clamps values exceeding the specified threshold.

entries.label: Wrangle
entries.summary: Runs a VEX snippet to modify layer values.

parameters.label: Volumes to Write to
parameters.description: Only modify layers if their names match this pattern. The default pattern allows any layer to be modified. You can speed up the node by only listing layers that are _actually_ modified by the snippet. For example, in the following snippet, only the density layer is modified. The temperature layer is not modified, only read. {{{ #!vex @density = @temperature; }}} However, for obscure reasons, the node will both modify density and _copy_ temperature. This uses time and memory. To prevent this, you could set this parameter to density to prevent the node from copying temperature. Of course, this requires that you explicitly manage the list of writable layers.

parameters.label: Enforce Prototypes
parameters.description: Requires that you declare @ bindings in snippets as prototypes before using them. This applies to both attributes (for example @Cd) and "convenience" bindings such as @ptnum and @Frame. For example

parameters.label: Evaluation Node Path
parameters.description: VEX functions like ch() usually evaluate with respect to this node. Providing a path here can override where the path search starts from. This is useful for embedding in a digital asset where you would like the top level digital asset to be the search root.

parameters.label: Export Parameters
parameters.description: This pattern can be used to override the export option on the VEX shader to avoid writing to certain volumes. The pattern matches the VEX parameter, not the bound volume. The volume will still be bound for reading.

parameters.label: Rename Wires Using Output Labels
parameters.description: When this toggle is enabled, name of each output wire is set based on its respective port label. Otherwise, wire names are propagated from inputs. Turn this option on if you'd like to discard incoming wire names and harden new ones for the downstream network to use.

parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: The type of the input. Layer inputs will be bound to a volume of the provided name. Geometry inputs will become extra geometry inputs accessible by the Input Index. Mono: A Mono layer corresponding to a float volume. UV: A UV layer corresponding to a vector2 volume. RGB: An RGB layer corresponding to a vector volume. RGBA: An RGBA layer corresponding to a vector4 volume. ID: An ID layer corresponding to a int volume. Geometry: A geoemtry input that will be bound to a given internal input. Float VDB: A Float VDB input that will correspond to a float VDB. Vector VDB: A Vector VDB input that will correspond to a vector VDB. Integer VDB: An Integer VDB input that will correspond to a int VDB.

parameters.label: Re-Center
parameters.description: Distorts outwards from the center, producing a symmetric result. When off, this applies the sampling distortion from left to right.

entries.label: Bake Geometry Textures
entries.summary: Generates textures by baking between a low-resolution and high-resolution mesh at interactive speeds.

parameters.label: Tracer
parameters.description: The tracer to use. This is an automatic menu that shows only available options based on your hardware. NOTE: OptiX is only available on NVIDIA hardware.
parameters.heading: Tracer

parameters.label: Tracing Mode
parameters.description: The tracing mode that the baker utilizes. Surface Normal: Traditional baking by firing rays bidirectionally from the normals of the low-resolution geometry. Requires a low and high input. Cage Mesh: Use a cage mesh to help improve the texture maps. It's sometimes problematic to determine the direction of the rays from the low-resolution mesh to the high-resolution mesh. When you specify a cage mesh, rays are sent from the position on the cage mesh towards the corresponding position on the low-resolution mesh. When you bake with a cage, the cage must be entirely outside of the high-resolution mesh. NOTE: The low-resolution and cage mesh must have the same topology. Cage meshes are used only when the Tracing Mode is Cage Mesh. Single Mesh (low): Bakes the data of a single mesh, and uses the same mesh for the low-resolution and high-resolution mesh. Requires a low input.
parameters.heading: Tracer

parameters.label: UDIM Override
parameters.description: Select a UDIM to bake, which overrides the UDIM context option.
parameters.heading: Tracer

parameters.label: Face Visibility Culling
parameters.description: The method used to handle secondary rays that interact with the geometry. This can allow floaters on the geometry to be projected onto the low-resolution map without casting a shadow. No Culling: Don't ignore any secondary rays. Backface: Ignore any secondary rays that hit the backfaces of the geometry.
parameters.heading: Tracer

parameters.label: Sample Multiplier
parameters.description: The amount to multiply against the Sample parameters, such as Occlusion Samples and Thickness Samples. This acts as a general quality scale. For example, a Sample Multiplier of 0.5 and Occlusion Samples of 256 bakes occlusion at 128.
parameters.heading: Tracer

parameters.label: Auto Generate Cage
parameters.description: Creates a duplicate mesh of the low-resolution mesh. This automatically generates a cage mesh internally instead of requiring a cage input.
parameters.heading: Auto Generate Cage

parameters.label: Cage Offset
parameters.description: How far the duplicate mesh peaks out from the normals of the original low-resolution mesh.
parameters.heading: Auto Generate Cage

parameters.label: Soften Cage
parameters.description: Facets the geometry before applying the Cage Offset. A soft cage isn't faceted and ensures a seamless result across sharp edges, but can cause projection errors and skewed detail as the normals are averaged. An unsoftened cage (which is faceted) can fix this projection skewing, but can cause missing detail capture on sharp edges. TIP: A skew input can apply projection error fixes on the output maps. It works by creating a copy of the cage mesh, but averages and softens its normals by face area. The final ray directions are then blended between the original low-resolution normals and the softened normals based on this mono map.
parameters.heading: Auto Generate Cage

parameters.label: Normals
parameters.description: How the node deals with low-resolution geometry that's missing normals. For texture baking to work, the low-resolution mesh should have normals. Error if Low Res Mesh Missing Normals: Produces an error if no normal attribute is present. Warning if Low Res Mesh Missing Normals: Produces a warning if no normal attribute is present, but adds point normals weighted by vertex angle internally. Silently Create Missing Normals: Silently adds point normals weighted by vertex angle internally.
parameters.heading: Setup

parameters.label: Tangents
parameters.description: How the node deals with low-resolution geometry that's missing tangent attributes. For texture baking to work, the low-resolution mesh should have tangent attributes. Add MikkT Tangents if Needed: Adds MikkT tangents using a Polyframe SOP internally. Add Texture UV Tangents if Needed: Adds texture UV tangents using a Polyframe SOP internally. Error if No Tangent Attributes Present: Produces an error if tangent attributes are missing.
parameters.heading: Setup

parameters.label: UV Attribute
parameters.description: The attribute to use for UV unwrapping and rasterization. This can be a vertex or point.
parameters.heading: Advanced

parameters.label: Ray Bias
parameters.description: The amount to offset a ray's origin from the surface of the low-resolution mesh when rays are sent from the low-resolution mesh to the scene. You can use this parameter to arbitrarily offset the low-resolution mesh along its normal without having to define a cage mesh.
parameters.heading: Advanced

parameters.label: Match Pieces by Name
parameters.description: Lets you control which primitives are visible when computing ray tracing effects like occlusion and curvature. This matches primitives between the low-resolution and high-resolution geometry and isolates them in their own pocket dimension, which can be used to prevent intersection errors. If a ray hits an object that doesn't belong to the current matched piece, it's ignored. This causes a rebake and changes the bake results. NOTE: This parameter is internally known as Trace Sets.
parameters.heading: Match Pieces by Name

parameters.label: Piece Attribute
parameters.description: The primitive piece attribute to use to identify the different pieces across the low-resolution, high-resolution, and cage.
parameters.heading: Match Pieces by Name

parameters.label: Include Pieces
parameters.description: The sets to always include in the bake. This uses standard Houdini pattern matching.
parameters.heading: Match Pieces by Name

parameters.label: Exclude Pieces
parameters.description: The sets to always exclude from the bake. This happens after the include pieces are gathered. This uses standard Houdini pattern matching. For example, if your include is * but your exclude is hat, the baker bakes every set available except hat.
parameters.heading: Match Pieces by Name

parameters.label: Enable UV Boundary Filling
parameters.description: Fills empty areas of the image using colors at the edges of non-empty areas. This is a post-process that fixes darker pixel values at the edges of UV seams, and can produce better results when MIP-mapping the textures. NOTE: This process can be time consuming. For faster iterations, turn this feature on only for the final baking.
parameters.heading: Enable UV Boundary Filling

parameters.label: Exterior
parameters.description: The method used to set the pixels beyond the edge padding. Unchanged: Leave the pixels unchanged. Black: Set the pixels to black (0). Diffuse Fill: Run a Smooth Fill COP over the region, which smoothly interpolates the pixel values.
parameters.heading: Enable UV Boundary Filling

parameters.label: Edge Padding
parameters.description: The distance (in image coordinates) to directly copy pixel values into the exterior.
parameters.heading: Enable UV Boundary Filling

parameters.label: Edge Offset
parameters.description: When reading the original value to copy outwards for edge padding, the value exactly at the edge padding may already have exterior color incorporated. This is the distance (in image coordinates) to backtrack and read clean values for extrapolation.
parameters.heading: Enable UV Boundary Filling

parameters.label: Exclude Alpha from UV Fill
parameters.description: Turns off UV filling on the alpha map. Adding UV filling to alpha often results in a fully white output.
parameters.heading: Enable UV Boundary Filling

parameters.label: Normal Y Direction
parameters.description: Determines the direction of the Y value of the tangent space normal (or rounded normal) AOVs.
parameters.heading: Alignment

parameters.label: Tangent Normal
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the Tangent Normal map. When off, the normal output is a Null layer.
parameters.heading: Tangent Normal

parameters.label: Normal Space
parameters.description: The normal type the layer outputs as. The natural way to represent normals and how they're represented in geometry is to use signed normals. The red, green, and blue channel can store the x, y, and z components of the normal and range from -1 to 1. However, historically GPUs and photoediting software don't support negative ranges, so normal maps in image files are usually stored in an offset format where they have values from 0 to 1. Signed (-1 to 1): Signed normals where the x, y, and z components range from -1 to 1. Offset (0 to 1): Offset normals where the x, y, and z components range from 0 to 1.
parameters.heading: Tangent Normal

parameters.label: Rounded Edge Normal
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the Rounded Edge Normal map. When off, the edgenormal output is a Null layer.
parameters.heading: Rounded Edge Normal

parameters.label: Rounded Normal Space
parameters.description: The normal type the layer outputs as. The natural way to represent normals and how they're represented in geometry is to use signed normals. The red, green, and blue channel can store the x, y, and z components of the normal and range from -1 to 1. However, historically GPUs and photoediting software don't support negative ranges, so normal maps in image files are usually stored in an offset format where they have values from 0 to 1. Signed (-1 to 1): Signed normals where the x, y, and z components range from -1 to 1. Offset (0 to 1): Offset normals where the x, y, and z components range from 0 to 1.
parameters.heading: Rounded Edge Normal

parameters.label: Rounded Samples
parameters.description: The number of indirect rays used when computing Rounded Edge Normal. If the resulting AOV is noisy, increase Rounded Samples to reduce noise.
parameters.heading: Rounded Edge Normal

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: Whether to capture concave or convex edges in the rounded edge normal map.
parameters.heading: Rounded Edge Normal

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: The radius for the rounded normals.
parameters.heading: Rounded Edge Normal

parameters.label: Cusp Angle
parameters.description: Polygons that have an angle less than this threshold are assumed to be a smooth surface and not appear in the rounded normal map.
parameters.heading: Rounded Edge Normal

parameters.label: World Space
parameters.description: Whether to record the world space position in left or right handed space with Y or Z as the up axis.
parameters.heading: Alignment

parameters.label: World Normal
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the World Normal map. When off, the worldnormal output is a Null layer.
parameters.heading: World Normal

parameters.label: World Normal Space
parameters.description: How to represent the normal map. Signed (-1 to 1): Signed normals where the x, y, and z components range from -1 to 1. Offset (0 to 1): Offset normals where the x, y, and z components range from 0 to 1.
parameters.heading: World Normal

parameters.label: Position
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the Position map. When off, the position output is a Null layer.
parameters.heading: Position

parameters.label: Position Space
parameters.description: How to represent the position map. Absolute ( Use Actual Position Values ): The position isn't normalized and dependent on object size and world position. Relative ( Use Position Within Bounding Box): The position is normalized relative to its bounding box.
parameters.heading: Position

parameters.label: Bounding Box
parameters.description: When the Position is stored, this is how the position is represented. Fit to Bounding Box: The shading position is fit to the bounding box of the low-resolution mesh. Fit to Uniform Box (No Stretching): The shading position is fit to a uniform bounding box of the low-resolution mesh. In this mode, all three axes of the bounding box have the same length.
parameters.heading: Position

parameters.label: Ambient Occlusion
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the Ambient Occlusion map. When off, the occlusion output is a Null layer.
parameters.heading: Ambient Occlusion

parameters.label: Occlusion Samples
parameters.description: The number of indirect rays used when computing Occlusion. If the resulting AOV is noisy, increase Occlusion Samples to reduce noise.
parameters.heading: Ambient Occlusion

parameters.label: Max Distance
parameters.description: The maximum distance to consider when computing Occlusion. A small distance can speed up occlusion shading at the cost of accuracy.
parameters.heading: Ambient Occlusion

parameters.label: Curvature
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the Curvature map. When off, the curvature output is a Null layer.
parameters.heading: Curvature

parameters.label: Curvature Samples
parameters.description: The number of indirect rays used when computing Curvature. If the resulting AOV is noisy, increase Curvature Samples to reduce noise.
parameters.heading: Curvature

parameters.label: Curvature Scale
parameters.description: Controls the overall intensity or contrast of the curvature by amplifying the difference between convex and concave responses.
parameters.heading: Curvature

parameters.label: Max Distance
parameters.description: Smaller values (which create smaller distance) emphasize the concavity. Larger values (which represent greater distance) reveal more curvature and improve the visibility of the convex features.
parameters.heading: Curvature

parameters.label: Bias
