parameters.description: Controls whether the map looks more concave or more convex. Smaller values emphasize concavity, higher values enhance convexity.
parameters.heading: Curvature

parameters.label: Edge
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the Edge map. When off, the edge output is a Null layer.
parameters.heading: Edge

parameters.label: Edge Samples
parameters.description: The number of indirect rays used when computing Edge. If the resulting AOV is noisy, increase Edge Samples to reduce noise.
parameters.heading: Edge

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: The types of edges (concave or convex) to smooth.
parameters.heading: Edge

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: The radius of the rounded edge.
parameters.heading: Edge

parameters.label: Cusp Angle
parameters.description: Polygons with an angle below this threshold are considered smooth and don't appear in the Edge map.
parameters.heading: Edge

parameters.label: Cavity
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the Cavity map. When off, the cavity output is a Null layer.
parameters.heading: Cavity

parameters.label: Cavity Samples
parameters.description: The number of indirect rays used when computing Cavity. If the resulting AOV is noisy, increase Cavity Samples to reduce noise.
parameters.heading: Cavity

parameters.label: Max Distance
parameters.description: Limits how far rays can detect nearby geometry. Smaller values (smaller distance) emphasize concavity.
parameters.heading: Cavity

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.description: Blends between a full cavity contrast (0) and a flat result (1).
parameters.heading: Cavity

parameters.label: Thickness
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the Thickness map. When off, the thickness output is a Null layer.
parameters.heading: Thickness

parameters.label: Thickness Samples
parameters.description: The number of indirect rays used when computing Thickness. If the resulting AOV is noisy, increase Thickness Samples to reduce noise.
parameters.heading: Thickness

parameters.label: Invert Thickness Map
parameters.description: Inverts the Thickness map so that thinner areas create darker values and thicker areas create brighter values.
parameters.heading: Thickness

parameters.label: Height
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the Height map. When off, the height output is a Null layer.
parameters.heading: Height

parameters.label: Height Space
parameters.description: Height bakes the true displacement between the low-resolution and high-resolution. This distance may be miniscule so the output image can appear nearly entirely black, which may not be useful when used in masking or shaders so may require manual remapping later. Set this to Custom to remap the height map. True Displacement: True displacement values. These may be visually unfriendly results, and for some bake meshes appear completely black if the geometric difference between the low-resolution and high-resolution is small. Custom: Remap the height layer according to inner and outer distance parameters.
parameters.heading: Height

parameters.label: Inner Distance
parameters.description: Remaps the data within the height map from the inner distance to 0.0.
parameters.heading: Height

parameters.label: Outer Distance
parameters.description: Remaps the data within the height map from the outer distance to 1.0.
parameters.heading: Height

parameters.label: Alpha
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the Alpha map. When off, the alpha output is a Null layer.
parameters.heading: Alpha

parameters.label: Mask Out High Resolution Mesh
parameters.description: Checks for any valid hits on the high-resolution mesh and creates an alpha mask from this, rather than the low-resolution UV map.
parameters.heading: Alpha

parameters.label: Quick Setups
parameters.description: Add a geometry attribute to bake.
parameters.heading: Custom Attributes

parameters.label: Attribute Name
parameters.description: Turns on the Position map's baking, which bakes the world position values to the RGB components of the layer. When off, the position output is a Null layer.
parameters.heading: Custom Attributes

parameters.label: Attribute Name
parameters.description: The name of the attribute to rasterize. This must match the attribute present on the geometry. This can be a Point, Vertex, or Primitive.
parameters.heading: Custom Attributes

parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: The output type for the rasterized attribute. To be rasterized, an attribute must either be an integer or a float of four or less components. Mono: Mono layer for single float attributes. UV: UV layer for float2 attributes. RGB: RGB layer for float3 attributes. RGBA: RGBA layer for float4 attributes. ID: ID layer for integer attributes.
parameters.heading: Custom Attributes

entries.label: Block to Geometry
entries.summary: Compiles a block and produces its geometry representation.

parameters.label: Block End Node
parameters.description: The path to the Block End COP that's the final and closing node of the block that you want converted to geometry.

parameters.label: Input States
parameters.description: The input states seen during compilation. The compilation of the block takes into account which of the block inputs have concrete data flowing into them. All Connected: The compilation assumes all inputs exist. This option is useful for compiling blocks that run with all inputs bound. Network: The current network is compiled as is. In particular, only the Block Begin node ports with data plugged into them are treated as connected.

entries.label: Bokeh
entries.summary: Creates a Bokeh effect by expanding each pixel by an aperture shape.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Bokeh Map Filter
parameters.description: The aperture map can be filtered to give a higher quality Bokeh effect. See Filters for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. You can also set the RGBA channels to which you apply the effects of this node. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information. Toggle RGB: Turns the Red, Green, and Blue channels on and off. Red: Applies this node's effects to the Red channel. Green: Applies this node's effects to the Green channel. Blue: Applies this node's effects to the Blue channel. Alpha: Applies this node's effects to the Alpha channel.

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: The maximum radius of the bokeh effect, in pixels. This can be expensive for a large radius as a lot of scattering has to be done.

parameters.label: Bokeh Gain
parameters.description: The aperture mask is normalized so the Bokeh doesn't change the total brightness, but it can be useful to boost the result to gain or lose total luminance.

parameters.label: Bokeh Resolution
parameters.description: The aperture layer is resampled to this resolution. This speeds up filtering of the aperture layer to make sure high resolution apertures don't cause issues.

parameters.label: Normalize Gathered Light
parameters.description: The amount of light gathered by a pixel is normalized by the amount of pixels contributing to it. This avoids halos when transitioning between large and small bokeh regions; but doesn't preserve energy.

entries.label: Bounding Rectangle
entries.summary: Finds the bounding rectangle of a mask.

parameters.label: Inside Is
parameters.description: The values contained by the bounding rectangle. Below Threshold: All pixels below the threshold are in the final rectangle. Above Threshold: All pixels above the threshold are in the final rectangle.

parameters.label: Threshold
parameters.description: The value to compare with to determine if a pixel should expand the bounding rectangle. TIP: Click Smallicon:BUTTONS/layer_sample and then click on the layer to set the Threshold.

parameters.label: Inside Value
parameters.description: The output mask is set to this value inside the bounding rectangle.

parameters.label: Outside Value
parameters.description: The output mask is set to this value outside the bounding rectangle.

parameters.label: Geometry Units
parameters.description: The unit of measurement that the generated geoemtry's points represent. NOTE: If using the Crop COP, set this parameter to the same units specified on that COP. Image: The points represent image coordinates. Texture: The points represent texture coordinates. Pixel: The points represent pixel coordinates.

entries.label: Bright
entries.summary: Brightens a layer, VDB, or attribute.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. You can also set the RGBA channels to which you apply the effects of this node. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information. Toggle RGB: Turns the Red, Green, and Blue channels on and off. Red: Applies this node's effects to the Red channel. Green: Applies this node's effects to the Green channel. Blue: Applies this node's effects to the Blue channel. Alpha: Applies this node's effects to the Alpha channel.

parameters.label: Brightness
parameters.description: The scale factor to control how bright or dim the layer, VDB, or attribute is. Higher values increase the brightness. Lower values decrease the brightness. The default value is 1.

parameters.label: Tint Brightness
parameters.description: The tint (color) to apply to the Brightness of the layer, VDB, or attribute. The default value is 1, 1, 1.

parameters.label: Shift
parameters.description: The amount to increase or decrease the layer, VDB, or attribute's pixel value. Higher values increase the pixel value and overall brightness. Lower values decrease the pixel value and overall brightness. The default value is 0.

parameters.label: Tint Shift
parameters.description: The tint (color) to apply to the layer, VDB, or attribute's pixel value. The default value is 1, 1, 1.

parameters.label: Scale by Timestep
parameters.description: Adjust the brightness and shift amounts so they will occur over one second. This is a direct scale of shift; but is a more complicated operation on bright to ensure applying the scale repeatedly will get the same result.

entries.label: Cable Merge
entries.summary: Combines two cables into one cable.

parameters.label: Operation
parameters.description: The method used to combine the two input cables into one output. Union: The output cable contains every wire in the first cable, followed by every wire in the second cable that's not already in the first cable. Intersection: The output cable contains every wire that's in both cables. A wire's data comes from the first cable if it's present in both cables. Difference: The output cable contains every wire in the first cable that's not in the second cable. Copy: The output cable's structure matches the second cable. To form this cable, data is preferentially taken from the first cable. Wires that don't exist in the first cable instead carry data from the second cable. Full Union: The output cable contains every wire in the first cable, followed by every wire in the second cable. This is similar to Union, but doesn't avoid the duplication of wires. Rename: The output cable contains the first cable's data, but is named according to the wires of the second cable. If the second cable has fewer wires than the first cable, the output is truncated to that size.

entries.label: Cable Pack
entries.summary: Combines input layers into a cable.

parameters.label: Set Fields from Inputs
parameters.description: Autofills the Name parameters with the names from the connected inputs.

parameters.label: Name
parameters.description: The name of the respective wire in the output cable. The Set Fields from Inputs button populates this, but you can rename it.

entries.label: Cable Rename
entries.summary: Renames a cable's wires based on filters.

parameters.label: Filters
parameters.description: The number of filters to set, which the node sequentially runs.

parameters.label: Filter #
parameters.description: Applies the string replacement.

parameters.label: Use Regular Expressions
parameters.description: Uses extended regular expression syntax to replace the strings instead of Houdini's pattern replacement syntax.

parameters.label: Replace Every Occurrence
parameters.description: Replaces every occurrence of the specified pattern. By default, the node replaces only the first occurrence. For example, replacing foo with bar in foo_foo_foo yields bar_foo_foo when this is off and bar_bar_bar when this is on.

parameters.label: From
parameters.description: The string pattern to replace.

parameters.label: To
parameters.description: The replacement pattern for the string.

parameters.label: Add Wire Index
parameters.description: Adds a wire index.

parameters.label: Token Position
parameters.description: Set whether to add the wire index at the start or end of the wire name.

parameters.label: Index Offset
parameters.description: The amount to offset the wire index. The wire index starts at 0.

entries.label: Cable Sort
entries.summary: Sorts a cable's wires by name.

parameters.label: Reverse
parameters.description: Reverses the sorted cable. For example, a cable containing c, a, b, e is sorted to a, b, c, e and then reversed to e, c, b, a.

entries.label: Cable Split
entries.summary: Splits a cable based on filtering parameters.

parameters.label: Split by Pattern
parameters.description: Filters wires based on a name pattern.
parameters.heading: Split by Pattern

parameters.label: Name Pattern
parameters.description: The name pattern to filter by. This uses Houdini's pattern matching.
parameters.heading: Split by Pattern

parameters.label: Split by Type
parameters.description: Filters wires based on a data type.
parameters.heading: Split by Type

parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: The data type that the wire must match to come out of the matching output.
parameters.heading: Split by Type

parameters.label: Split by Range
parameters.description: Filters wires based on a set range. NOTE: A Start value of 0 and an End value of 1 includes wire 0 and wire 1, which are the first two wires of your cable.
parameters.heading: Split by Range

parameters.label: Select
parameters.description: Select every Nth wire in the cable. This selects every other wire by default.
parameters.heading: Split by Range

parameters.label: Start
parameters.description: The index of the first wire to include in the range.
parameters.heading: Split by Range

parameters.label: End
parameters.description: The index of the last wire to include in the range.
parameters.heading: Split by Range

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.description: The value to add to the wire index before computing whether the wire is within the selected range.
parameters.heading: Split by Range

parameters.label: Split by Chance
parameters.description: Filters wires based on probability.
parameters.heading: Split by Chance

parameters.label: Probability
parameters.description: The chance (percentage) that a wire comes out of the matching output. A value of 1 selects all the wires in the incoming cable.
parameters.heading: Split by Chance

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.description: The initial seed that determines which wires to include. Changing this value causes each wire to generate a new random value, which results in a new split.
parameters.heading: Split by Chance

entries.label: Cable Switch
entries.summary: Selects an input cable.

parameters.label: Select Input
parameters.description: The input to provide as the output. 0 outputs the first input cable and 1 outputs the second input cable.

entries.label: Cable Unpack
entries.summary: Extracts individual wires from a cable.

parameters.label: Set Fields from Input
parameters.description: Autofills the Fields parameters with the wires from the input cable.

parameters.label: Fields
parameters.description: The number of wires to extract.

parameters.label: Name
parameters.description: The name of the wire to extract. Use the dropdown menu to choose a specific wire from the input cable.

parameters.label: Index
parameters.description: The index of the wire to extract. The node uses this index to distinguish between wires with the same name. For example, the first instance of a Name has an Index of 0 and the second instance of that same Name has an Index of 1.

parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: The data type of the wire. This parameter affects the node's signature.

entries.label: Cache
entries.summary: Caches the input layers for faster playback.

parameters.label: Clear Cache
parameters.description: Erases all cached data to free memory and make sure new results are cooked.

parameters.label: Reload Playbar Range
parameters.description: Caches all frames over the current playbar range. This makes the frames able to playback at an increased speed. You don't need to first wait through a slower playback to build the cache.

parameters.label: Max Frames
parameters.description: The maximum number of frames to store in the cache. Lower values reduce the maximum memory usage, which increases the playback speed around key frames.

parameters.label: Clear Cache when Change Upstream
parameters.description: Autodetects upstream changes and clears the cache when nodes upstream change (except through usual time-based operations). Turn this off to make the cache sticky (persistent). This is useful when you want to create a flipbook of results before a change was made.

parameters.label: Output #
parameters.description: The name of the node output. If the name isn't blank, it's kept as a placeholder for future wiring even if you remove the corresponding wires.

entries.label: Camera from Points
entries.summary: Solves for intrinsic and extrinsic camera properties given a set of image-world correspondences.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: World Point Attribute
parameters.description: The point attribute on matches containing the world space coordinate of a point.

parameters.label: Image Point Attribute
parameters.description: The point attribute on matches containing the image space coordinate of a point.

parameters.label: Edit Intrinsics
parameters.description: Enable the use of known camera intrinsics.
parameters.heading: Camera Intrinsics

parameters.label: Focal Length
parameters.description: The camera focal length to use if this parameter is enabled. When disabled, the PnP solver will estimate this parameter with the assumption that the aperture is 2.
parameters.heading: Camera Intrinsics

parameters.label: Camera Center
parameters.description: The method used to set the projective center if this parameter is enabled. When disabled, the center is assumed to be at the image origin. Image Center: Manually set the image space coordinate of the projective center. Use Estimator: Use an orthocenter image estimator to recover the projective center of the image if it is unknown.
parameters.heading: Camera Intrinsics

parameters.label: Image Center
parameters.description: A vector specifying the image space coordinate of the projective center.
parameters.heading: Camera Intrinsics

parameters.label: Parallel Lines
parameters.description: Number of axis definitions.
parameters.heading: Camera Intrinsics

parameters.label: Line A#
parameters.description: The first line used to define an axis, defined by a start and end point in image coordinates.
parameters.heading: Camera Intrinsics

parameters.label: Line B#
parameters.description: The second line used to define an axis, defined by a start and end point in image coordinates.
parameters.heading: Camera Intrinsics

parameters.label: RANSAC Seed
parameters.description: The seed used to randomly select candidate point correspondences used to solve for a camera.
parameters.heading: Advanced Settings

parameters.label: RANSAC Iterations
parameters.description: The number of RANSAC loop iterations executed to solve for a camera. Increasing this can improve the accuracy of the solution.
parameters.heading: Advanced Settings

parameters.label: RANSAC Tolerance
parameters.description: The reprojection error tolerance used to determine if a camera solution is acceptable.
parameters.heading: Advanced Settings

parameters.label: Subset Mode
parameters.description: The method used to select the size of the subset of points which RANSAC should use to generate a candidate solution for the camera. By default, this node uses a fixed count of 7 point correspondences. Percentage of Input Points: Set the solver to use a percentage of the total point correspondences in matches. This is set in Percentage. Count: Set the solver to use as an absolute number of point correspondences. This is set in Count.
parameters.heading: Advanced Settings

parameters.label: Percentage
parameters.description: If enabled, this is the percentage of point correspondences used in the RANSAC solver. The percentage of selected points must evaluate to at least 7.
parameters.heading: Advanced Settings

parameters.label: Count
parameters.description: If enabled, this is the number of point correspondences used in the RANSAC solver. This number must be at least 7.
parameters.heading: Advanced Settings

parameters.label: PnP Reprojection Error
parameters.description: The reprojection error tolerance used to determine if a camera solution is acceptable when assuming camera intrinsics, which is required if the number of point correspondences is less than 7 but at least 3.
parameters.heading: Advanced Settings

parameters.label: Apply Estimated Intrinsics
parameters.description: Set the solved aspect ratio, aperture, and focal length on camera.
parameters.heading: Advanced Settings

entries.label: Camera Import
entries.summary: Creates a layer in a camera's space.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Camera
parameters.description: The object camera to put this layer in the view of. See Camera path syntax for more information.

parameters.label: Near
parameters.description: The near clipping plane for the layer.

parameters.label: Far
parameters.description: The far clipping plane for the layer.

entries.label: Channel Extract
entries.summary: Extracts a channel from a layer, VDB, or attribute.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the input accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Channel to Extract
parameters.description: The channel to extract from the input. If you specify a channel that's not in the input, the standard channel extension rules apply. The default value is 0, which corresponds to Red (x).

entries.label: Channel Join
entries.summary: Combines multiple Mono layers, VDBs, or attributes into one multichannel output.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The output layer, VDB, or attribute type to create. Extra input layers, VDBs, or attributes that the output type doesn't need aren't used. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Default Color
parameters.description: If an input channel is missing, it uses the corresponding channel of this default color. The default value is 0, 0, 0, 1.

entries.label: Checkerboard
entries.summary: Creates an alternating checker pattern.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The output layer type to create. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Rows
parameters.description: The number of rows to divide the overall checker pattern into. The default value is 8.

parameters.label: Columns
parameters.description: The number of columns to divide the overall checker pattern into. The default value is 8.

parameters.label: Even Color
parameters.description: The color to make the even squares. The default value is 1, 1, 1, 1.

parameters.label: Odd Color
parameters.description: The color to make the odd squares. The default value is 0, 0, 0, 0.

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.description: The location (in image space) of the checker pattern's center. The default value is 0, 0. TIP: Setting this parameter to smaller values makes the offset of the center more apparent. TIP: Click Icon:BUTTONS/layer_position_sample and then click a location in the image to set the Offset.

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.description: The amount to offset the x and y axis of the overall checker pattern that's proportional to the individual square's size. For example, set both values to 0.5 to shift the x and y axis of the pattern half a square size. The default value is 0, 0.

parameters.label: Tile Size
parameters.description: The size (in image space) of the squares to create. This determines the square size that repeats as a tile over the image space. The default value is 2, 2.

entries.label: Chladni Cymatic Patterns
entries.summary: Generates interference patterns that represent various vibration modes.

parameters.label: Output Mode
parameters.description: The method used to output the amplitude as a pattern. This provides a view of the dynamic effect that's not affected by time. Nodal Lines: Output the values below the Threshold as a smooth transition from white to black into the values above the Threshold. This simulates the effect of dust gathering in the unmoving parts of the plate, which creates a line art effect. Absolute Value: Output the absolute value of the wave's amplitude. This is similar to the inverse of the Nodal Lines output, but provides unmodified data to support more refined processing. Signed Value: Output the signed value of the wave's amplitude. This outputs negative values for areas where the nominal phase is inverted. The pattern isn't tiled because the sign switches between quadrants. NOTE: The nominal phase is when the maximum values of the superimposed vibrating waves are extracted.

parameters.label: Threshold
parameters.description: When Output Mode is Nodal Lines, this is the maximum Amplitude amount to output as white.

parameters.label: Smoothing Width
parameters.description: When Output Mode is Nodal Lines, this is the amount of Amplitude that applies a blur effect to the transition from white to black. Higher values increase the thickness of the blurring effect between the a and b waves to smooth the transition. Lower values decrease the thickness of the blurring effect between the a and b waves to sharpen the transition. This parameter can prevent harsh, aliased lines since it smooths transitions. NOTE: The smoothing width is the difference in amplitude values to smooth, so the amount of smoothing isn't consistent.

parameters.label: Amplitude
parameters.description: The amplitude of the primary (or a) wave. This value changes the range of the output, which scales the a and b waves.

parameters.label: Amplitude Ratio
parameters.description: The ratio of the a and b waves' amplitudes. Higher values apply more of the b wave to the overall pattern. Lower values apply more of the a wave to the overall pattern.

parameters.label: Frequency
parameters.description: The vertical frequency of the a wave and the horizontal frequency of the b wave. Higher values zoom outward to increase how often the a wave repeats vertically and the b wave repeats horizontally. Lower values zoom inward to decrease how often these waves repeat vertically and horizontally. This is the primary frequency.

parameters.label: Frequency Anisotropy
parameters.description: The horizontal frequency of the a wave and the vertical frequency of the b wave. Higher values increase how often the a wave repeats horizontally and the b wave repeats vertically. Lower values decrease how often these waves repeat horizontally and vertically. This is the secondary frequency scale for the waves and a logarithmic adjustment. Each unit difference doubles or halves the actual frequency.

parameters.label: Tile Size
parameters.description: The size (in image space) of the waves to create. This controls the distance over which the Frequency is measured, which determines the wave size that repeats over the image space. You can adjust this value to gain anisotropy over the entire effect.

entries.label: Color Correct
entries.summary: Adjusts colors in the image.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. You can also set the RGBA channels to which you apply the effects of this node. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information. Toggle RGB: Turns the Red, Green, and Blue channels on and off. Red: Applies this node's effects to the Red channel. Green: Applies this node's effects to the Green channel. Blue: Applies this node's effects to the Blue channel. Alpha: Applies this node's effects to the Alpha channel.

parameters.label: Treat RGBA as Premultiplied
parameters.description: Treats RGBA as premultiplied, which multiplies the red, green, and blue channels by the alpha channel.

parameters.label: Master
parameters.description: Applies the master adjustments to the combined image after the Shadow, Midtone, and Highlight color corrections.
parameters.heading: Master

parameters.label: Master Add
parameters.description: The amount to offset the incoming values. Positive values brighten the image and negative values darken the image. This affects the pixels of all values.
parameters.heading: Master

parameters.label: Master Mult
parameters.description: The amount to scale the incoming values. Values greater than 1 brighten the image, while values between 0 and 1 darken the image. This also affects pixels at the white point (value of 1).
parameters.heading: Master

parameters.label: Master Gamma
parameters.description: Take the incoming values to the specified power. Values greater than 1 often darken the image, while values between 0 and 1 brighten the image. This doesn't change pixels at the white or black points (values of 1 and 0, respectively).
parameters.heading: Master

parameters.label: Master Contrast
parameters.description: Adjust the pixels depending on how they compare to the middle gray value, which boosts the distance of each pixel from 0.5. Larger values increase this boosting effect. A value of 1 results in no adjustment and a value of 0 destroys any contrast in the image, producing 0.5 for every pixel.
parameters.heading: Master

parameters.label: Shadow
parameters.description: Adds the shadow component of the image to the final result. This component's weight is calculated as exp(-7*t^2), where t is the original color.
parameters.heading: Shadow

parameters.label: Midtone
parameters.description: Adds the midtone component of the image to the final result. This component's weight is calculated as exp(-7*(1-t)^2), where t is the original color.
parameters.heading: Midtone

parameters.label: Highlight
parameters.description: Adds the highlight component of the image to the final result. This component's weight is equal to 1-exp(-7*t^2)-exp(-7*(1-t)^2), where t is the original color.
parameters.heading: Highlight

entries.label: Combine Normals
entries.summary: Blends two normal maps together.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information.

parameters.label: Normal Type
parameters.description: The type of the input normal maps. The output updates to match this input type. Signed (-1 to 1): Input signed normals, such as from geometry, which range from -1 to 1. Offset (0 to 1): Input offset normals, such as from normal maps, which range from 0 to 1.

parameters.label: Combine Method
parameters.description: The method used to blend the bg and fg normal maps. Whiteout: Add the x and y components together while multiplying the z components. UDN: Add the x and y components together while using the z component of the base normal map. This is faster than the Whiteout method, but can result in a loss of detail over flatter normals. Reoriented: Rotate the detail normal map onto the base normal map. This preserves the strength of both normal maps. This method often produces more accurate results but decreases performance.

entries.label: Compare
entries.summary: Creates a mask by comparing two layers, VDBs, or attributes.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Comparison Value
parameters.description: The value to compare with if the second input is not wired. This is compared against each of the channels of the first layer, VDB, or attribute.

parameters.label: Tolerance
parameters.description: Tolerance for the comparison. This tolerance will be applied two-sided for the equal comparisons, and one-sided for the strict inequality comparisions. Pixels within the tolerance will gain a soft mask value according to the fall off.

parameters.label: True If
parameters.description: The condition for which the output mask will be 1. Equal to each other (==): If the two pixels have the same value. Not equal to each other (!=): If the two pixels have different values. A greater than B (>): If the first input is strictly greater than the second. A greater than or equal to B (>=): If the first input is greater than or equal to the second. B greater than A (<): If the first input is strictly less than the second. B greater than or equal to A (<=): If the first input is less than or equal to the second.

parameters.label: Components
parameters.description: With multi-channel layers, VDBs, or attributes (such as UV, RGB, and RGBA), it is possible only some of the channels pass the comparison operator. True if All: The mask is 1 only if all of the channels pass the test. True if Any: The mask is 1 if any of the channels pass the test.

parameters.label: Falloff
parameters.description: For values that do not pass the test, but are within the tolerance, this controls how they fall off. None: No fall off is performed, a hard cutoff is done. Linear: A linear fall off from 1 to 0. Elendt: An S-shaped smooth fall off that is smooth at the start and end.

entries.label: Constant
entries.summary: Initializes pixels to constant values.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. You can also set the RGBA channels to which you apply the effects of this node. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information. Toggle RGB: Turns the Red, Green, and Blue channels on and off. Red: Applies this node's effects to the Red channel. Green: Applies this node's effects to the Green channel. Blue: Applies this node's effects to the Blue channel. Alpha: Applies this node's effects to the Alpha channel.

parameters.label: Value
parameters.description: The value to replace Mono layers with.

parameters.label: Value
parameters.description: The pair of values to replace UV layers with.

parameters.label: Color
parameters.description: The color to replace RGB layers with.

parameters.label: Color
parameters.description: The color and alpha to replace RGBA layers with.

entries.label: Contact Sheet
entries.summary: Arranges input layers into a contact sheet.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Images per Line
parameters.description: How many layers to arrange on a line before moving to the next row.

parameters.label: Stack Vertically
parameters.description: What order to stack the layers in vertically. Top to Bottom: Start with the top line, and add additional layers in a line below it. Bottom to Top: Start with the bottom line, and add additional layers in a line above it.

parameters.label: Stack Horizontally
parameters.description: What order to stack the layers horizontally. Left to Right: Each layer is placed to the right of the previous. Right to Left: Each layer is placed to the left of the previous.

parameters.label: Stack Images in Rows
parameters.description: Start stacking the layers along a line first, moving to the next line when full. With this off, layers will be stacked vertically first.

parameters.label: Max Lines
parameters.description: Limit the number of lines that can be output. Will generate additional output layers if this is exceeded.

parameters.label: Keep Full Size
parameters.description: Output the maximum size for the provided limits, even if there are not enough input layers.

parameters.label: Background Color
parameters.description: The color to use for regions where no layer is present.

parameters.label: First Input Offset
parameters.description: The offset in the stacking rules to use for the first input. This can be used to position a new sequence in a larger texture.

parameters.label: Scale Output Resolution
parameters.description: Scale down the output resolution. For a quick contact sheet you likely do not need the full resolution of all the inputs, as the size can get very large.

parameters.label: Scale Input Images
parameters.description: The input layers are scaled to a matching space. This is the data window that is adjusted, not the display window (see Spaces).

parameters.label: Scale Input Method
parameters.description: How to scale the incoming data windows. X Axis: Match the first inputs x-axis. Y Axis: Match the first inputs y-axis. Stretch to Fit: Stretch the layer to fit.

parameters.label: Clipped Sampling
parameters.description: When sampling outside of the layer's data window, return the background color rather than using the layer's border settings.

parameters.label: Filter
parameters.description: The method used to sample the image. The default value is Box. See Filters for more information.

entries.label: Contrast
entries.summary: Applies contrast to a layer, VDB, or attribute.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. You can also set the RGBA channels to which you apply the effects of this node. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information. Toggle RGB: Turns the Red, Green, and Blue channels on and off. Red: Applies this node's effects to the Red channel. Green: Applies this node's effects to the Green channel. Blue: Applies this node's effects to the Blue channel. Alpha: Applies this node's effects to the Alpha channel.

parameters.label: Contrast
parameters.description: How much contrast to apply. 1 will leave the image unchanged. Larger values will brighten light areas and darken dark areas, and lower values will do the opposite. 0 will cause all values to be the contrast center.

parameters.label: Contrast Center
parameters.description: The pivot around which contrast will occur.

parameters.label: Red
parameters.description: Contrast and offset pair to apply to the red channel.

parameters.label: Green
parameters.description: Contrast and offset pair to apply to the green channel.

parameters.label: Blue
parameters.description: Contrast and offset pair to apply to the blue channel.

parameters.label: Alpha
parameters.description: Contrast and offset pair to apply to the alpha channel.

parameters.label: Clamp Below Zero
parameters.description: Black values will be pushed into negative values, but often negative light isn't reasonable, so this will clamp them at zero.

parameters.label: Clamp Above One
parameters.description: White areas can be pushed beyond one, which is reasonable for HDR images, but if applying contrast to a mask it may be desireable to limit the growth to 1.

parameters.label: Treat RGBA as Premultiplied
parameters.description: RGBA layers are often premultiplied, so using a fixed pivot that doesn't take the alpha into consideration will cause low coverage areas to be considered dark. This option will implicitly un-premultiply, contrast, and then pre-multiply, so the pivot works as expected.

entries.label: Convert Depth
entries.summary: Converts depth layers between height, depth, and distance.

parameters.label: Source Space
parameters.description: The incoming layer's depth type. Depth: The input is a perpendicular distance to the eye. Zero values are taken to represent missed rays. Distance: The input is a Euclidean distance to the eye. Zero values are taken to represent missed rays. Height: The input is a heightfield where distances are offset from the image plane in the direction of the eye.

parameters.label: Dest Space
parameters.description: The outgoing layer's depth type. Depth: The output is a perpendicular distance to the eye. Distance: The output is a Euclidean distance to the eye. Height: The output is a heightfield where distances are offset from the image plane in the direction of the eye. The output type info is set to height to allow for visualization.

parameters.label: Zero Depth Value
parameters.description: The set depth for zero depths and distances. Zero depths and distances represent a missed ray, so are at an infinite distance. They require a specific value when you convert to a heightfield.

entries.label: Convert Normal
entries.summary: Converts normal layers between signed and offset.

parameters.label: Conversion
parameters.description: Which direction the normals should be converted. Offset to Signed (-1 to 1): The input normals are offset, such as those from a texture map, and need to be converted to signed normals for geometric operations. Signed to Offset (0 to 1): The input normals are signed, such as those from geometry map, and need to be converted to signed normals for texture maps.

parameters.label: Normalize
parameters.description: Ensures the input normals are unit-length before applying the transformation.

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.description: The offset to use for the conversion. If the final output is 0..255, it is possible the canonical conversion is not at 0.5 precisely, so for an exact conversion something slightly off 0.5 may be required.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: The scale to use for the conversion. If the output is 0..255, it is possible the canonical conversion will not be exactly 0.5 to account the choice of offset.

entries.label: Convolve 3x3
entries.summary: Convolves a layer by a 3x3 kernel.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. You can also set the RGBA channels to which you apply the effects of this node. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information. Toggle RGB: Turns the Red, Green, and Blue channels on and off. Red: Applies this node's effects to the Red channel. Green: Applies this node's effects to the Green channel. Blue: Applies this node's effects to the Blue channel. Alpha: Applies this node's effects to the Alpha channel.

parameters.label: Uniform Scale
parameters.description: The amount to scale all coefficients of the kernel. Use this value to set the normalization constant to make the kernel values integral. This value doesn't apply if Normalize Kernel is on. Use the following dimensions to additionally scale the coefficients by the distance between samples used for the convolution. The samples are the buffer elements in a 3x3 neighborhood around the currently processed buffer element. See /copernicus/spaces for more information about buffer space. (asterisk)1: Don't scale the coefficients. (asterisk)dX: Scale the coefficients by the image space distance between horizontally adjacent samples. This is the buffer element width. /dX: Divide the coefficients by the image space distance between horizontally adjacent samples. This is the buffer element width. NOTE: Use this value when building gradient kernels.
parameters.heading: Multiplicative

parameters.label: Top
parameters.description: The three coefficients to multiply with the (x-1, y+1), (x, y+1), and (x+1, y+1) pixels.
parameters.heading: Multiplicative

parameters.label: Middle
parameters.description: The three coefficients to multiply with the (x-1, y), (x, y), and (x+1, y) pixels.
parameters.heading: Multiplicative

parameters.label: Bottom
parameters.description: The three coefficients to multiply with the (x-1, y-1), (x, y-1), and (x+1, y-1) pixels.
parameters.heading: Multiplicative

parameters.label: Normalize Kernel
parameters.description: Normalizes the kernel by the sum of all coefficients. This prevents the application of the kernel from brightening or darkening the image. The node doesn't normalize the kernel if the kernel sums to zero (for example, as it does when you use the Outline recipe).
parameters.heading: Multiplicative

parameters.label: Uniform Scale
parameters.description: The amount to scale all additive values. Use the following dimensions to additionally scale the additive values by the distance between samples used for the convolution. The samples are the buffer elements in a 3x3 neighborhood around the currently processed buffer element. See /copernicus/spaces for more information about buffer space. (asterisk)1: Don't scale the values. (asterisk)dX: Scale the values by the image space distance between horizontally adjacent samples. This is the buffer element width. NOTE: Use this value when building distance fall-off kernels. /dX: Divide the values by the image space distance between horizontally adjacent samples. This is the buffer element width.
parameters.heading: Additive

parameters.label: Top
parameters.description: The three values to add to the (x-1, y+1), (x, y+1), and (x+1, y+1) pixels.
parameters.heading: Additive

parameters.label: Middle
parameters.description: The three values to add to the (x-1, y), (x, y), and (x+1, y) pixels.
parameters.heading: Additive

parameters.label: Bottom
parameters.description: The three values to add to the (x-1, y-1), (x, y-1), and (x+1, y-1) pixels.
parameters.heading: Additive

parameters.label: Combine Operation
parameters.description: Mixes each active pixel in the 3x3 neighborhood together to create the output. This combination occurs after each pixel is scaled by the coefficent and has added additional values. This parameter considers only the Active Terms that are on. Add: Add the computed pixel values together. Multiply: Multiply the computed pixel values together. Maximum: Use the pixel value with the largest component out of all computed values. Minimum: Use the pixel value with the smallest component out of all computed values.
parameters.heading: Additive

parameters.label: Active Terms
parameters.description: Controls which pixels in the 3x3 neighborhood are active and contribute to the final result. Terms you turn off aren't read from the input layer, which slightly increases performance. Off terms also don't contribute to the Combine Operation or have their weights included in the normalization.
parameters.heading: Additive

parameters.label: Clamp Below Zero
parameters.description: Clamps final resulting values below zero to zero before mixing these pixel values into the original image.
parameters.heading: Additive

parameters.label: Clamp Above One
parameters.description: Clamps final resulting values above one to one before mixing these pixel values into the original image.
parameters.heading: Additive

parameters.label: Treat RGBA as Premultiplied
parameters.description: Un-premultiplies the RGBA layers before applying the kernel, and then premultiplies the RGBA layers after applying the kernel. Turn this off when you blur the alpha and color (RGB) layers, because blur operations require premultiplied space. NOTE: RGBA layers are usually premultiplied, so applying edge detection to RGB channels reports edges where opacity varies. This lets kernels used for edge detection perform as if the image isn't premultiplied.
parameters.heading: Additive

entries.label: Copy and Transform
entries.summary: Copies stamps and applies transformations to the copies.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Total Number
parameters.description: The total number of copies to create. This includes the original geometry.

parameters.label: Order
parameters.description: The order in which Houdini applies the Translate, Rotate, and Scale values.

parameters.label: Translate
parameters.description: The location in world space to move the copies' origin to along the x and y axes.

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.description: The amount of rotation (in degrees) along the z-axis.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: The amount in world space by which to multiply the copies' x and y axes, which compresses (lower values) and stretches (higher values) the copies.

parameters.label: Uniform Scale
parameters.description: The amount by which to multiply the Scale parameter's x and y values.

parameters.label: Center Pivot on Shape
parameters.description: Centers the pivot point in the bounds of the input stamp. This is useful when your input stamp isn't in the center of the image.

parameters.label: Pivot Translate
parameters.description: The local pivot point of the copy. For example, if the shape's center point is -0.5x, set this parameter to -0.5 so the node acts like the point's in the center. To do this automatically, turn Center Pivot on Shape on. TIP: Click Icon:BUTTONS/layer_position_sample and then click a location in the image to set the Pivot Translate.

parameters.label: Pivot Rotate
parameters.description: The local pivot rotation (in degrees) of the copy, which rotates the pivot's local coordinate frame.

parameters.label: Blend Method
parameters.description: When mulitple stamps overlap, this controls how they blend together. Over: Render new copies over previous copies. The copies are presorted by their creation, which can be expensive. Under: Render new copies underneath previous copies. The copies are presorted by their creation, which can be expensive. Add: Add the overlapping pixel values of the stamps together. Subtract: Subtract the original pixel value from the new overlapping stamp's pixel value. This method works better when you're not subtracting from zero. Multiply: Multiply the overlapping pixel values of the stamps together. This method works better when the background starts at a non-zero value. Maximum: Compare the stamps along with the background color and use the maximum value. Minimum: Compare the stamps along with the background color and use the minimum value.

parameters.label: Filter
parameters.description: The method used to sample the image. See Filters for more information.

parameters.label: Wrap Mode
parameters.description: The wrapping behavior of the stamps. Auto: Wrap copies outside of the main tile (whose size is controlled by Tile Size) back into the tile when the size_ref input image's Border type is Wrap. Off: Don't wrap the stamps. On: Wrap copies outside of the main tile (whose size is controlled by Tile Size) back into the tile. This makes the main tile seamlessly repeat.

parameters.label: Tile Size
parameters.description: When Wrap Mode is Auto or On, this is the size (in world space) of the region to wrap into. The resultant image periodically repeats in this size.

parameters.label: Stamp Color
parameters.description: A tint for the stamp.
parameters.heading: Stamping

parameters.label: Change per Copy
parameters.description: A variable tint for the stamp, which can cause a color change for each copy. This is an additive, not a multiplier. For example, a change of R: 0.1, G: 0.2, B: 0.0 means that each copy becomes more red, but also becomes more green twice as fast.
parameters.heading: Stamping

parameters.label: Color Ramp
parameters.description: Applies a ramp over all copies and multiplies the ramp by the stamp's color. When on, this turns Change per Copy off. See Ramp parameters for more information.
parameters.heading: Stamping

parameters.label: Uniform Alpha
parameters.description: The amount of black (0) and white (1) by which to multiply the stamp's Background Alpha.
parameters.heading: Stamping

parameters.label: Change per Copy
parameters.description: A variable scale for the stamp, which can create an alpha change for each copy. This is an additive, not a multiplier.
parameters.heading: Stamping

parameters.label: Alpha Ramp
parameters.description: Applies a ramp over all copies and multiplies the ramp by the stamp's alpha. When on, this turns Change per Copy off. See Ramp parameters for more information.
parameters.heading: Stamping

parameters.label: Background Color
parameters.description: The initial background color of the space around the stamps.
parameters.heading: Background

parameters.label: Background Alpha
parameters.description: The initial background alpha of the space around the stamps.
parameters.heading: Background

entries.label: Corner Pin
entries.summary: Pins a layer's corners in a reference layer.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Units
parameters.description: The space in which to specify the corners. This applies to the size_ref input, which is the reference layer. Image: Use image coordinates that range from -1 to 1 on the display window of the layer. Texture: Use texture coordinates that range from 0 to 1 on the data window of the layer. Pixels: Use absolute pixel locations in the layer. World: Use coordinates in world space that project through the layer's implicit camera.

parameters.label: Bottom Left
parameters.description: The lower-left coordinate. The Units parameter determines if this is in image, texture, pixel, or world space.

parameters.label: Bottom Right
parameters.description: The lower-right coordinate. The Units parameter determines if this is in image, texture, pixel, or world space.

parameters.label: Top Left
parameters.description: The upper-left coordinate. The Units parameter determines if this is in image, texture, pixel, or world space.

parameters.label: Top Right
parameters.description: The upper-right coordinate. The Units parameter determines if this is in image, texture, pixel, or world space.

entries.label: Cross Product
entries.summary: Performs a cross product of two RGB layers, VDBs, or attributes.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

entries.label: Cryptomatte
entries.summary: Builds a matte from cryptomatte layers.

parameters.label: Select All
parameters.description: Select all IDs. This essentially sums up the coverage of all the provided layers, creating a mask of everything that isn't present with any hash.

parameters.label: Selection
parameters.description: A comma-spearated list of object names to include in the selection. Each of these names will have any surrounding spaces trimmed, sent through the standard murmur hash, and then that ID will be used for the list of IDs to use for coverage. This requires that the cryptomatte used a standard hash. Available object names can be found in the metadata of the .exr. iinfo -v filename.exr will list the information, the cryptomatte/hexnumber/manifest will list the object names in dictionary format. TIP: Click Smallicon:BUTTONS/layer_sample and then click the area of the image you want to mask to set the Selection.

entries.label: Curve 3D
entries.summary: Lets you interactively draw Bézier curves using tools similar to 2D illustration programs, as well as polylines and NURBS.

parameters.label: Primitive Type
parameters.description: Type of curve primitives to create. Polygon: Create a polyline. NURBS Curve: Create a NURBS curve. Bezier Curve: Create a Bézier curve.

parameters.label: Order
parameters.description: The order of the NURBS or Bézier curve. Higher order curves give more control vertices and smoother curve interpolation between on-curve knots. However, you should generally use the default order (4) unless you have a reason for needing higher-order curves. Note that changing the Order changes the interpretation of all existing curves to use the new order value. The drawing mode is optimized for cubic Bézier curves (Order set to 4, the default). For higher-order Bézier curves, the drawing interface is the same as for cubic Bézier curves, but after you drag out the tangent handles, the node creates _more than one_ tangent handle on the trailing side of the point. It creates the extra control points in line, so they have the same shape as a cubic Bézier would, but after you're finished drawing you can use the Edit mode to move the extra control points independently. For NURBS, the drawing interface is always the same: placing points by clicking.

parameters.label: Reinterpret Curves as Current Type and Order
parameters.label_norm: reinterpret curves as current type and order
parameters.description: When on, all existing curves are converted by reinterpretting the curve points as the current Primitive Type and Order. When converting curves to NURBs or Bezier, the last point on the curve may be repeated to fully define the curve. When off, only newly created curves are given the current Primitive Type and Order.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: The mode that the tool is currently in. Select/Edit Mode: Modifies existing curves. Draw Mode: Puts down new points. Auto-Bezier Draw Mode: Put down new points when creating Bezier curves. Points are created as Auto Points. Tangents are optimized to create a bezier curve continuous in the first and second derivatives. Previous points are optimized until it either reaches back to the start of the curve, or a non-auto point. Orient Mode: Create an orient attribute along curves by specifying target up vectors at specified anchor points.

parameters.label: Delete Selected Points
parameters.description: Removes the selected point(s), if any.

parameters.label: Join Selected Points
parameters.description: Joins two selected vertices together into a single vertex. If the two selected vertices are on the same curve, the result is one closed curve. If the vertices are from different curves, the result is one curve instead of two.

parameters.label: Cut Curves at Selected Points
parameters.description: Cuts the curve at each selected point. After the cut, each selected point becomes an end point. Any branches are also split prior to cutting curve vertices.

parameters.label: Add Segment Between Selected Endpoints
parameters.description: Joins the two selected vertices with a straight line. If the two selected vertices are on the same curve, the result is one closed curve. If the vertices are from different curves, the result is one curve instead of two, with a segment added between the end vertices.

parameters.label: Delete Segments Between Selected Points
parameters.description: Removes any selected segments, possibly splitting curves around selected segments.

parameters.label: Fuse Branch
parameters.description: Fuse all selected points into a single branch point containing all the vertices from the selected points.

parameters.label: Split Branch
parameters.description: Split the selected branch points to create separate points for each vertex of the branched point.

parameters.label: Make Selected Points Corner
parameters.description: Turns an anchor point into a corner point.

parameters.label: Make Selected Points Smooth
parameters.description: Turns an anchor point into a smooth point, possibly snapping handles to be aligned.

parameters.label: Make Selected Points Balanced
parameters.description: Turns an anchor point into a balanced point, possibly snapping handles to be aligned.

parameters.label: Retract Tangents at Selected Points
parameters.description: Collapses the bezier handles down into a sharp bezier corner point.

parameters.label: Expand Tangents at Selected Points
parameters.description: Expands out the bezier handles to be intractable, if the selected point is collapsed.

parameters.label: Make Segments Between Selected Points Straight
parameters.label_norm: make segments between selected points straight
parameters.description: Collapses the handles on the ends of the selected segments, converting the segment into a straight line.

parameters.label: Close Selected Curves
parameters.description: Closes all curves with at least one point selected.

parameters.label: Create Rounded Corners
parameters.description: Turns the selected corner points into rounded corners.

parameters.label: Remove Rounded Corners
parameters.description: Turns the selected rounded corners into ordinary corners.

parameters.label: Make Selected Points Auto
parameters.description: Makes selected points into auto points. Bezier curves are automatically computed to interpolate any auto points.

parameters.label: Make Selected Points Manual
parameters.description: Makes selected auto points into non-auto points and freezes the local interpolated curve so that it can be manually edited.

parameters.label: Reverse
parameters.description: Reverse selected curves.

parameters.label: Reset Operations
parameters.description: Resets all modeling operations that have been done. Resets the output geometry to the input geometry.

parameters.label: Snap Tangents when Fusing Ends in Draw Mode
parameters.label_norm: snap tangents when fusing ends in draw mode
parameters.description: Whether to snap the final tangent when fusing curves together or closing curves by clicking on the end point of another curve or the opposite end point of the same curve. Dragging out the tangent while fusing doesn't snap the tangents.

parameters.label: Approximate Shape on Delete
parameters.description: Approximates the previous curve shape on a point delete.

parameters.label: Approximate End Tangents
parameters.description: Prioritizes keeping the end derivatives of a segment when approximating the previous curve shape on a point delete.

parameters.label: Soft Transform Radius
parameters.description: The soft transform radius when soft transforms are on. Soft transforms are used when doing operations that manually move anchor points, including dragging points in edit and draw mode, dragging segments in polygons or NURBs curves, or bezier segments adjacent to rounded corners or auto points. This radius is relative to the distance along the backbone polygon of the given curve. For Polygons this is equivalent to the surface distance along the curve. For NURBS Curves this is equivalent to the distance along the control polygon of the curve. And for Bezier Curves, this is equivalent to the distance along the polygon that results from reinterpreting the curve as a polygon. In particular, in this polygon, auto points and rounded corners are collapsed to a single point, which can result in distances along the curve being slightly different than expected when looking at a curve.

parameters.label: Corner Points Group
parameters.description: The name of the group to create that contains the corner points. When chaining curve nodes, this can be used to ensure later curve nodes pick up the corner points from this node.
parameters.heading: Output

parameters.label: Smooth Points Group
parameters.description: The name of the group to create that contains the smooth points. When chaining curve nodes, this can be used to ensure later curve nodes pick up the smooth points from this node.
parameters.heading: Output

parameters.label: Auto Points Group
parameters.description: The name of the group to create that contains the auto points. When chaining curve nodes, this can be used to ensure later curve nodes pick up the auto points from this node.
parameters.heading: Output

parameters.label: Name
parameters.description: The name to place in the name attribute on all created geometry. Defaults to the name of the SOP ($OS).
parameters.heading: Output

parameters.label: X Axis
parameters.description: The name of the attribute to create to store the X Axis of the orientations created on points in the Orient Mode. When active, geometry showing the x axis is present in the viewport. The density and scale of guide gnomons showing the axes can be controlled in the state parameters.
parameters.heading: Output

parameters.label: Y Axis
parameters.description: The name of the attribute to create to store the Y Axis of the orientations created on points in the Orient Mode. When active, geometry showing the y axis is present in the viewport. The density and scale of guide gnomons showing the axes can be controlled in the state parameters.
parameters.heading: Output

parameters.label: Z Axis
parameters.description: The name of the attribute to create to store the Z Axis of the orientations created on points in the Orient Mode. When active, geometry showing the x axis is present in the viewport. The density and scale of guide gnomons showing the axes can be controlled in the state parameters.
parameters.heading: Output

parameters.label: Orient
parameters.description: The name of the orient attribute to create. The orient attribute created in the Orient Mode is stored in this attribute. When active, guide geometry showing the orient attribute is present in the viewport. In the state parameters, you can toggle drawing the orient guide geometry, as well as control the density and scale of guide gnomons.
parameters.heading: Output

parameters.label: Tangent Type
parameters.description: The method used to determine the implicit curve tangent. This tangent is used to parallel transport the orient attributes from the target points along the curves.
parameters.heading: Output

parameters.label: Align with Curve Tangent
parameters.description: When on, aligns orient attribute values with the curve tangent. When off, orient attribute values on target points are aligned with the value in Tangent.
parameters.heading: Output

parameters.label: Target Orientations
parameters.description: The target orientations specified on points along curves. When determining the orient attribute, these target orientations are placed on curves, and a parallel transport is used between target points to create an orient attribute that smoothly blends between target orientations. For any curves that do not have any target orientations, a default orient is placed on the first point of the curve, achieved by rotating the vector (0,0,1) onto the curve tangent.
parameters.heading: Output

parameters.label: Enable Target Orientation
parameters.description: Toggles this target orientation.
parameters.heading: Output

parameters.label: Point
parameters.description: The point to place the target orientation on.
parameters.heading: Output

parameters.label: Up
parameters.description: The target up vector. Target up vectors are made perpendicular to the curve tangent if Align with Curve Tangent is on, and are otherwise made perpendicular to the specified Tangent vector.
parameters.heading: Output

parameters.label: Tangent
parameters.description: The target tangent vector. When Align with Curve Tangent is off, this parameter is available to set alongside the Up vector, allowing you to fully specify the orientation of this target Point, without being constrained by the curve tangent.
parameters.heading: Output

parameters.label: Active Points
parameters.description: Points used in the current operation.
parameters.heading: Current Operation

parameters.label: Translate
parameters.description: The amount to translate the selected points or the selected handle end point by.
parameters.heading: Current Operation

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.description: The amount to rotate (in degrees) the selected points with respect to the pivot.
parameters.heading: Current Operation

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: The amount to scale the selected points with respect to the pivot.
parameters.heading: Current Operation

parameters.label: Corner Points
parameters.description: A group parameter specifying the corner points. When chaining multiple curve nodes, this can be set with an input group, such as that created through Corner Points Group, to pick up the corner points from previous nodes.
parameters.heading: Current Operation

parameters.label: Smooth Points
parameters.description: A group parameter specifying the smooth points. When chaining multiple curve nodes, this can be set with an input group, such as that created through Smooth Points Group, to pick up the smooth points from previous nodes.
parameters.heading: Current Operation

parameters.label: Auto Points
parameters.description: A group parameter specifying the auto points. When chaining multiple curve nodes, this can be set with an input group, such as that created through Auto Points Group, to pick up the auto points from previous nodes.
parameters.heading: Current Operation

parameters.label: Pivot Translate
parameters.description: The position of the pivot, before any further translations.
parameters.heading: Pivot Transform

parameters.label: Pivot Rotate
parameters.description: Specifies the axis to align the transform handle with. Upon finishing any operation with the transform handle, it snaps back to this rotation to begin a new edit. Is specified as three angles in degrees representing the amount to rotate around each axis.
parameters.heading: Pivot Transform

parameters.label: Fixed Pivot
parameters.description: Whether to keep the pivot position the same when selecting new points. If off, the pivot resets to the center of the bounding box of the selected points on a selection change.
parameters.heading: Pivot Transform

parameters.label: View Rounded Corners
parameters.description: Whether to view rounded corners. When off, rounded corners are all shown with a radius of 0.0. The topology of created curves is not changed when this toggle is off.
parameters.heading: Rounded Corners

parameters.label: Round Corner Points
parameters.description: A string parameter encoding the rounded corners and their radii.
parameters.heading: Rounded Corners

parameters.label: Round Corner Radius
parameters.description: Sets the radius of the selected rounded corners.
parameters.heading: Rounded Corners

parameters.label: Bake Selected Rounded Corners
parameters.description: Convert selected rounded corners into regular bezier segments.
parameters.heading: Rounded Corners

parameters.label: Show Rounded Corner Widget
parameters.description: Whether to show a widget to modify rounded corner radii.
parameters.heading: Rounded Corners

parameters.label: Show Rounded Corner Labels
parameters.description: Whether to show labels for the radii on the rounded corner widgets. These labels are off if Show Rounded Corner Widget is off.
parameters.heading: Rounded Corners

entries.label: Scatter on Curves
entries.summary: Scatters input stamps along an input curve using randomization controls.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the node outputs. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Distribution
parameters.description: The distribution mode for how to scatter the stamps along the curve. Distance: Scatter stamps equidistant from each other based on a set distance. Scatter: Scatter stamps randomly based on a density input or the Max Count. By Count: Scatter stamps randomly based on a specific count.
parameters.heading: Scattering

parameters.label: Segment Length
parameters.description: When Distribution is Distance, this is the maximum segment length of resulting edges.
parameters.heading: Scattering

parameters.label: Maximum Segments
parameters.description: When Distribution is Distance, this is the maximum number of edges.
parameters.heading: Scattering

parameters.label: Treat Input Curve As
parameters.description: How to inteprolate the input curves. Straight: Directly interpolate maintaining the straight lines. Subdivision: Smooth the curves with a subdivision approach. This will not interpolate the original points. Interpolating: Smooth the curves with a bicubic approach, this will interpolate the original points but oscillate.
parameters.heading: Scattering

parameters.label: Density Layer Mask
parameters.description: When Distribution is Scatter, this is the amount of the density input's mono value to mix in with the Density value. Higher values mix in more of the input's value. Lower values mix in less of the input's value.
parameters.heading: Scattering

parameters.label: Density Scale
parameters.description: When Distribution is Scatter, this is the amount to scale the density of the points. This parameter doesn't apply when Max Count is on.
parameters.heading: Scattering

parameters.label: Max Count
parameters.description: When Distribution is Scatter or By Count, this is the amount of points to generate.
parameters.heading: Scattering

parameters.label: Relaxation
parameters.description: When Distribution is Scatter or By Count, this relaxes points by pushing them away from each other to avoid clumping. More relaxation iterations result in further separation between the points. Relaxation is done gradually to avoid chaotic behavior and allow control over how much relaxation takes place.
parameters.heading: Scattering

parameters.label: Scatter Seed
parameters.description: The seed value for all randomization that deals with stamp placement. This includes jitter, density, angle and direction, scale, and stretch.
parameters.heading: Scattering

parameters.label: Scale Layer Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the scale input's mono value to mix in with the Scale value, which impacts the stamps' scale. Higher values mix in more of the input's value. Lower values mix in less of the input's value.
parameters.heading: Scale

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: The scale of the stamps in image space. Use the dropdown menu to set the method of post-processing that applies to the scale of the stamps. Uniform: No post-processing. Variance: Apply random variance to the scale. Min/Max: The minimum and maximum range of values that each stamp randomly picks from, and then multiplies against the original Scale.
parameters.heading: Scale

parameters.label: Scale Variance
parameters.description: The amount of random variance to apply to the scale. This is applied as a post-process. If Scale is 1 and Scale Variance 1 for example, this represents a 100% range in sizes. This means the output stamps have a random scale from 0.5 * Scale to 2.0 * Scale.
parameters.heading: Scale

parameters.label: Min Scale
parameters.description: The minimum value that the stamps can randomly select, and then multiply against the original Scale. This is applied as a post-process.
parameters.heading: Scale

parameters.label: Max Scale
parameters.description: The maximum value that the stamps can randomly select, and then multiply against the original Scale. This is applied as a post-process.
parameters.heading: Scale

parameters.label: Apply Scale along Curve
parameters.description: Applies a ramp along the curve and multiplies the ramp by the stamp's scale. The curve of the ramp determines which stamps to scale. See Ramp parameters for more information.
parameters.heading: Scale

parameters.label: Cut Curves by Relative Arc Length
parameters.label_norm: cut curves by relative arc length
parameters.description: Solves for the actual location halfway along the curve as measured by distance. This is useful since curves have a parameterization that doesn't match the actual distance along the curve. For example, a curve of 0.5 isn't halfway along the curve but halfway along its parameterization.
parameters.heading: Curve

parameters.label: Start Point
parameters.description: The start point in image space of the curve.
parameters.heading: Curve

parameters.label: End Point
parameters.description: The end point in image space of the curve.
parameters.heading: Curve

parameters.label: Smoothing
parameters.description: The amount of smoothing to apply to the curve.
parameters.heading: Curve

parameters.label: Mirror Stamps
parameters.description: Creates a mirrored version of the stamps on the other side of the curve. Use the dropdown menu to set the mirror's behavior. Treat Independently: Apply randomization and scattering separately. NOTE: This mode's angle mirroring isn't done as a post-process, so any randomization breaks the mirroring of the angle across the curve. Use Values from Original: Takes the mirrored curve and copies all values and looks from the original to the mirrored copy. This occurs after the randomization and scattering. Use Values from Mirrored Copy: Takes the original curve and copies all values and looks from the mirrored to the original copy. This occurs after the randomization and scattering.
parameters.heading: Mirror and Offset

parameters.label: From Curve
parameters.description: The amount to perpendicularly offset the stamps from the tangent of the curve.
parameters.heading: Mirror and Offset

parameters.label: Mirrored From Curve
parameters.description: The amount to perpendicularly offset the mirrored stamps from the tangent of the curve.
parameters.heading: Mirror and Offset

parameters.label: Jitter
parameters.description: The amount of random position offset to add to each stamp's position on the grid.
parameters.heading: Mirror and Offset

parameters.label: Offset along Curve
parameters.description: The amount to offset the stamp placement along the curve.
parameters.heading: Mirror and Offset

parameters.label: Angle Layer Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the angle input's mono value to mix in with the Angle value, which impacts the degree of the stamps' angles. Higher values mix in more of the input's value. Lower values mix in less of the input's value. NOTE: For the stamp input, the incoming stamp's upward direction is taken as its forward position and points along the curve in default behavior. The following example shows this behavior using an upward facing arrow as the stamp input.
parameters.heading: Angle

parameters.label: Direction Layer Mask
