parameters.description: The amount of the direction input's UV value to mix in with the Angle value, which impacts the direction of the stamps' angles. Higher values mix in more of the input's value. Lower values mix in less of the input's value.
parameters.heading: Angle

parameters.label: Angles Relative to Curve Direction
parameters.description: Accounts for the curve's usual direction when calculating the angle.
parameters.heading: Angle

parameters.label: Angle
parameters.description: The angle in degrees to rotate each stamp. Use the dropdown menu to set the method of post-processing that applies to the angle of the stamps. Uniform: No post-processing. Variance: Apply random variance to the angles. Min/Max: The minimum and maximum range of values in degrees that each stamp randomly picks from, and then multiplies against the original angle.
parameters.heading: Angle

parameters.label: Angle Variance
parameters.description: The amount of random variance to apply to the angles. This is applied as a post-process. For example, a value of 30 makes each stamp have a random offset between -30 degrees and 30 degrees.
parameters.heading: Angle

parameters.label: Min Angle
parameters.description: The minimum degree that the stamps can randomly select, and then multiply against the original Angle. This is applied as a post-process.
parameters.heading: Angle

parameters.label: Max Angle
parameters.description: The maximum degree that the stamps can randomly select, and then multiply against the original Angle. This is applied as a post-process.
parameters.heading: Angle

parameters.label: Increment per Stamp
parameters.description: The amount of angle increase for each stamp along the curve. For example, if Increment per Stamp is 10 and your curve has 36 points, each stamp progressively rotates more and the end stamp makes a full rotation.
parameters.heading: Angle

parameters.label: Round to Multiples
parameters.description: Snaps all stamps to a specified angle. This is applied as a post-process.
parameters.heading: Angle

parameters.label: Stretch Layer Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the stretch input's UV value to mix in with the Stretch X and Stretch Y values, which impacts the XY scale. Higher values mix in more of the input's value. Lower values mix in less of the input's value.
parameters.heading: Stretch

parameters.label: Stretch Mode
parameters.description: The method of post-processing that applies to the non-uniform scale (stretch) of the stamps. Uniform: No post-processing. Variance: Apply random variance to the scale of the X and Y-axes. Min/Max: The minimum and maximum range of values that each stamp randomly picks from, and then multiplies against the original Stretch X and Stretch Y.
parameters.heading: Stretch

parameters.label: Stretch X
parameters.description: The scale of the stamps along the X-axis in image space.
parameters.heading: Stretch

parameters.label: Stretch Y
parameters.description: The scale of the stamps along the Y-axis in image space.
parameters.heading: Stretch

parameters.label: Stretch Variance
parameters.description: The amount of random variance to apply to the scale of the X and Y-axes. This is applied as a post-process. If Stretch X is 1, Stretch Y is 0, and Stretch Variance is 1, 0 for example, this represents a 100% range in sizes. This means the output stamps have a random scale from 0.5 * Stretch x to 2.0 * Stretch x.
parameters.heading: Stretch

parameters.label: Min Stretch
parameters.description: The minimum value that the stamps can randomly select, and then multiply against the original Stretch X and Stretch Y. This is applied as a post-process.
parameters.heading: Stretch

parameters.label: Max Stretch
parameters.description: The maximum value that the stamps can randomly select, and then multiply against the original Stretch X and Stretch Y. This is applied as a post-process.
parameters.heading: Stretch

parameters.label: Stretch along Curve
parameters.description: Applies two ramps along the curve to scale stamps along the X and Y-axes.
parameters.heading: Stretch

parameters.label: Stretch X along Curve
parameters.description: Applies a ramp along the curve and multiplies the ramp by the stamp's scale along the X-axis. The curve of the ramp determines which stamps to scale. See Ramp parameters for more information.
parameters.heading: Stretch

parameters.label: Stretch Y along Curve
parameters.description: Applies a ramp along the curve and multiplies the ramp by the stamp's scale along the Y-axis. The curve of the ramp determines which stamps to scale. See Ramp parameters for more information.
parameters.heading: Stretch

parameters.label: Blend Method
parameters.description: When mulitple stamps overlap, this controls how they blend together. Depth-Sorted Over: Presort the points by their depth. The node renders the farthest points first, so closer points paint over them. This option can be expensive since it requires sorting. Unsorted Depth-Weighted Over: Apply a non-linear weighting that approximates depth-sorting without the need for sorting. Add: Add the overlapping pixel values of the stamps together. Subtract: Subtract the original pixel value from the new overlapping stamp's pixel value. This method works better when you're not subtracting from zero. Multiply: Multiply the overlapping pixel values of the stamps together. This method works better when the background starts at a non-zero value. Maximum: Compare the stamps along with the background color and use the maximum value. Minimum: Compare the stamps along with the background color and use the minimum value.
parameters.heading: Blend

parameters.label: Use Sort Layer
parameters.description: Multiply the Depth-Sorted Over or Unsorted Depth-Weighted Over sort values by the sort input's value.
parameters.heading: Blend

parameters.label: Apply Sort along Curve
parameters.description: Applies a ramp along the curve to sort the stamps. See Ramp parameters for more information.
parameters.heading: Blend

parameters.label: Color Seed
parameters.description: The seed value for randomization that deals with stamp color and alpha.
parameters.heading: Color

parameters.label: Color Layer Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the color input's RGB value to mix in with the Stamp Color value, which impacts the stamps' tint. Higher values mix in more of the input's value. Lower values mix in less of the input's value.
parameters.heading: Color

parameters.label: Stamp Color
parameters.description: A tint for the stamp. Use the dropdown menu to set how the color applies to the stamps. Uniform: Apply the same color to each stamp. Variance: Apply random variance to the hue, saturation, and value of the stamps. Random from Ramp: Pick randomly from a color ramp. See Ramp parameters for more information. Ramp along Curve: Applies a ramp along the curve and multiplies the ramp by the stamp's color. The curve of the ramp determines which colors apply to the stamps. See Ramp parameters for more information.
parameters.heading: Color

parameters.label: Hue
parameters.description: The amount of random variance to apply to the hue. This is applied as a post-process. If set to 30 for example, the stamps randomly pick a hue offset from the range of 0 to 30.
parameters.heading: Color

parameters.label: Saturation
parameters.description: The amount of random variance to apply to the saturation. This is applied as a post-process. If set to 0.5 for example, the stamps randomly pick a saturation from the range of 0 to 0.5.
parameters.heading: Color

parameters.label: Value
parameters.description: The amount of random variance to apply to the value. This is applied as a post-process. If set to 0.5 for example, the stamps randomly pick a value from the range of 0 to 0.5.
parameters.heading: Color

parameters.label: Alpha Layer Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the alpha input's mono value to mix in with the Stamp Alpha value, which impacts the stamps' alpha. Higher values mix in more of the input's value. Lower values mix in less of the input's value.
parameters.heading: Alpha

parameters.label: Stamp Alpha
parameters.description: The amount of black (0) and white (1) by which to multiply the stamp's alpha. Use the dropdown menu to set how the alpha applies to the stamps. Uniform: Apply the same amount of alpha to each stamp. Variance: Apply random variance to the alpha of the stamps. Random from Ramp: Pick randomly from a mono ramp. See Ramp parameters for more information. Ramp along Curve: Applies a ramp along the curve and multiplies the ramp by the stamp's alpha. The curve of the ramp determines how much alpha applies to the stamps. See Ramp parameters for more information.
parameters.heading: Alpha

parameters.label: Alpha Variance
parameters.description: The amount of random variance to apply to the alpha. This is applied as a post-process.
parameters.heading: Alpha

parameters.label: Background Color
parameters.description: The initial background color of the space around the stamps.
parameters.heading: Background

parameters.label: Background Alpha
parameters.description: The initial background alpha of the space around the stamps.
parameters.heading: Background

parameters.label: Selection Mode
parameters.description: The stamps to place in the image. When no stamps input is wired in, this parameter applies to the default star pattern. Cycle: Loop through all stamps in a repetitive cycle. Random: Randomly choose stamps based on the Select Seed. Layer Select: Use the select input to choose stamps. The parameter uses the first stamp when a pixel value is 0.0 and the last stamp when a pixel value is 1.0.
parameters.heading: Stamp Selection

parameters.label: Limit Selection
parameters.description: Limits the maximum number of stamps that the node uses.
parameters.heading: Stamp Selection

parameters.label: Select Seed
parameters.description: The seed value for randomization that deals with stamp selection.
parameters.heading: Stamp Selection

parameters.label: Filter
parameters.description: The method used to sample the image. See Filters for more information.
parameters.heading: Options

parameters.label: Wrap Mode
parameters.description: The wrapping behavior of the stamps. Auto: Wrap points outside of the main tile (whose size is controlled by Tile Size) back into the tile when the size_ref input image's Border type is Wrap. Off: Don't wrap the stamps. On: Wrap points outside of the main tile (whose size is controlled by Tile Size) back into the tile. This makes the main tile seamlessly repeat.
parameters.heading: Options

parameters.label: Tile Size
parameters.description: When Wrap Mode is Auto or On, this is the size (in image space) of the region to wrap into. The resultant image periodically repeats in this size.
parameters.heading: Options

entries.label: Defocus
entries.summary: Defocuses an input layer.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information.

parameters.label: Focal Length
parameters.description: The focal length (zoom) of the camera.
parameters.heading: Focus

parameters.label: Focus Distance
parameters.description: The distance from the camera at which objects are in focus. Objects outside of this distance are blurred. TIP: Enter the viewer state and click on the area of the layer you'd like to be in focus.
parameters.heading: Focus

parameters.label: F-Stop
parameters.description: The F-Stop of the camera. The f-stop determines the blurriness of the defocus.
parameters.heading: Focus

parameters.label: Focus Plane Blur
parameters.description: The amount to blur the focus mask to smooth the transition between in and out of focus. NOTE: The focus mask is a mono layer that determines what areas of the image are in or out of focus.
parameters.heading: Focus

parameters.label: Focus Ramp
parameters.description: Remaps the focus mask. See Ramp parameters for more information.
parameters.heading: Focus

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: The maximum radius (in pixels) of the bokeh effect for out of focus areas. This can be expensive for a large radius since a lot of scattering is done.
parameters.heading: Bokeh

parameters.label: Gain
parameters.description: The aperture mask is normalized so the bokeh doesn't change the total brightness, but it can be useful to boost the result to gain or lose total luminance.
parameters.heading: Bokeh

parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.description: The resolution to resample the aperture layer to, which speeds up filtering of the aperture layer.
parameters.heading: Bokeh

parameters.label: Resample Input
parameters.description: The amount to resample the input layer before computing the bokeh layer. This speeds up computing at the slight cost of quality.
parameters.heading: Bokeh

parameters.label: Color Correct
parameters.description: Applies color correction on the image's out of focus areas.
parameters.heading: Color Correct

parameters.label: Brightness threshold
parameters.description: The threshold that a pixel's luminance value must be above for the pixel to brighten.
parameters.heading: Color Correct

parameters.label: Brightness Blur
parameters.description: The amount to blur the brightness mask, which smooths the transition between pixels in and out of the threshold.
parameters.heading: Color Correct

parameters.label: Brightness
parameters.description: The amount to brighten the pixels within the Brightness threshold.
parameters.heading: Color Correct

parameters.label: Saturation Threshold
parameters.description: The threshold that a pixel's luminance value must be above for the pixel to desaturate.
parameters.heading: Color Correct

parameters.label: Saturation Blur
parameters.description: The amount to blur the saturation mask, which smooths the transition between pixels in and out of the threshold.
parameters.heading: Color Correct

parameters.label: Saturation Scale
parameters.description: The amount to desaturate the pixels within the Saturation Threshold. Bright pixels tend to be slightly desaturated.
parameters.heading: Color Correct

parameters.label: Gamma
parameters.description: The gamma of the out of focus areas.
parameters.heading: Color Correct

parameters.label: Depth Blend
parameters.description: Applies depth to blend the original layer with the out of focus layer.
parameters.heading: Depth Blend

parameters.label: Min
parameters.description: The amount to remap the minimum depth of the mask that blends the original layer with the out of focus layer.
parameters.heading: Depth Blend

parameters.label: Max
parameters.description: The amount to remap the maximum depth of the mask that blends the original layer with the out of focus layer.
parameters.heading: Depth Blend

entries.label: Denoise AI
entries.summary: Denoises an input layer.

parameters.label: Denoiser
parameters.description: The library to use to denoise the image. Intel Denoiser: Use the Intel Open Image Denoise library. This library ships with Houdini so it should always be available. OptiX Denoiser: Use the NVIDIA OptiX library. This option is only available if you have an NVIDIA graphics card with the approriate driver.

parameters.label: Auxiliary Planes Are Clean
parameters.description: Sets the _cleanAux_ filter parameter for further improving quality when the auxilary feature (albedo, normal) planes are noise-free, as described in the OIDN documentation.

parameters.label: Prefilter Auxiliary Planes
parameters.description: Whether to prefilter the albedo and normal auxiliary planes before denoising the image planes. For the best possible quality, it is recommended to prefilter the auxiliary planes if they are noisy and turn on Auxiliary Planes Are Clean. While prefiltering generates better results and should be used for final frames, it will hurt performance and thus should be turned off when doing previews or interactive rendering.

parameters.label: Use CPU Only
parameters.description: Some denoising libraries can run on CPU or GPU. Normally, the denoiser will use the fastest device. This option will force the denoiser to choose the CPU device. You can use this option to minimize GPU memory requirements, for example when denoising large images or rendering on GPU-enabled farm machines.

entries.label: Denoise TVD
entries.summary: Removes white noise from an image.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. You can also set the RGBA channels to which you apply the effects of this node. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information.

parameters.label: Iterations
parameters.description: Governs the number of rounds of denoising that will be performed on the image. Running time is proportional to the number of rounds. Additional iterations will increase the removal of noise at the expense of losing more fine detail.

parameters.label: Speed
parameters.description: A scale factor for the amount of diffusion to apply in each round of iteration. The total amount of diffusion is this value times the Iterations value. However, if this is made too large, the process can become unstable and not converge to a good result.

entries.label: Distort
entries.summary: Distorts an input layer.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Border
parameters.description: The sampling behavior outside of the incoming layer's boundaries. Automatically uses the layer's border property. See Border types for more information.

parameters.label: Filter
parameters.description: The filtering method used for sampling the source layer. Consider using one of the area filters (Box and later) if the distortion shrinks large regions and you notice noise. See Filters for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. A value of 1 means this node uses only the new value. The default value is 1. See Mask for more information.

parameters.label: Direction Type
parameters.description: Specifies the direction in which to distort the layer. This can be an angle in degrees (Angle) or a two-component vector representing the X and Y directions in image space (Coordinates). NOTE: Direction Type and its related parameters apply only when there is no dir input.

parameters.label: Direction
parameters.description: Specifies the X and Y directions in image space when Direction Type is set to Coordinates.

parameters.label: Normalize Direction
parameters.description: Normalizes Direction when turned on.

parameters.label: Angle
parameters.description: Specifies the angle of distortion when Direction Type is set to Angle. Value of 0 corresponds to the positive X direction in image space.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: Overall strength of distortion. Negative values follow the directions backwards when tracing. NOTE: If you wire in only a source UV input, this parameter only shifts the UVs left and right.

parameters.label: Scale by Timestep
parameters.description: Adjusts the distortion's overall strength by the current timestep. The timestep is usually 1/$FPS, but in a sub-stepped simulation it represents the current step size.

parameters.label: Streak
parameters.description: The method used to combine the pixel values along the direction of distortion. Off: Don't smear the image. Blur: Average the samples together. This smears the image along the distortion direction. Min: Accept the smallest value encountered along the trajectory. This is useful when eroding an input shape. Max: Accept the largest value encountered along the trajectory. This is useful when adding edge roughness on an input shape.

parameters.label: Use Streak Weight Ramp
parameters.description: When Streak is Blur, Min, or Max , weight the samples encountered along the path. Use Streak Weight to weaken the values over the trajectory.

parameters.label: Streak Weight
parameters.description: When Use Streak Weight Ramp is on, this ramp acts as a multiplier on the pixel values when streaking. The left side of the ramp corresponds to the start of the trajectory. For example, when the Streak is Blur, the default linear ramp fades the pixels over their path. This makes the pixels more faint near the start. For more information about using ramps, see Ramp parameters.

parameters.label: Pixels per Step
parameters.description: When off, a single step is taken for each pixel to figure out the source location. Although this is fast, it produces inaccurate results when the directions or scales vary. Turning on this parameter uses a more accurate algorithm to trace curved trajectories. The provided value controls the tracing quality. More pixels per step allows the node to take larger steps (this runs faster, but may miss intermediate variations in the distortion directions).

parameters.label: Maximum Steps
parameters.description: Clamps the number of steps taken when Pixels per Step is on. You can raise this parameter (and lower Pixels per Step) if the distortion doesn't faithfully follow the directions. This can be especially noticeable when Streak is turned on.

entries.label: Dot Product
entries.summary: Performs dot product between two layers.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

entries.label: Edge Detect
entries.summary: Detects edges in the input image.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: Computes the edge based on the Luminance value of the input signal or Per Channel values of RGB and RGBA inputs.

parameters.label: Method
parameters.description: Choose an edge detection method. Sobel Prewitt: A 3x3 kernel detector with less contrast compared to Sobel. Laplacian Simple Thresholded Sobel

parameters.label: Normalize
parameters.description: Normalizes the output result, which makes the output values stay in the 0 to 1 range. The normalization constant is based on the maximum values that a 0 to 1 input image could have achieved.

parameters.label: Blur Before
parameters.description: Blurs the initial image before edge detection.

parameters.label: High Threshold
parameters.description: Identifies the strong pixels with intensities higher than the adjusted value. Applicable for the Thresholded Sobel method only.

entries.label: Edge Detect by Contour
entries.summary: Detects varying-width silhouette lines.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Thickness Scale
parameters.description: A scale of the kernel to detect edges. Defines a radius in pixel units to detect a difference between the current pixel and its neighbors. If there is a thickness input connected, then this value acts as a multiplier.

parameters.label: Edge Spread
parameters.description: The amount by which to multiply the Gaussian weight's spread. This controls the edge gradient spread.

parameters.label: Blur
parameters.description: Blurs the initial image before silhouette detection.

parameters.label: Contour Tolerance
parameters.description: Defines a minimal difference between the current pixel and the neighbor pixels that are part of the line.

parameters.label: Min Probe Radius
parameters.description: A minimal search radius for probe pixels.

entries.label: Edge Detect by Depth
entries.summary: Detects varying-width self-occluding silhouettes.

parameters.label: Thickness Scale
parameters.description: A scale of the kernel to detect edges. Defines a radius in pixel units to detect a difference between the current pixel and its neighbors. If there is a thickness input connected, then this value acts as a multiplier.

parameters.label: Edge Spread
parameters.description: The amount by which to multiply the Gaussian weight's spread. This controls the edge gradient spread.

parameters.label: Blur
parameters.description: Blurs the initial image before line detection.

parameters.label: Depth Tolerance
parameters.description: This parameter defines a minimal difference between the Z-depth of the current pixel and the Z-depth of its neighbor pixels that are part of the line.

parameters.label: Min Probe Radius
parameters.description: A minimal search radius for probe pixels.

entries.label: Edge Detect by Normal
entries.summary: Detects varying-width crease-lines.

parameters.label: Thickness Scale
parameters.description: A scale of the kernel to detect edges. Defines a radius in pixel units to detect a difference between the current pixel and its neighbors. If there is a thickness input connected, then this value acts as a multiplier.

parameters.label: Edge Spread
parameters.description: The amount by which to multiply the Gaussian weight's spread. This controls the edge gradient spread.

parameters.label: Blur
parameters.description: Blurs the initial image before line detection.

parameters.label: Normal Tolerance
parameters.description: Defines a minimal dot product value between the surface normal of the current pixel and the surface normals of its neighbor pixels that are part of the line.

parameters.label: Min Probe Radius
parameters.description: A minimal search radius for probe pixels.

entries.label: Eikonal
entries.summary: Computes distances by solving the Eikonal equation.

parameters.label: Speed
parameters.description: The global rate of change.

parameters.label: Iterations
parameters.description: One iteration is sufficient to converge if there is a uniform speed field. If the speed varies in complicated fashions, it may require more passes for the distances to fully propagate.

parameters.label: Tile Size
parameters.description: The size of the blocks that the layer is broken up into. This helps balance the serial and parallel components of the algorithm. If it has converged, this should have no effect on the behavior. The default values should be sufficient.

entries.label: Equalize
entries.summary: Equalizes colors by stretching or shifting their range.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. You can also set the RGBA channels to which you apply the effects of this node. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information. Toggle RGB: Turns the Red, Green, and Blue channels on and off. Red: Applies this node's effects to the Red channel. Green: Applies this node's effects to the Green channel. Blue: Applies this node's effects to the Blue channel. Alpha: Applies this node's effects to the Alpha channel.

parameters.label: Equalize By
parameters.description: The method used to equalize the colors. Stretch to Black and White: Map the minimum and maximum values found in the image to the Black and White values. Move Minimum to Black: Adjust the colors so the minimum value is the Black value. Move Maximum to White: Adjust the colors so the maximum value is the White value. Move Average to Value: Adjust the colors so the average luminance matches the given Target Average. Scale to Maximum Length: Scale the colors so the maximum luminance matches the given White value.

parameters.label: Fit Method
parameters.description: The method used to move a certain color to a goal value. NOTE: This parameter doesn't apply when Equalize By is set to Stretch to Black and White or Scale to Maximum Length. Shifting Values: Match the goal value by adding the difference to all pixels. Scaling Values: Match the goal value by scaling all pixels by the ratio.

parameters.label: Luminance Type
parameters.description: The luminance type to apply to the colors. SGI Luminance: This is a historical luminance computation used in Houdini, which is believed to originate with SGI. lum = 0.3086 * red + 0.6094 * green + 0.0820 * blue NTSC Luminance: The standard NTSC luminance computation, which is a common luminance option. lum = 0.299 * red + 0.587 * green + 0.114 * blue HDTV Luminance: The HDTV standard luminance from BT 709. lum = 0.2126 * red + 0.7152 * green + 0.0722 * blue Average: An average of the channels. Maximum Channel: The maximum of the channels. Minimum Channel: The minimum of the channels. Magnitude / Length: The length of the vector formed by taking the channels as components. For a mono input, this is the absolute value. Hue: Convert to HSV and return the hue channel. Saturation: Convert to HSV and return the saturation channel. Value: Convert to HSV and return the value channel. Red: Extract the red, or x, channel. Green: Extract the green, or y, channel. Blue: Extract the blue, or z, channel. Alpha: Extract the alpha, or w, channel.

parameters.label: Black
parameters.description: The value to use for black, which is usually 0.

parameters.label: White
parameters.description: The value to use for white, which is usually 1.

parameters.label: Target Average
parameters.description: When Equalize By is Move Average to Value, this is the goal average value.

entries.label: Error
entries.summary: Generates a message, warning, or error.

parameters.label: Number of Errors
parameters.description: The number of messages, warnings, or errors to generate.

parameters.label: Error Message
parameters.description: The text that displays when this notice is active. If this is an empty string, the notice isn't reported.

parameters.label: Severity
parameters.description: The severity and behavior of the notice's feedback. Message: This notice appears in the node info window. Warning: This notice displays a badge on the node and warning text in the node info window, but allows cooking to continue. Error: This notice displays a prominent badge on the node and error text in the node info window, but prevents subsequent nodes from cooking. NOTE: Use Error only for problems that the network can't recover from.

parameters.label: Report This Error
parameters.description: If this expression evaluates to a non-zero value, the node reports the notice.

entries.label: Feather
entries.summary: Smooths out sharp changes in contrast.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information.

parameters.label: Feather from High to Low
parameters.description: Leaves bright pixels unchanged, but raises the value of the surrounding darker pixels until the slope is met. When off, this leaves dark pixels unchanged and reduces the value of bright pixels to enforce the maximum slope. This determines the direction in which to enforce the change.

parameters.label: Include Border
parameters.description: Whether to source the initial pixel values from outside of the image bounds. You can use this parameter to create an edge-mask if you have constant borders. NOTE: Turn this on when tiling textures.

parameters.label: Feather Direction
parameters.description: The method used to perform the slope enforcement as a series of passes in each direction. Diamond: Enforce in horizontal and vertical passes, which results in diamond-shaped islands. Square: Enforce in diagonal passes, which results in square-shaped islands. Octagon: Enforce in horizontal, vertical, and diagonal passes, which results in octagon-shaped islands. Custom: Specify which passes to enforce using the Sweep Directions parameter. Circle: Enforce uniformally in all directions using a different algorithm. This results in circular-shaped islands.

parameters.label: Sweep Directions
parameters.description: When Feather Direction is Custom, this controls which directions apply feather. This lets you create a one-sided feather that you can use to make ramp-like shapes. -X: Applies the feather effect towards negative X. +X: Applies the feather effect towards positive X. -Y: Applies the feather effect towards negative Y. +Y: Applies the feather effect towards positive Y. -X-Y: Applies the feather effect diagonally towards negative X and negative Y. -X+Y: Applies the feather effect diagonally towards negative X and positive Y. +X-Y: Applies the feather effect diagonally towards positive X and negative Y. +X+Y: Applies the feather effect diagonally towards positive X and positive Y.

parameters.label: Feather Method
parameters.description: The method used to enforce the maximum change. The methods are inverses of each other. Distance for Unit Change: The distance (in image coordinates) where a 1 value can change to a 0 value. Change per Distance: The amount that a value can change over a unit distance (in image coordinates).

parameters.label: Distance for Unit Change
parameters.description: When Feather Method is Distance for Unit Change, this is the distance (in image coordinates) at which the values can change by a value of 1.

parameters.label: Change per Distance
parameters.description: When Feather Method is Change per Distance, this is the amount that values can change for every unit distance (in image coordinates).

entries.label: Fetch
entries.summary: Brings a COP node's outputs into the current network.

parameters.label: COP Path
parameters.description: The path to a COP node whose outputs you want to fetch. The outputs you bring in from the target COP become the Fetch COP's outputs. TIP: In a COP network, you can also drag the node you want to save into the COP Path parameter. The parameter adds the pathname.

parameters.label: Set Outputs from Selected COP
parameters.description: Sets up this node's output ports to match the outputs of the target COP set in the COP Path. This uses the target COP's signature to populate the number of outputs and their information in the Outputs parameter.

parameters.label: Outputs
parameters.description: The number of outputs to fetch from the target COP. These become the outputs of the Fetch COP.

parameters.label: Source Port
parameters.description: The index of the output to fetch from the target COP. This parameter is 0-indexed, which means 0 refers to the first output. Whether a Fetch COP's output uses an output of the target COP is based on either the set Source Port or, if off, the order of the outputs. When this parameter is off, the Fetch COP pulls in the output based on where the target and Fetch COP outputs are in order. For example, if the Fetch COP's third output has this parameter off, it exports the target COP's third output.

parameters.label: Output Label
parameters.description: The name of the target COP's output port, which is used as the Fetch COP's output name. The Setup Outputs from Selected COP parameter populates this with the output name from the selected COP, but you can rename it.

parameters.label: Output Type
parameters.description: The data type of the target COP's output port, which is used as the Fetch COP's output type. If you change this parameter value, you may receive an error if the source type can't convert into the new value. The Setup Outputs from Selected COP parameter populates this with the output type from the selected COP.

entries.label: Fill
entries.summary: Fills a layer with a constant value.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information.

parameters.label: Source
parameters.description: The source of the color with which to fill the layer. Value: Use a set integer ID for ID layers and a set Color for other layers. Image Location: Use a specific location from the input image. First Pixel: Use the first valid pixel in the input, which is the bottom left value. This is useful when you want to output the result of a prefix sum. Last Pixel: Use the last valid pixel in the input, which is the top right value. This is useful when you want to output the result of a prefix sum.

parameters.label: Color
parameters.description: When Source is Value, this is the color that mixes into Mono, UV, RGB, and RGBA layers.

parameters.label: ID
parameters.description: When Source is Value, this is the integer that mixes into ID layers.

parameters.label: Image Location
parameters.description: The image location (in image coordinates) in the input from which to extract the color, which then mixes back into the original layer. This uses the image location of the source input, except when there is a fillvalue input it can use. TIP: Click Icon:BUTTONS/layer_position_sample and then click a location in the image to set the Image Location.

entries.label: Fill Connected
entries.summary: Flood fills the connected regions of a layer.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information.

parameters.label: Seed Location
parameters.description: The location in image coordinates to start the flood fill. TIP: Click Icon:BUTTONS/layer_position_sample and then click a location in the image to set the Seed Location.

parameters.label: Tolerance
parameters.description: The maximum difference in pixel values from the seed location to continue to spread the fill. NOTE: Though fall-off can reduce the intensity, the fill is all-or-nothing for determining connectivity.

parameters.label: Fall Off
parameters.description: A ramp to adjust the alpha of the fill by how closely the pixels match the seed value. See Ramp parameters for more information.

parameters.label: Source
parameters.description: The value with which to replace the flooded area. Value: Use a specific color. Image Location: Sample a value from the fillvalue input. First Pixel: Use the first pixel of the fillvalue input. Last Pixel: Use the last pixel of the fillvalue input.

parameters.label: Color
parameters.description: The color to flood the image with.

parameters.label: ID
parameters.description: The ID to flood with when flooding ID layers.

parameters.label: Source Location
parameters.description: The location (in image space) in the fillvalue input to use as the flood color.

entries.label: Flip
entries.summary: Flips a layer horizontally, vertically, or diagonally.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information.

parameters.label: Flip Horizontally
parameters.description: Flips the layer about the y-axis in image space.

parameters.label: Flip Vertically
parameters.description: Flips the layer about the x-axis in image space.

parameters.label: Flip Diagonally
parameters.description: Flips the layer diagonally in image space, which flips the layer's resolution. For example, if you flip a 1920x1080 layer diagonally it becomes 1080x1920.

entries.label: Flow Block Begin
entries.summary: Start of a Flow simulation block.

parameters.label: Block Path
parameters.description: The path to the Flow Block End COP that's the final and closing node of this block. The Block End node must be at the same network level as this Block Begin node.

parameters.label: Buoyancy
parameters.description: The strength of the internal buoyancy force. The temperature field will be scaled by this to add a force to the velocity.

parameters.label: Buoyancy Direction
parameters.description: The direction that higher temperatures will move in.

parameters.label: Correct Initial Velocity
parameters.description: The incoming velocities will be pressure-projected to ensure they are valid velocities for fluid motion.

parameters.label: Layers to Advect
parameters.description: The wire-names of the layers to advect by the velocity layer. Note that the velocity layer v is always advected.

entries.label: Flow Block End
entries.summary: End of a Flow simulation block.

parameters.label: Simulate
parameters.description: While Flow will always need to feedback to do anything interesting, it can either work in a simulation mode where it feeds back over time; or for each frame run a set number of steps independently.

parameters.label: Time Scale
parameters.description: Control the size of the timestep within the simulation.

parameters.label: Iterations
parameters.description: When simulation is off, this controls the number of steps the solver will run in an evaluation.

parameters.label: Substeps
parameters.description: When simulation is on, each frame will be broken into this number of substeps. Substeps allow for more accurate behavior, but might also increase diffusion.

parameters.label: Reset Simulation
parameters.description: When Simulate is on, this clears the entire simulation cache.

parameters.label: Start Frame
parameters.description: When Simulate is on, this is the frame on the Houdini playbar where the simulation starts.

parameters.label: Live Simulation
parameters.description: When Simulate is on, this turns on live simulation to provide an interactive, non-deterministic simulation mode. It simulates independent of the playbar and isn't associated with any keyframes or caching. This parameter (and its associated parameters) is intended as a sandbox mode where you don't have to rely on the playbar. TIP: Live Simulation doesn't save the results like other simulation types in Houdini, so use a Stash COP to save results.

parameters.label: Toggle Live Simulation
parameters.description: When Live Simulation is on, this lets you pause and resume the live simulation. TIP: You can also use the Icon:BUTTONS/live_disable Live Simulation button to pause and resume live simulation. See Cooking controls for more information.

parameters.label: Live Tick
parameters.description: When Live Simulation is on, this is the current tick (frame) within the live simulation.

parameters.label: Cache Simulation
parameters.description: When Simulate is on, this enables the caching of the simulation. If the simulation is uncached, it will always have to cook from the start frame on any new frame.
parameters.heading: Caching

parameters.label: Cached Frames
parameters.description: When Simulate is on, this is how many frames behind the current frame to keep cached.
parameters.heading: Caching

parameters.label: Checkpoint Rate
parameters.description: When Simulate is on, this is the rate at which the node continually caches a single frame. For example, set this to 24 to cache frames 24, 48, 72, etc. This allows random-scrubbing to be faster as it only has to re-cook from the checkpoint frame. Set to 0 to disable checkpointing.
parameters.heading: Caching

parameters.label: Collision Iterations
parameters.description: Number of collision iterations to perform. Higher iterations will result in better avoidance of the collision object, but will increase execution times.
parameters.heading: Pressure Projection

parameters.label: Multigrid Iterations
parameters.description: Number of multigrid iterations to perform. Higher iterations will result in matching the goal divergence better, but will increase execution times.
parameters.heading: Pressure Projection

parameters.label: X Border
parameters.description: State of borders on the left and right sides of the image. Open borders allow flow to leave the image's bounds without resistance. Closed borders act like solid walls. When set to Periodic, flow leaving through the right side re-enters on the left side (and vice versa).
parameters.heading: Pressure Projection

parameters.label: Y Border
parameters.description: State of borders on the bottom and top sides of the image. Open borders allow flow to leave the image's bounds without resistance. Closed borders act like solid walls. When set to Periodic, flow leaving through the top side re-enters on the bottom side (and vice versa).
parameters.heading: Pressure Projection

entries.label: Flow Project Non-Divergent Multigrid
entries.summary: Removes divergent components from a 2-dimensional vector field.

parameters.label: Collision Iterations
parameters.description: Number of collision iterations to perform. Higher iterations will result in better avoidance of the collision object, but will increase execution times.

parameters.label: Multigrid Iterations
parameters.description: Number of multigrid iterations to perform. Higher iterations will result in matching the goal divergence better, but will increase execution times.

parameters.label: X Borders
parameters.description: State of borders on the left and right sides of the image. Open borders allow flow to leave the image's bounds without resistance. Closed borders act like solid walls. When set to Periodic, flow leaving through the right side re-enters on the left side (and vice versa).

parameters.label: Y Borders
parameters.description: State of borders on the bottom and top sides of the image. Open borders allow flow to leave the image's bounds without resistance. Closed borders act like solid walls. When set to Periodic, flow leaving through the top side re-enters on the bottom side (and vice versa).

entries.label: Font
entries.summary: Rasterizes text onto a layer from Type 1, TrueType, and OpenType fonts.

parameters.label: Font
parameters.description: The font to use for drawing the text. This parameter lists all known system fonts by default. You can browse for a specific font file if it's not listed.

parameters.label: Text
parameters.description: The text to generate.

parameters.label: Output Type
parameters.description: The output type of the node. Mask: Output the rasterized font as a mask. SDF: Output the rasterized font as a signed distance field.

parameters.label: Smoothing
parameters.description: Adds smoothing to produce non-jagged edges on the font.

parameters.label: Units
parameters.description: The unit of measurement used to determine the size of the smooth's width. Image: Sets the smooth's width to use image space units. Pixels: Sets the smooth's width to use units of the number of pixels.

parameters.label: Width
parameters.description: The width in image space or pixels to smooth the edge of the font.

parameters.label: Horizontal Alignment
parameters.description: The horizontal alignment of the text around the origin. Left: The beginning of the text aligns with the x-coordinate. For example, if Translate is (0.5,0), then the left-side of the text is flush against the 0.5 x-coordinate. Center: The middle of the text aligns with the x-coordinate. For example, if Translate is (0.5,0), then the center of the text is at the 0.5 x-coordinate. Right: The end of the text aligns with the x-coordinate. For example, if Translate is (0.5,0), then the right-side of the text is flush against the 0.5 x-coordinate.

parameters.label: Vertical Alignment
parameters.description: The vertical alignment of the text around the origin. First Line: The bottom of the text's first line aligns with the y-coordinate. For example, if Translate is (0,0.5), then the bottom of the text's first line is flush against the 0.5 y-coordinate. Top: The top of the text aligns with the y-coordinate. For example, if Translate is (0,0.5), then the top of the text's first line is flush against the 0.5 y-coordinate. Middle: The middle of the text aligns with the y-coordinate. For example, if Translate is (0,0.5), then the center of the text is at the 0.5 y-coordinate. Bottom: The bottom of the text aligns with the y-coordinate. For example, if Translate is (0,0.5), then the bottom of the text's last line is flush against the 0.5 y-coordinate.

parameters.label: Include Descender in Vertical Alignment
parameters.description: Sets the vertical alignment baseline to the descender of the text, rather than the text's baseline. The baseline is the line that letters sit on. A descender is the portion of a letter that extends below the text's baseline (for example, the stem of a lowercase p).

parameters.label: Font Size
parameters.description: The size of the font. The Scale parameter is applied on top of this value.

parameters.label: Translate
parameters.description: The origin of the text along the world x- and y-axes. TIP: Click Icon:BUTTONS/layer_position_sample and then click a location in the image to set the Translate.

parameters.label: Rotate Z
parameters.description: The rotation of the text about the world z-axis.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: The amount to scale factors along the x- and y-axes. This value is applied on top of the Font Size parameter value.

parameters.label: Tracking
parameters.description: The amount of space between characters in the x-direction (left and right).

parameters.label: Leading
parameters.description: The amount of space between characters in the y-direction (up and down). NOTE: This parameter takes effect when you have multiple lines of text.

parameters.label: Oblique Angle
parameters.description: The amount of slant (in degrees) to apply to the text.

parameters.label: Level of Detail
parameters.description: The number of points in polygonal fonts.

entries.label: Function
entries.summary: Applies a mathematical function to a layer.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: The amount by which to multiply the incoming layer.

parameters.label: Shift
parameters.description: The amount to add to the incoming layer after it's been multiplied by the Scale parameter.

parameters.label: Function Class
parameters.description: The functions to expose in this node. Arithmetic: Expose simple mathematical operations. Powers: Expose exponential and logarithmic functions. Trigonometry: Expose trigonometric and hyperbolic functions.

parameters.label: Arithmetic
parameters.description: When Function Class is Arithmetic, this is the mathematical operation to use. Absolute: Returns the absolute value of each channel. Sign: Returns the sign of each channel. Negative values return -1, 0 values return 0, and positive values return 1. Normalize: Normalizes the input layer by dividing each channel by the magnitude of the incoming vector. Negate: Negates each channel, which multiplies them by -1. Reciprocal: Returns the reciprocal of each channel, which divides a value of 1 by the channel's value. Floor: Returns the largest integer that is less than or equal to the channel's value. Round: Rounds each channel to the closest integer. Ceil: Returns the smallest integer that's greater than or equal to the channel's value. Modulus: Returns the fractional part of each channel's values.

parameters.label: Power
parameters.description: When Function Class is Powers, this is the exponential or logarithmic function to use. Square Root: Returns the square root of each channel. pow(x, E): Raises each channel to the power of the Exponent value. pow(b, x): Raises the Base value to the power of the channel's value. exp(x): Raises e (2.17128128) to the power of each channel's value. Base-Log: Returns the logarithm of each channel with respect to the Base value. Natural Log: Returns the natural logarithm of each channel (for base e).

parameters.label: Trigonometry
parameters.description: When Function Class is Trigonometry, this is the trigonometric or hyperbolic function to use. Sin: Returns the sine of each channel. Cos: Returns the cosine of each channel. Tan: Returns the tangent of each channel. Arc Sin: Returns the arc sine of each channel. Arc Cos: Returns the arc cosine of each channel. Arc Tan: Returns the arc tangent of each channel. To get the equivalent of atan2(), the UV to Polar COP node can be used. Hyperbolic Sin: Returns the hyperbolic sine of each channel. Hyperbolic Cos: Returns the hyperbolic cosine of each channel. Hyperbolic Tan: Returns the hyperbolic tangent of each channel.

parameters.label: Base
parameters.description: When Arithmetic is Modulus or Power is pow(b, x) or Base-Log, this is the base to use.

parameters.label: Exponent
parameters.description: When Power is pow(x, E), this is the exponent to use.

parameters.label: Angle Units
parameters.description: When Function Class is Trigonometry, this is the unit to use for the trigonometric function. Radians: Interpret the pixel values as radians. For example, this interprets a pixel value of 1 as one radian. Degrees: Interpret the pixel values as degrees. For example, this interprets a pixel value of 1 as one degree. Circles (2pi): Interpret the pixel values as circles. For example, this interprets a pixel value of 1 as one circle (which is 2 pi radians or 360 degrees).

entries.label: Gamma
entries.summary: Applies gamma correction to a layer, VDB, or attribute.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. You can also set the RGBA channels to which you apply the effects of this node. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information. Toggle RGB: Turns the Red, Green, and Blue channels on and off. Red: Applies this node's effects to the Red channel. Green: Applies this node's effects to the Green channel. Blue: Applies this node's effects to the Blue channel. Alpha: Applies this node's effects to the Alpha channel.

parameters.label: Gamma
parameters.description: The gamma correction factor to use. The common sRGB conversion is 2.2. By default this is an encoding gamma, so the color values are raised to the inverse of this exponent.

parameters.label: Invert
parameters.description: Switches from an encoding gamma to a decoding gamma. This does the opposite operation by inverting the gamma exponent.

parameters.label: Treat RGBA as Premultiplied
parameters.description: Un-premultiplies the RGBA layers before applying the contrast and then premultiplies the RGBA layers. RGBA layers are often premultiplied, so using an exponentiation that doesn't consider the alpha causes low coverage areas to be considered dark. This parameter makes the exponentiation work as expected.

entries.label: Geometry to Layer
entries.summary: Converts a 2D volume into a layer.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type to output. This must match the type of the volume, otherwise the conversion fails. NOTE: This doesn't collate volume triples (such as Cd.r, Cd.g, and Cd.b), so you may need a Volume Vector Join SOP before collating.

parameters.label: Precision
parameters.description: Overrides the output's precision, which is often the same precision as the input volume, with a set precision. 8: Set the precision to 8-bits. NOTE: This option is only possible with integer volumes and ID layers. 16: Set the precision to 16-bits. 32: Set the precision to 32-bits.

entries.label: Geometry to Layer
entries.summary: Converts a volume, VDB, or camera primitive into a layer or VDB.

parameters.label: Precision
parameters.description: The layer's storage precision. This controls how many bytes of storage each channel of the layer requires. More bytes allow for larger integer values or more accuracy for floating point values, but require more memory. 8: The channel uses 8-bits and defaults to quarter-precision. 16: The channel uses 16-bits and defaults to half-precision. 32: The channel uses 32-bits and defaults to full-precision.

parameters.label: Border
parameters.description: The sampling behavior outside of the incoming layer's boundaries. Automatically uses the layer's border property. See Border types for more information.

parameters.label: Slice
parameters.description: The plane to slice along when you convert a 3D volume. XY Plane: Slice the volume along the X and Y axes. YZ Plane: Slice the volume along the Y and Z axes. ZX Plane: Slice the volume along the Z and X axes.

parameters.label: Densify VDBs
parameters.description: Active regions of VDBs with constant values are collapsed into tiles to use less memory. However, as the GPU can't just-in-time unpack tiles; if one wants to do random writes the VDB has to be fully converted to leaves. This option will fully densify the VDB prior to converting. NOTE: This will move the VDB back to the CPU, and possibly require a massive amount of memory, so care should be used.

parameters.label: Set Imports from Geometry
parameters.description: Imports the volumes, VDBs, or camera primitives from the incoming geometry and populates the Outputs with the volumes', VDBs', or camera primitives' names and data types. When a volume, VDB, or camera primitive doesn't have a name attribute, Primitive Name is set to the volume's, VDB's, or camera primitive's primitive number.

parameters.label: Outputs
parameters.description: The number of outputs for the node, which are the number of volumes, VDBs, or camera primitives from the incoming geometry to convert. The Set Imports from Geometry parameter creates a node output for each volume, VDB, or camera primitive.

parameters.label: Primitive Name
parameters.description: The name of the volume, VDB, or camera primitive to convert. You can also set this to a primitive index. Use the dropdown menu to set the volume's, VDB's, or camera primitive's data type. When blank, it looks for a volume, VDB, or camera primitive with a primitive number that corresponds to the multiparm index. For example, the first multiparm index looks for primitive 0 by default. TIP: Enter vel.* in Primitive Name and set its data type to RGB to collate volume triples (such as vel.x, vel.y, and vel.z) into a single RGB layer. This also works when slicing 3D volumes.

parameters.label: Optional
parameters.description: If the specified volume or camera primitive can't be found, fall back to the layer defined by the size_ref input and the Default Value parameter. If the specified VDB cannot be found, fall back to the vdb_ref input.

parameters.label: Default Value
parameters.description: When Optional is on for an ID, Mono, UV, RGB, or RGBA type, this is the value to use for the layer.

entries.label: Glow
entries.summary: Adds glow to an image based on its luminance.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. A value of 1 means this node uses only the new value. The default value is 1. See Mask for more information.

parameters.label: Glow Threshold
parameters.description: Any pixel with a luminance value above this threshold has the glow effect. This lets you apply glow to only high luminance parts of your source layer. The default value is 0.75. TIP: Click Smallicon:BUTTONS/layer_sample and then click on the layer to set the Glow Threshold.

parameters.label: Output Glow Only
parameters.description: Outputs only the glow effect, which displays a preview of the effect. Turn this on if you want to make the glow a separate AOV or configure the glow further before you composite it on top of the source layer. TIP: Turn this parameter on and use the Blend COP to put the glow back over the original image. Wire the original image into the bg input and the Glow COP into the fg input of the Blend COP. You can then set the Blend COP's Mode and Mask parameters to configure how the glow effect mixes with the original image.

parameters.label: Brightness
parameters.description: The amount of brightness to apply to the glow effect. Higher values increase the brightness to lighten and expand the glow effect. Lower values decrease the brightness to dim and shrink the glow effect. The default value is 2.
parameters.heading: Glow

parameters.label: Saturation
parameters.description: The amount of saturation to apply to the glow effect. Higher values increase the saturation to make the hue of the glow effect more intense. Lower values decrease the saturation to make the hue of the glow effect less intense, which results in an absence of hue (grayscale). High luminance parts of a layer are often desaturated. The default value is 1.
parameters.heading: Glow

parameters.label: Tint
parameters.description: The tint (color) to apply to the glow effect. The default value is 1, 1, 1.
parameters.heading: Glow

parameters.label: Filter
parameters.description: The filter that the Blur COPs in the node's subnetwork use. Gaussian (default): Image:/images/nodes/cop/glow_only_gaussian.jpg Box: Image:/images/nodes/cop/glow_only_box.jpg
parameters.heading: Glow

parameters.label: Units
parameters.description: The unit of measurement that the Blur COPs in the node's subnetwork use to determine the size of the glow effect's radius. Image (default): Use image space to configure the size of the glow effect's radius. Pixels: Use pixels to configure the size of the glow effect's radius.
parameters.heading: Glow

parameters.label: Size
parameters.description: The size of the glow effect's radius in image space or pixels, which the Units parameter determines. Higher values expand the circumference of the radius to enhance the smooth blur of the glow effect. Lower values contract the circumference of the radius to remove blurring and sharpen the glow effect. When Units is Image, the default value is 0.05. When Units is Pixels, the default value is 3.
parameters.heading: Glow

parameters.label: Scale Size
parameters.description: Anistropic scaling of the size of the glow effect.
parameters.heading: Glow

entries.label: Heat Distort
entries.summary: Distorts the input layer to simulate heat around fire and other mirage effects.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information.

parameters.label: Distortion
parameters.description: The overall strength of distortion that scales the Base Distortion and Detail Distortion noises.
parameters.heading: General

parameters.label: Element Size
parameters.description: The size (in image coordinates) of the distortion that scales the Base Distortion and Detail Distortion noises. You can turn on the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button to adjust this further using the Element Scale parameter.
parameters.heading: General

parameters.label: Element Scale
parameters.description: When the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button is on, this is the per-axis scaling of the element size.
parameters.heading: General

parameters.label: Angle
parameters.description: The angle of distortion. A value of 0 corresponds to the positive X direction in image space.
parameters.heading: General

parameters.label: Accurate Distortion
parameters.description: When off, a single step is taken for each pixel to figure out the source location. Although this is fast, it produces inaccurate results when the directions or scales vary. Turning on this parameter uses a more accurate algorithm to trace curved trajectories. The provided value controls the tracing quality. More pixels per step allows the node to take larger steps (this runs faster, but may miss intermediate variations in the distortion directions).
parameters.heading: General

parameters.label: Streak Blur
parameters.description: Combines the pixel values along the direction of distortion by averaging the samples together. This smears the image along the distortion direction.
parameters.heading: General

parameters.label: Scale by Timestep
parameters.description: Adjusts the distortion's overall strength by the current timestep. The timestep is usually 1/$FPS, but in a sub-stepped simulation it represents the current step size.
parameters.heading: General

parameters.label: Base Distortion
parameters.description: Adds large scale distortion for the heat haze. This controls the generic shape of the heat waves. Turn on Detail Distortion to add finer detail.
parameters.heading: Base Distortion

parameters.label: Distortion Scale
parameters.description: The strength of the base distortion, which controls the generic shape of the heat waves. The Distortion parameter scales this amount.
parameters.heading: Base Distortion

parameters.label: Element Size Scale
parameters.description: The size (in image coordinates) of the base distortion that's scaled by Element Size. You can turn on the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button to adjust this further using the Element Scale parameter.
parameters.heading: Base Distortion

parameters.label: Element Scale
parameters.description: When the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button is on, this is the per-axis scaling of the element size.
parameters.heading: Base Distortion

parameters.label: Detail Distortion
parameters.description: Adds small scale distortion for the heat haze. This controls the finer details of the heat waves. Turn on Base Distortion to control the overall shapes.
parameters.heading: Detail Distortion

parameters.label: Distortion Scale
parameters.description: The strength of the detail distortion, which controls the finer details of the heat waves. The Distortion parameter scales this amount.
parameters.heading: Detail Distortion

parameters.label: Element Size Scale
parameters.description: The size (in image coordinates) of the detail distortion that's scaled by Element Size. You can turn on the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button to adjust this further using the Element Scale parameter.
parameters.heading: Detail Distortion

parameters.label: Element Scale
parameters.description: When the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button is on, this is the per-axis scaling of the element size.
parameters.heading: Detail Distortion

parameters.label: Cutoff
parameters.description: Lower this value to make the detail distortion appear where there is less base distortion. By default, the detail noise is only prominent where there is strong base distortion.
parameters.heading: Detail Distortion

parameters.label: Roughness
parameters.description: The amount of detail in the distortion. Higher values increase how fine the distortion details are.
parameters.heading: Detail Distortion

parameters.label: Blur Source
parameters.description: Blurs the source input relative to the strength of distortion. This increases how realistic the heat haze effect is.
parameters.heading: Blur Source

parameters.label: Blur Scale
parameters.description: The size of the source blur effect's radius in image space. You can turn on the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button to adjust this further using the Scale parameter.
parameters.heading: Blur Source

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: When the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button is on, this is the per-axis scaling of the blur size.
parameters.heading: Blur Source

parameters.label: Chromatic Aberration
parameters.description: Distorts the RGB channels of the image separately with different amounts. This creates colorization along the distortion unique to the chromatic aberration effect.
parameters.heading: Chromatic Aberration

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: The amount (in image space) to scale all three channels.
parameters.heading: Chromatic Aberration

parameters.label: Red
parameters.description: The amount (in image space) to scale the red channel. Higher values increase the offset between the channels, making the red channel expand outwards and become more apparent.
parameters.heading: Chromatic Aberration

parameters.label: Green
parameters.description: The amount (in image space) to scale the green channel. Higher values increase the offset between the channels, making the green channel expand outwards and become more apparent.
parameters.heading: Chromatic Aberration

parameters.label: Blue
parameters.description: The amount (in image space) to scale the blue channel. Higher values increase the offset between the channels, making the blue channel expand outwards and become more apparent.
parameters.heading: Chromatic Aberration

parameters.label: Time Offset
parameters.description: The amount of time (in seconds) that's added to the start frame.
parameters.heading: Animation

parameters.label: Pulse Length
parameters.description: The interval length (in seconds) of the noise's pulse in the third dimension. Lower values increase the rate at which the noise switches its appearance, while higher values decrease this rate.
parameters.heading: Animation

parameters.label: Direction
parameters.description: Adds directional movement to the heat distortion. This is useful when the heat haze is moving along a constant direction, such as a mirage that moves upwards.
parameters.heading: Animation

parameters.label: Angle
parameters.description: The angle of distortion. A value of 0 corresponds to the positive X direction in image space.
parameters.heading: Animation

parameters.label: Speed
parameters.description: How fast the heat haze moves in the given direction. Higher values increase the speed of the heat haze's movement.
parameters.heading: Animation

entries.summary: Distorts the input layer using another layer to simulate heat around fire and other mirage effects.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: When the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button is on, this is the per-axis scaling of the blur size.

parameters.label: Blur Noise
parameters.description: Blurs the noise input before it's used to generate the direction map when no dir input is wired in.
parameters.heading: Blur Noise

parameters.description: The size of the noise blur effect's radius in image space. You can turn on the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button to adjust this further using the Scale parameter.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: When the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button is on, this is the per-axis scaling of the blur size.

entries.label: HeightField Clip
entries.summary: Clamps height values to a minimum and/or maximum value.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of clipped height to mix with the original height.

parameters.label: Compute Range
parameters.description: Click to fill in the Lower Limit and Upper Limit parameters with the minimum and maximum values of the input height layer.

parameters.label: Lower Limit
parameters.description: When enabled, clamps height values that are below the limit. TIP: Click Smallicon:BUTTONS/layer_sample and then click the layer in the viewport to set the Lower Limit.

parameters.label: Upper Limit
parameters.description: When enabled, clamps height values that are above the limit. TIP: Click Smallicon:BUTTONS/layer_sample and then click the layer in the viewport to set the Upper Limit.

parameters.label: Clamped Values
parameters.description: The value that replaces the clamped values. Replace with Limit Value: Clamped values are replaced by the value they went over or under. For example, when clamping between 0 and 1, -1 becomes 0 and 2 becomes 1. Soft Clip: Clamped values are smoothly transitioned across a Soft Clip Range to avoid hard edges.

parameters.label: Soft Clip Direction
parameters.description: The direction to smoothly transition the clamped values. Soft Clip Outside Range: Transition of the clamped values below the Lower Limit and above the Upper Limit, extending the effects of clamping. Soft Clip Inside Range: Transition of the clamped values above the Lower Limit and below the Upper Limit, narrowing the effects of clamping.

parameters.label: Soft Clip Range
parameters.description: A smoothing range for the transition from the limit value to the original values.

entries.label: HeightField Erode
entries.summary: Simulates hydraulic and thermal erosion at a specific scale to create more realistic terrain.

parameters.label: Simulate
parameters.description: Turns on simulation, so the node updates with the Playbar. When turned off, the node simulates a fixed number of erosion iterations.

parameters.label: Iterations
parameters.description: When Simulate is off, the number of erosion timesteps to simulate. This controls the duration of the erosion process.

parameters.label: Reset Simulation
parameters.description: When Simulate is on, clears the entire simulation cache. ((Ctrl))-click to also reset to the start frame.

parameters.label: Start Frame
parameters.description: When Simulate is on, this is the frame on the Houdini playbar where the simulation starts.

parameters.label: Substeps
parameters.description: When Simulate is on, how many iterations of the simulation to run per frame. Higher values create stronger erosion effects, but also take longer to simulate.

parameters.label: Cache Simulation
parameters.description: Turns on caching of the simulation. If the simulation is uncached, it will always have to cook from the start frame on any new frame.
parameters.heading: Caching

parameters.label: Cached Frames
parameters.description: How many frames behind the current frame to keep cached.
parameters.heading: Caching

parameters.label: Checkpoint Rate
parameters.description: The rate at which the node continually caches a single frame. For example, set this to 5 to cache frames 5, 10, 15, and such. This allows random-scrubbing to be faster as it only has to re-cook from the checkpoint frame. Set to 0 to turn off checkpointing.
parameters.heading: Caching

parameters.label: Feature Size
parameters.description: The width of erosion features, in meters. Higher values will create wider channels, slopes, and deposits. Lower values will create sharper features. The smallest possible feature size is 3x the input terrain's pixel size. Features will be clamped to this size.
parameters.heading: Erosion Model

parameters.label: Spread Iterations
parameters.description: How many iterations of material transport to simulate in each frame. The number of iterations, together with the Feature Size, control the distance that eroded material can be transported within a single frame.
parameters.heading: Erosion Model

parameters.label: Random Seed
parameters.description: The seed used to randomize the erosion process. With each new value, the distribution of erosion features changes.
parameters.heading: Erosion Model

parameters.label: Erodability
parameters.description: How prone the terrain is to hydro and thermal erosion. You can use the erodability input to vary the softness of the terrain.
parameters.heading: Erosion Model

parameters.label: Flow Force
parameters.description: The force of hydro erosion. With 0 you turn off hydro erosion.
parameters.heading: Hydro

parameters.label: Bank Angle
parameters.description: Controls the angle of channel walls. Higher values will create steeper channels that appear to cut deeper into the terrain, creating a jagged appearance.
parameters.heading: Hydro

parameters.label: Rainfall Coverage
parameters.description: The amount of rainfall to simulate each frame as a proportion of the terrain's surface. This controls the intensity of hydro erosion in each frame. You can use the rainfall input to vary the rainfall across the terrain.
parameters.heading: Hydro

parameters.label: Slope Influence
parameters.description: Controls how closely streams will follow the slope of the terrain. Higher values will result in winding channels. Lower values will result in straighter channels.
parameters.heading: Hydro

parameters.label: Erosion Rate
parameters.description: The rate at which a stream erodes and accumulates material from the terrain.
parameters.heading: Hydro

parameters.label: Deposition Rate
parameters.description: Controls how quickly sediment is deposited once the stream's transport capacity is exceeded.
parameters.heading: Hydro

parameters.label: Removal Rate
parameters.description: The rate at which a stream's accumulated sediment decays. Higher values will _reduce_ the amount of deposited sediment, allowing hydro erosion to cut deeper into the terrain, creating a rocky appearance.
parameters.heading: Hydro

parameters.label: Evaporation Rate
parameters.description: The rate at which a stream's sediment capacity decays. Lower values will create more prominent channels that persist across longer distances with a rocky appearance. Higher values will create smaller local depressions with a soil-like or sandy appearance.
parameters.heading: Hydro

parameters.label: Weathering Force
parameters.description: The force of thermal erosion. With 0 you can turn off thermal erosion.
parameters.heading: Thermal

parameters.label: Cut Angle
parameters.description: The angle that thermal erosion will cut until. A lower angle will make the cuts flatter, and allow for more thermal erosion to take place.
parameters.heading: Thermal

parameters.label: Repose Angle
parameters.description: The angle at which the thermal erosion debris will remain in place without sliding.
parameters.heading: Thermal

entries.label: HeightField Mask by Feature
entries.summary: Creates a mask based on different features of the heightfield.

parameters.label: Smooth Radius
