parameters.description: The blur radius in local space used to smooth the input heightfield before the features are measured.

parameters.label: Blend Mode
parameters.description: When more than one feature is being measured, you can choose a compositing operation to combine each feature's mask. Add: Add the feature masks together. Multiply: Multiply the feature masks together. Average: Compute the average value of the feature masks. Minimum: Compute the minimum value of the feature masks. Maximum: Compute the maximum value of the feature masks.

parameters.label: Invert Mask
parameters.description: When enabled, inverts the resulting mask values.

parameters.label: Mask by Slope
parameters.description: Generate a mask based on the slope of the heightfield.
parameters.heading: Slope

parameters.label: Min Slope Angle
parameters.description: Mask areas with slope greater than or equal to this value.
parameters.heading: Slope

parameters.label: Max Slope Angle
parameters.description: Mask areas with slope less than or equal to this value.
parameters.heading: Slope

parameters.label: Slope Ramp
parameters.description: Controls the value of the mask over the range from the Min Slope Angle to the Max Slope Angle.
parameters.heading: Slope

parameters.label: Mask by Height
parameters.description: Generate a mask based on the height.
parameters.heading: Height

parameters.label: Compute Range
parameters.description: Click to fill in the Min Height and Max Height parameters with the minimum and maximum values of the input height layer.
parameters.heading: Height

parameters.label: Min Height
parameters.description: Mask areas with height greater than or equal to this value.
parameters.heading: Height

parameters.label: Max Height
parameters.description: Mask areas with height less than or equal to this value.
parameters.heading: Height

parameters.label: Height Ramp
parameters.description: Controls the value of the mask over the range from the Min Height to the Max Height.
parameters.heading: Height

parameters.label: Mask by Curvature
parameters.description: Generate a mask based on the maximum curvature.
parameters.heading: Peaks and Valleys

parameters.label: Max Curvature
parameters.description: Mask areas with absolute curvature less than or equal to this value.
parameters.heading: Peaks and Valleys

parameters.label: Curvature Ramp
parameters.description: Controls the value of the mask over the range from negative Max Curvature to the positive Max Curvature.
parameters.heading: Peaks and Valleys

parameters.label: Mask by Direction
parameters.description: Generate a mask based on the heightfield's slope direction.
parameters.heading: Direction

parameters.label: Goal Angle
parameters.description: Define an angle and all surfaces facing that direction get masked. 0 degrees is in the direction of increasing pixels along the height layer's width.
parameters.heading: Direction

parameters.label: Angle Spread
parameters.description: Mask areas with this amount of variance from the Goal Angle. The range of directions is the Goal Angle minus/plus the Angle Spread.
parameters.heading: Direction

parameters.label: Direction Ramp
parameters.description: Controls the value of the mask over the range, from the Goal Angle minus the Angle Spread, to the Goal Angle plus the Angle Spread.
parameters.heading: Direction

parameters.label: Mask by Occlusion
parameters.description: Generate a mask based on the heightfield's ambient occlusion.
parameters.heading: Occlusion

parameters.label: Compute Range
parameters.description: Click to fill in the Minimum Occlusion and Maximum Occlusion parameters with the minimum and maximum ambient occlusion of the input height layer.
parameters.heading: Occlusion

parameters.label: Minimum Occlusion
parameters.description: Mask areas with ambient occlusion greater than or equal to this value.
parameters.heading: Occlusion

parameters.label: Maximum Occlusion
parameters.description: Mask areas with ambient occlusion less than or equal to this value.
parameters.heading: Occlusion

parameters.label: Height Scale
parameters.description: The scale applied to input height values before computing ambient occlusion. Higher values exaggerate the amount of occlusion and small variations in height appear more pronounced.
parameters.heading: Occlusion

parameters.label: Occlusion Ramp
parameters.description: Controls the value of the mask over the range from the Minimum Occlusion to the Maximum Occlusion.
parameters.heading: Occlusion

parameters.label: View Radius
parameters.description: The distance in local space to send rays to determine if a pixel is occluded. Higher values extend the reach of the rays, producing more precise results, but at the cost of longer calculation times. Lower values decrease the distance you send the rays.
parameters.heading: Quality

parameters.label: Step Scale
parameters.description: How many steps (in buffer space) to take along the rays to determine if a pixel is occluded. Higher values create less steps and therefore calculate faster, but may miss thin features since the steps are more spread out. Lower values create more steps, which are closer together.
parameters.heading: Quality

parameters.label: Sample Count
parameters.description: The amount of rays to send to determine if a pixel is occluded. Higher values increase the number of rays sent and provide more accurate measurements, but at the cost of longer calculation times. Lower values decrease the number of rays sent.
parameters.heading: Quality

parameters.label: Sample from Hemisphere
parameters.description: Divides the point's calculated angle by 90 degrees instead of 180 degrees.
parameters.heading: Quality

entries.label: HeightField Project
entries.summary: Projects 3D geometry onto a heightfield.

parameters.label: Project
parameters.description: Specifies which height sample to rasterize. Minimum Height: Rasterize the minimum height sample. Maximum Height: Rasterize the maximum height sample.

parameters.label: Max Projection Height
parameters.description: The maximum absolute height that can be projected. The node will not project geometry that is outside of this range.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of projected height to mix with the original height.

parameters.label: Blend Mode
parameters.description: Specifies how the projected height is mixed with the input height. Blend: Replaces the input height with the projected height. Add: Adds the projected height to the input height. Multiply: Multiplies the input height by the projected height. Maximum: Takes the maximum of the projected height and the input height. Minimum: Takes the minimum of the projected height and the input height.

parameters.label: Output Projection Only
parameters.description: When enabled, outputs only the projected height values.

entries.label: HeightField Slump
entries.summary: Simulates loose material sliding down inclines and piling at the bottom.

parameters.label: Slump Mode
parameters.description: The method used to slump the input debris layer. Smooth: Slump the debris using smooth diffusion. This models liquid-like transport mechanisms. Granular: Slump the debris using chunky slumping with randomization. This models granular flow transport mechanisms. Rainfall: Slump the debris by suspending and transporting the debris in streams. This models hydraulic erosion transport mechanisms.

parameters.label: Debris Scale
parameters.description: The scale factor applied to the debris layer before simulating the slumping processes. This allows you to convert a mask into a depth of debris. If the debris input is unwired, the simulation begins with a constant depth of debris set by this Debris Scale.

parameters.label: Spread Iterations
parameters.description: How many iterations of material transport to simulate.

parameters.label: Repose Angle
parameters.description: The maximum slope, measured in degrees from the horizontal, at which loose solid material will remain in place without sliding.

parameters.label: Spread Rate
parameters.description: Controls how fast material spreads across the terrain in each iteration.

parameters.label: Random Seed
parameters.description: The seed used to randomize the slumping process.

parameters.label: Flow Force
parameters.description: When Slump Mode is set to Rainfall, controls how strongly streams erode the debris.

parameters.label: Rainfall Coverage
parameters.description: When Slump Mode is set to Rainfall, the amount of rainfall to simulate each frame as a proportion of the terrain's surface.

parameters.label: Slope Influence
parameters.description: When Slump Mode is set to Rainfall, controls how closely streams will follow the slope of the terrain. Lower values will result in straighter channels. Higher values will result in winding channels.

parameters.label: Erosion Rate
parameters.description: When the Slump Mode is set to Rainfall, the rate at which a stream erodes and accumulates material from the terrain.

parameters.label: Deposition Rate
parameters.description: When the Slump Mode is set to Rainfall, the rate at which a stream deposits its excess accumulated sediment.

parameters.label: Removal Rate
parameters.description: When the Slump Mode is set to Rainfall, the rate at which a stream's accumulated sediment decays. Higher values will _reduce_ the amount of deposited sediment, allowing hydro erosion to cut deeper into the terrain, creating a rocky appearance.

parameters.label: Evaporation Rate
parameters.description: When the Slump Mode is set to Rainfall, the rate at which a stream's sediment capacity decays. Lower values will create more prominent channels that persist across longer distances with a rocky appearance. Higher values will create smaller local depressions with a soil-like or sandy appearance.

parameters.label: Remove Debris from Input Height
parameters.description: Before simulating the slumping process, remove the input debris from the input height.

parameters.label: Add Debris to Output Height
parameters.description: After simulating the slumping process, add the slumped debris to the input height.

entries.label: HeightField Strata
entries.summary: Adds sedimentary layering patterns to a HeightField.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of strata noise to mix into the input height layer.

parameters.label: Blend Mode
parameters.description: Specifies how the strata layer is combined with the input height layer. Add: Adds the foreground to the background. Subtract: Subtracts the foreground from the background. Multiply: Multiplies the background by the foreground. Difference: Takes the absolute difference between the foreground and the background. Maximum: Takes the maximum of the foreground and background. Minimum: Takes the minimum of the foreground and background.

parameters.label: Output Strata Only
parameters.description: When enabled, outputs only the strata layer, instead of blending the strata with the input height layer.

parameters.label: Amplitude
parameters.description: The multiplication factor for the strata noise applied by the node before the Center adjustment. For example, a value of 0.5 makes a pixel value of 0.5 become 0.25.
parameters.heading: Range

parameters.label: Center
parameters.description: The center of the output strata noise range, which offsets the pixel values. For example, a value of 0.5 makes a pixel value of 0.5 become 1.
parameters.heading: Range

parameters.label: Noise Contrast
parameters.description: The amount of contrast to apply to the noise before the Amplitude and Center parameters. You can use this parameter to make the strata noise more extreme.
parameters.heading: Range

parameters.label: Noise Type
parameters.description: The underlying noise function that's iteratively sampled to generate the strata noise. Simplex: Create Perlin noise on a simplex grid. Perlin: Create Perlin noise on a regular grid. This type of noise generates more natural results. Worley Cellular F1: Create Worley noise using its distance to the closest Worley point. This generates a cell-like pattern. Worley Cellular F2-F1: Create Worley noise using the difference between its second closest and closest points. This generates a cell border-like noise. White (Random): Create white noise where each noise element is given a constant, but random value. Alligator: Create Alligator noise to produce a bumpy output that resembles alligator skin. Sparse Convolution: Create a type of value noise that smoothly blends values on a regular grid. This type of noise generates natural results that are smoother than Perlin noise.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Metric
parameters.description: When Noise Type is Worley Cellular F1 or Worley Cellular F2-F1, you can define different metrics for computing the distance to a point. Euclidean: Use the length of the line segment between the two axial points to define the distance between the two points. This can result in circular shapes. See Euclidean distance for more information. Manhattan: Use the sum of the differences between the two axial points to define the distance between the two points. This can result in diamond shapes. See Taxicab geometry for more information. Chebyshev: Use the maximum difference between the two axial points to define the distance between the two points. This can result in square shapes. See Chebyshev distance for more information.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Worley Jitter
parameters.description: When Noise Type is Worley Cellular F1 or Worley Cellular F2-F1, this is the amount of random noise to add to each point's position on a grid. The random noise is added before the Worley noise measures the distance to the points. NOTE: Values greater than 1 may produce artifacts as they can jitter past the search radius
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Units
parameters.description: The unit of measurement to control the strata noise pattern. See /copernicus/spaces for more information.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Element Size
parameters.description: The size of the basic element of the strata noise in image or local coordinates (determined by the Space). You can turn on the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button to adjust this further using the Element Scale parameter.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Element Scale
parameters.description: When the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button is on, this is the per-axis scaling of the element size for anisotropic noise.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.description: An offset for the entire noise function in image or local coordinates (determined by the Space parameter).
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Strata Size
parameters.description: The thickness of the strata.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Strata Offset
parameters.description: The offset of the strata.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Tilt
parameters.description: The angle of the strata in degrees. When set to zero, the layers are perpendicular to the height. If increased, the layers cut across the height.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.description: The rotation of the strata about the Origin.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Origin
parameters.description: The center of rotation of the strata in image or local coordinates (defined by the Space parameter).
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Add Layers
parameters.description: When enabled, adds numerous additional Layers of strata noise, with randomly varying orientations.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Layers
parameters.description: When Add Layers is enabled, the number of additional layers of strata noise to add.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Roughness
parameters.description: When Add Layers is enabled, the amount to scale the amplitude of each successive strata noise.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Tilt Variance
parameters.description: When Add Layers is enabled, the maximum amount in degrees to vary each additional strata from the set Tilt.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Rotate Variance
parameters.description: When Add Layers is enabled, the maximum amount in degrees to vary each additional strata from the set Rotate.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.description: When Add Layers is enabled, the random seed used to vary the orientation of the additional strata layers.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Base Height Influence
parameters.description: Controls how much the baseheight input affects the pattern of the strata.
parameters.heading: Pattern

parameters.label: Fractal Type
parameters.description: How to accumulate successive layers of noise to create finer-scale details. None: Don't add any additional layers of noise. Sharp: Add sharp layers of noise. Dampened: Add dampened layers of noise. Terrain: Add smoother layers of noise resembling terrain. Hybrid Terrain: Add smooth layers of noise that are sharpened at the peaks resembling rocky terrain.
parameters.heading: Fractal

parameters.label: Max Octaves
parameters.description: The number of times the noise is scaled and layered on top of itself.
parameters.heading: Fractal

parameters.label: Lacunarity
parameters.description: The amount to scale the noise for each iteration.
parameters.heading: Fractal

parameters.label: Octave Offset
parameters.description: The amount to offset the noise for each iteration.
parameters.heading: Fractal

parameters.label: Roughness
parameters.description: The amount to scale the amplitude of each successive noise.
parameters.heading: Fractal

parameters.label: NOTE
parameters.description: The node applies the post-processing operations in the order they're listed.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Fold
parameters.description: Sets the noise values to the absolute value. For example, a pixel value of -2 becomes 2. NOTE: This parameter doesn't impact the output when there's only positive values.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Complement
parameters.description: Sets the pixel value x to 1 - x. NOTE: This method works for values in the 0 to 1 range. For images outside of this range, using Complement results in negative or out of range values.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.description: The amount to pull the medium grey values (around 0.5) towards zero (if Bias is less than 1) or one (if Bias is greater than 1). A bias value of 0.5 doesn't affect the values. Image:/images/nodes/cop/postprocessing_bias.jpg
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Gain
parameters.description: The amount to pull the medium grey values (around 0.5) together, while values around 0 and 1 are pulled apart. A gain value of 0.5 doesn't affect the noise values. Image:/images/nodes/cop/postprocessing_gain.jpg
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Gamma
parameters.description: The overall gamma of the generated noise. Values greater than 1 increase the range of values in originally bright areas, which darkens the noise. Values less than 1 stretch out the range of values for originally dark areas, which increases the overall brightness of the noise.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Contrast
parameters.description: The amount to expand or shrink the overall range of tonal values. Each noise value is pushed towards (if Contrast is less than 1) or away from (if Contrast is greater than 1) medium grey values (around 0.5). NOTE: This is not the same as Noise Contrast, which appears in some noise nodes and applies contrast during the noise function.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Clamp Minimum
parameters.description: Clamps values below the specified threshold.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Clamp Maximum
parameters.description: Clamps values exceeding the specified threshold.
parameters.heading: Post Processing

entries.label: HeightField Terrace
entries.summary: Creates stepped plains from the slopes of a HeightField.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of terraces to mix with the original height.

parameters.label: Compute Range
parameters.description: Click to fill in the Min Height and Max Height parameters with the minimum and maximum values of the input height layer.

parameters.label: Min Height
parameters.description: The minimum height value where terraces are created. TIP: Click Smallicon:BUTTONS/layer_sample and then click the layer in the viewport to set the Min Height.

parameters.label: Max Height
parameters.description: The maximum height value where terraces are created. TIP: Click Smallicon:BUTTONS/layer_sample and then click the layer in the viewport to set the Max Height.

parameters.label: Method
parameters.description: The method of specifying the terrace step size. Step Size: Specify the terrace step size directly. Number of Terraces: Specify the terrace step size as a number of steps in the range from the Min Height and Max Height.

parameters.label: Step Size
parameters.description: When the Method is set to Step Size, sets the height of each terrace step.

parameters.label: Terraces
parameters.description: When the Method is set to Number of Terraces, sets the number of terrace steps to fit between the Min Height and the Max Height.

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.description: Shifts the height where each terrace step occurs.

parameters.label: Random Step
parameters.description: Scales the random height that is added to each terrace level. With Random Step set to 0, each terrace level has the same step size.

parameters.label: Step Seed
parameters.description: When Random Step is non-zero, the seed generates the random height that is added to each terrace level.

parameters.label: Add Layers
parameters.description: This options adds numerous additional Layers of terraces with randomly varying offsets.

parameters.label: Layers
parameters.description: When Add Layers is enabled, the number of layers of terraces to add.

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.description: When Add Layers is enabled, the seed sets the random offset of each layer of terraces.

parameters.label: Global Seed
parameters.description: The global seed for randomizing the terraces steps and layers.

entries.label: HeightField Visualize
entries.summary: Visualizes layers as a colored heightfield by converting them into geometry

parameters.label: Height Scale
parameters.description: The amount to scale the incoming heightfield's values. This converts them to the proper world space locations. The world space is required for visualization.

parameters.label: Height Offset
parameters.description: The amount to offset the heightfield's values.

parameters.label: Split Channels
parameters.description: Split vector volumes into individual float volumes. The resulting volumes will be named <<input>>.x, <<input>>.y, <<input>>.z, and <<input>>.w.
parameters.heading: Conversion

parameters.label: Tint
parameters.description: Controls the layer to visualize as a tint on the heightfield. Color: Tint the heightfield with the color input. Mask: Tint the heightfield with the mask input.
parameters.heading: Conversion

parameters.label: Input Range
parameters.description: Sets the minimum and maximum values in the tint layer to map to the start and end of the ramp.
parameters.heading: Conversion

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: Sets the transformation to perform before the node applies the ramp. No Ramp: Linearly map the values with respect to the Input Range, extrapolating past the minimum and maximum values. Clamped Ramp: Clamp the values by the Input Range. Periodic Ramp: Wrap the values around the Input Range.
parameters.heading: Conversion

parameters.label: Diffuse Ramp
parameters.description: Sets the color ramp to visualize values in the tint layer. The ramp's range is set by the Input Range.
parameters.heading: Conversion

entries.label: HeightField Transform 3D
entries.summary: Transforms a height layer in 3D.

parameters.label: Transform Order
parameters.description: Order in which transformations occur.

parameters.label: Rotate Order
parameters.description: Order in which rotations occur.

parameters.label: Translate
parameters.description: Amount of translation along the XYZ axes.

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.description: Amount of rotation, in degrees, about the XYZ axes.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: Non-uniform scaling along the XYZ axes.

parameters.label: Shear
parameters.description: Amount of shearing. The three values represent shearing in the X direction on the XY plane, in the X direction on the XZ plane, and in the Y direction on the YZ plane, respectively.

parameters.label: Uniform Scale
parameters.description: Uniform scaling along all three axis.

parameters.label: Invert Transformation
parameters.description: Use the inverse of the transformation. This is the transformation which undoes the specified transformation. Two HeightField Transform 3D COPSs with all parameters but this equal will cancel out each other's transformation.

parameters.label: Pivot Translate
parameters.description: The translation value of the local pivot space for transformations.
parameters.heading: Pivot Transform

parameters.label: Pivot Rotate
parameters.description: The rotation value of the local pivot space for transformations.
parameters.heading: Pivot Transform

parameters.label: Apply Transform Scale to Height
parameters.description: Scale the height layer pixels with the 3D transform.
parameters.heading: Height Scaling

parameters.label: Grid Scale
parameters.description: Scales the grid spacing, stretching or contracting the height layer horizontally.
parameters.heading: Height Scaling

parameters.label: Height Scale
parameters.description: Scales the height values, stretching or contracting the height layer vertically.
parameters.heading: Height Scaling

parameters.label: Height Offset
parameters.description: Shifts the height values, moving the height layer vertically.
parameters.heading: Height Scaling

entries.label: HeightField Transform 2D
entries.summary: Transforms a height layer in 2D.

parameters.label: Units
parameters.description: The unit of measurement that determines the size of translations. See /copernicus/spaces for more information.

parameters.label: Transform Order
parameters.description: Order in which transformations occur.

parameters.label: Translate
parameters.description: The amount to translate the height layer in image, texture, pixel, or local space (determined by the Units parameter).

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.description: The amount to rotate the height layer about the pivot in degrees.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: A non-uniform scale of the height layer.

parameters.label: Shear
parameters.description: A XY shear transformation of the height layer.

parameters.label: Uniform Scale
parameters.description: Uniform scaling of the height layer.

parameters.label: Pivot Translate
parameters.description: The translation value of the local pivot space for transformations in image, texture, pixel, or local space (determined by the Units parameter).

parameters.label: Invert Transformation
parameters.description: Use the inverse of the transformation. This is the transformation which undoes the specified transformation. Two HeightField Transform 2D COPs with all parameters but this equal will cancel out each other's transformation.

parameters.label: Apply Transform Scale to Height
parameters.description: Scale the height layer pixels with the 2D transform.
parameters.heading: Height Scaling

parameters.label: Grid Scale
parameters.description: Scales the grid spacing, stretching or contracting the height layer horizontally.
parameters.heading: Height Scaling

parameters.label: Height Scale
parameters.description: Scales the height values, stretching or contracting the height layer vertically.
parameters.heading: Height Scaling

parameters.label: Height Offset
parameters.description: Shifts the height values, moving the height layer vertically.
parameters.heading: Height Scaling

entries.label: HeightField to Mono
entries.summary: Converts a heightfield into a grayscale mono layer.

parameters.label: Compute Range
parameters.description: Click to fill in the Input Min and Input Max parameters with the minimum and maximum values of the input height layer.

parameters.label: Input Min
parameters.description: Height values less than or equal to this value are remapped to Output Min. TIP: Click Smallicon:BUTTONS/layer_sample. Then click the layer in the viewport to set the Input Min.

parameters.label: Input Max
parameters.description: Height values greater than or equal to this value are remapped to be Output Max. TIP: Click Smallicon:BUTTONS/layer_sample. Then click the layer in the viewport to set the Input Max.

parameters.label: Output Min
parameters.description: The lower end of the output range.

parameters.label: Output Max
parameters.description: The higher end of the output range.

parameters.label: Clamp to Output Range
parameters.description: When disabled, values outside the input range can extend beyond the output range. When enabled, the output values are clamped to the output range.

entries.label: Height to Normal
entries.summary: Converts a height layer to a normal layer.

parameters.label: Normal Type
parameters.description: The method used to store the normals (see Normals for more information). Signed (-1 to 1): Output signed normals, compatible with geometry attributes. Offset (0 to 1): Output offset normals, compatible with normal maps.

parameters.label: Height Scale
parameters.description: The amount to globally scale the height before computing normals. Higher numbers create steeper normals.

parameters.label: Read Pixels outside Image
parameters.description: Derivatives at the boundary read outside of the image. When off, derivatives at the boundary are restricted to the image range. Turning this parameter on is useful when building seamless textures with a wrap border type. Turn this off if you want to avoid artificial flattening of the derivative at the boundary in a clamp border type, as it acts like an extrapolation.
parameters.heading: Derivatives

parameters.label: Kernel Size
parameters.description: The distance (in buffer elements) to compute the derivative, which might remove stepping artifacts from the derivative. A derivative is often computed with adjacent pixels, but if the values are slowly varying there may not be enough bit-depth to get smooth derivatives.
parameters.heading: Derivatives

entries.label: Hex Tile
entries.summary: Randomly tiles texture.

parameters.label: Size
parameters.description: The tiles' size based on canvas XY-coordinates.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: The global scale of hex tiles.

parameters.label: Scale Random
parameters.description: The amount to randomly scale each hexagonal texture cell.

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.description: The global rotation of hex tiles.

parameters.label: Rotate Random
parameters.description: The amount to randomly rotate each hexagonal texture cell.

parameters.label: Random Seed
parameters.description: The seed that the random number generator uses. Change this parameter to generate a new random color for each seed.

parameters.label: Contrast
parameters.description: The contrast between blended hexagonal cells.

parameters.label: Falloff
parameters.description: The contrast falloff between blended hexagonal cells. A value of 0 creates a hard transition.

parameters.label: Weight Exp
parameters.description: The weight of transition areas between hexagonal cells exponentially.

entries.label: Histogram
entries.summary: Builds a histogram from a layer.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: The type of histogram to output. Colored Bars: Output the histogram as a horizontal ramp. Each vertical line is colored by how many pixels in the source fall in that bucket range. If alpha is in the source, this affects the bars and can result in clipping. Separate Bars: Output the histogram as separate horizontal bars for each channel. Each bar is grayscale, where red is the bottom bar and alpha (if present) is the top bar. Graph: Control how high to draw the bar instead of controlling the bar's intensity. Each channel is done independently, which results in a mixture of red, green, blue, and alpha bars overlapping.

parameters.label: Buckets
parameters.description: The number of buckets to divide the range into. Finer buckets provide a more accurate graph. NOTE: The Histogram node bases the height or intensity of a bar on the percentage of total pixels that fall into the bucket.

parameters.label: Minimum
parameters.description: The value at which to start the histogram. This is usually 0 for black. TIP: Click Smallicon:BUTTONS/layer_sample and then click on the layer to set the Minimum.

parameters.label: Maximum
parameters.description: The value at which to end the histogram. This is usually 1 for white. TIP: Click Smallicon:BUTTONS/layer_sample and then click on the layer to set the Maximum.

parameters.label: Outside Values
parameters.description: The method used to manage pixel values that lie outside of the histogram range. Discarding and clamping are done per-channel, so the totals of each channel may not be the same if you use Discard. Discard: Ignore values outside of the range so they don't contribute to the histogram. Clamp: The values outside of the range contribute to either the first or last bucket. This method causes the buckets to have extreme values, but can help you determine how much the window has cropped out.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: The amount to scale the percentage of total pixels that fall into the bucket. This is often a small percentage, so increasing that value enhances the chart's legibility.

parameters.label: Channel Scope
parameters.description: The RGBA channels to which you apply the effects of this node. NOTE: The number of bars or channels don't change, so unscoped channels have zero contributions. Toggle RGB: Turns the Red, Green, and Blue channels on and off. Red: Applies this node's effects to the Red channel. Green: Applies this node's effects to the Green channel. Blue: Applies this node's effects to the Blue channel. Alpha: Applies this node's effects to the Alpha channel.

entries.label: HSV Adjust
entries.summary: Converts between RGB and HSV color spaces, or modifies HSV.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information.

parameters.label: Operation
parameters.description: The operation that this node performs. Hue/Sat/Val Adjust: Modify the hue, saturation, and value of the pixels. Convert RGB to HSV: Convert the RGB space into the HSV space. Convert HSV to RGB: Convert the HSV space into the RGB space.

parameters.label: Hue Shift
parameters.description: The amount (in degrees) to shift the hue around the HSV cone. This changes all colors to different hues. Gray pixels aren't affected.

parameters.label: Hue Shift Mode
parameters.description: When a hueshift input is wired in, this is how to shift the source layer's hue values. Min/Max: Remap the incoming hueshift to set 0 and 1 to specific degrees. Width: Remap the incoming hueshift to set the width between 0 and 1 to a specific distance in degrees.

parameters.label: Hue Shift Min
parameters.description: When Hue Shift Mode is Min/Max, this is the degree to remap 0 to on the hue wheel. A value of 0 represents no shift. For example, when set to -60 the hue is shifted by -60 degrees where the input equals 0. The node interpolates for values between this setting and the Hue Shift Max.

parameters.label: Hue Shift Max
parameters.description: When Hue Shift Mode is Min/Max, this is the degree to remap 1 to on the hue wheel. A value of 0 represents no shift. For example, when set to 88 the hue is shifted by 88 degrees where the input equals 1. The node interpolates for values between this setting and the Hue Shift Min.

parameters.label: Hue Shift Width
parameters.description: When Hue Shift Mode is Width, this is the distance in degrees to remap the width between 0 and 1 to on the hue wheel. A value of 0 represents no shift. For example, when set to 40 this remaps 0 to -20 and 1 to 20.

parameters.label: Keep Luminance
parameters.description: Maintains the perceptual luminance of the pixel when hues shift since some hues appear brighter than others.

parameters.label: Saturation Scale
parameters.description: The amount to increase (>1) or decrease (<1) the color saturation of the image. This multiplies the saturation.

parameters.label: Saturation Shift
parameters.description: The amount to shift the color saturation of the pixels. Higher values add to the saturation while lower values subtract from the saturation. Shifting is normally used only to reduce the saturation, otherwise grayscale elements suddenly take on a random color.

parameters.label: Value Scale
parameters.description: The amount to adjust the value (brightness) of the pixel. This multiplies the brightness.

parameters.label: Value Shift
parameters.description: The value (brightness) to add to all pixels. Higher values add to the brightness while lower values subtract from the brightness.

parameters.label: Treat RGBA as Premultiplied
parameters.description: Treats RGBA as premultiplied, which multiplies the red, green, and blue channels by the alpha channel.

entries.label: Hyperbolic Tile
entries.summary: Generates hyperbolic polygon tiles for texture patterns.

parameters.label: Iterations
parameters.description: The number of times that the base regular polygon's pattern repeats within the boundary of the Poincaré disk. Each copy reflects and inverts the previous copy's pattern.

parameters.label: Polygons
parameters.description: The amount of sides to give the base regular polygon.

parameters.label: Rectanglize
parameters.description: Changes the Poincaré disk's boundary to the image space square instead of a circle. Choose a mapping type from the dropdown menu to set how the pattern within the Poincaré disk's boundary maps outwards to occupy the entire image space square. Conformal: Preserves the angles of the tiles. Each corner of the square is a singularity of this mapping, so artifacts may appear near the corners. Elliptic Grid: Uses an elliptic grid to map the Poincaré disk to the square. This creates curved radial grid lines in the square region. NOTE: Though this mapping type minimizes distortion in the diagonal regions of the square, it can cause additional stretching near the corners. Squircle: Uses squircular mapping from the Poincaré disk to the square. This stretches the radial direction uniformly in a straight manner. NOTE: The diagonal regions of this mapping type have more distortion than the Elliptic Grid type. However, the overall appearance may appear more uniform because the distortion is more evenly distributed. Equal Area: Uses a map that preserves the area up to the constant ratio. This can make the base polygon include additional sides and vertices.

parameters.label: Stretch to Fit
parameters.description: When Rectanglize is on and the size_ref has a rectangle input, this option stretches the square to fill the given rectangular region.

parameters.label: Flattening
parameters.description: The amount to flatten circular arcs in the base polygon. When set to 0, the base polygon fits within the Poincaré disk. Higher values expand the circular arcs in the base regular polygon out towards the image's border to flatten them. They can't be entirely flat because straight lines must pass the center of the Poincaré disk to define the hyperbolic regular polygons.

parameters.label: Size
parameters.description: The length of straight lines in the base polygon. This parameter corresponds to the radius of the Poincaré disk when Flattening is 0.

parameters.label: Tile Fitting
parameters.description: Fills the image to tiles when the uv output is used. A value of 0 makes the image appear as a square within each tile. Increasing the value to 1 stretches the image to fill the entire tile area.

parameters.label: Poincaré Disk Mask
parameters.description: Displays only the pattern that's within the boundary of the Poincaré disk. This parameter doesn't apply if Rectanglize is on.

entries.label: ID to Mask
entries.summary: Creates a mask from an ID layer based on filtering parameters.

parameters.label: ID Pattern
parameters.description: The group syntax to use to filter IDs. If this is blank, the node filters all IDs. TIP: Click Smallicon:BUTTONS/layer_sample and then click on the IDs you want to select to set the ID Pattern.

parameters.label: Invert Mask
parameters.description: Inverts the mask that the node generates.

parameters.label: Keep by Range
parameters.description: Filters IDs based on a range.
parameters.heading: Keep by Range

parameters.label: Range Type
parameters.description: Specifies the range that determines how to filter the IDs. Start and End (default): Set a range that starts and ends with a specific ID. The range includes the start and end ID. Start and Length: Set a range that starts with a specific ID and ends once the range includes a specific number of IDs.
parameters.heading: Keep by Range

parameters.label: Start ID
parameters.description: When this parameter is on and the Range Type is Start and End, this is the ID at the start of the range. For example, a value of 0 means the range includes IDs greater than and equal to 0. The default value is 0. When this parameter is off, there is no limit for the start of the range.
parameters.heading: Keep by Range

parameters.label: End ID
parameters.description: When this parameter is on and the Range Type is Start and End, this is the ID at the end of the range. For example, a value of 100 means the range includes IDs less than and equal to 100. The default value is 100. When this parameter is off, there is no limit for the end of the range.
parameters.heading: Keep by Range

parameters.label: Range Offset
parameters.description: When Range Type is Start and End, this is the value to add to the Start ID and End ID parameters. The default value is 0.
parameters.heading: Keep by Range

parameters.label: Start ID
parameters.description: When Range Type is Start and Length, this is the ID at the start of the range. For example, a value of 0 means the range includes IDs greater than and equal to 0. The default value is 0.
parameters.heading: Keep by Range

parameters.label: Length
parameters.description: When Range Type is Start and Length, this is how many IDs to include in the range. The default value is 5.
parameters.heading: Keep by Range

parameters.label: Select/of
parameters.description: The number of IDs to select out of every block of IDs. For example, set Select to 1 and of to 2 so the filter selects half of the integer values. The Offset parameter impacts whether the selected values are odd or even. The default values are 1 of 2.
parameters.heading: Range Filter

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.description: The start of the range filter, which is measured relative to the start of the range. The default value is 0.
parameters.heading: Range Filter

parameters.label: Keep by Chance
parameters.description: Filters by selecting a subset of IDs by random chance.
parameters.heading: Keep by Chance

parameters.label: Probability
parameters.description: The chance (percentage) that the group includes the ID. For example, a value of 0.1 means that the group includes about 10% of the IDs. The default value is 0.5.
parameters.heading: Keep by Chance

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.description: The initial seed that determines which elements to include. Changing this value causes each ID to generate a new random value, which results in a new pattern. The default value is 30.
parameters.heading: Keep by Chance

parameters.label: Keep within Mask
parameters.description: When you have a mask input, this filters by keeping a subset of IDs within a mask layer.
parameters.heading: Keep within Mask

parameters.label: Threshold
parameters.description: When you have a mask input, pixels in the mask layer that have a value greater than this threshold are considered when masking. The default value is 0.5.
parameters.heading: Keep within Mask

entries.label: ID to RGB
entries.summary: Converts an ID layer, VDB, or attribute into an RGB layer, VDB, or attribute.

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.description: The seed that the random number generator uses. Changing this parameter generates a new random color for each seed.

entries.label: ID to SDF
entries.summary: Computes a signed distance field from changes in ID values.

parameters.label: Invert
parameters.description: Inverts the sign. Since an ID field is two-sided and has no inside or outside, its values usually have a positive distance. Inverting therefore changes this to a negative distance.

parameters.label: Iterations
parameters.description: The number of times to compute the distance to changes in ID values. A value of 1 is sufficient when there's a uniform speed field, but you may need higher values for the distances to fully propagate if the speed has complex variations.

parameters.label: Tile Size
parameters.description: The size of the blocks to break the layer up into. This parameter helps balance the serial and parallel components of the algorithm. This shouldn't affect the behavior when the algorithm's converged. The default values should be sufficient.

entries.label: Illegal Pixel
entries.summary: Detects and then fixes or highlights illegal pixels in images.

parameters.label: Illegal Pixels
parameters.description: The method used to fix or flag illegal pixels. Often, fixing is used when you want to continue with the image as-is and flagging is used to debug the shader. Fix by Blending Surrounding Pixels: Replace a bad pixel by blending the surrounding pixels together. This method is best for small numbers or isolated pixels. Fix by Zeroing: Clear the NANs so that downstream operations behave. This method doesn't visually correct the image. Show with Highlight: Show bad pixels by highlighting them based on the Highlight Color value. Show by Isolating: Show bad pixels by highlighting them and clearing all correct pixels.

parameters.label: Highlight Color
parameters.description: When Illegal Pixels is Show with Highlight, this is the color in which to highlight the bad pixels.

parameters.label: Detect
parameters.description: The type of illegal pixels to find. NaN Values: Find only NaN values. Infinite Values: Find only infinite values. NaN and Infinite Values: Find both NaN and infinite values. Custom: Find values according to a custom Rule.

parameters.label: Rule
parameters.description: The custom rule to use. Less Than: Flag pixels less than the comparison value. Less Than or Equal: Flag pixels less than or equal to the comparison value. Greater Than: Flag pixels greater than the comparison value. Greater Than or Equal: Flag pixels greater than or equal to the comparison value. Equal: Flag pixels equal to the comparison value.

entries.label: Integrate Volume
entries.summary: Integrates a VDB along camera rays.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. The output is mono when the input's a Float VDB. The output is RGB when the input's a Vector VDB, accumulating each channel separately along the view ray. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Move to Origin
parameters.description: Moves the output layer to the origin.

parameters.label: Depth Conversion
parameters.description: Convert the mindepth and maxdepth inputs to distances from the camera from this kind of input. Distance: Doesn't modify the inputs since they're already distances. Depth: The inputs are depths. These are distances projected along the forward direction of the camera, like you can get from Node:cop/rasterizegeo. Height: The inputs are heights. These are displacements from the imaging plane toward the camera position.

parameters.label: Operation
parameters.description: The value to compute along each view ray. Integral: Integrate the input field along the view ray. This adds up the value in the VDB, sampled along the view ray. Transmittance: Calculate the transmittance along the view ray. This treats the input volume as optical density. Minimum: Find the minimum value along the view ray. If not hit, this is infinity. Maximum: Find the maximum value along the view ray. If not hit, this is -infinity.

parameters.label: Density Scale
parameters.description: The amount by which to scale the density. The node applies this scale after it linearly maps and applies the ramp to the density.
parameters.heading: Density

parameters.label: Min
parameters.description: The lower bound of the interval to linearly map to (0, 1). For each sample of the VDB, the node linearly maps the Density interval to (0, 1).
parameters.heading: Density

parameters.label: Max
parameters.description: The upper bound of the interval to linearly map to (0, 1). For each sample of the VDB, the node linearly maps the Density interval to (0, 1).
parameters.heading: Density

parameters.label: Ramp Mode
parameters.description: The transformation to perform before the node applies the ramp. No Ramp: Don't apply the map. This turns off the ramp. Clamped Ramp: Clamp the remapped values to 0 and 1, respectively. Periodic Ramp: Wrap the remapped values around at 0 and 1.
parameters.heading: Density

parameters.label: Density Ramp
parameters.description: The map to apply to the density after it's linearly remapped to (0, 1). See Ramp parameters for more information.
parameters.heading: Density

parameters.label: Seed Jitter with Time
parameters.description: Makes the sample location jittering depend on time.
parameters.heading: Quality

parameters.label: Sample Jitter Scale
parameters.description: The amount by which to jitter sample locations. When 0, sample locations are always at the centre of ray slices. When 1, sample locations can be drawn from anywhere along their respective ray slice. There is never more than one sample drawn per ray slice.
parameters.heading: Quality

parameters.label: Stratification Jitter Scale
parameters.description: The amount by which to jitter ray slice locations. This is a single offset applied to each view ray, not per sample. When 0, the start of ray slice #0 coincides with the ray origin. When 1, the start of ray slice #0 varies from backward and forward along the ray by half the step length.
parameters.heading: Quality

parameters.label: Integration Step Size
parameters.description: The length of ray slices. This is the expected distance between samples when samples are jittered.
parameters.heading: Quality

parameters.label: Max Step Count
parameters.description: Used to prevent the OpenCL kernel from running forever or timing out. You shouldn't need to change the 4096 value unless rastering a very deep volume.
parameters.heading: Quality

parameters.label: Transmittance Cutoff
parameters.description: When Operation is Integral or Transmittance, this is the transmittance of the accumulated portion of the ray after which to stop raymarching. A value of -1 turns this off, which may be necessary to calculate the integral of a field that doesn't represent an optical density. This is an optimization for when a very dense region of the volume is encountered, where almost none of the light from behind this region reaches the camera so you can stop raymarching early to save time. Due to rounding error, it's possible for the accumulated transmittance to reach 0 despite this not being physically possible, and this is seen when rasterizing very dense volumes.
parameters.heading: Quality

entries.label: Invert
entries.summary: Inverts a layer, VDB, or attribute.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. You can also set the RGBA channels to which you apply the effects of this node. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information. Toggle RGB: Turns the Red, Green, and Blue channels on and off. Red: Applies this node's effects to the Red channel. Green: Applies this node's effects to the Green channel. Blue: Applies this node's effects to the Blue channel. Alpha: Applies this node's effects to the Alpha channel.

parameters.label: Invert By
parameters.description: The method used to invert the values. Complement: The pixel value x is set to 1 - x. NOTE: This method works for images in the 0 to 1 range. For images outside of this range, using Complement results in negative or out of range values. To resolve this, you can use a Clamp COP. Negate: The pixel value x is set to - x. This is useful for switching a value's sign. Reciprocal: The pixel value x is set to 1 / x.

entries.label: Invoke Geometry
entries.summary: Runs a program saved into geometry using inputs plugged into this node.

parameters.label: Iterations
parameters.description: The number of times to run the program, with outputs feeding back as inputs into the subsequent iteration. NOTE: This node can repeatedly run the program only when its outputs can be converted into the respective inputs (matched by index). Otherwise, this node performs a single iteration and sends a warning.

parameters.label: Set Inputs and Outputs from Incoming Program
parameters.label_norm: set inputs and outputs from incoming program
parameters.description: Sets up this node's input and output ports to match the incoming program. This populates the Inputs and Outputs multiparameters using the program's signature.

parameters.label: Inputs
parameters.description: The number of this node's input ports, which are based on the Block Inputs of the Block Begin COP that generated the program geometry.

parameters.label: Input Label
parameters.description: The name of the program input to bind the respective incoming layer to. This is matched against the Input Name values on the Block Begin COP that generated the program geometry.

parameters.label: Input Type
parameters.description: The data type of the input and the corresponding port on this node.

parameters.label: Outputs
parameters.description: The number of this node's output ports, which are based on the Block Outputs of the Block End COP that generated the program geometry.

parameters.label: Output Label
parameters.description: The name of the program output that comes out of the respective port. This is matched against the Output Name values on the Block End COP that generated the program geometry.

parameters.label: Output Type
parameters.description: The data type of the output and the corresponding port on this node.

entries.label: Julia Fractal
entries.summary: Computes the Julia set to create a fractal.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the node outputs. You can output a mono (Float) layer of the normalized time-to-escape or an ID (Integer) layer that contains the actual number of iterations before escape. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: The amount to scale the incoming x and y image coordinates.

parameters.label: Real Coefficient
parameters.description: The real coefficient to set up the Julia fractal.

parameters.label: Imaginary Coefficient
parameters.description: The imaginary coefficient to set up the Julia fractal.

parameters.label: Escape Radius
parameters.description: The threshold at which the point is considered to have escaped.

parameters.label: Maximum Iterations
parameters.description: The number of iterations at which to conclude the point hasn't escaped.

entries.label: Kuwahara Filter
entries.summary: Applies the Kuwahara filter, which creates painterly effects.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information.

parameters.label: Method
parameters.description: The method used to compute the filter. NOTE: The Kuwahara filter requires access to k^2 pixels for every pixel, where k is the kernel diameter, which means large kernels can become expensive. Approximate: Rather than computing the standard deviations and means for each pixel, generate it in a single pre-pass. This speeds up computation but causes variations in radius, which affects neighboring pixels. Exact: Compute the filter exactly for each pixel. GPUs often make this practical even for large radii.

parameters.label: Luminance
parameters.description: The common standard deviation for quadrant selection. When the node processes more than one channel, the filter still picks the same source quadrant for all channels. SGI Luminance: This is a historical luminance computation used in Houdini, which is believed to originate with SGI. lum = 0.3086 * red + 0.6094 * green + 0.0820 * blue NTSC Luminance: The standard NTSC luminance computation, which is a common luminance option. lum = 0.299 * red + 0.587 * green + 0.114 * blue HDTV Luminance: The HDTV standard luminance from BT 709. lum = 0.2126 * red + 0.7152 * green + 0.0722 * blue Average: An average of the channels. Maximum Channel: The maximum of the channels. Minimum Channel: The minimum of the channels. Magnitude / Length: The length of the vector formed by taking the channels as components. For a mono input, this is the absolute value. Hue: Convert to HSV and return the hue channel. Saturation: Convert to HSV and return the saturation channel. Value: Convert to HSV and return the value channel. Red: Extract the red, or x, channel. Green: Extract the green, or y, channel. Blue: Extract the blue, or z, channel. Alpha: Extract the alpha, or w, channel.

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: The radius (in pixels) of each of the four regions on which to perform blur. The radius offsets the four regions so they don't overlap.

parameters.label: Blur Scale
parameters.description: When computing the average of a region, this is the amount to scale the size of the region. Lower values select a sharper source area, but use the larger area to determine the standard deviation. Higher values increase the blur effect but don't affect which quadrant is picked.

parameters.label: Blend to Blur
parameters.description: A value of 0 picks the average from the region with the smallest standard deviation. A value of 1 averages the averages, which effectively performs a larger blur. Inbetween values adjust the weighting, increasing the weight of areas with large standard deviations.

parameters.label: Separation
parameters.description: The amount to scale the offset of the four regions, which is determined by the Radius. A value of 0 makes all the regions sample the same location, causing this to be a box blur. Values over 1 make the regions sample dislocated areas of the image.

entries.label: Layer from Curves
entries.summary: Render Curves into a Layer.

parameters.label: Width
parameters.description: Width in image space of the curves.
parameters.heading: Look

parameters.label: Width along Curve
parameters.description: Adjust the width of the curve along its length.
parameters.heading: Look

parameters.label: Profile
parameters.description: Adjust the profile output across the width of the curve.
parameters.heading: Look

parameters.label: Color along Length
parameters.description: Set the color along the length of the curve.
parameters.heading: Look

parameters.label: Color across Width
parameters.description: Set the color across the width of the curve.
parameters.heading: Look

parameters.label: UV Twist Rate
parameters.description: Scroll the u value across the length of the curve; this allows for a twisted rope look on the texture map.
parameters.heading: Look

parameters.label: Tile
parameters.description: Replicate the curves so the layer will tile.
parameters.heading: Rasterizaton

parameters.label: Tile Size
parameters.description: The size of the tile in image space. For non square images this should reflect the aspect ratio.
parameters.heading: Rasterizaton

parameters.label: Force Tilable V
parameters.description: Round the v channel of any intrinsic:uv output down to the closest integer to allow tiling.
parameters.heading: Rasterizaton

parameters.label: Joints
parameters.description: How to join the corners of curve. Round: Use a round circle to apply the corners. Sharp: Extend the corner to a sharp point.
parameters.heading: Rasterizaton

parameters.label: Endpoints
parameters.description: How to rasterize the endpoints of the input curves. Flat: Leave the two ends of the curves as flat. Round: Create rounded (spherical) caps at the two ends of the curves.
parameters.heading: Rasterizaton

parameters.label: Max Joint Scale
parameters.description: The amount to multiply the curve width to control how far the corner extends. This prevents spikes at sharp corners in curves.
parameters.heading: Rasterizaton

parameters.label: Resample
parameters.description: Resample the input curves to smooth them out.
parameters.heading: Rasterizaton

parameters.label: Segment Length
parameters.description: The length to break the curves into.
parameters.heading: Rasterizaton

parameters.label: Treat Polygons As
parameters.description: How to inteprolate polygonal curves. Straight: Directly interpolate maintaining the straight lines. Subdivision: Smooth the curves with a subdivision approach. This will not interpolate the original points. Interpolating: Smooth the curves with a bicubic approach, this will interpolate the original points but oscillate.
parameters.heading: Rasterizaton

parameters.label: Resample by Polygon Edge
parameters.description: Each edge of the polygon will be resampled independently. This option will preserve corners in the input.
parameters.heading: Rasterizaton

entries.label: Layer from VDB
entries.summary: Sets a layer's values from a VDB.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

entries.label: Layer Properties
entries.summary: Edits basic layer metadata.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Precision
parameters.description: The layer's storage precision. This controls how many bytes of storage each channel of the layer requires. More bytes allow for larger integer values or more accuracy for floating point values, but require more memory. 8: The channel uses 8-bits and defaults to quarter-precision. 16: The channel uses 16-bits and defaults to half-precision. 32: The channel uses 32-bits and defaults to full-precision.

parameters.label: Use Fixed Point Storage
parameters.description: Stores 8-bit unsigned and 16-bit signed floating point values as fixed point values. This clamps 8-bit fixed point values to the 0 to 1 range and 16-bit fixed point values to the -1 to 1 range. This parameter applies to only non-ID layers. Storage types are propagated through the network, so nodes often use the same storage type as their inputs. Fixed point storage offers more consistent precision for the same amount of storage compared to floating point, but can only represent values in a limited range. TIP: Hold ((MMB)) on the node to use the node info window to check the storage type of each layer.

parameters.label: Border
parameters.description: The sampling behavior outside of the incoming layer's boundaries. Automatically uses the layer's border property. See Border types for more information.

parameters.label: Type Info
parameters.description: The layer's type information. This controls the visualization of the layer in the 3D viewport. See Type info for more information.

entries.label: Layer to Geometry
entries.summary: Converts a layer into a 2D volume.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The type of layer to accept for conversion. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Empty Geometry If Unwired
parameters.description: If the input isn't connected, produce an empty geometry rather than erroring.

entries.label: Layer to Points
entries.summary: Creates points based on a layer.

parameters.label: Method
parameters.description: The method used to create the points from a layer. All Pixel: Create a point for each pixel in the input. Non-Zero Pixels: Create a point if the pixel isn't zero. Count per Pixel: Each pixel stores how many points to create, so create that many points per pixel. Unique Values: Create a point for each unique value in the input layer. If the input layer's integer values are 1, 1, 5, 3, 23, 3, and 5 for example, then the unique values are 1, 5, 3, and 23. This means the node makes four points. This option is useful in workflows such as with the Segment by Connectivity COP where you want to create a point for each segment. Count from First Pixel: The first pixel in the layer stores how many points to create, so create that many points. Count from Last Pixel: The last pixel in the layer stores how many points to create, so create that many points.

parameters.label: Layer Attrib
parameters.description: The name of the integer attribute to set with the value of the pixel that generated the point. This stores the original pixel's value. This parameter is useful when you want to know the original value, such as for non-zero or unique values.

parameters.label: Index Attrib
parameters.description: The name of the integer attribute that stores the raw offset (x + y * xres) of the source pixel in the input layer's buffer. This lets you know where the point came from.

parameters.label: Set Positions
parameters.description: Initializes the position attribute with the pixel location. When off, the position attribute is zero. TIP: Zero attributes don't require memory, so turn this off for optimization if you don't care about the position.

parameters.label: Ignore Minus One
parameters.description: Ignores the layer value -1 when computing unique values. A value of -1 in an ID layer often means an invalid ID, so ignoring it ensures that points are created for only valid IDs. When off, -1 is generated with the unique values.

parameters.label: Point Attributes
parameters.description: The amount of additional point attributes, which are available in later OpenCL nodes. This lets you define the default attributes of the geometry.

parameters.label: Name
parameters.description: The name of the point attribute.

parameters.label: Class
parameters.description: The classification of the point attribute. NOTE: Only the Detail and Point options are directly applicable since this node creates points. If there are no primitives or vertices, they still have attribute tables.

parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: The type of attribute to create, which is either an integer or float. See Data types for more information.

parameters.label: Tuple Size
parameters.description: The tuple size of the attribute.

entries.label: Layer to VDB Leaf Points
entries.summary: Creates a point for each leaf of a VDB that would be in an envelope.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Thickness
parameters.description: A global scale on the thickness input, allowing a 0-1 layer to be rescaled to world units.

entries.label: Lens Distort
entries.summary: Adds radial and tangential distortion to a layer based on OpenCV coefficients.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information.

parameters.label: Low Order Barrel (k1)
parameters.description: Positive values will produce a barrel distortion, and negative values will produce a pincushion distortion. The k<sub>1</sub> radial distortion constant in the intrinsic camera parameters defined by OpenCV.

parameters.label: Mid Order Barrel (k2)
parameters.description: Positive values will produce a barrel distortion, and negative values will produce a pincushion distortion. The k<sub>2</sub> radial distortion constant in the intrinsic camera parameters defined by OpenCV.

parameters.label: High Order Barrel (k3)
parameters.description: Positive values will produce a barrel distortion, and negative values will produce a pincushion distortion. The k<sub>3</sub> radial distortion constant in the intrinsic camera parameters defined by OpenCV.

parameters.label: Low Order Inverse (k4)
parameters.description: Negative values will produce a barrel distortion, and positive values will produce a pincushion distortion. The k<sub>4</sub> radial distortion constant in the intrinsic camera parameters defined by OpenCV.

parameters.label: Mid Order Inverse (k5)
parameters.description: Negative values will produce a barrel distortion, and positive values will produce a pincushion distortion. The k<sub>5</sub> radial distortion constant in the intrinsic camera parameters defined by OpenCV.

parameters.label: High Order Inverse (k6)
parameters.description: Negative values will produce a barrel distortion, and positive values will produce a pincushion distortion. The k<sub>6</sub> radial distortion constant in the intrinsic camera parameters defined by OpenCV.

parameters.label: Vertical Tilt (p1)
parameters.description: Positive values will give the effect that the top of the image plane is farther away than the bottom, and negative values will do the opposite. The p<sub>1</sub> tangential distortion constant in the intrinsic camera parameters defined by OpenCV.

parameters.label: Horizontal Tilt (p2)
parameters.description: Positive values will give the effect that the right side of the image plane is farther away than the left side, and negative values will do the opposite. The p<sub>2</sub> tangential distortion constant in the intrinsic camera parameters defined by OpenCV.

parameters.label: Center
parameters.description: The pivot point for the distortion. TIP: Click Icon:BUTTONS/layer_position_sample and then click a location in the image to set the Center.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: The amount to scale the distortion along the X and Y-axes.

parameters.label: Aspect
parameters.description: The ratio between the width and height. This value should match your lens's aspect ratio. This is different from your input layer's aspect ratio. The shape of the sensor behind a lens doesn't affect the lens' distortion.

entries.label: Live Video
entries.summary: Captures images from a live video source.

parameters.label: Source
parameters.description: The video source to connect to.

parameters.label: Configuration
parameters.description: A string that describes a configuration for the video source. The configuration must be supported by the video source in order to be used. Since the configuration is dependent on the source, the source parameter must be specified before the configuration. The format is: {format}:{xres}x{yres}@{framerate}

parameters.label: Connect to Source
parameters.description: When enabled, a connection is established to the video source. When disabled, the connection is terminated. The value of this parameter is not saved in the hip file due to privacy concerns and must therefore be re-enabled whenever opening the hip file.

parameters.label: Live Stream
parameters.description: When Connect to Source is on, this turns on live streaming to provide an interactive, non-deterministic streaming mode. It streams independent of the playbar and isn't associated with any keyframes or caching. This parameter (and its associated parameters) is intended as a sandbox mode where you don't have to rely on the playbar. TIP: Live Stream doesn't save the results like other streaming types in Houdini, so use a Stash COP to save results.

parameters.label: Toggle Live Stream
parameters.description: When Live Stream is on, this lets you pause and resume the live stream. TIP: You can also use the Icon:BUTTONS/live_disable Live Stream button to pause and resume live stream. See Cooking controls for more information.

parameters.label: Live Tick
parameters.description: When Live Stream is on, this is the current tick (frame) within the live stream.

entries.label: Match UDIM
entries.summary: Reframes pixels of a layer to match a particular UDIM tile.

parameters.label: UDIM
parameters.description: The tile at which to relocate the input image (assuming its starting position corresponds to tile 1001).

parameters.label: Invert Transformation
parameters.description: Inverts the transformation. This relocates the input image from the UDIM value to tile 1001.

parameters.label: Method
parameters.description: The method used to move the image. Move Camera: Reposition the camera so it's looking at the desired tile. Adjust Data Window: Don't move the camera, but instead change the layer's data window to move its pixels outside of the display window.

entries.label: Median
entries.summary: Applies a median filter to an image.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information.

parameters.label: Filter Size
parameters.description: The size (in pixels) of the area over which to compute the median. 3x3: Apply a 3 x 3 median filter. 5x5: Apply a 5 x 5 median filter.

entries.label: Mirror
entries.summary: Mirrors an image based on an arbitrary number of planes.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: The method you use to specify and configure the number of mirror planes. Number and Offset (default): Set the total number of mirror planes and the angle between and offset of each plane. Custom Mirror Planes: Add a custom number of mirror planes and a custom angle and offset for each plane.

parameters.label: Number of Planes
parameters.description: When Mode is Number and Offset, this is the total number of mirror planes to apply. The Angle parameter values are cumulative. The default value is 1.

parameters.label: Mirrors
parameters.description: When Mode is Custom Mirror Planes, this is the number of mirror planes to apply. The node sequentially performs mirroring, applying the Angle and Offset parameters from the first to the last in the list. The default value is 1.

parameters.label: Angle
parameters.description: When Mode is Number and Offset, this is the angle (in degrees) between each mirror plane. When Mode is Custom Mirror Planes, this is the angle (in degrees) of the mirror plane. Positive values mirror the left side of the image. Negative values mirror the right side of the image. When Mode is Number and Offset

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.description: When Mode is Number and Offset, this is the amount (in image space) of perpendicular offset from the origin. When Mode is Custom Mirror Planes, this is the amount (in image space) to perpendicularly offset the mirror plane along the image. Positive values move the mirror plane towards the right side of the image. Negative values move the mirror plane towards the left side of the image. The default value is 0.

parameters.label: Reverse Mirror Plane Direction
parameters.description: Flips the Mirror Plane. For example, an angle of 180 is equal to an angle of 0 with Reverse Mirror Plane Direction on.

entries.label: Mono
entries.summary: Converts a layer, VDB, or attribute into a mono, VDB, or attribute.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Operation
parameters.description: The method used to combine the source channels into the final value. The standard channel extension rules apply unless specified otherwise. NOTE: Some luminance methods assume a source color space. No implicit conversion is done from your scene_linear to this space. SGI Luminance: This is a historical luminance computation used in Houdini, which is believed to originate with SGI. lum = 0.3086 * red + 0.6094 * green + 0.0820 * blue NTSC Luminance: The standard NTSC luminance computation, which is a common luminance option. lum = 0.299 * red + 0.587 * green + 0.114 * blue HDTV Luminance: The HDTV standard luminance from BT 709. lum = 0.2126 * red + 0.7152 * green + 0.0722 * blue Average: An average of the channels. Maximum Channel: The maximum of the channels. Minimum Channel: The minimum of the channels. Magnitude / Length: The length of the vector formed by taking the channels as components. For a mono input, this is the absolute value. Hue: Convert to HSV and return the hue channel. Saturation: Convert to HSV and return the saturation channel. Value: Convert to HSV and return the value channel. Red: Extract the red, or x, channel. Green: Extract the green, or y, channel. Blue: Extract the blue, or z, channel. Alpha: Extract the alpha, or w, channel. Custom: Perform custom weighting of the channels. Use the Dot Product COP if you want this weighting to vary per pixel.

parameters.label: Weights
parameters.description: When Operation is Custom, this is the weight by which to multiply each channel before adding them up to get the luminance.

parameters.label: Normalize Weights
parameters.description: When Operation is Custom, this scales the provided weights by their total to make sure the total equals one.

entries.label: Mono to HeightField
entries.summary: Converts a mono layer into a heightfield.

parameters.label: Height Scale
parameters.description: The amount to scale the height values. This converts them to the proper world space locations.

parameters.label: Height Offset
parameters.description: The amount to offset the height values.

entries.label: Mono to RGBA
entries.summary: Converts a mono layer into an RGBA layer.

parameters.label: Fill Alpha
