parameters.description: Turns on the Axis Control Ramp, to change how the position along the axis should scale the effect between the minimum and maximum values of Axis Range.
parameters.heading: Axis Mask

parameters.label: Axis Control Ramp
parameters.description: This ramp controls how the position is mapped between the minimum and maximum values of Axis Range.
parameters.heading: Axis Mask

parameters.label: Minimum Limit
parameters.description: The output VDB is clamped below by this value.
parameters.heading: Limit Values

parameters.label: Maximum Limit
parameters.description: The output VDB is clamped above by this value.
parameters.heading: Limit Values

entries.label: Pyro Disturbance Force
entries.summary: Applies disturbance to a velocity VDB to break up still air.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The VDB type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Operation
parameters.description: Set: The velocities are replaced by the disturbance values. This is useful for visualizing the effect, or controlling more precisely how it is applied. Add: The disturbance is added to the incoming velocity. Rotate: The values in the incoming velocity are rotated towards the randomly-generated directions without changing their length.
parameters.heading: Force

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: Controls the nature of the generated random vectors. Continuous: Every voxel gets an independently-assigned random vector. Block-Based: The random pattern is formed by composing several layers of blockwise-constant noise.
parameters.heading: Force

parameters.label: Disturbance
parameters.description: Controls strength of the applied force. NOTE: When Rotate is used, Strength governs how fast the vectors are rotated towards their goal.
parameters.heading: Force

parameters.label: Reference Scale
parameters.description: Variance of the aggregated noise field over a region of this size will be equal to Strength when Mode is set to Continuous. Provides a scale for normalizing the force against voxel size. A larger value for this parameter will increase magnitude of the applied force. TIP: You should set this parameter to a reasonable value for your scene scale and leave it there. Strength can be used to more finely control how much force is applied.
parameters.heading: Force

parameters.label: Block Size
parameters.description: Controls size of the biggest blocks in the generated noise pattern when Mode is set to Block-Based.
parameters.heading: Force

parameters.label: Pulse Length
parameters.description: Length of time (in seconds) that the noise pattern is held fixed. This only applies when Mode is set to Block-Based. NOTE: The noise pattern changes on every frame in Continuous mode.
parameters.heading: Force

parameters.label: Max Octaves
parameters.description: The maximum number of noise levels to compose in Block-Based mode.
parameters.heading: Fractal

parameters.label: Lacunarity
parameters.description: The ratio of block sizes between successive noise layers. For example, a value of 2 means that the first layer has blocks that are twice the size of the second layer; the second layer will in turn have blocks that are twice as large as the next layer. This parameter is only applicable in Block-Based mode.
parameters.heading: Fractal

parameters.label: Roughness
parameters.description: The ratio of amplitudes between successive noise layers. For example a value of 0.5 means that the second layer will have half the amplitude of the first one. This parameter is only applicable in Block-Based mode. TIP: Lower Roughness values will better preserve the block structure in the generated noise, whereas higher ones (nearing or exceeding 1) will yield more chaotic patterns resembling white noise.
parameters.heading: Fractal

entries.label: Pyro Emit from Flame
entries.summary: Burns up the flame field.

parameters.label: Activation
parameters.description: Turns the effect of this node on and off. This node is only active when this value is 1.

parameters.label: Cool Flame
parameters.description: Controls when to dissipate the flame field. When this is turned on, the amount of smoke, temperature, and expansion is scaled by the amount of dissipated flame.
parameters.heading: Flame

parameters.label: Dissipation Mode
parameters.description: Controls the rate by which to dissipate the VDB. Dissipation Rate: The percentage of the current amount to be lost per fixed interval (per second). Subtraction Rate: Specific amount to be lost per fixed interval (per second). Lifespan: The interval (per second) in which a fixed amount (1 unit) to be lost. Half-Life: The interval (per second) in which half the amount to be lost (half-life).
parameters.heading: Flame

parameters.label: Dissipation Rate
parameters.description: The percentage of the current amount to be lost per fixed interval (per second).
parameters.heading: Flame

parameters.label: Subtraction Rate
parameters.description: Specific amount to be lost per fixed interval (per second).
parameters.heading: Flame

parameters.label: Lifespan
parameters.description: The interval (per second) in which a fixed amount (1 unit) to be lost.
parameters.heading: Flame

parameters.label: Half-Life
parameters.description: The interval (per second) in which half the amount to be lost (half-life).
parameters.heading: Flame

parameters.label: Goal Value
parameters.description: The reference value to which the field will cool to, usually zero.
parameters.heading: Flame

parameters.label: Goal Tolerance
parameters.description: When turned on and the VDB's value cools below Goal Value + Goal Tolerance, the VDB's value will be driven down all the way to the Goal Value.

parameters.label: Control Volume
parameters.description: Mask out the effect using the control field. Control fields are usually used the same way as masks, and represent a smooth engagement of the effect.
parameters.heading: Control Mask

parameters.label: Control Range
parameters.description: The value of the control field is mapped from this range to 0-1 and applied as a multiplier on top of Scale. The default 0 to 1 range is designed to concentrate the effect on regions with higher control field values. When the control field is a Vector VDB, this value represents the length of the given vector field.
parameters.heading: Control Mask

parameters.label: Use Ramp
parameters.description: Turns on the Control Ramp, to change how the control field should scale the effect between the minimum and maximum values of Control Range.
parameters.heading: Control Mask

parameters.label: Control Ramp
parameters.description: This ramp controls how the control field values are mapped between the minimum and maximum values of Control Range.
parameters.heading: Control Mask

parameters.label: Emit Density
parameters.description: When turned on, density is added to the incoming density field, representing smoke in the simulation.
parameters.heading: Density

parameters.label: Operation
parameters.description: Controls how the emitted density is mixed with the incoming density field. Add: The result is the sum of the values in the emitted density and the incoming density field. Maximum: The result is the larger of the values in the emitted density and the incoming density field. Average: The result is the average of the values in the emitted density and the incoming density field. Blend: The result is a blend of the values in the emitted density and the incoming density field, using the Blend parameter as weight. Pull: Values in the emitted density are pushed toward the corresponding incoming density field values, according to the Acceleration and Deceleration settings.
parameters.heading: Density

parameters.label: Emission Scale
parameters.description: Scales the amount of density output from the flame, which is calculated by first remapping the flame field from Flame Range to 0-1 or optionally to the range given by Emission Range. When Cool Flame is turned on, this is further scaled by the flame cooling ratio before multiplying the density output by this number.
parameters.heading: Density

parameters.label: Flame Range
parameters.description: Controls the flame region to emit density from. The flame field is first fitted from this range to 0-1 or optionally to the range given by Emission Range. Turn on Use Ramp to change how the flame values scale between the minimum and maximum of this range.
parameters.heading: Density

parameters.label: Emission Range
parameters.description: When turned on, this maps the flame field from the minimum and maximum values of Flame Range to this range.
parameters.heading: Density

parameters.label: Acceleration
parameters.description: Where the emitted density values are smaller than the incoming density field values, controls how strongly those values are pushed toward the incoming density field.

parameters.heading: Density

parameters.label: Blend
parameters.description: Controls the weight by which to blend between the incoming density field and the emitted density values.
parameters.heading: Density

parameters.label: Use Ramp

parameters.heading: Density

parameters.label: Flame Ramp

entries.label: Pyro Light Ambient
entries.summary: Builds a light field of ambient illumination of a VDB.

parameters.label: Exposed Color
parameters.description: The color of light that is exposed to the ambient surroundings. This is normally white, but can be used to tint the effective environment map.
parameters.heading: Shading

parameters.label: Occluded Color
parameters.description: The color of light where the voxel is exposed to the ambient surroundings. Normally this is black, but setting this to white and the Exposed Color to a dark color will result in a self-lit look which works well for clouds.
parameters.heading: Shading

parameters.label: Intensity
parameters.description: Controls the linear brightness of the light.
parameters.heading: Shading

parameters.label: Exposure
parameters.description: Controls the exponential brightness of the light. Each increase of 1 doubles the brightness.
parameters.heading: Shading

parameters.label: Density Scale
parameters.description: Scales the density VDB values, causing it to occlude light more quickly.
parameters.heading: Shading

parameters.label: Environment Map Offset
parameters.description: Controls the angle used to rotate the environment map around the Y-axis
parameters.heading: Shading

parameters.label: Steps Per MipMap
parameters.description: Controls how many tracing steps are performed before dropping to the next MipMap level when tracing occlusion rays. Lower values make the rays effectively thicker, causing them to become more like cones than rays.
parameters.heading: Quality

parameters.label: Max Steps
parameters.description: Controls the maximum number of samples taken while tracing an occlusion ray. Since higher MipMap levels have larger step sizes, the distance covered will be larger than just the voxelsize times the maxsteps.
parameters.heading: Quality

parameters.label: Environment Map Resolution
parameters.description: Because only a few rays are used to sample the ambient light, the environment map must be downsampled to avoid aliasing. This parameter controls the resolution to which it is resampled.
parameters.heading: Quality

parameters.label: MipMap Level
parameters.description: Controls the starting mipmap level. Starting at MipMap level 1 computes the light in a half-resolution VDB and interpolates the result back to full resolution, making the operation more than eight times faster.
parameters.heading: Quality

entries.label: Pyro Light from Points
entries.summary: Builds a light field of points lighting a VDB.

parameters.label: Directional
parameters.description: When turned on, the light is considered to be at infinity and all light rays are parallel. If point geometry is used as the source, the direction from each point to the origin defines the light direction. When turned off, the lights are treated as point lights that emanate from their 3D positions.
parameters.heading: Light Type

parameters.label: Light Position
parameters.description: When no point geometry is provided, specifies the center of the light when it is not directional.
parameters.heading: Light Type

parameters.label: Light Direction
parameters.description: When no point geometry is provided, specifies the direction of the light when it is directional.
parameters.heading: Light Type

parameters.label: Light Radius
parameters.description: Point lights have a singularity at their location, so if a point light is inside the volume it becomes infinitely bright at that location. This regularizes the falloff by treating the light as a sphere with the specified radius. This value is multiplied by the pscale point attribute.
parameters.heading: Light Type

parameters.label: Color
parameters.description: The color of the light. This value is multiplied by the Cd point attribute.
parameters.heading: Shading

parameters.label: Intensity
parameters.description: Controls the linear brightness of the light.
parameters.heading: Shading

parameters.label: Exposure
parameters.description: Controls the exponential brightness of the light. Each increase of 1 doubles the brightness.
parameters.heading: Shading

parameters.label: Density Scale
parameters.description: Scales the density VDB values, causing the volume to occlude light more quickly.
parameters.heading: Shading

parameters.label: Steps Per MipMap
parameters.description: Controls how many tracing steps are performed before dropping to the next MipMap level when tracing occlusion rays. This causes the rays to become cones, producing blurrier shadows farther from the light source.
parameters.heading: Quality

parameters.label: Max Steps
parameters.description: Controls the maximum number of samples taken while tracing an occlusion ray. Since higher MipMap levels have larger step sizes, the distance covered will be larger than just the voxelsize times the maxsteps.
parameters.heading: Quality

entries.label: Pyro Light Scatter
entries.summary: Builds a light field of internal glow of a VDB.

parameters.label: Density Scale
parameters.description: Scales the density VDB values, causing it to occlude light more quickly.

parameters.label: Absorption
parameters.description: Controls how quickly emitted light is absorbed by the smoke particles instead of being scattered further through the volume.

parameters.label: Emission Scale
parameters.description: Applies a global scale to the incoming emission VDB.

parameters.label: Emission Color Ramp
parameters.description: The emission VDB is sent through this ramp to generate an emission color.

parameters.label: Iterations
parameters.description: Controls how many diffusion iterations are performed when scattering light through the volume. The emission is treated as a source term during diffusion. Although the process eventually converges, it is typically stopped early to keep it fast and to adjust the look.

parameters.label: MipMap Level
parameters.description: Controls the MipMap level used for the light scattering computation. A mipmap level of 1 computes at half the original resolution and halves the number of iterations, making the process approximately sixteen times faster. The final scatter values are the interpolated back to the original resolution.
parameters.heading: Quality

entries.label: Pyro Packed MipMap
entries.summary: Builds an in-place MipMap of a VDB.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: Controls the VDB type accepted by the node. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: MipMap Depth
parameters.description: Controls the number of mipmap levels stored in the VDB. Each layer is half the resolution of the previous one. Most nodes use only the first three layers, but higher values can be used for custom operations. The maximum supported depth is 10.

entries.label: Pyro Project Non-Divergent Electro Static
entries.summary: Removes divergence from a velocity VDB.

parameters.label: Iterations
parameters.description: Controls how many times the projection process is repeated. Higher values increase computation time but produce more accurate results and improve the reliability of collision handling.

parameters.label: Ambient Velocity
parameters.description: Specifies the global implied velocity. The input velocity is assumed not to include this value. When using v, the ambient velocity is implicitly added to obtain the world-space velocity. Collision velocities are specified in world-space, not wind-space, and are adjusted accordingly.

parameters.label: Voxel Kernel Size
parameters.description: Controls the size of the voxel kernel. Larger values improve quality but significantly increase computation time.

parameters.label: Double Voxel Pass
parameters.description: Applies two voxel kernel passes before performing a block pass.

parameters.label: Block Pass
parameters.description: Turn on the block pass. During the block pass, divergence is reduced to dipoles over large blocks, allowing action at distance without having to increase the voxel kernel size.

parameters.label: Block Kernel Size
parameters.description: The size, in blocks, to accumulate the surrounding block's dipoles when updating a voxel. Larger values improve quality but significantly increase computation time.

parameters.label: Feather Blocks
parameters.description: Reduce the strength of the block correction over the farthest blocks. This helps avoid sharp transitions in the corrected velocity when strong impulses are present, but may require more iterations or computation time to fully remove divergence.

parameters.label: Point Pass
parameters.description: Combines the block dipoles into an even coarser set of points. These points are then applied to every voxel, allowing divergence to have a global effect in a single pass.

parameters.label: Hourglass Filter
parameters.description: Applies a smoothing operation to remove velocity modes that can be missed when projecting using corner-sampled divergence. This can reduce jagged artifacts.

entries.label: Pyro Source from Layer
entries.summary: Sources from a layer's envelope into a VDB.

parameters.label: Method
parameters.description: Controls how the VDB is updated using the envelope values. Add: Adds the envelope value to the current value. Copy: Replaces the current value with the envelope value. Maximum: Uses the larger of the current value and the envelope value. Average: Uses the average of the current value and the envelope value. Blend: Blend the current value with the envelope values using Blend as the weight. Pull: Pushes the current value toward the envelope value according to the Acceleration Strength and Deceleration Strength.

parameters.label: Border
parameters.description: Controls the border mode used when sampling the reference layers. The reference layers can use wrapping border modes to create tiling sources. However, when the source is not expected to extend beyond the layer boundaries, this parameter can be used to override the input border mode. Auto uses the border mode of the input layer. See Border types for more information.

parameters.label: Acceleration
parameters.description: Controls how strongly envelope values that are smaller than the current values are pushed toward the current values.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Deceleration
parameters.description: Controls how strongly envelope values that are larger than the current values are pushed toward the current values.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Blend
parameters.description: Controls the weight used to blend between the envelope values and the current values.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: Scales the envelope values before they are mixed.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Thickness
parameters.description: Applies a global scale to the thickness input, allowing a 0–1 layer to be rescaled to world units.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Scale by Timestep
parameters.description: Scales the envelope values by the current timestep. In Add mode, this ensures that the same amount is added over one second, even when substepping occurs.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Falloff
parameters.description: Scales the density using the falloff ramp. The left side of the ramp corresponds to the outer surface of the envelope. The distance along the ramp is based on the distance from the surface, scaled by the global thickness rather than the local thickness. This ensures that thin areas also decrease in magnitude.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Noise Enable
parameters.description: scales the envelope values using a noise function.
parameters.heading: Enable Noise

parameters.label: Noise Scale
parameters.description: Controls how much the envelope values are scaled by the noise.
parameters.heading: Enable Noise

parameters.label: Element Size
parameters.description: Controls the world-space size of the noise features.
parameters.heading: Enable Noise

parameters.label: Element Scale
parameters.description: Applies anisotropic scaling to the noise feature size.
parameters.heading: Enable Noise

parameters.label: Noise Offset
parameters.description: Controls the offset of the noise in noise space. The first three components define the spatial offset, and the fourth defines the time offset.
parameters.heading: Enable Noise

parameters.label: Noise Pulse
parameters.description: Controls how quickly the noise pattern changes over time. The value is specified in seconds and roughly determines the rate at which the noise appears to pulse.
parameters.heading: Enable Noise

parameters.label: Distort Enable
parameters.description: Distorts the shape of the envelope using a noise function.
parameters.heading: Enable Distortion

parameters.label: Distort Scale
parameters.description: Controls the maximum distortion distance in world-space.
parameters.heading: Enable Distortion

parameters.label: Element Size
parameters.description: Controls the world-space size of the noise features.
parameters.heading: Enable Distortion

parameters.label: Element Scale
parameters.description: Applies anisotropic scaling to the noise feature size.
parameters.heading: Enable Distortion

parameters.label: Distort Offset
parameters.description: Controls the offset of the noise in noise space. The first three components define the spatial offset, and the fourth defines the time offset.
parameters.heading: Enable Distortion

parameters.label: Distort Pulse
parameters.description: Controls how quickly the noise pattern changes over time. The value is specified in seconds and roughly determines the rate at which the noise appears to pulse.
parameters.heading: Enable Distortion

entries.label: Pyro Source from Layer
entries.summary: Sources from a layer's envelope into a VDB.

parameters.label: Method
parameters.description: How to update the VDB from the envelope values. Set: Replace the value. Add: Add to the current value. Minimum: Take the minimum of the current value with the envelope values. Maximum: Take the maximum of the current value with the envelope values.

parameters.label: Border
parameters.description: The wrapping mode of the reference layers can be used to make tiling sources. However, it is often expected for the source to not be present past the layer, so this allows just in time overriding of the border type. Auto will use the input's border type. See Border types for more information.

parameters.label: Thickness
parameters.description: A global scale on the thickness input, allowing a 0-1 layer to be rescaled to world units.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Scale by Timestep
parameters.description: Scale the envelope values by the current timestep. In Add mode, this ensures the same amount will be added over a second even if substepping occurs.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Amount
parameters.description: The density to use for voxels in the envelope. This is scaled by the density input.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Falloff
parameters.description: The density is scaled by the falloff ramp. The left side is the outer surface of the envelope. The distance along the ramp is based on the distance from the surface scaled by the global thickness (rather than the local thickness). This ensures that thin areas also decrease in magnitude.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Noise Enable
parameters.description: Enable scaling the value by a noise function.
parameters.heading: Enable Noise

parameters.label: Noise Scale
parameters.description: How much to scale the value by.
parameters.heading: Enable Noise

parameters.label: Element Size
parameters.description: The size in world space of the feature size of the noise.
parameters.heading: Enable Noise

parameters.label: Element Scale
parameters.description: The anisotropic scaling of the noise feature sizes.
parameters.heading: Enable Noise

parameters.label: Noise Offset
parameters.description: The offset of the noise in noise-space, the first three are the spatial offset and the fourth the time offset.
parameters.heading: Enable Noise

parameters.label: Noise Pulse
parameters.description: The time in seconds for the feature size of the noise's change over time. This is roughly the rate at which it will seem to pulse.
parameters.heading: Enable Noise

parameters.label: Distort Enable
parameters.description: Enable distorting of the shape of the sphere by a noise function.
parameters.heading: Enable Distortion

parameters.label: Distort Scale
parameters.description: How far to distort in worldspace.
parameters.heading: Enable Distortion

parameters.label: Element Size
parameters.description: The size in world space of the feature size of the noise.
parameters.heading: Enable Distortion

parameters.label: Element Scale
parameters.description: The anisotropic scaling of the noise feature sizes.
parameters.heading: Enable Distortion

parameters.label: Distort Offset
parameters.description: The offset of the noise in noise-space, the first three are the spatial offset and the fourth the time offset.
parameters.heading: Enable Distortion

parameters.label: Distort Pulse
parameters.description: The time in seconds for the feature size of the noise's change over time. This is roughly the rate at which it will seem to pulse.
parameters.heading: Enable Distortion

entries.label: Pyro Source from Points
entries.summary: Sources points into a VDB.

parameters.label: Method
parameters.description: Controls how the VDB is updated using the point values. Set: Replaces the current value. Add: Adds to the current value. Minimum: Take the minimum of the current value with the point values. Maximum: Take the maximum of the current value with the point values.

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: Controls the radius of the sphere stamped into the VDB. This is scaled by the pscale point attribute.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Center
parameters.description: If no geometry input is connected, a single point is sourced at this location.

parameters.label: Scale by Timestep
parameters.description: Scales the point values by the current timestep. In Add mode, this ensures that the same amount is added over one second, even when substepping occurs.

parameters.label: Amount
parameters.description: The density to use for the point. This is scaled by the density point attribute.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Falloff
parameters.description: The amount is scaled by this ramp. The left side of the ramp corresponds to the point location, and the right side corresponds to the value at the point's radius.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Noise Enable
parameters.description: Scales the value using a noise function.
parameters.heading: Enable Noise

parameters.label: Noise Scale
parameters.description: Controls how much the value is scaled by the noise.
parameters.heading: Enable Noise

parameters.label: Element Size
parameters.description: Controls the world-space size of the noise features.
parameters.heading: Enable Noise

parameters.label: Element Scale
parameters.description: Applies anisotropic scaling to the noise feature size.
parameters.heading: Enable Noise

parameters.label: Noise Offset
parameters.description: Controls the offset of the noise in noise-space. The first three components define the spatial offset, and the fourth defines the time offset.
parameters.heading: Enable Noise

parameters.label: Noise Pulse
parameters.description: Controls how quickly the noise pattern changes over time. The value is specified in seconds and roughly determines the rate at which the noise appears to pulse.

parameters.label: Distort Enable

parameters.label: Distort Scale

parameters.heading: Enable Distortion

parameters.label: Element Size
parameters.description: Controls the world-space size of the noise features.
parameters.heading: Enable Distortion

parameters.label: Element Scale
parameters.description: Applies anisotropic scaling to the noise feature size.
parameters.heading: Enable Distortion

parameters.label: Distort Offset
parameters.description: Controls the offset of the noise in noise-space. The first three components define the spatial offset, and the fourth defines the time offset.
parameters.heading: Enable Distortion

parameters.label: Distort Pulse
parameters.description: Controls how quickly the noise pattern changes over time. The value is specified in seconds and roughly determines the rate at which the noise appears to pulse.
parameters.heading: Enable Distortion

entries.label: Pyro Source from Volume
entries.summary: Sources from a VDB into another VDB.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The VDB type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Activation
parameters.description: Turns this the effect of this node on and off. This node is only active when this value is 1.

parameters.label: Source Mode
parameters.description: Controls when the source volume is mixed with the target volume. Continuous: Sourcing remains active throughout the simulation and is applied on every solver step. Use this when you need a constant supply of density, temperature or other quantities. First Frame Only: Sourcing is applied only on the first simulation frame. This is useful when the fluid is already present when the simulation begins. If the source is animated, those animations are ignored after the first frame. Copy on First Frame: Sourcing remains active throughout the simulation, as in Continuous mode. On the first simulation frame, the source volume is copied into the target volume. On subsequent frames, the operation is determined by Operation.
parameters.heading: Source

parameters.label: Operation
parameters.description: Controls how the source volume is mixed with the target volume. Add: The result is the sum of the source and target values. Copy: The result is copied from the source volume. Maximum: The result is the greater of the source and target values. Average: The result is the average of the source and target values. Blend: The result is a blend between the source and target values, using Blend as the weight. Pull: Pushes source values toward the corresponding target values according to the Acceleration Strength and Deceleration Strength settings.
parameters.heading: Source

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: Scales the source values before they are mixed with the target volume.
parameters.heading: Source

parameters.label: Scale by Timestep
parameters.description: Scales the effect of sourcing by the timestep. This ensures that the amount of sourcing remains consistent when substepping occurs. Turn off this parameter if you need the instantaneous source value.
parameters.heading: Source

parameters.label: Acceleration
parameters.description: Controls how strongly source values that are smaller than the corresponding target values are pushed toward the target field.
parameters.heading: Source

parameters.label: Deceleration
parameters.description: Controls how strongly source values that are larger than the corresponding target volume values are pushed toward the target field.
parameters.heading: Source

parameters.label: Blend
parameters.description: Controls the weight used to blend between the source values and the target values.
parameters.heading: Source

entries.label: Pyro Source Shape
entries.summary: Creates points representing implicit surfaces to source into a Pyro simulation.

parameters.label: Activation
parameters.description: Turns this node on or off. This node is only active when this value is 1.

parameters.label: Shape
parameters.description: Controls the type of shape to create.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Size
parameters.description: Controls the size of the box. Click the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per Component button for separate scale along each axis.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Size Scale
parameters.description: Controls the size of the box separately across each axis.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Roundness
parameters.description: Radius used to round the box edges. A value of 0 creates a sharp box.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: Controls the size of the sphere. Click the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per Component button for separate scale along each axis.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Radius Scale
parameters.description: Controls the radius of the sphere separately across each axis.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Cut Sphere
parameters.description: When tunred on, cuts the sphere with a plane at the Y position specified by this parameter.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: Major radius and tube radius of the torus.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Link Length
parameters.description: Stretches the torus into a chain link shape. A value of 0 creates a regular torus.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Length
parameters.description: Length of the tube along its local axis.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: Radii at the two ends of the tube. Matching values create a straight tube; different values create a tapered tube.

parameters.label: Radius Scale
parameters.description: Uniform scale applied to the tube radii.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Round Caps
parameters.description: Rounds the tube ends.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Translate
parameters.description: Controls the translation along the X, Y, and Z axes.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.description: Controls the rotation about the X, Y, and Z axes.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Uniform Scale
parameters.description: Controls the uniform scale of the shape.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Distortion Noise
parameters.description: When turned on, distorts the source shape over time using generated noise. This can help add visual breakup to basic primitive shapes.

parameters.label: Amplitude
parameters.description: Controls the strength of the distortion along each axes.
parameters.heading: Distortion Noise

parameters.label: Element Size
parameters.description: Controls the uniform scale of the noise elements.
parameters.heading: Distortion Noise

parameters.label: Pulse Duration
parameters.description: Controls the rate at which the noise pattern changes. Set this to 0 to keep the noise pattern constant over time.
parameters.heading: Distortion Noise

parameters.label: Roughness
parameters.description: The scale increment between iterations of fractal noise added to the basic output. The higher the value the larger the "jaggies" added to the output. You can use a negative value for roughness. :video:
parameters.heading: Distortion Noise

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.description: Defines the initial noise offset.
parameters.heading: Distortion Noise

parameters.label: Source Density
parameters.description: When turned on, sources the shape into the density volume.
parameters.heading: Density

parameters.label: Source Mode
parameters.description: Controls when the source volume is mixed with the target volume. Continuous: Sourcing remains active throughout the simulation and is applied on every solver step. Use this when you need a constant supply of density, temperature or other quantities. First Frame Only: Sourcing is applied only on the first simulation frame. This is useful when the fluid is already present when the simulation begins. If the source is animated, those animations are ignored after the first frame. Copy on First Frame: Sourcing remains active throughout the simulation, as in Continuous mode. On the first simulation frame, the source volume is copied into the target volume. On subsequent frames, the operation is determined by Operation.

parameters.label: Operation
parameters.description: Controls how the source volume is mixed with the target volume. Add: The result is the sum of the source and target values. Copy: The result is copied from the source volume. Maximum: The result is the greater of the source and target values. Average: The result is the average of the source and target values. Blend: The result is a blend between the source and target values, using Blend as the weight. Pull: Pushes source values toward the corresponding target values according to the Acceleration Strength and Deceleration Strength settings.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: Scales the source values before they are mixed with the target volume.
parameters.heading: Density

parameters.label: Scale by Timestep
parameters.description: Scales the effect of sourcing by the timestep. This ensures that the amount of sourcing remains consistent when substepping occurs. Turn off this parameter if you need the instantaneous source value.
parameters.heading: Density

parameters.label: Blend
parameters.description: Controls the weight used to blend between the source values and the corresponding volume values.
parameters.heading: Density

parameters.label: Acceleration
parameters.description: Controls how strongly source values that are smaller than the corresponding target values are pushed toward the target field.
parameters.heading: Density

parameters.label: Deceleration
parameters.description: Controls how strongly source values that are larger than the corresponding target volume values are pushed toward the target field.
parameters.heading: Density

parameters.label: Enable Noise
parameters.description: When turned on, multiplies the uniform source value by a generated noise pattern.
parameters.heading: Scale by Noise

parameters.label: Scale Min/Max
parameters.description: Sets the minimum and maximum values of the noise range. To create larger empty spaces, lower the minimum value to negative numbers and turn on Avoid Negatives.
parameters.heading: Scale by Noise

parameters.label: Avoid Negatives
parameters.description: When this is on, negative values will be set to zero.
parameters.heading: Scale by Noise

parameters.label: Element Size
parameters.description: Controls the base feature size of the generated noise. This applies uniformly to each axis.
parameters.heading: Scale by Noise

parameters.label: Pulse Duration
parameters.description: Controls the rate at which the noise pattern changes. Set this to 0 if static noise is required.
parameters.heading: Scale by Noise

parameters.label: Roughness
parameters.description: Controls the scale increment between iterations of the fractal noise. Higher values produce finer detail, while lower values produce a smoother noise field.
parameters.heading: Scale by Noise

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.description: Defines the initial noise offset.
parameters.heading: Scale by Noise

parameters.label: Source Temperature
parameters.description: When turned on, the shape is sourced into the temperature volume.
parameters.heading: Temperature

parameters.label: Source Velocity
parameters.description: When turned on, the shape is sourced into the velocity volume.
parameters.heading: Velocity

parameters.label: Point Velocity
parameters.description: When turned on, calculates the velocity of the implicit surface from its motion using the Velocity Approximation parameter. This is useful for moving or rotating sources.
parameters.heading: Inherited Velocity

parameters.label: Velocity Scale
parameters.description: Scales the strength of the velocity calculated from the motion.
parameters.heading: Inherited Velocity

parameters.label: Enable Force
parameters.description: When turned on, calculates an additional force field that can push quantities away from or around the source shape.
parameters.heading: Force

parameters.label: Force Type
parameters.description: Controls the type of force added to the velocity field. Directional: Applies a uniform velocity throughout the field. All vectors point in the direction specified by the Direction. Spherical: Calculates the velocities based on the distance from a center point. Vectors point outward from the shape. Spin: Creates a vortex field. Vectors are calculated perpendicular to the center of the source, causing motion to spiral around the axis specified by the Axis. Radial: Generates vectors that point away from the line defined by the Axis, which passes through the center of the source, spreading outward across the volume.
parameters.heading: Force

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: Scales the strength of the calculated velocity force.
parameters.heading: Force

parameters.label: Direction
parameters.description: When Force Type is set to Directional, specifies the direction in which all velocity vectors point.
parameters.heading: Force

parameters.label: Axis
parameters.description: When Force Type is set to Spin, this controls the direction of rotation. Just like a wheel, the axis is the invisible pole the velocity vectors spin around. When Force Type is set to Radial, defines the orientation of the line from which the velocity vectors point away.
parameters.heading: Force

parameters.label: Noise
parameters.description: When turned on, calculates an additional vector field based on a generated noise pattern.
parameters.heading: Curl Noise

parameters.label: Amplitude
parameters.description: Controls the strength of the calculated noise field.
parameters.heading: Curl Noise

parameters.label: Source Flame
parameters.description: When turned on, the shape is sourced into the flame volume.
parameters.heading: Flame

parameters.label: Source Divergence
parameters.description: When turned on, the shape is sourced into the divergence volume.
parameters.heading: Divergence

entries.label: Pyro Turbulence Force
entries.summary: Apply turbulence to a velocity VDB.

parameters.label: Operation
parameters.description: Controls how the force is combined with the incoming velocity field. Set: Replaces the incoming velocities with the force values. Force: Adds the force values to the incoming velocities.
parameters.heading: Force

parameters.label: Amplitude
parameters.description: Controls the overall strength of the force.
parameters.heading: Force

parameters.label: Amplitude Scale
parameters.description: Applies an anisotropic scale to the force.
parameters.heading: Force

parameters.label: Element Size
parameters.description: Controls the size of the noise elements at the base level of the noise.
parameters.heading: Force

parameters.label: Element Scale
parameters.description: Applies an anisotropic scale to the base-level noise element size.
parameters.heading: Force

parameters.label: Pulse Duration
parameters.description: The time, in seconds, required for the base level of the noise to fully change.
parameters.heading: Force

parameters.label: Attenuation
parameters.description: Controls the gradual loss of intensity.
parameters.heading: Force

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.description: Defines the initial noise offset.
parameters.heading: Force

parameters.label: Use Curl Noise
parameters.description: Uses curl noise instead of regular noise. Curl noise is divergence-free, so it remains relatively unchanged by pressure projection. It is best suited for introducing smooth motion, while non-curl noise is faster and better suited for adding energy.
parameters.heading: Force

parameters.label: Max Octaves
parameters.description: Controls the number of turbulence levels applied relative to the initial Element Size.
parameters.heading: Fractal

parameters.label: Lacunarity
parameters.description: Controls the scale factor between successive turbulence octaves.
parameters.heading: Fractal

parameters.label: Roughness
parameters.description: Controls how much each octave contributes relative to the previous one. Values below 1 ensure that smaller features do not overwhelm larger features.
parameters.heading: Fractal

parameters.description: The VDB type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Activation
parameters.description: Turns this the effect of this node on and off. This node is only active when this value is 1.

parameters.label: Operation
parameters.description: Controls how the force is combined with the incoming velocity field. Set: Replaces the incoming velocities with the force values. Add: Adds the force values to the incoming velocities. Drag: Treats the force direction as a velocity and blends the incoming velocities toward it.
parameters.heading: Force

parameters.label: Uniform Scale
parameters.description: Applies a global scale to the force.
parameters.heading: Force

parameters.label: Gravity Acceleration
parameters.description: The acceleration due to gravity. Stronger gravity produces a stronger uniform force.
parameters.heading: Force

parameters.label: Direction
parameters.description: The direction in which the force is applied. In Drag mode, this value is treated as the target velocity.
parameters.heading: Force

parameters.label: Use Terminal Velocity
parameters.description: Enables a limit on fluid acceleration in the direction of the uniform force.
parameters.heading: Force

parameters.label: Terminal Velocity
parameters.description: Fluid with a velocity in the direction of the uniform force that is greater than or equal to this value will not have any force applied. Turn on this parameter if the fluid accelerates more than desired due to the uniform force. Increase this value if the uniform force stops affecting the fluid sooner than expected.
parameters.heading: Force

parameters.label: Scale by Timestep
parameters.description: Scales the force by the timestep. This ensures that the amount of force remains consistent when substepping occurs. Turn off this parameter if you need the instantaneous force value.

parameters.label: Threshold Volume
parameters.description: Mask out the effect using the threshold field. Threshold fields are intended to provide harsh on/off effects, but the range can be used to soften the transition.
parameters.heading: Threshold Mask

parameters.label: Threshold Range
parameters.description: The value of the threshold field is mapped from this range to 0-1 and applied as a multiplier on top of Scale. The default 0.01 to 0 range is designed to concentrate the effect on the edges and empty regions of the threshold field, but not inside it. When the threshold field is a Vector VDB, this value represents the length of the given vector field.
parameters.heading: Threshold Mask

parameters.label: Use Ramp
parameters.description: Turns on the Threshold Ramp, to change how the threshold field should scale the effect between the minimum and maximum values of Threshold Range.
parameters.heading: Threshold Mask

parameters.label: Threshold Ramp
parameters.description: This ramp controls how the threshold field values are mapped between the minimum and maximum values of Threshold Range.
parameters.heading: Threshold Mask

parameters.label: Control Volume
parameters.description: Mask out the effect using the control field. Control fields are usually used the same way as masks, and represent a smooth engagement of the effect.
parameters.heading: Control Mask

parameters.label: Control Range
parameters.description: The value of the control field is mapped from this range to 0-1 and applied as a multiplier on top of Scale. The default 0 to 1 range is designed to concentrate the effect on regions with higher control field values. When the control field is a Vector VDB, this value represents the length of the given vector field.
parameters.heading: Control Mask

parameters.label: Use Ramp
parameters.description: Turns on the Control Ramp, to change how the control field should scale the effect between the minimum and maximum values of Control Range.
parameters.heading: Control Mask

parameters.label: Control Ramp
parameters.description: This ramp controls how the control field values are mapped between the minimum and maximum values of Control Range.
parameters.heading: Control Mask

parameters.label: Angle Mask
parameters.description: Mask out the effect by the angle between the velocity field values and a direction vector.

parameters.label: Angle Direction

parameters.heading: Angle Mask

parameters.label: Spread Angle
parameters.description: The value of the calculated angle is mapped until this angle range to 1-0 and applied as a multiplier on top of Scale. At the default 90 degrees, the effect is strongest where the vectors align, and gradually diminishes to zero as the angle reaches this value.

parameters.label: Angle Control Ramp
parameters.description: This ramp controls how the angle deviation is mapped between the aligned vectors and the given Spread Angle.

parameters.label: Axis Mask

parameters.label: Axis Range

parameters.label: Use Ramp
parameters.description: Turns on the Axis Control Ramp, to change how the position along the axis should scale the effect between the minimum and maximum values of Axis Range.
parameters.heading: Axis Mask

parameters.label: Axis Control Ramp
parameters.description: This ramp controls how the position is mapped between the minimum and maximum values of Axis Range.
