entries.label: Pyro Vortex Confinement Force
entries.summary: Applies a vortex confinement force to a velocity field.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The VDB type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Activation
parameters.description: Turns this the effect of this node on and off. This node is only active when this value is 1.

parameters.label: Operation
parameters.description: Controls how the force is combined with the incoming velocity field. Set: Replaces the incoming velocities with the force values. Add: Adds the force values to the incoming velocities. Rotate: Rotates the force to align with the direction of the incoming velocities.
parameters.heading: Force

parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: Controls the method used to recover detail lost through diffusion. The first-order method uses first derivatives to approximate the local vorticity gradient. This method is fast and stable, but tends to introduce more numerical diffusion, resulting in greater loss of fine-scale detail. The second-order method uses a higher-order approximation that better preserves energy and small-scale features. This method can produce more detailed results, but is slower and may introduce instabilities. These can be mitigated using the Positive Diffusion Scale and Negative Diffusion Scale parameters.
parameters.heading: Force

parameters.label: Confinement Scale
parameters.description: Controls the strength of the vortex confinement force.
parameters.heading: Force

parameters.label: Positive Diffusion Scale
parameters.description: Controls the amount of positive diffusion applied. Positive diffusion improves stability by smoothing high-frequency noise and sharp numerical spikes in the vorticity field.
parameters.heading: Force

parameters.label: Negative Diffusion Scale
parameters.description: Controls the amount of negative diffusion applied. Negative diffusion acts as an anti-diffusion process, concentrating energy toward the centers of vortex structures instead of spreading it outward.
parameters.heading: Force

parameters.label: Kernel Size
parameters.description: Controls the size of the neighborhood stencil used to compute curvature at each pixel. Larger values generally produce smoother curvature results. This parameter has a similar effect to Frequency Separation, as it removes high-frequency detail that can cause unnatural jittering.
parameters.heading: Force

parameters.label: Target Energy
parameters.description: Applies smooth clamping based on the energy of the band. The target energy determines the maximum energy level at which curl can be amplified. This can help reduce unstable or noisy behavior.
parameters.heading: Force

parameters.label: Adaptive Confinement
parameters.description: Restricts vortex confinement to areas where vorticles are more likely to develop. This can help reduce the unnatural jittering that vortex confinement can introduce throughout the simulation.
parameters.heading: Force

parameters.label: Use Frequency Separation
parameters.description: Enables frequency separation, allowing you to control which swirl sizes are affected by this node.
parameters.heading: Frequency Separation

parameters.label: Min Swirl Size
parameters.description: Defines the smallest swirl size to include. Swirls with a width equal to this value define the starting frequency of the band. When turned off, all swirl sizes up to Max Swirl Size are included. Increase this value together with Max Swirl Size, or set it close to Max Swirl Size, to affect only larger swirls.
parameters.heading: Frequency Separation

parameters.label: Max Swirl Size
parameters.description: Defines the largest swirl size to include. Swirls with a width equal to this value define the ending frequency of the band. Increase this value together with Min Swirl Size to affect only larger swirls.
parameters.heading: Frequency Separation

parameters.label: Threshold Volume
parameters.description: Mask out the effect using the threshold field. Threshold fields are intended to provide harsh on/off effects, but the range can be used to soften the transition.
parameters.heading: Threshold Mask

parameters.label: Threshold Range
parameters.description: The value of the threshold field is mapped from this range to 0-1 and applied as a multiplier on top of Scale. The default 0.01 to 0 range is designed to concentrate the effect on the edges and empty regions of the threshold field, but not inside it. When the threshold field is a Vector VDB, this value represents the length of the given vector field.
parameters.heading: Threshold Mask

parameters.label: Use Ramp
parameters.description: Turns on the Threshold Ramp, to change how the threshold field should scale the effect between the minimum and maximum values of Threshold Range.
parameters.heading: Threshold Mask

parameters.label: Threshold Ramp
parameters.description: This ramp controls how the threshold field values are mapped between the minimum and maximum values of Threshold Range.
parameters.heading: Threshold Mask

parameters.label: Control Volume
parameters.description: Mask out the effect using the control field. Control fields are usually used the same way as masks, and represent a smooth engagement of the effect.
parameters.heading: Control Mask

parameters.label: Control Range
parameters.description: The value of the control field is mapped from this range to 0-1 and applied as a multiplier on top of Scale. The default 0 to 1 range is designed to concentrate the effect on regions with higher control field values. When the control field is a Vector VDB, this value represents the length of the given vector field.
parameters.heading: Control Mask

parameters.label: Use Ramp
parameters.description: Turns on the Control Ramp, to change how the control field should scale the effect between the minimum and maximum values of Control Range.
parameters.heading: Control Mask

parameters.label: Control Ramp
parameters.description: This ramp controls how the control field values are mapped between the minimum and maximum values of Control Range.
parameters.heading: Control Mask

parameters.label: Angle Mask
parameters.description: Mask out the effect by the angle between the velocity field values and a direction vector.
parameters.heading: Angle Mask

parameters.label: Angle Direction
parameters.description: The reference vector used to calculate the angle deviation against the velocity field.
parameters.heading: Angle Mask

parameters.label: Spread Angle
parameters.description: The value of the calculated angle is mapped until this angle range to 1-0 and applied as a multiplier on top of Scale. At the default 90 degrees, the effect is strongest where the vectors align, and gradually diminishes to zero as the angle reaches this value.
parameters.heading: Angle Mask

parameters.label: Use Ramp
parameters.description: Turns on the Angle Control Ramp, to change how the angle deviation should scale the effect between the aligned vectors and the given Spread Angle.
parameters.heading: Angle Mask

parameters.label: Angle Control Ramp
parameters.description: This ramp controls how the angle deviation is mapped between the aligned vectors and the given Spread Angle.
parameters.heading: Angle Mask

parameters.label: Axis Mask
parameters.description: Mask out the effect along an axis direction. Rather than requiring the construction of VDBs to represent this, this allows direct specification of the world space range over which the effect is to be scaled.
parameters.heading: Axis Mask

parameters.label: Axis Direction
parameters.description: The reference vector along which the effect will be masked.
parameters.heading: Axis Mask

parameters.label: Axis Range
parameters.description: The position along the axis mask is mapped from this range to 0-1 and applied as a multiplier on top of Scale.
parameters.heading: Axis Mask

parameters.label: Use Ramp
parameters.description: Turns on the Axis Control Ramp, to change how the position along the axis should scale the effect between the minimum and maximum values of Axis Range.
parameters.heading: Axis Mask

parameters.label: Axis Control Ramp
parameters.description: This ramp controls how the position is mapped between the minimum and maximum values of Axis Range.
parameters.heading: Axis Mask

entries.label: Python Snippet
entries.summary: Runs a snippet of Python on layers.

parameters.label: Python Code
parameters.description: The Python code to run. Use the provided kwargs dictionary, which contains the bound parameters and input geometry and layers, to return a dictionary of named outputs. You can also use the #bind syntax to define the signature and bound parameters. The Smallicon:BUTTONS/create_parm_from_ch button sets up the Signature and Bindings tabs.
parameters.heading: Kernel

parameters.label: Maintain State
parameters.description: When on, the node doesn't clear the underlying Python interpreter between cooks. This can enhance performance, but may result in unexpected behavior. It's recommended to turn this off in most scenarios.
parameters.heading: Options

parameters.label: Inputs
parameters.description: The number of this node's inputs.
parameters.heading: Signature

parameters.label: Input #
parameters.description: The name of the input, which is what you reference in the #bind command.
parameters.heading: Signature

parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: The data type or port for the node input. Varying: Accepts mono, UV, RGB, or RGBA layers. All inputs of Varying type are set to the same type. The Varying type matches the input's signature, and the signature must be the same type for all Varying inputs. If available, the signature matching selects the signature that fits. ID: Accepts ID layers. Mono: Accepts mono layers. UV: Accepts UV layers. RGB: Accepts RGB layers. RGBA: Accepts RGBA layers. Geometry: Accepts a geometry type. You must refer to this type's name in an attribute or volume binding. Metadata: This input isn't read, but used only for size and metadata information. Integer VDB: Accepts integer VDBs. Float VDB: Accepts float VDBs. Vector VDB: Accepts vector VDBs. Varying VDB: Accepts float or vector VDBs.
parameters.heading: Signature

parameters.label: Optional
parameters.description: Makes the input optional. When on, make sure to mark the corresponding binding as optional.
parameters.heading: Signature

parameters.label: Outputs
parameters.description: The number of this node's outputs.
parameters.heading: Signature

parameters.label: Output #
parameters.description: The name of the output, which is what you reference in the #bind command.
parameters.heading: Signature

parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: The data type or port for the node output. Varying: A mono, UV, RGB, or RGBA layer that matches the corresponding Varying input layers. ID: An ID layer. Mono: A mono layer. UV: A UV layer. RGB: An RGB layer. RGBA: An RGBA layer. Geometry: A geometry type. Integer VDB: An integer VDB. Float VDB: A float VDB. Vector VDB: A vector VDB. Varying VDB: A float or vector VDB.
parameters.heading: Signature

parameters.label: Bindings
parameters.description: The number of this node's bound parameters. Expand a Bind# parameter's dropdown menu to configure its Name, Type, and other values.
parameters.heading: Bindings

parameters.label: Name
parameters.description: The name of the parameter. This is the value used in the kwargs dictionary.
parameters.heading: Bindings

parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: The type of parameter to create and bind. Integer Float Vector2 Vector Vector4 Ramp: A floating point (spline) ramp or RGB color ramp. This becomes a hou.Ramp object. String: A constant string value.
parameters.heading: Bindings

parameters.label: Value
parameters.description: The value to use for the set Type's parameters. When Type is set to * Integer, this is the integer value used for integer parameters. * Float, this is the float value used for float parameters. * Vector2, this is the float2 value used for float2 parameters. * Vector, this is the float3 value used for float3 parameters. * Vector4, this is the float4 value used for float4 parameters. * String, this is the string value used for string parameters. NOTE: This parameter doesn't apply when the Type is Ramp.
parameters.heading: Bindings

parameters.label: Data Type
parameters.description: When Type is Ramp, this is the type of ramp to bind. Float: Bind a floating point (spline) ramp. Vector: Bind an RGB color ramp.
parameters.heading: Bindings

parameters.label: Ramp
parameters.description: The floating point (spline) ramp or RGB color ramp. See Ramp parameters for more information.
parameters.heading: Bindings

entries.label: Rasterize Volume
entries.summary: Renders a volume viewed through a camera.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. Float VDBs are interpreted as providing the same value for all three components, prior to any remapping. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Move to Origin
parameters.description: Moves the output image to the origin.

parameters.label: Depth Conversion
parameters.description: Convert the mindepth and maxdepth inputs to distances from the camera from this kind of input. Distance: Doesn't modify the inputs since they're already distances. Depth: The inputs are depths. These are distances projected along the forward direction of the camera, like you can get from Node:cop/rasterizegeo. Height: The inputs are heights. These are displacements from the imaging plane toward the camera position.

parameters.label: Density Scale
parameters.description: The amount by which to multiply the remapped value. The node applies this scale after the ramp.
parameters.heading: Density

parameters.label: Min
parameters.description: The minimum value to use for the interval. The Diffuse Color, Emission, and Emission Color fields use this value for the interval by default. Turn on a field's Input Range to set a different minimum interval.
parameters.heading: Density

parameters.label: Max
parameters.description: The maximum value to use for the interval. The Diffuse Color, Emission, and Emission Color fields use this value for the interval by default. Turn on a field's Input Range to set a different maximum interval.
parameters.heading: Density

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: The transformation to perform before the node applies the ramp. No Ramp: Linearly map the rest of the domain the same way. Clamped Ramp: Clamp the remapped values to 0 and 1, respectively. Periodic Ramp: Wrap the remapped values around at 0 and 1.
parameters.heading: Density

parameters.label: Diffuse Tint
parameters.description: The RGB values by which to multiply the remapped value. The node applies this scale after the ramp. This outputs more color where there's more density since the light reflects off of the particles.
parameters.heading: Diffuse Color

parameters.label: Input Range
parameters.description: The minimum and maximum interval to use instead of the Density interval (Min and Max).
parameters.heading: Diffuse Color

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: The transformation to perform before the node applies the ramp. No Ramp: Linearly map the rest of the domain the same way. Clamped Ramp: Clamp the remapped values to 0 and 1, respectively. Periodic Ramp: Wrap the remapped values around at 0 and 1.
parameters.heading: Diffuse Color

parameters.label: Emission Scale
parameters.description: The amount by which to multiply the remapped value. The node applies this scale after the ramp.
parameters.heading: Emission

parameters.label: Input Range
parameters.description: The minimum and maximum interval to use instead of the Density interval (Min and Max).
parameters.heading: Emission

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: The transformation to perform before the node applies the ramp. No Ramp: Linearly map the rest of the domain the same way. Clamped Ramp: Clamp the remapped values to 0 and 1, respectively. Periodic Ramp: Wrap the remapped values around at 0 and 1.
parameters.heading: Emission

parameters.label: Emission Tint
parameters.description: The RGB values by which to multiply the remapped value. The node applies this scale after the ramp.
parameters.heading: Emission Color

parameters.label: Input Range
parameters.description: The minimum and maximum interval to use instead of the Density interval (Min and Max).
parameters.heading: Emission Color

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: The transformation to perform before the node applies the ramp. No Ramp: Linearly map the rest of the domain the same way. Clamped Ramp: Clamp the remapped values to 0 and 1, respectively. Periodic Ramp: Wrap the remapped values around at 0 and 1.
parameters.heading: Emission Color

parameters.label: Bake Light Fields
parameters.description: Bakes the light fields together before raymarching through them. This remaps the values in the VDBs before starting to raymarch. The node iterates over the density field and light field VDBs (the combination of Diffuse Color and Emission Color). Quality decreases and the output can appear more blocky when the VDB contains tiles. Turn this off if you want higher quality output. NOTE: Use the VDB Visualize Tree SOP to see if tiles are in the structure of the VDB. If present, tiles are red.
parameters.heading: Quality

parameters.label: Multiply Diffuse with Density before Interpolation
parameters.label_norm: multiply diffuse with density before interpolation
parameters.description: Determines the amount of diffuse light at any point. The node finds the eight voxels that surround the sample locations in the Density field and multiply these by the corresponding voxels in the Diffuse field. The node linearly interpolates the eight voxel values at the sample location. This has higher accuracy but can be slow since the node remaps each field eight times. This can cause a difference near the boundaries of the active region of the density field since you might expect regions with zero density to not contribute any color to the final raster. When off, the node samples the two fields at the given sample location and multiplies the interpolated values together. This is faster but has lower accuracy. Turn this on when there are visual artifacts in the output or the density changes very quickly from inactive (0) to a high density. This option may not make a difference for rasterizing pyro simulations because density often varies smoothly, so turn this off for better performance. For example, consider sampling halfway between a voxel with nonzero density and an inactive density voxel. In the color field there may be some non-black color where the density field is nonzero and a black background color. If you sample halfway between these two voxels, the interpolated density is nonzero but the interpolated color is darker because it's halfway between black and the active voxel's color. This results in the boundary of the active region looking darker than it should. When this option is turned on, the node first multiplies the density and diffuse fields and the inactive voxels with a black color don't contribute to the final output because they have zero density.
parameters.heading: Quality

parameters.label: Integration Step Size
parameters.description: The length of ray slices. This is the expected distance between samples when samples are jittered.
parameters.heading: Quality

parameters.label: Max Step Count
parameters.description: Used to prevent the OpenCL kernel from running forever or timing out. You shouldn't need to change the 4096 value unless rastering a very deep volume.
parameters.heading: Quality

parameters.label: Transmittance Cutoff
parameters.description: The transmittance of the accumulated portion of the ray after which to stop raymarching. A value of -1 turns this off and forces raymarching to continue until the ray exits the volume's bounding box, though there should be no difference in the output between 0 and -1. This is an optimization for when a very dense region of the volume is encountered, where almost none of the light from behind this region reaches the camera so you can stop raymarching early to save time. Due to rounding error, it's possible for the accumulated transmittance to reach 0 despite this not being physically possible, and this is seen when rasterizing very dense volumes.
parameters.heading: Quality

parameters.label: Seed Jitter with Time
parameters.description: Makes the sample location jittering depend on time.
parameters.heading: Quality

parameters.label: Sample Jitter Scale
parameters.description: The amount by which to jitter sample locations. When 0, sample locations are always at the centre of ray slices. When 1, sample locations can be drawn from anywhere along their respective ray slice. There is never more than one sample drawn per ray slice.
parameters.heading: Quality

parameters.label: Stratification Jitter Scale
parameters.description: The amount by which to jitter ray slice locations. This is a single offset applied to each view ray, not per sample. When 0, the start of ray slice #0 coincides with the ray origin. When 1, the start of ray slice #0 varies from backward and forward along the ray by half the step length.
parameters.heading: Quality

entries.label: Reaction-Diffusion Block End
entries.summary: Creates unique patterns by solving the reaction and diffusion of multiple chemicals as described by its inputs and parameters.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: Signature which controls the output of the node. Pattern (Mono): Mono output of the chemical pattern with various optional remappings and output correction applied. Chemical (UV): UV output of the raw chemical values. NOTE: Chemical output mode is outputting the raw values, and does not allow for any control for color customisation. Therefore results may be visually unfriendly.

parameters.label: Model
parameters.description: The model to use to describe how the chemicals interact, which includes presets. Gray-Scott: Two chemicals reacting with two input parameters for how the chemicals interact. Kenjiro Maginu: Two chemicals reacting with three input parameters for how the chemicals interact.

parameters.label: Preset
parameters.description: Sets parameters to create Gray-Scott preset patterns. Small Waves: Smaller oscillating waves. Large Waves: Larger oscillating waves. Spots: Self-replicating cells. Blinking Blobs: Tiny oscillating waves that bounce against each other, creating a blinking effect. Worms: Long stretchy blobs that resemble worms or snakes. Labyrinth: Maze-like labyrinth pattern with many corners and loops. Negatons: Creates a subcritical cellular look. Chaos with Negatons: Reaction that fluctuates between a stable state and a chaotic state mixed with subcritical cells. Spatiotemporal Chaos: Reaction that fluctuates between a stable state and a chaotic state.

parameters.label: Preset
parameters.description: Sets parameters to create Kenjiro Maginu preset patterns. Blobs & Spots: Tiny cellular blobs amongst larger blobs. Wormy: Long wormy structures with singular cells broken up throughout. Abstract: Creates a blobby abstract look with large blobs containing smaller blobs. Noisy: Chaotic noisy pattern. Brusselator: Creates a fast oscillating spiral look. Foamy: Chaotic pattern with similarities to foam. Oily: Pattern that slowly diffuses from large blobs (given the input was already chaotic). Nearly Chaos: Chaotic pattern with stable areas and unstable areas. Moving Brusselator: A Brusselator pattern with a more chaotic structure and moving spirals.

parameters.label: Simulate
parameters.description: Simulate: Turns on simulation so block outputs feed directly back into the inputs, which creates a feedback loop. This is useful for complex motion and simulations.
parameters.heading: Time

parameters.label: Reset Simulation
parameters.description: Reset Simulation: When Simulate is on, this clears the entire simulation cache.
parameters.heading: Time

parameters.label: Iterations
parameters.description: Amount of iterations to run in non-simulation mode.
parameters.heading: Time

parameters.label: Iterations per Step
parameters.description: Amount of iterations to take per step within non-simulation, simulation, or Live Simulation.
parameters.heading: Time

parameters.label: Live Simulation
parameters.description: Live Simulation: When Simulate is on, this turns on live simulation to provide an interactive, non-deterministic simulation mode. It simulates independent of the playbar and isn't associated with any keyframes or caching. This parameter (and its associated parameters) is intended as a sandbox mode where you don't have to rely on the playbar. TIP: Live Simulation doesn't save the results like other simulation types in Houdini, so use a Stash COP to save results.
parameters.heading: Time

parameters.label: Toggle Live Simulation
parameters.description: Toggle Live Simulation: When Live Simulation is on, this lets you pause and resume the live simulation. TIP: You can also use the Icon:BUTTONS/live_disable Live Simulation button to pause and resume live simulation. See Cooking controls for more information.
parameters.heading: Time

parameters.label: Live Tick
parameters.description: Live Tick: When Live Simulation is on, this is the current tick (frame) within the live simulation.
parameters.heading: Time

parameters.label: Time Scale
parameters.description: Time Scale: When Simulate is on, this is the amount to scale the time inside the block. A value of 1 maintains the normal speed, a value greater than 1 speeds up the simulation, and a value less than 1 slows down the simulation. NOTE
parameters.heading: Time

parameters.label: Substeps
parameters.description: Sets the amount of substeps for each simulated frame.
parameters.heading: Time

parameters.label: NOTE
parameters.description: When Live Simulation is on, the Start Frame, Cached Frames, and Checkpoint Rate parameters no longer apply.
parameters.heading: Caching

parameters.label: Caching
parameters.description: Turns on caching of frames.
parameters.heading: Caching

parameters.label: Start Frame
parameters.description: Start Frame: When Simulate is on, this is the frame on the Houdini playbar where the simulation starts.
parameters.heading: Caching

parameters.label: Cached Frames
parameters.description: Cached Frames: When Simulate is on, this is how many frames behind the current frame to keep cached.
parameters.heading: Caching

parameters.label: Checkpoint Rate
parameters.description: Checkpoint Rate: When Simulate is on, this is the rate at which the node continually caches a single frame. For example, set this to 24 to cache frames 24, 48, 72, and such. This allows random-scrubbing to be faster as it only has to re-cook from the checkpoint frame. Set to 0 to disable checkpointing.
parameters.heading: Caching

parameters.label: Switch to Raw Values
parameters.description: Interprets the parameters and input layers as raw. NOTE: It's recommended that you keep this off since the normalized parameters and layers are warped to limit the possibility of instability, create the most artistically interesting results, and stop the reaction from dying out or overreacting.
parameters.heading: Reaction Parameters

parameters.label: Scale Multiplier
parameters.description: Changes the size of the patterns by altering the reaction rate relative to the diffusion rate. This leads to the reaction happening slower at extreme scales, and tiny scales freeze the reaction altogether. Therefore, having a larger scale may require letting the reaction run for more iterations/ticks to fully grow into the requested scale.
parameters.heading: Reaction Parameters

parameters.label: NOTE
parameters.description: Input layers for alpha, beta, and gamma on the Reaction-Diffusion Block Begin COP override these parameters. Input layers for scale and coefficient on the Reaction-Diffusion Block Begin COP multiply these parameters.
parameters.heading: Reaction Parameters

parameters.label: Alpha α (Feed)
parameters.description: Chemical A is added into the simulation at a given "feed" rate. This is scaled with (1.0f - A) so that A does not exceed 1.0.
parameters.heading: Gray-Scott Model

parameters.label: Beta β (Kill)
parameters.description: Chemical B is removed from the simulation at a given "kill" rate. This is scaled with (kill + feed) * B so that it does not go below 0.0.
parameters.heading: Gray-Scott Model

parameters.label: Alpha α
parameters.description: Controls the nonlinear self-activation of A. Essentially the reaction strength of A.
parameters.heading: Kenjiro Maginu Model

parameters.label: Beta β
parameters.description: Determines how strongly Chemical B reacts to the presence of Chemical A.
parameters.heading: Kenjiro Maginu Model

parameters.label: Gamma γ
parameters.description: Controls how strongly B is pulled back towards A. Essenially a damping or decay coefficient that prevents B from growing indefinitely.
parameters.heading: Kenjiro Maginu Model

parameters.label: NOTE
parameters.description: The coefficient input on the Reaction-Diffusion Block Begin COP multiplies these parameters.
parameters.heading: Diffusion Coefficients

parameters.label: Diffusion A
parameters.description: Controls how fast chemical A diffuses. Generally, the Gray-Scott model sits at 1.0 and the Kenjiro Maginu model sits at 1.0.
parameters.heading: Diffusion Coefficients

parameters.label: Diffusion B
parameters.description: Controls how fast chemical B diffuses. Generally, the Gray-Scott model sits at 0.5 and the Kenjiro Maginu model sits at 1.0.
parameters.heading: Diffusion Coefficients

parameters.label: NOTE
parameters.description: The activation mask must have an activation area within a valid area of the boundary otherwise the reaction can't grow.
parameters.heading: Boundary

parameters.label: Invert Boundary
parameters.description: Inverts the input boundary shape.
parameters.heading: Boundary

parameters.label: Boundary Threshold
parameters.description: The offset of the boundary shape. Higher values grow the shape and lower values shrink the shape.
parameters.heading: Boundary

parameters.label: Boundary Smoothing
parameters.description: The amount to blur the boundary shape, which causes the reaction to contract away from the border of the boundary. At lower Reaction Scales, high values of smoothing can sometimes cause instability.
parameters.heading: Boundary

parameters.label: Invert
parameters.description: Inverts the values of the output pattern.
parameters.heading: Output Correction

parameters.label: Normalize Model
parameters.description: Remaps the range of the output to keep the values consistent across models. This is useful since some models and modes have 'weaker' values.
parameters.heading: Output Correction

parameters.label: Clamp Minimum
parameters.description: The minimum pixel value of the image.
parameters.heading: Output Correction

parameters.label: Clamp Maximum
parameters.description: The maximum pixel value of the image.
parameters.heading: Output Correction

entries.label: Resample
entries.summary: Performs image scaling by changing the width, height, and pixel sizes.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Size Control
parameters.description: The method used to control how resampling is done. Resolution: Control the number of pixels in the width or height. Aspect Ratio: Control the ratio between the width and height. Pixel Size: Control the size of the pixels.
parameters.heading: Canvas

parameters.label: Base Size
parameters.description: The base size to use as the final output's dimensions. Parameter: Set the base parameters directly using Base Resolution, Base Aspect Ratio, or Pixel Size. Size Input: Inherit the base parameters from the size_ref input or, if not wired in, the source input.
parameters.heading: Canvas

parameters.label: Base Resolution
parameters.description: When Size Control is Resolution and Base Size is Parameter, this is the base number of pixels for the final image's width and height.
parameters.heading: Canvas

parameters.label: Base Aspect Ratio
parameters.description: When Size Control is Aspect Ratio and Base Size is Parameter, this is the base aspect ratio for the final image.
parameters.heading: Canvas

parameters.label: Pixel Size
parameters.description: When Size Control is Pixel Size and Base Size is Parameter, this is the base pixel size for the final image. The base pixel size is square pixels, so this size is for both the width and height of a pixel.
parameters.heading: Canvas

parameters.label: Uniform Scale
parameters.description: The scale to apply to the Base Size. For Resolution, this scales the number of pixels in both dimensions. For Aspect Ratio, this scales the aspect ratio. For Pixel Size, this scales the pixel's dimensions.
parameters.heading: Canvas

parameters.label: Resolution Scale
parameters.description: When Size Control is Resolution, this scales the number of pixels in width and height respectively.
parameters.heading: Canvas

parameters.label: Fixed Dimension
parameters.description: When Size Control is Aspect Ratio, this determines which dimension stays constant from the input image. The other dimension changes to match the aspect ratio. Width: The width matches the input image's width. Height: The height matches the input image's height. Smaller Dimension: The smaller resolution matches the input image's smaller resolution. Larger Dimension: The larger resolution matches the input image's larger resolution.
parameters.heading: Canvas

parameters.label: Size Scale
parameters.description: When Size Control is Pixel Size, this scales the pixel's width and height respectively.
parameters.heading: Canvas

parameters.label: Reframe to Destination
parameters.description: Stretches the input image through resampling to conform to the entire boundary of the output and maintains the given pixel size. Specifically, this makes the display window match the data window. See Data and display windows for more information.
parameters.heading: Canvas

parameters.label: Filter
parameters.description: The filter used to sample. See Filters for more information. Point: Sets the pixel value to the pixel value of the nearest neighbor. Bilinear: Sets the pixel value through bilinear interpolation. Box: Sets the pixel value through a box filter, done by sampling all pixels within a box on the original image's matching pixel. Bartlett: Sets the pixel value through interpolating according to a triangular window or a Bartlett window, taking each pixel as a sample of this signal. Catmull-Rom: Sets the pixel value through a bicubic spline known as the Catmull-Rom spline. This is a special case of the Mitchell-Netravali filter. Mitchell: Sets the pixel value through a bicubic spline known as the Mitchell-Netravali filter. B-spline: Sets the pixel value through a bicubic spline known as the B-spline. This is a special case of the Mitchell-Netravali filter.
parameters.heading: Sampling

parameters.label: Stretch Behavior
parameters.description: Determine how the image stretches after the resample operation. Specifically, this determines how to stretch the display window. NOTE: If Reframe to Destination is on, this parameter has no effect since the display window doesn't stretch differently. Stretch to Fit: Stretches the pixels to fit within the new display window. The display window is scaled naively according to the same scale that the data window is scaled at. Fit Horizontally: Maintains the original pixel aspect ratio and aspect ratio by scaling the display window's x dimension in relation to the data window's x dimension. Fit Vertically: Maintains the original pixel aspect ratio and aspect ratio by scaling the display window's y dimension in relation to the data window's y dimension. Fit Maximally: Maintains the original pixel aspect ratio and aspect ratio by scaling the display window according to the original image's data window's maximal dimension. Fit Minimally: Maintains the original pixel aspect ratio and aspect ratio by scaling the display window according to the original image's data window's minimal dimension.
parameters.heading: Sampling

entries.label: RGBA to RGB
entries.summary: Converts RGBA layers or attributes to RGB.

parameters.label: Remove Premultiplied Alpha
parameters.description: Undoes the premultiplication of the RGBA layers or attributes (which are usually premultiplied) to give you the unassociated RGB layer. When off, the node directly splits the RGB and alpha channels.

entries.label: RGB to RGBA
entries.summary: Converts RGB layers or attributes to RGBA.

parameters.label: Premultiply Alpha
parameters.description: Premultiplies the inputs to create an associated RGBA layer. When off, the node directly joins the RGB and alpha channels. NOTE: RGBA layers are usually premultiplied.

entries.label: UV Sample
entries.summary: Samples an input layer using a UV layer or attribute.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: UV Space
parameters.description: The space that the UV input is in. This affects the required range of the UV input. Texture: Use texture space, which is 0 to 1 in the data window of the input. This provides normalized coordinates that're independent of the source's aspect ratio. For example, use this space when looking up into a latitude and longitude map. Image: Use image space, which is -1 to 1 in the display window of the input. This preserves square pixels for non-square aspect ratios. This space is invariant to cropping or overscanning.

parameters.label: Filter Scale
parameters.description: For non-identity UV maps, the input must be filtered to avoid aliasing. This value defaults to the size of the voxels, but can be increased or decreased to reflect the actual nature of the UV map. Note that attributes lack an intrinsic filter size so this likely has to be manually adjusted to the pixel size.

parameters.label: Filter
parameters.description: The method used to sample the image. The default value is Box. See Filters for more information.

entries.label: SDF Adjust
entries.summary: Modifies the values for a Mono SDF layer.

parameters.label: Iso Offset
parameters.description: Controls the crossing point of the signed distance field values that is considered the border of the shape. Higher values will enlarge the shape, while lower values will shrink the shape.

parameters.label: Outline
parameters.description: When turned on, the shape is made into a hollowed thin shape, and this value controls the thickness around the original border. This is achieved by taking the field's absolute value and subtracting this number from it.

parameters.label: Absolute Value
parameters.description: When turned on, this changes all negative values into positives. This will remove what would be considered the inside of the shape, only leaving a thin border of the shape.

parameters.label: Invert
parameters.description: When turned on, this will swap positive and negative values, making the outside region to be considered the inside of the shape.

entries.label: SDF Blend
entries.summary: Combines two Mono SDF layers.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: Controls the operation to combine the two signed distance fields. Union: Creates a new solid shape which encloses the combined shape(s) of the two inputs. Intersect: Creates a new solid shape which encloses any shared shape(s) between the two inputs. Subtract: Removes from the first input the shape(s) based on the second input. Difference: Removes the shared shape(s) of the two inputs.

parameters.label: Fillet
parameters.description: Controls how to join the input shapes at the intersection points. None: No fillet operation is applied. Smooth: The intersection points between the shapes will be smoothed. Round: Similar to the smooth, but it uses a quarter-circle to join the two shapes smoothly. Chamfer: The intersection points between the shapes will make a 45-degree chamfered edge.

parameters.label: Smooth
parameters.description: Controls the amount of smoothing applied where the two input shapes join together.

parameters.label: Round
parameters.description: Controls the amount of rounding applied where the two input shapes join together.

parameters.label: Chamfer
parameters.description: Controls the amount of chamfer applied where the two input shapes join together.

parameters.label: Re-Normalize
parameters.description: When turned on, the signed distance field is re-calculated after the blend. This is needed as some operations do not preserve the correct field values.

entries.label: SDF Shape
entries.summary: Builds a 2D signed distance field of a selected shape.

parameters.label: Shape Class
parameters.description: Shapes are organized into various groups. Basic shapes are consist of elementary algebraic shapes, while Marker and Compound contain shapes of various complexities.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Basic Shapes
parameters.description: The list of available elementary algebraic shapes when Shape Class is set to Basic. See Basic Shapes for more information.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Markers
parameters.description: The list of available marker shapes when Shape Class is set to Marker. See Markers for more information.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Compound Shapes
parameters.description: The list of available complex shapes when Shape Class is set to Compound. See Compound Shapes for more information.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: The radius of the circle. Use this parameter to control the size of the circle.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Arc
parameters.description: When turned on, and the value is less than 1, the circle becomes an open arc, which can be used to create shapes of a sliced pie.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Thickness
parameters.description: When turned on, and the value is less than 1, the circle becomes hollowed, which can be used to create ring-like shapes.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Round Ends
parameters.description: When both Arc and Thickness are turned on, use this to make the end of the ring shape rounded.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Quadratic Circle
parameters.description: When turned on, the circle changes into a quadratic circle shape.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Size
parameters.description: Controls the horizontal and vertical size of the diamond shape.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Length
parameters.description: Sets the length of the line, which is oriented horizontally at the center. Turn on Use Points next to this parameter if you need to control the exact positions for the start and end points of the line.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Use Points
parameters.description: When this is turned on, the start and end points of the lines can be controlled by Start Point and End Point parameters.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Start Point
parameters.description: Sets the horizontal and vertical position for the start point of the line.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: End Point
parameters.description: Sets the horizontal and vertical position for the end point of the line.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Add Thickness
parameters.description: When turned on, the start and end thickness of the lines can be controlled by Start Thickness and End Thickness.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Start Thickness
parameters.description: The thickness of the line at the start point.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: End Thickness
parameters.description: The thickness of the line at the end point.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Bulge
parameters.description: When turned on, controls the thickness at the center of the line. A value of 0 means no bulging. In this mode, only Start Thickness is on to control the same thickness at both ends of the line.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Size
parameters.description: Controls the horizontal and vertical size of the rectangle shape.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Round Corners
parameters.description: When turned on, controls the roundness of the corners. With a value of 1 and both horizontal and vertical size is equal, the shape becomes a circle. When this is set to 0, the rectangle is not rounded. Use Separate Controls next to this parameter to control the roundness for each corner separately.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Separate Controls
parameters.description: When turned on, the roundness of each corner can be controlled separately.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Top Left
parameters.description: Controls the roundness for the top left corner of the rectangle. Value of 1 means the corner is rounded to the maximum, and the value of 0 means that the corner is not rounded.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Top Right
parameters.description: Controls the roundness for the top right corner of the rectangle. Value of 1 means the corner is rounded to the maximum, and the value of 0 means that the corner is not rounded.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Bottom Left
parameters.description: Controls the roundness for the bottom left corner of the rectangle. Value of 1 means the corner is rounded to the maximum, and the value of 0 means that the corner is not rounded.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Bottom Right
parameters.description: Controls the roundness for the bottom right corner of the rectangle. Value of 1 means the corner is rounded to the maximum, and the value of 0 means that the corner is not rounded.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: The size of the radius for the polygon shape.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Number of Sides
parameters.description: Controls the number of sides for the polygon. The larger the number the more the shape will resemble a circle.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: The size of the radius for the spiral shape.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Arc Bend
parameters.description: Controls how much each arc length segment should bend towards the center. When this value is set to 0 and the Number of Arcs is set to 4, the arc is a perfect circle.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Number of Arcs
parameters.description: Controls the number of components the spiral is made of. When Arc Bend is set to 0, a value of 4 creates a perfect circle.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: The size of the radius for a squircle, which is a shape intermediate between a square and a circle.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Blend
parameters.description: Controls the shape of the squircle. The value of 2 creates a perfect circle. Values above this will blend the shape more into a square. A value of 1 creates a diamond shape.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: The size of the radius for the star shape.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Number of Sides
parameters.description: Controls the number of sides for the star. The larger the number, the more the shape will resemble a circle.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Angle Factor
parameters.description: Controls how much the center of the sides push towards the center of the shape. The angle factor of 2 will create a regular polygon shape instead of a star.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Height
parameters.description: Controls the vertical height of the trapezoid.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Bottom Length
parameters.description: Controls the horizontal length at the bottom of the trapezoid.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Top Length

entries.label: Segment by Connectivity
entries.summary: Segment a layer into connected components.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Connectivity
parameters.description: The rule that determines whether pixels are connected or unconnected. Below Threshold: Connect all pixels below the threshold. Above Threshold: Connect all pixels above the threshold. At Threshold: Connect pixels to their neighbors if they're on the same side of the threshold. At Levels: Connect pixels if they're in the same band of values. Each band is the Threshold size.

parameters.label: Threshold
parameters.description: The threshold for connectivity. When Connectivity is At Levels, this is the width of a band of connectivity. TIP: Click Smallicon:BUTTONS/layer_sample and then click on the layer to set the Threshold.

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.description: When Connectivity is At Levels, this is the global offset to adjust where the bands split.

parameters.label: Collapse IDs
parameters.description: Collapse the generated ID values so they range from zero to the number of segments. While the order is deterministic, it will vary depending on where the first pixel of each region is located, so should not be relied upon for an animated source.

entries.label: Segment by Value
entries.summary: Segment a mono layer into bands of similar value.

parameters.label: Method
parameters.description: The method used to specify the bands of similar value. Width and Offset: Specify the width of the band and an offset from zero. Number of Segments: Specify the number of segments that fit inside the provided range.

parameters.label: Width
parameters.description: When Method is Width and Offset, this is the maximum difference in value to belong to the same segment.

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.description: When Method is Width and Offset, this is the offset of where to start the first segment.

parameters.label: Segments
parameters.description: When Method is Number of Segments, this is the number of segments to fit in the provided minimum to maximum values.

parameters.label: Segment Location
parameters.description: The method used to convert the value into a segment integer. Starts at Value: Floor to convert the value into a segment integer. Centered at Value: Round to convert the value into a segment integer.

parameters.label: Minimum Value
parameters.description: The minimal input value to use. Values outside of this follow the Values Below rules. When Method is Number of Segments, this is the start of the interval. TIP: Click Smallicon:BUTTONS/layer_sample and then click on the layer to set the Minimum Value.

parameters.label: Maximum Value
parameters.description: The maximal input value to use. Values outside of this follow the Values Above rules. When Method is Number of Segments, this is the end of the interval. TIP: Click Smallicon:BUTTONS/layer_sample and then click on the layer to set the Maximum Value.

parameters.label: Values Below
parameters.description: The method used to treat values below the Minimum Value. Extend: Convert and round values with no clamping. Invalid (-1): An explicit -1 is output for the segment ID. Clamp: Clamp values to the minimal value. Wrap: Wrap values, which means segment values repeat cyclicly.

parameters.label: Values Above
parameters.description: The method used to treat values above the Maximum Value. Extend: Convert and round values with no clamping. Invalid (-1): An explicit -1 is output for the segment ID. Clamp: Clamp values to the minimal value. Wrap: Wrap values, which means segment values repeat cyclicly.

entries.label: Sequence Blend
entries.summary: Blends multiple layers together.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source image accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Invert
parameters.description: Inverts the Blend value.

parameters.label: Blend
parameters.description: The blend factor to map input images. This value is normalized and blends between all image# inputs if you range from 0 to 1.

entries.label: Slap Comp Import
entries.summary: Import live layers from the Solaris Viewport.

parameters.label: Reload Image
parameters.description: Dirty this node and try to re-load the last layers that were posted by an interactive render.

parameters.label: Live Recook
parameters.description: When live, any interactive render dirties this node whenever it generates new frames. This will cause it to continuously recook showing a live output, but may slow down the render process if the COP network is visible.

parameters.label: Import Cameras with Slap Comp Inputs
parameters.label_norm: import cameras with slap comp inputs
parameters.description: A rendered layer has a location in space from the original camera. Often this isn't relevant to Slap Comp, so this can be disabled to always import layers in the canonical coordinates.

parameters.label: Add AOVs from Last Render
parameters.description: Updates the AOV list with all of the AOVs exported by the last render. This may contain extra unnecessary AOVs that can be deleted. This method is more reliable than manually setting up the correct names and types for AOVs.

parameters.label: Slap Comp AOV
parameters.description: The name of the AOV to import as a layer.
parameters.heading: Number of AOVs

parameters.label: Channel Type
parameters.description: The data type of the AOV that is imported.
parameters.heading: Number of AOVs

entries.label: Smooth Fill
entries.summary: Smoothly fills a region of a layer.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. A value of 1 means this node uses only the new value. The default value is 1. See Mask for more information.

parameters.label: Fill
parameters.description: The fillarea input defines what is inside and should be filled. Below Threshold: Anything below the threshold will be filled. Above Threshold: Anything above the threshold will be filled.

parameters.label: Threshold
parameters.description: The threshold value in the fillarea layer to start filling. TIP: Click Smallicon:BUTTONS/layer_sample and then click on the layer to set the Threshold.

parameters.label: Iterations
parameters.description: The number of iterations to relax the filled values to achieve a smooth result.

parameters.label: Acceleration
parameters.description: A value of 1 ensures the values strictly smooth as iterations increase, ensuring stability and that uncoverged pixels are still artifact free. However, successive over relaxation can be performed to speed up convergence, so this can be raised as high as 1.98 to speed up the process.

entries.label: Solve Poisson Multigrid
entries.summary: Solves Poisson's equation in a rectangular region using geometric multigrid.

parameters.label: Iterations
parameters.description: Number of V-cycle iterations to perform. The solution will be more accurate with a higher number of iterations, but will also take longer to produce.

parameters.label: Smoothing Method
parameters.description: The method used for relaxation on up- and down-strokes. Gauss-Seidel offers better asymptotic convergence; it also requires less memory, as the red-black partitioning of cells allows for in-place smoothing. The Jacobi method, on the other hand, works on all pixels at once. This avoids systemic checkerboard patterns in the residuals, but requires an extra copy of the image.

parameters.label: Up Smoothing Iterations
parameters.description: Number of smoothing iterations to perform on the up-stroke (after prolongation of the coarse solution). Higher values will increase cost, but also improve the solution.

parameters.label: Down Smoothing Iterations
parameters.description: Number of smoothing iterations to perform on the down-stroke (before restriction of the fine residual). Higher values will increase cost, but also improve the solution.

parameters.label: Coarsest Smoothing Iterations
parameters.description: Number of smoothing iterations to perform at the final coarsest level (in lieu of an exact solution). Higher values will increase cost, but also improve the solution. Value of this parameter should be on the same order as square of Target Coarse Dimensions.

parameters.label: Target Coarse Dimensions
parameters.description: The multigrid solver iteratively coarsens the layer to build a hierarchy of grids for rapid convergence at all scales. This parameter controls when the coarsening ceases; namely, coarsening along a dimension will stop once the number of cells falls below Target Coarse Dimensions. While larger values give a leaner hierarchy with fewer levels, they also result in larger number of variables at the coarsest level, which in turn may require more Coarsest Smoothing Iterations for adequate convergence.

parameters.label: X Borders
parameters.description: State of borders on the left and right sides of the layer. Open borders correspond to Dirichlet boundary conditions (prescribing value of 0). Closed borders correspond to Neumann boundary conditions (enforcing normal derivative of 0). When set to Periodic, left and right sides of the layer are virtually connected.

parameters.label: Y Borders
parameters.description: State of borders on the bottom and top sides of the image. Open borders correspond to Dirichlet boundary conditions (prescribing value of 0). Closed borders correspond to Neumann boundary conditions (enforcing normal derivative of 0). When set to Periodic, bottom and top sides of the layer are virtually connected.

entries.label: SOP Import
entries.summary: Imports SOP geometry into Copernicus.

parameters.label: Use External SOP
parameters.description: Uses an explicit SOP path for the source of the geometry. When off, the SOP Import node's own geometry is used.

parameters.label: SOP Path
parameters.description: When Use External SOP is on, this is the path of the SOP node to use as a geometry source.

entries.label: SOP Invoke
entries.summary: Invokes a compiled SOP block on the inputs.

parameters.label: Inputs
parameters.description: The number of inputs.

parameters.label: Input #

entries.label: Space Transform

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Vector Type

parameters.label: Source Space

Buffer: The index with respect to the actual raw data. This may differ from Pixels if running with a pixel scale. Pixel: Pixel indices, which are unaffected by pixel scale. Texture: A 0 to 1 value within the data window of the layer or attribute. Image: The unstreteched -1 to 1 position within the fitted display window. World: The location in world space.

parameters.label: Destination Space

Buffer: The index with respect to the actual raw data. This may differ from Pixels if running with a pixel scale. Pixel: Pixel indices, which are unaffected by pixel scale. Texture: A 0 to 1 value within the data window of the layer or attribute. Image: The unstreteched -1 to 1 position within the fitted display window. World: The location in world space.

entries.label: Surface Dither
entries.summary: Applies a halftone dithering pattern relative to UVs.

parameters.label: Density Scale
parameters.description: The overall scale of the surface-stable pattern. This controls how big the halftone pattern is in UV space.

parameters.label: Pattern Scale
parameters.description: The overall scale of the textured pattern. This is a UV scaling factor.

parameters.label: Pattern Scale XY
parameters.description: The per-axis scaling of the textured pattern in UV space.

parameters.label: Pattern Offset
parameters.description: The translation of the pattern in UV space. As the pattern repeats, large changes may appear to do nothing.

parameters.label: Pattern Rotate
parameters.description: The rotation of the pattern in UV space.

parameters.label: Dot Scale
parameters.description: The global scale of the dotscale input and the Level Transition.

parameters.label: Output Type
parameters.description: The type of the dither output. The dither pattern internally generates an SDF. Mask: Internally convert the SDF to a black and white mask using the ISO value and smooth rate. SDF: Output the internal SDF for further post-processing.

parameters.label: Iso Offset
parameters.description: The crossing point to use for converting the SDF into a mask. You can use this to adjust the dot size without affecting level transitions.

parameters.label: Smooth
parameters.description: The width to smooth out the SDF conversion when crossing over the ISO offset.

parameters.label: Level Transition
parameters.description: How to adjust the dot scale when switching texture scales, which can help minimize the jump across levels. See Ramp parameters for more information.

parameters.label: Shape Resolution
parameters.description: The shape input is resampled to this resolution. This speeds up filtering of the shape layer.

entries.label: Switch
entries.summary: Selects an input layer.

parameters.label: Select Input
parameters.description: Which input to provide as the output. If the input is out of range, the nearest input is used.

entries.label: Switch by Type
entries.summary: Selects an output layer by the type of the inputs.

parameters.label: If No Matches
parameters.description: What to output if none of the rules match the type_ref. Unwire: Output a unwired result. Use Test Input: Output the test_ref. Use First Choice: Output the first choice, which is the input after the test_ref.

parameters.label: Choice #
parameters.description: Negates the rule - accepts where it would have rejected, and rejects where it would have accepted.
parameters.heading: Inputs

parameters.label: Rule #
parameters.description: The rule is true if the input matches this type. Any: This wll match against all types. Layer: Matches against any layer, Mono, UV, RGB, RGBA, or ID. Mono/Color: Matches against Mono, UV, RGB, and RGBA layers. ID: Matches against ID layers. Mono: Matches against Mono layers. UV: Matches against UV layers. RGB: Matches against RGB layers. RGBA: Matches against RGBA layers. Geometry: Matches against Geometry. Metadata: Matches against metadata.
parameters.heading: Inputs

parameters.label: Output Type

Mono: The output is a Mono layer. UV: The output is a UV layer. RGB: The output is an RGB layer. RGBA: The output is an RGBA layer. Geometry: The output is a Geometry. parameters.heading: Inputs

entries.label: Switch If Wired
entries.summary: Selects an input based on what is connected.

parameters.label: Selection
parameters.description: The rule used to determine the output. Use First Wired to output the first wired input if one exists. Use First Unless Unwired to output the first input if all inputs are wired. First Wired: The first input that is wired is output. If none are, the output is unwired. First Unless Unwired: If all the inputs are wired, return the first input. Otherwise return unwired. This allows you to "erase" a wire if an optional path shouldn't be used if an external input wasn't wired.

entries.label: Tone Map
entries.summary: Applies a filmic tone mapping curve to compress a high dynamic range input into a displayable range.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Operator
parameters.description: The filmic tone mapping operator to use. Reinhard: Computes a global scale factor that preserves detail in low contrast areas, while compressing high luminances to a displayable range. This function ensures that the output approaches 1 as luminance increases, which prevents overexposure while preserving details in both shadows and highlights. This is a simple and fast function. Ward: Yields a display with roughly the same contrast visibility as the actual scene. This uses a constant scale factor that, when applied to the calculated pixel values, makes the differences visible in only the real-world visible in only your display. ACES Filmic: Applies an efficient approximation of the Academy Color Encoding System (ACES) tone mapping curve. Hable Filmic: Applies a filmic tone mapping curve with cinematic highlight rolloff and contrast shaping. Hable Filmic Updated: Uses piecewise power curves for improved artistic control over contrast, shoulder rolloff, and toe response. An enhanced version of Hable Filmic, this offers a more intuitive way to independently adjust the highlight and shadow curves. Unreal: Unreal Engine's filmic tonemapper implements the ACES standard while providing more controls on adjusting different parts of the S-curve.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. You can also set the RGBA channels to which you apply the effects of this node. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information. Toggle RGB: Turns the Red, Green, and Blue channels on and off. Red: Applies this node's effects to the Red channel. Green: Applies this node's effects to the Green channel. Blue: Applies this node's effects to the Blue channel. Alpha: Applies this node's effects to the Alpha channel.

parameters.label: Treat RGBA as Premultiplied
parameters.description: Treats RGBA as premultiplied, which multiplies the red, green, and blue channels by the alpha channel.

parameters.label: Exposure
parameters.description: The overall brightness of the image before the node applies tone mapping. Each unit increases brightness by one stop (doubling the light) and negative values darken the image.

parameters.label: Shoulder Strength
parameters.description: The strength of the curve at the shoulder section. Lower values cause a more gradual falloff at high luminance. The curve bends downward earlier and compresses the highlights more aggressively, which mutes the highlights. Higher values make the curve compress the highlights less initially so the curve stays linear for longer and only flattens near the top, which lets bright areas stay brighter. This value is in the 0 to 1 range.

parameters.label: Linear Strength
parameters.description: The linear (straight) part of the curve between the toe (shadows) and shoulder (highlights). Higher values steepen the mid section slope, which enhances contrast and brightness. This value is in the 0 to 1 range.

parameters.label: Linear Angle
parameters.description: The angle of the linear (straight) part of the curve.

parameters.label: Toe Strength
parameters.description: The amount to lift the dark parts of the image. Higher values lift shadows, which makes them more visible but less contrasted. This value is in the 0 to 1 range.

parameters.label: Toe Length
parameters.description: How much of the dynamic range is in the toe. With a small value, the toe is short and quickly transitions into the linear section. A value of 0 means there's no toe and a value of 1 means the toe takes up half the curve. This value is in the 0 to 1 range.

parameters.label: Shoulder Strength
parameters.description: The speed at which bright highlights fall off to white. Higher values create a stronger falloff and more compressed highlight. This value is in the 0 to 1 range.

parameters.label: Shoulder Length
parameters.description: Adds extra stops (F-stops) beyond the point where the curve normally hits pure white if the Shoulder Strength is 0. This controls the dynamic range of the curve and stretches the highlight's range so the curve stays below white longer. This value is in the 0 to 1 range.

parameters.label: Shoulder Angle
parameters.description: The angle of the curve at the shoulder section.

parameters.label: Toe Strength
parameters.description: The amount to adjust the dark color in the tonemapper. This value is in the 0 to 1 range.

parameters.label: Shoulder Strength
parameters.description: The amount to adjust the bright color in the tonemapper. This value is in the 0 to 1 range.

parameters.label: Slope
parameters.description: The amount to adjust the steepness of the S-curve. Higher values increase the slope's steepness (darker) and lower values decrease the slope's steepness (lighter). This value is in the 0 to 1 range.

entries.label: Two Way Switch If Wired
entries.summary: Selects between two inputs based on if you wire in another input.

parameters.label: Selection
parameters.description: The input to use when you wire in a test input. First Input If Wired: Use the first input. If you don't wire in a test input, use the second input. Second Input If Wired: Use the second input. If you don't wire in a test input, use the first input.

entries.label: UV Map
entries.summary: Generates a UV Map.

parameters.label: UV Space
parameters.description: Controls which coordinate system is used to generate the UV Map. Texture: Texture coordinates go from 0 at the bottom left of the data window to 1 at the top right. The size of pixels isn't square - a 16:9 image will have non-square pixels. The default visualization for these is a red/green map. Image: Image coordinates go from -1 at the bottom left of the framed display window to 1 at the top right. The display window is framed so pixels are square, regardless of the image's aspect ratio. The default visualization for these is a red/blue map. Pixel: Pixel coordinates are 0.5, 0.5 for the center of the bottom-left most pixel, and increase to the right and to the top.

parameters.label: U Border
parameters.description: When the pixel's location lies out of the canonical range for the coordinate system (0..1 for texture, -1..1 for image), this controls how it is adjusted. Clamp: The location is clamped to the nearest valid value. Mirror: The location values are mirrored about the boundary. Wrap: The location values repeat from the far side of the image. Extend: No adjustment is made and the locations are left unchanged, useful for recording overscan.

parameters.label: U Shift
parameters.description: Horizontal adjustment to the pixel's location, prior to clamping by the border.

parameters.label: U Cycles
parameters.description: Multiplicative scale on the pixels horizontal location. In wrapped mode, effectively allows the creation of repeating cycles.

parameters.label: V Border
parameters.description: When the pixel's location lies out of the canonical range for the coordinate system (0..1 for texture, -1..1 for image), this controls how it is adjusted. Clamp: The location is clamped to the nearest valid value. Mirror: The location values are mirrored about the boundary. Wrap: The location values repeat from the far side of the image. Extend: No adjustment is made and the locations are left unchanged, useful for recording overscan.

parameters.label: V Shift
parameters.description: Vertical adjustment to the pixel's location, prior to clamping by the border.

parameters.label: V Cycles
parameters.description: Multiplicative scale on the pixels vertical location. In wrapped mode, effectively allows the creation of repeating cycles.

entries.label: UV Map by ID
entries.summary: Creates a UV Map for each connected ID island.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: What should be output in each pixel. UV Map: The relative location of the pixel in its island's uv map is output. Center: The center of the bounding box of the island. Minimum: The bottom left of the bounding box of the island. Maximum: The top right of the bounding box of the island. Size: The size of the bounding box of the island.

parameters.label: UV Space
parameters.description: The space to define the islands in. Texture: Texture space ranges from 0 to 1 and will be stretched to fit the bounding box. Image: Image space ranges from -1 to 1 and will be framed to fit the bounding box, so keep pixels square.

parameters.label: Auto Scale
parameters.description: Controls if the UV Map should be scaled to fit the island's bounding box.

parameters.label: U Border
parameters.description: When the pixel's location lies out of the canonical range for the coordinate system (0..1 for texture, -1..1 for image), this controls how it is adjusted. Clamp: The location is clamped to the nearest valid value. Mirror: The location values are mirrored about the boundary. Wrap: The location values repeat from the far side of the image. Extend: No adjust ment is made and the locations are left unchanged, useful for recording overscan.

parameters.label: U Shift
parameters.description: Horizontal adjustment to the pixel's location, prior to clamping by the border.

parameters.label: U Cycles
parameters.description: Multiplicative scale on the pixels horizontal location. In wrapped mode, effectively allows the creation of repeating cycles.

parameters.label: V Border
parameters.description: When the pixel's location lies out of the canonical range for the coordinate system (0..1 for texture, -1..1 for image), this controls how it is adjusted. Clamp: The location is clamped to the nearest valid value. Mirror: The location values are mirrored about the boundary. Wrap: The location values repeat from the far side of the image. Extend: No adjust ment is made and the locations are left unchanged, useful for recording overscan.

parameters.label: V Shift
parameters.description: Vertical adjustment to the pixel's location, prior to clamping by the border.

parameters.label: V Cycles
parameters.description: Multiplicative scale on the pixels vertical location. In wrapped mode, effectively allows the creation of repeating cycles.

parameters.label: Zero Negative IDs
parameters.description: Negative IDs normally form their own connected islands. This can be distracting if negative IDs are used for invalid IDs. This will set them to zero.

entries.label: VDB Activate from Points
entries.summary: Activates leaves on a VDB according to a point cloud.

parameters.label: Leaf Dilation
parameters.description: Expand the active region a fixed number of leaves. The maximum of Leaf Dilation Dist and Leaf Dilation are used.

parameters.label: Leaf Dilation Dist
parameters.description: Expand the active region a fixed distance in world space; this is raised to the nearest leaf. The maximum of Leaf Dilation Dist and Leaf Dilation are used.

parameters.label: Voxel Scale
parameters.description: Scale the reference VDB's voxel size by this, allowing for the creation of a higher or lower resolution VDB.

parameters.label: Sort Leaves
parameters.description: The order of the leaves is normally non-deterministic, which does not matter if the VDB is accessed spatially. Sorting the leaves can ensure the leaves will always process in the same order if an algorithm depends on this, at the cost of extra time.

parameters.label: Clip Min X
parameters.description: Deactivate any leaves with world positions less than this in X.

parameters.label: Clip Min Y
parameters.description: Deactivate any leaves with world positions less than this in Y.

parameters.label: Clip Min Z
parameters.description: Deactivate any leaves with world positions less than this in Z.

parameters.label: Clip Max X
parameters.description: Deactivate any leaves with world positions greater than this in X.

parameters.label: Clip Max Y
parameters.description: Deactivate any leaves with world positions greater than this in Y.

parameters.label: Clip Max Z
parameters.description: Deactivate any leaves with world positions greater than this in Z.

entries.label: VDB from Layer
entries.summary: Sets VDB values from the closest values in a layer.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

entries.label: VDB Leaf Points
entries.summary: Creates a point for each active leaf in a VDB.

parameters.label: Set Positions
parameters.description: Sets the P attribute of the point to the center voxel of the leaf.

parameters.label: Name
parameters.description: Name of an extra attribute to create.
parameters.heading: Point Attributes

parameters.label: Class
parameters.description: The classification of the point attribute. Since only points are created, only the Detail and Point choices are directly applicable, but the others are provided for completeness.
parameters.heading: Point Attributes

parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: The type of attribute to create, either integer or float.
parameters.heading: Point Attributes

parameters.label: Tuple Size
parameters.description: The tuplesize of the attribute.
parameters.heading: Point Attributes

entries.label: VDB Position Map
entries.summary: Stores in each voxel that voxel's position.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The VDB type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Space
parameters.description: A voxel has multiple positions depending on which space it is measured in. World: The world location of the voxel. This is where it appears in the viewport. Image: The unrotated and untranslated location of the voxel. This is the voxel index scaled by the voxel size. Texture: The relative location inside the current bounding box of the VDB. Since VDBs often change size, this is not a very stable number. Voxel: The voxel index of the voxel.

entries.label: VDB Visualize
entries.summary: Creates multi-volume visualization.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The VDB type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Density Scale
parameters.description: Fixed multiplier on the density field to control how opaque the volume is. If you are using a larger scene scale, you may need a smaller density scale.
parameters.heading: Density

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: How to apply the ramp to the emission amount. To have unbounded emission values, no ramp should be used.
parameters.heading: Density

parameters.label: Density Ramp
parameters.description: A ramp mapping the density color into a final density color.
parameters.heading: Density

parameters.label: Input Range
parameters.description: The input diffuse color will be remapped from this range to 0 to 1.
parameters.heading: Diffuse Color

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: How to apply the ramp to the diffuse color. To have unbounded diffuse colors, such as from light fields, no ramp should be used.
parameters.heading: Diffuse Color

parameters.label: Diffuse Ramp
parameters.description: A ramp mapping the remapped diffuse color into a final diffuse color.
parameters.heading: Diffuse Color

parameters.label: Emission Scale
parameters.description: Intensity of the emissive component for smoke visualization. Higher values increase brightness of the internal glow. For example, of the flames in a fire simulation.
parameters.heading: Emission

parameters.label: Input Range
parameters.description: The input emission amount will be remapped from this range to 0 to 1.
parameters.heading: Emission

parameters.label: Mode
