parameters.description: How to apply the ramp to the emission amount. To have unbounded emission values, no ramp should be used.
parameters.heading: Emission

parameters.label: Emission Ramp
parameters.description: A ramp mapping the remapped emission amount into a final emission amount.
parameters.heading: Emission

parameters.label: Input Range
parameters.description: The input emission color will be remapped from this range to 0 to 1.
parameters.heading: Emission Color

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: How to apply the ramp to the emission color. To have unbounded emission colors, such as from light fields, no ramp should be used.
parameters.heading: Emission Color

parameters.label: Emission Color Ramp
parameters.description: A ramp mapping the remapped emission color into a final emission color.
parameters.heading: Emission Color

parameters.label: Shadow Scale
parameters.description: An additional multiplier on the density field, applied after the Density Scale, when the volume is used for lighting. Increase this parameter to get darker self-shadows on low-density volumes.
parameters.heading: Shadows

parameters.label: Set Ambient Colors
parameters.description: Enable this toggle to control the appearance of smoke volumes lit with ambient light sources (by specifying Exposed Color and Occluded Color).
parameters.heading: Shadows

parameters.label: Exposed Color
parameters.description: Color of smoke that's receiving direct light from an ambient light source. The default white setting indicates that areas exposed to external lights are bright. You can set this darker than Occluded Color to achieve a more cloud-like look, where areas deeper within the cloud experience more light scattering and thus appear brighter. Set Ambient Colors must be enabled to control this parameter.
parameters.heading: Shadows

parameters.label: Occluded Color
parameters.description: Color of smoke that's not receiving any light from an ambient light source. The default black setting indicates that areas occluded from light are dark. You can set this brighter than Exposed Color to achieve a more cloud-like appearance, where areas deeper within the cloud (that is, those occluded from outside light) are more luminous due to a greater degree of internal scattering. Set Ambient Colors must be enabled to control this parameter.
parameters.heading: Shadows

parameters.label: Ambient Shadow Scale
parameters.description: Determines the intensity of self shadows from ambient light sources. The final amount of self-shadowing from these lights is controlled by the product of Density Scale, Shadow Scale, and Ambient Shadow Scale. The video demonstrates the value increasing from 0 to 1. NOTE: Turning off this checkbox does not disable ambient shadowing. Instead, it keeps this property of the geometry unchanged. If no Ambient Shadow Scale is set, Ambient Occlusion on the Geometry tab of the Display Options controls the default amount of self-shadowing from ambient lights. NOTE: The default headlight is treated as an ambient source by fog volumes.
parameters.heading: Shadows

parameters.label: Shadow Color
parameters.description: Controls the color of shadows cast by the smoke. The complements of these values act like additional density multipliers for light of each color (red, green, or blue).
parameters.heading: Shadows

entries.label: VDB Visualize Slice
entries.summary: Extracts a slice from a VDB as Geometry for visualization.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The VDB type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Plane
parameters.description: What axis to extract from the volume. This is local to the volume's space. Rotated or transformed volumes will have a corresponding rotated or transformed plane.

parameters.label: Relative Location
parameters.description: Controls if the slicing plane will be relative to the volume or in world coordinates. Relative ensures that volumes will always generate a slice through their data. Absolute ensures that animated volumes don't have their slices jump around.

parameters.label: Position
parameters.description: The center of the point to start slicing from when in world coordinate mode.

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.description: Where the plane should be positioned inside the volume. In Relative Location mode, this is a relative coordinate, with -1..1 being the total range, so 0 means the center of the volume. In world coordinate mode, this is added to the world-axis perpendicular to the selected plane. Note that if the volume is rotated this will not align with the volume's axes.

parameters.label: Snap to Voxel
parameters.description: The points of the slice match the actual voxel coordinates along the slice plane direction, but if the slice offset itself doesn't go through a voxel, they will be a blend of two voxels. Snapping ensures that values in the resulting slice are values in the original voxels and not blended.

parameters.label: Visualization Min
parameters.description: The VDB values that correspond to the beginning of the visualization ramp.

parameters.label: Visualization Max
parameters.description: The VDB values that correspond to the end of the visualization ramp.

parameters.label: Visualization Ramp
parameters.description: The color scheme for visualizing the attribute values. This is used if there is only one volume present, otherwise the first three volumes are mapped to red green and blue.

entries.label: VDB Visualize Tree
entries.summary: Builds a geometry visualizing the topology of a VDB.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The VDB type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Leaf Nodes
parameters.description: When turned on, it will draw leaf nodes with the specified method. They are drawn in blue. Wireframe Boxes: Draw as wireframe boxes. Solid Boxes: Draw as solid boxes.

parameters.label: Internal Nodes
parameters.description: When enabled, it will draw non-leaf nodes with the specified method. The first internal node level is shown in green, the others in orange. Wireframe Boxes Solid Boxes: Draw as solid boxes.

parameters.label: Active Tiles
parameters.description: When turned on, draw nodes that are active but hold the default (empty) value in the specified method. Positive values are red, negative values are white. Points: Draw a single point in the middle of each node. Wireframe Boxes: Draw as wireframe boxes. Solid Boxes: Draw as solid boxes.

entries.label: VDB Visualize Velocity
entries.summary: Traces streamers through a velocity VDB.

parameters.label: Trail per Voxel
parameters.description: Instead of scattering a fixed number of streamers, every voxel in the plane is used as a streamer source. This can get heavy with high resolutions.

parameters.label: Number Trails
parameters.description: Scatter a fixed number of streamer sources in the source plane. This ensures the density is the same regardless of resolution, so the visualization does not become too slow or crowded.

parameters.label: Plane
parameters.description: What axis to extract from the volume. This is local to the volume's space. Rotated or transformed volumes will have a corresponding rotated or transformed plane.

parameters.label: Relative Location
parameters.description: Controls if the slicing plane will be relative to the volume or in world coordinates. Relative ensures that volumes will always generate a slice through their data; but absolute ensures that animated volumes don't have their slices jump around.

parameters.label: Position
parameters.description: The center of the point to start slicing from when in world coordinate mode.

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.description: Where the plane should be positioned inside the volume. In Relative Location mode, this is a relative coordinate, with -1..1 being the total range, so 0 means the center of the volume. In world coordinate mode, this is added to the world-axis perpendicular to the selected plane. Note that if the volume is rotated this will not align with the volume's axes.

parameters.label: Trail Length
parameters.description: How long the trail should be in seconds.

parameters.label: Maximum Velocity
parameters.description: The speed of each point on the trail is visualized after dividing by the maximum velocity.

entries.label: Vector Transform
entries.summary: Transforms values of an RGB layer, attribute, or Vector VDB in 3D space.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. You can also set the RGBA channels to which you apply the effects of this node. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information.

parameters.label: Transform Order
parameters.description: Order in which transformations occur.

parameters.label: Rotate Order
parameters.description: Order in which rotations occur.

parameters.label: Translate
parameters.description: Amount of translation along xyz axes.

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.description: Amount of rotation, in degrees, about xyz axes.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: Non-uniform scaling along xyz axes.

parameters.label: Shear
parameters.description: Amount of shearing. The three values represent shearing in the X direction on the XY plane, in the X direction on the XZ plane, and in the Y direction on the YZ plane, respectively.

parameters.label: Uniform Scale
parameters.description: Uniform scaling.

parameters.label: Pivot Translate
parameters.description: The local pivot space's translation value for transformations.
parameters.heading: Pivot Transform

parameters.label: Pivot Rotate
parameters.description: The local pivot space's rotation value for transformations.
parameters.heading: Pivot Transform

parameters.label: Invert Transformation
parameters.description: Use the inverse of the transformation. This is the transformation which undoes the specified transformation. Two transform SOPs with all parameters but this equal will cancel out each other's transformation.
parameters.heading: Pivot Transform

entries.label: Vector Transform 2D
entries.summary: Transforms the values of a UV layer or attribute in 2D space.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information.

parameters.label: Order
parameters.description: The order in which to apply the translate, rotate, and scale transforms.

parameters.label: Translate
parameters.description: The amount to translate the values in their coordinates.

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.description: The amount in degrees to rotate the values about the pivot.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: The non-uniform scale of the values about the pivot.

parameters.label: Shear
parameters.description: The XY shear of the values.

parameters.label: Uniform Scale
parameters.description: The uniform scale of the values.

parameters.label: Pivot
parameters.description: The pivot used for rotations and scales, defined in their coordinates.

parameters.label: Invert Transformation
parameters.description: Inverts the computed transform before applying.

entries.label: Vignette
entries.summary: Darkens the corners of an input layer.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information.

parameters.label: Brightness
parameters.description: The scale factor to control how bright or dim the vignette is. Higher values increase the brightness. Lower values decrease the brightness.

parameters.label: Shape
parameters.description: The shape of the vignette. Round: The darkened corners create a circular shape around the center. Rectangle: The darkened corners create a rectangular shape around the center. Blend: Blend between the Round and Rectangle outputs.

parameters.label: Circle Radius
parameters.description: When Shape is Round or Blend, this is the radius of the vignette. Higher values shrink the vignette outwards towards the corners, while lower values expand the vignette inwards towards the center.

parameters.label: Circle Scale
parameters.description: When Shape is Round or Blend, this is the non-uniform scale of the vignette. This value is useful when your layer's aspect ratio isn't 1:1.

parameters.label: Rectangle Size
parameters.description: When Shape is Rectangle or Blend, this is the size of the vignette.

parameters.label: Round Corners
parameters.description: When Shape is Rectangle or Blend, this is the amount to round the corners of the rectangle. A value of 0 results in a sharp-angled rectangle.

parameters.label: Blend
parameters.description: When Shape is Blend, this is the amount to blend between the Round and Rectangle shapes. A value of 0 outputs only the Round values, while a value of 1 outputs only the Rectangle values.

parameters.label: Center
parameters.description: The center of the vignette in image space. TIP: Click Icon:BUTTONS/layer_position_sample and then click a location in the image to set the Center.

parameters.label: Blur
parameters.description: The amount to blur the vignette. Higher values expand the blur radius outwards to smooth the vignette. Lower values contract the blur radius to sharpen the vignette.

parameters.label: Shape Ramp
parameters.description: The shape of the vignette, where a Value of 1 represents the black areas. This parameter's output is noticeable only if your vignette is somewhat smooth (blurry). See Ramp parameters for more information.

entries.label: Z Composite
entries.summary: Composites two layers by depth.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Convert Depth
parameters.description: How to interpret the input layers. Depth and Distance layers have zero to mean infinity and increase as they go away from the camera. Height layers have no special values and increase as they go towards the camera. This is an internal conversion, the resulting combined depth is in the same type as the input.

parameters.label: FG Offset
parameters.description: Bias the foreground depth towards the camera this amount. This can be used to ensure that when the foreground and background are at the same depth, the foreground will win and avoid z-fighting. The output depth is unaffected by this bias.

entries.label: Add Variant
entries.summary: Adds one or more variants to a variant set on a primitive. This node creates the primitive if it doesn't exist.

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.description: The path to the primitive to which the new variant information will be added. Optionally, you can specify a space separated list of explicit primpaths or a prim pattern to add the variant to.

parameters.label: Source Primitive
parameters.description: The path to the primitive that is the base definition on which the variants will be authored. This primitive will be referenced into the new primitive(s) at the primitive path(s) where the variant will be defined. This indirection ensures that opinions in the variant will be stronger than opinions that already exist on the source primitive.

parameters.label: Warn of Weak Variant Opinions
parameters.description: Adds a warning if any variant opinions are weaker than existing opinions. As each variant is added, this option examines the composed stage with that variant selected. If any opinions added by the variant are not the strongest opinion on the composed stage, add a warning. Turn off this option to avoid the performance penalty of checking for this condition.

parameters.label: Primitive Kind
parameters.description: If no primitive exists at the specified Primitive Path, and this node must create a new Xform primitive at the specified location, this parameter controls the kind that will be authored on this new primitive.

parameters.label: Parent Primitive Type
parameters.description: If no primitive exists at the specified Primitive Path, and this node creates a new primitive at that location, this parameter controls the primitive type of any ancestor primitives that may have to be created prior to creating the final primitive.

parameters.label: Create Options Block
parameters.description: You usually don't need to set or change this parameter yourself. This parameter is set to on when this node is part of a "variant block" (when created by the Add Variants to Existing Primitive tool), or off when this node is stand-alone (created by the Add Variants to New Primitive tool). (As this node cooks each node connected to its multi-input, it sets a context option containing the name of the current variant being created. When this is _off_, the context option is available to all nodes in the input chain. When this is _on_, the context option is pushed on the stack, and the Begin Context Options Block LOP at the start of the block will pop it off the stack, hiding it from nodes further up the chain.)

parameters.label: Variant Set
parameters.description: The name of the variant set to which this node should add its variants.

parameters.label: Variant Set Strength
parameters.description: If the Variant Set is new, indicates the strength of this variant set relative to other variant sets on this primitive. Like references, variant sets are applied in a well defined order so that overlapping opinions in a stronger variant set will always take precedence over opinions in weaker variant sets.

parameters.label: Variant Source Primitive
parameters.description: The path to the root of the primitives that should be copied from each variant input's scene graph into the variant.

parameters.label: Variant Name Default
parameters.description: Each variant input allows you to control the name of the variant that it will create within the variant set. This variant name is set in the second column of the interface displaying the list of connected inputs. The Variant Name Default parameter controls the variant name that is used if no name is explicitly set in that second column of the connected inputs interface. In the expression you can use the @input local variable ($IIDX is deprecated) as the index of the current input (numbered from left to right starting at 1 for the multi-inputs).

parameters.label: Set Variant Selection
parameters.description: When this is on, this node also _selects_ (switches the primitive to) the last variant added. When this is off, this node does not affect the currently selected variant. (You can also use the Set Variant LOP to select a variant.)

entries.label: APEX Animate (Beta)
entries.summary: Edits the animation on an APEX scene.

parameters.label: APEX Scene Primitive
parameters.description: The path to the HoudiniApexScene primitive on the stage that is edited.

parameters.label: Character Primitives
parameters.description: The primitives that are bound to the APEX Scene Primitive and included in the animation scene. The default pattern includes all the characters on the stage - prims with the HoudiniApexCharacterAPI schema.

parameters.label: Animation Save Path
parameters.description: When turned on, configures the save path for the animation data and any other changes made in the animate state. When you write out USD using a USD Render ROP, the geometry is saved to a .bgeo.sc file using this file path (after output processing).

entries.label: APEX SOP Rig Builder (Beta)
entries.summary: Authors APEX rigs and binds them to USD primitives.

parameters.label: Character Primitive
parameters.description: The primitive path that represents the character (typically this is the asset's root primitive). The HoudiniApexCharacterAPI schema is applied to this primitive, which references the rig and binds the Shape Primitives to the rig's inputs and outputs.

parameters.label: Shape Primitives
parameters.description: The pattern specifying the primitives under the Character Primitive to convert to geometry and add to the packed folder structure for the SOP dive target's input geometry. The packed folder paths are named based on the relative path to the Character Primitive. The Character Primitive configures bindings for these primitives to the character's rig inputs and outputs. The default pattern includes all the geometry primitives.

parameters.label: Rig Save Path
parameters.description: When turned on, configures the save path for the rig data. When you write out USD using a USD Render ROP, the geometry is saved to a .bgeo.sc file using this file path (after output processing). When turned off, the save path is automatically determined based on the node name.
parameters.heading: Edit Folder Paths

parameters.label: Enable Attributes
parameters.description: When turned on, the Attributes setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a usdconfigattribs detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the USD Configure SOP).
parameters.heading: Import Geometry Data

parameters.label: Attributes
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to import into USD as primvars. In addition to matching attribute names directly, there are some values with special meanings bounds: Authors the USD extent attribute using the calculated bounding box of the associated SOP geometry. visibility: Authors the USD visibility attribute based on the value of the usdvisibility geometry attribute.
parameters.heading: Import Geometry Data

parameters.label: Enable Indexed Attributes
parameters.description: When turned on, the Indexed Attributes setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a usdconfigindexattribs detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the USD Configure SOP).
parameters.heading: Import Geometry Data

parameters.label: Indexed Attributes
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to import into USD as indexed primvars. If a SOP attribute matches this pattern, the importer authors the primvar as an indexed array of values (that is, an array of values called primvars:<<name>>, and an array of indices into those values called primvars:<<name>>:indices). Preparing an indexed primvar can be expensive for attributes that are not integers or strings. You should only use indexed primvars where it is likely to result in significant savings in storage size due to a small number of unique values being used across a large number of components.
parameters.heading: Import Geometry Data

parameters.label: Enable Import as Single Element Array
parameters.label_norm: enable import as single element array
parameters.description: When turned on, the Import as Single Element Array setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a usdconfigconstantattribs detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the USD Configure SOP).
parameters.heading: Import Geometry Data

parameters.label: Import as Single Element Array
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to import into USD as primvars with Constant interpolation (an array with a single value for the whole primitive), regardless of whether the SOP geometry attribute is a point, primitive, or vertex attribute. If multiple values could be chosen for a particular USD primitive, the importer chooses the first value it encounters. Importing as a single element array (versus Import as Single Value) can be useful since it allows the primvar's interpolation to be overridden without changing the primvar's type.
parameters.heading: Import Geometry Data

parameters.label: Enable Import as Single Value
parameters.description: When turned on, the Import as Single Value setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a usdconfigscalarconstantattribs detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the USD Configure SOP).
parameters.heading: Import Geometry Data

parameters.label: Import as Single Value
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to import into USD as primvars with Constant interpolation and a single value for the whole primitive, regardless of whether the SOP geometry attribute is a point, primitive, or vertex attribute. If multiple values could be chosen for a particular USD primitive, the importer chooses the first value it encounters. This is the default behavior for how detail attributes are imported. This is similar to Import as Single Element Array, but the primvar's type is a scalar value instead of an array with a single element (for example, vector3f instead of vector3f[]).
parameters.heading: Import Geometry Data

parameters.label: Enable Boolean Attributes
parameters.description: When turned on, the Boolean Attributes setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a usdconfigboolattribs detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the USD Configure SOP).
parameters.heading: Import Geometry Data

parameters.label: Boolean Attributes
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying which integer SOP attributes should be converted to primvars of type bool.
parameters.heading: Import Geometry Data

parameters.label: Enable Unsigned 32-bit Attributes
parameters.description: When turned on, the Unsigned 32-bit Attributes setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a usdconfiguintattribs detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the USD Configure SOP).
parameters.heading: Import Geometry Data

parameters.label: Unsigned 32-bit Attributes
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying which integer SOP attributes should be converted to primvars of type uint.
parameters.heading: Import Geometry Data

parameters.label: Enable Unsigned 64-bit Attributes
parameters.description: When turned on, the Unsigned 64-bit Attributes setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a usdconfiguint64attribs detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the USD Configure SOP).
parameters.heading: Import Geometry Data

parameters.label: Unsigned 64-bit Attributes
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying which integer SOP attributes should be converted to primvars of type uint64.
parameters.heading: Import Geometry Data

parameters.label: Enable Asset Path Attributes
parameters.description: When enabled, the Asset Path Attributes setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a usdconfigassetpathattribs detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the USD Configure SOP)
parameters.heading: Import Geometry Data

parameters.label: Asset Path Attributes
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying which string SOP attributes should be converted to primvars of type asset.
parameters.heading: Import Geometry Data

parameters.label: Enable USD Custom Attributes
parameters.description: When turned on, the USD Custom Attributes setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a usdconfigcustomattribs detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the USD Configure SOP).
parameters.heading: Import Geometry Data

parameters.label: USD Custom Attributes
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to import into USD as attributes (rather than primvars).
parameters.heading: Import Geometry Data

parameters.label: Enable Translate UV Attribute to ST
parameters.label_norm: enable translate uv attribute to st
parameters.description: When turned on, the Translate UV Attribute to ST setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a usdconfigtranslateuvtost detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the USD Configure SOP).
parameters.heading: Import Geometry Data

parameters.label: Translate UV Attribute to ST
parameters.description: When turned on, converts the SOP vertex attribute uv into a USD primvar called primvars:st. Whether you need to turn this on depends on the renderer you are using and how your shaders are authored. If you are rendering with Karma, leave this off. (As of this writing there is no strict standard for texture coordinate naming in USD, but the use of st is a common convention, whereas in SOP geometry, using uv is the common convention.)
parameters.heading: Import Geometry Data

entries.label: Asset Reference
entries.summary: Reference, Transform, and select variants of a USD Asset.

parameters.label: Destination Primitive
parameters.description: Scene graph path where the referenced asset will be attached.

parameters.label: Primitive Kind
parameters.description: If the prim at Primitive Path doesn't exist, this node will create it. If it has to create the prim, it will set it to have this kind. Setting this parameter to Auto will not author a Kind on the leaf primitive where the reference is added. Instead, it will examine the Kind of the prim after setting the reference, and automatically set the Kind of ancestor prims to ensure the leaf primitive is part of a valid model hierarchy. Note that this may result in adding a Kind to ancestor prims that were not created by this node. If the referenced prim has no kind, or is not a model kind, Auto mode will not author Kind on any prim.

parameters.label: Parent Primitive Type
parameters.description: If the prim at Primitive Path doesn't exist, this node will create it. If it has to create the prim, it will give any intermediate prims it has to create this type.

parameters.label: Make Instanceable
parameters.description: Mark the new or modified prims as instanceable (as in "native instancing"). This saves memory if you reference the same branch into multiple places, but makes the descendants of the referenced prim not editable. If this option is off, the prims are not explicitly marked as not instanceable. Instead, the current instanceable value on each prim is left unchanged.

parameters.label: Source
parameters.description: The source of the asset being referenced. By default, this node will switch to the second input, when connected, and use File otherwise. Users can also specify which source if they wish. File: Reference in a prim from an external USD file. Second Input: Reference in a prim from a this node's second input. Second Input if Connected: Reference from the Second Input if connected, otherwise from a file.
parameters.heading: Reference

parameters.label: Reference File
parameters.description: Click the Smallicon:BUTTONS/chooser_file Open floating file chooser button to load the USD file from disk you want to add as a reference.
parameters.heading: File Reference

parameters.label: Reference Primitive
parameters.description: Reference Automatically Chosen Primitive: If the referenced file has a default primitive set, use that. If there is no default prim, use the first Xform prim at the root. If there is no Xform prim at the root, use the first root prim of any type. Reference Default Primitive: If the referenced file has a default primitive set, use that. If not, display a warning on this node. Reference Specific Primitive: Reference in the scene graph path in the Reference Primitive Path parameter.
parameters.heading: File Reference

parameters.label: Reference Primitive Path
parameters.description: Drag a primitive from the Scene Graph Tree to this field or enter a path to the primitive you want to use as a reference.
parameters.heading: File Reference

parameters.label: Time Offset (in Frames)
parameters.description: Offsets all time samples from the file or target primitive on the first input. You can use this to re-time animations in the references file.
parameters.heading: Options

parameters.label: Time Scale
parameters.description: Scales all time samples from the file or target primitive on the first input. You can use this to re-time animations in the references file. A value of 1 means normal speed. Values smaller than 1 make animations slower, values greater than 1 make the animation appear in slow motion.
parameters.heading: Options

parameters.label: Handle Missing Files
parameters.description: If the reference is to an external file, this controls what the node does if the referenced file does not exist. Error for Missing Files: The node errors, preventing cooking the rest of the network. Warn for Missing Files: The node shows a warning, then passes through the first input unchanged. Ignore Missing Files: The node silently ignores the missing file, and passes through the first input unchanged. Allow Missing Files on the Stage: Author the reference to the sublayer even if it currently doesn't exist. This node and the following nodes will probably print warnings from the USD libraries about missing files.
parameters.heading: Options

parameters.label: Transform
parameters.description: How the transform parameters below apply to the primitive. (Because each USD prim can contain multiple transforms, _and_ be affected by parent transforms, there are many different ways to apply new transforms.) Append: Apply the parameters as a new, most local transform. Prepend: Apply the parameters as a new, _least_ local transform. Overwrite or Append: If a local transform exists with the name xformOp:transform, _overwrite_ it with the parameters. Otherwise, apply it as a new, most local transform. If this replaces an existing transform, that transform's order in the local transform stack is not affected. Overwrite or Prepend: Like Overwrite or Append, but _least_ local. Apply Transform in World Space: Apply the parameters as a new, most local transform. However, prior to applying the transform, it is updated so that the result of the transform appears as if the transform was being applied in world space, before any local or ancestor transformations were applied to the primitive. Replace All Local Transforms: The transform specified in the remaining transform parameters is always applied as a new transform. Prior to applying this transform, all existing transform operations on the local transform stack are cleared so that only the supplied transform remains on the local transform stack (though ancestor transforms still have an effect). Apply XformCommonAPI: The transform specified in the remaining transform parameters will be applied as if it were appended to whatever the current transform on the prim is. But the resulting final transform will be expressed using the USD XformCommonAPI specification. Note that this specification cannot express shears, and so cannot express some transforms which may result in unexpected changes to transforms that already have shears. Apply Extended XformCommonAPI (with Shear + Pivot Rotate): The transform specified in the remaining transform parameters will be applied as if it were appended to whatever the current transform on the prim is. But the resulting final transform will be expressed using a Houdini-defined extension of the USD XformCommonAPI specification. This extension is accessible through the husd.UsdHoudini.HoudiniXformCommonAPI python class. This class provides a very similar interface to pxr.UsdGeom.XformCommonAPI but allows for shears in the transform, is able to store a pivot rotation value, and can express rotations as a quaternion if the rotations are animated. Using quaternions to express rotations avoids motion blur artifacts that can occur when using Euler angles to express the rotation.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Transform Order
parameters.description: The order in which Houdini applies translates, rotates, and scales, and the order in which it applies rotation.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Translate
parameters.description: Movement amount along XYZ axes.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.description: Degrees rotation around XYZ axes.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: Non-uniform scaling along XYZ axes.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Shear
parameters.description: Amount of shearing. The three values represent shearing in the X direction on the XY plane, in the X direction on the XZ plane, and in the Y direction on the YZ plane, respectively.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Uniform Scale
parameters.description: Scales the object uniformly along all three axes.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Align To Up Axis
parameters.description: When enabled, the reference will be transformed so its up axis matches the current stage.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Pivot Translate
parameters.description: Moves the local origin of the object.
parameters.heading: Pivot Primitives

parameters.label: Pivot Rotate
parameters.description: Rotates the local origin of the object after translation.
parameters.heading: Pivot Primitives

parameters.label: Number of Variants
parameters.description: You can perform multiple variant selections in a single Set Variant node. Set this to the number of selections you want to make, or use the plus and minus buttons to add or remove selections.
parameters.heading: Variants

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.description: The primitive(s) you want to define as variants of a Variant Set. You can click the Smallicon:BUTTONS/reselect Select button beside the text box to select the primitives from the scene graph tree. You can also use primitive patterns for advanced matching.
parameters.heading: Variants

parameters.label: Variant Set
parameters.description: The name of the variant set to select a variant from.
parameters.heading: Variants

parameters.label: Variant Name
parameters.description: If not choosing the variant by index, this parameter is the name of the variant that should be selected within the specified variant set. If this value is an empty string, any existing variant selection specified in the active layer will be cleared. This will "reveal" any variant selection opinions authored in weaker layers. If this value is set to the special string <block>, an explicit empty variant selection will be made, blocking any variant selection opinions from weaker layers, leaving the chosen set without any variant selected. If this is set to a list of variant names (space or comma- separated), then this will use the first one that matches a valid variant name in each prim's variant set.
parameters.heading: Variants

entries.label: Assign Material
entries.summary: Assigns a material to one or more USD primitives. You can use also programmatically assign materials using VEX, programmatically override material settings for each assignment, and programmatically assign materials to geometry subsets.

parameters.label: Number of Materials
parameters.description: You can perform multiple assignments within one node. Set this to the number of assignments you want to perform, or use the plus and minus button to add or remove assignments.

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.description: The primitive(s) you want to assign the material to. You can click the Smallicon:BUTTONS/reselect Select button beside the text box to select the primitives from the scene graph tree. You can also use primitive patterns for advanced matching.

parameters.label: Pattern Is USD Path Expression
parameters.description: Authors the collection as a USD path expression instead of a hard coded list of includes and excludes. USD path expressions are evaluated as needed by comparing the expression to the prims on the composed stage. This approach is slower than an explicit list of includes and excludes, but allows for more dynamic collection contents. For example, the path expression //chair will find all prims named chair in the composed stage, even if the prims didn't exist when the collection was authored. There are several modes of this LOP that do not support USD path expressions. If you are doing direct bindings, or using VEXpressions or CVEX to calculate material assignments or material property overrides per-primitive, path expressions are not supported. In these cases, the path expression will be evaluated for the current stage, and replaced with a hard coded list. If this occurs, a warning will appear on this node to indicate that the path expression will not be saved to the USD stage.

parameters.label: Specify Material Using
parameters.description: How to specify the material to assign. Explicit path: Assign a material at a certain path in the scene graph tree. VEXpression: Assign a material to each selected primitive based on the results of computing a VEX snippet. CVEX Script: Run a VEX program, provided by a CVEX node, to compute override values for materials.

parameters.label: Material Path
parameters.description: When Specify Material Using is Explicit path, the USD path to the material primitive to use for binding.

parameters.label: VEXpression
parameters.description: When Specify Material Using is VEXpression, this VEX snippet is computed for each selected primitive. You can use @primpath (the path of the current primitive), @elemnum (the index of the current prim in the list of selected prims), and @numelem (the total number of selected prims). Must return a string containing a path to the material to assign to the current prim. For example, this snippet alternates between assigning rough_red and rough_blue based on whether a primitive is at an odd or even position in the list of selected primitives

parameters.label: CVEX Node
parameters.description: When Specify Material Using is CVEX, the path to a CVEX VOP network. See CVEX VOP networks above.

parameters.label: Parameters Override
parameters.description: Whether and how to override individual material parameters for each assignment. None: Do not override material parameters. VEXpression: Run a VEX snippet for each assignment that can compute new parameter values. CVEX Script: Run a VEX program, provided by a CVEX node, to compute override values for material parameters.

parameters.label: Override VEXpression
parameters.description: When Parameter Override is VEXpression, this VEX snippet is run for each selected primitive. The settings under CVEX Bindings control how material parameters are mapped to VEX variables. You override a material parameter by assigning to the corresponding variable. You can also use @primpath (the path of the current primitive), @elemnum (the index of the current prim in the list of selected prims), and @numelem (the total number of selected prims). For example, if the material has a parameter named roughness (and Autobind by Name is on, the default), you can override it by setting the corresponding variable in the VEX snippet

parameters.label: Override CVEX Node
parameters.description: When Parameters override is CVEX, the path to a CVEX VOP network. See CVEX VOP networks above.

parameters.label: VEX Bindings to Export
parameters.description: A pattern that selects VEXpression parameters that should be exported from the final VEX program. I.e., these are the output parameters that will be used for material parameter override.

parameters.label: Materials Parent Path
parameters.description: Specifies the USD path to the parent primitive inside which the LOP should author any automatically created materials with overrides.

parameters.label: Materials Parent Type
parameters.description: Specifies the primitive type of any ancestors that needs to be authored in order to automatically create materials with overrides. Autobind by Name: When this is on, attributes on the current primitive (when computing assignment) or on the material (when computing overrides) are automatically made available as VEX variables with the same name in the relevant VEXpression (or CVEX network). You can turn this off and map attribute names to VEX variable names manually using the multiparm below. Number of Bindings: The number of manual attributes to VEX variable bindings to create. Attribute Name: In a binding pair, the name of the USD attribute to convert to a VEX variable. VEX Parameter: In a binding pair, the name of the VEX variable to create to mirror the USD attribute.

parameters.label: Create and Bind Geometry Subsets
parameters.description: When this is on, the Primitives parameter should point to a geometry or geometry subset primitive, and the node runs the VEX snippet for each _geometry element_ (for example, polygon face) in the geometry, instead of for each selected primitive. In the snippet, @elemnum is the index of the current element, and @numelem is the total number of elements in the geometry. The node will automatically create geometry subsets for each set of elements with the same material path.
parameters.heading: Material Binding

parameters.label: Purpose
parameters.description: Sets the Purpose method for the assignments. This controls what types of renders the assignment applies to. All: The assignments apply to all rendering. Full Render: The assignments only apply in full/final renders. Preview Render: The assignments only apply in preview renders.
parameters.heading: Material Binding

parameters.label: Strength
parameters.description: Controls the strength of the assignment "opinion" relative to any conflicting assignments on descendant prims under the assigned primitives in the tree. For example, if this node assigns /materials/zerbra to /a, but /a/b/c already is assigned /materials/tiger. Default: Use normal rules for opinion strengths (assignments on descendants override assignments on ancestors). Stronger than Descendants: This assignment always overrides assignments on primitives lower in the tree. This is useful if you want collection-based binding to override child primitives that already have a material binding. This option ensures the collection-based binding on the ancestor takes effect despite the general rule that descendant opinions are stronger than ancestors. Weaker than Descendants: This assignment is always overridden by assignments on primitives lower in the tree. This is the same as Default.
parameters.heading: Material Binding

parameters.label: Method
parameters.description: How to express the material assignment in USD. Direct: Assign the material by authoring a material:binding relationship on each individual primitive. Collection based: Assign each material to a collection of primitives on a common ancestor using the material:binding:collection relationship. If you specified the primitives using a collection in the Primitives parameter, this will re-use that collection. Otherwise, you can specify the path to the a prim using the Path parameter below and the node will create a new collection on that prim. NOTE: The USD specification for the collection-based material binding says that the material is assigned only to primitives that are descendants of the primitive on which the binding relationship is defined (see Path parameter). That is, the binding does not affect any primitives in the collection that are not descendants of that primitive.
parameters.heading: Material Binding

parameters.label: Include Descendant Primitives in Collection
parameters.description: When Method is Collection Based, turn on this option to have the collection authored for the collection-based binding be marked to expand all descendants of the target primitives. This will cause the material assignment to be applied to the entire scene graph tree branch. The equivalent of this behavior always occurs when using Direct binding, which always inherits down the scene graph tree.
parameters.heading: Material Binding

parameters.label: Path
parameters.description: When Method is Collection Based, the collection-based binding will be defined on a primitive at this path. Also, if this LOP node needs to create a new collection, it will create it on a this primitive as well. If the path is empty, the LOP node tries to use the deepest ancestor common to all primitives given in the Primitives parameter.
parameters.heading: Material Binding

parameters.label: Name
parameters.description: Specifies the collection-based material binding name. If empty, the name of the material will be used.
parameters.heading: Material Binding

entries.label: Assign Prototypes
entries.summary: Switch point instances or USD instanceable prims to instance a different prototype.

parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: How you specify what to replace. PointInstancer - By Prototype: Specify the path to a point instancer prim, and the index of a prototype. All instances that refer to that prototype will be switched to use the new prototype. PointInstancer - By Instance: Specify a list of individual instances using /<<path>><<instance_index>> syntax. Native Instances: Specify a list of paths to instanceable prims to replace.

parameters.label: Instancer Path
parameters.description: When Type is PointInstancer - By Prototype, the scene graph path to the instancer containing the prototype you want to replace. This can be a space-separated list of multiple instancer paths.

parameters.label: Prototype Index
parameters.description: When Type is PointInstancer - By Prototype, the index of the prototype you want to replace.

parameters.label: Instances
parameters.description: A space-separated list of instances, using /<<path>><<instance_index>> syntax (for example, /geometry/instancer0 /geometry/instancer1). To select all instances in an instancer, use /<<path>>*. To select a range, use /geometry/instancer4-7 (the range is inclusive). To select instances inside nested instancers, use multiple indexes, for example /geometry/instancer27. VEXpressions can be used to specify instances, for example, /geometry/instancer{@weights>0.5}.

parameters.label: Instances
parameters.description: When Type is Native Instances, a list of paths to instanceable prims.

parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: How to choose the replacement prim. Existing Prototype: Replace the current prototype with the prototype at a certain index. When Type is Native Instances, this is an index into the list of selected instanceable prims from the Instances parameter. This will replace the prototypes of _all_ selected prims with the prototype of _one of_ the selected prims. Primitives: Creates a new prototype based on an existing prim from somewhere else in the scene graph tree.
parameters.heading: Replace With

parameters.label: Source
parameters.description: When Replace With > Type is Primitives, where to find the replacement primitives. First Input: Select primitive from the first input's stage. Second Input: Select the entire stage from the second input. Reference File: Select a primitive from a USD file on disk.
parameters.heading: Replace With

parameters.label: Reference File
parameters.description: When Source is Reference File, the file path of the USD file to get the replacement prim from.
parameters.heading: Replace With

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.description: When Replace With > Type is Primitives, the scene graph path to the replacement prim.
parameters.heading: Replace With

parameters.label: Prototype Name
parameters.description: When Replace With > Type is Primitives, turn this on to explicitly set the name of the new prototype. If this is off, the node uses the name of the prim the prototype is based on.
parameters.heading: Replace With

parameters.label: Frame Offset
parameters.description: If the prototype is animated, use this to get the prototype as it appears at a different point in the timeline. This lets you replace instances with a re-timed prototype, without affecting the other instances.
parameters.heading: Replace With

parameters.label: Time Scale
parameters.description: If the prototype is animated, use this to scale the animation on the replacement. This lets you replace instances with a re-timed prototype, without affecting the other instances.
parameters.heading: Replace With

parameters.label: Modify Source Primitive
parameters.description: When Replace With > Type is Primitives and Source is First input, what to do with the primitive you based the new prototype on (from Primitive Path). Do Not Modify Source Primitive: Don't do anything to the original prim. Hide Source Primitive: Set the visibility of the original prim to hidden.
parameters.heading: Replace With

entries.label: Attribute VOP
entries.summary: Create/edit USD attribute values using a VOP network.

parameters.label: Sampling Behavior
parameters.description: Cooking this node can generate many USD time samples, rather than just a single time sample at the current time. This can be equivalent to having a Cache LOP following this node, but it will evaluate much faster, and does not cache data from any other nodes. This allows animated data to be authored to USD without introducing a node time dependency which would then cause all following nodes to also be time dependent. This can vastly improve playback performance of some LOP Networks. In all sampling modes, if a parameter on this node does not vary with time, and does not rely on other time sampled data from the stage, only a single default value will be generated in USD for the corresponding attribute. USD time samples are only generated for parameters that may vary over time. Sample Current Frame: A single time sample will be generated for the current time. Sample Frame Range If Input Is Not Time Dependent: If the input to this node is time dependent, this node behaves as if it is in Sample Current Frame mode. Otherwise it behaves as if it is in Sample Frame Range mode. Sample Frame Range: The Start/End/Inc parameter is used to generate multiple times at which this node's parameters are evaluated, and a USD time sample is created for each attribute at each one of these times.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Start/End/Inc
parameters.description: When the Sampling behavior is Sample Frame Range, this parameter controls the number and spacing of base time samples to be generated by this node. The default values of this parameter are @fstart, @fend, and @finc. These values correspond to the start, end, and step size of the global Houdini animation settings when interacting with Houdini. When using a ROP node to generate a range of frames, these values correspond to the start, end, and increment values specified on the ROP node being executed. This default ensures that a USD file written to disk will contain time samples for exactly the frame range requested by the ROP (regardless of the Houdini animation settings).
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Subframe Sampling
parameters.description: For each primary sample generated by this node, these parameters can cause additional samples to be generated around that primary sample time. This is most often used to ensure that accurate data exists at exactly the camera shutter open and close times, as well as at the primary sample time.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Shutter
parameters.description: Controls the method used to specify the shutter open and close times relative to the primary sample times. Specify Manually: The Shutter Open/Close parameter values provide exact offset values relative to the primary sample time. Use Camera Prim: The Camera Prim parameter provides the scene graph path of a camera primitive from which the shutter open and close times are extracted to provide the offset values relative to the primary time sample.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Shutter Open/Close
parameters.description: When Shutter is set to Specify Manually, these two offset values are added to the primary sample time to indicate the shutter open and close times. The open time should be less than or equal to zero, and the close time should be greater than or equal to zero.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Camera Prim
parameters.description: When Shutter is set to Use Camera Prim, this is the scene graph path of a camera prim on the input node's stage. The shutter open and close attribute values are read from this primitive.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Samples
parameters.description: The number of subframe samples to create for each primary sample. These samples are evenly distributed between the shutter open and close times. Note that such an even distribution may or may not create a sample at exactly the primary sample time.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Always Include Frame Sample
parameters.description: When turned on, forces a sample to be created at exactly the primary sample time. If the Samples value, together with the shutter open and close times, already place a sample at the primary sample time, turning on this option has no effect. Otherwise, this option causes an addition sample to be added. This means that the actual number of samples per primary sample may in fact be one more than the number specified in the Samples parameter.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.description: The primitive(s) the node should operate on. You can drag primitives from the scene graph tree pane into this textbox to add their paths, or click the Smallicon:BUTTONS/reselect Reselect button beside the text box to select the primitives in the viewer, or ((Ctrl))-click the Reselect button to choose prims from a pop-up tree window. You can also use primitive patterns for advanced matching, including matching all prims in a collection (using /path/to/prim.collection:<<name>>). You can drag and drop a specific (or multiple specific) USD prim(s) from the Scene Graph Tree into the window to run validation on only these USD primitives. NOTE: This parameter needs to be exposed in order for the transform handles to be context-aware. Without it, the handles may not be positioned properly.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Allow Instance Proxy Primitives
parameters.description: When this is on, the pattern in the Primitives parameter will be allowed to match instance proxy primitives (instanced ancestors of a primitive marked as instanceable). Since instance proxy primitives cannot be directly modified in USD, this mode is primarily used to allow the VEX code to pull data from the instance proxy primitives, and apply values to some non-instanced ancestor primitive.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Run on Elements of Array Attributes
parameters.label_norm: run on elements of array attributes
parameters.description: When this is on, the node evaluates the VOP network *for each array element* of array attributes, on each prim. In this mode, the built-in elemnum refers to the array index, and numelem refers to the length of the _largest_ array. (When this is off, array attributes are available in the network as array-type variables.) If some array attributes have shorter length, their elements are padded with the last element. This mode may be useful for running over geometry-related attributes such as points.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Vex Source
parameters.description: Where to get the VEX to run. You should usually leave this set to Myself and build a VOP network inside this node, unless you have a good reason to choose one of the other options. Myself: Use the CVEX VOP network inside this node. Other Node: Specify another node that generates VEX code. Script: Specify a compiled .vex file on disk.
parameters.heading: Vex Setup

parameters.label: Node Path
parameters.description: When Vex Source is Other Node, the node path of the node that generates the VEX code.
parameters.heading: Vex Setup

parameters.label: Script
parameters.description: When Vex Source is Script, the file path to the compiled .vex file.
parameters.heading: Vex Setup

parameters.label: Re-load VEX Functions
parameters.description: When Vex Source is Script, click this to force reload all .vex files on disk.
parameters.heading: Vex Setup

parameters.label: Compiler
parameters.description: The VEX compiler command to use to compile the VOP network inside this node. You should not change this unless you really have a good reason to do so.
parameters.heading: Vex Setup

parameters.label: Force Compile
parameters.description: Clear the cached VEX code generated from the children VOPs, forcing it to be generated and compiled again. Normally the node should automatically recompile whenever the network changes, but this may be useful when debugging problems.
parameters.heading: Vex Setup

parameters.label: Evaluation Node Path
parameters.description: Certain VEX functions, like ch(), evaluate parameters on this node. In some cases you want these functions to be relative to a different node (for example, with nodes inside a digital asset, you often want to evaluate functions relative to the parent asset). This is a relative node path to the node to use as "the current node" in the program.
parameters.heading: Vex Setup

parameters.label: Export Parameters
parameters.description: When a VEX parameter is exported, the bound attribute will be created if it doesn't exist. This pattern can be used to override this option to avoid writing to or creating certain attributes. The pattern matches the VEX parameter, not the bound attribute. The attribute will still be bound for reading.
parameters.heading: Vex Setup

parameters.label: Autobind by Name
parameters.description: Automatically bind Parameter or Bind nodes to attributes if they have the same name (default is on). When this is off, bindings only work if they are also listed in the multi-parm below.
parameters.heading: Attribute Bindings

parameters.label: Number of Bindings
parameters.description: The number of USD attributes to bind to VEX variables.
parameters.heading: Attribute Bindings

parameters.label: Attribute Name
parameters.description: The name of the USD attribute to bind to a VEX variable. Note that this attribute does not need to exist yet. You can bind it to a VEX variable, and if the VEX writes to the variable, the node will create the attribute.
parameters.heading: Attribute Bindings

parameters.label: Attribute Type
parameters.description: The USD datatype of the attribute. You should usually leave this set to Auto, so the node will use the known type of an existing attribute. If you are going to create the attribute, and node doesn't translate the VEX type into the correct USD type (for example, it becomes string but you want a token), you can change this to the type you want.
parameters.heading: Attribute Bindings

parameters.label: VEX Parameter
parameters.description: The name of the VEX parameter bound to the attribute.
parameters.heading: Attribute Bindings

entries.label: Auto Select LOD

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.description: The primitive(s) the node should operate on. You can drag primitives from the scene graph tree pane into this textbox to add their paths, or click the Smallicon:BUTTONS/reselect Reselect button beside the text box to select the primitives in the viewer, or ((Ctrl))-click the Reselect button to choose prims from a pop-up tree window. You can also use primitive patterns for advanced matching, including matching all prims in a collection (using /path/to/prim.collection:<<name>>). You can drag and drop a specific (or multiple specific) USD prim(s) from the Scene Graph Tree into the window to run validation on only these USD primitives. NOTE: This parameter needs to be exposed in order for the transform handles to be context-aware. Without it, the handles may not be positioned properly.

parameters.label: Camera
parameters.description: Path to the USD render camera in the scene graph tree. The node will use the distance between this camera and the selected prim to choose the level of detail.

parameters.label: Variant Set
parameters.description: The name of the variant set to select a variant from.

parameters.label: Number of LODs
parameters.description: Set this to the number of LOD variants in the specified Variant Set.

parameters.label: Threshold Distance
parameters.description: When the camera is _this distance or farther_ to the target prim, select the corresponding variant. That is, the first Threshold Distance in the multiparm sets the minimum distance for the first variant, the second Threshold Distance sets the minimum distance for the second variant, and so on.

parameters.label: Specify LOD
parameters.description: If disabled, the variant chosen for this threshold distance will be based on the multiparm instance looked up in the array of available variant choices in the requested variant set. Enable this parameter to explicitly choose which variant will be used for this threshold distance.

entries.label: Karma Background Plate
entries.summary: Sets up "hold-out" or "matte" objects that leave "holes" in the scene through which the background is visible. These prims still take shadows and contribute to reflections as if they were the background.

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.description: A space-separated list of prim paths for the objects you want to act as hold-outs.

parameters.label: Quick Setups
parameters.description: Add example COP graph to composite output AOVs.

parameters.label: Rendersettings Primitive Path
parameters.description: The prim path of a USD Render Settings prim to use to set up the background and matte settings. The default is /Render/rendersettings, which is the default for where the Karma render node looks for render settings. If this prim doesn't already exist in the incoming stage, this node will create it.
parameters.heading: Background

parameters.label: Allow Shader Parameter Animation
parameters.description: When it is turned off, all USD values are assumed non-animatable and will be authored at a default time code. And, with this option turned on, shader node parameters that are time-dependent will get translated to USD values at non-default time codes, while time-independent parameters will still author a value at a default time code. Note, checking parameter time dependency can be costly and may add up to a large portion of the shader translation time. Since the vast majority of shader nodes don't have animated parameters, this toggle is off by default to save the work involved in checking it.
parameters.heading: Background

parameters.label: Plate
parameters.description: The file path of the background image to use.
parameters.heading: Background

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: Horizontal and vertical scaling factors for the background image. These are normalized relative to the rendered image size, so for example a horizontal scale of 1 is the width of the rendered image.
parameters.heading: Background

parameters.label: Translate
parameters.description: Horizontal and vertical offsets for the background image. These are normalized relative to the rendered images size, so for example a horizontal offset of 0.25 moves the background image to the right 1/4 of the width of the rendered image.
parameters.heading: Background

parameters.label: Use Offscreen Texture
parameters.description: If the background plate does not perfectly cover the camera view, the "real" background (empty space) will show through. Use this to replace empty space with a texture. If you leave this off, the node will fill empty space with the Offscreen Color instead.
parameters.heading: Background

parameters.label: Offscreen Texture
parameters.description: When Use Offscreen Texture is on, the file path of the texture image to use to cover empty space.
parameters.heading: Background

parameters.label: Offscreen Color
parameters.description: When Use Offscreen Texture is off, the color to use for any "empty space" if the background plate does not fully cover the camera view.
parameters.heading: Background

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.description: When Use Offscreen Texture is on, this sets the rotation of the offscreen texture in 3D space.
parameters.heading: Background

parameters.label: Metallic
parameters.description: Metallic: Values closer to 1 give the shader a more metallic appearance. This is done by fading out the diffuse component and driving reflectivity by Base Color. This makes it easy to create the colored reflections typical of metallic materials. Image:/images/nodes/vop/principled_shader_metallic.png
parameters.heading: Shader Parameters

parameters.label: Reflectivity
parameters.description: Reflectivity: Controls the reflectivity of surfaces facing the viewer. This is also affected by the Index of Refraction. When a surface is rotated away from the viewer, more and more light is reflected regardless of this parameter's value. At 90 degrees away from the viewer, 100% of the light is reflected, as in the real world. TIP
parameters.heading: Shader Parameters

parameters.label: Roughness
parameters.description: Roughness: Controls how dull a surface appears. A value of 0.0 results in a smooth surface with perfectly sharp reflections. A value of 1.0 produces a completely dull surface. This simulates microscopic bumps which become more pronounced the higher the Roughness, causing reflected light to be scattered more. The effect of Roughness on a material with Metallic set to 1.0 The effect of Roughness on a material with Metallic set to 0.0
parameters.heading: Shader Parameters

parameters.label: IOR
parameters.description: IOR: Higher values reflect more light and bend refraction rays more. The impact on reflectivity is strongest on surfaces facing directly towards the viewer. Surfaces facing less directly towards the viewer generally reflect more light, regardless of this parameter's value. NOTE
parameters.heading: Shader Parameters

parameters.label: Shadows
parameters.description: Whether to record all holdout shadows in a single AOV, or generate a separate AOV for each light LPE tag.
parameters.heading: Holdout AOVs

parameters.label: Diffuse
parameters.description: Generate an AOV for diffuse bounces on holdout objects.
parameters.heading: Holdout AOVs

parameters.label: Emission
parameters.description: Generate an AOV for light emissions on holdout objects.
parameters.heading: Holdout AOVs

parameters.label: Glossy Reflection
parameters.description: Generate an AOV for glossy reflections on holdout objects. When disabled, the background shader will become diffuse only, reflectivity and metallic shader parameters will be set to 0.

parameters.label: Sampling Behavior
parameters.description: Cooking this node can generate many USD time samples, rather than just a single time sample at the current time. This can be equivalent to having a Cache LOP following this node, but it will evaluate much faster, and does not cache data from any other nodes. This allows animated data to be authored to USD without introducing a node time dependency which would then cause all following nodes to also be time dependent. This can vastly improve playback performance of some LOP Networks. In all sampling modes, if a parameter on this node does not vary with time, and does not rely on other time sampled data from the stage, only a single default value will be generated in USD for the corresponding attribute. USD time samples are only generated for parameters that may vary over time. Sample Current Frame: A single time sample will be generated for the current time. Sample Frame Range If Input Is Not Time Dependent: If the input to this node is time dependent, this node behaves as if it is in Sample Current Frame mode. Otherwise it behaves as if it is in Sample Frame Range mode. Sample Frame Range: The Start/End/Inc parameter is used to generate multiple times at which this node's parameters are evaluated, and a USD time sample is created for each attribute at each one of these times.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Start/End/Inc
parameters.description: When the Sampling behavior is Sample Frame Range, this parameter controls the number and spacing of base time samples to be generated by this node. The default values of this parameter are @fstart, @fend, and @finc. These values correspond to the start, end, and step size of the global Houdini animation settings when interacting with Houdini. When using a ROP node to generate a range of frames, these values correspond to the start, end, and increment values specified on the ROP node being executed. This default ensures that a USD file written to disk will contain time samples for exactly the frame range requested by the ROP (regardless of the Houdini animation settings).
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Subframe Sampling
parameters.description: For each primary sample generated by this node, these parameters can cause additional samples to be generated around that primary sample time. This is most often used to ensure that accurate data exists at exactly the camera shutter open and close times, as well as at the primary sample time.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Shutter
parameters.description: Controls the method used to specify the shutter open and close times relative to the primary sample times. Specify Manually: The Shutter Open/Close parameter values provide exact offset values relative to the primary sample time. Use Camera Prim: The Camera Prim parameter provides the scene graph path of a camera primitive from which the shutter open and close times are extracted to provide the offset values relative to the primary time sample.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Shutter Open/Close
parameters.description: When Shutter is set to Specify Manually, these two offset values are added to the primary sample time to indicate the shutter open and close times. The open time should be less than or equal to zero, and the close time should be greater than or equal to zero.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Camera Prim
parameters.description: When Shutter is set to Use Camera Prim, this is the scene graph path of a camera prim on the input node's stage. The shutter open and close attribute values are read from this primitive.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Samples
parameters.description: The number of subframe samples to create for each primary sample. These samples are evenly distributed between the shutter open and close times. Note that such an even distribution may or may not create a sample at exactly the primary sample time.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Always Include Frame Sample
parameters.description: When turned on, forces a sample to be created at exactly the primary sample time. If the Samples value, together with the shutter open and close times, already place a sample at the primary sample time, turning on this option has no effect. Otherwise, this option causes an addition sample to be added. This means that the actual number of samples per primary sample may in fact be one more than the number specified in the Samples parameter.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Action
parameters.description: Whether this node should create new prims, or edit existing prims. In addition, the Force Edit option can be chosen to cause this node to ignore the houdini:editable attribute on prims, and always edit the specified attributes. This is in contrast to the Edit mode which will trigger a warning and not set attributes on prims with the houdini:editable attribute set to false.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.description: In Create mode, this lets you control where in the scene graph to create the prim(s). The default is usually /$OS. This creates a primitive at the root level with the same name as the node (for example, /tube1). This is a useful default for preventing naming conflicts, but terrible for organization. You should try to remember to change the Primitive Path to a better value when you create prims. For example, instead of naming models after the node that created them, you might want to name them after the geometry inside, and organize them under a /Models branch. The Create Primitives section contains basic controls for how to create the new prim(s).
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.description: In Edit mode, the node has a Primitive Pattern parameter. This lets you specify the prim(s) the node should operate on. You can click the select button beside the text box to select the primitives from the scene graph tree. You can also use primitive patterns for advanced matching, including matching all prims in a collection.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Allowed Primitive Types
parameters.description: In Edit mode, only prims that match one of the specified primitive types (or API schemas) can be modified by this node. Leave this parameter empty to permit editing any primitive type.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Handle Disallowed Types
parameters.description: In Edit mode, specifies what should happen when a primitive that is not one of the Allowed primitive types matches the primitive pattern Ignore Disallowed Prim Types: Do not set any attributes on this primitive, but do not notify the user.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Initialize Parameters
parameters.description: Changes the state of all control menu parameters to Do Nothing, so that this node will not apply any changes. Also grabs the current values of each property from the first Primitives match, and sets the values of the corresponding parameters to match. This means that changing any parameter's control menu to Set or Create mode will set the property to its current value, making it easier to apply changes to an existing value rather than setting a brand new value. With Rebuild Render-Specific Parameters you reset all parameters from render-specific tabs to their default values for the specific node. If you want to reset the parameters for the entire scene, you can also open the top-level Render menu and choose Rebuild All Render-Specific LOP Parameters.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Primitive Count
parameters.description: The number of primitives to create.
