entries.label: Edit Prototypes
entries.summary: Modify the prototypes of native or point instances in-place, without disturbing the instancing setup.

parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: Specify whether the instances edited are Point Instances or Native Instances.

parameters.label: Instances
parameters.description: The pattern of selected instanceable prims or point instances. Native Instances: Specify a list of paths to instanceable prims to replace. Point Instances: Specify a list of individual instances using /<<path>><<instance_index>> syntax

parameters.label: Edit
parameters.description: Whether to edit the Prototypes, or to directly edit the Selected Instances (native instances only). When set to Selected Instances, each selected native instance is made available for editing within the subnet. The node will apply the edits and the prims will remain instanceable. This will cause USD to generate one new prototype for each selected instance.

parameters.label: Apply to Selected Instances Only
parameters.description: This toggle will use the prototypes to the edits, and generate new prototypes that only apply to the selected instances. When editing Native Instances, this will simply apply the edits to the selected primitives only. When this node is set to edit Point Instances, it will first make a reference copy of the original prototype, then apply the users changes only to the new prototype.

parameters.label: Modify Prototypes at Origin
parameters.description: This toggle will present the prototypes within the subnet either at the origin (default), or in their world space position.
parameters.heading: Advanced

parameters.label: Reference Type
parameters.description: Choose whether to apply the edits as Reference, or as Inherit. A value of None means the edits are not applied to any prims. Use this to author class prims that are the target of an existing composition arc.
parameters.heading: Advanced

parameters.label: Make Instanceable
parameters.description: If the toggle is on, the newly created referencing primitive will be instanceable.
parameters.heading: Advanced

parameters.label: Dive-Target Mask
parameters.description: This node uses a population mask to isolate the stage, and only present the prototypes for editing. If you need to include extra primitives for visual reference, you can add their paths here.
parameters.heading: Edits Destination

parameters.label: New Prototype Suffix
parameters.description: When Apply to Selected Instances Only is enable for a PointInstancer, this is the suffix added to the new prototypes.
parameters.heading: Edits Destination

entries.label: Edit Target Layer
entries.summary: Allows you to apply edits directly in a lower layer, instead of overriding prims and attributes in the active layer.

parameters.label: Edit Layer Pattern
parameters.description: A file path or string pattern which matches the file path of the layer you want to edit.

parameters.label: Edit Layer Full Path
parameters.description: The full path to the layer file you want to edit. This is specified separately from the Edit Layer Pattern so that the pattern string can use wild cards, which will make it more likely to match the way the layer is identified internally by USD. For example, you may use an Edit Layer Pattern of */foo.usd, but set the Edit Layer Full Path to /work/usd/foo.usd. This parameter's value is only used to load this layer inside the editable subnet within this node.

parameters.label: Edit Layer Is Referenced
parameters.description: Turn this on if the layer was referenced into a branch, rather than overlayed as a sublayer.

parameters.label: Primitive With Reference
parameters.description: When Edit Layer is Referenced is on, set this to the scene graph path of the prim that referenced in the layer. For example, if /Models/bedside_lamp referenced in /lamp from lamp.usd, set this to /Models/bedside_lamp.

parameters.label: Referenced Primitive
parameters.description: When Edit Layer is Referenced is on, set this to the scene graph path of the prim that was referenced in. For example, if /Models/bedside_lamp referenced in /lamp from lamp.usd, set this to /lamp. This information is necessary to re-apply layer edits onto their corresponding location in the original file.

parameters.label: Output Modified Layer in Isolation
parameters.description: When this is on, the node outputs the modified layer, rather than the composed stage. This can be useful for debugging, to check the changes to the layer using tools such as the scene graph tree and scene graph details panes.

entries.label: Error
entries.summary: Generates a message, warning, or error, which can show up on a parent asset.

parameters.label: Number of Errors
parameters.description: The number of notices to evaluate.

parameters.label: Error Message
parameters.description: The text to show to the user when this notice is active. If this is an empty string, the notice is not reported.

parameters.label: Severity
parameters.description: What kind of feedback this notice is. A Message only shows up in the node info window. A Warning shows a badge on the node and warning text in the node info, but allows cooking to continue. An Error prevents cooking subsequent nodes, and displays a prominent badge on the node and error text in the node info. Error should only be used for problems that the network can't recover from.

parameters.label: Report this Error
parameters.description: If this expression evaluates to a non-zero value, the node reports this message/warning/error.

entries.label: Explore Variants
entries.summary: Visualize, set, or extract variants on primitives.

parameters.label: Source Prims
parameters.description: A space-separated list of prims to visualize, set the variant on, or copy variants from, depending on the Mode.
parameters.heading: Input

parameters.label: Nested Variants
parameters.description: Recurse through all variant combinations to find variants that might only be available when certain variant sets and variants are set.
parameters.heading: Input

parameters.label: Include Variant Sets with No Selection
parameters.label_norm: include variant sets with no selection
parameters.description: Include variants with no name.
parameters.heading: Input

parameters.label: Variant Set Filter
parameters.description: Specify a subset of the variant sets to explore as a space separated list. Wildcards are supported.
parameters.heading: Input

parameters.label: Variant Selection Filter
parameters.description: Specify a subset of the variants to explore as a space separated list. Wildcards are supported.
parameters.heading: Input

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: Duplicate Variants: Creates new primitives of the selected variants with the specified variant and variant set, under the Destination Prim. Explore Variants: Displays all available variants under the specified primitives. Set Variants: Sets the variant and variant set for the specified primitives.
parameters.heading: Output

parameters.label: Destination Prim
parameters.description: When Mode is Duplicate Variants, this is the _destination_ path under which the node creates duplicated prims. By default, the node's name is being used (/$OS).
parameters.heading: Output

parameters.label: Flatten Hierarchy
parameters.description: Copy all variant primitives directly under the Destination Prim path.
parameters.heading: Output

parameters.label: Create References
parameters.description: Rather than creating copies of all the variant primitives data, creates references to the original explored prim(s).
parameters.heading: Output

parameters.label: Flatten Input Layers
parameters.description: When Create References is disabled, the Sdf.CopySpec method requires all opinions relating to the explored primitives' to live on a single layer. This ensures the input layers are flattened before copying the variant data.
parameters.heading: Output

parameters.label: Include Input Stage
parameters.description: When disabled, copies/references all variants into an empty stage to simplify instancing variants.
parameters.heading: Output

parameters.label: Variant Selection
parameters.description: When Mode is Explore Variants or Set Variants, select the variants to duplicate or set, from the variants created. NOTE: When setting variants, if multiple variants are selected for a single primitive, the last selected variant will be used.
parameters.heading: Output

parameters.label: Layout
parameters.description: At Origin: Creates the duplicated variants, centered at the world origin. Stacked (XY): Creates/displays the variants in a vertical grid, along the XY plane with 1 row per primitive, with its bottom left corner at the world origin. Side by Side (XZ): Creates/displays the variants in a horizontal grid, along the XZ plane with 1 row per primitive, with its bottom left corner at the world origin.
parameters.heading: Layout

parameters.label: Use Bounds
parameters.description: When enabled, uses each variants bounds to avoid overlaps when created/displayed in a grid.
parameters.heading: Layout

parameters.label: Spacing
parameters.description: Adds spacing between variants created/displayed in a grid.
parameters.heading: Layout

parameters.label: Use Extents Hint
parameters.description: When Use Bounds is enabled, use primitive extent hints for bounding box instead of computing them.
parameters.heading: Layout

parameters.label: Justify
parameters.description: None: Space out the variants visually using their actual pivot points. Center: Space out the variants based on the centroids of the models. Y Min: Space out the variants based on their bottoms (minimum Y coordinate)
parameters.heading: Layout

entries.label: Extract Instances
entries.summary: Converts ("heroes") an instance into a "real" editable prim.

parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: How to select the instance(s) to extract. PointInstancer: Specify a list of individual instances using /<<path>><<instance_index>> syntax. Native Instances: Specify a list of paths to instanceable prims.

parameters.label: Instances
parameters.description: A space-separated list of instances, using /<<path>><<instance_index>> syntax (for example, /geometry/instancer0 /geometry/instancer1). To select all instances in an instancer, use /<<path>>*. To select a range, use /geometry/instancer4-7 (the range is inclusive). To select instances inside nested instancers, use multiple indexes, for example /geometry/instancer27. VEXpressions can be used to specify instances, for example, /geometry/instancer{@weights>0.5}.

parameters.label: Instances
parameters.description: When Type is Native Instances, a list of paths to instanceable prims.

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.description: The scene graph path _under_ which to put newly extracted prims. Under this prim, for each extracted instance, the node will create an Xform prim with the same name as the instancer, and under that the extracted prim (named instance_<<index_number>>). For example, if you set Primitive Path to /geometry/heroes, and extract instances 5 and 10 from /geometry/instancer1, the node creates the extracted prims at /geometry/heroes/instancer1/instance_5 and /geometry/heroes/instancer1/instance_10.

parameters.label: Primitive Name
parameters.description: When enabled, set the extracted primitive names to be prefixed by this instead of the original primitive name.

parameters.label: Flatten Hierarchy
parameters.description: Output all extracted primitives directly under the Primitive Path. WARNING: This can cause output primitive path clashes when extracting from multiple instancers simultaneously.

parameters.label: Prototype
parameters.description: Where to copy the "extracted" prim from. From instances: Use the prototype the instance was instancing. From Existing Primitives: Get the prim from an arbitrary path in the scene graph tree. For example, you might replace an instance with a higher-resolution "hero" geometry, or switch between render and proxy purposes. The node takes care of hiding the instance and copying its transform.

parameters.label: Prototype Primitive
parameters.description: When Prototype is From Existing Primitives, the scene graph path to the prim to copy to make the "extracted" prim.

parameters.label: Modify Source Primitive
parameters.description: When Prototype is From Existing Primitives, what to do with the primitive you based the "extracted" prim on (from Prototype Primitive). Do Not Modify Source Primitives: Don't do anything to the original prim. Hide Source Primitive: Set the visibility of the original prim to "hidden".

parameters.label: Make Instanceable
parameters.description: Make extracted reference prims instanceable.

parameters.label: Bind Materials
parameters.description: Recreate the instance's material bindings on the extracted prim. (If the bound material is a descendant of the prototype, the materials will work automatically when extracted. Otherwise you can turn this on to rewrite the bindings.)

parameters.label: Deactivate Entirely Extracted Instancers
parameters.description: When all instances are extracted, this option deactivates the original point instancer.

parameters.label: Scalar Primvars with Unauthored Element Size
parameters.label_norm: scalar primvars with unauthored element size
parameters.description: When inherited primvars' element size isn't authored, create scalar primvars instead of array primvars on the extracted instances.

parameters.label: Method
parameters.description: How to specify the time at which to extract the instance(s), either by frame or by time.
parameters.heading: Extraction Frame

parameters.label: Frame
parameters.description: The frame number at which to extract the instance(s). The default is an expression $F, which uses animation if present. To always extract from a frozen stage, delete the expression and set this to an explicit frame number.
parameters.heading: Extraction Frame

parameters.label: Time
parameters.description: The time (in seconds) at which to extract the instance(s). The default is an expression $T, which uses animation if present. To always extract from a frozen stage, delete the expression and set this to an explicit time.
parameters.heading: Extraction Frame

parameters.label: Integer Frames
parameters.description: Rounds the Frame to the nearest integer frame, avoiding fractional frame cooking. Note that when shifting by time, fractional frames are always allowed.
parameters.heading: Extraction Frame

entries.label: Fetch
entries.summary: Grabs the output of another LOP, potentially in another LOP network.

parameters.label: LOP Path
parameters.description: Node path to the LOP node you want to grab the output from.

parameters.label: Output
parameters.description: Which output to fetch from the source LOP node.

parameters.label: Perform Layer Break
parameters.description: This node behaves as if it is immediately followed by a Layer Break LOP. The layers making up the fetched stage will be stripped away when flattening into a reference or sublayer, or saving the stage to disk.

parameters.label: Remove Context Option Blocks
parameters.description: Specifies the number of Edit Context Option LOP blocks should be removed from the context option stack before cooking the fetched node. This can be used to shield the fetched nodes from any context options that are meant to be local to the subnet where the Fetch LOP resides. The default value of zero propagates all context option blocks to the fetched LOP node, allowing these options to affect the cooked result. Setting this value to -1 will remove all context option blocks from the stack, leaving only global context options set when cooking the fetched LOP node.

entries.label: File Cache
entries.summary: Caches (writes out once and then reads from) USD layers (possibly animated) to disk.

parameters.label: Load from Disk
parameters.description: When this is on, the node reads its output from the cached disk files, rather than cooking its input. When you click Save to Disk or Save to Disk in Background (on the Caching tab) to write out the cache files, the node automatically turns this checkbox on.

parameters.label: Reload Geometry
parameters.description: Force a reload of the file. This will also clear any cached data for packed disk primitives (see also the geocache command).

parameters.label: File Path
parameters.description: When this is Constructed (the default), the node builds up the cache file path(s) from the values of various parameters, allowing features such as versioning and animation options. If you set this to Explicit, you need to manually write a single expression in the Geometry File parameter with all the variables you want in the path (including the frame number when Time Dependent Cache is on).

parameters.label: Base Name
parameters.description: When File Path is Constructed, this is the first part of the cache file name. The default is $HIPNAME.$OS (the name of the current scene file without the .hip extension, then a dot, then the name of this node). This is usually sufficient to prevent filename collisions between files/nodes if you give this node an meaningful, unique name (if you have two networks containing nodes both named filecache1, you will get a collision). The drop down menu to the right of the text field has some more possible expressions.

parameters.label: File Type
parameters.description: The default is .bgeo.sc, which can handle any type of Houdini geometry and uses compression, so it's always safe to use. If _all_ the primitives in the input are _always_ VDB volumes, you can switch the file type to save the files directly as .vdb. When you set the File Type to .vdb, the node converts Houdini's primitive attributes to VDB grid metadata, and detail attributes to file metadata.

parameters.label: Base Folder
parameters.description: When File Path is Constructed, this is the folder to save the cache files into. The default is $HIP/geo (a folder named geo in the same directory as the current scene file). (When Version is on it adds another directory level inside the base folder.)

parameters.label: Open Directory
parameters.description: Click to show the contents of the Base Folder in the file manager. This can be useful when you want to clean up old cache files.

parameters.label: Version
parameters.description: When File Path is Constructed and the checkbox to the left is on, the node adds a directory level (and filename part) to the cache file path(s) indicating the version. This lets you cache multiple variations of the input network.

parameters.label: Save to Disk
parameters.description: Saves the geometry to disk with the last control settings.
parameters.heading: Cache

parameters.label: Save to Disk in Background
parameters.description: Use a TOP network to cook and save the cache files to disk in a separate background process. This allows you to keep working on other parts of Houdini. The cached frames will show up as they are completed by the other process.
parameters.heading: Cache

parameters.label: Cancel Cook
parameters.description: Stops all background caching processes, if any exist.
parameters.heading: Cache

parameters.label: TIP
parameters.description: You can collapse the box around these buttons as a "safety latch", to prevent yourself from clicking them and rebuilding the cache accidentally.
parameters.heading: Cache

parameters.label: Evaluate As
parameters.description: When this is Frame Range the node writes a cache file for every frame (see Start/End/Inc below). If you don't want pre-generate all frames at once, or if you know you only need to regenerate a single changed frame, you can set this to Single Frame. This makes the node write out a cache file only for the current frame (or the frame you set in Override Frame).
parameters.heading: Cache Range

parameters.label: Override Frame
parameters.description: When Evaluate As is Single Frame and the checkbox to the left is on, cache this explicit frame number instead of the current frame from the timeline.
parameters.heading: Cache Range

parameters.label: Start/End/Inc
parameters.description: Specifies the range of frames to render (start frame, end frame, and increment). All values may be floating point values. The range is inclusive. These parameters determine the values of the local variables for the output driver. $NRENDER: The number of frames to be rendered by the output driver. $N: The current frame being rendered (starting at 1 and going to $NRENDER).
parameters.heading: Cache Range

parameters.label: Substeps
parameters.description: When Evaluate As is Frame Range, this is the number of fractional sub-frames to divide each frame into. Caching sub-frames increases the quality of motion blur rendering for cached animated geometry. If you set Substeps greater than 1 and you've set File Path to Explicit, make sure your explicit path expression can handle fractional frames, by using $T (floating point time in seconds) or $FF (fractional frame number) instead of $F (whole frame number).
parameters.heading: Cache Range

parameters.label: Custom TOP Scheduler
parameters.description: This parameter overrides the TOP scheduler for this node.
parameters.heading: Scheduling

parameters.label: Strip Layers Above Layer Breaks
parameters.description: Enable this option to prevent layers authored above Layer Break nodes from being written to disk by this ROP. This allows a Layer Break node to dictate which portions of the LOP Network are to be saved. Disabling this option allows this behavior to be overridden, forcing the full stage authored by the LOP network to be written to disk. This may be used for debugging purposes, or to write a complete scene to disk for rendering.
parameters.heading: Layers

parameters.label: Strip Post-Layers
parameters.description: Enable this option to prevent layers added using the Hom:hou.LopNetwork#editablePostLayer method from being written to disk. With this option disabled, these post-layers are flattened into the layer Output File layer.
parameters.heading: Layers

parameters.label: Flush Data After Each Frame
parameters.description: When this is on, the node writes out each frame's data to disk before cooking the LOP Network to generate the next frame of data. When this is off (the default), the node cooks the data for all frames into memory and writes out the animated files all at once. Turning on this option ensures that only a single frame worth of data is in RAM at any one time, allowing arbitrarily large USD files to be created. But saving each frame can be slightly slower, and the generated files may be larger because of the way USD files append new data to an existing file. See saving animation above. When this option is on, this ROP can also generate separate USD files for each frame. To do this, embed the local variable for the current frame number in the Output File path (and other layer save paths) so each frame will write out files with unique names. For example
parameters.heading: Layers

parameters.label: Track Primitive Existence to Set Visibility
parameters.label_norm: track primitive existence to set visibility
parameters.description: LOP networks may generate vastly different scene graphs from one frame to the next. When combining these scene graphs over a frame range into a single animated scene graph, the set of primitives in the combined scene graph will be the union of the primitives in each frame's hierarchy. But if a mesh appears at frame 50, this generally means that it is desired for this mesh to not be visible prior to frame 50. Enable this option to cause this node to track a list of all primitives at each frame, and automatically author animated visibility attributes for any primitives that are added to or removed from the scene graph over time. This gives the appearance of primitives being added and removed over time. Only subclasses of UsdGeomImageable primitives will be tracked this way, since these are the only USD primitive types which respect the visibility attribute.
parameters.heading: Layers

parameters.label: Use Network Drive Safe Save (Windows Only)
parameters.label_norm: use network drive safe save (windows only)
parameters.description: When running on Windows, the USD library often has issues saving layers to network mounted drives when those layers are currently loaded into a USD stage. This can make it impossible to overwrite a USD layer that is in use, even by the current Houdini session. This option works around this issue by having the USD ROP mute each layer right before ti is saved to disk (but only when running under Windows - on Linux and MacOS this parameter has no effect). Once the layer is saved, it is un-muted. This approach incurs a performance penalty as any stages using this layer will be recomposed twice instead of once. But in some settings this can make the save process much more robust.
parameters.heading: Layers

parameters.label: Filter Time Samples
parameters.description: When to remove time samples that lie outside the frame(s) of the USD being exported, potentially reducing the size of the data generated. Never: Time samples should never be filtered during export. When Using Frame Franges: Time samples should only be filtered when exporting a frame range (i.e., not a single frame). Always: Time samples should always be filtered during export.
parameters.heading: Layers

parameters.label: Extra Frames
parameters.description: How much to expand the window of time samples to keep during filtering. Note that, in addition to any extra frames specified, there is always one additional extra sample included both before and after the window, to better support motion blur. Generally this value can safely be left at 0 (the default) and typically only needs changing when using multi-segment motion blur. See Filter Time Samples
parameters.heading: Layers

parameters.label: Files to Save
parameters.description: A list of patterns matching which files the node is _allowed_ to save. If this is blank (the default), the node saves all files. You can use this, for example, to avoid rewriting layer files that you know will never change.
parameters.heading: Extra files

parameters.label: Error Saving Layers with Implicit Paths
parameters.label_norm: error saving layers with implicit paths
parameters.description: When this is on (the default), the node errors if it would otherwise write an anonymous in-memory layer (that is, a layer with no file path metadata) to disk. You will usually only turn this off if you are using Save Style > Separate Layers (Preserve All Sublayers and References) to write out every layer separate for debugging purposes.
parameters.heading: Extra files

parameters.label: Save Updates to Modified Files From Disk
parameters.label_norm: save updates to modified files from disk
parameters.description: If you use the Load Layer LOP to bring a layer onto the stage, this "editable" version of the layer on disk has metadata marking it as originally coming from disk, rather than being created from scratch by LOPs. When this is on, layers created this way are saved to disk just like any other layer with file path metadata. Turning this off prevents saving these layers to disk. This can be useful if you never want these "edited from disk" layers to overwrite the original files, or at least prevent overwriting them until you are certain the output of the LOP network is correct, when you can allow the edited layers to be written to disk.
parameters.heading: Extra files

parameters.label: Flatten File Layers
parameters.description: When Save Style is Flatten Implicit Layers (Collapes Implicit Sublayers, Preserve References), files loaded from disk with a Sublayer LOP are not considered anonymous layers, and so are not composed down. Turn this on to flatten layers from disk as if they were anonymous layers. This can be useful for generating more portable USD layers that rely on a minimal number of external layers. It can also be used to "harden" the sublayered files on disk in their current state if they may be changing, but you are generating a USD file for archiving purposes and do not want it to reflect any upcoming changes to the external files.
parameters.heading: Extra files

parameters.label: Flatten SOP Layers
parameters.description: When Save Style is Flatten Implicit Layers (Collapse Implicit Sublayers, Preserve References), layers generated by importing data from SOPs with SOP Import are not considered anonymous layers, and so are not composed down. Turn this on to flatten layers imported from SOPs as if they were anonymous layers. This can be useful for generating more portable USD layers that rely on a minimal number of external layers.
parameters.heading: Extra files

parameters.label: Output Processors
parameters.description: Add an output processor to this node. Output processors are Python plugins that can alter the file locations and file path strings used for external files. The USD render node starts with one default output processor (called Use Relative Paths, see below). (See output processors for information on how to write an output processor plugin.) The following built-in processors are available Use Relative Paths: This is automatically added by default. This processor changes absolute file paths to relative paths in layer files. This allows you to use paths such as $HIP/usd/foo.usd for loading, but have them written out as paths relative to the source file. This is recommended practice so you probably do not want to remove this processor. Match Output Layer Extension: Normally, if you change the extension of the output file, it only affects that "top-level" output file. All other external files are written to their embedded save paths, with their embedded extension. This processor changes the extension on all paths to match the extension of the output file. This means if you change the output file to use .usda (the textual format), when this processor is active, all external USD files will also switch to .usda. Save Paths Relative to Output Path: Causes any Save Path parameters that are relative paths to be treated as if they are relative to the Output File parameter value. This makes it easy to ensure all files generated by a LOP network are saved into a common root directory. Changing the save location of the output file will implicitly change the save location of all other files. This processor has a Root Directory parameter which, if set, specifies a location other than the Output File to which Save Paths will be considered relative. Use Search Paths: This processor includes a Search Path parameter. Each asset path is compared against the directories listed in this path. If the asset is inside one of the search paths, the asset will be referenced with a search path rather than a full path or relative path. Copy All Assets to Referencing Layer Directory: This processor makes copies of all non-USD assets (such as UDIMs, texture maps, and volume files) in the same directory as the USD file that references them. The USD file is updated to refer to these local copies of the assets. These updated references will use absolute paths, so it is recommended that you use this in conjunction with a Use Relative Paths output processor. This localizing of assets makes it much easier to create USDZ archives of assets, since that format requires texture maps and similar assets to be in or contained under same directory holding the USD file. This processor has an Output Subdirectory parameter which causes the assets to be copied into a specific subdirectory inside the directory where the USD file is being written. This parameter should be a relative path, such as textures, not a full path to a directory. USD assets are not localized because doing so would break relative path references within those USD files. If USD data must also be localized to a single directory, it is recommended that this be accomplished by setting the Save Style on the USD ROP to Flatten Stage (Collapse All Sublayers and References), which will gather all USD data into a single layer. If an asset file doesn't exist, or the asset file is already located in the same directory or any subdirectory of the referencing layer file, the asset is not copied. This output processor should be moved above the "Use Relative Paths" output processor to ensure that the asset paths written to the USD file produce the simplest possible paths to the localized file locations.
parameters.heading: Output processing

parameters.label: Default Primitive
parameters.description: Set this to the *name* of a root primitive on the current stage to set it as the default primitive for the top-level file.
parameters.heading: Layer metadata

parameters.label: Error Saving Layer with No Default Primitive
parameters.label_norm: error saving layer with no default primitive
parameters.description: When this is on, the render node will error and stop cooking if you haven't specified a default primitive for all layers being written out. This is a way to force yourself to make sure layers have default prims, so you know you can reference in files without having to manually specify a top-level prim.
parameters.heading: Layer metadata

parameters.label: Save ROP's Time Information to Output
parameters.label_norm: save rop's time information to output
parameters.description: Write the start and end frames, as well as the current frames per second setting, to the top-level output file.
parameters.heading: Layer metadata

parameters.label: Clear Houdini-Specific Custom Data
parameters.description: LOP networks often attach Houdini-specific custom data to layers, prims, and properties. Houdini does not need this data to be stored on disk (usually it is related to how to write files), so by default Houdini strips out this data before saving. Normally there's no reason to turn this parameter off (it's possible it might help SideFX diagnosing a problem).
parameters.heading: Layer metadata

parameters.label: Ensure Basic Metrics are Set on All Layers
parameters.label_norm: ensure basic metrics are set on all layers
parameters.description: This options ensures that the upAxis and metersPerUnit metadata is set in every USD file written to disk. If a value has not been explicitly authored on a layer by the LOP Network, the default up axis and meters per unit values from the Lighting Preferences are used.
parameters.heading: Layer metadata

parameters.label: Pre-Render Script
parameters.description: Run this script before any rendering.
parameters.heading: Context options

parameters.label: Pre-Frame Script
parameters.description: Run this script before each frame.
parameters.heading: Context options

parameters.label: Post-Frame Script
parameters.description: Run this script after each frame.
parameters.heading: Context options

parameters.label: Post-Write Script
parameters.description: Run this script after each frame's data finishes writing to disk.
parameters.heading: Context options

parameters.label: Post-Render Script
parameters.description: Run this script after all rendering.
parameters.heading: Context options

parameters.label: Initialize Simulation OPs
parameters.description: Initialize DOP simulations before rendering.
parameters.heading: Context options

parameters.label: Alfred Style Progress
parameters.description: Print percentage complete value as files are written. This is in the style expected by Pixar's Alfred render queue.
parameters.heading: Context options

parameters.label: Report Network Use
parameters.description: Print the number of bytes sent or received by the distributed simulation nodes during cooks triggered by this node. This does not track network usage from, for example, saving a file to an NFS mount. It only tracks the network communication of distributed Houdini nodes. When this is on, the node writes out each frame's data to disk before cooking the LOP Network to generate the next frame of data. When this is off (the default), the node cooks the data for all frames into memory and writes out the animated files all at once. Turning on this option ensures that only a single frame worth of data is in RAM at any one time, allowing arbitrarily large USD files to be created. But saving each frame can be slightly slower, and the generated files may be larger because of the way USD files append new data to an existing file. See saving animation above. When this option is on, this ROP can also generate separate USD files for each frame. To do this, embed the local variable for the current frame number in the Output File path (and other layer save paths) so each frame will write out files with unique names. For example
parameters.heading: Context options

parameters.label: Track Primitive Existence to Set Visibility
parameters.label_norm: track primitive existence to set visibility
parameters.description: LOP networks may generate vastly different scene graphs from one frame to the next. When combining these scene graphs over a frame range into a single animated scene graph, the set of primitives in the combined scene graph will be the union of the primitives in each frame's hierarchy. But if a mesh appears at frame 50, this generally means that it is desired for this mesh to not be visible prior to frame 50. Enable this option to cause this node to track a list of all primitives at each frame, and automatically author animated visibility attributes for any primitives that are added to or removed from the scene graph over time. This gives the appearance of primitives being added and removed over time. Only subclasses of UsdGeomImageable primitives will be tracked this way, since these are the only USD primitive types which respect the visibility attribute.
parameters.heading: Context options

parameters.label: Use Network Drive Safe Save (Windows Only)
parameters.label_norm: use network drive safe save (windows only)
parameters.description: When running on Windows, the USD library often has issues saving layers to network mounted drives when those layers are currently loaded into a USD stage. This can make it impossible to overwrite a USD layer that is in use, even by the current Houdini session. This option works around this issue by having the USD ROP mute each layer right before ti is saved to disk (but only when running under Windows - on Linux and MacOS this parameter has no effect). Once the layer is saved, it is un-muted. This approach incurs a performance penalty as any stages using this layer will be recomposed twice instead of once. But in some settings this can make the save process much more robust.
parameters.heading: Context options

parameters.label: Filter Time Samples
parameters.description: When to remove time samples that lie outside the frame(s) of the USD being exported, potentially reducing the size of the data generated. Never: Time samples should never be filtered during export. When Using Frame Franges: Time samples should only be filtered when exporting a frame range (i.e., not a single frame). Always: Time samples should always be filtered during export.
parameters.heading: Context options

parameters.label: Extra Frames
parameters.description: How much to expand the window of time samples to keep during filtering. Note that, in addition to any extra frames specified, there is always one additional extra sample included both before and after the window, to better support motion blur. Generally this value can safely be left at 0 (the default) and typically only needs changing when using multi-segment motion blur. See Filter Time Samples
parameters.heading: Context options

parameters.label: Files to Save
parameters.description: A list of patterns matching which files the node is _allowed_ to save. If this is blank (the default), the node saves all files. You can use this, for example, to avoid rewriting layer files that you know will never change.
parameters.heading: Extra files

parameters.label: Error Saving Layers with Implicit Paths
parameters.label_norm: error saving layers with implicit paths
parameters.description: When this is on (the default), the node errors if it would otherwise write an anonymous in-memory layer (that is, a layer with no file path metadata) to disk. You will usually only turn this off if you are using Save Style > Separate Layers (Preserve All Sublayers and References) to write out every layer separate for debugging purposes.
parameters.heading: Extra files

parameters.label: Save Updates to Modified Files From Disk
parameters.label_norm: save updates to modified files from disk
parameters.description: If you use the Load Layer LOP to bring a layer onto the stage, this "editable" version of the layer on disk has metadata marking it as originally coming from disk, rather than being created from scratch by LOPs. When this is on, layers created this way are saved to disk just like any other layer with file path metadata. Turning this off prevents saving these layers to disk. This can be useful if you never want these "edited from disk" layers to overwrite the original files, or at least prevent overwriting them until you are certain the output of the LOP network is correct, when you can allow the edited layers to be written to disk.
parameters.heading: Extra files

parameters.label: Flatten File Layers
parameters.description: When Save Style is Flatten Implicit Layers (Collapes Implicit Sublayers, Preserve References), files loaded from disk with a Sublayer LOP are not considered anonymous layers, and so are not composed down. Turn this on to flatten layers from disk as if they were anonymous layers. This can be useful for generating more portable USD layers that rely on a minimal number of external layers. It can also be used to "harden" the sublayered files on disk in their current state if they may be changing, but you are generating a USD file for archiving purposes and do not want it to reflect any upcoming changes to the external files.
parameters.heading: Extra files

parameters.label: Flatten SOP Layers
parameters.description: When Save Style is Flatten Implicit Layers (Collapse Implicit Sublayers, Preserve References), layers generated by importing data from SOPs with SOP Import are not considered anonymous layers, and so are not composed down. Turn this on to flatten layers imported from SOPs as if they were anonymous layers. This can be useful for generating more portable USD layers that rely on a minimal number of external layers.
parameters.heading: Extra files

parameters.label: Output Processors
parameters.description: Add an output processor to this node. Output processors are Python plugins that can alter the file locations and file path strings used for external files. The USD render node starts with one default output processor (called Use Relative Paths, see below). (See output processors for information on how to write an output processor plugin.) The following built-in processors are available Use Relative Paths: This is automatically added by default. This processor changes absolute file paths to relative paths in layer files. This allows you to use paths such as $HIP/usd/foo.usd for loading, but have them written out as paths relative to the source file. This is recommended practice so you probably do not want to remove this processor. Match Output Layer Extension: Normally, if you change the extension of the output file, it only affects that "top-level" output file. All other external files are written to their embedded save paths, with their embedded extension. This processor changes the extension on all paths to match the extension of the output file. This means if you change the output file to use .usda (the textual format), when this processor is active, all external USD files will also switch to .usda. Save Paths Relative to Output Path: Causes any Save Path parameters that are relative paths to be treated as if they are relative to the Output File parameter value. This makes it easy to ensure all files generated by a LOP network are saved into a common root directory. Changing the save location of the output file will implicitly change the save location of all other files. This processor has a Root Directory parameter which, if set, specifies a location other than the Output File to which Save Paths will be considered relative. Use Search Paths: This processor includes a Search Path parameter. Each asset path is compared against the directories listed in this path. If the asset is inside one of the search paths, the asset will be referenced with a search path rather than a full path or relative path. Copy All Assets to Referencing Layer Directory: This processor makes copies of all non-USD assets (such as UDIMs, texture maps, and volume files) in the same directory as the USD file that references them. The USD file is updated to refer to these local copies of the assets. These updated references will use absolute paths, so it is recommended that you use this in conjunction with a Use Relative Paths output processor. This localizing of assets makes it much easier to create USDZ archives of assets, since that format requires texture maps and similar assets to be in or contained under same directory holding the USD file. This processor has an Output Subdirectory parameter which causes the assets to be copied into a specific subdirectory inside the directory where the USD file is being written. This parameter should be a relative path, such as textures, not a full path to a directory. USD assets are not localized because doing so would break relative path references within those USD files. If USD data must also be localized to a single directory, it is recommended that this be accomplished by setting the Save Style on the USD ROP to Flatten Stage (Collapse All Sublayers and References), which will gather all USD data into a single layer. If an asset file doesn't exist, or the asset file is already located in the same directory or any subdirectory of the referencing layer file, the asset is not copied. This output processor should be moved above the "Use Relative Paths" output processor to ensure that the asset paths written to the USD file produce the simplest possible paths to the localized file locations.
parameters.heading: Output processing

parameters.heading: Layer metadata

parameters.label: Error Saving Layer with No Default Primitive

parameters.label: Save Paths Relative to Output Path
parameters.label_norm: save paths relative to output path
parameters.description: Causes any Save Path parameter that are relative paths to be treated as if they are relative to the output file. This makes it easy to ensure all files generated by a LOP network are saved into a common root directory. Changing the save location of the output file will implicitly change the save location of all other files.
parameters.heading: Output Processing

parameters.label: Use Search Paths
parameters.description: This processor includes a Search Path parameter. Each asset path is compared against the directories listed in this path. If the asset is inside one of the search paths, the asset will be referenced with a search path rather than a full path or relative path.
parameters.heading: Output Processing

parameters.label: Match Output Layer Extension
parameters.description: Normally, if you change the extension of the output file, it only affects that "top-level" output file. All other external files are written to their embedded save paths, with their embedded extension. This processor changes the extension on all paths to match the extension of the output file. This means if you change the output file to use .usda (the textual format), when this processor is active, all external USD files will also switch to .usda.
parameters.heading: Output Processing

parameters.label: Save Retries
parameters.description: If saving the geometry to disk fails due to a disk writing error, Houdini will usually error the output node immediately. This is desirable for most cases where a failure to save means an illegal path, which is not recoverable. However, sometimes files fail to save due to network issues. If the number of save retries is non-zero, Houdini will re-attempt to save this number of times. Each time will be accompanied with an output to the console of the failure to save and a five second wait in the hopes that the network will clear up.

parameters.label: Missing Frame

Report Error sets an error on the node, preventing the rest of the network from cooking. This makes it obvious when a problem happens. No Geometry (the default) sets a warning on the node rather than an error, and outputs empty geometry. This can be useful if your network has a way of dealing with missing cache frames, or if they're not important.
parameters.heading: Load

parameters.label: Load Retries
parameters.description: If loading the geometry from disk fails due to a disk writing error, Houdini will usually error the output node immediately. This is desirable for most cases where a failure to load means an illegal path, which is not recoverable. However, sometimes files fail to load due to network issues. If the number of Load Retries is non-zero, Houdini will re-attempt to load this number of times. Each time will be accompanied with an output to the console of the failure to load and a five second wait in the hopes that the network will clear up.
parameters.heading: Load

parameters.label: Pre-fetch Geometry
parameters.description: Attempt to predict the next frame that will be needed and load it in the background. This lets computation be overlapped with file IO. If you are blending multiple frames, the Cache Frames needs to be large enough for only the net-new frame to be loaded each cook. Otherwise the simple predictive model of the prefetcher will be confused and stop working.
parameters.heading: Load
