parameters.description: When turned on, the Subset Attributes setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a usdconfigpartitionattribs detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the USD Configure SOP).
parameters.heading: Import Data

parameters.label: Subset Attributes
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying which SOP string or integer attributes represent subsets of the geometry. The importer puts elements with the same value for this attribute into their own geometry subsets. Each attribute's subsets are added to a subset family (named from the original attribute) which indicates that the subsets are related. The subset family's type is set to partition to indicate that the subsets are non-intersecting and that every element of the primitive appears in a subset. If there are elements with empty string values (which are not added to a subset), the family type is instead set to nonOverlapping to indicate that the subsets are non-intersecting but some elements do not appear in a subset. The family's type is authored as an attribute on the parent primitive, for example subsetFamily:shop_materialpath:familyType. Subsets can be created from point or primitive partition attributes on SOP meshes, curves, tetrahedra, and points. The importer will try to set the subset name to the attribute value, but may need to change the name to make it a legal USD primitive name. The importer stores the raw attribute value on the geometry subset prim as Custom Data with the key partitionValue.
parameters.heading: Import Data

parameters.label: Enable Prefix Subsets with Attribute Name
parameters.label_norm: enable prefix subsets with attribute name
parameters.description: When turned on, the Prefix Subsets with Attribute Name setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a usdconfigprefixpartitionsubsets detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the USD Configure SOP).
parameters.heading: Import Data

parameters.label: Prefix Subsets with Attribute Name
parameters.description: When creating subsets from Subset Attributes, the subsets are named by combining the attribute name with the partition attribute's value (a string or integer). This avoids name collisions when multiple partition attributes contain the same values, but can be undesirable if precise control of the subset names is required. For string attributes, if this option is turned off, the attribute values are directly used as the subset names.
parameters.heading: Import Data

parameters.label: Enable Subset Groups
parameters.description: When turned on, the Subset Groups setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a usdconfigsubsetgroups detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the USD Configure SOP).
parameters.heading: Import Data

parameters.label: Subset Groups
parameters.description: A space-separated list of group names/patterns specifying SOP groups. SOP elements in each group are imported as a geometry subset, named for the group. Subsets can be created from point or primitive groups on SOP meshes, curves, tetrahedra, and points.
parameters.heading: Import Data

parameters.label: Enable USD Custom Attributes
parameters.description: When turned on, the USD Custom Attributes setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a usdconfigcustomattribs detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the USD Configure SOP).
parameters.heading: Import Data

parameters.label: USD Custom Attributes
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to import into USD as attributes (rather than primvars).
parameters.heading: Import Data

parameters.label: Enable Capture Weights
parameters.description: When turned on, the Capture Weights setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a usdconfigcaptureweights detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the USD Configure SOP).
parameters.heading: Import Data

parameters.label: Capture Weights
parameters.description: Controls how capture weights (represented by the boneCapture SOP attribute) are translated. This does not affect agent primitives, which are always translated to UsdSkel. Translate to UsdSkel: Translates boneCapture to the primvars required for UsdSkel (primvars:skel:jointIndices and primvars:skel:jointWeights) and applies the SkelBindingAPI to the USD prim. Translate to APEX: Translates boneCapture to the primvars required for APEX animation (primvars:houdini:apex:deform:jointIndices and primvars:houdini:apex:deform:jointWeights) and applies the HoudiniApexShapeDeformAPI to the USD prim. Additionally, the joint names are translated to the houdini:apex:deform:joints attribute.
parameters.heading: Import Data

parameters.label: Enable Translate UV Attribute to ST
parameters.label_norm: enable translate uv attribute to st
parameters.description: When turned on, the Translate UV Attribute to ST setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a usdconfigtranslateuvtost detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the USD Configure SOP).
parameters.heading: Import Data

parameters.label: Translate UV Attribute to ST
parameters.description: When turned on, converts the SOP vertex attribute uv into a USD primvar called primvars:st. Whether you need to turn this on depends on the renderer you are using and how your shaders are authored. If you are rendering with Karma, leave this off. (As of this writing there is no strict standard for texture coordinate naming in USD, but the use of st is a common convention, whereas in SOP geometry, using uv is the common convention.)
parameters.heading: Import Data

entries.label: Geometry Subset VOP
entries.summary: Creates USD geometry subsets within geometry prims (similar to groups in SOPs) based on evaluating a VEXpression or VOP network.

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.description: The primitive(s) the node should operate on. You can drag primitives from the scene graph tree pane into this textbox to add their paths, or click the Smallicon:BUTTONS/reselect Reselect button beside the text box to select the primitives in the viewer, or ((Ctrl))-click the Reselect button to choose prims from a pop-up tree window. You can also use primitive patterns for advanced matching, including matching all prims in a collection (using /path/to/prim.collection:<<name>>). You can drag and drop a specific (or multiple specific) USD prim(s) from the Scene Graph Tree into the window to run validation on only these USD primitives. NOTE: This parameter needs to be exposed in order for the transform handles to be context-aware. Without it, the handles may not be positioned properly.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: How the VEX program specifies subset contents. Selection: Set the name of a subset. Evaluate the network for each polygonal face. The network should output an integer. If the network output is 1 (really, non-zero), the face is included in the subset. If the output is 0, the face is excluded from in the subset. (This method can only create a single subset at a time.) Partition: Evaluate the network for each polygonal face. The network should output a string, containing the name of the subset to put the current face into. (This method can only create non-overlapping subsets.)

parameters.label: Subset Name
parameters.description: When Mode is Selection, this is the name of the subset to create/edit. When Mode is Partition, this string (if any) is prefixed to all subset names generated by the VEX program.

parameters.label: Family Name
parameters.description: Specifies the family name for the created geometry subset. In USD, a geometry primitive can have several related subsets. This is indicated by the subset family name. I.e., subsets with the same family name are considered related, and can be validated together for properties such as overlapping membership or coverage of the parent geometry primitive.

parameters.label: Family Type
parameters.description: Specifies the coverage of the family to which the created subset belongs

parameters.label: Vex Source
parameters.description: Where to get the VEX to run. You should usually leave this set to Myself and build a VOP network inside this node, unless you have a good reason to choose one of the other options. Myself: Use the CVEX VOP network inside this node. Other Node: Specify another node that generates VEX code. Script: Specify a compiled .vex file on disk. VEXpression: Write a VEX expression in a parameter.
parameters.heading: VEX Setup

parameters.label: Node Path
parameters.description: When Vex Source is Other Node, the node path of the node that generates the VEX code.
parameters.heading: VEX Setup

parameters.label: Script
parameters.description: When Vex Source is Script, the file path to the compiled .vex file.
parameters.heading: VEX Setup

parameters.label: Vexpression
parameters.description: A bit of VEX to evaluate. The path to the current prim is available as @primpath. You can read current attribute values using @<<name>>. If this is one line, you can omit the return keyword and the semicolon at the end. However, if this takes more than one line or involves statements, you must use return and end each statement with a semicolon. For example
parameters.heading: VEX Setup

parameters.label: Vexpression Returns a String
parameters.description: Whether to interpret the result of the VEXpression as a string or integer. Turn this on when Mode is Partition, turn it off when Mode is Selection.
parameters.heading: VEX Setup

parameters.label: Re-load VEX Functions
parameters.description: When Vex Source is Script, click this to force reload all .vex files on disk.
parameters.heading: VEX Setup

parameters.label: Compiler
parameters.description: The VEX compiler command to use to compile the VOP network inside this node. You should not change this unless you really have a good reason to do so.
parameters.heading: VEX Setup

parameters.label: Force Compile
parameters.description: Clear the cached VEX code generated from the children VOPs, forcing it to be generated and compiled again. Normally the node should automatically recompile whenever the network changes, but this may be useful when debugging problems.
parameters.heading: VEX Setup

parameters.label: Evaluation Node Path
parameters.description: Certain VEX functions, like ch(), evaluate parameters on this node. In some cases you want these functions to be relative to a different node (for example, with nodes inside a digital asset, you often want to evaluate functions relative to the parent asset). This is a relative node path to the node to use as "the current node" in the program.
parameters.heading: VEX Setup

parameters.label: Autobind by Name
parameters.description: In a VEXpression, automatically create @ variables corresponding to existing attributes. In a VOP network, automatically bind Parameter or Bind nodes to attributes if they have the same name. (Default is on.)
parameters.heading: Attribute Bindings

parameters.label: Number of Bindings
parameters.description: The number of USD attributes to bind to VEX variables.
parameters.heading: Attribute Bindings

parameters.label: Attribute Type
parameters.description: The USD datatype of the attribute. You should usually leave this set to Auto, so the node will use the known type of an existing attribute. If you are going to create the attribute, and node doesn't translate the VEX type into the correct USD type (for example, it becomes string but you want a token), you can change this to the type you want.
parameters.heading: Attribute Bindings

parameters.label: VEX Parameter
parameters.description: The name of the VEX parameter bound to the attribute.
parameters.heading: Attribute Bindings

entries.label: Graft Branches
entries.summary: Takes prims/branches from the second input and attaches them onto branches of the scene graph tree in the first input.

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.description: The parent scene graph path of all grafted sub-trees. The Destination Prim Path of each grafted prim is appended to this path. See Where to attach each subtree above.

parameters.label: Primitive Kind
parameters.description: If the parent prim in Primitive Path does not exist, it will be created, and set to be this kind. If the prim already exists, this parameter does nothing.

parameters.label: Parent Primitive Type
parameters.description: If this node generates a path where intermediate prims do not exist yet, it will create them. This controls the type of any intermediate prims this node creates.

parameters.label: Primitive Specifier
parameters.description: This controls the specifier(Define/Over/Class) of any intermediate prims this node creates.

parameters.label: Make Destination Primitive Paths Unique
parameters.description: It is possible to set multiple inputs to have the same destination path. If this parameter is off, the trees are merged. If this is on, the node adds increasing numbers on to the end of each destination path until it is unique.

parameters.label: Treat Destination Paths as Parents
parameters.description: Controls whether source prims will be copied as children of the specified destination prim (on), or copied directly into the destination prim (off).

parameters.label: Frame Offset Mode
parameters.description: Controls how/whether to edit time samples on the grafted prims. (To not edit time samples, set this to Offset and Frame Offset to 0.) Note that this parameter edits the time samples in terms of *frames*, not seconds. Match Start Times: Time-shift the animation based on the first time sample. For example, if the current stage (first input) is a shot with frame range 200-300, and you graft from a stage with frame range 100-200, the grafted animation will be shifted by +100 frames. Offset: Adds or subtracts a constant number of frames to the animation, specified in the Frame Offset parameter below. Match and Offset: Combination of the other two options: shifts the animation based on start times, _and then also_ applies a constant offset.

parameters.label: Frame Offset
parameters.description: When Frame Offset Mode is Offset or Match and Offset, the number of frames (positive or negative) to offset the grafted time samples. Note that this parameter edits the time samples in terms of *frames*, not seconds.

parameters.label: Number of Source Prims
parameters.description: How many prims to graft.

parameters.label: Enable
parameters.description: Whether the node applies this graft in the output.
parameters.heading: Source Prim

parameters.label: Source Prim Path
parameters.description: The path to the prim to grab from the second input.
parameters.heading: Source Prim

parameters.label: Destination Prim Path
parameters.description: Where to put the grafted prim in the scene graph tree of the first input. This path is added on to the path in the Primitive Path parameter.
parameters.heading: Source Prim

parameters.label: Keep Position
parameters.description: Keep the worldspace position of the prim(s) being grafted. This may be useful if the source and destination hierarchies have different transformation stacks.
parameters.heading: Source Prim

parameters.label: Keep Material
parameters.description: Keep the material assignment for the prim(s) being grafted. This may be useful if the source prim's material assignment comes from a parent but it is being grafted under a different parent that has a different material assignment.
parameters.heading: Source Prim

entries.label: Graft Stages
entries.summary: Takes scene graph trees from other inputs and attaches them onto branches of the scene graph tree in the first input.

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.description: The parent scene graph path of all grafted sub-trees. The destination path of each subtree is appended to this path. See Where to attach each subtree above.

parameters.label: Primitive Kind
parameters.description: If the parent prim in Primitive Path does not exist, it will be created, and set to be this kind. If the prim already exists, this parameter does nothing.

parameters.label: Parent Primitive Type
parameters.description: If this node generates a path where intermediate prims do not exist yet, it will create them. This controls the type of any intermediate prims this node creates.

parameters.label: Primitive Specifier
parameters.description: This controls the specifier(Define/Over/Class) of any intermediate prims this node creates.

parameters.label: Make Destination Primitive Paths Unique
parameters.description: It is possible to set multiple inputs to have the same destination path. If this parameter is off, the trees are merged. If this is on, the node adds increasing numbers on to the end of each destination path until it is unique.

parameters.label: Destination Path Default
parameters.description: You can set the destination path (which is then appended to the Primitive Path) for each wire into the multi-input by clicking in the table below this node's parameters. If you don't give an input a custom destination path, the node evaluates this expression to compute destination path. The default is the name of the node connected into the multi-input. In the expression you can use the @input local variable ($IIDX is deprecated) as the index of the current input (numbered from left to right starting at 0).

entries.label: HDA Dynamic Payload
entries.summary: Cooks a OBJ or SOP asset on disk and imports the animated geometry output as a USD payload.

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.description: In create mode, this parameter specifies a single primitive path. This is the scene graph path where the referenced branch will be attached. If this prim doesn't exist, the node will create it. In edit mode, this parameter is a primitive pattern that will be matched against the existing primitives on the stage connected to this node's first input. You can use local variables to control the reference primitive path.
parameters.heading: Destination Primitive

parameters.label: Primitive Kind
parameters.description: If the prim at Primitive Path doesn't exist, this node will create it. If it has to create the prim, it will set it to have this kind. Setting this parameter to Auto will not author a Kind on the leaf primitive where the reference is added. Instead, it will examine the Kind of the prim after setting the reference, and automatically set the Kind of ancestor prims to ensure the leaf primitive is part of a valid model hierarchy. Note that this may result in adding a Kind to ancestor prims that were not created by this node. If the referenced prim has no kind, or is not a model kind, Auto mode will not author Kind on any prim.
parameters.heading: Destination Primitive

parameters.label: Primitive Purpose
parameters.description: Set the primitive's purpose. Purposes are a way to control what gets rendered. The viewer/renderer only shows primitives tagged with one of a specified set of purposes. If you set up purposes on your primitives, then you can control visibility of all primitives with the same purpose at render time by setting what purposes are visible in the render settings. Default: No set purpose, rendered by default. Render: Should be used to tag high-resolution geometry that should appear in final renders. Proxy: Should be used to tag faster/cheaper/lower-resolution proxy geometry. This may be used for test renders. Guide: Should be used to tag "guide geometry" that should appear in an interactive viewer but not a rendered image. For example, collision geometry for a simulation.
parameters.heading: Destination Primitive

parameters.label: Parent Primitive Type
parameters.description: If the prim at Primitive Path doesn't exist, this node will create it. If it has to create the prim, it will give any intermediate prims it has to create this type.
parameters.heading: Destination Primitive

parameters.label: Make Instanceable
parameters.description: Mark the new or modified prims as instanceable (as in "native instancing"). This saves memory if you reference the same branch into multiple places, but makes the descendants of the referenced prim not editable. If this option is off, the prims are not explicitly marked as not instanceable. Instead, the current instanceable value on each prim is left unchanged.
parameters.heading: Destination Primitive

parameters.label: HDA File
parameters.description: The file path of the digital asset file to load.
parameters.heading: HDA

parameters.label: Operator Type
parameters.description: If the library file in HDA File contains more than one asset, this controls which asset to load and cook. If this is blank, the node just uses the first asset in the file.
parameters.heading: HDA

parameters.label: Reload
parameters.description: Click the reload the asset definition from disk. You should do this if you overwrite the .hda file with a new definition of the asset.
parameters.heading: HDA

parameters.label: Other Primitives
parameters.description: What to do with regular non-packed primitives (points, curves, polygons, spheres, and so on). Define: Create the USD prims for the imported geometry if they don't already exist. This is the standard way to import geometry. Overlay: Create the USD prims as overrides. They will only be visible as changes to any prims that exist at a lower level with the same paths. This may be useful where you only want to import and modify certain attributes from SOPs onto existing USD geometry. Overlay Transforms: Like Overlay, but only imports transform data.
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition

parameters.label: Define Only Leaf Primitives
parameters.description: Author intermediate primitives (for example, any Xform prims created for the Import Path Prefix) as overrides instead of definitions. This means if they don't match up with underlying prims in lower layers, the leaf prims won't be added to the scene. This is useful if you only want to import the geometry if its ancestors already exist in the scene tree. (Note that all of the data is still imported, it just may not be visible in the scene graph tree or the viewport.)
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition

parameters.label: Packed Primitives
parameters.description: What to do with SOP-native packed primitives. Create Xforms: Creates an Xform prim from the packed primitive's transform and attributes, and the packed primitive's geometry is imported underneath. This mode is used by default when importing packed folders. You can assign a SOP primitive string attribute to the packed primitive named usdprimtype to author a primitive type of Scope or None rather than Xform. Create Native Instances: Import the geometry in packed primitives as instanceable references. This imports each piece as a prototype under a Prototypes prim under the Import Path Prefix prim. You can assign a SOP primitive attribute to the packed primitives named usdprototypespath to specify a custom USD scene graph path to place the prototypes under. Create PointInstancer: Import the geometry in packed primitives as point instanced geometry. This imports each unique piece as a prototype under the point instancer prim. You can assign a SOP primitive attribute to the packed primitive named usdinstancerpath to specify the USD scene graph path of the instancer. Unpack: Only imports the packed primitive's geometry. Unlike the Create Xforms mode, this does not create any additional hierarchy, and is equivalent to unpacking the packed primitive prior to being imported. This can be useful for importing multiple pieces of geometry without merging their attributes.
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition

parameters.label: NURBS Curves
parameters.description: What to do with NURBS curve primitives. Convert to Basis Curves: Import the curves as a BasisCurves primitive. For curves where the end points should be interpolated, additional vertices are explicitly inserted at the beginning and end of the curve rather than setting the wrap attribute to pinned. This method is provided for backward compatibility, as previously pinned curves were not supported by some render delegates. This only supports cubic curves, but is useful for rendering through Hydra. Convert to Pinned Basis Curves: Import the curves as a BasisCurves primitive. For curves where the end points should be interpolated, the curve's wrap attribute is set to pinned so that additional points are inserted implicitly when rendering. This only supports cubic curves, but is useful for rendering through Hydra. Create NURBS Curves: Import the curves as a NurbsCurves primitive. This provides complete round-tripping of NURBS curves, but has limited support for rendering through Hydra.
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition

parameters.label: Kind Authoring
parameters.description: How to assign kinds to imported prims. All Geometry is One Component: Set root primitives in the imported tree to Component. Do not set kinds on descendants. Nested Groups and Components: Set leaf primitives in the imported tree to Component. Set branch primitives to Group. Nested Assembly, Groups, and Components: Set root prims in the imported tree to Assembly. Set intermediate branch prims to Group. Set leaf prims to Component. None: Do not set kinds on the imported prims.
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition

parameters.label: Path Attributes
parameters.description: A (comma or space-separated) list of names of SOP *primitive string attributes* to use to use as prim paths to put the SOP geometry into. The default is path,name. See geometry hierarchy above. If the list has more than one attribute, the importer checks each attribute for the first non-empty value. If the string value a full path, that path is used as the USD scene graph path for that primitive. If the string is a relative path (or just a name), the string is appended to the Import Path Prefix string to generate a full scene graph path. If none of the listed attributes exist on a given SOP primitive, or all values are an empty string, the importer generates a name automatically (for example, sphere_0).
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition

parameters.label: Reverse Polygon Vertex Ordering
parameters.description: USD supports an orientation attribute on mesh primitives that indicates whether polygons have a left-handed or right-handed ordering, while SOP geometry is always left-handed ordering. When this option is on, the importer always reorders vertices (and associated primvars) to be right-handed. This is useful when round tripping right-handed oriented polygons from USD into SOPs and back into USD. The data is always converted to a left handed ordering when importing it into SOPs. If you imported the polygons back into USD without this option, they would be left-handed, unlike the original.
parameters.heading: Geometry Handling

parameters.label: Topology Attributes
parameters.description: Controls whether USD topology attributes should be authored as time sampled or default values. The following attributes are treated as topology attributes Animated: If you know that topology is changing in the source geometry over time, choose this option to record topology attributes as time samples in the USD scene graph. Having animated topology can be very expensive during playback, so only use this option when necessary. Static: Write topology attributes as default values. This can make playback much faster, but limits how the topology can change over time. None: Do not author topology attributes. This is useful when USD data is sent to SOPs for processing, then brought back into LOPs. Using this option tells the importer that the geometry topology has not changed in this process, so only the changing point positions or other primvars will be imported.
parameters.heading: Import Data

parameters.label: Attributes
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to import into USD as primvars. In addition to matching attribute names directly, there are some values with special meanings bounds: Authors the USD extent attribute using the calculated bounding box of the associated SOP geometry. visibility: Authors the USD visibility attribute based on the value of the usdvisibility geometry attribute.
parameters.heading: Import Data

parameters.label: Indexed Attributes
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to import into USD as indexed primvars. If a SOP attribute matches this pattern, the importer authors the primvar as an indexed array of values (that is, an array of values called primvars:<<name>>, and an array of indices into those values called primvars:<<name>>:indices). Preparing an indexed primvar can be expensive for attributes that are not integers or strings. You should only use indexed primvars where it is likely to result in significant savings in storage size due to a small number of unique values being used across a large number of components.
parameters.heading: Import Data

parameters.label: Import as Single Element Array
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to import into USD as primvars with Constant interpolation (an array with a single value for the whole primitive), regardless of whether the SOP geometry attribute is a point, primitive, or vertex attribute. If multiple values could be chosen for a particular USD primitive, the importer chooses the first value it encounters. Importing as a single element array (versus Import as Single Value) can be useful since it allows the primvar's interpolation to be overridden without changing the primvar's type.
parameters.heading: Import Data

parameters.label: Import as Single Value
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to import into USD as primvars with Constant interpolation and a single value for the whole primitive, regardless of whether the SOP geometry attribute is a point, primitive, or vertex attribute. If multiple values could be chosen for a particular USD primitive, the importer chooses the first value it encounters. This is the default behavior for how detail attributes are imported. This is similar to Import as Single Element Array, but the primvar's type is a scalar value instead of an array with a single element (for example, vector3f instead of vector3f[]).
parameters.heading: Import Data

parameters.label: Set Default Values
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to always author as default values for USD primvars (never time samples). This is the list of exclusions when Author Time Samples is set to If Not Specifically Excluded.
parameters.heading: Import Data

parameters.label: USD Custom Attributes
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to import into USD as attributes (rather than primvars).
parameters.heading: Import Data

parameters.label: Translate UV Attribute to ST
parameters.description: When turned on, converts the SOP vertex attribute uv into a USD primvar called primvars:st. Whether you need to turn this on depends on the renderer you are using and how your shaders are authored. If you are rendering with Karma, leave this off. (As of this writing there is no strict standard for texture coordinate naming in USD, but the use of st is a common convention, whereas in SOP geometry, using uv is the common convention.)
parameters.heading: Import Data

parameters.label: Caching Mode
parameters.description: How to cache time samples of animated geometry. Loading a time sample for the first time can be slow, but subsequent loads are faster when the time sample is cached. None: Do not cache any time samples. Choosing this option also clears any currently cached samples. Continuous: Cache time samples as they are needed. Range: Cache a specified range of time samples all at once. This "front-loads" the caching time, but once the cache is warmed up, interactions will be much faster than if you were caching frame-by-frame. Do not use this mode while you are tweaking parameters on the Geometry tab, since changing those parameters invalidates the cache, and the node will keep trying to re-cache the full frame range on every change.
parameters.heading: Time Sample Caching

parameters.label: Time Start/End/Interval
parameters.description: When Caching Mode is Range, the start frame, end frame, and interval to cache.
parameters.heading: Time Sample Caching

parameters.label: Keep Houdini Engine Open
parameters.description: Turn this on while you're tweaking the geometry parameters and checking the output in the viewer, for faster interaction. Once you've settled on the parameters you want to cook with, you can turn this off, so the node only runs Houdini Engine when needed.
parameters.heading: Houdini Engine Options

parameters.label: Generate Parameters
parameters.description: After you choose an asset to import (HDA File on the Payload tab), click this button to duplicate the imported asset's parameter interface on this tab. You can then use this tab to control what parameter settings to cook the asset with.
parameters.heading: Geometry

entries.label: Hermite Curves
entries.summary: Creates or edits a hermite curves shape primitive.

parameters.label: Sampling Behavior
parameters.description: Cooking this node can generate many USD time samples, rather than just a single time sample at the current time. This can be equivalent to having a Cache LOP following this node, but it will evaluate much faster, and does not cache data from any other nodes. This allows animated data to be authored to USD without introducing a node time dependency which would then cause all following nodes to also be time dependent. This can vastly improve playback performance of some LOP Networks. In all sampling modes, if a parameter on this node does not vary with time, and does not rely on other time sampled data from the stage, only a single default value will be generated in USD for the corresponding attribute. USD time samples are only generated for parameters that may vary over time. Sample Current Frame: A single time sample will be generated for the current time. Sample Frame Range If Input Is Not Time Dependent: If the input to this node is time dependent, this node behaves as if it is in Sample Current Frame mode. Otherwise it behaves as if it is in Sample Frame Range mode. Sample Frame Range: The Start/End/Inc parameter is used to generate multiple times at which this node's parameters are evaluated, and a USD time sample is created for each attribute at each one of these times.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Start/End/Inc
parameters.description: When the Sampling behavior is Sample Frame Range, this parameter controls the number and spacing of base time samples to be generated by this node. The default values of this parameter are @fstart, @fend, and @finc. These values correspond to the start, end, and step size of the global Houdini animation settings when interacting with Houdini. When using a ROP node to generate a range of frames, these values correspond to the start, end, and increment values specified on the ROP node being executed. This default ensures that a USD file written to disk will contain time samples for exactly the frame range requested by the ROP (regardless of the Houdini animation settings).
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Subframe Sampling
parameters.description: For each primary sample generated by this node, these parameters can cause additional samples to be generated around that primary sample time. This is most often used to ensure that accurate data exists at exactly the camera shutter open and close times, as well as at the primary sample time.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Shutter
parameters.description: Controls the method used to specify the shutter open and close times relative to the primary sample times. Specify Manually: The Shutter Open/Close parameter values provide exact offset values relative to the primary sample time. Use Camera Prim: The Camera Prim parameter provides the scene graph path of a camera primitive from which the shutter open and close times are extracted to provide the offset values relative to the primary time sample.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Shutter Open/Close
parameters.description: When Shutter is set to Specify Manually, these two offset values are added to the primary sample time to indicate the shutter open and close times. The open time should be less than or equal to zero, and the close time should be greater than or equal to zero.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Camera Prim
parameters.description: When Shutter is set to Use Camera Prim, this is the scene graph path of a camera prim on the input node's stage. The shutter open and close attribute values are read from this primitive.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Samples
parameters.description: The number of subframe samples to create for each primary sample. These samples are evenly distributed between the shutter open and close times. Note that such an even distribution may or may not create a sample at exactly the primary sample time.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Always Include Frame Sample
parameters.description: When turned on, forces a sample to be created at exactly the primary sample time. If the Samples value, together with the shutter open and close times, already place a sample at the primary sample time, turning on this option has no effect. Otherwise, this option causes an addition sample to be added. This means that the actual number of samples per primary sample may in fact be one more than the number specified in the Samples parameter.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Action
parameters.description: Whether this node should create new prims, or edit existing prims. In addition, the Force Edit option can be chosen to cause this node to ignore the houdini:editable attribute on prims, and always edit the specified attributes. This is in contrast to the Edit mode which will trigger a warning and not set attributes on prims with the houdini:editable attribute set to false.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.description: In Create mode, this lets you control where in the scene graph to create the prim(s). The default is usually /$OS. This creates a primitive at the root level with the same name as the node (for example, /tube1). This is a useful default for preventing naming conflicts, but terrible for organization. You should try to remember to change the Primitive Path to a better value when you create prims. For example, instead of naming models after the node that created them, you might want to name them after the geometry inside, and organize them under a /Models branch. The Create Primitives section contains basic controls for how to create the new prim(s).
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.description: In Edit mode, the node has a Primitive Pattern parameter. This lets you specify the prim(s) the node should operate on. You can click the select button beside the text box to select the primitives from the scene graph tree. You can also use primitive patterns for advanced matching, including matching all prims in a collection.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Allowed Primitive Types
parameters.description: In Edit mode, only prims that match one of the specified primitive types (or API schemas) can be modified by this node. Leave this parameter empty to permit editing any primitive type.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Handle Disallowed Types
parameters.description: In Edit mode, specifies what should happen when a primitive that is not one of the Allowed primitive types matches the primitive pattern Ignore Disallowed Prim Types: Do not set any attributes on this primitive, but do not notify the user.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Initialize Parameters
parameters.description: Changes the state of all control menu parameters to Do Nothing, so that this node will not apply any changes. Also grabs the current values of each property from the first Primitives match, and sets the values of the corresponding parameters to match. This means that changing any parameter's control menu to Set or Create mode will set the property to its current value, making it easier to apply changes to an existing value rather than setting a brand new value. With Rebuild Render-Specific Parameters you reset all parameters from render-specific tabs to their default values for the specific node. If you want to reset the parameters for the entire scene, you can also open the top-level Render menu and choose Rebuild All Render-Specific LOP Parameters.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Primitive Count
parameters.description: The number of primitives to create.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Primitive Type
parameters.description: Set all created prims to have this type.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Primitive Kind
parameters.description: Set all created prims to have this kind.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Primitive Specifier
parameters.description: The USD operator to use when creating the new prims. Define: Authors a completely new prim. Use this if you want to create a brand new prim or replace an existing prim. Over: Authors an override of an existing prim. Attributes not explicitly authored on this prim will get their values from the existing prim on the lower layer. Class: Define a primitive class. This is usually not necessary unless you are doing deep USD magic.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Class Ancestor
parameters.description: If Primitive Specifier is Define or Over, this parameter will cause some ancestor primitives to be authored with a specifier of Class. This makes it easy to create an Over or Define within a Class without having to use two separate nodes. When Primitive Specifier is Class, this parameter is disabled because the entire primitive hierarchy is already authored as Class primitives.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Parent Primitive Type
parameters.description: If any parents of a path in Primitive Paths do not exist, this node will automatically create them. In this case, it will create parent nodes of this type.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Color
parameters.description: Sets a "default" color for this shape, which will be used in the viewport if the prim does not have a shader/material. You can write shaders to take this displayColor parameter as an override.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Opacity
parameters.description: Sets the opacity of the display Color. This is a separate attribute (instead of specifying the display color as RGBA) so it can be independently overridden, and also because shaders don't usually accept RGBA parameters.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Double Sided
parameters.description: For renderers that distinguish between single-sided and double-sided surfaces, controls whether this prim is double-sided. Making surfaces double-sided is necessary for flat thin surfaces, or open surfaces where the camera can see both the inside and outside of the surface.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Transform
parameters.description: How the transform parameters below apply to the primitive. (Because each USD prim can contain multiple transforms, _and_ be affected by parent transforms, there are many different ways to apply new transforms.) Append: Apply the parameters as a new, most local transform. Prepend: Apply the parameters as a new, _least_ local transform. Overwrite or Append: If a local transform exists with the name xformOp:transform, _overwrite_ it with the parameters. Otherwise, apply it as a new, most local transform. If this replaces an existing transform, that transform's order in the local transform stack is not affected. Overwrite or Prepend: Like Overwrite or Append, but _least_ local. Apply Transform in World Space: Apply the parameters as a new, most local transform. However, prior to applying the transform, it is updated so that the result of the transform appears as if the transform was being applied in world space, before any local or ancestor transformations were applied to the primitive. Replace All Local Transforms: The transform specified in the remaining transform parameters is always applied as a new transform. Prior to applying this transform, all existing transform operations on the local transform stack are cleared so that only the supplied transform remains on the local transform stack (though ancestor transforms still have an effect). Apply XformCommonAPI: The transform specified in the remaining transform parameters will be applied as if it were appended to whatever the current transform on the prim is. But the resulting final transform will be expressed using the USD XformCommonAPI specification. Note that this specification cannot express shears, and so cannot express some transforms which may result in unexpected changes to transforms that already have shears. Apply Extended XformCommonAPI (with Shear + Pivot Rotate): The transform specified in the remaining transform parameters will be applied as if it were appended to whatever the current transform on the prim is. But the resulting final transform will be expressed using a Houdini-defined extension of the USD XformCommonAPI specification. This extension is accessible through the husd.UsdHoudini.HoudiniXformCommonAPI python class. This class provides a very similar interface to pxr.UsdGeom.XformCommonAPI but allows for shears in the transform, is able to store a pivot rotation value, and can express rotations as a quaternion if the rotations are animated. Using quaternions to express rotations avoids motion blur artifacts that can occur when using Euler angles to express the rotation.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Transform Order

entries.label: Houdini Procedural: Crowd
entries.summary: Houdini Crowd Procedural for Solaris.

parameters.label: Procedural Prim
parameters.description: The scene graph path at which to apply the HoudiniProceduralAPI ApiSchema to define the procedural. When Visualize Instances is turned on, the materials used for visualization are also authored under this path. TIP: This path can be located anywhere since the SkelRoot Primitives parameter identifies which primitives the procedural can modify. For organization, a suitable choice could be the parent primitive enclosing the crowd's SkelRoot primitives.

parameters.label: SkelRoot Primitives
parameters.description: A primitive pattern specifying the SkelRoot instances to apply the procedural to. The default pattern selects all the visible SkelRoot instances.

parameters.label: LOD Camera
parameters.description: When turned on, specifies a camera to use instead of the render camera for evaluating LOD. This can be used to produce consistent results when the viewing camera is moving.

parameters.label: LOD Threshold
parameters.description: The threshold at which the LOD optimization is used. The default value of 1.0 means that the optimization is used when the tolerance between the agent poses is less than approximately 1 pixel. Lower values can eliminate deformed geometry differences that might still be noticeable, depending on the scene. However, the lower levels could make it less likely for the LOD optimization to trigger, and may also increase the render's memory footprint.

parameters.label: Optimize Identical Poses
parameters.description: When turned on, allows foreground agents with exactly the same pose as another agent to be instanced. In most scenarios, it is rare for agents to have identical poses (for example, due to randomizing clip speeds or time offsets), so this is turned off by default to avoid unnecessary computation.

parameters.label: Offscreen Quality
parameters.description: Scales the approximate size of the agent in screen space for agents that are not directly visible to the camera. Smaller values will make offscreen agents more likely to become an instance of another agent.

parameters.label: Bake Skinning for Prototype Agents
parameters.description: When turned on, deformed geometry is generated for the SkelRoot Primitives that became prototypes for background agents. This geometry is instanced by the matching background agents as well as the prototype's original source agent. When turned off, the procedural only authors overrides for the skel:animationSource relationship to bind background agents to the same SkelAnimation primitive (skeleton pose) as their prototype agent. This produces the same final result, rendering background agents as instances of the prototype's deformed geometry, but is only supported in Hydra 2 and will not work if the USDIMAGINGGL_ENGINE_ENABLE_SCENE_INDEX environment variable is set to 0. This method can be more efficient since the procedural authors a smaller set of changes to the stage, and the deformed point positions are generated through Hydra at render time in the usual manner.

parameters.label: Bake Skinning for All Agents
parameters.description: When turned on, deformed geometry is also generated for the remaining SkelRoot Primitives that did not become an instance or prototype. This can be useful if the deformed geometry is required for subsequent procedurals. Otherwise, the deformed point positions for these agents will be generated through Hydra at render time.

parameters.label: Visualize Instances
parameters.description: When turned on, applies materials to the SkelRoot Primitives to visualize the changes made by the procedural.
parameters.heading: Visualize Instances

parameters.label: Prototype Color
parameters.description: When Visualize Instances is turned on, this is the color of the SkelRoot Primitives whose deformed geometry was used as a prototype for background primitives.
parameters.heading: Visualize Instances

parameters.label: Instance Color
parameters.description: When Visualize Instances is turned on, this is the color of the background SkelRoot Primitives that became an instance of another primitive's deformed geometry.
parameters.heading: Visualize Instances

parameters.label: Default Color
parameters.description: When Visualize Instances is turned on, this is the color of the SkelRoot Primitives that were not modified by the procedural.
parameters.heading: Visualize Instances

parameters.label: Enable Visualization
parameters.description: Controls when the visualization materials are applied to the SkelRoot Primitives. Viewport Only: The materials are only applied when previewing the procedural in the viewport using the Preview Houdini Procedurals LOP. On the other hand, when rendering normally, the materials are not enabled, and you will see the original materials. Always: The materials are always applied to the primitives. This can be used to explicitly render with the visualization enabled.
parameters.heading: Visualize Instances

entries.label: Houdini Procedural: Feather

parameters.label: Procedural Prim

TIP: You can generate velocities on the deformer using a Trail SOP. NOTE: Currently, only surface deformers are supported.

You can read current attribute values using @<<name>>, and create/update attribute values by writing to variables with the same name as the attribute. You can also use VEX USD functions to manipulate the primitive. See VEX snippets for more information.

entries.label: Houdini Procedural: Hair
entries.summary: Houdini Procedural: Haie for Solaris.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: Which mode of hair procedural to setup. Generate will produce new curves, interpolated from existing guides. Deform deforms existing render curves, using the guides.

parameters.label: Procedural Prim
parameters.description: Path of the render primitive. This prim must be directly editable on the stage.

parameters.label: Deformed Curves
parameters.description: BasisCurves primitives which are deformed by the Guide Curves.

parameters.label: Guide Curves
parameters.description: BasisCurves primitives used by the procedural to generate or deform hair.

parameters.label: Skin Prims
parameters.description: Mesh primitives used by the procedural to generate or deform hair.

parameters.label: Animated Procedural
parameters.description: Identify this procedural to be evaluated before each frame in the render, or only at the beginning of a render. If a procedural doesn't need to be re-generated on every frame of the render, you can turn this off as an optimization step.

parameters.label: Number of Hairs
parameters.description: Total number of hairs to generate on the skin surface.
parameters.heading: Hair

parameters.label: Scale by Density Attrib on Skin
parameters.label_norm: scale by density attrib on skin
parameters.description: If the character's skin has a density attribute, you can use it to drive the scale of the hair.
parameters.heading: Hair

parameters.label: Relax Iterations
parameters.description: Number of iterations to relax the hair roots onto the skin.
parameters.heading: Hair

parameters.label: Length Min Scale
parameters.description: Minimum scale to randomize the length interpolated from the guide curves.
parameters.heading: Hair

parameters.label: Length Max Scale
parameters.description: Maximum scale to randomize the length interpolated from the guide curves.
parameters.heading: Hair

parameters.label: Width Scale
parameters.description: Multiplier on the pscale copied from the Guide Curves.
parameters.heading: Hair

parameters.label: Resample Segments
parameters.description: Set the number of segments on the render curves.
parameters.heading: Hair

parameters.label: Attributes to Copy
parameters.description: Which attributes to copy from the guide curves onto the render curves.
parameters.heading: Guides

parameters.label: Influence Radius
parameters.description: The radius within which guides have influence over generated hair. See Hair Generate SOP for more details.
parameters.heading: Guides

parameters.label: Influence Decay
parameters.description: Controls how steeply the weight of a guide drops with distance. See Hair Generate SOP for more details.
parameters.heading: Guides

parameters.label: Max Guide Count
parameters.description: The maximum number of guides to take into account. Any exceeding guides found within the Influence Radius are ignored. See Hair Generate SOP for more details.
parameters.heading: Guides

parameters.label: Max Guide Angle
parameters.description: Ignore guides that face away from the skin normal at the hair root by more than this angle in degrees. See Hair Generate SOP for more details.
parameters.heading: Guides

parameters.label: Clump Crossover
parameters.description: Blends the shapes of clumps of guide hair. See Hair Generate SOP for more details.
parameters.heading: Guides

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.description: Seed to randomize the distribution of hair curves.
parameters.heading: Guides

parameters.label: NOTE
parameters.description: This tab and its associated parameter set is only visible when you set Mode to Deform.
parameters.heading: Guides

parameters.label: Deform Mode
parameters.description: Method used to deform the hair. * Skin will deform the hair using the skin only. * Capture and Deform will use the specified skin and guide curves to capture and deform the hair. * Deform - Use Existing Weights deforms the hair using capture attributes authored on the render curves using the guides.
parameters.heading: Guides

parameters.label: Split Clumps
parameters.description: For curves that are influences by the guides of multiple clumps, discards any weights that are not part of the most influential clump.
parameters.heading: Capture and Deform

parameters.label: Pick Single Best Guide
parameters.description: Discards all but the single most influential guide. This can significantly speed up deformation and can be useful for outputting quick tests. Results can potentially be good enough for the final output when the guide density is very high relative to the final hair density.
parameters.heading: Capture and Deform

parameters.label: Maximum Split Passes
parameters.description: Polygons of the skin surface are split at guide locations, adding the root point into the surface topology. For polygons containing multiple guides, this is done a guide at a time, until all guides have a point on the surface or until this maximum number of passes is reached.
parameters.heading: Capture and Deform

parameters.label: Edge Flip Passes
parameters.description: Edges are flipped to create a more uniformly distributed triangle surface, which results in smoother weights. This is a maximum number of passes to perform.
parameters.heading: Capture and Deform

parameters.label: Max Sample Count
parameters.description: Maximum number of points to interpolate from.
parameters.heading: Velocity from Guides or Skin

parameters.label: Distance Threshold
parameters.description: The maximum distance that the source guides/skin can be at to be considered.
parameters.heading: Velocity from Guides or Skin

parameters.label: Blend Width
parameters.description: Distance on top of the Distance Threshold, blending the velocity from guides/skin.
parameters.heading: Velocity from Guides or Skin

parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: When Mode is set to Generate, you can control the type of BasisCurve. Linear is polygonal, and Cubic is smoothed, depending on the selected Basis method. See BasisCurves LOP for more details.
parameters.heading: Velocity from Guides or Skin

parameters.label: Basis
parameters.description: When Mode is set to Generate, you can determine how the curve is drawn between points. See BasisCurves LOP for more details.
parameters.heading: Velocity from Guides or Skin

parameters.label: Wrap
parameters.description: When Mode is set to Generate, you can tell USD how to treat the ends of the curves. See BasisCurves LOP for more details.
parameters.heading: Velocity from Guides or Skin

parameters.label: Calculate Rest Positions for Guide Curves
parameters.label_norm: calculate rest positions for guide curves
parameters.description: Creates primvars:rest for the Guide Curves, using the current @points positions.
parameters.heading: Velocity from Guides or Skin

parameters.label: Calculate Rest Positions for Skin Prims
parameters.label_norm: calculate rest positions for skin prims
parameters.description: Creates primvars:rest for the Skin Prims, from the current @points positions.
parameters.heading: Velocity from Guides or Skin

parameters.label: Subframe Samples
parameters.description: Specifies the number of time samples to generate when executing the procedural. A value of 2 or more is required for deformation-based motion blur. Higher values will result in longer execution times for the procedural.
parameters.heading: Velocity from Guides or Skin

parameters.label: Enable Karma Velocity Blur
parameters.description: Enables the controls for setting Karma velocity blur properties on the hair and skin.
parameters.heading: Karma Velocity Blur

parameters.label: Hair Velocity Blur
parameters.description: Enables Karma velocity blur property on the hair curves.
parameters.heading: Karma Velocity Blur

parameters.label: Skin Velocity Blur
parameters.description: Enables Karma velocity blur property on the skin meshes.
parameters.heading: Karma Velocity Blur

parameters.label: Velocity Blur Mode
parameters.description: Lets you choose whether to use velocity-based motion blur, or acceleration-based motion blur. Velocity blur uses the velocities and is always linear, but is fast. Acceleration blur uses accelerations and lets you get curved motion blur, but requires three or more samples for Karma to generate smooth motion.
parameters.heading: Karma Velocity Blur

parameters.label: Acceleration Samples
parameters.description: The number of interpolation copies that Karma produces internally, using the accelerations values, to produce the smooth motion.
parameters.heading: Karma Velocity Blur

entries.label: Houdini Procedural: Ocean
entries.summary: Houdini Ocean Procedural for Solaris.

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.description: The scene graph path at which to create the ocean procedural prim.

parameters.label: Spectrum File
parameters.description: The location of the ocean spectrum file, containing one or more ocean spectra as created by the Ocean Spectrum SOP.
parameters.heading: Spectrum

parameters.label: Mask File
parameters.description: An optional animated file sequence of mask geometry that can be used to mask the ocean displacement, often created by the Particle Fluid Mask SOP SOP and set up by the Ocean Flat Tank or Guided Ocean Layer shelf tools.
parameters.heading: Spectrum

parameters.label: Time
parameters.description: The time at which the ocean surface should be evaluated.
parameters.heading: Spectrum

parameters.label: Reload Geometry
parameters.description: Force a reload of the Spectrum File geometry, which will refresh any previews of the ocean after a change to the spectrum file on disk,
parameters.heading: Spectrum

parameters.label: Render Geometry
parameters.description: The path to the geometry that will be diced and displaced by the procedural.
parameters.heading: Geometry

parameters.label: Group
parameters.description: The primitive group on the Render Geometry that should be diced and displaced.
parameters.heading: Geometry

parameters.label: Reference Render Geometry as Interior
parameters.description: Create a second USD reference to the Render Geometry that will be rendered as the ocean interior, usually using a uniform volume material to give the appearance of depth falloff within the ocean volume.
parameters.heading: Geometry

parameters.label: Viewport Quality
parameters.description: The dicing resolution for the procedural when previewing the ocean in the Solaris viewport with a Preview Houdini Procedurals LOP. NOTE: The full render quality is controlled by the main Dicing Quality parameter.
parameters.heading: Geometry

parameters.label: Dicing Quality
parameters.description: The dicing resolution of the procedural. A setting of 1 generally gives full resolution, but can be increased for more detail. If you only require more detail at the horizon, consider increasing Z Importance instead.
parameters.heading: Dicing

parameters.label: Geometry Z Measure
parameters.description: The space in which the diced ocean geometry's z-coordinate should be projected before measuring if it meets the Dicing Quality criterion. The X and Y coordinates are always in pixel space, but the Z coordinate along the camera direction can be in a different space. Camera Space: The Z coordinate is mapped to camera space, and its value will range 0 to (camera_far - camera_near). This mapping works well for most small to medium-scale scenes, and retains good detail at the horizon. However, for very large camera distances, it can lead to excessive dicing and memory usage as the geometry becomes very stretched at the horizon. Pixel Space: The Z coordinate is mapped to pixel space, and its value will range from 0 to max(xres, yres). This mapping gives more consistent dicing across widely varying scales, but might require increasing Z Importance for long camera views to keep sufficient horizon detail.
parameters.heading: Dicing

parameters.label: Z Importance
parameters.description: A scale on the mapping specified in the Geometry Z Measure parameter. Increasing this value will increase detail at distance along the horizon, generally with lower memory usage than increasing the overall Dicing Quality.
parameters.heading: Dicing

parameters.label: Screen Window Size
parameters.description: The size of the screen window. Increasing this value will extend the subdivision to the offscreen area, which is especially useful if the resulting geometry might be displaced horizontally into view.
parameters.heading: Dicing

parameters.label: Downsample
parameters.description: Downsample the incoming ocean spectra before evaluating any ocean values. This parameter specifies the number of powers of two to remove from the resolution of the incoming ocean spectrum. For example, if the spectrum was originally specified at resolution 10 to generate a 1024 x 1024 volume, downsampling by 2 will evaluate ocean volumes at resolution 8, a 256 x 256 volume.
parameters.heading: Dicing

parameters.label: Anti-Alias Blur
parameters.description: A scale on the polygon size before measuring against wavelength for anti-aliasing. Decrease its value to reduce the amount of downsampling done, or set to zero to disable completely.
parameters.heading: Dicing

parameters.label: Verbose
parameters.description: Output statistics to the console about ocean dicing, displacement, and foam splatting.
parameters.heading: Dicing

parameters.label: Surface Material
parameters.description: The material applied to the surface render geometry. The default material is a MaterialX shader that will work with many renderers that support MaterialX.
parameters.heading: Shading

parameters.label: Interior Material
parameters.description: The material applied to the interior ocean volume, usually rendered as a uniform volume to emulate depth falloff beneath the surface of the water. The default material will work with Karma CPU and XPU.
parameters.heading: Shading

parameters.label: Proxy Material
parameters.description: The material used for viewport display of the ocean surface, with some features like refraction disabled.
parameters.heading: Shading

parameters.label: Point Velocity
parameters.description: Generate a velocities primvar that can be used for shading or motion blur.
parameters.heading: Shading

parameters.label: Cusp Min/Max
parameters.description: When enabled, the procedural will generate a cusp primvar that can be used for shading and/or displacement of the procedural surface. The Cusp Min/Max parameter remaps the specified cusp range to 0-1.
parameters.heading: Shading

parameters.label: Cusp Gamma
parameters.description: Applies a gamma curve to the cusp value after remapping according to Cusp Min/Max.
parameters.heading: Shading

parameters.label: Cusp Intensity
parameters.description: A multiplier applied to the cusp value after remapping and gamma scaling.
parameters.heading: Shading

parameters.label: Foam Particles
parameters.description: An optional animated file sequence of foam particles that can be used to create a foam primvar on the ocean for shading and/or displacement of the procedural surface.
parameters.heading: Shading

parameters.label: Radius Scale
parameters.description: A scale on the particle radius applied before looking up foam particles around a shading point. Increase this value and decrease Alpha to smooth out the look of the foam.
parameters.heading: Foam Pattern

parameters.label: Alpha
parameters.description: The amount of opacity each particle will contribute. Increase this value for a thicker foam layer.
parameters.heading: Foam Pattern

parameters.label: Filter Width
parameters.description: How much to filter the streak pattern to avoid aliasing artifacts when viewed from a distance.
parameters.heading: Foam Pattern

parameters.label: Foam Min/Max
parameters.description: When enabled, the procedural will generate a foam primvar that can be used for shading and/or displacement of the procedural surface. The Foam Min/Max parameter remaps the specified foam range to 0-1.
parameters.heading: Foam Pattern

parameters.label: Foam Gamma
parameters.description: Applies a gamma curve to the foam value after remapping according to Foam Min/Max.
parameters.heading: Foam Pattern

parameters.label: Foam Intensity
parameters.description: A multiplier applied to the foam value after remapping and gamma scaling.
parameters.heading: Foam Pattern

parameters.label: Direction
parameters.description: The direction in which to stretch the Frequency to stretch out the foam in that direction. Setting this to the prevailing wind direction or wind direction plus 90 degrees can give interesting effects.
parameters.heading: Streaks

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.description: The amount of Frequency stretching to do along the streak Direction.
parameters.heading: Streaks

parameters.label: Sharpness
parameters.description: How sharp the edges of the foam are. High values will create a sharper more web-like pattern, low values will create a softer, rounder pattern.
parameters.heading: Streaks

parameters.label: Frequency
parameters.description: The frequency of the streak pattern.
parameters.heading: Streaks

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.description: How much to offset the streak pattern.
parameters.heading: Streaks

parameters.label: Frequency
parameters.description: The frequency of the bubble pattern.
parameters.heading: Bubbles

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.description: How much to offset the bubble pattern.
parameters.heading: Bubbles

parameters.label: Cusp Displacement
parameters.description: The diced ocean surface will be displaced in the normal direction by the output cusp primvar scaled by this amount.
parameters.heading: Displacement

parameters.label: Foam Displacement
parameters.description: The diced ocean surface will be displaced in the normal direction by the output foam primvar scaled by this parameter.
parameters.heading: Displacement

By default, piecename is used. NOTE: The primvar on the mesh should contain only the local piece name (for example, piece0-0, piece0-1, piece0-2). Geometry Blur: The procedural is sampled multiple times, generating geometric motion samples for geometry-based motion blur.
