parameters.heading: Sky

parameters.label: Horizon Blur Falloff
parameters.description: The angle in degrees below horizon where the sky and the ground color are blended to blur the horizon.
parameters.heading: Sky

parameters.label: Enable Sky Light
parameters.description: Creates the sky Karma Sky Dome Light LOP in the scene.
parameters.heading: Sky

parameters.label: Intensity
parameters.description: A linear scale on the power output of the light.
parameters.heading: Base

parameters.label: Exposure
parameters.description: Scales the power output exponentially as a power of 2, similar to an F-stop control. 0 maintains the adjusted Intensity, negative numbers scale Intensity down by the square, positive numbers scale Intensity up. You typically set Intensity to what looks like the right amount of light, and then use this parameter to fine-tune it.
parameters.heading: Base

parameters.label: Color
parameters.description: The color of the light, in energy-linear terms.
parameters.heading: Base

parameters.label: Diffuse Multiplier
parameters.description: Scales the effect of the light on the diffuse response of shaders. This is a non-physical "tweak".
parameters.heading: Base

parameters.label: Specular Multiplier
parameters.description: Scales the effect of the light on the specular response of shaders. This is a non-physical "tweak".
parameters.heading: Base

parameters.label: Render Light Geometry
parameters.description: An override for the global Render Light Geometry parameter. Force Disable: Don't render the light's geometry even when the main Render Light Geometry parameter is turned _on_. Force Enable: Render the light's geometry even when the main Render Light Geometry parameter is turned _off_. Use Global Control: The default choice uses the setting of the equally named parameter from the node's main section.
parameters.heading: Base

parameters.label: MIS Bias
parameters.description: Controls whether multiple importance sampling will sample from the BSDF, the light, or both the BSDF and light.
parameters.heading: Sampling

parameters.label: Sampling Mode
parameters.description: When using the light tree for rendering, Karma will try to put any light source that’s compatible into the tree. This option can force a light to be excluded from the tree and subject to uniform sampling, which can sometimes yield an improved sampling quality the light at the expense of speed.
parameters.heading: Sampling

parameters.label: Sampling Quality
parameters.description: This is the per-light sampling quality, that acts as a multiplier on the global Light Sampling Quality. Increasing the quality will add additional samples for this light source, improving the sampling quality of this light relative to other light sources.
parameters.heading: Sampling

parameters.label: Contributions
parameters.description: Provides detailed control over which BSDF component the light affects.
parameters.heading: Light

parameters.label: LPE Tag
parameters.description: Custom label assigned to lights or objects for use with light path expression.
parameters.heading: Light

parameters.label: Scatter
parameters.description: This parameter is multiplied by Scale and creates a Rayleigh scattering coefficient for each color channel representing the amount of light that is scattered by pure air.
parameters.heading: Rayleigh

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: Multiplier for Rayleigh Scatter.
parameters.heading: Rayleigh

parameters.label: Distribution
parameters.description: Controls, how fast the air density falls off with increasing altitude. This parameter is measured in kilometers and multiplied by Unit Scale. For example, with the default of 8 km and a Unit Scale of 1000, air density is 37% at 8000 units above sea level. Distribution uses Nishita's exponential decay model (referred to as "Scale Height" in literature) for calculating air density.
parameters.heading: Rayleigh

parameters.label: Scatter
parameters.description: This parameter is multiplied by Scale and creates a Mie scattering coefficient for each color channel representing the amount of light that is scattered by aerosols.
parameters.heading: Mie

parameters.label: Scatter Scale
parameters.description: Multiplier for Mie Scatter.
parameters.heading: Mie

parameters.label: Absorption
parameters.description: This parameter is multiplied by Absorption Scale and creates a Mie absorption coefficient for each color channel representing the amount of light that is absorbed by aerosols.
parameters.heading: Mie

parameters.label: Absorption Scale
parameters.description: Multiplier for Mie Absorption.
parameters.heading: Mie

parameters.label: Distribution
parameters.description: Controls, how fast the air density falls off with increasing altitude. This parameter is measured in kilometers and multiplied by Unit Scale. For example, with the default of 8 km and a Unit Scale of 1000, air density is 37% at 8000 units above sea level. Distribution uses Nishita's exponential decay model (referred to as "Scale Height" in literature) for calculating air density.
parameters.heading: Mie

parameters.label: Phase
parameters.description: Phase ranges from -1 to 1 and covers full back scatter to full forward scatter. Scattering represents the atmosphere's anisotropy. Aniostropy means that rays don't propagate evenly in all directions.
parameters.heading: Mie

parameters.label: Absorption
parameters.description: This parameter is multiplied by Scale and creates an ozone absorption coefficient for each color channel representing the amount of light that is scattered by the ozone layer.
parameters.heading: Ozone

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: Multiplier for ozone Absorption.
parameters.heading: Ozone

parameters.label: Altitude
parameters.description: The maximum ozone density/absorption is reached at the parameter's value given in kilometers measured from the Earth's surface. The value is multiplied by Unit Scale. For example, at an Altitude of 8 km and a Unit Scale of 1000, the final value will be 8000.
parameters.heading: Ozone

parameters.label: Width
parameters.description: This value indicates the total height range in kilometers at which ozone absorbs (sun)light. Absorption reaches its maximum at the Altitude parameter's value. Note, that Width is multiplied by Unit Scale. For example, when Width is 10 km and Unit Scale is 1000, the final value will be 10000.
parameters.heading: Ozone

parameters.label: Ground Albedo
parameters.description: The ground reflectivity that affects the sky color (when multiple scattering is turned on), as well as its appearance in primary and bounce rays.
parameters.heading: Ground

parameters.label: Ground Visibility
parameters.description: Controls visibility of the ground depending on different types of rays. For instance, you may not want the ground to be visible in the camera, but still want the sky and indirect bounce rays from underside of clouds (and other geometry) to be affected by the ground color. You can use one of the following expressions *: Visible to both primary and indirect bounce rays. primary: Visible to primary rays only. -primary: Visible to indirect bounce rays only.
parameters.heading: Ground

parameters.label: Planet Center
parameters.description: This parameter is multiplied by Unit Scale and represents the position where the planetary atmosphere is centered around. Planet Center is measured in kilometers.
parameters.heading: Geometry

parameters.label: Sea Level
parameters.description: This parameter is multiplied by Unit Scale and represents the distance from the Planet Center in which the atmosphere starts. Sea Level is measured in kilometers.
parameters.heading: Geometry

parameters.label: Unit Scale
parameters.description: Multiplier to every parameter in Karma Sky Atmosphere that represents position or distance.
parameters.heading: Geometry

parameters.label: LPE Tag
parameters.description: Custom label assigned to atmospheric volume for use with Light Path Expressions.
parameters.heading: Sampling

parameters.label: Minimum Stepsize
parameters.description: This parameter is multiplied by Unit Scale and represents the minimum distance between samples when marching through atmosphere. Reducing this parameter can help eliminate banding artifacts when modeling a particularly thick atmosphere, but at extra cost.
parameters.heading: Sampling

parameters.label: Maximum Stepsize
parameters.description: This parameter is multiplied by Unit Scale represents the maximum distance between samples when marching through atmosphere. We recommend leaving Maximum Stepsize at 5 to 10 times the value of Minimum Stepsize.
parameters.heading: Sampling

parameters.label: Multi Scatter Limit
parameters.description: Specifies, how often an atmospheric ray can propagate through the atmosphere. NOTE: Increasing depth will impact render times. A depth of 1 or 2 is typically enough for the realistic appearance of a clear sky on Earth, with diminishing returns beyond that. A limit of 1 or greater is required if Ground Albedo should have an effect on the color of the sky.
parameters.heading: Sampling

parameters.label: Internal Color Space
parameters.description: Scatter and absorption coefficients are interpreted in the OpenColorIO color space specified by this parameter, and transformed into scene_linear (i.e. working space) when computing transmittance. Leave it empty to apply no transformation. This can help in preserving the look if the lookdev for the atmosphere was done in a different color space than the project's working space (however, due to the nature of RGB rendering, it can never be an exact match).
parameters.heading: Advanced

parameters.label: LUT Resolution
parameters.description: X and Y resolution for the transmittance table. The X axis corresponds to the light angle, and the Y axis corresponds to the viewer's altitude. With appropriate settings, there is no need to deviate from the default settings. An exception is if there are huge differences between the Distribution or ozone Altitude parameters. In this case it can help to increase the Y resolution to avoid bias.
parameters.heading: Advanced

parameters.label: Ground Offset
parameters.description: Distance between ground level and sea level. Ground is modeled as a sphere with radius calculated as Sea Level - Ground Offset. You can set this parameter to values greater than zero to lower the ground and avoid discontinuity artifacts from objects crossing ground level. As a consequence, you'll see a vacuum between the atmosphere and the ground which may be noticeable near horizon. We recommend leaving this parameter at 0 and keeping the rest of the scene above Sea Level instead.
parameters.heading: Advanced

parameters.label: Ground Receives Shadows
parameters.description: Allow ground elements to receive shadows (i.e. cast shadow rays).
parameters.heading: Advanced

parameters.label: Render Backside Atmosphere
parameters.description: Allows rendering of the atmosphere on the other side of the planet.
parameters.heading: Advanced

parameters.label: Solid Alpha in IPR
parameters.description: Set alpha to 1 in IPR mode. Turned on by default to avoid misleading appearance due to compositing against light viewport background.
parameters.heading: Advanced

parameters.label: Ignore Camera Far Clip
parameters.description: Ignore camera's far clip distance when computing atmospheric contribution on primary rays. This allows correct appearance of the sky without having to increase camera's far clip distance to encompass the entire atmosphere.
parameters.heading: Advanced

parameters.label: Sky Prim Name
parameters.description: The name of the Karma Sky Dome Light LOP prim.
parameters.heading: Advanced

parameters.label: Sun Prim Name
parameters.description: The name of the Distant Light LOP prim.
parameters.heading: Advanced

parameters.label: Sun Light Map
parameters.description: The look-up table used by the node, to give the sun light the correct color and intensity.
parameters.heading: Advanced

parameters.label: Up Axis
parameters.description: The up-axis of the light.
parameters.heading: Advanced

entries.label: Karma Procedural
entries.summary: Sets up render-time instantiation for Karma.

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.description: Create a primitive at this path in the scene graph tree. This creates an Xform prim with attributes that tell Karma what to do at render time. The Xform prim contains the generated point geometry as a USD Points prim.

parameters.label: Procedurals
parameters.description: This node can create multiple render-time point replacements. Set the number of replacements, or click the plus and minus buttons to add or remove replacements.

parameters.label: Group
parameters.description: Specify the points in the generated geometry you want to replace. This can be the name of a point group, or space-separated group syntax. For example, 0 1 2 5-7 to select points by point number.

parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: What to replace the selected points with at render time. Sphere: Replace the points with spheres. File: Replace each point with geometry loaded from a file. Karma supports loading all file formats understood by Houdini. VDB Iso Surface: Replace each point with a VDB iso-surface loaded from a file.

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: When Type is Sphere, the radius of the sphere. If the point has scale or pscale SOP attributes, those values are multiplied by this. If you turn this off, the default radius is 1.

parameters.label: Use VEXpressions
parameters.description: When Type is Sphere, set the radius of each sphere using a VEX snippet. Write the radius into the radius float variable. You can use the variables typically available to an Attribute Wrangle SOP. The current point number is available as @ptnum.

parameters.label: Color
parameters.description: When Type is Sphere, set the displayColor of each sphere. If the point has a Cd SOP attribute, that value is multiplied by this. If you turn this off, the default color is 1.0, 1.0, 1.0.

parameters.label: Use VEXpressions
parameters.description: When Type is Sphere, set the color of each sphere using a VEX snippet. Write the radius into the color vector variable. You can use the variables typically available to an Attribute Wrangle SOP. The current point number is available as @ptnum.

parameters.label: File
parameters.description: When Type is File, the file path to the geometry file to instantiate at render time. Karma supports loading all file formats understood by Houdini.

parameters.label: VDB File
parameters.description: When Type is VDB Iso Surface, the file path to the VDB file to instantiate at render time.

entries.label: Karma Render Products
entries.summary: Create multiple render products sharing common settings.

parameters.label: Parent Primitive Path
parameters.description: Here you can define the path where in the Scene Graph Tree your AOVs will appear.

parameters.label: Default Ordered Render Vars
parameters.description: The list of render vars (AOVs) the render products will use by default.
parameters.heading: Common Settings

parameters.label: Default Camera
parameters.description: The path of the camera to use by default.
parameters.heading: Common Settings

parameters.label: Output Colorspace
parameters.description: The default OCIO color space for Render Vars. Normally this will be determined by the OCIO file rules and should not be required.
parameters.heading: Common Settings

parameters.label: Render Products
parameters.description: Specify the number of render products to create.
parameters.heading: Render Products

parameters.label: Enable
parameters.description: Enable this particular instance of render products.
parameters.heading: Render Products

parameters.label: Name
parameters.description: The name of the render product prim to be created under /Render/Products.
parameters.heading: Render Products

parameters.label: Product Name
parameters.description: Specify the name that the output/display driver should give the product. This is provided as-authored to the driver, whose responsibility is to situate the product on a filesystem or other storage, in the desired location.
parameters.heading: Render Products

parameters.label: Ordered Render Vars
parameters.description: When enabled, this particular instance of render products will use this list of render vars (AOVs).
parameters.heading: Render Products

parameters.label: Camera
parameters.description: When enabled, this particular instance of render products will use this camera.
parameters.heading: Render Products

parameters.label: Output Colorspace
parameters.description: The specific OCIO color space for this Render Var. Normally this will be determined by the OCIO file rules and should not be required.
parameters.heading: Render Products

entries.label: Karma Render Settings
entries.summary: Configure Render Settings for Karma.

parameters.label: Render Settings Primitive Path
parameters.description: This node creates a RenderSettings prim with the configuration you set up using the parameters. This is the scene tree path where this node will create the RenderSettings prim.

parameters.label: Output Picture
parameters.description: An output image filename (usually an .EXR file), or ip which renders the image in MPlay. Include $F in the file name to insert the frame number. This is necessary when rendering animation. See expressions in file names for more information.

parameters.label: Camera
parameters.description: Path to a USD camera (UsdGeomCamera) prim to render the scene from.

parameters.label: Resolution Mode
parameters.description: Use the USD Camera's aperture aspect ratio to automatically set one dimension of the resolution. The computed parm is set using an expression, but is locked to prevent accidental edits. Manual: Set the resolution height and width values. Set Width, Compute Height from Aperture: Set the width size, while height is computed from the width and the camera aspect ratio. Set Height, Compute Width from Aperture: Set the height size, while width is computed from the width and the camera aspect ratio.

parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.description: The horizontal and vertical size of the output image, in pixels.

parameters.label: Rendering Engine
parameters.description: Select the rendering engine. CPU: Runs entirely on the CPU. Since this engine is entirely in software, it will _generally_ have more features and more correct output, however it is much slower than the XPU engine. XPU: The XPU engine uses available CPU and GPU (graphics card hardware) resources. Since this engine inherits the limits of what can be done on a GPU, it will _generally_ lag behind the CPU engine in features, however it is much faster than the CPU engine.

parameters.label: Simplified Shading
parameters.description: Disable all shading and lighting (render with one headlight on the camera). This might be useful for preview purposes if a shaded view is too slow to render.

parameters.label: Primary Samples
parameters.description: The number of ray-samples sent through each pixel. More samples will result in a less noisy image. Pixel Samples and Primary Samples are the same.

parameters.label: Path Traced Samples
parameters.description: The number of ray-samples sent through each pixel when using the path traced convergence mode. More samples will result in a less noisy image.

parameters.label: Min Secondary Samples
parameters.description: Minimum number of rays to cast in per-component variance anti-aliasing.
parameters.heading: Secondary

parameters.label: Max Secondary Samples
parameters.description: Maximum number of rays to cast in per-component variance anti-aliasing.
parameters.heading: Secondary

parameters.label: Diffuse Quality
parameters.description: This parameter acts as a multiplier on Min Secondary Samples and Max Secondary Samples for indirect diffuse component.
parameters.heading: Indirect Samples Quality

parameters.label: Reflection Quality
parameters.description: This parameter acts as a multiplier on Min Secondary Samples and Max Secondary Samples for indirect reflect component.
parameters.heading: Indirect Samples Quality

parameters.label: Refraction Quality
parameters.description: This parameter acts as a multiplier on Min Secondary Samples and Max Secondary Samples for indirect refract component.
parameters.heading: Indirect Samples Quality

parameters.label: Volume Quality
parameters.description: This parameter acts as a multiplier on Min Secondary Samples and Max Secondary Samples for indirect volume component.
parameters.heading: Indirect Samples Quality

parameters.label: SSS Quality
parameters.description: This parameter acts as a multiplier on Min Secondary Samples and Max Secondary Samples for the SSS component.
parameters.heading: Indirect Samples Quality

parameters.label: Light Sampling Mode
parameters.description: Whether Karma should perform uniform sampling of lights or whether rendering should use the light tree. The light tree can be significantly faster for scenes that have large numbers of lights. Some lights cannot be added to the light tree, and will all be sampled by Karma
parameters.heading: Lights Quality

parameters.label: Light Sampling Quality
parameters.description: This is a global control to improve sampling quality for all lights. This acts as a multiplier on the individual light quality controls. Increasing the quality will improve direct light sampling as well as shadows/occlusion.
parameters.heading: Lights Quality

parameters.label: Diffuse Limit
parameters.description: The number of times diffuse rays can propagate through your scene.
parameters.heading: Volumes and Opacity

parameters.label: Volume Limit
parameters.description: The number of times a volumetric ray can propagate through a scene. It functions in a similar fashion to the Diffuse Limit parameter.
parameters.heading: Volumes and Opacity

parameters.label: SSS Limit
parameters.description: The number of times a SSS ray can propagate through a scene. It functions in a similar fashion to the Diffuse Limit parameter. This is a float because all limits are stochastically picked per-sample, so for example you can set the diffuse limit to 3.25 and have 25% of the rays with a diffuse limit of 4 and 75% of rays with a diffuse limit of 3.
parameters.heading: Volumes and Opacity

parameters.label: Color Limit
parameters.description: The maximum value a shading sample is allowed to contribute to an LPE image plane to reduce appearance of "fireflies" caused by undersampling of extremely bright light sources. Note that reducing this value can result in an overall reduction in the amount of light in your scene.
parameters.heading: Volumes and Opacity

parameters.label: Shared Color Limit
parameters.description: When turned on, indirect bounces use Color Limit value and Indirect Color Limit parameter is ignored.
parameters.heading: Volumes and Opacity

parameters.label: Indirect Color Limit
parameters.description: Color limit applied to indirect bounce only. Note that this parameter is ignored unless Shared Color Limit is turned off.
parameters.heading: Volumes and Opacity

parameters.label: Russian Roulette Cutoff Depth
parameters.description: Depth at which indirect rays start to get stochastically pruned based on ray throughput.
parameters.heading: Volumes and Opacity

parameters.label: Enable Depth of Field
parameters.description: Turn on the depth of field rendering.
parameters.heading: Camera Effects

parameters.label: Enable Motion Blur
parameters.description: Whether to turn on motion blur. Changing this in the display options will require a restart of the render.
parameters.heading: Camera Effects

parameters.label: Per-object Motion Blur
parameters.description: Whether motion blur should be on or off for objects that don't explicitly have an opinion. If this is On by default, the parameters below let you set the defaults.
parameters.heading: Camera Effects

parameters.label: Transform Time Samples
parameters.description: The number of samples to compute when rendering _transformation_ motion blur over the shutter open time. The default is 2 samples (at the start and end of the shutter time), giving one blurred segment.
parameters.heading: Camera Effects

parameters.label: Geometry Time Samples
parameters.description: The number of sub-frame samples to compute when rendering _deformation_ motion blur over the shutter open time. The default is 1 (sample only at the start of the shutter time), giving *no* deformation blur by default. If you want rapidly deforming geometry to blur properly, you must increase this value to 2 or more. Note that this value is limited by the number of sub-samples available in the USD file being rendered. An exception to this is the USD Skel deformer which allows. "Deformation" may refer to simple transformations at the Geometry (SOP) level, or actual surface deformation, such as a character or object which changes shape rapidly over the course of a frame.
parameters.heading: Camera Effects

parameters.label: Velocity Blur
parameters.description: This parameter lets you choose what type of _geometry velocity blur_ to do on an object, if any. Separate from _transform blur_ and _deformation blur_, you can render motion blur based on point movement, using attributes stored on the points that record change over time. You should use this type of blur if the number points in the geometry changes over time (for example, a particle simulation where points are born and die). If your geometry changes topology frame-to-frame, Karma will not be able to interpolate the geometry to correctly calculate Motion Blur. In these cases, motion blur can use a velocities and/or accelerations attribute which is consistent even while the underlying geometry is changing. The surface of a fluid simulation is a good example of this. In this case, and other types of simulation data, the solvers will automatically create the velocity attribute. NOTE: In Solaris, velocities, accelerations, and angularVelocities attributes are equivalent to v, accel, and w in SOPs, respectively. No Velocity Blur: Do not render motion blur on this object, even if the renderer is set to allow motion blur. Velocity Blur: To use velocity blur, you must compute and store point velocities in a point attribute velocities. The renderer uses this attribute, if it exists, to render velocity motion blur (assuming the renderer is set to allow motion blur). The velocities attribute may be created automatically by simulation nodes (such as particle DOPs), or you can compute and add it using the Point velocity SOP. The velocities attribute value is measured in Houdini units per second. Acceleration Blur: To use acceleration blur, you must compute and store point acceleration in a point attribute accelerations. The renderer uses this attribute, if it exists, to render multi-segment acceleration motion blur (assuming the renderer is set to allow motion blur). The accel attribute may be created automatically by simulation nodes, or you can compute and add it using the Point velocity SOP. When Acceleration Blur is on, if the geometry has a _angular velocity_ attribute (w), rapid rotation will also be blurred. This should be a vector attribute, where the components represent rotation speeds in radians per second around X, Y, and Z.
parameters.heading: Camera Effects

parameters.label: Instance Velocity Blur
parameters.description: When defining motion blur on instances, the transform of each instance can be blurred in addition to any motion blur occurring on the prototype. This option controls how the instance will compute the motion blur of the transform on each instance. For example, when instancing prototypes to a particle system, you'd likely want to use velocity blur to compute motion blur (the transform on the prototype would be blurred by the velocity on the particles). No Velocity Blur: Use deformation blur of the instance to compute the blur on the transform. Velocity Blur: To use velocity blur, the instance must be a point instancer with a velocities attributes on the points, or a native instance with a v primvar. The velocities attribute (or v primvar) value is measured in Houdini units per second. Acceleration Blur: To use acceleration blur, the instance must be a point instancer with point velocities and acceleration values. The renderer uses this attribute, if it exists, to render multi-segment acceleration motion blur (assuming the renderer is set to allow motion blur). The accel attribute may be created automatically by simulation nodes, or you can compute and add it using the Point velocity SOP; this will be converted to accelerations when the SOP geometry is converted to USD.
parameters.heading: Camera Effects

parameters.label: Instance Motion Samples
parameters.description: When motion blur on instances is computed using Acceleration Blur or Deformation Blur, this parameter specifies the number of motion segments used for motion blur.
parameters.heading: Camera Effects

parameters.label: Motion Blur Style
parameters.description: Defines the type of motion blur. The default Rotation Blur is suited for most applications, esp. spinning wheels or rotor blades, but also almost any other type of motion. Linear Blur is only required in very rare cases.
parameters.heading: Camera Effects

parameters.label: Instance Velocity Blur Scale
parameters.description: Velocity multiplier used to reduce or exaggerate amount of motion blur on volumes.
parameters.heading: Camera Effects

parameters.label: Disable Image Blur
parameters.description: If you turn this off, Karma still calculates velocities (and the velocities can be stored in an AOV), but it sends all camera rays at shutter open, so the image will not have any apparent motion blur. This may be useful if you simply don't want any motion blur to create a certain visual effect.
parameters.heading: Camera Effects

parameters.label: Render Points as
parameters.description: When rendering point clouds, they can be rendered as camera oriented discs, spheres or discs oriented to the normal attribute.
parameters.heading: Geometry and Shading

parameters.label: Render Curves as
parameters.description: When rendering curves, they can be rendered as ribbons oriented to face the camera, rounded tubes or ribbons oriented to the normal attribute attached to the points.
parameters.heading: Geometry and Shading

parameters.label: Override Curve Basis
parameters.description: USD supports Curve Basis types that may not be supported directly in Houdini. In some cases, you may want to override the Houdini curve basis. For example, if you have linear curves in Houdini, you may want to render them with a Bezier, B-Spline or Catmull-Rom basis. This menu will force Karma to override the basis that's tied to the USD primitives. Note that the topology of the curves must match the target basis. For example, when selecting any cubic curve basis, every curves must have at least 4 vertices. For the Bezier basis, curves must have 4+3*N vertices.
parameters.heading: Geometry and Shading

parameters.label: Cull Backfaces
parameters.description: If enabled, geometry that are facing away from the camera are not rendered.
parameters.heading: Geometry and Shading

parameters.label: Enable Caustics
parameters.description: Allows evaluation of glossy BSDF that's seen by indirect diffuse bounce. This is a brute-force solution which may require significant number of diffuse rays to resolve, especially if Caustics Roughness Clamp parameter is set to very small value or Indirect Guiding feature is disabled.
parameters.heading: Geometry and Shading

parameters.label: Caustics Roughness Clamp
parameters.description: Increasing this value can make caustics less noisy at the cost of accuracy. NOTE: Roughness clamp only works with GGX BSDF and may not have any effect with Phong, cone, or specular BSDFs.
parameters.heading: Geometry and Shading

parameters.label: Ray Bias
parameters.description: The minimum distance used when testing if _secondary rays_ from a surface intersect with other objects in the scene. The distance is measure from surface along the direction of the ray. Objects within the ray bias distance are ignored.
parameters.heading: Shading

parameters.label: Constrain by Maximum Roughness
parameters.description: Roughness parameter in GGX BSDFs are clamped by the maximum roughness value propagated down the ray chain in pathtracing. Enabling this option can cut out a lot of noise in indirect specular (in particular, cases where glossy surface is reflected by a rough specular surface) at the cost of a bit of accuracy.
parameters.heading: Shading

parameters.label: Automatic Headlight Creation
parameters.description: If there are no lights in the scene, a headlight is created by default. To disable, turn off this checkbox.
parameters.heading: Shading

parameters.label: Dicing Camera
parameters.description: Specifies a camera that is used for dicing complicated surfaces. This can provide consistent dicing of surfaces when the viewing camera is moving.
parameters.heading: Dicing

parameters.label: Offscreen Quality
parameters.description: This parameter controls the shading quality scale factor for geometry that is not directly visible to the camera. For geometry that is outside the field of view (i.e. visible only to secondary rays), karma will smoothly reduce the shading quality based on the angle between the geometry and the edge of the viewing frustum. Smaller values can increase performance particularly in scenes where the camera is within the displacement bound of nearby geometry, where it permits the hidden primitives to be diced more coarsely than those that are directly visible.
parameters.heading: Dicing

parameters.label: Dicing Quality Scale
parameters.description: This parameter is a global multiplier for dicing quality of all objects.
parameters.heading: Dicing

parameters.label: Import Render Vars from Second Input
parameters.label_norm: import render vars from second input
parameters.description: Finds RenderVar prims in this node's second input and adds them to this stage, so they add to the list of render vars to generate. This allows other LOP nodes (such as Background Plate) to "offer" render vars related to that node to be generated.
parameters.heading: AOVs (Render Vars)

parameters.label: Import Render Products from Second Input
parameters.label_norm: import render products from second input
parameters.description: Finds RenderProduct prims in this node's second input and adds them to this stage, so they add to the list of products to generate. This allows other LOP nodes to "offer" products related to that node to be generated.
parameters.heading: AOVs (Render Vars)

parameters.label: Pixel Filter
parameters.description: Controls the distribution of pixel samples. Box uses a uniform distribution inside each pixel. Gaussian, Blackman, and Blackman-Harris use smooth, bell-shaped weightings around the pixel center. Box: A uniform distribution inside each pixel Gaussian: A Gaussian distribution with a standard deviation of 0.5 Blackman: A Blackman distribution with a radius of 1.5 Blackman-Harris: A Blackman-Harris distribution with a radius of 1.8
parameters.heading: AOVs (Render Vars)

parameters.label: Pixel Filter Scale
parameters.description: Scales the default size of the pixel filter. Larger values like 2 blur, smaller values like 0.5 or 0.25 sharpen.
parameters.heading: AOVs (Render Vars)

parameters.label: The following checkbox is available next to each common render var
parameters.label_norm: the following checkbox is available next to each common render var
parameters.heading: AOVs (Render Vars)

parameters.label: Split Per LPE Tag
parameters.description: When this is on, the renderer creates additional AOVs specific to each tagged light. To manage LPE Tags for lights, use the LPE Tag LOP.
parameters.heading: AOVs (Render Vars)

parameters.label: Name

parameters.label: Format
parameters.description: The data format that should be used when saving this image plane to the output file. This value is also passed to the render delegate when it allocates the render buffer for the AOV.

parameters.description: Whether the render buffer should be multi-sampled. This value is also passed to the render delegate when it allocates the render buffer for the AOV.

parameters.label: Clear Value
parameters.description: The initial value to fill the buffer with before rendering. Usually this is 0, however for example for Pz you might set it to 1e17. This value is also passed to the render delegate when it allocates the render buffer for the AOV.
parameters.heading: Render Vars

parameters.label: Data Type
parameters.description: The USD data type of the render variable. When saving to OpenEXR files, the data type is used to determine the channel names. For example, if the data type is color3f, the channel names will be R, G, B, while if the data type is normal3f, the channel names will be x, y, z. TIP: If you're rendering with husk and want color channel names to be lower case (for example r, g, b), add another Render Var LOP and use it to set the driver:parameters:aov:husk:channel_lower_rgb (bool) render var to true.
parameters.heading: Render Vars

parameters.label: Source Name
parameters.description: Where to get the render variable contents. See Source Type below. The renderer should look for an output with this name as the computed value for the RenderVar. TIP: In Karma, with Raw and Primvar (including Cryptomatte) Source Type, it's possible to prefix variable name with noholdouts; to indicate that matte or background holdouts should *not* contribute to the AOV. For example, to output normal N AOV without holdouts, enter: ray:noholdouts;N
parameters.heading: Render Vars

parameters.label: Source Type
parameters.description: How to interpret the Source Name parameter. Raw: Pass the source name directly to the renderer. This assumes the renderer knows how to interpret the source name string. This is the default. Primvar: The Source Name is the name of primvar. Some renderers may use this to ensure that the primvar is provided to the renderer. Other renderers may require that a suitable material network be provided, in which case this is simply an advisory setting. LPE: The Source Name is a Light Path Expression. (Some renderers may accept extensions to the OSL Light Path Expression syntax, which will necessarily be non-portable.) Intrinsic: *Currently not implemented*. In the future, USD may provide for a portable list of baseline render vars, such as camera depth, that would be implemented by all renderers.

parameters.description: Choose a denoiser to run on the finished image output, or No Denoiser. This utility currently supports Intel Open Image Denoise (included with Houdini) and the NVIDIA OptiX Denoiser (must be installed separately). You must be on a supported platform and have the chosen denoising library installed for this to work. TIP: You can also run the Intel OIDN exclusively on the CPU using the idnoise tool's --oidn-cpu option, for example idenoise --oidn-cpu input.exr output.exr. This will prevent OIDN from failing when it's running out of VRAM.
parameters.heading: Image Filters

parameters.label: Use Albedo
parameters.description: Some denoising libraries can use albedo to get a better sense of the image, guiding how and where it reduces noise.

parameters.label: Use N Input
parameters.description: Some denoising libraries can use normals to get a better sense of the image, guiding how and where it reduces noise.
parameters.heading: Image Filters

parameters.label: AOVS
parameters.description: Space-separated list of AOVs to run the denoiser on.
parameters.heading: Image Filters

parameters.label: Tone Map
parameters.description: The basic idea behind tone mapping is the conversion from HDR real world luminances to LDR display values, i.e. for making images displayable on monitors. Another aspect is to simulate a particular film look. Film material is designed to have a certain "response" to light to enhance contrast and colors, represented as a characteristic curve. A filmic tone mapping curve is subdivided into toe, shoulder and linear sections for an image's dark, bright, and mid tones. Houdini provides several common operators for filmic tone mapping and each operator applies a specific S-shaped tone mapping curve. * Reinhard, Ward and Aces don't provide any further parameters to adjust the toe, shoulder and linear sections. * Hable, Hable2 and Unreal, however, have specific parameters for customizing the curve. TIP: The external links below provide more information about tone mapping * Unreal * Hable2 * ACES
parameters.heading: Image Filters

parameters.label: Tonemap Curve
parameters.description: Tone map curves apply to the Reinhard, Unreal, Aces and Hable operators. The curve is a visual representation of the mathematical model of each operator. You can fine-tune tone mapping through the curve's control points.
parameters.heading: Image Filters

parameters.label: AOVs
parameters.description: Space-separated list of AOVs that will be affected by the chosen Tone Map operator.
parameters.heading: Image Filters

parameters.label: Toe
parameters.description: This parameter applies to the Hable, Hable2 and Unreal operators and ranges between 0 and 1. The default values for Hable and Hable2 is 0.5. For Unreal, the default value is 0.55. The value controls the strength (curvature) of the toe segment in dark areas. Higher values create a darker image, smaller values brighten the dark tones.
parameters.heading: Image Filters

parameters.label: Shoulder
parameters.description: This parameter applies to the Hable, Hable2 and Unreal operators and ranges between 0and 1. The default values for Hable and Hable2 is 0.5. For Unreal, the default value is 0.26. Shoulder controls to curve's amount of curvature for bright tone values. The value affects where the shoulder curve starts in the graph: a value of 1 means that the shoulder starts exactly where the toe ends.
parameters.heading: Image Filters

parameters.label: Slope
parameters.description: This parameter applies to the Unreal operator and ranges between 0 and 1. The default value is 0.88. Controls the tone mapping curve's steepness, where higher settings (steeper curve) make the image darker and increase contrast; smaller values brighten the image and make it pale.
parameters.heading: Image Filters

parameters.label: Linear
parameters.description: This parameter applies to the Hable operator and ranges between 0 and 2. The default value is 0.3. Tones in the linear section should not (or hardly) change during the tone mapping process and represent the image's original tones. The Linear value describes the distance between toe and shoulder. Higher values mean that the tow and shoulder sections become smaller, while more tones remain unchanged: the overall curve becomes more linear.
parameters.heading: Image Filters

parameters.label: Linear Angle
parameters.description: This parameter applies to the Hable operator and ranges between 0 and 1. The default value is 0.1. Here you control the slope of the linear part of the tone mapping curve.
parameters.heading: Image Filters

parameters.label: Toe Length
parameters.description: This parameter applies to the Hable2 operator and ranges between 0 and 1. The default value is 0.5. A small value creates a short toe section that quickly transitions into the linear section. A value of 0 eliminates the toe, and value of 1 means the toe takes up half the curve. Note that there are two ways to disable the toe: you can either set Toe Length or Toe to 0.
parameters.heading: Image Filters

parameters.label: Shoulder Length
parameters.description: This parameter applies to the Hable2 operator and ranges between 0 and 1. The default value is 0.5. Shoulder Length describes how many F stops you want to add to the dynamic range of the curve. Here you control the transition point from the linear section to the shoulder section.
parameters.heading: Image Filters

parameters.label: Shoulder Angle
parameters.description: This parameter applies to the Hable2 operator and ranges between 0 and 1. The default value is 1. Here you control how much overshoot you want to add the curve's shoulder.
parameters.heading: Image Filters

parameters.label: OCIO
parameters.description: OCIO image filters can be added to various render vars/image planes.
parameters.heading: Image Filters

parameters.label: Enable
parameters.description: Enables the OCIO image filter defined below.
parameters.heading: Image Filters

parameters.label: Planes
parameters.description: The render var names to which the OCIO image filter will be applied.

parameters.label: Output Space
parameters.description: Specify the OCIO color output space the image filter will apply.
