parameters.label: Render Vars
parameters.description: Use this multiparm to add custom AOVs (render vars) to the image output.
parameters.heading: Extra Render Vars

parameters.label: Name
parameters.description: The name of the AOV in the output image that stores the data from this render var.
parameters.heading: Render Var

parameters.label: Format
parameters.description: The data format that should be used when saving this image plane to the output file. This value is also passed to the render delegate when it allocates the render buffer for the AOV.
parameters.heading: Render Var

parameters.label: Multi Sampled
parameters.description: Whether the render buffer should be multi-sampled. This value is also passed to the render delegate when it allocates the render buffer for the AOV.
parameters.heading: Render Var

parameters.label: Clear Value
parameters.description: The initial value to fill the buffer with before rendering. Usually this is 0, however for example for Pz you might set it to 1e17. This value is also passed to the render delegate when it allocates the render buffer for the AOV.
parameters.heading: Render Var

parameters.label: Data Type
parameters.description: The USD data type of the render variable. When saving to OpenEXR files, the data type is used to determine the channel names. For example, if the data type is color3f, the channel names will be R, G, B, while if the data type is normal3f, the channel names will be x, y, z. TIP: If you're rendering with husk and want color channel names to be lower case (for example r, g, b), add another Render Var LOP and use it to set the driver:parameters:aov:husk:channel_lower_rgb (bool) render var to true.
parameters.heading: Render Var

parameters.label: Source Name
parameters.description: Where to get the render variable contents. See Source Type below. The renderer should look for an output with this name as the computed value for the RenderVar. TIP: In Karma, with Raw and Primvar (including Cryptomatte) Source Type, it's possible to prefix variable name with noholdouts; to indicate that matte or background holdouts should *not* contribute to the AOV. For example, to output normal N AOV without holdouts, enter: ray:noholdouts;N
parameters.heading: Render Var

parameters.label: Source Type
parameters.description: How to interpret the Source Name parameter. Raw: Pass the source name directly to the renderer. This assumes the renderer knows how to interpret the source name string. This is the default. Primvar: The Source Name is the name of primvar. Some renderers may use this to ensure that the primvar is provided to the renderer. Other renderers may require that a suitable material network be provided, in which case this is simply an advisory setting. LPE: The Source Name is a Light Path Expression. (Some renderers may accept extensions to the OSL Light Path Expression syntax, which will necessarily be non-portable.) Intrinsic: *Currently not implemented*. In the future, USD may provide for a portable list of baseline render vars, such as camera depth, that would be implemented by all renderers.
parameters.heading: Render Var

parameters.label: Sample Blending
parameters.description: You can use Solaris filter syntax in this parameter to blend the sample values. The default "ubox", {} simply averages all the sample values within each pixel.
parameters.heading: Karma

parameters.label: Cryptomatte
parameters.description: Enable this to turn this image plane into Cryptomatte layer. See Cryptomatte for more info.
parameters.heading: Karma

parameters.label: Overlap Limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of IDs that can be stored in a single pixel. A value of 6 is recommended.
parameters.heading: Karma

parameters.label: Manifest File
parameters.description: Optional external manifest file. It will be saved into same directory as the render product. If this path is unspecified, the manifest will be embedded into render product as metadata.
parameters.heading: Karma

parameters.label: Output Colorspace
parameters.description: Specify the OCIO color output space for the component.
parameters.heading: Karma

parameters.label: Utility Path Expression
parameters.description: Using the same syntax as Light Path Expressions, this determines at what path vertex (ie scattering event) to write out the utility AOV. The default is CO meaning it gets written out from the first hit from the initial camera ray. Another example is C<TG>O which means to write out the AOV from the next hit after the first refration event (which would write out the AOV from behind the first layer of refraction). With C(<T>.O)O you can create a Crypotmatte that shows refractive _and_ non-refractive rays together. This only works for Raw, Primvar and ShaderExport (ie via kma_aov) AOV types. Note: Beware that this writes out value of the last vertex that matches the expression without any regards to ray throughput, so the look can be affected by sampling odds of indirect rays. For example, Automatic convergence mode may look very different from Path Traced convergence mode under karma CPU.
parameters.heading: Karma

parameters.label: Add Holdout Shadows To Beauty
parameters.description: This will add a holdout_shadow shadow AOV to Karma but also tell Karma that the shadow information from holdout objects should be written into the Alpha of the beauty AOV. This disables the more sophisticated Background Plate LOP workflow, but is a quick way to get shadow catchers to affect the beauty image.
parameters.heading: Shadow Catcher

parameters.label: Holdout Shadow Alpha
parameters.description: Controls the strength of the shadows AOV written by holdout objects.
parameters.heading: Shadow Catcher

parameters.label: Automatically Create Required COP Image Filter AOVs
parameters.label_norm: automatically create required cop image filter aovs
parameters.description: Some Image Filters require depth, normal or albedo inputs. When turned on, Karma generates these AOVs (unless there's an existing RenderVar). The created AOVs will not be saved to the resulting render products.
parameters.heading: Shadow Catcher

parameters.label: COP Image Filter Lists
parameters.description: An ordered list of Image Filter primitives which will be run by husk before saving the image.
parameters.heading: Shadow Catcher

parameters.label: Denoiser
parameters.description: Choose a denoiser to run on the finished image output, or No Denoiser. This utility currently supports Intel Open Image Denoise (included with Houdini) and the NVIDIA OptiX Denoiser (must be installed separately). You must be on a supported platform and have the chosen denoising library installed for this to work. The NVIDIA OptiX Denoiser only works with NVIDIA cards. It is now included with the NVIDIA driver (version 435 or later). Karma uses a blue noise distribution. This noise type works better with denoisers, because it has randomization only in high frequencies, while some other noise have randomization in all frequencies. When blue noise is blurred, the high frequency noise is removed and leaves the lower frequencies of the image intact.
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters

parameters.label: Use Albedo
parameters.description: Some denoising libraries can use albedo to get a better sense of the image, guiding how and where it reduces noise.
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters

parameters.label: Use N Input
parameters.description: Some denoising libraries can use normals to get a better sense of the image, guiding how and where it reduces noise.
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters

parameters.label: AOVS
parameters.description: Space-separated list of AOVs to run the denoiser on.
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters

parameters.label: Create Separate Denoised AOVs
parameters.description: When you turn on this option, Karma will create separate AOVs for the denoised versions of the source AOVs. Each new AOV will have a _denoise suffix.
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters

parameters.label: Use CPU Only
parameters.description: Some denoising libraries can run on CPU or GPU. Normally, the denoiser will use the fastest device. This option will force the denoiser to choose the CPU device. You can use this option to minimize GPU memory requirements, for example when denoising large images or rendering on GPU-enabled farm machines.
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters

parameters.label: Tone Map
parameters.description: The basic idea behind tone mapping is the conversion from HDR real world luminances to LDR display values, i.e. for making images displayable on monitors. Another aspect is to simulate a particular film look. Film material is designed to have a certain "response" to light to enhance contrast and colors, represented as a characteristic curve. A filmic tone mapping curve is subdivided into toe, shoulder and linear sections for an image's dark, bright, and mid tones. Houdini provides several common operators for filmic tone mapping and each operator applies a specific S-shaped tone mapping curve. * Reinhard, Ward and Aces don't provide any further parameters to adjust the toe, shoulder and linear sections. * Hable, Hable2 and Unreal, however, have specific parameters for customizing the curve. TIP: The external links below provide more information about tone mapping * Unreal * Hable2(Filmic curve by John Hable. Based on the original version from the "Filmic Tonemapping for Real-time Rendering") * ACES(Krzysztof Narkowicz aprox. of ACES filmic curve)
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters

parameters.label: Tonemap Curve
parameters.description: Tone map curves apply to the Reinhard, Unreal, Aces and Hable operators. The curve is a visual representation of the mathematical model of each operator. You can fine-tune tone mapping through the curve's control points.
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters

parameters.label: AOVs
parameters.description: Space-separated list of AOVs that will be affected by the chosen Tone Map operator.
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters

parameters.label: Toe
parameters.description: This parameter applies to the Hable, Hable2 and Unreal operators and ranges between 0 and 1. The default values for Hable and Hable2 is 0.5. For Unreal, the default value is 0.55. The value controls the strength (curvature) of the toe segment in dark areas. Higher values create a darker image, smaller values brighten the dark tones.
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters

parameters.label: Shoulder
parameters.description: This parameter applies to the Hable, Hable2 and Unreal operators and ranges between 0and 1. The default values for Hable and Hable2 is 0.5. For Unreal, the default value is 0.26. Shoulder controls to curve's amount of curvature for bright tone values. The value affects where the shoulder curve starts in the graph: a value of 1 means that the shoulder starts exactly where the toe ends.
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters

parameters.label: Slope
parameters.description: This parameter applies to the Unreal operator and ranges between 0 and 1. The default value is 0.88. Controls the tone mapping curve's steepness, where higher settings (steeper curve) make the image darker and increase contrast; smaller values brighten the image and make it pale.
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters

parameters.label: Linear
parameters.description: This parameter applies to the Hable operator and ranges between 0 and 2. The default value is 0.3. Tones in the linear section should not (or hardly) change during the tone mapping process and represent the image's original tones. The Linear value describes the distance between toe and shoulder. Higher values mean that the tow and shoulder sections become smaller, while more tones remain unchanged: the overall curve becomes more linear.
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters

parameters.label: Linear Angle
parameters.description: This parameter applies to the Hable operator and ranges between 0 and 1. The default value is 0.1. Here you control the slope of the linear part of the tone mapping curve.
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters

parameters.label: Toe Length
parameters.description: This parameter applies to the Hable2 operator and ranges between 0 and 1. The default value is 0.5. A small value creates a short toe section that quickly transitions into the linear section. A value of 0 eliminates the toe, and value of 1 means the toe takes up half the curve. Note that there are two ways to disable the toe: you can either set Toe Length or Toe to 0.
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters

parameters.label: Shoulder Length
parameters.description: This parameter applies to the Hable2 operator and ranges between 0 and 1. The default value is 0.5. Shoulder Length describes how many F stops you want to add to the dynamic range of the curve. Here you control the transition point from the linear section to the shoulder section.
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters

parameters.label: Shoulder Angle
parameters.description: This parameter applies to the Hable2 operator and ranges between 0 and 1. The default value is 1. Here you control how much overshoot you want to add the curve's shoulder.
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters

parameters.label: OCIO
parameters.description: OCIO image filters can be added to various render vars/image planes.
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters

parameters.label: Enable
parameters.description: Enables the OCIO image filter defined below.
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters

parameters.label: Planes
parameters.description: The render var names to which the OCIO image filter will be applied.
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters

parameters.label: Output Space
parameters.description: Specify the OCIO color output space the image filter will apply.
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters

parameters.label: Input Space
parameters.description: In most cases this should be left at data. There may be some strange case where the source of the AOV is already in a defined color space, in which case you can specify the source space here.
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters

parameters.label: Looks
parameters.description: Space-separated list of looks to apply to the finished image. A "look" is a named OCIO color transform, usually intended to achieve an artistic effect. See the OCIO documentation for more information.
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters

parameters.label: Aspect Ratio Conform Policy
parameters.description: What to do if the aspect ratio of the output image (Resolution width divided by height) doesn't match the aspect ratio of the camera aperture (controlled by attributes on the camera). This allows a standard renderer to do something reasonable when you switch between cameras. Expand Aperture: If necessary, expand the camera aperture to match the image. Crop Aperture: If necessary, crop the camera aperture to match the image. Adjust Aperture Width: If necessary, change the camera aperture width to match the image. Adjust Aperture Height: If necessary, change the camera aperture height to match the image. Adjust Pixel Aspect Ratio: Change the aspect ratio of the image to match the camera.
parameters.heading: Aspect Ratio

parameters.label: Data Window NDC
parameters.description: Directs the renderer to only render within this window of the entire output image. You specify the window as minX, minY, maxX, maxY, where each number is a normalized value from 0 to 1. 0, 0 is the bottom left, 1, 1 is the top right, 0.5, 0.5 is the center, and so on. The default is 0, 0, 1, 1 (no cropping). Note that you can use _negative_ values. For example, -0.1, -0.1, 1.1, 1.1 will give you 10% overscan on each side. There's also an associated dropdown menu with several preadjusted percentage values. You can use this window to temporarily _crop_ the render to a smaller region, for testing purposes. Pixels are only rendered if they are _fully_ inside the window. The normalized coordinates map to the image _after_ any adjustments by the Aspect ratio conform policy.
parameters.heading: Aspect Ratio

parameters.label: Pixel Aspect Ratio
parameters.description: The aspect ratio (width/height) of image _pixels_ (_not_ the image itself). The default is 1.0, indicating square pixels.
parameters.heading: Aspect Ratio

parameters.label: Artist
parameters.description: The name of the person, department, or studio that created the image file. The node will set this field on the output image if the image format supports metadata (for example, .exr).
parameters.heading: Metadata

parameters.label: Comment
parameters.description: An arbitrary comment, for example a description of the purpose of the output image. The node will set this field on the output image if the image format supports metadata (for example, .exr).
parameters.heading: Metadata

parameters.label: Hostname
parameters.description: The name of the computer that generated this the output file. The node will set this field on the output image if the image format supports metadata (for example, .exr).
parameters.heading: Metadata

parameters.label: EXR Compression
parameters.description: Sets the compression for saved OpenEXR files. When saving multi-part OpenEXR files, you can specify compression per AOV through a Render Var LOP.
parameters.heading: Metadata

parameters.label: Custom Metadata
parameters.description: Add additional custom metadata that husk will save to render products.
parameters.heading: Metadata

parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: The type of metadata (string, integer, float, or color).
parameters.heading: Metadata

parameters.label: Key
parameters.description: The key for the metadata. This should be a unique name used to identify the metadata. TIP: If you want the metadata to be written out specifically for a single format, you can prefix the metadata key with the Houdini format identifier, for example OpenEXR:metadata_key.
parameters.heading: Metadata

parameters.label: Value
parameters.description: The value of the metadata.
parameters.heading: Metadata

parameters.label: Deep Camera Map
parameters.description: Generate a deep camera map image recording depth. Deep camera maps are rendered images, where semi-transparent areas (such as volumes) between the camera and the nearest opaque surface are stored with depth information. Each pixel in the image is represented as a curve describing how the transparency value changes across the depth of the scene. This allows you to composite rendered images and have the semi-transparent areas blend correctly according to their depth.
parameters.heading: Metadata

parameters.label: DCM Filename
parameters.description: The filename to save the deep camera map image to (this should be an .exr file). Include $F in the file name to insert the frame number. This is necessary when rendering animation. See expressions in file names for more information.
parameters.heading: Metadata

parameters.label: DCM Render Vars
parameters.description: Space separated list of RenderVar _prim paths_ (_not_ a list of AOV names). These must be the fully qualified path to the RenderVar prim and the render var name. You can use patterns to match multiple prims. The default is /Render/Products/Vars/*, which matches all prims in the branch where Houdini usually creates RenderVar prims. You can also leave this field empty to omit all RenderVars and only include alpha and depth planes (like a Deep Shadow Map).
parameters.heading: Metadata

parameters.label: DCM Compression
parameters.description: Compression value between 0 and 10. Used to limit the number of samples which are stored in a lossy compression mode for volume samples. The compression parameter determines the maximum possible error in scalar channels for each sample. For compression greater than 0, the following relationship holds: Error = 1/(2^(10-compression))
parameters.heading: Metadata

parameters.label: DCM Of Size
parameters.description: Opacity is usually computed as a full-color value and stored as such. To cut down on file size, if full color is not needed, this settings can be used to store a monochromatic version of the full color value. Set this value to 1 for monochrome, 3 for full color.
parameters.heading: Metadata

parameters.label: DCM Z-Bias
parameters.description: Used in compression to merge together samples which are closer than the given threshold. Samples that are closer together than this bias value are merged into a single sample whose Z-front and Z-back span encompasses all the merged samples.
parameters.heading: Metadata

parameters.label: Set as Default Render Settings Prim
parameters.label_norm: set as default render settings prim
parameters.description: A layer in USD can define a default render settings primitive for husk or other tools to use when rendering.
parameters.heading: Metadata

parameters.label: Convergence Mode
parameters.description: When set to Path Traced, maximum of 1 indirect ray is generated per bounce. When set to Automatic, the number of indirect rays is calculated based on initial noise estimate, target noise threshold, and the maximum number of camera rays. Also note that under Automatic mode, number ofsamples for direct lighting is adjusted based on noise estimate as well.
parameters.heading: Metadata

parameters.label: Pixel Oracle
parameters.description: When rendering, a Pixel Oracle tells karma which pixels need additional sampling and which pixels are converged. This parameter tells karma which oracle to use. Uniform: Uniformly distribute rays to each pixel. Each pixel will always get the same number of ray-samples. Variance: Distribute rays based on variance in the rendered image.
parameters.heading: Primary Samples

parameters.label: Minimum Samples
parameters.description: The minimum number of camera rays (primary samples) for each pixel.
parameters.heading: Primary Samples

parameters.label: Planes
parameters.description: Space separated list of AOVs used to measure variance (using summed pixel value of the AOVs). Typically only beauty AOV is needed, but when rendering holdout beauty or holdout shadows alongside beauty, you may want to include those AOVs to the list in order to prevent holdouts from getting undersampled.
parameters.heading: Primary Samples

parameters.label: Variance Threshold
parameters.description: The amount of variance that triggers more rays.
parameters.heading: Primary Samples

parameters.label: Random Seed
parameters.description: Variance sampling involves some randomness. You can change this number to get slightly different results.--->
parameters.heading: Primary Samples

parameters.label: OCIO Transform
parameters.description: Whether to apply an OCIO transform to the pixels before measuring variance. Disabled: Do not apply an OCIO transform. Display View: Transform to the color space of a display. Explicit: Transform to a named color space.
parameters.heading: Primary Samples

parameters.label: Display
parameters.description: When OCIO Transform is Display View, the display to transform to before measuring variance.
parameters.heading: Primary Samples

parameters.label: View
parameters.description: When OCIO Transform is Display View, the view to transform to before measuring variance.
parameters.heading: Primary Samples

parameters.label: Color Space
parameters.description: When OCIO Transform is Explicit, the color space to transform to before measuring variance.
parameters.heading: Primary Samples

parameters.label: Noise Level
parameters.description: Noise threshold to determine the number of indirect rays cast for indirect bounce when the Convergence Mode is set to Automatic. Decreasing this threshold (for example, to 0.001) will theoretically send more indirect rays and decrease noise, however the "extra" rays will likely be cancelled out by the Max Ray Samples parameter. The correct way to decrease noise is to increase the Primary Samples rather than changing this threshold. If you are using Variance Pixel Oracle, you should set the same value for both threshold parameters. Setting the oracle's threshold lower may make the indirect component reach its threshold sooner and cast fewer indirect rays, but the oracle decides to cast more expensive camera rays because the amount of final noise in the beauty pass is higher than the oracle's threshold.
parameters.heading: Secondary Samples

parameters.label: Enable Indirect Guiding
parameters.description: When turned on, Karma does a pre-render to roughly estimate of the light in the scene, and uses that to guide indirect diffuse rays, rather than just relying on the BSDF sampling distribution. This can improve "difficult" lighting (for example, caustics, and mostly indirect lighting), but can make "easy" lighting noisier. Before using this, you can try rendering direct and indirect AOVs to see where the noise is. If the noise is mostly caused by the direct lighting, there's no point in turning on path guiding.
parameters.heading: Secondary Samples

parameters.label: Output Checkpoint Files
parameters.description: When this is on, Karma will periodically write out image tile data to a checkpoint file. If the process is terminated before completing the render, you can resume it by turning on Resume from Checkpoint and restarting.
parameters.heading: Secondary Samples

parameters.label: Checkpoint File
parameters.description: When Output checkpoint files is on, the name of the checkpoint file to write to. The default ($HIP/render/$HIPNAME.$OS.$F4.checkpoint) puts the checkpoint file inside a render directory next to the current scene file, and includes the base name of the current scene file ($HIPNAME), this node's name ($OS), and the render frame ($F) in the filename to help avoid two processes trying to use the same checkpoint file at the same time.
parameters.heading: Secondary Samples

parameters.label: Save Frequency
parameters.description: When Output checkpoint files is on, Karma waits this number of seconds between writing out a checkpoint file. The default is 60.
parameters.heading: Secondary Samples

parameters.label: Resume From Checkpoint
parameters.description: If this is on and you start a render and the renderer notices there is a valid checkpoint file, it will try to resume rendering from that checkpoint. If you want to restart the render from the beginning, you can turn this off or just delete the checkpoint file(s).
parameters.heading: Secondary Samples

parameters.label: Image Mode
parameters.description: Determines how the image will be rendered. Progressive: The entire image will be progressively rendered, so the whole image resolves at the same time. This mode gives you a sense of what the whole image will look like without waiting for the render to complete. Bucket: Each bucket renders to completion before advancing to the next bucket. This mode lets you see what the final quality will be like without waiting for the whole image to render. This mode isn't available with Enable Indirect Guiding turned on.
parameters.heading: Secondary Samples

parameters.label: Progressive Passes
parameters.description: When rendering in bucket mode (see imagemode), this is the number of progressive passes over the image to perform before switching to bucket mode.
parameters.heading: Secondary Samples

parameters.label: Bucket Size
parameters.description: Karma breaks down an image into multiple buckets for rendering. This is the side length (in pixels) of the square bucket. The default is 32, specifying a 32 pixel x 32 pixel bucket. Threads operate at the bucket level, so it might be useful to lower the bucket size if there are only a few buckets that are particularly expensive. That way the expensive areas can be divided across more threads. For example, if the image is mostly empty, but there's a distant object that fits within single 32 x 32 bucket, then that object will only be rendered using 1 thread. If you switch to a 16 x 16 bucket, then the object might be split across 4 buckets and have 4 threads working on it. Ideally changing the bucket size doesn't change the results, but Karma measures variance across pixels within the current bucket, so if you set it to a low value, for example 4, Karma only has 4 x 4 = 16 pixels to look at, so Karma will tend to make very poor variance estimates. This can show up as black pixels, where pixel rendering terminated prematurely due to a bad variance estimate.
parameters.heading: Secondary Samples

parameters.label: Bucket Order
parameters.description: Specifies which buckets are rendered first. Values can be Middle: Buckets start from the middle of the image. Top: Buckets at the top of the image are rendered first. Bottom: Buckets at the bottom of the image are rendered first. Left: Buckets at the left side of the image are rendered first. Right: Buckets at the right side of the image are rendered first. NOTE: When rendering to Mplay, the user can click to focus on an area to render. Click to focus is not available with Enable Indirect Guiding turned on.
parameters.heading: Secondary Samples

parameters.label: Cache Limit
parameters.description: Whether to use a fixed size cache (karma:global:cachesize) or whether to use a proportion of physical memory (karma:global:cacheratio).
parameters.heading: Secondary Samples

parameters.label: Cache Memory Ratio
parameters.description: The proportion of physical memory Karma will use for its unified cache. For example, with the default vm_cacheratio of 0.25 and 16 Gb of physical memory, Karma will use 4 Gb for its unified cache. The unified cache stores dynamic, unloadable data used by the render including the following
parameters.heading: Secondary Samples

parameters.label: Cancel Render if Missing Texture is Discovered
parameters.label_norm: cancel render if missing texture is discovered
parameters.description: Turning on this option will cause Karma to stop the render with an error if it encounters a missing texture map
parameters.heading: Secondary Samples

parameters.label: Cancel Render on No Working GPU Devices
parameters.label_norm: cancel render on no working gpu devices
parameters.description: Turning on this option will cause Karma to stop the render with an error if no working GPU devices are discovered.
parameters.heading: Secondary Samples

parameters.label: Export Componetents
parameters.description: A space-separated list of shading component names that will be computed for export. If you have defined new component labels in your materials, these can be added to the list so that they are exported for per-component export planes. If you are not using some components, remove them from the list to improve render efficiency. PBR light exports assume that this list is complete - that is, all components created by shaders are listed. If there are unlisted components, light exports may be missing illumination from these components.
parameters.heading: Secondary Samples

parameters.label: Diffuse Components
parameters.description: A space-separated list of component types that will behave like diffuse bounces. This will affect which reflection scope is used based on the ray type and also which bounce limit to use. Not categorized component types are assumed to be reflections.
parameters.heading: Secondary Samples

parameters.label: Refract Components
parameters.description: A space-separated list of component types that will behave like refract bounces. This will affect which reflection scope is used based on the ray type and also which bounce limit to use. Not categorized component types are assumed to be reflections.
parameters.heading: Secondary Samples

parameters.label: Volume Components
parameters.description: A space-separated list of component types that will behave like volume bounces. This will affect which reflection scope is used based on the ray type and also which bounce limit to use. Not categorized component types are assumed to be reflections.
parameters.heading: Secondary Samples

parameters.label: SSS Components
parameters.description: A space-separated list of component types that will behave like subsurface scatter bounces. This will affect which reflection scope is used based on the ray type and also which bounce limit to use. Not categorized component types are assumed to be reflections.
parameters.heading: Secondary Samples

entries.label: Karma Sky Atmosphere
entries.summary: Creates or edits a Karma Sky Atmosphere.

parameters.label: Sampling Behavior
parameters.description: Cooking this node can generate many USD time samples, rather than just a single time sample at the current time. This can be equivalent to having a Cache LOP following this node, but it will evaluate much faster, and does not cache data from any other nodes. This allows animated data to be authored to USD without introducing a node time dependency which would then cause all following nodes to also be time dependent. This can vastly improve playback performance of some LOP Networks. In all sampling modes, if a parameter on this node does not vary with time, and does not rely on other time sampled data from the stage, only a single default value will be generated in USD for the corresponding attribute. USD time samples are only generated for parameters that may vary over time. Sample Current Frame: A single time sample will be generated for the current time. Sample Frame Range If Input Is Not Time Dependent: If the input to this node is time dependent, this node behaves as if it is in Sample Current Frame mode. Otherwise it behaves as if it is in Sample Frame Range mode. Sample Frame Range: The Start/End/Inc parameter is used to generate multiple times at which this node's parameters are evaluated, and a USD time sample is created for each attribute at each one of these times.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Start/End/Inc
parameters.description: When the Sampling behavior is Sample Frame Range, this parameter controls the number and spacing of base time samples to be generated by this node. The default values of this parameter are @fstart, @fend, and @finc. These values correspond to the start, end, and step size of the global Houdini animation settings when interacting with Houdini. When using a ROP node to generate a range of frames, these values correspond to the start, end, and increment values specified on the ROP node being executed. This default ensures that a USD file written to disk will contain time samples for exactly the frame range requested by the ROP (regardless of the Houdini animation settings).
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Subframe Sampling
parameters.description: For each primary sample generated by this node, these parameters can cause additional samples to be generated around that primary sample time. This is most often used to ensure that accurate data exists at exactly the camera shutter open and close times, as well as at the primary sample time.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Shutter
parameters.description: Controls the method used to specify the shutter open and close times relative to the primary sample times. Specify Manually: The Shutter Open/Close parameter values provide exact offset values relative to the primary sample time. Use Camera Prim: The Camera Prim parameter provides the scene graph path of a camera primitive from which the shutter open and close times are extracted to provide the offset values relative to the primary time sample.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Shutter Open/Close
parameters.description: When Shutter is set to Specify Manually, these two offset values are added to the primary sample time to indicate the shutter open and close times. The open time should be less than or equal to zero, and the close time should be greater than or equal to zero.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Camera Prim
parameters.description: When Shutter is set to Use Camera Prim, this is the scene graph path of a camera prim on the input node's stage. The shutter open and close attribute values are read from this primitive.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Samples
parameters.description: The number of subframe samples to create for each primary sample. These samples are evenly distributed between the shutter open and close times. Note that such an even distribution may or may not create a sample at exactly the primary sample time.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Always Include Frame Sample
parameters.description: When turned on, forces a sample to be created at exactly the primary sample time. If the Samples value, together with the shutter open and close times, already place a sample at the primary sample time, turning on this option has no effect. Otherwise, this option causes an addition sample to be added. This means that the actual number of samples per primary sample may in fact be one more than the number specified in the Samples parameter.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Action
parameters.description: Whether this node should create new prims, or edit existing prims. In addition, the Force Edit option can be chosen to cause this node to ignore the houdini:editable attribute on prims, and always edit the specified attributes. This is in contrast to the Edit mode which will trigger a warning and not set attributes on prims with the houdini:editable attribute set to false.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.description: In Create mode, this lets you control where in the scene graph to create the prim(s). The default is usually /$OS. This creates a primitive at the root level with the same name as the node (for example, /tube1). This is a useful default for preventing naming conflicts, but terrible for organization. You should try to remember to change the Primitive Path to a better value when you create prims. For example, instead of naming models after the node that created them, you might want to name them after the geometry inside, and organize them under a /Models branch. The Create Primitives section contains basic controls for how to create the new prim(s).
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.description: In Edit mode, the node has a Primitive Pattern parameter. This lets you specify the prim(s) the node should operate on. You can click the select button beside the text box to select the primitives from the scene graph tree. You can also use primitive patterns for advanced matching, including matching all prims in a collection.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Allowed Primitive Types
parameters.description: In Edit mode, only prims that match one of the specified primitive types (or API schemas) can be modified by this node. Leave this parameter empty to permit editing any primitive type.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Handle Disallowed Types
parameters.description: In Edit mode, specifies what should happen when a primitive that is not one of the Allowed primitive types matches the primitive pattern Ignore Disallowed Prim Types: Do not set any attributes on this primitive, but do not notify the user.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Initialize Parameters
parameters.description: Changes the state of all control menu parameters to Do Nothing, so that this node will not apply any changes. Also grabs the current values of each property from the first Primitives match, and sets the values of the corresponding parameters to match. This means that changing any parameter's control menu to Set or Create mode will set the property to its current value, making it easier to apply changes to an existing value rather than setting a brand new value. With Rebuild Render-Specific Parameters you reset all parameters from render-specific tabs to their default values for the specific node. If you want to reset the parameters for the entire scene, you can also open the top-level Render menu and choose Rebuild All Render-Specific LOP Parameters.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Scatter
parameters.description: This parameter is multiplied by Scale and creates a Rayleigh scattering coefficient for each color channel representing the amount of light that is scattered by pure air.
parameters.heading: Rayleigh

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: Multiplier for Rayleigh Scatter.
parameters.heading: Rayleigh

parameters.label: Distribution
parameters.description: Controls, how fast the air density falls off with increasing altitude. This parameter is measured in kilometers and multiplied by Unit Scale. For example, with the default of 8 km and a Unit Scale of 1000, air density is 37% at 8000 units above sea level. Distribution uses Nishita's exponential decay model (referred to as "Scale Height" in literature) for calculating air density.
parameters.heading: Rayleigh

parameters.label: Scatter
parameters.description: This parameter is multiplied by Scale and creates a Mie scattering coefficient for each color channel representing the amount of light that is scattered by aerosols.
parameters.heading: Mie

parameters.label: Scatter Scale
parameters.description: Multiplier for Mie Scatter.
parameters.heading: Mie

parameters.label: Absorption
parameters.description: This parameter is multiplied by Absorption Scale and creates a Mie absorption coefficient for each color channel representing the amount of light that is absorbed by aerosols.
parameters.heading: Mie

parameters.label: Absorption Scale
parameters.description: Multiplier for Mie Absorption.
parameters.heading: Mie

parameters.label: Distribution
parameters.description: Controls, how fast the air density falls off with increasing altitude. This parameter is measured in kilometers and multiplied by Unit Scale. For example, with the default of 8 km and a Unit Scale of 1000, air density is 37% at 8000 units above sea level. Distribution uses Nishita's exponential decay model (referred to as "Scale Height" in literature) for calculating air density.
parameters.heading: Mie

parameters.label: Phase
parameters.description: Phase ranges from -1 to 1 and covers full back scatter to full forward scatter. Scattering represents the atmosphere's anisotropy. Aniostropy means that rays don't propagate evenly in all directions.
parameters.heading: Mie

parameters.label: Absorption
parameters.description: This parameter is multiplied by Scale and creates an ozone absorption coefficient for each color channel representing the amount of light that is scattered by the ozone layer.
parameters.heading: Ozone

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: Multiplier for ozone Absorption.
parameters.heading: Ozone

parameters.label: Altitude
parameters.description: The maximum ozone density/absorption is reached at the parameter's value given in kilometers measured from the Earth's surface. The value is multiplied by Unit Scale. For example, at an Altitude of 8 km and a Unit Scale of 1000, the final value will be 8000.
parameters.heading: Ozone

parameters.label: Width
parameters.description: This value indicates the total height range in kilometers at which ozone absorbs (sun)light. Absorption reaches its maximum at the Altitude parameter's value. Note, that Width is multiplied by Unit Scale. For example, when Width is 10 km and Unit Scale is 1000, the final value will be 10000.
parameters.heading: Ozone

parameters.label: Ground Albedo
parameters.description: The ground reflectivity that affects the sky color (when multiple scattering is turned on), as well as its appearance in primary and bounce rays.
parameters.heading: Ground

parameters.label: Ground Visibility
parameters.description: Controls visibility of the ground depending on different types of rays. For instance, you may not want the ground to be visible in the camera, but still want the sky and indirect bounce rays from underside of clouds (and other geometry) to be affected by the ground color. You can use one of the following expressions *: Visible to both primary and indirect bounce rays. primary: Visible to primary rays only. -primary: Visible to indirect bounce rays only.
parameters.heading: Ground

parameters.label: Planet Center
parameters.description: This parameter is multiplied by Unit Scale and represents the position where the planetary atmosphere is centered around. Planet Center is measured in kilometers.
parameters.heading: Geometry

parameters.label: Sea Level
parameters.description: This parameter is multiplied by Unit Scale and represents the distance from the Planet Center in which the atmosphere starts. Sea Level is measured in kilometers.
parameters.heading: Geometry

parameters.label: Unit Scale
parameters.description: Multiplier to every parameter in Karma Sky Atmosphere that represents position or distance.
parameters.heading: Geometry

parameters.label: LPE Tag
parameters.description: Custom label assigned to atmospheric volume for use with Light Path Expressions.
parameters.heading: Sampling

parameters.label: Minimum Stepsize
parameters.description: This parameter is multiplied by Unit Scale and represents the minimum distance between samples when marching through atmosphere. Reducing this parameter can help eliminate banding artifacts when modeling a particularly thick atmosphere, but at extra cost.
parameters.heading: Sampling

parameters.label: Maximum Stepsize
parameters.description: This parameter is multiplied by Unit Scale represents the maximum distance between samples when marching through atmosphere. We recommend leaving Maximum Stepsize at 5 to 10 times the value of Minimum Stepsize.
parameters.heading: Sampling

parameters.label: Multi Scatter Limit
parameters.description: Specifies, how often an atmospheric ray can propagate through the atmosphere. NOTE: Increasing depth will impact render times. A depth of 1 or 2 is typically enough for the realistic appearance of a clear sky on Earth, with diminishing returns beyond that. A limit of 1 or greater is required if Ground Albedo should have an effect on the color of the sky.
parameters.heading: Sampling

parameters.label: Internal Color Space
parameters.description: Scatter and absorption coefficients are interpreted in the OpenColorIO color space specified by this parameter, and transformed into scene_linear (i.e. working space) when computing transmittance. Leave it empty to apply no transformation. This can help in preserving the look if the lookdev for the atmosphere was done in a different color space than the project's working space (however, due to the nature of RGB rendering, it can never be an exact match).
parameters.heading: Advanced

parameters.label: LUT Resolution
parameters.description: X and Y resolution for the transmittance table. The X axis corresponds to the light angle, and the Y axis corresponds to the viewer's altitude. With appropriate settings, there is no need to deviate from the default settings. An exception is if there are huge differences between the Distribution or ozone Altitude parameters. In this case it can help to increase the Y resolution to avoid bias.
parameters.heading: Advanced

parameters.label: Ground Offset
parameters.description: Distance between ground level and sea level. Ground is modeled as a sphere with radius calculated as Sea Level - Ground Offset. You can set this parameter to values greater than zero to lower the ground and avoid discontinuity artifacts from objects crossing ground level. As a consequence, you'll see a vacuum between the atmosphere and the ground which may be noticeable near horizon. We recommend leaving this parameter at 0 and keeping the rest of the scene above Sea Level instead.
parameters.heading: Advanced

parameters.label: Ground Receives Shadows
parameters.description: Allow ground elements to receive shadows (i.e. cast shadow rays).
parameters.heading: Advanced

parameters.label: Render Backside Atmosphere
parameters.description: Allows rendering of the atmosphere on the other side of the planet.
parameters.heading: Advanced

parameters.label: Solid Alpha in IPR
parameters.description: Set alpha to 1 in IPR mode. Turned on by default to avoid misleading appearance due to compositing against light viewport background.
parameters.heading: Advanced

parameters.label: Ignore Camera Far Clip
parameters.description: Ignore camera's far clip distance when computing atmospheric contribution on primary rays. This allows correct appearance of the sky without having to increase camera's far clip distance to encompass the entire atmosphere.
parameters.heading: Advanced

parameters.label: Transform
parameters.description: How the transform parameters below apply to the primitive. (Because each USD prim can contain multiple transforms, _and_ be affected by parent transforms, there are many different ways to apply new transforms.) Append: Apply the parameters as a new, most local transform. Prepend: Apply the parameters as a new, _least_ local transform. Overwrite or Append: If a local transform exists with the name xformOp:transform, _overwrite_ it with the parameters. Otherwise, apply it as a new, most local transform. If this replaces an existing transform, that transform's order in the local transform stack is not affected. Overwrite or Prepend: Like Overwrite or Append, but _least_ local. Apply Transform in World Space: Apply the parameters as a new, most local transform. However, prior to applying the transform, it is updated so that the result of the transform appears as if the transform was being applied in world space, before any local or ancestor transformations were applied to the primitive. Replace All Local Transforms: The transform specified in the remaining transform parameters is always applied as a new transform. Prior to applying this transform, all existing transform operations on the local transform stack are cleared so that only the supplied transform remains on the local transform stack (though ancestor transforms still have an effect). Apply XformCommonAPI: The transform specified in the remaining transform parameters will be applied as if it were appended to whatever the current transform on the prim is. But the resulting final transform will be expressed using the USD XformCommonAPI specification. Note that this specification cannot express shears, and so cannot express some transforms which may result in unexpected changes to transforms that already have shears. Apply Extended XformCommonAPI (with Shear + Pivot Rotate): The transform specified in the remaining transform parameters will be applied as if it were appended to whatever the current transform on the prim is. But the resulting final transform will be expressed using a Houdini-defined extension of the USD XformCommonAPI specification. This extension is accessible through the husd.UsdHoudini.HoudiniXformCommonAPI python class. This class provides a very similar interface to pxr.UsdGeom.XformCommonAPI but allows for shears in the transform, is able to store a pivot rotation value, and can express rotations as a quaternion if the rotations are animated. Using quaternions to express rotations avoids motion blur artifacts that can occur when using Euler angles to express the rotation.

parameters.description: The vertical angle of the sun in the sky measured in degrees from horizon.

parameters.label: Solar Azimuth
parameters.description: The horizontal angle along the horizon, where 0 corresponds to the -Z axis.
parameters.heading: Base Properties

parameters.label: Turbidity
parameters.description: Measure of the aerosol content of the air which defines the sky appearance. A Turbidity value of 2 yields a very clear, Arctic-like sky, 3 a clear sky in a temperate climate, 6 a sky on a warm, moist day, 10 a slightly hazy day.
parameters.heading: Base Properties

parameters.label: Ground Albedo
parameters.description: The ground reflectivity that affects the sky color. Ground Albedo does not change the ground brightness.
parameters.heading: Base Properties

parameters.label: Ground Color
parameters.description: The visual ground color as seen in the render.
parameters.heading: Base Properties

parameters.label: Horizon Blur Falloff
parameters.description: The angle in degrees below horizon where the sky and the ground color are blended to blur the horizon.

parameters.heading: Base Properties

parameters.label: Exposure
parameters.description: Scales the power output exponentially as a power of 2, similar to an F-stop control. 0 does not scale intensity, negative numbers scale intensity down by the square, positive numbers scale intensity up. Often you will set the Intensity to what looks like the right amount of light, and then use this parameter to "tweak" it.
parameters.heading: Base Properties

parameters.label: Color
parameters.description: The color of the light, in energy-linear terms.
parameters.heading: Base Properties

parameters.label: Enable Color Temperature
parameters.description: Use Color Temperature to control the light color. The color calculated by Color Temperature is *multiplied* by the RGB color in Color, so if you want the "pure" temperature color, you should set Color to 1.0, 1.0, 1.0.
parameters.heading: Base Properties

parameters.label: Color Temperature
parameters.description: When Enable Color Temperature is on, the temperature (in degrees Kelvin) to simulate. The valid range is from 1000 to 10000. Lower values are warmer and higher values are cooler. The default is the common D65 white point. If necessary, you can compute the same color value using the UsdLuxBlackbodyTemperatureAsRgb() function from the USD library.
parameters.heading: Base Properties

parameters.label: Filters
parameters.description: Optional light filter primitives that you want to apply to this light.
parameters.heading: Base Properties

parameters.label: Portals
parameters.description: Optional portal geometry prim(s) to use to guide light sampling.
parameters.heading: Base Properties

parameters.label: Normalize Power
parameters.description: Divides the set power output (intensity scaled by exposure) by the surface area or angular size of the light. This makes it easier to adjust and compare energy output without it being affected by the size of the light.
parameters.heading: Base Properties

parameters.label: Diffuse Multiplier
parameters.description: Scales the effect this light has on the diffuse response of shaders. This is a non-physical "tweak".
parameters.heading: Base Properties

parameters.label: Specular Multiplier
parameters.description: Scales the effect this light has on the specular response of shaders. This is a non-physical "tweak".
parameters.heading: Base Properties

parameters.label: Scale Guide Geometry
parameters.description: Applies a uniform scaling factor on the guide geometry that is drawn for the light in the viewport. The default value is an expression that inverts the "meters per unit" value of the USD stage to produce a consistent real-world size for the guide geometry.
parameters.heading: Base Properties

parameters.label: Show in Viewport Camera Menu
parameters.description: Turn off this option to prevent this light from showing up in the camera menu in the viewport. This can be useful to hide lights that are embedded in props, or other lights that are not meant to be modified.
parameters.heading: Base Properties

parameters.label: Light Filters
parameters.description: A space-separated list of light filters you want to use with the light. You can create a light filter in a Light Filter Library LOP.
parameters.heading: Base Properties

parameters.label: Enable
parameters.description: When this is on, objects hit by this light will cast shadows (subject to shadow masks).
parameters.heading: Shadow

parameters.label: Color
parameters.description: Tints the color of shadows cast by this light. Changing this from black (0, 0, 0) is a non-physical "tweak".
parameters.heading: Shadow

parameters.label: Distance
parameters.description: The maximum distance to check for objects shadowing this light. The default is -1, meaning no limit. Setting this may speed up rendering if you know all objects you want shadowed are within a certain distance.
parameters.heading: Shadow

parameters.label: MIS Bias
parameters.description: Controls whether multiple importance sampling will sample from the BSDF, the light, or both the BSDF and light.
parameters.heading: Sampling

parameters.label: Sampling Quality
parameters.description: This is the per-light sampling quality, that acts as a multiplier on the global Light Sampling Quality. Increasing the quality will add additional samples for this light source, improving the sampling quality of this light relative to other light sources.
parameters.heading: Sampling

parameters.label: Sampling Mode
parameters.description: When using the light tree for rendering, Karma will try to put any light source that's compatible into the tree. This option can force a light to be excluded from the tree and subject to uniform sampling, which can sometimes yield an improved sampling quality the light at the expense of speed.
parameters.heading: Sampling

parameters.label: Maximum HDRI Size
parameters.description: If an environment map is larger than this resolution, it will be scaled down when performing texture analysis. If the map has some very small, very bright values, this filtering may affect how sampling of the environment map is performed.
parameters.heading: Sampling

parameters.label: Portal MIS Bias
parameters.description: Controls whether the dome light is more likely to sample from the environment map or the portal geometry. For high-contrast HDRI with strong light sources, it may be beneficial to sample more from the environment map (set it less than 0), and for low-contrast/flat HDRI, the opposite may be true (set it greater than 0). Leave it at ß for balanced approach.
parameters.heading: Sampling

parameters.label: Improve Volume Sampling (Equiangular MIS)
parameters.description: Reduce noise in cases where the light is inside a volume, or in very close proximity to a volume (does not apply to directional light or dome light which do not have defined origin in world space). This feature is most effective in cases where the noise is mostly caused by sparsity of volume samples near the light source, either because the volume is too thin, or because the light has relatively small surface area. NOTE: If the volume has spectral opacity, this might introduce slight bias in output hue.
parameters.heading: Sampling

parameters.label: Light Shader
parameters.description: Defines a VEX shader to be used for light evaluation. If the string is empty, the value will be taken from the HOUDINI_VEX_DEFAULT_LIGHTSURFACE configuration variable.
parameters.heading: Light

parameters.label: Active Radius
parameters.description: Artificially clamp the illumination distance from the light. Outside this radius, the light will have no effect.
parameters.heading: Light

parameters.label: Point Light Radius
parameters.description: As point lights get closer to geometry, the attenuation equation causes the intensity of lights to go to infinity (a singularity caused by the division by the distance between the light and the surface). Increasing this value to something larger than zero creates an artificial buffer zone to prevent the light from going to infinity. If the radius is set to 1, the brightest value for the point light will be twice the intensity specified on the light. If the value is 1.4142 (sqrt(2)), the brightest value will be the intensity specified. For distant geometry, there should be very little change in the intensity.
parameters.heading: Light

parameters.label: Single Sided
parameters.description: Does the light emit light from a single side (ie along the normal) or from both sides? This only has effect on planar area light types.
parameters.heading: Light

parameters.label: Render Light Geometry
parameters.description: Causes the light source geometry to be visible in the render. Always turn this option on if you want to use the light as a portal light.
parameters.heading: Light

parameters.label: Light Geometry Casts Shadow
parameters.description: Causes the light source geometry to cast shadows in the render.
parameters.heading: Light

parameters.label: LPE Tag
parameters.description: Custom label assigned to lights or objects for use with Light Path Expressions.
parameters.heading: Light

parameters.label: Illuminate Background Holdout
parameters.description: If a light exists to add new light source instead of trying to replicate lighting in the live action plate, enable this parameter so that its effect on background holdout geometry shows up in indirect bounces and its contribution to shadow holdout AOVs is omitted.
parameters.heading: Light

parameters.label: Contributions
parameters.description: Provides detailed control over which BSDF component the light affects.
parameters.heading: Light

parameters.label: Contributes to Caustics
parameters.description: Default is true. Note that Karma only renders caustics if they are enabled on _both the light and the object_. This option has no effect unless you also turn on Enable Caustics on the geometry object.
parameters.heading: Light

parameters.label: Flip Rectangle Light Texture
parameters.description: Specifies how the texture applied to a rectangle light is flipped. Default is FlipX to match the USD specification. Only supported on rectangle light type. Options are None, FlipX, FlipY, and FlipXY.
parameters.heading: Light

parameters.label: Attenuation Type
parameters.description: Controls the type of attenuation on the light source in the default light shader. This may be none: No attenuation half: Half distance attenuation physical: Physically correct attenuation
parameters.heading: Light

parameters.label: Attenuation Start
parameters.description: Minimum light distance to be used for attenuation.
parameters.heading: Light

parameters.label: Attenuation
parameters.description: The distance from the light at which Half Distance Attenuation produces half the light intensity.
parameters.heading: Light

parameters.label: Spread
parameters.description: Ranges between 0 to 1 and controls beam direction along the light's normal. A value of 1 results in diffuse emission, and a value close to 0 gives parallel beams of light similar to directional light. Note that the Spread option is only supported for area lights with Type set to Rectangle or Disk. In conjunction with Disk lights you can, for example, create focused laser beams by leaving Spread at 0.
parameters.heading: Light

entries.label: Karma Texture Baker
entries.summary: Create a Render Settings primitive to create texture maps that define shading states for an object.

parameters.label: Rendersettings Primitive Path
parameters.description: Scene graph pattern specifying the RenderSettings prims to render with. Husk supports running multiple renders with different render settings prims from one process. When evaluating this pattern with Render existing file enabled, the specified file is opened as a USD stage with a population mask limiting the stage to the /Render branch, and the pattern is evaluated on that stage. If this is blank, the node looks for default render settings on the root prim. If the root prim has no render settings, the node will use default settings.

parameters.label: Baking Mode
parameters.description: Specifies how the shading point is determined for each point on the low-res mesh. The low_res mesh is the mesh you'll be baking. * Trace. This mode sends rays from the low-res/bake mesh in the direction of the surface normal to find the shading point. This method works if multiple objects are baked onto a single mesh. The other scene objects don't need UV coordinates. * UV Match. This method takes a single high-res mesh and determines the shading point by matching UV coordinates from the low-res mesh. UV Match makes sense if the high-res mesh doesn't align very well to the low-res mesh. * Single Mesh. To bake a single mesh, use the same mesh for Low Res Mesh and High Res Mesh.

parameters.label: Trace Mode
parameters.description: Determines how rays are traced from the low-resolution mesh to the high-resolution mesh during baking. There are three modes: Surface Normal (Bidirectional) traces rays in both forward and backward directions along the low-res normal to find the closest high-res surface match; Cage Mesh Topology traces a single ray from the cage mesh toward the low-res mesh using matching UV coordinates, ideal when a cage mesh with the same topology is available; Cage Offset traces a single ray by offsetting the low-res point along its normal and tracing backward, allowing cage-style baking without requiring a physical cage mesh. The Trace Bias parameter controls the offset distance used in Cage Offset mode.

parameters.label: Low Res Mesh
parameters.description: This is the mesh you're going to bake. The polygons are rasterized based on the mesh's UV coordinates.

parameters.label: Cage Mesh
parameters.description: This parameter is only available when you set Baking Mode to Trace. Sometimes it's problematic to determine the direction to trace rays from the low-res mesh to the scene. When you specify a cage mesh, rays are sent from the position on the cage mesh through the topology matching position on the low-res mesh. This leads to finer control when determining the shading position. Note that _low-res mesh_ and _cage mesh_ must have the same topology. Furthermore, the _cage mesh_ must enclose the _high-res_ mesh completely.

parameters.label: High Res Mesh
parameters.description: When you set Baking Mode to Trace, normally Karma will bake all visible surfaces. This allows convenient baking of complicated terrain with instanced boulders. However, this parameter lets you select the objects which will be baked to the low-res mesh. When you set Baking Mode to UV Mesh, this specifies the high-res mesh that has matching UV coordinates to the low.res mesh. The position data of this mesh are used to compute the shading information. When you set Baking Mode to Single Mesh, this specifies the high-res mesh. To bake a single mesh, use the same mesh for Low Res Mesh and High Res Mesh.

parameters.label: Dicing Camera
parameters.description: Specifies the camera for dicing subdivision or displaced surfaces. If no camera exists on the stage, the texture baker will create an automatic dicing camera.

parameters.label: Output Picture
parameters.description: The filename of the output image. When you bake a single image, the node uses the name exactly as entered here. However, when you render separate images for each AOV, this name will be the starting point for the individual AOV filename. The AOV name will be appended to the Output Picture just before the file extension. The file extension will be changed to the format that you've chosen from the Image Format dropdown on the Images tab.

parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.description: The horizontal and vertical size of the output image, in pixels.

parameters.label: UV Attribute
parameters.description: Specify the primvar name of the texture coordinate used for baking.

parameters.label: Default UDIM
parameters.description: When there are multiple UDIMs detected, the texture baker will create multiple USD rendersettings primitives - one for each UDIM (karmabake_<UDIM>). This parameter determines which of the rendersettings primitives will be the "default" for rendering. You can override the default primitive in the viewport display settings, or by specifying a specific rendersettings primitive when rendering with husk.

parameters.label: Create Separate Files
parameters.description: Renders either a single image with multiple AOVS, or store each AOV in a separate file. TIP: To see all AOVs, render a single image to MPlay.
parameters.heading: Images

parameters.label: Image Format
parameters.description: Specifies the format the image format of the separately rendered AOV. The file extension will change accordingly.
parameters.heading: Images

parameters.label: Save as Mip Mapped Texture
parameters.description: When saving separate files to .exr, .tif (.tx), or .rat files, enabling this option will ensure that the generated images have Mip Maps and are saved as tiled texture files suitable for use in rendering.
parameters.heading: Images

parameters.label: Name Separator
parameters.description: This character will be used to separate the file name from the Output Picture parameter and the AOV channel name. For example, when you bake Nt and P AOVs and Output Picture is render/bake.png, the output file names will be render/bake_Nt.png and render/bake_P.png. NOTE: You can inspect the stage and see details for all the render products in the created rendersettings primitive.
parameters.heading: Images

parameters.label: Expand UV Islands
parameters.description: Post-processes the images by smearing the boundaries of the UV islands into the empty areas of the image. This will produce better results when MIP-mapping the textures. This process can be time-consuming. For faster iterations, only turn on this feature for the final baking.
parameters.heading: Images

parameters.label: Denoiser
parameters.description: Choose a denoiser to run on the finished image output, or No Denoiser. This utility currently supports Intel Open Image Denoise (included with Houdini) and the NVIDIA OptiX Denoiser (must be installed separately). You must be on a supported platform and have the chosen denoising library installed for this to work. The NVIDIA OptiX Denoiser only works with NVIDIA cards. It is now included with the NVIDIA driver (version 435 or later).
parameters.heading: Images

parameters.label: Denoise AOVs
parameters.description: The denoiser will be applied to the parameter's space-separated list of AOVs.
parameters.heading: Images

parameters.label: Normal Y Direction
parameters.description: Determines the direction of the Y value of the tangent-space normal (or rounded normal) AOVs.
parameters.heading: Alignment

parameters.label: Tangent Space Normal
parameters.description: Creates an AOV for the tangent space normal. You can change the AOV's default Nt name.
parameters.heading: Tangent Space Normal

parameters.label: Rounded Normal
parameters.description: Creates an AOV for the rounded normal. You can change the AOV's default Rn name.
parameters.heading: Rounded Normal

parameters.label: Rounded Edge Samples
parameters.description: Specify the number of directions to compute the rounded normal. More samples will take a longer time but produce a less noisy result.
parameters.heading: Rounded Normal

parameters.label: Rounded Edge Ray Bias
parameters.description: The ray-bias for computing rounded normals to avoid self-intersection.
parameters.heading: Rounded Normal

parameters.label: Rounded Edge Radius
parameters.description: The radius for the rounded normals.
parameters.heading: Rounded Normal

parameters.label: Rounded Edge Cusp Angle
parameters.description: Polygons that have an angle less than this threshold will be assumed to be a smooth surface and not appear in the rounded normal map.
parameters.heading: Rounded Normal

parameters.label: Rounded Edge Mode
parameters.description: Whether to capture concave or convex edges in the rounded edge normal map.
parameters.heading: Rounded Normal

parameters.label: World Space
parameters.description: Whether the world space position should be recorded in left or right handed space with Y or Z as the up axis.
parameters.heading: Alignment

parameters.label: Position
parameters.description: The shading position. You can change the AOV's default P name.
parameters.heading: Position

parameters.label: Shading Space
parameters.description: When you store the P AOV, this is how the position should be represented * World Space. The shading position is written directly to the AOV. * Low Res Mesh Bounding Box. The shading position is fit to the bounding box of the low-res mesh. * Scene Bounding Box. The shading position is fit to the bounding box of the whole scene. * User Defined. The shading position is fit to user specified values.
parameters.heading: Position

parameters.label: Uniform Bounding Box (Not Stretched)
parameters.description: When you turn on this toggle, all three axes of the bounding box will have the same length. If unchecked, the box will fit the geometry tightly in all dimensions.
parameters.heading: Position

parameters.label: Normal
parameters.description: The shading normal. You can change the AOV's default N name.
parameters.heading: Normal

parameters.label: Geometric Normal
parameters.description: The geometric shading normal (the face/non-interpolated normal). You can change the AOV's default Ng name.
parameters.heading: Geometric Normal

parameters.label: Occlusion
parameters.description: Ambient occlusion. You can change the AOV's default Oc name.
parameters.heading: Occlusion

parameters.label: Occlusion Samples
parameters.description: Determines the number of indirect rays used when computing Occlusion. If the resulting AOV is noisy, you can increase Occlusion Samples without having to increase the Primary Samples.
parameters.heading: Occlusion

parameters.label: Occlusion Max Distance
parameters.description: The maximum distance to consider when computing Occlusion. A small distance can speed up occlusion shading at the cost of accuracy.
parameters.heading: Occlusion

parameters.label: Occlusion Ray Bias
parameters.description: Controls the ray bias when computing Occlusion.
parameters.heading: Occlusion

parameters.label: Curvature
parameters.description: The curvature at the shading position. You can change the AOV's default Cu name.
parameters.heading: Curvature

parameters.label: Curvature Samples
parameters.description: Determines the number of indirect rays used when computing Curvature. If the resulting AOV is noisy, you can increase Curvature Samples without having to increase the Primary Samples.
parameters.heading: Curvature

parameters.label: Curvature Scale
parameters.description: Controls the overall intensity or contrast of the curvature by amplifying the difference between convex and concave responses.
parameters.heading: Curvature

parameters.label: Max Distance
parameters.description: Smaller values (= smaller distance) emphasize the concavity. Larger values (= greater distance) reveal more curvature and improve the visibility of the convex features.
parameters.heading: Curvature

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.description: Controls whether the map looks more concave or more convex. Smaller values emphasize concavity, higher values enhance convexity.
parameters.heading: Curvature

parameters.label: Cavity
parameters.description: The occlusion along the inverted normal at the shading position. This produces "relief" shading. You can change the AOV's default Cv name.
parameters.heading: Cavity

parameters.label: Cavity Samples
parameters.description: Determines the number of indirect rays used when computing Cavity. If the resulting AOV is noisy, you can increase Cavity Samples without having to increase the Primary Samples.
parameters.heading: Cavity

parameters.label: Max Distance
parameters.description: Limits how far rays can detect nearby geometry. Smaller values (smaller distance) emphasize concavity.
parameters.heading: Cavity

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.description: Blends between full cavity contrast (0) and a flat result (1).
parameters.heading: Cavity

parameters.label: Thickness
parameters.description: The thickness at the shading position. You can change the AOV's default Th name.
parameters.heading: Thickness

parameters.label: Thickness Samples
parameters.description: Determines the number of indirect rays used when computing Thickness. If the resulting AOV is noisy, you can increase Thickness Samples without having to increase the Primary Samples.
parameters.heading: Thickness

parameters.label: Edge
parameters.description: Identify edges in the high res model. You can change the AOV's default Eg name.
parameters.heading: Edge

parameters.label: Edge Samples
parameters.description: Specify the number of directions to compute the Edge. More samples will take longer processing time, but produce a less noisy result.
parameters.heading: Edge

parameters.label: Edge Ray Bias
parameters.description: The ray-bias for computing rounded normals to avoid self-intersection.
parameters.heading: Edge

parameters.label: Edge Radius
parameters.description: The radius of the rounded edge.
parameters.heading: Edge

parameters.label: Edge Cusp Angle
parameters.description: Polygons with an angle below this threshold are considered smooth and won't appear in the Edge map.
parameters.heading: Edge

parameters.label: Edge Mode
parameters.description: Types of edges (concave or convex) to smooth

This AOV stores the multiplied result as a single channel. The Coat Normal, Shading Normal and Shading Tangent values are stored exactly as they are wired into the shader (in world position).

parameters.label: Make Low Res Mesh Invisible
parameters.description: In most cases, the low-res mesh should be invisible to any rays. This means that the mesh won't contribute to occlusion or other ray-traced effects. However, there might be situations where the low-res mesh remains visible.

parameters.label: Primary Samples
parameters.description: Specifies the number of camera rays sent for each pixel. Higher values improve the quality of the rendering.
parameters.heading: Baking

parameters.label: Trace Bias
parameters.description: When rays are sent from the low-res mesh to the scene, this bias is used to offset a ray's origin from the surface of the low-res mesh. You can use this parameter to arbitrarily offset the low-res mesh along its normal without having to define a cage mesh.
