parameters.label: Use MikkT Tangents
parameters.description: MikkT is a common standard for tangent space used in baking tools to produce normal maps.
parameters.heading: Baking

parameters.label: Low Res Normals
parameters.description: For texture baking to work, the Low Res Mesh should have normals. This parameter controls how the LOP will deal with low-res geometry that's missing normals.
parameters.heading: Baking

parameters.label: Dicing Quality
parameters.description: When baking displaced meshes or subdivision surfaces, this parameter can control the level of detail of the dicing.
parameters.heading: Baking

parameters.label: Displacement Style
parameters.description: Sometimes, displacement shading inverts the surface and produces bad normals. This parameter lets you run displacement shaders as bump map shaders. Alternatively, you can disable displacement shading entirely.
parameters.heading: Baking

parameters.label: Uncategorized Primitives
parameters.description: Determines the behavior of primitives that don't belong to any trace set. Global Visibility: These primitives will be part of the "global" trace set. All primitives in the hires mesh will affect ray tracing operations. Combine Into Single Trace Set: Combine uncategorized primitives into a single trace set. Only primitives in this group will affect each other in ray tracing operations. Separate Into Individual Trace Sets: Each uncategorized primitive will be put into a mutually exclusive trace set and not affected by other primitives.
parameters.heading: Trace Set

parameters.label: Trace Sets
parameters.description: The number of explicit trace sets.
parameters.heading: Trace Set

parameters.label: Enable
parameters.description: Turn on (or off) the creation of the trace set.
parameters.heading: Trace Set

parameters.label: Name
parameters.description: Specify a name for the trace set.
parameters.heading: Trace Set

parameters.label: Visibility
parameters.description: Specify the primitives visible to primitives in this trace set for ray tracing. This is specified as a space- or comma-separated list of other trace set names. Two special names are self (only consider primitives in this trace set) and * (consider all primitives). * If the visibility is self, only primitives in this trace set will be used for ray tracing operations. * If the visibility is *, all primitives in the scene will affect the visibility of these primitives. * You can also specify a pattern of trace set names which are used to determine visibility for ray-tracing operations. For example body*, face body hands or face body* ^knapsack to exclude knapsack.
parameters.heading: Trace Set

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.description: The primitives that belong to this trace set.

entries.label: SOP Import UsdSkel Character
entries.summary: Imports a character or animation from a SOP network into the USD scene graph.

parameters.label: Animated Pose
parameters.description: Path to the SOP node containing the animated skeleton geometry.

parameters.label: Rest Geometry
parameters.description: Optional path to the SOP node containing the rest skin geometry. If not specified, only the skeleton and animation are imported.

parameters.label: Capture Pose
parameters.description: Optional path to the SOP node containing the capture pose to use for the Rest Geometry.

parameters.label: Cache Behavior
parameters.description: Cache Behavior: Specifies when and how frames are combined into the cache. Always Cache All Frames: As soon as the node is cooked the first time, or whenever the input to the Cache LOP is modified, the node cooks the entire frame range and combines the results into a single stage. This can be very expensive in both time and memory. However, if you are caching the entire frame range, this method provides the lowest average per-frame caching time. Cache Cooked Frames: Frames of data are cooked and combined into the cache when that particular frame is requested. This is more expensive per-frame than cooking multiple frames at once, but it provides the best time to first result. Cache Up To Cooked Frames: This is a hybrid of the Always Cache All Frames and Cache Cooked Frames options. When a particular frame's data is requested, this LOP cooks and caches all frames from the start of the range up to the requested frame. This option is useful when the cooked data is coming from a simulation where it might be very expensive to go back and cook earlier frames. Cache Current Frame Only: In this mode, only the current frame is in the cache. This reduces memory usage considerably when scrubbing through the timeline. However, it must recook the time samples every time a frame of data is requested from this node. This mode is typically only used when Subframe Sampling is turned on for motion blur. In this mode, the Cache node is always time dependent, even after playing back an entire simulation.

parameters.label: Clip Range
parameters.description: Specifies how the cached frame range is determined. Use clipinfo Detail Attribute: Determines the frame range using the clipinfo detail attribute from the Animated Pose. If the attribute does not exist, the scene frame range is used. Custom Frame Range: Only cache the specified frame range.

parameters.label: Start/End/Inc
parameters.description: Start/End/Inc: The first frame, last frame, and increment size (in frames) between each cook request made of the input to populate the cache. The first two values control the range of frames over which the Cache should apply. The third value allows the stage to be super-sampled for improved motion blur, or sub-sampled to preserve memory (at the cost of accuracy, as USD simply uses linear interpolation between time sampled values).

parameters.label: Shift Range to Source
parameters.description: When turned on, shifts the animation so that it begins at the clipinfo attribute's source start time. This parameter is available when Clip Range is set to Use clipinfo Detail Attribute.

parameters.label: Subframe Sampling
parameters.description: For each primary sample generated by this node, these parameters can cause additional samples to be generated around that primary sample time. This is most often used to ensure that accurate data exists at exactly the camera shutter open and close times, as well as at the primary sample time.
parameters.heading: Subframe Sampling

parameters.label: Shutter
parameters.description: Controls the method used to specify the shutter open and close times relative to the primary sample times. Specify Manually: The Shutter Open/Close parameter values provide exact offset values relative to the primary sample time. Use Camera Prim: The Camera Prim parameter provides the scene graph path of a camera primitive from which the shutter open and close times are extracted to provide the offset values relative to the primary time sample.
parameters.heading: Subframe Sampling

parameters.label: Shutter Open/Close
parameters.description: When Shutter is set to Specify Manually, these two offset values are added to the primary sample time to indicate the shutter open and close times. The open time should be less than or equal to zero, and the close time should be greater than or equal to zero.
parameters.heading: Subframe Sampling

parameters.label: Camera Prim
parameters.description: When Shutter is set to Use Camera Prim, this is the scene graph path of a camera prim on the input node's stage. The shutter open and close attribute values are read from this primitive.
parameters.heading: Subframe Sampling

parameters.label: Samples
parameters.description: The number of subframe samples to create for each primary sample. These samples are evenly distributed between the shutter open and close times. Note that such an even distribution may or may not create a sample at exactly the primary sample time.
parameters.heading: Subframe Sampling

parameters.label: Always Include Frame Sample
parameters.description: When turned on, forces a sample to be created at exactly the primary sample time. If the Samples value, together with the shutter open and close times, already place a sample at the primary sample time, turning on this option has no effect. Otherwise, this option causes an addition sample to be added. This means that the actual number of samples per primary sample may in fact be one more than the number specified in the Samples parameter.
parameters.heading: Subframe Sampling

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.description: When turned on, imports the character's prims under a SkelRoot prim at the specified path in the scene graph. When turned off, the prims are imported at the default location (underneath a primitive named character), or at the path specified by the optional usdskelrootpath attribute on the Rest Geometry.
parameters.heading: Subframe Sampling

parameters.label: Skeleton Primitive Path
parameters.description: When turned on, imports the Skeleton prim at the specified path. The path can be relative to Primitive Path. When turned off, the skeleton is imported at the default location (a child primitive named skeleton), or at the path specified by the optional usdskelpath attribute on the Animated Pose geometry.
parameters.heading: Subframe Sampling

parameters.label: Animation Primitive Path
parameters.description: When turned on, imports the SkelAnimation prim at the specified path. The path can be relative to Primitive Path. When turned off, the animation is imported at the default location (a child primitive named animation), or at the path specified by the optional usdanimpath attribute on the Animated Pose geometry.
parameters.heading: Subframe Sampling

parameters.label: Animation Save Path
parameters.description: Layer Save Path: When turned on, sets the Save Path metadata for the layer containing the geometry to this file path. When you write out USD using a USD Render ROP, the geometry is saved out to a .usd layer file using this file path (after output processing).
parameters.heading: Subframe Sampling

parameters.label: Geometry Save Path
parameters.description: Layer Save Path: When turned on, sets the Save Path metadata for the layer containing the geometry to this file path. When you write out USD using a USD Render ROP, the geometry is saved out to a .usd layer file using this file path (after output processing).
parameters.heading: Subframe Sampling

parameters.label: Import Rest Geometry Data
parameters.description: When turned on, imports the rest geometry and skeleton. When turned off, only creates an override for the SkelAnimation prim.
parameters.heading: Import Rest Geometry Data

parameters.label: Bind Materials
parameters.description: Bind Materials: Binds materials to the imported USD primitives based on the usdmaterialpath SOP attribute. The usdmaterialpath value can specify either the path to a material primitive, or the path to another primitive to copy the material binding from. If the Subset Attributes include a materialBind SOP attribute, material bindings can also be created for the resulting geometry subsets. When creating missing materials, the usdmaterialreffile and usdmaterialrefprim attributes can optionally be used to author a reference to a material from the specified file.
parameters.heading: Import Rest Geometry Data

parameters.label: Enable Treat Polygons as Subdivision Surfaces
parameters.label_norm: enable treat polygons as subdivision surfaces
parameters.description: Enable Treat Polygons as Subdivision Surfaces: When turned on, the Treat Polygons as Subdivision Surfaces setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a usdconfigpolygonsassubd detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the USD Configure SOP).
parameters.heading: Import Rest Geometry Data

parameters.label: Treat Polygons as Subdivision Surfaces
parameters.description: Treat Polygons as Subdivision Surfaces: For polygon meshes that are not already tagged with a subdivision scheme, author a subdivisionScheme attribute set to catmullClark. This will convert them to subdivision surfaces.
parameters.heading: Import Rest Geometry Data

parameters.label: Enable Topology Attributes
parameters.description: Enable Topology Attributes: When turned on, the Topology Attributes setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a usdconfigtopology detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the USD Configure SOP).
parameters.heading: Import Rest Geometry Data

parameters.label: Topology Attributes
parameters.description: Controls whether USD topology attributes should be authored as time sampled or default values. The following attributes are treated as topology attributes Static: Write topology attributes as default values. This can make playback much faster, but limits how the topology can change over time. None: Do not author topology attributes. This is useful when USD data is sent to SOPs for processing, then brought back into LOPs. Using this option tells the importer that the geometry topology has not changed in this process, so only the changing point positions or other primvars will be imported.
parameters.heading: Import Rest Geometry Data

parameters.label: Enable Attributes
parameters.description: Enable Attributes: When turned on, the Attributes setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a usdconfigattribs detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the USD Configure SOP).
parameters.heading: Import Rest Geometry Data

parameters.label: Attributes
parameters.description: Attributes: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to import into USD as primvars. In addition to matching attribute names directly, there are some values with special meanings bounds: Authors the USD extent attribute using the calculated bounding box of the associated SOP geometry. visibility: Authors the USD visibility attribute based on the value of the usdvisibility geometry attribute.
parameters.heading: Import Rest Geometry Data

parameters.label: Enable Indexed Attributes
parameters.description: Enable Indexed Attributes: When turned on, the Indexed Attributes setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a usdconfigindexattribs detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the USD Configure SOP).
parameters.heading: Import Rest Geometry Data

parameters.label: Indexed Attributes
parameters.description: Indexed Attributes: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to import into USD as indexed primvars. If a SOP attribute matches this pattern, the importer authors the primvar as an indexed array of values (that is, an array of values called primvars:<<name>>, and an array of indices into those values called primvars:<<name>>:indices). Preparing an indexed primvar can be expensive for attributes that are not integers or strings. You should only use indexed primvars where it is likely to result in significant savings in storage size due to a small number of unique values being used across a large number of components.
parameters.heading: Import Rest Geometry Data

parameters.label: Enable Import as Single Element Array
parameters.label_norm: enable import as single element array
parameters.description: Enable Import as Single Element Array: When turned on, the Import as Single Element Array setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a usdconfigconstantattribs detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the USD Configure SOP).
parameters.heading: Import Rest Geometry Data

parameters.label: Import as Single Element Array
parameters.description: Import as Single Element Array: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to import into USD as primvars with Constant interpolation (an array with a single value for the whole primitive), regardless of whether the SOP geometry attribute is a point, primitive, or vertex attribute. If multiple values could be chosen for a particular USD primitive, the importer chooses the first value it encounters. Importing as a single element array (versus Import as Single Value) can be useful since it allows the primvar's interpolation to be overridden without changing the primvar's type.
parameters.heading: Import Rest Geometry Data

parameters.label: Enable Import as Single Value
parameters.description: Enable Import as Single Value: When turned on, the Import as Single Value setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a usdconfigscalarconstantattribs detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the USD Configure SOP).
parameters.heading: Import Rest Geometry Data

parameters.label: Import as Single Value
parameters.description: Import as Single Value: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to import into USD as primvars with Constant interpolation and a single value for the whole primitive, regardless of whether the SOP geometry attribute is a point, primitive, or vertex attribute. If multiple values could be chosen for a particular USD primitive, the importer chooses the first value it encounters. This is the default behavior for how detail attributes are imported. This is similar to Import as Single Element Array, but the primvar's type is a scalar value instead of an array with a single element (for example, vector3f instead of vector3f[]).
parameters.heading: Import Rest Geometry Data

parameters.label: Enable Subset Attributes
parameters.description: Enable Subset Attributes: When turned on, the Subset Attributes setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a usdconfigpartitionattribs detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the USD Configure SOP).
parameters.heading: Import Rest Geometry Data

parameters.label: Subset Attributes
parameters.description: Subset Attributes: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying which SOP string or integer attributes represent subsets of the geometry. The importer puts elements with the same value for this attribute into their own geometry subsets. Each attribute's subsets are added to a subset family (named from the original attribute) which indicates that the subsets are related. The subset family's type is set to partition to indicate that the subsets are non-intersecting and that every element of the primitive appears in a subset. If there are elements with empty string values (which are not added to a subset), the family type is instead set to nonOverlapping to indicate that the subsets are non-intersecting but some elements do not appear in a subset. The family's type is authored as an attribute on the parent primitive, for example subsetFamily:shop_materialpath:familyType. Subsets can be created from point or primitive partition attributes on SOP meshes, curves, tetrahedra, and points. The importer will try to set the subset name to the attribute value, but may need to change the name to make it a legal USD primitive name. The importer stores the raw attribute value on the geometry subset prim as Custom Data with the key partitionValue.
parameters.heading: Import Rest Geometry Data

parameters.label: Enable Prefix Subsets with Attribute Name
parameters.label_norm: enable prefix subsets with attribute name
parameters.description: Enable Prefix Subsets with Attribute Name: When turned on, the Prefix Subsets with Attribute Name setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a usdconfigprefixpartitionsubsets detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the USD Configure SOP).
parameters.heading: Import Rest Geometry Data

parameters.label: Prefix Subsets with Attribute Name
parameters.description: Prefix Subsets with Attribute Name: When creating subsets from Subset Attributes, the subsets are named by combining the attribute name with the partition attribute's value (a string or integer). This avoids name collisions when multiple partition attributes contain the same values, but can be undesirable if precise control of the subset names is required. For string attributes, if this option is turned off, the attribute values are directly used as the subset names.
parameters.heading: Import Rest Geometry Data

parameters.label: Enable Subset Groups
parameters.description: Enable Subset Groups: When turned on, the Subset Groups setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a usdconfigsubsetgroups detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the USD Configure SOP).
parameters.heading: Import Rest Geometry Data

parameters.label: Subset Groups
parameters.description: Subset Groups: A space-separated list of group names/patterns specifying SOP groups. SOP elements in each group are imported as a geometry subset, named for the group. Subsets can be created from point or primitive groups on SOP meshes, curves, tetrahedra, and points.
parameters.heading: Import Rest Geometry Data

parameters.label: Enable USD Custom Attributes
parameters.description: Enable USD Custom Attributes: When turned on, the USD Custom Attributes setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a usdconfigcustomattribs detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the USD Configure SOP).
parameters.heading: Import Rest Geometry Data

parameters.label: USD Custom Attributes
parameters.description: USD Custom Attributes: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to import into USD as attributes (rather than primvars).
parameters.heading: Import Rest Geometry Data

parameters.label: Enable Translate UV Attribute to ST
parameters.label_norm: enable translate uv attribute to st
parameters.description: Enable Translate UV Attribute to ST: When turned on, the Translate UV Attribute to ST setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a usdconfigtranslateuvtost detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the USD Configure SOP).
parameters.heading: Import Rest Geometry Data

parameters.label: Translate UV Attribute to ST
parameters.description: Translate UV Attribute to ST: When turned on, converts the SOP vertex attribute uv into a USD primvar called primvars:st. Whether you need to turn this on depends on the renderer you are using and how your shaders are authored. If you are rendering with Karma, leave this off. (As of this writing there is no strict standard for texture coordinate naming in USD, but the use of st is a common convention, whereas in SOP geometry, using uv is the common convention.)
parameters.heading: Import Rest Geometry Data

parameters.label: Enable Attributes
parameters.description: Enable Attributes: When turned on, the Attributes setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a usdconfigattribs detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the USD Configure SOP).
parameters.heading: Import Animation Data

In addition to matching attribute names directly, there are some values with special meanings bounds: Authors the USD extent attribute using the calculated bounding box of the associated SOP geometry. visibility: Authors the USD visibility attribute based on the value of the usdvisibility geometry attribute.

parameters.label: Enable Import as Single Element Array
parameters.label_norm: enable import as single element array
parameters.description: Enable Import as Single Element Array: When turned on, the Import as Single Element Array setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a usdconfigconstantattribs detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the USD Configure SOP).

If multiple values could be chosen for a particular USD primitive, the importer chooses the first value it encounters. Importing as a single element array (versus Import as Single Value) can be useful since it allows the primvar's interpolation to be overridden without changing the primvar's type.

parameters.description: Enable Import as Single Value: When turned on, the Import as Single Value setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a usdconfigscalarconstantattribs detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the USD Configure SOP).

This is similar to Import as Single Element Array, but the primvar's type is a scalar value instead of an array with a single element (for example, vector3f instead of vector3f[]).

parameters.label: Enable Set Default Values
parameters.description: Enable Set Default Values Enable Set Default Values: When turned on, the Set Default Values setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a usdconfigstaticattribs detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the USD Configure SOP).
parameters.heading: Import Animation Data

parameters.label: Set Default Values
parameters.description: Set Default Values: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to always author as default values for USD primvars (never time samples).

parameters.label: Enable USD Custom Attributes
parameters.description: Enable USD Custom Attributes: When turned on, the USD Custom Attributes setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a usdconfigcustomattribs detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the USD Configure SOP).

entries.label: Layer Replace
entries.summary: Replaces all uses of a certain layer with a substitute layer from its second input.

parameters.label: Replace Path
parameters.description: The file path of the layer you want to replace. This parameter can specify multiple paths, and use wildcards, which allows it to replace many layers with a single common replacement layer. The pattern is compared to both the original layer reference as it appears in the referencing layer, and as an absolute path (created by treating the referencing layer's path as the root location to resolve relative paths).

parameters.label: Modified Layer Path
parameters.description: This parameter is evaluated for each modified layer, and should contain an expression that computes the file path under which the modified layer will be saved. In the expression, the @oldpath local variable ($OLDPATH is deprecated) contains the layer's. Remember that, in a string parameter, you must surround expression code with backticks! The default saves the modified layers to the same paths as before. Note that this path will be run through the output processors when written out just like any other save path.

entries.label: Light
entries.summary: Creates or edits a USD Light prim. This node also adds some useful Karma-specific attributes.

parameters.label: Sampling Behavior
parameters.description: Cooking this node can generate many USD time samples, rather than just a single time sample at the current time. This can be equivalent to having a Cache LOP following this node, but it will evaluate much faster, and does not cache data from any other nodes. This allows animated data to be authored to USD without introducing a node time dependency which would then cause all following nodes to also be time dependent. This can vastly improve playback performance of some LOP Networks. In all sampling modes, if a parameter on this node does not vary with time, and does not rely on other time sampled data from the stage, only a single default value will be generated in USD for the corresponding attribute. USD time samples are only generated for parameters that may vary over time. Sample Current Frame: A single time sample will be generated for the current time. Sample Frame Range If Input Is Not Time Dependent: If the input to this node is time dependent, this node behaves as if it is in Sample Current Frame mode. Otherwise it behaves as if it is in Sample Frame Range mode. Sample Frame Range: The Start/End/Inc parameter is used to generate multiple times at which this node's parameters are evaluated, and a USD time sample is created for each attribute at each one of these times.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Start/End/Inc
parameters.description: When the Sampling behavior is Sample Frame Range, this parameter controls the number and spacing of base time samples to be generated by this node. The default values of this parameter are @fstart, @fend, and @finc. These values correspond to the start, end, and step size of the global Houdini animation settings when interacting with Houdini. When using a ROP node to generate a range of frames, these values correspond to the start, end, and increment values specified on the ROP node being executed. This default ensures that a USD file written to disk will contain time samples for exactly the frame range requested by the ROP (regardless of the Houdini animation settings).
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Subframe Sampling
parameters.description: For each primary sample generated by this node, these parameters can cause additional samples to be generated around that primary sample time. This is most often used to ensure that accurate data exists at exactly the camera shutter open and close times, as well as at the primary sample time.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Shutter
parameters.description: Controls the method used to specify the shutter open and close times relative to the primary sample times. Specify Manually: The Shutter Open/Close parameter values provide exact offset values relative to the primary sample time. Use Camera Prim: The Camera Prim parameter provides the scene graph path of a camera primitive from which the shutter open and close times are extracted to provide the offset values relative to the primary time sample.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Shutter Open/Close
parameters.description: When Shutter is set to Specify Manually, these two offset values are added to the primary sample time to indicate the shutter open and close times. The open time should be less than or equal to zero, and the close time should be greater than or equal to zero.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Camera Prim
parameters.description: When Shutter is set to Use Camera Prim, this is the scene graph path of a camera prim on the input node's stage. The shutter open and close attribute values are read from this primitive.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Samples
parameters.description: The number of subframe samples to create for each primary sample. These samples are evenly distributed between the shutter open and close times. Note that such an even distribution may or may not create a sample at exactly the primary sample time.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Always Include Frame Sample
parameters.description: When turned on, forces a sample to be created at exactly the primary sample time. If the Samples value, together with the shutter open and close times, already place a sample at the primary sample time, turning on this option has no effect. Otherwise, this option causes an addition sample to be added. This means that the actual number of samples per primary sample may in fact be one more than the number specified in the Samples parameter.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Action
parameters.description: Whether this node should create new prims, or edit existing prims. In addition, the Force Edit option can be chosen to cause this node to ignore the houdini:editable attribute on prims, and always edit the specified attributes. This is in contrast to the Edit mode which will trigger a warning and not set attributes on prims with the houdini:editable attribute set to false.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.description: In Create mode, this lets you control where in the scene graph to create the prim(s). The default is usually /$OS. This creates a primitive at the root level with the same name as the node (for example, /tube1). This is a useful default for preventing naming conflicts, but terrible for organization. You should try to remember to change the Primitive Path to a better value when you create prims. For example, instead of naming models after the node that created them, you might want to name them after the geometry inside, and organize them under a /Models branch. The Create Primitives section contains basic controls for how to create the new prim(s).
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.description: In Edit mode, the node has a Primitive Pattern parameter. This lets you specify the prim(s) the node should operate on. You can click the select button beside the text box to select the primitives from the scene graph tree. You can also use primitive patterns for advanced matching, including matching all prims in a collection.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Allowed Primitive Types
parameters.description: In Edit mode, only prims that match one of the specified primitive types (or API schemas) can be modified by this node. Leave this parameter empty to permit editing any primitive type.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Handle Disallowed Types
parameters.description: In Edit mode, specifies what should happen when a primitive that is not one of the Allowed primitive types matches the primitive pattern Ignore Disallowed Prim Types: Do not set any attributes on this primitive, but do not notify the user.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Initialize Parameters
parameters.description: Changes the state of all control menu parameters to Do Nothing, so that this node will not apply any changes. Also grabs the current values of each property from the first Primitives match, and sets the values of the corresponding parameters to match. This means that changing any parameter's control menu to Set or Create mode will set the property to its current value, making it easier to apply changes to an existing value rather than setting a brand new value. With Rebuild Render-Specific Parameters you reset all parameters from render-specific tabs to their default values for the specific node. If you want to reset the parameters for the entire scene, you can also open the top-level Render menu and choose Rebuild All Render-Specific LOP Parameters.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: Cylinder Light: Light emitted outward from a cylinder. The cylinder is centered at the origin and has its major axis on the X axis. The cylinder does not emit light from the flat end-caps. Distant Light: Light emitted from a distant source along the -Z axis. Also known as a directional light. Disk Light: Light emitted from one side of a circular disk. The disk is centered in the XY plane and emits light along the -Z axis. Geometry Light: Light emitted outward from a geometric prim (UsdGeomGprim), which is typically a mesh. Point Light: Like a sphere light, but with zero radius. Rectangle Light: Light emitted from one side of a rectangle. The rectangle is centered in the XY plane and emits light along the -Z axis. The rectangle is 1 unit in length in the X and Y axis. In the default position, a texture file's min coordinates should be at (+X, +Y) and max coordinates at (-X, -Y). Sphere Light: Light emitted outward from a sphere.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Transform
parameters.description: How the transform parameters below apply to the primitive. (Because each USD prim can contain multiple transforms, _and_ be affected by parent transforms, there are many different ways to apply new transforms.) Append: Apply the parameters as a new, most local transform. Prepend: Apply the parameters as a new, _least_ local transform. Overwrite or Append: If a local transform exists with the name xformOp:transform, _overwrite_ it with the parameters. Otherwise, apply it as a new, most local transform. If this replaces an existing transform, that transform's order in the local transform stack is not affected. Overwrite or Prepend: Like Overwrite or Append, but _least_ local. Apply Transform in World Space: Apply the parameters as a new, most local transform. However, prior to applying the transform, it is updated so that the result of the transform appears as if the transform was being applied in world space, before any local or ancestor transformations were applied to the primitive. Replace All Local Transforms: The transform specified in the remaining transform parameters is always applied as a new transform. Prior to applying this transform, all existing transform operations on the local transform stack are cleared so that only the supplied transform remains on the local transform stack (though ancestor transforms still have an effect). Apply XformCommonAPI: The transform specified in the remaining transform parameters will be applied as if it were appended to whatever the current transform on the prim is. But the resulting final transform will be expressed using the USD XformCommonAPI specification. Note that this specification cannot express shears, and so cannot express some transforms which may result in unexpected changes to transforms that already have shears. Apply Extended XformCommonAPI (with Shear + Pivot Rotate): The transform specified in the remaining transform parameters will be applied as if it were appended to whatever the current transform on the prim is. But the resulting final transform will be expressed using a Houdini-defined extension of the USD XformCommonAPI specification. This extension is accessible through the husd.UsdHoudini.HoudiniXformCommonAPI python class. This class provides a very similar interface to pxr.UsdGeom.XformCommonAPI but allows for shears in the transform, is able to store a pivot rotation value, and can express rotations as a quaternion if the rotations are animated. Using quaternions to express rotations avoids motion blur artifacts that can occur when using Euler angles to express the rotation.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Transform Order
parameters.description: The order in which Houdini applies translates, rotates, and scales, and the order in which it applies rotation.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Translate
parameters.description: Movement amount along XYZ axes.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.description: Degrees rotation around XYZ axes.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: Non-uniform scaling along XYZ axes.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Uniform Scale
parameters.description: Scales the object uniformly along all three axes.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Pivot Translate
parameters.description: Moves the local origin of the object.
parameters.heading: Pivot Transform

parameters.label: Pivot Rotate
parameters.description: Rotates the local origin of the object after translation.
parameters.heading: Pivot Transform

parameters.label: NOTE
parameters.description: USD currently does not have look-at constraints. This node calculates the per-frame transform to fulfill the constraint and applies it to the object.
parameters.heading: Constraints

parameters.label: Enable Look At
parameters.description: Turns on the constraint that orients this object to look at a point or another object.
parameters.heading: Constraints

parameters.label: Look At Position
parameters.description: If Enable Look At is on and, this is a point in space this object will look at. If Look At Primitive is not blank, this is an *offset* from the centroid of the target object (in the local space of that object).
parameters.heading: Constraints

parameters.label: Look At Primitive
parameters.description: The path to a USD prim this object should look at. If this is not blank, Look At Position is an *offset* from this centroid of the target object.
parameters.heading: Constraints

parameters.label: Up Vector Method
parameters.description: Controls how the up vector is set. X Axis: Use 1,0,0 as the up axis. Y Axis: Use 0,1,0 as the up axis. Custom: Us the value of the Up Vector parameter as the up axis.
parameters.heading: Constraints

parameters.label: Up Vector
parameters.description: When Up Vector Method is Custom, this is the up axis to use for the look-at constraint.
parameters.heading: Constraints

parameters.label: Twist
parameters.description: A twist rotation (around the -Z axis, clockwise, in degrees), applied after the lookout transform.
parameters.heading: Constraints

parameters.label: Intensity
parameters.description: A linear scale on the power output of the light.
parameters.heading: Base Properties

parameters.label: Exposure
parameters.description: Scales the power output exponentially as a power of 2, similar to an F-stop control. 0 does not scale intensity, negative numbers scale intensity down by the square, positive numbers scale intensity up. Often you will set the Intensity to what looks like the right amount of light, and then use this parameter to "tweak" it.
parameters.heading: Base Properties

parameters.label: Color
parameters.description: The color of the light, in energy-linear terms.
parameters.heading: Base Properties

parameters.label: Enable Color Temperature
parameters.description: Use Color Temperature to control the light color. The color calculated by Color Temperature is *multiplied* by the RGB color in Color, so if you want the "pure" temperature color, you should set Color to 1.0, 1.0, 1.0.
parameters.heading: Base Properties

parameters.label: Color Temperature
parameters.description: When Enable Color Temperature is on, the temperature (in degrees Kelvin) to simulate. The valid range is from 1000 to 10000. Lower values are warmer and higher values are cooler. The default is the common D65 white point. If necessary, you can compute the same color value using the UsdLuxBlackbodyTemperatureAsRgb() function from the USD library.
parameters.heading: Base Properties

parameters.label: Clipping Range
parameters.description: Don't show geometry closer than the near distance or farther away than the far distance (in world units).
parameters.heading: Base Properties

parameters.label: Normalize Power
parameters.description: Divides the set power output (intensity scaled by exposure) by the surface area or angular size of the light. This makes it easier to adjust and compare energy output without it being affected by the size of the light.
parameters.heading: Base Properties

parameters.label: Diffuse Multiplier
parameters.description: Scales the effect this light has on the diffuse response of shaders. This is a non-physical "tweak".
parameters.heading: Base Properties

parameters.label: Specular Multiplier
parameters.description: Scales the effect this light has on the specular response of shaders. This is a non-physical "tweak".
parameters.heading: Base Properties

parameters.label: Scale Guide Geometry
parameters.description: Applies a uniform scaling factor on the guide geometry that is drawn for the light in the viewport. The default value is an expression that inverts the "meters per unit" value of the USD stage to produce a consistent real-world size for the guide geometry.
parameters.heading: Base Properties

parameters.label: Show in Viewport Camera Menu
parameters.description: Turn off this option to prevent this light from showing up in the camera menu in the viewport. This can be useful to hide lights that are embedded in props, or other lights that are not meant to be modified.
parameters.heading: Base Properties

parameters.label: Light Filters
parameters.description: A space-separated list of light filters you want to use with the light. You can create a light filter in a Light Filter Library LOP.
parameters.heading: Base Properties

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: When Type is Cylinder, Disk, or Sphere, the radius of the light.
parameters.heading: Base Properties

parameters.label: Length
parameters.description: When Type is Cylinder, the length of the light from end to end.
parameters.heading: Base Properties

parameters.label: Geometry
parameters.description: When Type is Geometry, the path to a geometry prim to use as the light shape.
parameters.heading: Base Properties

parameters.label: Width
parameters.description: When Type is Rectangle, the width of the light area.
parameters.heading: Base Properties

parameters.label: Height
parameters.description: When Type is Rectangle, the height of the light area.
parameters.heading: Base Properties

parameters.label: Angle
parameters.description: When Type is Distant, the angular size of the light in degrees. As an example, the Sun is approximately 0.53 degrees as seen from Earth. Higher values broaden the light and therefore soften shadow edges.
parameters.heading: Base Properties

parameters.label: Texture
parameters.description: Maps a texture to the area geometry of lights. This is currently only supported with rectangular lights.
parameters.heading: Base Properties

parameters.label: Spotlight
parameters.description: Turn the light into a spotlight.
parameters.heading: Shaping

parameters.label: Angle
parameters.description: The spread angle of the spotlight beam, in degrees.
parameters.heading: Shaping

parameters.label: Softness
parameters.description: Blurs the edges of the spotlight beam, simulating light leakage and bounce.
parameters.heading: Shaping

parameters.label: Left Barndoor
parameters.description: Slides in a light blocker from the left, covering part of the spotlight cone. 1.0 reaches all the way across the cone, blocking all light.
parameters.heading: Shaping

parameters.label: Left Barndoor Edge
parameters.description: Extends the solid light blocker above by an additional soft edge. 1.0 creates a gradient as wide as the spotlight cone.
parameters.heading: Shaping

parameters.label: Right Barndoor
parameters.description: Slides in a light blocker from the right, covering part of the spotlight cone. 1.0 reaches all the way across the cone, blocking all light.
parameters.heading: Shaping

parameters.label: Right Barndoor Edge
parameters.description: Extends the solid light blocker above by an additional soft edge. 1.0 creates a gradient as wide as the spotlight cone.
parameters.heading: Shaping

parameters.label: Top Barndoor
parameters.description: Slides in a light blocker from the top, covering part of the spotlight cone. 1.0 reaches all the way across the cone, blocking all light.
parameters.heading: Shaping

parameters.label: Top Barndoor Edge
parameters.description: Extends the solid light blocker above by an additional soft edge. 1.0 creates a gradient as wide as the spotlight cone.
parameters.heading: Shaping

parameters.label: Bottom Barndoor
parameters.description: Slides in a light blocker from the bottom, covering part of the spotlight cone. 1.0 reaches all the way across the cone, blocking all light.
parameters.heading: Shaping

parameters.label: Bottom Barndoor Edge
parameters.description: Extends the solid light blocker above by an additional soft edge. 1.0 creates a gradient as wide as the spotlight cone.
parameters.heading: Shaping

parameters.label: Focus
parameters.description: When turned, you can focus the beam with the numerical Focus parameter.
parameters.heading: Shaping

parameters.label: Focus
parameters.description: A control to shape the spread of light. Higher focus values pull light towards the center and narrow the spread. (This is implemented as an off-axis cosine power exponent.)
parameters.heading: Shaping

parameters.label: Focus Tint
parameters.description: Off-axis color tint, tints the light in the falloff region. The default is black.
parameters.heading: Shaping

parameters.label: IES
parameters.description: Use an IES file describing angular distribution of light.
parameters.heading: Shaping

parameters.label: File
parameters.description: An IES (Illumination Engineering Society) format file to use to control angular distribution of light.
parameters.heading: Shaping

parameters.label: Normalize
parameters.description: When turned on, the IES intensities are normalized to preserve the light's energy output. Note, that IES profiles have no effect on distant lights.
parameters.heading: Shaping

parameters.label: Angle Scale
parameters.description: A global scale on angles found in the IES file.
parameters.heading: Shaping

parameters.label: Enable
parameters.description: When this is on, objects hit by this light will cast shadows (subject to shadow masks).
parameters.heading: Shadow

parameters.label: Color
parameters.description: Tints the color of shadows cast by this light. Changing this from black (0, 0, 0) is a non-physical "tweak".
parameters.heading: Shadow

parameters.label: Falloff Start Distance
parameters.description: The near distance at which shadow falloff begins. The default value (-1) indicates no falloff.
parameters.heading: Shadow

parameters.label: Falloff Gamma
parameters.description: A gamma (i.e., exponential) control over shadow strength with linear distance within the falloff zone (between Falloff and Distance).
parameters.heading: Shadow

parameters.label: Distance
parameters.description: The maximum distance to check for objects shadowing this light. The default is -1, meaning no limit. Setting this may speed up rendering if you know all objects you want shadowed are within a certain distance.
parameters.heading: Shadow

parameters.label: MIS Bias
parameters.description: Controls whether multiple importance sampling will sample from the BSDF, the light, or both the BSDF and light.
parameters.heading: Sampling

parameters.label: Sampling Quality
parameters.description: This is the per-light sampling quality, that acts as a multiplier on the global Light Sampling Quality. Increasing the quality will add additional samples for this light source, improving the sampling quality of this light relative to other light sources.
parameters.heading: Sampling

parameters.label: Sampling Mode
parameters.description: When using the light tree for rendering, Karma will try to put any light source that's compatible into the tree. This option can force a light to be excluded from the tree and subject to uniform sampling, which can sometimes yield an improved sampling quality the light at the expense of speed.
parameters.heading: Sampling

parameters.label: Maximum HDRI Size
parameters.description: If an environment map is larger than this resolution, it will be scaled down when performing texture analysis. If the map has some very small, very bright values, this filtering may affect how sampling of the environment map is performed.
parameters.heading: Sampling

parameters.label: Portal MIS Bias
parameters.description: Controls whether the dome light is more likely to sample from the environment map or the portal geometry. For high-contrast HDRI with strong light sources, it may be beneficial to sample more from the environment map (set it less than 0), and for low-contrast/flat HDRI, the opposite may be true (set it greater than 0). Leave it at ß for balanced approach.
parameters.heading: Sampling

parameters.label: Improve Volume Sampling (Equiangular MIS)
parameters.description: Reduce noise in cases where the light is inside a volume, or in very close proximity to a volume (does not apply to directional light or dome light which do not have defined origin in world space). This feature is most effective in cases where the noise is mostly caused by sparsity of volume samples near the light source, either because the volume is too thin, or because the light has relatively small surface area. NOTE: If the volume has spectral opacity, this might introduce slight bias in output hue.
parameters.heading: Sampling

parameters.label: Light Shader
parameters.description: Defines a VEX shader to be used for light evaluation. If the string is empty, the value will be taken from the HOUDINI_VEX_DEFAULT_LIGHTSURFACE configuration variable.
parameters.heading: Light

parameters.label: Active Radius
parameters.description: Artificially clamp the illumination distance from the light. Outside this radius, the light will have no effect.
parameters.heading: Light

parameters.label: Point Light Radius
parameters.description: As point lights get closer to geometry, the attenuation equation causes the intensity of lights to go to infinity (a singularity caused by the division by the distance between the light and the surface). Increasing this value to something larger than zero creates an artificial buffer zone to prevent the light from going to infinity. If the radius is set to 1, the brightest value for the point light will be twice the intensity specified on the light. If the value is 1.4142 (sqrt(2)), the brightest value will be the intensity specified. For distant geometry, there should be very little change in the intensity.
parameters.heading: Light

parameters.label: Single Sided
parameters.description: Does the light emit light from a single side (ie along the normal) or from both sides? This only has effect on planar area light types.
parameters.heading: Light

parameters.label: Render Light Geometry
parameters.description: Causes the light source geometry to be visible in the render. Always turn this option on if you want to use the light as a portal light.
parameters.heading: Light

parameters.label: Light Geometry Casts Shadow
parameters.description: Causes the light source geometry to cast shadows in the render.
parameters.heading: Light

parameters.label: LPE Tag
parameters.description: Custom label assigned to lights or objects for use with Light Path Expressions.
parameters.heading: Light

parameters.label: Illuminate Background Holdout
parameters.description: If a light exists to add new light source instead of trying to replicate lighting in the live action plate, enable this parameter so that its effect on background holdout geometry shows up in indirect bounces and its contribution to shadow holdout AOVs is omitted.
parameters.heading: Light

parameters.label: Contributions
parameters.description: Provides detailed control over which BSDF component the light affects.
parameters.heading: Light

parameters.label: Contributes to Caustics
parameters.description: Default is true. Note that Karma only renders caustics if they are enabled on _both the light and the object_. This option has no effect unless you also turn on Enable Caustics on the geometry object.
parameters.heading: Light

parameters.label: Flip Rectangle Light Texture
parameters.description: Specifies how the texture applied to a rectangle light is flipped. Default is FlipX to match the USD specification. Only supported on rectangle light type. Options are None, FlipX, FlipY, and FlipXY.
parameters.heading: Light

parameters.label: Attenuation Type
parameters.description: Controls the type of attenuation on the light source in the default light shader. This may be none: No attenuation half: Half distance attenuation physical: Physically correct attenuation
parameters.heading: Light

parameters.label: Attenuation Start
parameters.description: Minimum light distance to be used for attenuation.
parameters.heading: Light

parameters.label: Attenuation
parameters.description: The distance from the light at which Half Distance Attenuation produces half the light intensity.
parameters.heading: Light

parameters.label: Spread
parameters.description: Ranges between 0 to 1 and controls beam direction along the light's normal. A value of 1 results in diffuse emission, and a value close to 0 gives parallel beams of light similar to directional light. Note that the Spread option is only supported for area lights with Type set to Rectangle or Disk. In conjunction with Disk lights you can, for example, create focused laser beams by leaving Spread at 0.
parameters.heading: Light

entries.label: Light Filter Library
entries.summary: Authors USD light filter primitives from VOP nodes.

parameters.label: Allow Shader Parameter Animation
parameters.description: When it is turned off, all USD values are assumed non-animatable and will be authored at a default time code. And, with this option turned on, shader node parameters that are time-dependent will get translated to USD values at non-default time codes, while time-independent parameters will still author a value at a default time code. Note, checking parameter time dependency can be costly and may add up to a large portion of the shader translation time. Since the vast majority of shader nodes don't have animated parameters, this toggle is off by default to save the work involved in checking it.

parameters.label: Parent Primitive Type
parameters.description: If the intermediate prims in a material path don't exist, the node will create them. This controls the type of the intermediate prims this node creates.

parameters.label: Light Filter Path Prefix
parameters.description: This is automatically prefixed to any material paths that are not absolute (do not start with a slash). This lets you specify relative paths in the multi-parm, and set their common USD parent hierarchy in this one parameter.

parameters.label: Tab Menu Mask
parameters.description: Defines the node categories you want to show in the tab menu when you dive into the library.
parameters.heading: Tab Menu

parameters.label: Light Filter Network
parameters.description: Node path to the VOP network containing light filter nodes to import. The node looks for light filters here when you click Auto-fill Light Filters. Set this to . (a single period) to use the VOP subnet inside this node.
parameters.heading: Fill

parameters.label: Container Path
parameters.description: The default parent scene graph path of newly created light filters. This is prefixed to the ligtht filter names to get the filter prim path when you click Auto-fill Materials.
parameters.heading: Fill

parameters.label: Auto-fill Light Filters
parameters.description: Click this to automatically create instances of the multi-parm for each light filter node in Fill > Material Network. This button will look for the light filters VOP with material flag turned on inside the network specified in Fill > Light Filter Network. Each such node will be filled into own multi-parm instance. The filled entry will also use the Fill > Container Path for the USD path at which to author the USD light filter translated from that node.
parameters.heading: Fill

parameters.label: Number of Light Filters
parameters.description: The number of light filters to create. Set the number or click the plus and minus buttons to add or remove light filters.
parameters.heading: Fill

parameters.label: Include Only VOPs with Material Flag Set
parameters.label_norm: include only vops with material flag set
parameters.description: If Light Filter VOP is a pattern, this excludes VOP nodes that don't have the Material flag on.
parameters.heading: Fill

parameters.label: Light Filter VOP
parameters.description: The Houdini node path to a VOP node representing a light filter. This can be a node pattern, in which case this node will translate all matched nodes to USD light filter primitives.
parameters.heading: Fill

parameters.label: Light Filter Path
parameters.description: The scene graph path at which to create the USD prim. If this is an absolute path (starts with a slash), it is used as-is. If this path is relative, it is relative to the path in the Path Prefix parameter.
parameters.heading: Fill

parameters.label: Assign to Light
parameters.description: When this is on, you can assign the newly created light filters to light prims using the Light Path parameter below.
parameters.heading: Fill

parameters.label: Light Path
parameters.description: When Assign to Light is on, assigns the newly created light filters to the USD light primitives listed in this parameter.
parameters.heading: Fill

entries.label: Light Linker
entries.summary: Creates USD light link properties based on rules.

parameters.label: Number of Collections
parameters.description: The number of USD collections that this node will create. For each collection, a separate set of parameters are used to define the collection's name, USD prim and members.

parameters.label: Collection # Prim
parameters.description: The USD prim where the collection will be authored.

parameters.label: Collection # Name
parameters.description: The name of the new collection. Replaces any existing group of the same name on the same prim.

parameters.label: Collection # Includes
parameters.description: Space separated list of prim patterns that will be included in the collection.

parameters.label: Collection # Excludes
parameters.description: Space separated list of prim patterns that will be excluded from the include list.

parameters.label: Number of Links
parameters.description: The number of link rules defined. Each rule will define its own source primitive, includes list, excludes list, link type, and enable control.

parameters.label: Rule # Enabled
parameters.description: If false (unchecked) this rule will be ignored completely.

parameters.label: Rule # Prim
parameters.description: The source primitive or collection for this rule. A standard rule will author the link on this primitive or each primitive in the collection.

parameters.label: Rule # Includes
parameters.description: Space separated list of prim patterns that will be included in the link.

parameters.label: Rule # Excludes
parameters.description: Space separated list of prim patterns that will be excluded from the include list.

parameters.label: Rule # Type
parameters.description: Indicates the type of link that will be created, this could be either Light Link or Shadow Link.

parameters.label: Rule # Reversed
parameters.description: If true (checked) indicates that this rule will need to synthesize rules to produce the effect of the rule.

entries.label: Light Mixer
entries.summary: Lets you interactively edit USD properties for multiple lights.

parameters.label: Number of Collections
parameters.description: The number of USD collections that this node will create. For each collection, a separate set of parameters are used to define the collection's name, USD prim and members.

parameters.label: Collection # Prim
parameters.description: The USD prim where the collection will be authored.

parameters.label: Collection # Name
parameters.description: The name of the new collection. Replaces any existing group of the same name on the same prim.

parameters.label: Collection # Includes
parameters.description: Space separated list of prim patterns that will be included in the collection.

parameters.label: Collection # Excludes
parameters.description: Space separated list of prim patterns that will be excluded from the include list.

parameters.description: The order in which Houdini applies translates, rotates, and scales, and the order in which it applies rotation.
parameters.heading: Transforms

parameters.label: Translate
parameters.description: Movement amount along XYZ axes.
parameters.heading: Transforms

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.description: Degrees rotation around XYZ axes.
parameters.heading: Transforms

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: Non-uniform scaling along XYZ axes.
parameters.heading: Transforms

parameters.label: Shear
parameters.description: Amount of shearing. The three values represent shearing in the X direction on the XY plane, in the X direction on the XZ plane, and in the Y direction on the YZ plane, respectively.
parameters.heading: Transforms

parameters.label: Uniform Scale
parameters.description: Scales the object uniformly along all three axes.
parameters.heading: Transforms

entries.label: Live Render
entries.summary: Launches renders which react to upstream LOP changes and send the image to the Render Gallery.

parameters.label: Start Render
parameters.description: Starts a render and creates a new entry in the Render Gallery for it.

parameters.label: Stop Render
parameters.description: Stops the current render associated with this node. In the Render Gallery, the imaged rendered thus far will be saved to disk.

parameters.label: Render Delegate
parameters.description: The Hydra client to use to render the images. The default is Karma CPU. Alternate Hydra clients must be registered with Houdini's USD libraries. The USD Render ROP has more information on how the node gets the list of available renderers.

parameters.label: Render Settings
parameters.description: Scene graph path to the RenderSettings prim to render with. If this is blank, the node looks for default render settings on the root prim. If the root prim has no render settings, the node will use default settings.

parameters.label: Render Pass
parameters.description: Scene graph path to the RenderPass prim to use for specifying object visibility etc. If this is blank, the default setting, the render will continue with no pass (i.e., all contents will be rendered).

parameters.label: Override Camera
parameters.description: Scene graph path to the Camera prim to render from. If this is blank, the node uses the camera specified on the render settings primitive.

parameters.label: Override Resolution
parameters.description: Override the resolution by either scaling the USD resolution by a percentage or by specifying a specific resolution.

parameters.label: Resolution Scale
parameters.description: Specify a scale (as a percentage) for the output resolution.

parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.description: Specify a resolution explicitly.

parameters.label: Expand Procedurals
parameters.description: Run all the procedurals on the stage. Note that this takes place before the custom dive target LOP network is cooked (if Run Internal LOP Network is enabled).

parameters.label: Run Internal LOP Network
parameters.description: Execute the custom LOP network inside this node's dive target. This is useful for any further "end-of-chain" overrides, not exposed via the parameters mentioned above, that you still want applied to a live render. Note that this takes place after procedurals have been expanded (if Expand Procedurals is enabled).

entries.label: Loft Payload Info
entries.summary: Adds basic information from inside a payload to the primitive that loads the payload.

parameters.label: Sampling Behavior
parameters.description: Cooking this node can generate many USD time samples, rather than just a single time sample at the current time. This can be equivalent to having a Cache LOP following this node, but it will evaluate much faster, and does not cache data from any other nodes. This allows animated data to be authored to USD without introducing a node time dependency which would then cause all following nodes to also be time dependent. This can vastly improve playback performance of some LOP Networks. In all sampling modes, if a parameter on this node does not vary with time, and does not rely on other time sampled data from the stage, only a single default value will be generated in USD for the corresponding attribute. USD time samples are only generated for parameters that may vary over time. Sample Current Frame: A single time sample will be generated for the current time. Sample Frame Range If Input Is Not Time Dependent: If the input to this node is time dependent, this node behaves as if it is in Sample Current Frame mode. Otherwise it behaves as if it is in Sample Frame Range mode. Sample Frame Range: The Start/End/Inc parameter is used to generate multiple times at which this node's parameters are evaluated, and a USD time sample is created for each attribute at each one of these times.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Start/End/Inc
parameters.description: When the Sampling behavior is Sample Frame Range, this parameter controls the number and spacing of base time samples to be generated by this node. The default values of this parameter are @fstart, @fend, and @finc. These values correspond to the start, end, and step size of the global Houdini animation settings when interacting with Houdini. When using a ROP node to generate a range of frames, these values correspond to the start, end, and increment values specified on the ROP node being executed. This default ensures that a USD file written to disk will contain time samples for exactly the frame range requested by the ROP (regardless of the Houdini animation settings).
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Subframe Sampling
parameters.description: For each primary sample generated by this node, these parameters can cause additional samples to be generated around that primary sample time. This is most often used to ensure that accurate data exists at exactly the camera shutter open and close times, as well as at the primary sample time.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Shutter
parameters.description: Controls the method used to specify the shutter open and close times relative to the primary sample times. Specify Manually: The Shutter Open/Close parameter values provide exact offset values relative to the primary sample time. Use Camera Prim: The Camera Prim parameter provides the scene graph path of a camera primitive from which the shutter open and close times are extracted to provide the offset values relative to the primary time sample.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Shutter Open/Close
parameters.description: When Shutter is set to Specify Manually, these two offset values are added to the primary sample time to indicate the shutter open and close times. The open time should be less than or equal to zero, and the close time should be greater than or equal to zero.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Camera Prim
parameters.description: When Shutter is set to Use Camera Prim, this is the scene graph path of a camera prim on the input node's stage. The shutter open and close attribute values are read from this primitive.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Samples
parameters.description: The number of subframe samples to create for each primary sample. These samples are evenly distributed between the shutter open and close times. Note that such an even distribution may or may not create a sample at exactly the primary sample time.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Always Include Frame Sample
parameters.description: When turned on, forces a sample to be created at exactly the primary sample time. If the Samples value, together with the shutter open and close times, already place a sample at the primary sample time, turning on this option has no effect. Otherwise, this option causes an addition sample to be added. This means that the actual number of samples per primary sample may in fact be one more than the number specified in the Samples parameter.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.description: The primitive(s) the node should operate on. You can drag primitives from the scene graph tree pane into this textbox to add their paths, or click the Smallicon:BUTTONS/reselect Reselect button beside the text box to select the primitives in the viewer, or ((Ctrl))-click the Reselect button to choose prims from a pop-up tree window. You can also use primitive patterns for advanced matching, including matching all prims in a collection (using /path/to/prim.collection:<<name>>). You can drag and drop a specific (or multiple specific) USD prim(s) from the Scene Graph Tree into the window to run validation on only these USD primitives. NOTE: This parameter needs to be exposed in order for the transform handles to be context-aware. Without it, the handles may not be positioned properly.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Set Primitive Statistics
parameters.description: Adds metadata to the prim containing information about the number of primitives appearing under the payload prim.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Set Geometry Count Statistics
parameters.description: If Set Primitive Statistics is turned on, this option can also be turned on to generated more detailed statistics such as the number of faces on mesh prims. Calculating this additional information will be slower than simply collecting primitive counts.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Number of Colors
parameters.description: Specify colors to be applied to the payload primitives which will control the appearance of the bounding box representation of the prim when the payload is unloaded.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Set Color
parameters.description: For this multiparm instance, control whether the specified color will be applied to the prim. Expressions for this parmeter can use the @numprim (total number of prims being processed), @prim (index of the current prim being processed) and @primpath (scene graph path of the prim being processed) local variables to help provide variation across many primitives.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Color
parameters.description: The color applied to each primitive. This parameter can also use the @numprim, @prim, and @primpath local variables to provide variation across prims.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

entries.label: Look At Constraint
entries.summary: Constrains a prim to always point toward a target.
