parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: Whether the source (the thing that looks) is a regular primitive, or a point instance. You *cannot* use a nested point instance as a source.
parameters.heading: Source

parameters.label: Source
parameters.description: When Source Type is Primitive, the scene graph path to the prim to use.
parameters.heading: Source

parameters.label: Source Instances
parameters.description: When Source Type is PointInstancer, the point instance to use, using /<<path>><<instance_index>> syntax (for example, /geometry/instancer1).
parameters.heading: Source

parameters.label: Target Source
parameters.description: Where to get the target to look at: a prim from the first input or the second input, or a world space position specified by a parameter.
parameters.heading: Look At

parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: When Target Source is First Input or Second Input, whether the thing to look at is a regular primitive, or a point instance. You *can* use a nested point instance as a target.
parameters.heading: Look At

parameters.label: Target Position
parameters.description: When Target Source is Position, the world space position to look at. You can use expressions to compute or animate the target position.
parameters.heading: Look At

parameters.label: Target
parameters.description: When Target Type is Primitive, the scene graph path to the prim to use.
parameters.heading: Look At

parameters.label: Target Instance
parameters.description: When Target Type is PointInstancer, the point instance to use, using /<<path>><<instance_index>> syntax (for example, /geometry/instancer1).
parameters.heading: Look At

parameters.label: Hide Target
parameters.description: When Target Source is First Input and Type is Primitive, whether to hide set the path's visibility to "hidden".
parameters.heading: Look At

parameters.label: Import Time
parameters.description: Specify the frame at which the source and/or target geometry are imported into the embedded SOP network to build the constraints. The default $FF expression forces the constraint LOP to be time dependent, which is needed when operating on a non time-dependent network that has time samples driving the source or target primitives. However, for better performance with a non time-dependent network with no time samples, it is recommended to use a static value instead.
parameters.heading: Look At

parameters.label: Look At Axis
parameters.description: Which axis on the source object to match to the look at vector. You can use this to compensate for the orientation the source object was created in. This can't be the same as the Look Up Axis.
parameters.heading: Orientation

parameters.label: Look Up Axis
parameters.description: Which axis on the source object to match to the up vector. You can use this to compensate for the orientation the source object was created in. This can't be the same as the Look At Axis.
parameters.heading: Orientation

parameters.label: Up Vector
parameters.description: How to compute the up vector. X Axis: Use the world +X direction as the up vector. Y Axis: Use the world +Y direction as the up vector. Z Axis: Use the world +Z direction as the up vector. From Primitive: Rotate the source prim so its up vector points at a specific prim as it moves along the curve. Custom: Use the vector in the Up Vector parameter.
parameters.heading: Orientation

parameters.label: Up Vector Source
parameters.description: When Up Vector is From Primitive, where to get the primitive to point the up vector at (the first or second input).
parameters.heading: Orientation

parameters.label: Up Vector Xform
parameters.description: When Look Up Mode is From Primitive, the scene graph path of the prim to point the up vector at. (This does not support point instances.)
parameters.heading: Orientation

parameters.label: Twist
parameters.description: Angle (in degrees) to rotate around the look-at direction.
parameters.heading: Orientation

entries.label: LPE Tag
entries.summary: Manage Lights' LPE Tags.

parameters.label: LPE Tag Attribute
parameters.description: Specify the LPE Tag attribute. By default, the node uses inputs:karma:light:lpetag to work with Karma, however, other renderers may require a different attribute altogether.

parameters.label: Geo Light LPE Tag Attribute
parameters.description: Specify the geometry LPE Tag attribute. By default, the node uses primvars:karma:object:lpetag to work with Karma, however, other renderers may require a different attribute altogether.

parameters.label: Additional Geometry Prims
parameters.description: Specify the geo prims to assign or modify LPE tags.

parameters.label: Default LPE Tag
parameters.description: Specify a default LPE tag to assign to lights or prims without an existing LPE tag.

parameters.label: Tag Using
parameters.description: None: No rule based tag will be applied. Light Name: Create a unique LPE tag per light, using the light's name. If multiple lights share the same name, an _ and a digit will be appended to the tag, ensuring they remain unique. Light Index: Create a unique LPE tag per light, using the prefix and the lights index for the tag. Type Name: Create a unique LPE tag per light type. Lights of the same type will share the same LPE tag. Token: With the Separator to tokenize the lights name, uses the token at the index given at Index as LPE tag. VEXpression: Use VEX to set the tag value.

parameters.label: Prefix
parameters.description: When Tag Using is Light Index, you can specify a prefix for the LPE tag.

parameters.label: Separator
parameters.description: When Tag Using is Token, you can enter the character that is used to tokenize the lights' name.
parameters.heading: Tokens

parameters.label: Index
parameters.description: When Tag Using is Token,. this is the index of the tokenized lights' name to use as LPE tag. For example, with Separator set to _ and an index of 0, lights Key_spotlight1, Fill_pointlight1, Fill_pointlight2, Env_domelight1 will result in LPE tags Key, Fill and Env. NOTE: Negative indices can be used. -1will ensure the last token is always used.
parameters.heading: Tokens

parameters.label: VEXpression
parameters.description: When Tag Using is VEXpression, you can add VEX code here to be run over the lights, setting the tag value.
parameters.heading: Tokens

parameters.label: Populate
parameters.description: Automatically populate the multiparm based on the default tag and rule based LPE Tag assignments.
parameters.heading: Tokens

parameters.label: Manual Tags
parameters.description: Specify manual LPE Tag assignments for more explicit control.
parameters.heading: Tokens

parameters.label: Enable
parameters.description: Turn on the following LPE Tag assignment.
parameters.heading: Tokens

parameters.label: LPE Tag
parameters.description: The LPE tag to assign.
parameters.heading: Tokens

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.description: The USD primitives to assign the LPE Tag to.
parameters.heading: Tokens

entries.label: Mask from Bounds
entries.summary: Sets a primvar based on whether/by how much selected prims are inside a bounding shape.

parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: What type of primitives to add the primvar to. Point Instances: Specify a list of individual instances using /<<path>><<instance_index>> syntax. Primitives/Native Instances: Specify a list of prim paths, including instanceable prims.

parameters.label: Instances
parameters.description: A space-separated list of instances, using /<<path>><<instance_index>> syntax (for example, /geometry/instancer0 /geometry/instancer1). To select all instances in an instancer, use /<<path>>*. To select a range, use /geometry/instancer4-7 (the range is inclusive). To select instances inside nested instancers, use multiple indexes, for example /geometry/instancer27. VEXpressions can be used to specify instances, for example, /geometry/instancer{@weights>0.5}.

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.description: When Type is Primitives/Native Instances, a space-separated list of prim paths/patterns to add the primvar to.

parameters.label: Bounding Type
parameters.description: Choose between a box, sphere, or use external geometry prims as the boundary.
parameters.heading: Bounds

parameters.label: Size
parameters.description: When Bounding Type is Box or Sphere, the size of the bounding volume.
parameters.heading: Bounds

parameters.label: Center
parameters.description: Moves the bounding volume.
parameters.heading: Bounds

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.description: Rotation of the bounding volume.
parameters.heading: Bounds

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: When Bounding Type is Primitives (Geometry), scales the bounding volume created from the external geometry.
parameters.heading: Bounds

parameters.label: Pivot Translate
parameters.description: When Bounding Type is Primitives (Geometry), moves the pivot for rotating ans scaling the bounding volume created from the external geometry.
parameters.heading: Bounds

parameters.label: Primitive Source
parameters.description: When Bounding Type is Primitives (Geometry), whether to get bounding primitives from the stage connected to this node's first input or the second input.
parameters.heading: Bounds

parameters.label: Bounding Primitives
parameters.description: When Bounding Type is Primitives (Geometry), a space-separated list of prim paths/patterns to use to define the bounding volume.
parameters.heading: Bounds

parameters.label: Feather
parameters.description: Creates a soft falloff between values "inside" and "outside" the bounding shape. Negative values apply the falloff inside the boundary, positive values apply falloff outside the boundary. The greater the difference from 0, the larger the falloff radius. When this is non-zero, primvar values on points/faces (0.0 or 1.0) are multiplied by a linear gradient from 1 to 0 between the bounds and this distance.
parameters.heading: Bounds

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.description: Shrinks (negative values) or grows (positive values) the boundary shape.
parameters.heading: Bounds

parameters.label: Invert Bounds
parameters.description: Reverses the meaning of the primvar values, so 0.0 indicates _inside_ and 1.0 indicates _outside_.
parameters.heading: Bounds

parameters.label: Ignore Primitives Outside Bounds
parameters.description: When this on, the node does not author the primvar on selected prims outside the bounding box. This is faster than authoring 0.0 values.
parameters.heading: Bounds

parameters.label: Add Primvar
parameters.description: Adds a primvar indicating how much of each prim is inside the bounding volume.
parameters.heading: Primvar

parameters.label: Name
parameters.description: The name of the primvar to create.
parameters.heading: Primvar

parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: Specify the data type for the primvar. The default is float. If you choose boolean or a number type that does not support decimals, features such as Feather will have no effect. This should be boolean, int, float, or double. Most other types won't work (the values will all be zero).
parameters.heading: Primvar

parameters.label: Interpolation
parameters.description: This controls the "level" at which the node creates the primvar. Constant: Calculates one inside/outside value for the *entire mesh*, by combining the values for each point using the Method below. Uniform: Sets a 1.0 or 0.0 on each *face* indicating whether the face is inside or outside the bounding volume. Vertex: Sets a 1.0 or 0.0 on each *point*. Face Varying: Sets a 1.0 or 0.0 on each *polygon corner*. NOTE: * In USD, Constant interpolation is equivalent to a Houdini detail attribute. * Uniform interpolation is equivalent to a Houdini primitive attribute. * FaceVarying interpolation is equivalent to a Houdini vertex attribute. * Vertex interpolation is (confusingly) equivalent to a Houdini point attribute.
parameters.heading: Primvar

parameters.label: Method
parameters.description: When Interpolation is Constant, this is the node combines the point values to compute an overall value for the entire mesh. The default is Average, which is the most useful method. Maximum: Use the highest point value. Minimum: Use the lowest point value. Average: Use the mean (average) of all point values across the mesh. First Match: Use the value of the first point. Last Match: Use the value of the last point. Centroid: Don't use point values, instead calculate if the mesh's centroid is inside or outside.
parameters.heading: Primvar

parameters.label: Value
parameters.description: The value to use for "inside". The default is 1.0.
parameters.heading: Primvar

parameters.label: Add Weights
parameters.description: Creates a property (not a primvar) on the prims, set to the same value as would be computed for a Constant primvar, using the Method below.
parameters.heading: Weights, Collection and Selection Rule

parameters.label: Weight Name
parameters.description: The name of the weight property to create.
parameters.heading: Weights, Collection and Selection Rule

parameters.label: Method
parameters.description: See above.
parameters.heading: Weights, Collection and Selection Rule

parameters.label: Add Collection
parameters.description: Creates a new collection containing the prims that have a non-zero weight attribute. This is only available when Add Weights is on.
parameters.heading: Weights, Collection and Selection Rule

parameters.label: Collection Name
parameters.description: The name of the collection to add the primitives to. This is always created on the /collections prim (this node creates /collections if it doesn't already exist).
parameters.heading: Weights, Collection and Selection Rule

parameters.label: Add Selection Rule
parameters.description: When Type is Primitives/Native Instances, create a selection rule with a given name.
parameters.heading: Weights, Collection and Selection Rule

parameters.label: Selection Rule Name
parameters.description: Specify the selection rule name, which can then be used using the %rule:selectionrulename syntax by downstream LOP nodes.
parameters.heading: Weights, Collection and Selection Rule

parameters.label: Import Frame
parameters.description: The frame at which to cook the LOP node and sample the stage. When importing animated geometry, this could be set to $FF.
parameters.heading: Time

entries.summary: Authors USD material primitives from shader VOP nodes.

parameters.label: Auto-generate Preview Surface Shaders
parameters.description: When possible, the LOP will generate a USD Preview Surface VOP primitive. This shader type is part of the USD standard and should be implemented by all USD renderers, so this shader (which may be an approximation of the original shader) should show up in any renderer, even if the renderer doesn't understand the original shader type. Note, if textures are involved, the auto-generated preview network will wire the alpha output of a USD Texture Reader primitive to the opacity input of a USD Preview Surface shader primitive. Some renderers, like Storm, are known to mishandle the opacity, leading to artifacts in the viewport. To workaround such cases, you can turn this toggle off and then you can manually create a USD Preview network inside, feeding it to the Collect VOP along with the original surface shader.

parameters.label: Allow Shader Parameter Animation
parameters.description: When it is turned off, all USD values are assumed non-animatable and will be authored at a default time code. And, with this option turned on, shader node parameters that are time-dependent will get translated to USD values at non-default time codes, while time-independent parameters will still author a value at a default time code. Note, checking parameter time dependency can be costly and may add up to a large portion of the shader translation time. Since the vast majority of shader nodes don't have animated parameters, this toggle is off by default to save the work involved in checking it.

parameters.label: Reference Material Render Vars into Render Products
parameters.label_norm: reference material render vars into render products
parameters.description: When this checkbox is turned on, the LOP will reference the render vars parent scope primitive (if it exists) into the global render products namespace (i.e., /Render/Products/Vars). Some shader translators author render vars primitives inside the material, and referencing them into the global location makes it easy for renderers to include them in the render product, without traversing the whole stage to look for materials and information about their potential render vars. But if this behavior is not desirable, you can toggle this checkbox off.

parameters.label: Parent Primitive Type
parameters.description: If the intermediate prims in a material path don't exist, the node will create them. This controls the type of the intermediate prims this node creates.

parameters.label: Material Path Prefix

entries.label: Merge
entries.summary: Merges the layers from incoming stages into a unified layer stack.

parameters.label: Merge Style
parameters.description: Separate Layers: Each layer from each input is merged into a new sublayer stack in the output, sorted by strongest to weakest from the strongest (last) input, then strongest to weakest from the next strongest (second-to-last) input, and so on. This includes layers from above a Layer Break LOP, which allows such layers to continue to provide context for all subsequent layers. Separate Layers, File Layers Weakest: Like "Separate Layers" (above), except that any sublayers that refer to *existing layer files on disk* are ordered to be *weaker* than any layers authored purely in the LOP network. This is useful when combining several LOP node streams where each stream begins with one of more file layers, then applies modifications to a new layer on top of that layer. After merging these streams, all the LOP-authored modification layers will be adjacent to each other in the sublayer list for the stage. This allows all these new layers to be flattened into a single layer by the USD ROP without also flattening the layers from disk. (In the regular Separate Layers mode, layers from disk would alternate with layers authored in LOPs, and each LOP layer would have to be saved to a separate new layer on disk.) NOTE: This option can change the result of composing the stage if the opinions from layers on disk were intended to be stronger than opinions authored in the LOP network. Separate Layers, File and SOP Layers Weakest: Like Separate Layers, File Layers Weakest (above), except that sublayers imported from SOP nodes are also sorted with files loaded from disk, appearing before any layers authored purely in the LOP network. This is useful when you want the layers authored from SOPs to be saved to separate layers rather than flattened together with the layers authored in the LOP Network. Flatten Layers: All layers from all inputs are flattened together into a single output layer. Layers from above Layer Break nodes are removed prior to flattening and so do not contribute to the output. Flatten Into First Input's Active Layer: The layers on the *first* input are passed through without flattening. All layers from all other inputs are flattened into the *active layer* of the *first input*. Layers from above Layer Break nodes other than on the first input are removed prior to flattening and so do not contribute to the output. Flatten Each Input: For each input its layers are flattened, and then the flattened inputs are merged into a new sublayer stack in the output. Layers from above Layer Break nodes are removed prior to flattening and so do not contribute to the output. Simple Merge: The layer stacks from each input are combined, and sorted such that sublayers from files on disk or representing SOP nodes are made weaker than layers authored by LOP nodes. Then the layers authored by LOP nodes are flattened into a single layer that becomes the active layer for the Merge LOP. This provides a very simple and intuitive behavior in terms of combining LOP-authored layers from multiple inputs, without pulling data from disk or SOPs into this combined layer. Note that as with any operation that reorders layers, it is possible that the relative strength of some opinions may change. Specifically, after this operation, opinions from files on disk will all be weaker that any opinions authored on sublayers in the LOP Network. NOTE: Inside an Edit Layer Block this parameter will be disabled, and Flatten Into First Input's Active Layer will be used.

parameters.label: Strip Layers Above Layer Breaks
parameters.description: Enable this option to remove all layers created above Layer Break nodes on every input to this node. This option is useful when creating diamond shaped node graphs, where on one branch the top of the diamond connects to the merge at the bottom of the diamond without a Layer Break, and the other branch(es) use Layer Breaks. Without this option, in any of the Separate Layer modes, the layer stack would include two copies of every layer created above the Layer Break, which degrades performance without affecting the final composed stage. Merge styles which cause layers from inputs to be flattened always strip layers above Layer Breaks, and so will hide this parameter. This is because layers cannot be stripped after they have been flattened. The Flatten Into First Input's Active Layer merge style is a special case which flattens (and therefore strip layers) from all inputs after the first input. Note that layers above Layer Breaks will not be stripped from the first input in this mode.

entries.label: Merge PointInstancers
entries.summary: Merges point instancers into a single consolidated point instancer.

parameters.label: Target Instancer
parameters.description: Specify the path to the consolidated point instancer. This can be an existing point instancer or a new primitive entirely.

parameters.label: Instances
parameters.description: A space-separated list of instances, using /<<path>><<instance_index>> syntax (for example, /geometry/instancer0 /geometry/instancer1). To select all instances in an instancer, use /<<path>>*. To select a range, use /geometry/instancer4-7 (the range is inclusive). To select instances inside nested instancers, use multiple indexes, for example /geometry/instancer27. VEXpressions can be used to specify instances, for example, /geometry/instancer{@weights>0.5}.

parameters.label: Prune Merged Instances
parameters.description: Hide: Hides merged point instances from their previous point instancer. Delete: Removes merged point instances from their previous point instancer.

parameters.label: New Prototypes
parameters.description: In Place: When merging point instances if their prototype isn't already in the point instancer's prototypes relationship, the existing prototype primitive will be added to the prototypes relationship. Reference: When merging point instances if their prototype isn't already in the point instancer's prototypes relationship, a reference to the prototype will be created under the point instancer's Prototypes Scope primitive and added to the prototypes relationship.

entries.label: Mesh
entries.summary: Creates or edits a mesh shape primitive.

parameters.label: Sampling Behavior
parameters.description: Cooking this node can generate many USD time samples, rather than just a single time sample at the current time. This can be equivalent to having a Cache LOP following this node, but it will evaluate much faster, and does not cache data from any other nodes. This allows animated data to be authored to USD without introducing a node time dependency which would then cause all following nodes to also be time dependent. This can vastly improve playback performance of some LOP Networks. In all sampling modes, if a parameter on this node does not vary with time, and does not rely on other time sampled data from the stage, only a single default value will be generated in USD for the corresponding attribute. USD time samples are only generated for parameters that may vary over time. Sample Current Frame: A single time sample will be generated for the current time. Sample Frame Range If Input Is Not Time Dependent: If the input to this node is time dependent, this node behaves as if it is in Sample Current Frame mode. Otherwise it behaves as if it is in Sample Frame Range mode. Sample Frame Range: The Start/End/Inc parameter is used to generate multiple times at which this node's parameters are evaluated, and a USD time sample is created for each attribute at each one of these times.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Start/End/Inc
parameters.description: When the Sampling behavior is Sample Frame Range, this parameter controls the number and spacing of base time samples to be generated by this node. The default values of this parameter are @fstart, @fend, and @finc. These values correspond to the start, end, and step size of the global Houdini animation settings when interacting with Houdini. When using a ROP node to generate a range of frames, these values correspond to the start, end, and increment values specified on the ROP node being executed. This default ensures that a USD file written to disk will contain time samples for exactly the frame range requested by the ROP (regardless of the Houdini animation settings).
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Subframe Sampling
parameters.description: For each primary sample generated by this node, these parameters can cause additional samples to be generated around that primary sample time. This is most often used to ensure that accurate data exists at exactly the camera shutter open and close times, as well as at the primary sample time.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Shutter
parameters.description: Controls the method used to specify the shutter open and close times relative to the primary sample times. Specify Manually: The Shutter Open/Close parameter values provide exact offset values relative to the primary sample time. Use Camera Prim: The Camera Prim parameter provides the scene graph path of a camera primitive from which the shutter open and close times are extracted to provide the offset values relative to the primary time sample.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Shutter Open/Close
parameters.description: When Shutter is set to Specify Manually, these two offset values are added to the primary sample time to indicate the shutter open and close times. The open time should be less than or equal to zero, and the close time should be greater than or equal to zero.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Camera Prim
parameters.description: When Shutter is set to Use Camera Prim, this is the scene graph path of a camera prim on the input node's stage. The shutter open and close attribute values are read from this primitive.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Samples
parameters.description: The number of subframe samples to create for each primary sample. These samples are evenly distributed between the shutter open and close times. Note that such an even distribution may or may not create a sample at exactly the primary sample time.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Always Include Frame Sample
parameters.description: When turned on, forces a sample to be created at exactly the primary sample time. If the Samples value, together with the shutter open and close times, already place a sample at the primary sample time, turning on this option has no effect. Otherwise, this option causes an addition sample to be added. This means that the actual number of samples per primary sample may in fact be one more than the number specified in the Samples parameter.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Action
parameters.description: Whether this node should create new prims, or edit existing prims. In addition, the Force Edit option can be chosen to cause this node to ignore the houdini:editable attribute on prims, and always edit the specified attributes. This is in contrast to the Edit mode which will trigger a warning and not set attributes on prims with the houdini:editable attribute set to false.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.description: In Create mode, this lets you control where in the scene graph to create the prim(s). The default is usually /$OS. This creates a primitive at the root level with the same name as the node (for example, /tube1). This is a useful default for preventing naming conflicts, but terrible for organization. You should try to remember to change the Primitive Path to a better value when you create prims. For example, instead of naming models after the node that created them, you might want to name them after the geometry inside, and organize them under a /Models branch. The Create Primitives section contains basic controls for how to create the new prim(s).
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.description: In Edit mode, the node has a Primitive Pattern parameter. This lets you specify the prim(s) the node should operate on. You can click the select button beside the text box to select the primitives from the scene graph tree. You can also use primitive patterns for advanced matching, including matching all prims in a collection.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Allowed Primitive Types
parameters.description: In Edit mode, only prims that match one of the specified primitive types (or API schemas) can be modified by this node. Leave this parameter empty to permit editing any primitive type.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Handle Disallowed Types
parameters.description: In Edit mode, specifies what should happen when a primitive that is not one of the Allowed primitive types matches the primitive pattern Ignore Disallowed Prim Types: Do not set any attributes on this primitive, but do not notify the user.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Initialize Parameters
parameters.description: Changes the state of all control menu parameters to Do Nothing, so that this node will not apply any changes. Also grabs the current values of each property from the first Primitives match, and sets the values of the corresponding parameters to match. This means that changing any parameter's control menu to Set or Create mode will set the property to its current value, making it easier to apply changes to an existing value rather than setting a brand new value. With Rebuild Render-Specific Parameters you reset all parameters from render-specific tabs to their default values for the specific node. If you want to reset the parameters for the entire scene, you can also open the top-level Render menu and choose Rebuild All Render-Specific LOP Parameters.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Primitive Count
parameters.description: The number of primitives to create.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Primitive Type
parameters.description: Set all created prims to have this type.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Primitive Kind
parameters.description: Set all created prims to have this kind.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Primitive Specifier
parameters.description: The USD operator to use when creating the new prims. Define: Authors a completely new prim. Use this if you want to create a brand new prim or replace an existing prim. Over: Authors an override of an existing prim. Attributes not explicitly authored on this prim will get their values from the existing prim on the lower layer. Class: Define a primitive class. This is usually not necessary unless you are doing deep USD magic.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Class Ancestor
parameters.description: If Primitive Specifier is Define or Over, this parameter will cause some ancestor primitives to be authored with a specifier of Class. This makes it easy to create an Over or Define within a Class without having to use two separate nodes. When Primitive Specifier is Class, this parameter is disabled because the entire primitive hierarchy is already authored as Class primitives.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Parent Primitive Type
parameters.description: If any parents of a path in Primitive Paths do not exist, this node will automatically create them. In this case, it will create parent nodes of this type.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Color
parameters.description: Sets a "default" color for this shape, which will be used in the viewport if the prim does not have a shader/material. You can write shaders to take this displayColor parameter as an override.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Opacity
parameters.description: Sets the opacity of the display Color. This is a separate attribute (instead of specifying the display color as RGBA) so it can be independently overridden, and also because shaders don't usually accept RGBA parameters.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Subdivision Scheme
parameters.description: The subdivision scheme that should be used on this mesh to provide addition detail at render time. Catmull Clark: Use the Catmull Clark subdivision scheme to add detail to this mesh. Loop: Use the loop subdivision scheme to add detail to this mesh. Bilinear: Similar to a mesh with no subdivision, except that bilinearly subdivided meshes can be considered watertight, whereas there is no such guarantee for un-subdivided meshes, and more mesh features (e.g. holes) may apply to bilinear meshes but not simple polygon meshes. None: The mesh is not a subdivision surface, and should be treated as simple polygons.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Triangle Subdivision Rule
parameters.description: When Subdivision Scheme is Catmull Clark, the weights to use during triangle subdivision. Catmull Clark: Standard weighting method for Catmull Clark subdivision. Smooth: A smoother subdivision of triangles, but breaks the property that two separate meshes can be joined seamlessly by overlapping their boundaries.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Face Interpolation
parameters.description: How face varying (per-vertex) data is interpolated across the mesh faces during subdivision. All: Perform linear interpolation everywhere (at the boundaries and interior of the faces). None: Interpolation is smooth everywhere that the surface is smooth. Boundaries: Linearly interpolate along all boundary edges and corners. Corners Only: Linearly interpolate at corners only. Corners Plus One: Linearly interpolate at corners and do sharpening of junctions of three or more regions. Corners Plus Two: Linearly interpolate at corners, do sharpening of junctions of three or more regions, and sharpening of darts and concave corners.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Interpolation Boundary
parameters.description: How subdivision and the limit surface behave for faces adjacent to boundary edges and vertices. None: No boundary edge interpolation is applied by default. Boundary faces are treated as holes so that the boundary vertices continue to support the adjacent interior faces, but no surface corresponding to the boundary faces is generated. Edge and Corner: Similar to edge-only but the smooth curve resulting on the boundary is made to interpolate corner vertices (vertices with exactly one incident face). Edge Only: A sequence of boundary vertices defines a smooth curve to which the limit surface along boundary faces extends.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Orientation
parameters.description: Whether to compute the mesh's default surface normal using the right hand rule, or the left hand rule. The Unpack USD SOP nodes SOP Import LOP are able to change this option because Houdini geometry always uses a left handed orientation for computing normals.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Double Sided
parameters.description: For renderers that distinguish between single-sided and double-sided surfaces, controls whether this prim is double-sided. Making surfaces double-sided is necessary for flat thin surfaces, or open surfaces where the camera can see both the inside and outside of the surface.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Transform
parameters.description: How the transform parameters below apply to the primitive. (Because each USD prim can contain multiple transforms, _and_ be affected by parent transforms, there are many different ways to apply new transforms.) Append: Apply the parameters as a new, most local transform. Prepend: Apply the parameters as a new, _least_ local transform. Overwrite or Append: If a local transform exists with the name xformOp:transform, _overwrite_ it with the parameters. Otherwise, apply it as a new, most local transform. If this replaces an existing transform, that transform's order in the local transform stack is not affected. Overwrite or Prepend: Like Overwrite or Append, but _least_ local. Apply Transform in World Space: Apply the parameters as a new, most local transform. However, prior to applying the transform, it is updated so that the result of the transform appears as if the transform was being applied in world space, before any local or ancestor transformations were applied to the primitive. Replace All Local Transforms: The transform specified in the remaining transform parameters is always applied as a new transform. Prior to applying this transform, all existing transform operations on the local transform stack are cleared so that only the supplied transform remains on the local transform stack (though ancestor transforms still have an effect). Apply XformCommonAPI: The transform specified in the remaining transform parameters will be applied as if it were appended to whatever the current transform on the prim is. But the resulting final transform will be expressed using the USD XformCommonAPI specification. Note that this specification cannot express shears, and so cannot express some transforms which may result in unexpected changes to transforms that already have shears. Apply Extended XformCommonAPI (with Shear + Pivot Rotate): The transform specified in the remaining transform parameters will be applied as if it were appended to whatever the current transform on the prim is. But the resulting final transform will be expressed using a Houdini-defined extension of the USD XformCommonAPI specification. This extension is accessible through the husd.UsdHoudini.HoudiniXformCommonAPI python class. This class provides a very similar interface to pxr.UsdGeom.XformCommonAPI but allows for shears in the transform, is able to store a pivot rotation value, and can express rotations as a quaternion if the rotations are animated. Using quaternions to express rotations avoids motion blur artifacts that can occur when using Euler angles to express the rotation.

parameters.description: Enable this property to allow multiple rules to be applied to a single path. When this is disabled, the first rule that affects a path causes all following rules to be ignored for that path.

parameters.description: Paths with the supplied string as a prefix are affected by this rule. This string uses standard file path matching rules.

parameters.label: Replace Prefix
parameters.description: Paths with a matching Find Prefix have that prefix replaced with this value. This can be used to turn full paths into relative paths, or update full paths with a new root directory.

parameters.label: Find Suffix

parameters.label: Replace Suffix
parameters.description: Paths with a matching Find Suffix have that suffix replaced with this value. This can be used to update the file extension on texture map file paths.

parameters.label: Subnet Modified Primitives
parameters.description: The USD primitives matching this parameter are set as the last modified primitives of this node. If this Output LOP has its Output Index set to 0, the parent Subnetwork LOP will report this same set of last modified primitives.

entries.label: Paint Instances
entries.summary: Provides tools for populating a scene with USD assets in a point instancer. You can place individual instances, paint/scatter instances in different ways using customizable brushes, and edit existing instances.

parameters.label: Edit Last Stroke
parameters.description: Changes you make to the parameters change the outcome of the previous stroke. Turn this off to set up different values for the next stroke without affecting the last stroke.

parameters.label: Show Instance Points
parameters.description: Show orange square rings representing the points the assets are instanced onto.

parameters.label: Brush Intersection
parameters.description: All: Paint on both the input geometry _and_ any assets added by this node. Current Instances: Paint on existing instances added by this node, but _not_ on the input geometry. Input Stage: Paint on the input geometry, but _not_ on instances added by this node.

parameters.label: Reset Changes
parameters.description: Delete all points/instances added in this node.

parameters.label: Debug Brush
parameters.description: Enter Debug mode, in this mode you can draw a stroke in the viewport and the Paint Instances state will generate a SOP network emulation of the Paint Instances state containing the current brush. This allows you to step through the stroke which is useful for both debugging brush failures and for building new brushes.

parameters.label: Asset Scale
parameters.description: Post brush application scale factor that allows scaling of all assets independent of what the current brush is.

entries.label: Parent Constraint
entries.summary: Makes a primitive appear to inherit the transform hierarchy of another prim somewhere else in the tree.

parameters.label: Sampling Behavior
parameters.description: Cooking this node can generate many USD time samples, rather than just a single time sample at the current time. This can be equivalent to having a Cache LOP following this node, but it will evaluate much faster, and does not cache data from any other nodes. This allows animated data to be authored to USD without introducing a node time dependency which would then cause all following nodes to also be time dependent. This can vastly improve playback performance of some LOP Networks. In all sampling modes, if a parameter on this node does not vary with time, and does not rely on other time sampled data from the stage, only a single default value will be generated in USD for the corresponding attribute. USD time samples are only generated for parameters that may vary over time. Sample Current Frame: A single time sample will be generated for the current time. Sample Frame Range If Input Is Not Time Dependent: If the input to this node is time dependent, this node behaves as if it is in Sample Current Frame mode. Otherwise it behaves as if it is in Sample Frame Range mode. Sample Frame Range: The Start/End/Inc parameter is used to generate multiple times at which this node's parameters are evaluated, and a USD time sample is created for each attribute at each one of these times.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Start/End/Inc
parameters.description: When the Sampling behavior is Sample Frame Range, this parameter controls the number and spacing of base time samples to be generated by this node. The default values of this parameter are @fstart, @fend, and @finc. These values correspond to the start, end, and step size of the global Houdini animation settings when interacting with Houdini. When using a ROP node to generate a range of frames, these values correspond to the start, end, and increment values specified on the ROP node being executed. This default ensures that a USD file written to disk will contain time samples for exactly the frame range requested by the ROP (regardless of the Houdini animation settings).
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Subframe Sampling
parameters.description: For each primary sample generated by this node, these parameters can cause additional samples to be generated around that primary sample time. This is most often used to ensure that accurate data exists at exactly the camera shutter open and close times, as well as at the primary sample time.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Shutter
parameters.description: Controls the method used to specify the shutter open and close times relative to the primary sample times. Specify Manually: The Shutter Open/Close parameter values provide exact offset values relative to the primary sample time. Use Camera Prim: The Camera Prim parameter provides the scene graph path of a camera primitive from which the shutter open and close times are extracted to provide the offset values relative to the primary time sample.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Shutter Open/Close
parameters.description: When Shutter is set to Specify Manually, these two offset values are added to the primary sample time to indicate the shutter open and close times. The open time should be less than or equal to zero, and the close time should be greater than or equal to zero.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Camera Prim
parameters.description: When Shutter is set to Use Camera Prim, this is the scene graph path of a camera prim on the input node's stage. The shutter open and close attribute values are read from this primitive.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Samples
parameters.description: The number of subframe samples to create for each primary sample. These samples are evenly distributed between the shutter open and close times. Note that such an even distribution may or may not create a sample at exactly the primary sample time.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Always Include Frame Sample
parameters.description: When turned on, forces a sample to be created at exactly the primary sample time. If the Samples value, together with the shutter open and close times, already place a sample at the primary sample time, turning on this option has no effect. Otherwise, this option causes an addition sample to be added. This means that the actual number of samples per primary sample may in fact be one more than the number specified in the Samples parameter.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Action
parameters.description: Whether this node should create new prims, or edit existing prims. In addition, the Force Edit option can be chosen to cause this node to ignore the houdini:editable attribute on prims, and always edit the specified attributes. This is in contrast to the Edit mode which will trigger a warning and not set attributes on prims with the houdini:editable attribute set to false.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.description: In Create mode, this lets you control where in the scene graph to create the prim(s). The default is usually /$OS. This creates a primitive at the root level with the same name as the node (for example, /tube1). This is a useful default for preventing naming conflicts, but terrible for organization. You should try to remember to change the Primitive Path to a better value when you create prims. For example, instead of naming models after the node that created them, you might want to name them after the geometry inside, and organize them under a /Models branch. The Create Primitives section contains basic controls for how to create the new prim(s).
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.description: In Edit mode, the node has a Primitive Pattern parameter. This lets you specify the prim(s) the node should operate on. You can click the select button beside the text box to select the primitives from the scene graph tree. You can also use primitive patterns for advanced matching, including matching all prims in a collection.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Allowed Primitive Types
parameters.description: In Edit mode, only prims that match one of the specified primitive types (or API schemas) can be modified by this node. Leave this parameter empty to permit editing any primitive type.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Handle Disallowed Types
parameters.description: In Edit mode, specifies what should happen when a primitive that is not one of the Allowed primitive types matches the primitive pattern Ignore Disallowed Prim Types: Do not set any attributes on this primitive, but do not notify the user.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Initialize Parameters
parameters.description: Changes the state of all control menu parameters to Do Nothing, so that this node will not apply any changes. Also grabs the current values of each property from the first Primitives match, and sets the values of the corresponding parameters to match. This means that changing any parameter's control menu to Set or Create mode will set the property to its current value, making it easier to apply changes to an existing value rather than setting a brand new value. With Rebuild Render-Specific Parameters you reset all parameters from render-specific tabs to their default values for the specific node. If you want to reset the parameters for the entire scene, you can also open the top-level Render menu and choose Rebuild All Render-Specific LOP Parameters.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Primitive Count
parameters.description: The number of primitives to create.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Primitive Type
parameters.description: Set all created prims to have this type.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Primitive Kind
parameters.description: Set all created prims to have this kind.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Primitive Specifier
parameters.description: The USD operator to use when creating the new prims. Define: Authors a completely new prim. Use this if you want to create a brand new prim or replace an existing prim. Over: Authors an override of an existing prim. Attributes not explicitly authored on this prim will get their values from the existing prim on the lower layer. Class: Define a primitive class. This is usually not necessary unless you are doing deep USD magic.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Class Ancestor
parameters.description: If Primitive Specifier is Define or Over, this parameter will cause some ancestor primitives to be authored with a specifier of Class. This makes it easy to create an Over or Define within a Class without having to use two separate nodes. When Primitive Specifier is Class, this parameter is disabled because the entire primitive hierarchy is already authored as Class primitives.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Parent Primitive Type
parameters.description: If any parents of a path in Primitive Paths do not exist, this node will automatically create them. In this case, it will create parent nodes of this type.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Axis
parameters.description: The local axis along which the surface of the plane is aligned. When set to 'Z' the plane is in the xy-plane; when axis is 'X' the plane is in the yz-plane, and when axis is 'Y' the plane is in the xz-plane.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Length
parameters.description: The length of the plane, which aligns to the local y-axis when axis is 'Z' or 'X', or to the local z-axis when axis is 'Y'.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Width
parameters.description: The width of the plane, which aligns to the local x-axis when axis is 'Z' or 'Y', or to the local z-axis when axis is 'X'.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Color
parameters.description: Sets a "default" color for this shape, which will be used in the viewport if the prim does not have a shader/material. You can write shaders to take this displayColor parameter as an override.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Opacity
parameters.description: Sets the opacity of the display Color. This is a separate attribute (instead of specifying the display color as RGBA) so it can be independently overridden, and also because shaders don't usually accept RGBA parameters.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Double Sided
parameters.description: For renderers that distinguish between single-sided and double-sided surfaces, controls whether this prim is double-sided. Making surfaces double-sided is necessary for flat thin surfaces, or open surfaces where the camera can see both the inside and outside of the surface.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Transform
parameters.description: How the transform parameters below apply to the primitive. (Because each USD prim can contain multiple transforms, _and_ be affected by parent transforms, there are many different ways to apply new transforms.) Append: Apply the parameters as a new, most local transform. Prepend: Apply the parameters as a new, _least_ local transform. Overwrite or Append: If a local transform exists with the name xformOp:transform, _overwrite_ it with the parameters. Otherwise, apply it as a new, most local transform. If this replaces an existing transform, that transform's order in the local transform stack is not affected. Overwrite or Prepend: Like Overwrite or Append, but _least_ local. Apply Transform in World Space: Apply the parameters as a new, most local transform. However, prior to applying the transform, it is updated so that the result of the transform appears as if the transform was being applied in world space, before any local or ancestor transformations were applied to the primitive. Replace All Local Transforms: The transform specified in the remaining transform parameters is always applied as a new transform. Prior to applying this transform, all existing transform operations on the local transform stack are cleared so that only the supplied transform remains on the local transform stack (though ancestor transforms still have an effect). Apply XformCommonAPI: The transform specified in the remaining transform parameters will be applied as if it were appended to whatever the current transform on the prim is. But the resulting final transform will be expressed using the USD XformCommonAPI specification. Note that this specification cannot express shears, and so cannot express some transforms which may result in unexpected changes to transforms that already have shears. Apply Extended XformCommonAPI (with Shear + Pivot Rotate): The transform specified in the remaining transform parameters will be applied as if it were appended to whatever the current transform on the prim is. But the resulting final transform will be expressed using a Houdini-defined extension of the USD XformCommonAPI specification. This extension is accessible through the husd.UsdHoudini.HoudiniXformCommonAPI python class. This class provides a very similar interface to pxr.UsdGeom.XformCommonAPI but allows for shears in the transform, is able to store a pivot rotation value, and can express rotations as a quaternion if the rotations are animated. Using quaternions to express rotations avoids motion blur artifacts that can occur when using Euler angles to express the rotation.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Transform Order
parameters.description: The order in which Houdini applies translates, rotates, and scales, and the order in which it applies rotation.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Translate
parameters.description: Movement amount along XYZ axes.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.description: Degrees rotation around XYZ axes.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: Non-uniform scaling along XYZ axes.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Shear
parameters.description: Amount of shearing. The three values represent shearing in the X direction on the XY plane, in the X direction on the XZ plane, and in the Y direction on the YZ plane, respectively.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Uniform Scale
parameters.description: Scales the object uniformly along all three axes.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Pivot Translate
parameters.description: Moves the local origin of the object.
parameters.heading: Pivot Transform

parameters.label: Pivot Rotate
parameters.description: Rotates the local origin of the object after translation.
parameters.heading: Pivot Transform

entries.label: PointInstancer
entries.summary: Creates or edits USD PointInstancer prims from SOP points.

parameters.label: Sampling Behavior
parameters.description: Cooking this node can generate many USD time samples, rather than just a single time sample at the current time. This can be equivalent to having a Cache LOP following this node, but it will evaluate much faster, and does not cache data from any other nodes. This allows animated data to be authored to USD without introducing a node time dependency which would then cause all following nodes to also be time dependent. This can vastly improve playback performance of some LOP Networks. In all sampling modes, if a parameter on this node does not vary with time, and does not rely on other time sampled data from the stage, only a single default value will be generated in USD for the corresponding attribute. USD time samples are only generated for parameters that may vary over time. Sample Current Frame: A single time sample will be generated for the current time. Sample Frame Range If Input Is Not Time Dependent: If the input to this node is time dependent, this node behaves as if it is in Sample Current Frame mode. Otherwise it behaves as if it is in Sample Frame Range mode. Sample Frame Range: The Start/End/Inc parameter is used to generate multiple times at which this node's parameters are evaluated, and a USD time sample is created for each attribute at each one of these times.
parameters.heading: Per-Node Frame Sampling

parameters.label: Start/End/Inc
parameters.description: When the Sampling behavior is Sample Frame Range, this parameter controls the number and spacing of base time samples to be generated by this node. The default values of this parameter are @fstart, @fend, and @finc. These values correspond to the start, end, and step size of the global Houdini animation settings when interacting with Houdini. When using a ROP node to generate a range of frames, these values correspond to the start, end, and increment values specified on the ROP node being executed. This default ensures that a USD file written to disk will contain time samples for exactly the frame range requested by the ROP (regardless of the Houdini animation settings).
parameters.heading: Per-Node Frame Sampling

parameters.label: Subframe Sampling
parameters.description: For each primary sample generated by this node, these parameters can cause additional samples to be generated around that primary sample time. This is most often used to ensure that accurate data exists at exactly the camera shutter open and close times, as well as at the primary sample time.
parameters.heading: Subframe Sampling

parameters.label: Shutter
parameters.description: Controls the method used to specify the shutter open and close times relative to the primary sample times. Specify Manually: The Shutter Open/Close parameter values provide exact offset values relative to the primary sample time. Use Camera Prim: The Camera Prim parameter provides the scene graph path of a camera primitive from which the shutter open and close times are extracted to provide the offset values relative to the primary time sample.
parameters.heading: Subframe Sampling

parameters.label: Shutter Open/Close
parameters.description: When Shutter is set to Specify Manually, these two offset values are added to the primary sample time to indicate the shutter open and close times. The open time should be less than or equal to zero, and the close time should be greater than or equal to zero.
parameters.heading: Subframe Sampling

parameters.label: Camera Prim
parameters.description: When Shutter is set to Use Camera Prim, this is the scene graph path of a camera prim on the input node's stage. The shutter open and close attribute values are read from this primitive.
parameters.heading: Subframe Sampling

parameters.label: Samples
parameters.description: The number of subframe samples to create for each primary sample. These samples are evenly distributed between the shutter open and close times. Note that such an even distribution may or may not create a sample at exactly the primary sample time.
parameters.heading: Subframe Sampling

parameters.label: Always Include Frame Sample
parameters.description: When turned on, forces a sample to be created at exactly the primary sample time. If the Samples value, together with the shutter open and close times, already place a sample at the primary sample time, turning on this option has no effect. Otherwise, this option causes an addition sample to be added. This means that the actual number of samples per primary sample may in fact be one more than the number specified in the Samples parameter.
parameters.heading: Subframe Sampling

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.description: The scene graph path of the point instancer prim to create or edit. If the prim doesn't exist, this node creates it as a PointInstancer. If the prim exists but isn't a PointInstancer, the node errors. NOTE: This parameter applies only to source points that do *not* have a path attribute set. Points whose path attribute names a different scene graph path are routed there instead, and Primitive Path is ignored for those points.
parameters.heading: PointInstancer

parameters.label: Create Empty PointInstancer
parameters.description: When on (the default), the node authors a PointInstancer prim at Primitive Path even when the source SOP geometry has no points (or no points whose path attribute resolves to Primitive Path). Turn this off when you only want to edit existing instancers and don't want a stray empty one to be created at Primitive Path. The tab-menu Edit PointInstancer tool turns this off automatically so editing flows never accidentally author empty instancers.
parameters.heading: PointInstancer

parameters.label: Primitive Kind
parameters.description: The kind to set on any newly created instancer prim. Leave blank to author no kind.
parameters.heading: New PointInstancers

parameters.label: Primitive Specifier
parameters.description: The specifier (def, over, or class) used when creating new instancer prims. The default is def.
parameters.heading: New PointInstancers

parameters.label: Parent Primitive Type
parameters.description: The type used when this node has to create any intermediate ancestor prims along Primitive Path. The default is Xform.
parameters.heading: New PointInstancers

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.description: The scene graph path(s) of existing point instancer prims to edit. You can use pattern syntax to select multiple instancers. Each target point's path attribute selects which of these instancers it belongs to. Points whose path doesn't match any listed instancer fall back to Primitive Path.
parameters.heading: Existing PointInstancers

parameters.label: Edit Mode
parameters.description: Controls how the data on existing instancer prims is replaced. Sparse: Only re-author the instance entries (rows of the protoIndices, positions, orientations, etc. arrays) whose id is present in the SOP geometry. Ids absent from the SOP geometry are handled according to the Missing Points Policy. This is the recommended mode for partial edits. Overwrite: Replace the full per-instance arrays with whatever the SOP geometry provides. Ids in the source data are honoured, and missing ids are dropped entirely.
parameters.heading: Existing PointInstancers

parameters.label: Prototypes Relationship Mode
parameters.description: Controls how this node combines its prototype list with the existing prototypes relationship on the target instancer prim. Preserve: Keep the existing prototypes relationship targets exactly as they are. The cooked protoIndices values must reference indices in the preserved list. Prototype-related parameters on this node are disabled for existing instancers in this mode. Overwrite: Replace the prototypes relationship with the targets specified by this node. Existing protoIndices values are invalidated; supply new index assignments via the Prototype Assignment > Existing PointInstancers controls. Append: Append this node's prototypes to the existing prototypes relationship. Existing instance entries continue to point at the original prototypes; new entries can address the appended ones via the Existing PointInstancers assignment controls.
parameters.heading: Existing PointInstancers

parameters.label: Create Import Node
parameters.description: Click to add a USD PointInstancer Import SOP inside this node's internal SOP network, named existing_pointinstancers, with its key parameters wired to the parameters above. Use this as the starting point for an edit-existing-instancer setup.
parameters.heading: Existing PointInstancers

parameters.label: Prototype Source
parameters.description: Whether the prim(s) you want to reference/instance onto the points is/are in the first input or the second input.
parameters.heading: Existing PointInstancers

parameters.label: Use Entire Stage as Prototype
parameters.description: If Prototype Source is Second Input and this is on, the node copies everything from the second input's scene graph tree under a new prim and uses that as the prototype. This lets you build a node chain that builds the prototype and connect it to the second input, and not have to specify which prim in the second input to use. Using this option implies that there is only one prototype, because this node has no multi-input. If you have several full stages you want to use as prototypes, combine them with a Graft Stages LOP first, and feed the result into the second input, but with this option turned off.
parameters.heading: Source

parameters.label: Prototype Primitives
parameters.description: The scene graph path(s) of the primitive(s) you want to use as prototype(s). You can use pattern syntax to select multiple primitives.
parameters.heading: Source

parameters.label: Handle Missing Prototypes
parameters.description: If a point specifies a prototype that doesn't exist, this parameter controls whether the node will present a warning, enter an error state or create the missing primitives. The default is to enter an error state, which can be useful to catch accidental use of missing prototypes. The warning mode is useful for scenarios where prototypes may be added to the instancer later in the LOP network or through USD composition. The create mode will create placeholder prims in the scene to use as prototypes.
parameters.heading: Source

parameters.label: Make Prototype Source Primitives Invisible
parameters.description: If Prototype Source is First Input and Create Prototypes Area is enabled and this is on, the node sets the visibility of the prims used as primitives to "hidden" in the output. The default is on.
parameters.heading: Destination

parameters.label: Root Prim
parameters.description: The scene graph path to the root prim for the prototype area. This prim will be created if it doesn't already exist. This parm has access to the following local variables @primpath: The currently targeted prim path.
parameters.heading: Destination

parameters.label: Root Prim Kind
parameters.description: When Use Entire Stage is on, this sets the kind of the prim the node creates as a parent for root prims from the second input. The default is None.
parameters.heading: Destination

parameters.label: Name
parameters.description: The name for the prototype prims to be created under the prototype destination root prim. This parm has access to the following local variables @primpath: The currently targeted prim path. @protoprimpath: The source primpath for the current prototype. @protoprimname: The name of the source prototype prim. @protoindex: The index for the current prototype.
parameters.heading: Destination

parameters.label: Only Copy Specified Prototype Prims
parameters.description: If Prototype Source is Second Input and Use Entire Stage as Prototype is off, this controls whether to only copy the prototype primitives specified by Prototype Primitives, or the entire stage. The default is on. Using this option can result in a smaller stage, but requires that the prototype sources are fully self-contained (for example they cannot refer to materials that sit elsewhere in the prim hierarchy).
parameters.heading: Destination

parameters.label: Prototype Reference Type
parameters.description: If Prototype Source is First Input and Create Prototypes Area is enabled, this parameter controls the composition type to use when creating references to the source primitives from within the Prototypes folder in the scene graph. This parameter can be Reference, Inherit, or Specialize. See inherits and specializes for more information about how these choices differ from a simple reference.
parameters.heading: Destination

parameters.label: SOP Source
parameters.description: Where to find the SOP geometry that drives the per-instance data. Internal SOP: Use this node's internal SOP network. The display SOP of that subnet provides the points. External SOP: Use the output of a SOP elsewhere in the Houdini node hierarchy. Specify it in SOP Path.
parameters.heading: Import SOP Points

parameters.label: SOP Path
parameters.description: When SOP Source is External SOP, the node path of the SOP that generates the target points. Defaults to ..
parameters.heading: Import SOP Points

parameters.label: Show LOP Stage in SOPs
parameters.description: Points to a LOP node whose stage is rendered into the Scene Viewer along with the SOP geometry when you dive inside this node's internal SOP network. Any USD cameras and lights will also become available to look through in the viewport's camera menu. Specifying a LOP Network instead of a LOP node path fetches the stage of the display-flagged LOP node within the target LOP Network. This is only used when SOP Source is Internal SOP. The default expression looks at this node's first input.
parameters.heading: Import SOP Points

parameters.label: Point Group
parameters.description: Restrict the imported points to this named point group on the SOP geometry.
parameters.heading: Import SOP Points

parameters.label: Missing Points Policy
parameters.description: When Edit Mode is Sparse, controls what happens to instance ids on existing point instancers when those ids are absent from the SOP geometry (either because the upstream SOPs dropped them, or because the Point Group filter excluded them). Points marked with the delete SOP attribute are not handled here -- they are removed unconditionally, see Special SOP attributes. Do Nothing: Leave the existing instance entries untouched. The instance keeps its previous transform and visibility. Remove Instances: Delete the missing ids from the instancer. The corresponding instance entries are erased from protoIndices, positions, etc. Make Instances Invisible: Add the missing ids to the instancer's invisibleIds. The data for those instances is preserved so the instance can be re-shown later by re-adding its id.
parameters.heading: Import SOP Points

parameters.label: Ids
parameters.description: Author the USD ids attribute from the SOP id point attribute. Required when Edit Mode is Sparse (a warning notes that ids are handled automatically in sparse mode regardless of this toggle).
parameters.heading: Set Properties From Data

parameters.label: InvisibleIds
parameters.description: Author the USD invisibleIds attribute. Any point whose usdvisibility string attribute is invisible has its id added to invisibleIds. Requires the SOP id attribute (or an automatically assigned one).
parameters.heading: Set Properties From Data

parameters.label: Positions
parameters.description: Author the USD positions attribute from the SOP point position P.
parameters.heading: Set Properties From Data

parameters.label: Orientations
parameters.description: Author the USD orientations (or orientationsf) attribute from the SOP orient quaternion (or the standard N/up combination if orient isn't present).
parameters.heading: Set Properties From Data

parameters.label: Scales
parameters.description: Author the USD scales attribute from the SOP scale and/or pscale attributes.
parameters.heading: Set Properties From Data

parameters.label: Accelerations
parameters.description: Author the USD accelerations attribute from the SOP accel point attribute.
parameters.heading: Set Properties From Data

parameters.label: Velocities
parameters.description: Author the USD velocities attribute from the SOP v point attribute.
parameters.heading: Set Properties From Data

parameters.label: Angular Velocities
parameters.description: Author the USD angularVelocities attribute from the SOP w point attribute.
parameters.heading: Set Properties From Data

parameters.label: Point Attributes to Copy
parameters.description: A pattern matching point attribute names to copy onto the instancer prim as array primvars. Each listed attribute becomes one entry per instance. The default excludes the standard instancing attributes (which are handled by the toggles above), USD bookkeeping attributes, and the path attribute.
parameters.heading: Set Properties From Data

parameters.label: Missing Primvars Policy
parameters.description: When Edit Mode is Sparse, controls how mismatched primvar sets between the SOP geometry and an existing instancer prim are handled. Ignored when Edit Mode is Overwrite (the existing instancer's primvars are replaced wholesale in that mode). Do Nothing: If the SOP geometry lacks an attribute that exists as a primvar on the instancer, leave the primvar values for the affected ids unchanged. Create: Create any missing primvar on the instancer, using zero-valued entries for ids absent from the SOP geometry.
parameters.heading: Set Properties From Data

parameters.label: Common Primvars
parameters.description: A whitespace-separated list of primvar names that should be authored on every PointInstancer affected by this node. This is a finer-grained alternative to setting Missing Primvars Policy to Create (which authors every SOP primvar on every affected instancer) -- list only the primvars you want broadcast, and leave the rest to follow the per-instancer import set. The USD PointInstancer Import SOP writes this list to the geometry's importedprimvars detail attribute, and this LOP reads it to drive sparse primvar resampling.
parameters.heading: Set Properties From Data

parameters.label: Indexed Primvars
parameters.description: A space-separated list of primvar names or patterns specifying which primvars are authored as indexed (a deduplicated value array plus an index array) rather than flat per-instance arrays. type:string: Matches against any SOP string primvars. Indexed primvars are a useful optimization when a small number of unique values is repeated across a large number of instances. Preparing an indexed primvar can be expensive for attribute types other than integers or strings, so use this where the storage savings are clearly worth it.
parameters.heading: Set Properties From Data

parameters.label: Prototype Index
parameters.description: How the prototype index for each instance is determined. None: Don't author protoIndices from this node. Useful when another node downstream supplies the values. Random: Pick a prototype at random for each instance, using Seed as the seed. Integer Attribute: Use the value of an integer point attribute as the index into the prototype list. String Attribute: Use the value of a string point attribute. The value is matched against each prototype's prim name (or the path's basename); a match sets the corresponding protoIndices entry.
parameters.heading: New PointInstancers

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.description: When Prototype Index is Random, the seed for the random number generator.
parameters.heading: New PointInstancers

parameters.label: Integer Attribute
parameters.description: When Prototype Index is Integer Attribute, the name of the integer point attribute to read. Defaults to protoindex.
parameters.heading: New PointInstancers

parameters.label: String Attribute
parameters.description: When Prototype Index is String Attribute, the name of the string point attribute to read. Defaults to protoname.
parameters.heading: New PointInstancers

parameters.label: Prototype Index
parameters.description: Same as New PointInstancers > Prototype Index, applied to existing instancers. The default is None -- existing instances keep their authored protoIndices values.
parameters.heading: Existing PointInstancers

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.description: When Prototype Index is Random, the seed for the random number generator.
parameters.heading: Existing PointInstancers

parameters.label: Integer Attribute
parameters.description: When Prototype Index is Integer Attribute, the name of the integer point attribute to read.
parameters.heading: Existing PointInstancers

parameters.label: String Attribute
parameters.description: When Prototype Index is String Attribute, the name of the string point attribute to read.
parameters.heading: Existing PointInstancers

parameters.label: Warn on Skipped Instances
parameters.description: When a per-instance attribute lookup fails (an integer index out of range, or a string with no matching prototype name), emit a warning naming the first such instance. Visible only when one of the Prototype Index menus is set to Integer Attribute or String Attribute.
parameters.heading: Existing PointInstancers
