parameters.label: Volume Velocity Blur Mode
parameters.description: Choose velocity blur method for volumes. Lattice Deformation: Motion sampled via a deforming superstructure. Lookup Offset: Sample coordinate is offset by velocity field value. NOTE: Lattice Deformation mode can produce results with higher quality and handle cases such as disparate features of a volume overlapping post-blur. Lookup Offset mode can be more performant, particularly with reduced-resolution velocity fields. However, this mode is more prone to clipping issues if the sampled position is outside the bounds of velocity field. There, the lattice doesn't have velocity information.
parameters.heading: Motion Blur

parameters.label: Volume Velocity Blur Scale
parameters.description: Velocity multiplier used to reduce or exaggerate amount of motion blur on volumes.
parameters.heading: Motion Blur

parameters.label: Volume Velocity Lattice Quality
parameters.description: Controls the resolution of the lattice super structure that is used for volume motion blur. Values closer to 1 result in a structure with velocities closer to the original velocity data, but longer render time.
parameters.heading: Motion Blur

parameters.label: Diffuse Quality
parameters.description: This parameter acts as a multiplier on Min Secondary Samples and Max Secondary Samples for indirect diffuse component.
parameters.heading: Sampling

parameters.label: Reflection Quality
parameters.description: This parameter acts as a multiplier on Min Secondary Samples and Max Secondary Samples for indirect reflect component.
parameters.heading: Sampling

parameters.label: Refraction Quality
parameters.description: This parameter acts as a multiplier on Min Secondary Samples and Max Secondary Samples for indirect refract component.
parameters.heading: Sampling

parameters.label: Volume Quality
parameters.description: This parameter acts as a multiplier on Min Secondary Samples and Max Secondary Samples for indirect volume component.
parameters.heading: Sampling

parameters.label: SSS Quality
parameters.description: This parameter acts as a multiplier on Min Secondary Samples and Max Secondary Samples for SSS component.
parameters.heading: Sampling

parameters.label: Volume Shadow Step Rate
parameters.description: A factor to proportionally decrease the volume step rate only for shadows, relative to the volume step rate. Smaller values will cause Karma to use a larger ray march step size for shadow rays than other shading rays. A value of 1 will produce equal quality for shadow rays and shading rays.
parameters.heading: Sampling

parameters.label: Volume Sampling Field
parameters.description: Specifies the volume field by name that will be used for empty space culling. By default Karma will use the 'density' field if it exists. If you are rendering an emissive volume in which some parts of the volume have a 0 density, but still need to be rendered, you should specify a different field using this parameter.
parameters.heading: Sampling

parameters.label: Volume Filter
parameters.description: Some volume primitives can use a filter during evaluation of volume channels. This specifies the filter. The default box filter is fast to evaluate and produces sharp renders for most smooth fluid simulations. If your voxel data contains aliasing (stairstepping along edges), you may need to use a larger filter width or smoother filter to produce acceptable results. For aliased volume data, gaussian is a good filter with a filter width of 1.5. * point * box * gaussian * bartlett * catrom * hannig * blackman * blackmanharris * sinc
parameters.heading: Sampling

parameters.label: Volume Filter Width
parameters.description: This specifies the filter width for the Volume Filter property. The filter width is specified in number of voxels. Larger filter widths take longer to render and produce blurrier renders, but may be necessary to combat aliasing in some kinds of voxel data.
parameters.heading: Sampling

parameters.label: Diffuse Limit
parameters.description: The number of times diffuse rays can propagate through your scene. Unlike the Reflection Limit and Refraction Limit, this parameter will increase the overall amount of light in your scene and contribute to the majority of global illumination. With this parameter set above zero diffuse surfaces will accumulate light from other objects in addition to direct light sources.
parameters.heading: Limits

parameters.label: Reflection Limit
parameters.description: The number of times a ray can be reflected in your scene.
parameters.heading: Limits

parameters.label: Volume Limit
parameters.description: The number of times a volumetric ray can propagate through a scene. It functions in a similar fashion to the Diffuse Limit parameter.
parameters.heading: Limits

parameters.label: SSS Limit
parameters.description: The number of times a SSS ray can propagate through a scene. It functions in a similar fashion to the Diffuse Limit parameter.
parameters.heading: Limits

parameters.label: Limit Components
parameters.description: The ray types that the bounce limit color is applied to.
parameters.heading: Limits

parameters.label: Limit Color
parameters.description: The color that will be used when a specific ray type reaches the limit.
parameters.heading: Limits

parameters.label: Uniform Volume
parameters.description: Whether to render this object as if it was a uniform-density volume. Using this property on surface geometry is more efficient than actually creating a volume object of uniform density, since the renderer can assume that the volume density is uniform and place samples more optimally. The surface normal of the surface is used to determine which side of the surface will render as a volume - the normal will point away from the interior. The surface need not be closed on CPU (on XPU it must be closed mesh) - if the surface is not closed, the volume will extend an infinite distance away from the surface. Non-closed surfaces may produce unexpected results near the edge of the surface, so try to keep the viewing camera away from the edges.
parameters.heading: Volume

parameters.label: Uniform Volume Samples
parameters.description: The number of samples to generate when rendering a uniform volume (karma:object:volumeuniform is enabled). The samples will be distributed so as to produce an equal image contribution if they were all equal in brightness. Note that this property has no effect when global Screendoor Limit is greater than 0, so for all practical purposes it is deprecated.
parameters.heading: Volume

parameters.label: Render Visibility
parameters.description: Controls the visibility of an object to different types of rays using a category expression. This parameter generalizes the Phantom and Renderable toggles and allows more specific control over the visibility of an object to the different ray types supported by karma and VEX. primary | Rays sent from the camera shadow | Shadow rays diffuse| Diffuse rays reflect| Reflections refract| Refractions For example, to create a phantom object, set the expression to -primary. To create an unrenderable object, set the expression to an empty string . These tokens correspond to the string given to "raystyle" in the VEX trace() and gather() functions.
parameters.heading: Shading

parameters.label: Stencil Map
parameters.description: This map type controls polygon visibility without invoking the shading engine. This means that you typically don't need an opacity map on the shader/material. The stencil map uses the default texture coordinates (st) to do a quick unfiltered texture evaluation. By default, any pixel with a value of 0 makes the polygon invisible to any rays. However, you can change this limit with Stencil Threshold.
parameters.heading: Shading

parameters.label: Stencil Threshold
parameters.description: Pixels with values less than or equal to this threshold will be invisibles to rays.
parameters.heading: Shading

parameters.label: Cusp Angle
parameters.description: If there are no normals on an object, any edges with a dihedral angle greater than this value will be cusped. For compatibility with Mantra, Karma will also look for a detail attribute named vm_cuspangle (which takes priority over the setting).
parameters.heading: Shading

parameters.label: Holdout Mode
parameters.description: When this is set to Matte mode, the object will be considered to be a cutout matte. Any lighting contribution and alpha of the object will be redirected to LPE AOVs with "holdouts" prefix. Holdout Mode does not affect the utility AOVs such as ray:hitP and ray:hitN. Background mode is similar to Matte, except it's used for background plate so it will appear "pre-lit" in indirect bounces, multiplied by shadow contribution. Diffuse albedo of the shader is used to determine the pre-lit irradiance.
parameters.heading: Shading

parameters.label: Fix Shadow Terminator
parameters.description: Adjust shading position of shadow rays to avoid self-shadowing artifacts on low-poly meshes due to the discrepancy between smooth normals and face normals.
parameters.heading: Shading

parameters.label: Custom Tracesets
parameters.description: A space-separated list of custom traceset names. You can use tracesets to subdivide a mesh into different parts, i.e. in conjunction with the Karma Texture Baker LOP. For example, the clothing on a character might have tracesets like pants, shirt and jacket. On the Karma Texture Baker LOP's Bake Traceset parameter you can then define which part/traceset you want to bake.
parameters.heading: Shading

parameters.label: LPE Tag
parameters.description: Custom label assigned to lights or objects for use with Light Path Expressions.
parameters.heading: Shading

parameters.label: SSS Traceset
parameters.description: Custom traceset for random walk subsurface scatter. Without a traceset, random walk will only trace against itself. With a traceset, it will trace against every geometry in the scene that shares the same traceset name. NOTE: With instancing, this property must be defined on the prototype. Per-instance tracesets are not supported.
parameters.heading: Shading

parameters.label: Enable Internal Reflection
parameters.description: Lets you evaluate the internal reflection on the backface of a glossy transmissive BSDF. Turn on this option to apply internal reflections. Note that this option has no effect on MaterialX Standard Surfaces with Thin Walled turned on: these materials always show internal reflections. Internal reflections can cause black areas on an object's back faces due to a loss of energy. To avoid this, turn _off_ Enable Internal Reflection.
parameters.heading: Shading

parameters.label: Thinwall at Refract Limit
parameters.description: Paths can become trapped inside refractive objects due to total internal reflection, hitting the refract/reflect limits and causing dark artifacts. Thinwall At Refract Limit treats surfaces as "thin walled" once these limits are reached, allowing further hits to pass through without bending or reflecting. This helps paths escape refractive objects without needing high refract/reflect limits (improving both look and performance).
parameters.heading: Shading

parameters.label: Direct Refraction Subset
parameters.description: For compound BSDFs with refractive components, only apply direct lighting for lights that belong in specified location. A light ray facing the same direction as geometry normal is considered Outside. For transparent material that are solid/closed-manifold, setting this parameter to Outside can improve render performance by reducing noise in direct lighting and cut down on wasted shadow rays.
parameters.heading: Shading

parameters.label: Dielectric Priority
parameters.description: Specifies the priority of a refractive material, allowing the renderer to choose which of many overlapping refractive materials should take precedence while rendering. This enables effects like water in a glass with ice cubes. The default (highest priority) is 0, and as the number increases (1, 2, 3, etc.), the priority decreases.
parameters.heading: Shading

parameters.label: Bump Shadow Terminator
parameters.description: Softens harsh shadow transitions from strong bump or normal maps. The shadow terminator is smoothly blended up to the specified threshold (in radians). A value of 0 disables the effect. NOTE: Roughness clamp only works with GGX BSDF and may not have any effect with Phong, cone, or specular BSDFs.
parameters.heading: Shading

parameters.label: Efficient Emission Sampling
parameters.description: Any object with an emissive material will generate light within the scene. If an object is significant enough (e.g. size, brightness, etc...) then it is possible for Karma to treat that object as if it were an explicit light source (similar to regular lights), meaning the emitted light will be handled much more efficiently. But doing so will add extra overhead elsewhere in the system (e.g. increased memory usage, slower update times, etc...). There are three options. No will set the object as not being a light source. Yes will set the object as being a light source. Auto (default) means Karma will use an internal heuristic to decide if the object should be treated as a light source.
parameters.heading: Light

parameters.label: Is Portal
parameters.description: When enabled, the object will turn into a "light portal" that only lets in certain portion of dome lights based on portal geometry visibility.
parameters.heading: Light

parameters.label: Portal Dome Lights
parameters.description: Space-separated list of dome lights to associate this portal with.
parameters.heading: Light

parameters.label: Render Points As
parameters.description: When rendering point clouds, they can be rendered as camera oriented discs, spheres or discs oriented to the normal attribute.
parameters.heading: Geometry

parameters.label: Render Curves As
parameters.description: When rendering curves, they can be rendered as ribbons oriented to face the camera, rounded tubes or ribbons oriented to the normal attribute attached to the points. Note that, due to a technical limitation, Karma CPU can't render linear curves as oriented ribbons. In this case, go to the import LOP that loads the curve and turn on Geometry Handling > Treat Polygons as Subdivision Surfaces. This option will import the curves as B-Splines.
parameters.heading: Geometry

parameters.label: Override Curves Basis
parameters.description: USD supports Curve Basis types that may not be supported directly in Houdini. In some cases, you may want to override the Houdini curve basis. For example, if you have linear curves in Houdini, you may want to render them with a Bezier, B-Spline or Catmull-Rom basis. This menu will force Karma to override the basis that's tied to the USD primitives. Note that the topology of the curves must match the target basis. For example, when selecting any cubic curve basis, every curves must have at least four vertices. For the Bezier basis, curves must have 4 + 3*N vertices.
parameters.heading: Geometry

parameters.label: Width Scale
parameters.description: A uniform scale applied to point and curve widths. This can be used to adjust the size of points and the radius of curves without having to modify the geometry.
parameters.heading: Geometry

parameters.label: Cull Backface
parameters.description: If enabled, geometry that are facing away from the camera are not rendered.
parameters.heading: Geometry

parameters.label: Dicing Quality
parameters.description: This parameter controls the geometric subdivision resolution for smooth surfaces (subdivision surfaces and displaced surfaces). With all other parameters at their defaults, a value of 1 means that approximately _one_ micropolygon will be created per pixel. A higher value will generate smaller micropolygons meaning that more shading will occur - but the quality will be higher. The effect of changing the shading quality is to increase or decrease the amount of shading by a factor of karma:object:dicingquality *squared* - so a shading quality of 2 will perform four times as much shading. A shading quality of 0.5 will perform 1/4 times as much shading.
parameters.heading: Dicing

parameters.label: Displacement Style
parameters.description: This setting controls how the displacement shader on the object will be run. Displacement as Bump: The displacement shader is run, but only modifies the surface normal. This does not dice geometry and can save memory. With Karma XPU, this option only works in conjunction with float-based displacement maps. Also make sure to set the MtlX Image VOP's Signature drop down menu to Float. Vector-based displacement maps are not supported in Karma XPU with this mode turned on. Please also note that this mode generally doesn't work with Karma XPU when you mix two or more MtlX Standard Surface VOPs. True Displacement: The geometry is diced and displaced. This will cause proper silhouettes and shadowing of displaced surfaces. Disable Displacement Shader: Disable the displacement shader entirely. There will be no bump mapping or displaced geometry. Bump Added to Displacement: The geometry is diced and displaced, and also the surface normal is modified using the displacement shader when shading. This option allows increased apparent detail without having to increase dicing quality and incur heavier memory cost. With Karma XPU, the same limitation as Displacement as Bump applies (vector-based displacement maps are not supported).
parameters.heading: Dicing

parameters.label: Dicing Minimum Depth
parameters.description: When not set to -1, Karma will set minimum number of rows and columns on each face to be 2 to the power of this value when dicing for subdivision or displacement.
parameters.heading: Dicing

parameters.label: Dicing Maximum Depth
parameters.description: When not set to -1, Karma will set maximum number of rows and columns on each face to be 2 to the power of this value when dicing for subdivision or displacement. Setting the same (or lower) value as Dicing Minimum Depth is effectively equivalent to fixed parametric subdivision that ignores raster space/offscreen measurement. Recommended leaving this value at -1.
parameters.heading: Dicing

parameters.label: Dicing Predisplace
parameters.description: Enable this to apply trial displacement prior to dicing for improved raster space measurement. This helps avoid undertessellation with extreme displacements or when offscreen geometry is supposed to enter camera frustum post-displacement.
parameters.heading: Dicing

parameters.label: Dicing Z-Importance
parameters.description: Set it below 1 to reduce dicing rate based on incident angle between face and dicing camera to reduce memory usage. Value of 0 means that area measurement of a face during dicing is proportional to its projected raster area. 1 means that the area is measured as though the face is oriented head-on. Any value in between is a blend of the two. Recommended leaving it above 0.5 to avoid possible distortion or popping in animation due to low tessellation.
parameters.heading: Dicing

parameters.label: Low Resolution Object ID
parameters.description: Defines this object as the low resolution object corresponding to said Texture Baking Object ID. This means that the texture space of this object is what is being baked. If no high resolution object exists for this Object ID, this is the rendered appearance for the texture in that space as well. This is required for texture baking.
parameters.heading: Texture Baking

parameters.label: Cage Object ID
parameters.description: Defines this object as the cage object corresponding to said Texture Baking Object ID. This means that this object is used to help resolve normal discontinuities during texture baking of the low resolution object. This is optional for texture baking.
parameters.heading: Texture Baking

parameters.label: High Resolution Object ID
parameters.description: Defines this object as the high resolution object corresponding to said Texture Baking Object ID. This means that the rendered appearance of this object is what is being baked into the texture space the low resolution object. This is optional for texture baking.
parameters.heading: Texture Baking

parameters.label: Identifier Traceset
parameters.description: The name of the traceset on the high resolution object. A bake_traceset string primvar is also required on the low resolution object. When both, Identifier Traceset name and primvar, match, the object will be visible to primary rays.
parameters.heading: Texture Baking

parameters.label: Visibility Traceset
parameters.description: The traceset that is defined through Identifier Traceset. When availavle, it indicates which objects are visible to secondary rays, for example ambient occlusion, curvature, thickness, cavity, etc.
parameters.heading: Texture Baking

parameters.label: Visibility Cull Backface
parameters.description: If enabled, geometry that are facing away from the secondary ray (Ao, Cu, Cv, Th, etc.) are not intersected.
parameters.heading: Texture Baking

parameters.label: Enable
parameters.description: Per object lines on/off.
parameters.heading: Outline

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: Controls outline thickness. Arctangent of this parameter determines the cone angle to cast stencil rays to do edge detection. It will be multiplied by karma:global:outline_radius.
parameters.heading: Outline

parameters.label: Contour
parameters.description: Contour detection on/off. Contour lines are based on automatically assigned object id if export_outline_id is not provided as a value or texture (as shader export).
parameters.heading: Outline

parameters.label: Id Threshold
parameters.description: Threshold which estimates how different is id values of the main ray and stencil ray.
parameters.heading: Outline

parameters.label: Crease
parameters.description: Crease lines for hard surfaces on/off.
parameters.heading: Outline

parameters.label: Crease Threshold
parameters.description: Threshold which estimates how N direction changes in the area of stencil radius.
parameters.heading: Outline

parameters.label: Depth
parameters.description: Depth lines on/off.
parameters.heading: Outline

parameters.label: Depth Threshold
parameters.description: Threshold which estimates how z-depth values changes in the area of stencil radius.
parameters.heading: Outline

parameters.label: Secondary
parameters.description: Indirect lines on/off.
parameters.heading: Outline

parameters.label: Default Delegate
parameters.description: Specify the default render delegate that husk should use when rendering using this render settings primitive. The --renderer command line argument overrides this value. If the value is empty, the value of the HOUDINI_HUSK_DEFAULT_DELEGATE environment variable is used. If multiple render settings are rendered in a single husk process, the first render settings primitive will be used to determine the default delegate.
parameters.heading: Husk

parameters.label: Scene Materials
parameters.description: Specify the default behaviour for the --disable-scene-materials command line parameter in husk. By default this is true, but can be overridden by the command line option. If the value of this property is set to false, husk will act as if the command line option was specified.
parameters.heading: Husk

parameters.label: Scene Lights
parameters.description: Specify the default behaviour for the --disable-scene-lights command line parameter in husk. By default this is true, but can be overridden by the command line option. If the value of this property is set to false, husk will act as if the command line option was specified.
parameters.heading: Husk

parameters.label: Ordered Image Filters
parameters.description: Specify a list of HoudiniImageFilterList primitives to be used when rendering.
parameters.heading: Husk

entries.label: Render Var
entries.summary: Specifies a custom variable computed by the renderer and/or shaders, either a shader output or a light path expression (LPE).

parameters.label: Sampling Behavior
parameters.description: Cooking this node can generate many USD time samples, rather than just a single time sample at the current time. This can be equivalent to having a Cache LOP following this node, but it will evaluate much faster, and does not cache data from any other nodes. This allows animated data to be authored to USD without introducing a node time dependency which would then cause all following nodes to also be time dependent. This can vastly improve playback performance of some LOP Networks. In all sampling modes, if a parameter on this node does not vary with time, and does not rely on other time sampled data from the stage, only a single default value will be generated in USD for the corresponding attribute. USD time samples are only generated for parameters that may vary over time. Sample Current Frame: A single time sample will be generated for the current time. Sample Frame Range If Input Is Not Time Dependent: If the input to this node is time dependent, this node behaves as if it is in Sample Current Frame mode. Otherwise it behaves as if it is in Sample Frame Range mode. Sample Frame Range: The Start/End/Inc parameter is used to generate multiple times at which this node's parameters are evaluated, and a USD time sample is created for each attribute at each one of these times.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Start/End/Inc
parameters.description: When the Sampling behavior is Sample Frame Range, this parameter controls the number and spacing of base time samples to be generated by this node. The default values of this parameter are @fstart, @fend, and @finc. These values correspond to the start, end, and step size of the global Houdini animation settings when interacting with Houdini. When using a ROP node to generate a range of frames, these values correspond to the start, end, and increment values specified on the ROP node being executed. This default ensures that a USD file written to disk will contain time samples for exactly the frame range requested by the ROP (regardless of the Houdini animation settings).
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Subframe Sampling
parameters.description: For each primary sample generated by this node, these parameters can cause additional samples to be generated around that primary sample time. This is most often used to ensure that accurate data exists at exactly the camera shutter open and close times, as well as at the primary sample time.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Shutter
parameters.description: Controls the method used to specify the shutter open and close times relative to the primary sample times. Specify Manually: The Shutter Open/Close parameter values provide exact offset values relative to the primary sample time. Use Camera Prim: The Camera Prim parameter provides the scene graph path of a camera primitive from which the shutter open and close times are extracted to provide the offset values relative to the primary time sample.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Shutter Open/Close
parameters.description: When Shutter is set to Specify Manually, these two offset values are added to the primary sample time to indicate the shutter open and close times. The open time should be less than or equal to zero, and the close time should be greater than or equal to zero.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Camera Prim
parameters.description: When Shutter is set to Use Camera Prim, this is the scene graph path of a camera prim on the input node's stage. The shutter open and close attribute values are read from this primitive.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Samples
parameters.description: The number of subframe samples to create for each primary sample. These samples are evenly distributed between the shutter open and close times. Note that such an even distribution may or may not create a sample at exactly the primary sample time.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Always Include Frame Sample
parameters.description: When turned on, forces a sample to be created at exactly the primary sample time. If the Samples value, together with the shutter open and close times, already place a sample at the primary sample time, turning on this option has no effect. Otherwise, this option causes an addition sample to be added. This means that the actual number of samples per primary sample may in fact be one more than the number specified in the Samples parameter.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Action
parameters.description: Whether this node should create new prims, or edit existing prims. In addition, the Force Edit option can be chosen to cause this node to ignore the houdini:editable attribute on prims, and always edit the specified attributes. This is in contrast to the Edit mode which will trigger a warning and not set attributes on prims with the houdini:editable attribute set to false.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.description: In Create mode, this lets you control where in the scene graph to create the prim(s). The default is usually /$OS. This creates a primitive at the root level with the same name as the node (for example, /tube1). This is a useful default for preventing naming conflicts, but terrible for organization. You should try to remember to change the Primitive Path to a better value when you create prims. For example, instead of naming models after the node that created them, you might want to name them after the geometry inside, and organize them under a /Models branch. The Create Primitives section contains basic controls for how to create the new prim(s).
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.description: In Edit mode, the node has a Primitive Pattern parameter. This lets you specify the prim(s) the node should operate on. You can click the select button beside the text box to select the primitives from the scene graph tree. You can also use primitive patterns for advanced matching, including matching all prims in a collection.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Allowed Primitive Types
parameters.description: In Edit mode, only prims that match one of the specified primitive types (or API schemas) can be modified by this node. Leave this parameter empty to permit editing any primitive type.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Handle Disallowed Types
parameters.description: In Edit mode, specifies what should happen when a primitive that is not one of the Allowed primitive types matches the primitive pattern Ignore Disallowed Prim Types: Do not set any attributes on this primitive, but do not notify the user.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Initialize Parameters
parameters.description: Changes the state of all control menu parameters to Do Nothing, so that this node will not apply any changes. Also grabs the current values of each property from the first Primitives match, and sets the values of the corresponding parameters to match. This means that changing any parameter's control menu to Set or Create mode will set the property to its current value, making it easier to apply changes to an existing value rather than setting a brand new value. With Rebuild Render-Specific Parameters you reset all parameters from render-specific tabs to their default values for the specific node. If you want to reset the parameters for the entire scene, you can also open the top-level Render menu and choose Rebuild All Render-Specific LOP Parameters.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Primitive Count
parameters.description: The number of primitives to create.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Primitive Type
parameters.description: Set all created prims to have this type.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Primitive Kind
parameters.description: Set all created prims to have this kind.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Primitive Specifier
parameters.description: The USD operator to use when creating the new prims. Define: Authors a completely new prim. Use this if you want to create a brand new prim or replace an existing prim. Over: Authors an override of an existing prim. Attributes not explicitly authored on this prim will get their values from the existing prim on the lower layer. Class: Define a primitive class. This is usually not necessary unless you are doing deep USD magic.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Class Ancestor
parameters.description: If Primitive Specifier is Define or Over, this parameter will cause some ancestor primitives to be authored with a specifier of Class. This makes it easy to create an Over or Define within a Class without having to use two separate nodes. When Primitive Specifier is Class, this parameter is disabled because the entire primitive hierarchy is already authored as Class primitives.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Parent Primitive Type
parameters.description: If any parents of a path in Primitive Paths do not exist, this node will automatically create them. In this case, it will create parent nodes of this type.
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Data Type
parameters.description: The USD data type of the render variable. When saving to OpenEXR files, the data type is used to determine the channel names. For example, if the data type is color3f, the channel names will be R, G, B, while if the data type is normal3f, the channel names will be x, y, z. TIP: If you're rendering with husk and want color channel names to be lower case (for example r, g, b), add another Render Var LOP and use it to set the driver:parameters:aov:husk:channel_lower_rgb (bool) render var to true.
parameters.heading: Standard

parameters.label: Source Name
parameters.description: Where to get the render variable contents. See Source Type below. The renderer should look for an output with this name as the computed value for the RenderVar. TIP: In Karma, with Raw and Primvar (including Cryptomatte) Source Type, it's possible to prefix variable name with noholdouts; to indicate that matte or background holdouts should *not* contribute to the AOV. For example, to output normal N AOV without holdouts, enter: ray:noholdouts;N
parameters.heading: Standard

parameters.label: Source Type
parameters.description: How to interpret the Source Name parameter. Raw: Pass the source name directly to the renderer. This assumes the renderer knows how to interpret the source name string. This is the default. Primvar: The Source Name is the name of primvar. Some renderers may use this to ensure that the primvar is provided to the renderer. Other renderers may require that a suitable material network be provided, in which case this is simply an advisory setting. LPE: The Source Name is a Light Path Expression. (Some renderers may accept extensions to the OSL Light Path Expression syntax, which will necessarily be non-portable.) Intrinsic: *Currently not implemented*. In the future, USD may provide for a portable list of baseline render vars, such as camera depth, that would be implemented by all renderers.
parameters.heading: Standard

parameters.label: Sample Blending
parameters.description: Image plane pixel filters are used to combine multiple samples into a single pixel color. For example, the filter may choose a single sample (closest to the camera, or maximum value), or most commonly, the pixel filter will choose to average the sample values. This parameter specifies a list of filters. These filters are specified as a JSON list. Supported Blending Modes
parameters.heading: Karma

parameters.label: Dithering
parameters.description: When Karma quantizes pixels to 8 or 16 bit integer channels, this specifies the dithering to be used. This is only done if the AOV is specified as 8/16 bit output depth. It will not be done if conversion is done when writing floating point values to an image format that only supports 8/16 bit integer channel data.
parameters.heading: Karma

parameters.label: Default Value
parameters.description: This is the clear color for the image plane.
parameters.heading: Karma

parameters.label: Enable Cryptomatte
parameters.description: Enable this to turn this image plane into Cryptomatte layer. See Cryptomatte for more info.
parameters.heading: Karma

parameters.label: Cryptomatte Max Overlap
parameters.description: Maximum number of IDs that can be stored in a single pixel. A value of 6 is recommended.
parameters.heading: Karma

parameters.label: Cryptomatte Manifest File
parameters.description: Optional external manifest file. It will be saved into same directory as the render product. If this path is unspecified, the manifest will be embedded into render product as metadata.
parameters.heading: Karma

parameters.label: Utility Path Expression
parameters.description: Using the same syntax as Light Path Expressions, this determines at what path vertex (ie scattering event) to write out the utility AOV. The default is CO meaning it gets written out from the first hit from the initial camera ray. Another example is C<TG>O which means to write out the AOV from the next hit after the first refration event (which would write out the AOV from behind the first layer of refraction). With C(<T>.O)O you can create a Crypotmatte that shows refractive _and_ non-refractive rays together. This only works for Raw, Primvar and ShaderExport (ie via kma_aov) AOV types. Note: Beware that this writes out value of the last vertex that matches the expression without any regards to ray throughput, so the look can be affected by sampling odds of indirect rays. For example, Automatic convergence mode may look very different from Path Traced convergence mode under karma CPU.
parameters.heading: Karma

parameters.label: Name
parameters.description: The name of the AOV in the output image that stores the data from this render var.
parameters.heading: Husk

parameters.label: Format
parameters.description: The data format that should be used when saving this image plane to the output file. This value is also passed to the render delegate when it allocates the render buffer for the AOV.
parameters.heading: Husk

parameters.label: Multi Sampled
parameters.description: Whether the render buffer should be multi-sampled. This value is also passed to the render delegate when it allocates the render buffer for the AOV.
parameters.heading: Husk

parameters.label: Clear Value
parameters.description: The initial value to fill the buffer with before rendering. Usually this is 0, however for example for Pz you might set it to 1e17. This value is also passed to the render delegate when it allocates the render buffer for the AOV.
parameters.heading: Husk

parameters.label: Channel Prefix
parameters.description: When creating channel names for an AOV, husk will create channel component names based on the type of data. For example, a color channel's names would be R, G, B. This option allows you to prefix the component names with a common name. For example, setting the prefix to diffuse would cause the component names to be diffuse.R, diffuse.G, diffuse.B.
parameters.heading: Husk

parameters.label: Channel Lower RGB
parameters.description: Normally, husk will create OpenEXR channel suffixes for color channels using uppercase R, G, B and A. If this option is turned on, the suffixes will be lower-case r, g, b and a. For example diffuse.r, diffuse.g, diffuse.b instead of diffuse.R, diffuse.G, diffuse.B. This only applies to color channels.
parameters.heading: Husk

parameters.label: Source Color Space
parameters.description: Specifies the source color space for the RenderVar. This is usually the internal working space for the render delegate (i.e. scene_linear). This option allows the source color space to be manually specified. Normally. non-color AOVs (i.e. point or normal data) will default to the raw color space. This option can force these AOVs to be interpreted as a color with the given color space.
parameters.heading: Husk

parameters.label: Output Color Space
parameters.description: Specifies the output color space for the RenderVar. This is the color space that the source color data will be transformed to before writing to the render product output. By default, husk will use the OpenColorIO file_rules to determine the output color space automatically. Normally, non-color AOVs (i.e. point or normal data) will default to the raw color space. This option can force these AOVs to be interpreted as color data and transform the color before writing.
parameters.heading: Husk

parameters.label: Compression
parameters.description: Some formats allow per-AOV compression. This will set the compression on this AOV.
parameters.heading: Husk

parameters.label: OpenEXR Compression
parameters.description: When saving multi-part OpenEXR images, this specifies the compression for this AOV. For example, you may want to use a lossy compression (like DWA) for color channels, but a non-lossy compression (like piz) when saving geometric normals.
parameters.heading: Husk

parameters.label: DWA Compression Level
parameters.description: The compression level when using DWA-A or DWA-B compression.
parameters.heading: Husk

parameters.label: Bypass Save
parameters.description: Sometimes, certain AOVs are required for slap comp, but don't need to be saved. If turned on, husk computes the AOV's values and allocates memory, but won't save the AOV to the output image.
parameters.heading: Husk

entries.label: Resample Transforms
entries.summary: Generates interpolated transform time samples from existing time samples on USD prims.

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.description: The primitive(s) the node should operate on. You can drag primitives from the scene graph tree pane into this textbox to add their paths, or click the Smallicon:BUTTONS/reselect Reselect button beside the text box to select the primitives in the viewer, or ((Ctrl))-click the Reselect button to choose prims from a pop-up tree window. You can also use primitive patterns for advanced matching, including matching all prims in a collection (using /path/to/prim.collection:<<name>>). You can drag and drop a specific (or multiple specific) USD prim(s) from the Scene Graph Tree into the window to run validation on only these USD primitives. NOTE: This parameter needs to be exposed in order for the transform handles to be context-aware. Without it, the handles may not be positioned properly.

parameters.label: Time Sample Spacing
parameters.description: The spacing in time for the resampled data.

parameters.label: Include Original Samples
parameters.description: Whether to also include the original sample data or only the resampled data.

entries.label: Restructure Scene Graph
entries.summary: This node has various operations for editing prim paths, variant sets, and composition arcs.

parameters.label: Flatten Node Input Layers
parameters.description: Automatically flatten all incoming sublayers. If this is off, you can only edit the selected prims within a single sublayer. If you want to edit prims across sublayers, you must turn on Flatten Node Input Layers to flatten the incoming sublayers into a flat stage before the node moves the prims.

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.description: A space-separated list of prim paths to modify. This can include primitive pattern matching syntax, which allows advanced matching based on various criteria.

parameters.label: Operation
parameters.description: How this node should edit the prims selected in the Primitives parm above. Reparent Primitives: Moves the selected prims to be children of the New Parent Prim. Rename Primitives: Renames the selected prims. Uses the Old Name token and replaces any occurrences with New Name. Remove Primitives: Removes the selected prims. Rename Variant Set: Changes the name of a variant set on the selected prim(s). Remove Variant Set: Removes a named variant set from the selected prim(s). Remove References: Removes reference, payload, inherits, and/or specializes arcs from the selected prim(s).

parameters.label: New Parent Prim
parameters.description: When Operation is Reparent Primitives, use this prim as a new, _least_ local transform. By default creates missing primitives as over, but options exist to define new parent prims.

parameters.label: Create Parent Prims
parameters.description: Whether to create new intermediate prims when the New Parent Prim path does not already exist.
parameters.heading: Create Parent Prim(s)

parameters.label: Primitive Type
parameters.description: If any parents of a path in Primitive Paths do not exist, this node will automatically create them. In this case, it will create parent nodes of this type.
parameters.heading: Create Parent Prim(s)

parameters.label: Primitive Specifier
parameters.description: The USD operator to use when creating the new prims. Define: Authors a completely new prim. Use this if you want to create a brand new prim or replace an existing prim. Over: Authors an override of an existing prim. Attributes not explicitly authored on this prim will get their values from the existing prim on the lower layer. Class: Define a primitive class. This is usually not necessary unless you are doing deep USD magic.
parameters.heading: Create Parent Prim(s)

parameters.label: Only Define Missing Prims
parameters.description: When Create Parent Prims and this parameter are on, the node authors overrides on existing prims instead of redefining them in this layer. When Create Parent Prims is on but this is off, the node redefines all the parent prims even if they already exist in another layer.
parameters.heading: Create Parent Prim(s)

parameters.label: Old Name
parameters.description: When Operation is Rename Primitives, set this to pattern match the old name. For example, to rename all prims that end in _left to end in _right, set the Old name to *_left and the New Name below to *_right. Also see Rename primitives rules for more information.
parameters.heading: Operation: Rename Primitives

parameters.label: New Name
parameters.description: When Operation is Rename Primitives, set this parameter to match the new name. In this field, @name represents the old name, and @index represents the position of the prim in the selection (for example, for the first selected prim @index will be 0, for the second prim @index will be 1, and so on). For example, to append _post to the name of the selected prims, set Old name above to @name and New Name to @name_post. Also see Rename primitives rules for more information.
parameters.heading: Operation: Rename Primitives

parameters.label: Remove Empty Variants
parameters.description: When Operation is Remove Primitives, remove empty variants and variant sets left over after removing primitives.
parameters.heading: Operation: Remove Primitives

parameters.label: Old Variant Set Name
parameters.description: When Operation is Rename Variant Set, rename any variant set with this name on a selected prim to New Variant Set Name.
parameters.heading: Operation: Rename Variant Set

parameters.label: New Variant Set Name
parameters.description: When Operation is Rename Variant Set, this is the new name for variant sets on the selected prims that match Old Variant Set Name.
parameters.heading: Operation: Rename Variant Set

parameters.label: Variant Sets
parameters.description: When Operation is Remove Variant Set, delete any variant set with this name on any of the selected prims.
parameters.heading: Operation: Remove Variant Set

parameters.label: References
parameters.description: When Operation is Remove References and this is on, remove _any_ references on the selected prims.
parameters.heading: Operation: Remove References

parameters.label: Payloads
parameters.description: When Operation is Remove References and this is on, remove _any_ payloads on the selected prims.
parameters.heading: Operation: Remove References

parameters.label: Inherits
parameters.description: When Operation is Remove References and this is on, remove _any_ "inherits" relationships on the selected prims.
parameters.heading: Operation: Remove References

parameters.label: Specializes
parameters.description: When Operation is Remove References and this is on, remove _any_ "specializes" relationships on the selected prims.
parameters.heading: Operation: Remove References

entries.label: Retime Instances
entries.summary: Offsets and/or scales the timing of animation on selected instances.

parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: Whether you want to retime point instances, or instanceable primitives.

parameters.label: Instances
parameters.description: A space-separated list of instances, using /<<path>><<instance_index>> syntax (for example, /geometry/instancer0 /geometry/instancer1). To select all instances in an instancer, use /<<path>>*. To select a range, use /geometry/instancer4-7 (the range is inclusive). To select instances inside nested instancers, use multiple indexes, for example /geometry/instancer27. VEXpressions can be used to specify instances, for example, /geometry/instancer{@weights>0.5}.

parameters.label: Instances
parameters.description: When Type is Native Instances, a list of paths to instanceable prims.

parameters.label: Retime Using
parameters.description: How to compute the transform for each selected instance. Internal SOP: Uses the SOP subnet inside this node to process points representing the instances. External SOP: Uses an external SOP network that must generate points representing the instances from scratch. (See point cloud editing above.) Primitive Properties: Gets the offset/scale primvars on the instancer/instance primitives themselves. Random Values: Creates a set number of random offsets and scales distributed across instances.

parameters.label: Retime Method
parameters.description: When Retime Using is set to Internal SOP, External SOP or Primitive Properties, you can specify the retiming method. Frame Offset and Time Scale: Retime using a frame offset and a time scale. The referenced prototype/primvar/transform will be looked up using ($F + frame offset) / time scale. This is the preferred method as it can be expressed as a constant, non time-dependent, value which can improve performance when retiming prototypes. Explicit Frame: Set the time offset by specifying the frame at which the retimed prototype/primvar/transform should be referenced. NOTE: Since this will be a time dependent attribute or primvar in most cases, it will force the retimed prototype creation to be time dependent which will impact performance. When retiming prototypes by a fixed frame offset, it is generally recommended to use the Frame Offset and Time Scale retime method.

parameters.label: Match By ID
parameters.description: When Modify Using is External SOP and this is on, the node looks for id SOP attributes on the generated points. The id should be the index of the corresponding instance. (When this is off, the node matches point numbers to instance indices, which only works if you process every instance in a single instancer.)

parameters.label: SOP Path
parameters.description: When Modify Using is External SOP, the node path to the geometry node to cook to get the generated points. Each point in the output should correspond to one of the selected instances.

parameters.label: Group
parameters.description: When Modify Using is External SOP, if this is not blank, only consider points in this point group.

parameters.label: Retime Prototypes
parameters.description: Create retimed prototypes for the specified instances. When instance animation is driven by instance-level transforms, turning this off will greatly improve performance.

parameters.label: Retime Transforms
parameters.description: Even if instance transforms are animated, by default this node does not affect them. Turn this on to re-time transform animation as well.

parameters.label: Retime Primvars
parameters.description: Even if instance-level primvars are animated, by default this node does not affect them. Turn this on to re-time primvar animation as well.

parameters.label: Only Affect Retimed
parameters.description: When this options is enabled, retimed prototypes with frame offsets equal to zero and time scales equal to 1, or explicit frames equal to the current frame, will be ignored.

parameters.label: Evaluation Frame
parameters.description: In order to improve performance and to guarantee a fixed number of retimed prototypes, select a frame where the instances are retimed by a unique amount. Creating the retimed prototypes is split into its own non time-dependent process where possible which can have a significant impact on playback performance.

parameters.label: Use Frame Offset
parameters.description: Enable frame offsets to drive the instance retiming. This timeshifts the instance animation.
parameters.heading: Frame Offset

parameters.label: Attribute
parameters.description: When Retime Using is Internal SOP or External SOP, the name of the SOP point attribute that specifies the frame offset or time scale for each instance.
parameters.heading: Frame Offset

parameters.label: Primvar
parameters.description: When Retime Using is Primitive Properties, the name of a primvar on the instancer that specifies the frame offset or time scale for each instance.
parameters.heading: Frame Offset

parameters.label: Global Frame Offset
parameters.description: When Retime Using is Primitive Properties or Random Values, you can apply this offset to all instances equally, in addition to any per-instance offsets.
parameters.heading: Frame Offset

parameters.label: Variations
parameters.description: When Retime Using is Random Values, specify the total number of unique frame offset or time scale values.
parameters.heading: Frame Offset

parameters.label: Min/Max
parameters.description: When Retime Using is Random Values, specify the minimum and maximum values for the frame offset or time scales.
parameters.heading: Frame Offset

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.description: When Retime Using is Random Values, specify the seed to use when generating a random number for each instance.
parameters.heading: Frame Offset

parameters.label: Distribution
parameters.description: When Retime Using is Random Values, allows the user to control the distribution of the random values between the specified Min/Max.
parameters.heading: Frame Offset

parameters.label: Use Time Scale
parameters.description: Enable time scales to drive the instance retiming. This slows down or speeds up the instance animation.
parameters.heading: Time Scale

parameters.label: Variations
parameters.description: When Retime Using is Random Values, specify the total number of unique frame offset or time scale values.
parameters.heading: Time Scale

parameters.label: Min/Max
parameters.description: When Retime Using is Random Values, specify the minimum and maximum values for the frame offset or time scales.
parameters.heading: Time Scale

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.description: When Retime Using is Random Values, specify the seed to use when generating a random number for each instance.
parameters.heading: Time Scale

parameters.label: Distribution
parameters.description: When Retime Using is Random Values, allows the user to control the distribution of the random values between the specified Min/Max.
parameters.heading: Time Scale

parameters.label: Global Time Scale
parameters.description: Apply this time scaling factor to all instances equally, on top of any per-instance scales.
parameters.heading: Time Scale

parameters.label: Attribute
parameters.description: When Retime Using is set to Internal SOP or External SOP , the name of the SOP point attribute that specifies the frame the retimed prototype should be using.
parameters.heading: Explicit Frame

parameters.label: Primvar
parameters.description: When Retime Using is set to Primitive Properties, the name of the SOP point attribute that specifies the frame the retimed prototype should be using.
parameters.heading: Explicit Frame

entries.label: Scatter Instances
entries.summary: Hydra generative procedural and LOP node for scattering instances.

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.description: The scene graph path at which to create the generative procedural prim.

parameters.label: Execution Mode
parameters.description: Sets whether the scatter procedural should be executed at render-time in Hydra, or author the pointinstancer immediately. Generally, the results in the rendered frame should be indistinguishable from one another, apart from small calculation differences. Deferred | The scattering process is not computed in LOPs, instead Engine executes the scattering within a Hydra Scene Index. Immediate | The scattering process is executed as part of the LOP node cook, and the resulting instances are all authored to the stage.

parameters.label: Up Axis
parameters.description: The direction of the scene's up axis, for purposes of computer the instance scattering and transforms.

parameters.label: Enable Camera
parameters.description: Use a camera as part of the scattering procedural.

parameters.label: Camera Path
parameters.description: The scene graph path of the camera used for computing the scatter procedural. When cameras are enabled, but no path is specified, the current render camera is used instead.

parameters.label: Prim Pattern
parameters.description: The primitives onto which instances will be scattered.
parameters.heading: Source Geometry

parameters.label: Animation (Beta)
parameters.description: Scatter on transforming and deforming surfaces. Not fully supported yet.
parameters.heading: Source Geometry

parameters.label: Rest Primvar
parameters.description: The name of the primvar to use for rest space.
parameters.heading: Input Primvars

parameters.label: TexCoord Source
parameters.description: Geometry | Texture coordinates primvar authored on the scatter target geometry. Camera Projection | Texture coordinates are projected from the camera onto the scatter target geometry.
parameters.heading: Texture Coordinates

parameters.label: TexCoord Primvar
parameters.description: Name of the texture coordinate primvar.
parameters.heading: Texture Coordinates

parameters.label: Point Count Method
parameters.description: How the number of instance points is determined and computed. Note that even when scattering a specific number, masks or other control signals may affect the final number of instances. Number | Scatters an absolute number of points across the target geometry. Density | Roughly the number of points per area unit, distributed across the target geometry. Face Centroids | Creates a single point for each polygon on the scatter target geometry.
parameters.heading: Scattering

parameters.label: Scatter Count
parameters.description: The base number of points to be scattered on the target geometry.
parameters.heading: Number of Instances

parameters.label: Enable Scatter Count Map
parameters.description: Scales the number of points by a texture map.
parameters.heading: Number of Instances

parameters.label: Texture Map
parameters.description: The image of float values that scale the number of scattered points.
parameters.heading: Number of Instances

parameters.label: Enable Scatter Count Primvar
parameters.description: Scales the number of points by a primvar on the scatter target geometry.
parameters.heading: Number of Instances

parameters.label: Primvar
parameters.description: The name of the float primvar to adjust the number of points scattered.
parameters.heading: Number of Instances

parameters.label: Density
parameters.description: The base density of points across the surface.
parameters.heading: Instance Density

parameters.label: Enable Scatter Density Map
parameters.description: Use a texture map to scale the scatter density.
parameters.heading: Instance Density

parameters.label: Texture Map
parameters.description: The image of float values that scale the scattered point density.
parameters.heading: Instance Density

parameters.label: Enable Scatter Density Map
parameters.description: Scales the scattered point density by a texture map.
parameters.heading: Instance Density

parameters.label: Primvar
parameters.description: Scales the density of points by a float primvar on the scatter target geometry.
parameters.heading: Instance Density

parameters.label: Scatter in Texture Space
parameters.description: The name of the float primvar to adjust the scattered point density.
parameters.heading: Instance Density

parameters.label: Enable Map
parameters.description: Use a texture map to hide or show an instance on a given mesh face.
parameters.heading: Face Centroids

parameters.label: Texture Map
parameters.description: The image of float or integer values that hide or show an instance on a given mesh face.
parameters.heading: Face Centroids

parameters.label: Enable Primvar
parameters.description: Use a primvar to hide or show an instance on a given mesh face.
parameters.heading: Face Centroids

parameters.label: Primvar
parameters.description: The float or integer values that hide or show an instance on a given mesh face.
parameters.heading: Face Centroids

parameters.label: Max Point Limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of points that can be scattered by the procedural.
parameters.heading: Face Centroids

parameters.label: Relax Iterations
parameters.description: Number of iterations used to relax the scattered points.
parameters.heading: Face Centroids

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.description: Seed used to control the distribution of points.
parameters.heading: Face Centroids

parameters.label: Up Axis Direction
parameters.description: Whether to calculate a mask using the angle between the surface geometry and the up axis.
parameters.heading: Up Axis Direction

parameters.label: Max Angle
parameters.description: Maximum angle between the surface normal and up-axis, at which to scatter points on the target geometry.

parameters.label: Reverse Direction
parameters.description: Reverses the up axis direction.

parameters.label: Cast Shadows

parameters.label: Invert
parameters.description: Inverts the mask effect.

parameters.label: Ambient Occlusion
parameters.description: Whether to calculate an ambient occlusion mask on the surface geometry.

parameters.label: Maximum Ray Distance
parameters.description: Maximum distance in world units to cast rays and test for surfaces.

parameters.label: Input Min
parameters.description: Minimum occlusion sets the mask to 0.

parameters.label: Input Max
parameters.description: Maximum occlusion sets the mask to 1.

parameters.label: Enable Camera Mask

parameters.label: Frustum Padding

parameters.label: Enable Camera Mask Near

parameters.label: Enable Camera Mask Far

parameters.label: Override Far Plane

parameters.label: Invert
