entries.label: Store Parameter Values
entries.summary: Lets you store temporary (unsaved) data in the stage.

parameters.label: Parameters
parameters.description: You can store multiple parameter values in a single node. Set this to the number of values you want to store, or click the plus and minus buttons to add or remove values.

parameters.label: Enable
parameters.description: For each value, whether to actually compute and store the value.

parameters.label: Name
parameters.description: The property name to use to store the value. This should be a valid USD property name that doesn't conflict with existing property names. You may want to add a double-underscore at the start to make it more unique. For example, indices.

parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: USD data type of the value you want to store. If you want to store an array, set the type to "auto" and return a string that looks like a Python list literal (for example "1,2,3"). You should probably stick to int, float, double, or string. If you have more complex data, choose string and encode it as JSON.

parameters.label: Value
parameters.description: A string representation of the value to store. You will usually want to drive the value of this parameter with a Python script (see How to above). If you want to store an array, set the type to Auto and make this a string that looks like a Python list literal (for example 1,2,3).

entries.label: SubLayer
entries.summary: Imports from USD files or other LOP node chains into as sublayers, or removes/replaces/reorders existing sublayers.

parameters.label: Load Payloads
parameters.description: When this option is on (the default), the payload loading configuration of the input stage is not changed. When this option is off, the stage's load mask will be modified to turn off all payload loading. Note that this will affect the loading of payloads anywhere in the stage, not just payloads loaded by the sublayers added by this node. Use the Configure Stage LOP to have more control over which payloads are loaded on the stage.
parameters.heading: Parent Layer

parameters.label: Copy Layer Metadata to Stage Root Layer
parameters.label_norm: copy layer metadata to stage root layer
parameters.description: Layer metadata is not composed by USD following the normal rules. In order for values like the frames per second or up axis settings to apply to a USD stage, they must be set directly on the root layer of the stage. This means any layer metadata authored on a file being loaded by this node will not affect the stage level metadata. This options allow for the explicit copying of layer metadata from the first layer loaded by this node on to the stage's root layer. If multiple files are specified, it it always the first file that has its values copied to the root layer. The Auto option for this parameter acts like a Yes (copy the sublayer's metadata to the root layer) if there is no input connected to the first input of this node. Otherwise it behaves as a No (does not affect the stage's root layer metadata).
parameters.heading: Parent Layer

parameters.label: Edit Root Layer
parameters.description: When this is on (the default), the new sublayers are added to the layer stack. This is usually what you want. When this is off, the content of the imported layers become sublayers of the active layer. Turning this on or off usually does not make a visible difference, but affects the priority given to opinions on the layers, and what content is in what layers when you write USD to disk. NOTE: Inside an Edit Layer Block this parameter will be disabled, and will be treated as being off.
parameters.heading: Parent Layer

parameters.label: Find Sublayers
parameters.description: A space-separated list of patterns that match layers by their "source file" metadata. This selects the layers for removal or reordering when you use the Remove Found Sublayers or Sublayer Position parameters below.
parameters.heading: Parent Layer

parameters.label: Remove Found Sublayers
parameters.description: Turn this on to remove any layers that match the patterns the Find Sublayers. This is useful if you want to _replace_ layers rather than just add them. For example, you may be editing a layer that has sublayers for animation, effects, and lighting. If your LOP network generates a new version of the effects layer, you would want to remove the existing effects layer and replace it with the new one.
parameters.heading: Parent Layer

parameters.label: Sublayer Type
parameters.description: Where to add sublayers from. Sublayer Files and Inputs: Import layers from file(s) on disk, and then import layers from LOP node branches connected to this node's multi-input. Sublayer Files: Import layers from file(s) on disk. Sublayer Inputs: Import layers from LOP node branches connected to this node's multi-input.
parameters.heading: Composition

parameters.label: Handle Missing Files
parameters.description: When Sublayer Type is Sublayer Files, what to do when a file (either a file you specify or a file referenced inside another file) cannot be found. Error for Missing Files: The node errors, preventing cooking the rest of the network. Warn for Missing Files: The node shows a warning, then passes through the first input unchanged. Ignore Missing Files: The node silently ignores the missing file, and passes through the first input unchanged. Allow Missing Files on the Stage: Author the reference to the sublayer even if it currently doesn't exist. This node and the following nodes will probably print warnings from the USD libraries about missing files.
parameters.heading: Composition

parameters.label: Sublayer Position
parameters.description: Where in the sublayer stack to insert the new layers. The position affects the priority of its opinions compared to other layers. Strongest Position: Add the new layers as the strongest sublayers. The opinions in these layers override all other layers. Weakest Position: Add the new layers as the weakest sublayers. The opinions in these layers will be overridden by any sublayer with an opinion on the same data. Strongest File Layer’s Position: Add the new layers where their opinions are stronger than the strongest layer that is loaded from a file on disk. This option can be used to keep all LOP-authored layers together, allowing them to be flattened into a single layer when saving to disk. Strongest Found Layer’s Position: Add the new layers where their opinions are stronger than the strongest layer found by the Find Layers parameter. Weakest Found Layer’s Position: Add the new layers where their opinions are weaker than the weakest layer found by the Find Layers parameter. Specific Index: Insert the new layers into the sublayer stack at a specific position (set by the Position index parameter below). Lower numbers represent stronger opinions. Setting this to 0 is the same as choosing "Strongest Position".
parameters.heading: Composition

parameters.label: Position Index
parameters.description: When Sublayer Position is Specific index. Insert the new layers at this specific position. Lower numbers represent stronger opinions. Setting this to 0 is the same as setting Sublayer Position to Strongest Position.
parameters.heading: Composition

parameters.label: Number of Files
parameters.description: This node can sublayer in more than one file at a time. Enter the number of files to import, or click the plus and minus buttons to add or remove layer files.
parameters.heading: Composition

parameters.label: Reload Files
parameters.description: Click to reload the contents of all files imported by this node. This also clears the cache of file wildcard pattern expansions.
parameters.heading: Sublayer File #

parameters.label: Multi-inputs
parameters.description: Whether to add the LOP node layers connected to the multi-input to the stage.
parameters.heading: Sublayer File #

entries.label: Surface Constraint
entries.summary: Constrain a prim to stick to a surface.

parameters.label: Sampling Behavior
parameters.description: Cooking this node can generate many USD time samples, rather than just a single time sample at the current time. This can be equivalent to having a Cache LOP following this node, but it will evaluate much faster, and does not cache data from any other nodes. This allows animated data to be authored to USD without introducing a node time dependency which would then cause all following nodes to also be time dependent. This can vastly improve playback performance of some LOP Networks. In all sampling modes, if a parameter on this node does not vary with time, and does not rely on other time sampled data from the stage, only a single default value will be generated in USD for the corresponding attribute. USD time samples are only generated for parameters that may vary over time. Sample Current Frame: A single time sample will be generated for the current time. Sample Frame Range If Input Is Not Time Dependent: If the input to this node is time dependent, this node behaves as if it is in Sample Current Frame mode. Otherwise it behaves as if it is in Sample Frame Range mode. Sample Frame Range: The Start/End/Inc parameter is used to generate multiple times at which this node's parameters are evaluated, and a USD time sample is created for each attribute at each one of these times.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Start/End/Inc
parameters.description: When the Sampling behavior is Sample Frame Range, this parameter controls the number and spacing of base time samples to be generated by this node. The default values of this parameter are @fstart, @fend, and @finc. These values correspond to the start, end, and step size of the global Houdini animation settings when interacting with Houdini. When using a ROP node to generate a range of frames, these values correspond to the start, end, and increment values specified on the ROP node being executed. This default ensures that a USD file written to disk will contain time samples for exactly the frame range requested by the ROP (regardless of the Houdini animation settings).
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Subframe Sampling
parameters.description: For each primary sample generated by this node, these parameters can cause additional samples to be generated around that primary sample time. This is most often used to ensure that accurate data exists at exactly the camera shutter open and close times, as well as at the primary sample time.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Shutter
parameters.description: Controls the method used to specify the shutter open and close times relative to the primary sample times. Specify Manually: The Shutter Open/Close parameter values provide exact offset values relative to the primary sample time. Use Camera Prim: The Camera Prim parameter provides the scene graph path of a camera primitive from which the shutter open and close times are extracted to provide the offset values relative to the primary time sample.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Shutter Open/Close
parameters.description: When Shutter is set to Specify Manually, these two offset values are added to the primary sample time to indicate the shutter open and close times. The open time should be less than or equal to zero, and the close time should be greater than or equal to zero.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Camera Prim
parameters.description: When Shutter is set to Use Camera Prim, this is the scene graph path of a camera prim on the input node's stage. The shutter open and close attribute values are read from this primitive.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Samples
parameters.description: The number of subframe samples to create for each primary sample. These samples are evenly distributed between the shutter open and close times. Note that such an even distribution may or may not create a sample at exactly the primary sample time.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Always Include Frame Sample
parameters.description: When turned on, forces a sample to be created at exactly the primary sample time. If the Samples value, together with the shutter open and close times, already place a sample at the primary sample time, turning on this option has no effect. Otherwise, this option causes an addition sample to be added. This means that the actual number of samples per primary sample may in fact be one more than the number specified in the Samples parameter.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: Whether the source (the thing constrained to the surface) is a regular primitive, or a point instance. You *cannot* use a nested point instance as a source.
parameters.heading: Source

parameters.label: Source
parameters.description: When Source Type is Primitive, the scene graph path to the prim to use.
parameters.heading: Source

parameters.label: Source Instances
parameters.description: When Source Type is PointInstancer, the point instance to use, using /<<path>><<instance_index>> syntax (for example, /geometry/instancer1).
parameters.heading: Source

parameters.label: Target Source
parameters.description: Where to get the surface to stick to, either the node's First Input or the Second Input.
parameters.heading: Surface

parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: Whether the surface is a regular primitive, or a point instance.
parameters.heading: Surface

parameters.label: Target
parameters.description: When Target Type is Primitive, the scene graph path to the prim to use.
parameters.heading: Surface

parameters.label: Target Instance
parameters.description: When Target Type is PointInstancer, the point instance to use, using /<<path>><<instance_index>> syntax (for example, /geometry/instancer1).
parameters.heading: Surface

parameters.label: Hide Target
parameters.description: When Target Source is First Input and Type is Primitive, whether to hide set the path's visibility to "hidden".
parameters.heading: Surface

parameters.label: Import Time
parameters.description: Specify the frame at which the source and/or target geometry are imported into the embedded SOP network to build the constraints. The default $FF expression forces the constraint LOP to be time dependent, which is needed when operating on a non time-dependent network that has time samples driving the source or target primitives. However, for better performance with a non time-dependent network with no time samples, it is recommended to use a static value instead.
parameters.heading: Constraint Options

parameters.label: Maintain Local Offset
parameters.description: When this is off (the default), the source object snaps onto the surface. When this is on, the object maintains the same relative distance between itself and the surface as it follows the shape of the surface.
parameters.heading: Constraint Options

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: How to map a position parameter onto the surface. UV (Sticky): Look up the coordinates in the UV parameter on the surface using the texture coordinates from a primvar (specified in the UV Attribute parameter). Primitive + UV: Treat the coordinates in the UV parameter as intrinsic local UV coordinates on a specific polygon face, where the first two components are U and V coordinates, and the third component (W) is the index of the polygon face. This does not require an attribute containing texture coordinates. Point Group: Place the source object at the surface point closest to the centroid of the points in a certain geometry subset. Primitive Group: Place the source object at the surface point closest to the centroid of the polygon faces in a certain geometry subset. Closest Distance: Places the source object at the surface point closes to the world space position in the Position parameter.
parameters.heading: Constraint Options

parameters.label: UV Attribute
parameters.description: When Mode is UV (Sticky), the name of a primvar containing texture coordinates. For geometry imported from SOPs, this may be uv, however in USD it is usually called st. The texture coordinates must be non-overlapping.
parameters.heading: Constraint Options

parameters.label: UV
parameters.description: When Mode is UV (Sticky), the texture coordinate at which to place the source object.
parameters.heading: Constraint Options

parameters.label: Group
parameters.description: When Mode is Point Group or Primitive Group, the name of a geometry subset to find the closest surface point to.
parameters.heading: Constraint Options

parameters.label: Position Attribute
parameters.description: When Mode is Closest Distance, the name of a primvar containing point positions. For geometry imported from SOPs, this may be P, but in USD this is usually the positions attribute.
parameters.heading: Constraint Options

parameters.label: Position
parameters.description: When Mode is Closest Distance, the world space position to find the closest surface point to.
parameters.heading: Constraint Options

parameters.label: Use Snippet
parameters.description: When Mode is UV (Sticky), Primitive + UV, or Closest Distance, you can set the position/UV using a VEX snippet. @ptnum is the index of the current prim being constrained. You can use npoints(0) to get the total number of prims being constrained. You can use @Frame and @Time to make the snippet time-dependent. The initial value of pos (at the start of the snippet) is the evaluated value of the Position or UV parameter (depending on the Mode). So you can use an expression in that parameter to compute a "base" value, and modify it using the snippet.
parameters.heading: Constraint Options

parameters.label: Look At Mode
parameters.description: How to orient the source object. None: Don't rotate the source object. U Direction: Use the surface's U direction as the Look At direction. This works best with NURBS surfaces. V Direction: Use the surface's V direction as the Look At direction. This works best with NURBS surfaces. Direction Attribute from Geometry: Use the value of a vector primvar on the surface as the Look At vector. From Primitive: Rotate the source object to always point at a certain prim.
parameters.heading: Orientation

parameters.label: Look At Source
parameters.description: When Look At Mode is From Primitive, where to get the primitive to look at (the first or second input).
parameters.heading: Orientation

parameters.label: Look At Xform
parameters.description: When Look At Mode is From Primitive, the scene graph path of the prim to look at. (This does not support looking at a point instance.)
parameters.heading: Orientation

parameters.label: Direction Attribute
parameters.description: When Look At Mode is Direction Attribute from Geometry, the name of a vector primvar (without the primvar: prefix) on the surface to use as the look at vector.
parameters.heading: Orientation

parameters.label: Look Up Mode
parameters.description: How to compute the up vector. Up Vector Attribute from Geometry: Use vector3f primvar on the surface to specify the up vector at each point. U Direction: Use the surface's U direction as the up vector. This works best with NURBS surfaces. V Direction: Use the surface's V direction as the up vector. This works best with NURBS surfaces. X Axis: Use the world +X direction as the up vector. Y Axis: Use the world +Y direction as the up vector. Z Axis: Use the world +Z direction as the up vector. From Primitive: Rotate the source prim so its up vector points at a specific prim as it moves along the curve. Custom: Use the vector in the Up Vector Attribute from Geometry parameter.
parameters.heading: Orientation

parameters.label: Up Vector Source
parameters.description: When Look Up Mode is From Primitive, where to get the primitive to point the up vector at (the first or second input).
parameters.heading: Orientation

parameters.label: Up Vector Xform
parameters.description: When Look Up Mode is From Primitive, the scene graph path of the prim to point the up vector at. (This does not support point instances.)
parameters.heading: Orientation

parameters.label: Look At Axis
parameters.description: Which axis on the source object to match to the look at vector. You can use this to compensate for the orientation the source object was created in. This can't be the same as the Look Up Axis.
parameters.heading: Orientation

parameters.label: Look Up Axis
parameters.description: Which axis on the source object to match to the up vector. You can use this to compensate for the orientation the source object was created in. This can't be the same as the Look At Axis.
parameters.heading: Orientation

parameters.label: Up Attribute
parameters.description: When Look Up Mode is Up Vector Attribute from Geometry, the name of a vector3f primvar (minus the primvar: prefix) on the surface to use as the look up vector.
parameters.heading: Orientation

parameters.label: Roll
parameters.description: Roll angle (in degrees) around the look at direction.
parameters.heading: Orientation

parameters.label: Use Snippet
parameters.description: Set the roll using a VEX snippet. The snippet should write the roll degrees to the roll variable. You can use the variables typically available to an Attribute Wrangle SOP. @ptnum is the index of the current prim being constrained. You can use npoints(0) to get the total number of prims being constrained. You can use @Frame and @Time to make the snippet time-dependent. The initial value of roll (at the start of the snippet) is the evaluated value of the Roll parameter. So you can use an expression in that parameter to compute a "base" value, and modify it using the snippet.
parameters.heading: Orientation

entries.label: Switch
entries.summary: Passes through one of several inputs, based on a parameter choice or expression.

parameters.label: Choose Input
parameters.description: Specifies how this node decides which input to pass through. By Input Index: Choose the input by setting Select Input to position of the connection in the multi-input (numbered from left to right, starting at 0). By Input Name: Choose which input to pass through by setting Select Input to its name. By Pattern Matching: Choose which input to pass through by setting Select Input to a value which is compared to the Match Pattern of each input, starting with the input on the left and moving right. The first input with a pattern that matches the value is passed through.

parameters.label: Select Input (integer)
parameters.description: When Choose Input is set to By Index, the index of the input to pass through (the position of the connection in the node's multi-input, from left to right starting at 0).

parameters.label: Select Input (string)
parameters.description: When Choose Input is set to By Name, the name of the input to pass through. The expression in the Input Name Default field computes a default name for each input (by default, the name of the node connected to the input), and you can rename inputs manually by clicking in the list of inputs below the parameters.

parameters.label: Select Input (string to pattern match)
parameters.description: When Choose Input is set to By Pattern Matching, the value that is compared against each input's pattern. You can set the pattern associated with each input by clicking in the Match Pattern column of the list of inputs below the parameters.

parameters.label: Bad Input Response
parameters.description: Controls the behavior of this node if an invalid input is specified by the Select Input parameter. Output Empty Stage: An empty stage is output, ignoring all connected inputs. Warn And Output Empty Stage: An empty stage is output, ignoring all connected inputs. In addition, a warning is added to this node. Error: An error is added to this node, so nothing is output. Clamp to Input Range: If the input is selected by integer index, and the value is less than zero, the first input is passed through. If the value is greater than the number of inputs, the last input is passed through. If the input is selected by name and the specified input name doesn't exist, the first input is passed through. Use Fallback Input: The Fallback Input is used. If the Fallback Input is also invalid, this will always generate an error, and nothing will be output from this node.

parameters.label: Fallback Input (integer)
parameters.description: When Choose Input is By Index and Bad Input Response is Use Fallback Input, the index of the input to pass through if Select Input (integer) specifies an out of range input index.

parameters.label: Fallback Input (string)
parameters.description: When Choose Input is By Name or By Pattern Matching and Bad Input Response is Use Fallback Input, the name of the input to pass through if Select Input (string) specifies an input name that doesn't exist.

parameters.label: Input Name Default
parameters.description: Should contain an expression that computes a default name for inputs you haven't explicitly given names. The expression can use the @input local variable ($IIDX is deprecated) to represent the index of the input for which to compute a name. The default (opinput(".", @input)) uses the name of the node connected to the input.

entries.label: Texture Material Library
entries.summary: Authors USD material primitives whose texture inputs are driven by COPs.

parameters.label: Default Resolution
parameters.description: Sets the context option for default_xres and default_yres. This is the size of layers that don't have an explicit size set. The default is 1024x1024.
parameters.heading: COP Network

parameters.label: Default Pixel Scale
parameters.description: Sets the context option default_pixelscale. This is a scale for the size of the pixels in the image, causing the image to cook at a fractional effective resolution, but not changing any pixel-relative values.
parameters.heading: COP Network

parameters.label: Default Border
parameters.description: Sets the context option default_border. This is an integer context option which encodes what the border type of new layers should be. Constant: Outside the layer evaluates to 0. Clamp: Outside the layer evalutes to the closest pixel in the layer. Mirror: Outside values reflect off the boundaries. Wrap: Outside values wrap around.
parameters.heading: COP Network

parameters.label: Default Precision
parameters.description: Sets the context option default_precision to control how many bits are used for each channel. 16-bit: A value of 16 meaning to default to half-precision. 32-bit: A value of 32 meaning to default to full-precision.
parameters.heading: COP Network

parameters.label: Default UDIM
parameters.description: Sets the context option UDIM. This is the tile in UV space to which the layer applies. See /solaris/udim for more information.
parameters.heading: COP Network

parameters.label: Tile Visualization
parameters.description: When evaluating the geometry for the 3D viewport, attach the tilevis primitive property to have it displayed with a repeating pattern. This makes it easy to see how well the pattern will tile and to verify operations haven't made it not tile.
parameters.heading: COP Network

parameters.label: Parent Primitive Type
parameters.description: If the intermediate prims in a material path don't exist, the node will create them. This controls the type of the intermediate prims this node creates.
parameters.heading: COP Network

parameters.label: Material Path Prefix
parameters.description: This is automatically prefixed to any material paths that are not absolute (do not start with a slash). This lets you specify relative paths in the multi-parm, and set their common USD parent hierarchy in this one parameter.
parameters.heading: COP Network

parameters.label: Number of Materials
parameters.description: The number of materials to create. Set the number or click the plus and minus buttons to add or remove material imports.
parameters.heading: COP Network

parameters.label: Material COP
parameters.description: The Houdini node path to a COP node representing a material. This is usually a USD Material COP that represents an existing USD material to be referenced.
parameters.heading: COP Network

parameters.label: Create Material COP
parameters.description: A button that creates a USD Material COP child inside, and sets the Material COP parameter to point to it.
parameters.heading: COP Network

parameters.label: Material Path
parameters.description: The scene graph path at which to create the USD material. If this is an absolute path (starts with a slash), it is used as-is. If this path is relative, it is relative to the path in the Material Path Prefix parameter.
parameters.heading: COP Network

parameters.label: Assign to Geometry
parameters.description: When this is on, you can assign the newly created material to USD geometry prims using the Geometry Primitives parameter below.
parameters.heading: COP Network

parameters.label: Geometry Primitives
parameters.description: When Assign to Geometry is on, assigns the newly created material to the primitives listed in this parameter.
parameters.heading: COP Network

entries.label: TimeShift
entries.summary: Outputs the stage as it is at a different point in the timeline.

parameters.label: Cook Input at Specified Time
parameters.description: Cook the nodes in the input chain at the frame/time set below. This affects Houdini parameter keyframe animation and expressions driven by the current frame/time. This does *not* affect time samples on USD attributes (you can control that with the Evaluate USD Attributes at Specified Time parameter).
parameters.heading: Houdini Timeline

parameters.label: Evaluate USD Attributes at Specified Time
parameters.label_norm: evaluate usd attributes at specified time
parameters.description: Evaluate attributes that have time sample information at the frame/time set below, and interpolates time sample values when no information is available at the exact time specified. This does *not* affect Houdini parameter keyframe animation and expressions (you can control that with the Cook Input at Specified Time parameter).
parameters.heading: USD Time Samples

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.description: The primitive(s) the node should operate on. You can drag primitives from the scene graph tree pane into this textbox to add their paths, or click the Smallicon:BUTTONS/reselect Reselect button beside the text box to select the primitives in the viewer, or ((Ctrl))-click the Reselect button to choose prims from a pop-up tree window. You can also use primitive patterns for advanced matching, including matching all prims in a collection (using /path/to/prim.collection:<<name>>). You can drag and drop a specific (or multiple specific) USD prim(s) from the Scene Graph Tree into the window to run validation on only these USD primitives. NOTE: This parameter needs to be exposed in order for the transform handles to be context-aware. Without it, the handles may not be positioned properly.
parameters.heading: USD Time Samples

parameters.label: Properties
parameters.description: A space separated list of property names which should be affected by this node. Normal Houdini string matching rules apply (accepting wildcards and using ^ to exclude patterns). The node compares this pattern against every property name on every selected primitive. This can mean the node affects a different set of properties on each primitive.
parameters.heading: USD Time Samples

parameters.label: Read Default Values
parameters.description: Enable this parameter to read attribute default values and write them to the output layer (as a time sample or default value depending on the value of Write Default Values). When this parameter is disabled, source attributes which only have a default value will be ignored.
parameters.heading: USD Time Samples

parameters.label: Write Default Values
parameters.description: USD attributes have a default value, which is used when the attribute has no time samples, or when you don't ask for the value at a specific time. When Evaluate USD Attributes at Specified Time and this are on, the node sets each timeshifted attribute value as the attribute's default in the output, instead of as a time sample. This is useful when you want to "extract" a static frame without animation.
parameters.heading: USD Time Samples

parameters.label: Method
parameters.description: Whether to specify the sample time by frame number or by seconds.

parameters.label: Frame
parameters.description: When Method is By Frame, sample the stage at this frame

parameters.label: Integer Frames
parameters.description: When Method is By Frame, round fractional frame numbers to whole integers.
parameters.heading: Time Handling

parameters.label: Time
parameters.description: When Method is By Time, sample the stage this number of seconds along the timeline.
parameters.heading: Time Handling

parameters.label: Transform Order
parameters.description: The order in which Houdini applies translates, rotates, and scales, and the order in which it applies rotation.

parameters.description: Amount of translation along uvw axes.

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.description: Amount of rotation about uvw axes.

parameters.label: Scale

parameters.label: Shear

parameters.label: Metric

parameters.label: Ignore Point Connectivity
parameters.description: Affect only points connected to the points in the group, or all points within the radius.
parameters.heading: Soft settings

parameters.label: Ignore UV Connectivity
parameters.description: Affect only vertices connected to the vertices in the group as seen in the UV viewport.
parameters.heading: Soft settings

entries.label: Unassign Material
entries.summary: Unbinds a material from one or more USD primitives.

parameters.label: Number of Primitives
parameters.description: Specifies number of available material un-assignment rules. Usually there is one rule per primitive (or set of related primitives).

parameters.label: Enable
parameters.description: Toggles the removal of the material binding on and off.

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.description: The primitive(s) from which you want to un-assign the material. You can click the select button beside the text box to select the primitives from the scene graph tree. You can also use primitive patterns for advanced matching.

parameters.label: Action
parameters.description: Specifies which materials to unbind. In USD it is possible that a geometry primitive may be bound to several materials, either through various mechanisms (e.g., direct or collection bindings), or at different ancestor levels. Only one material wins in the end, but unbinding that single material means that the next material in the precedence order becomes the active one. Unassign All Unassign N (Debug)

parameters.label: Purpose
parameters.description: The USD binding purpose for which to unbind the material.

parameters.label: Number of Materials
parameters.description: When unbinding only a limited number of bound materials, i.e., when Unassign All Materials toggle parameter is off, this parameter specifies how many top priority materials should be unbound. TIP

entries.label: Vary Material Assignment
entries.summary: Assign different materials across a number of prims to create variation.

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.description: The primitive(s) the node should operate on. You can drag primitives from the scene graph tree pane into this textbox to add their paths, or click the Smallicon:BUTTONS/reselect Reselect button beside the text box to select the primitives in the viewer, or ((Ctrl))-click the Reselect button to choose prims from a pop-up tree window. You can also use primitive patterns for advanced matching, including matching all prims in a collection (using /path/to/prim.collection:<<name>>). You can drag and drop a specific (or multiple specific) USD prim(s) from the Scene Graph Tree into the window to run validation on only these USD primitives. NOTE: This parameter needs to be exposed in order for the transform handles to be context-aware. Without it, the handles may not be positioned properly.

parameters.label: Materials
parameters.description: The material prims to choose from. You can use primitive patterns, including matching all prims in a collection (using /path/to/prim.collection:<<name>>).

parameters.label: Purpose
parameters.description: TBD
parameters.heading: Material Binding

parameters.label: Strength
parameters.description: TBD
parameters.heading: Material Binding

parameters.label: Bind Method
parameters.description: TBD
parameters.heading: Material Binding

parameters.label: Binding Path
parameters.description: TBD
parameters.heading: Material Binding

parameters.label: Collection Path
parameters.description: TBD
parameters.heading: Material Binding

parameters.label: Collection Name
parameters.description: TBD
parameters.heading: Material Binding

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.description: The seed value for random material selection. Changing this changes the "random" choices generated. You can use this to try different variations, or change the random choices over time.
parameters.heading: Material Binding

parameters.label: Method
parameters.description: How to choose materials for each selected prim. Random: Choose materials at random. You can use the Bias ramp to influence the distribution. Spatial Distribution: Assign materials in Voronoi noise-based "clumps", so prims in close proximity often get the same material. Weighted Random: Like Random, but lets you assign weights to each material, so some materials are chosen more often than others.
parameters.heading: Material Binding

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.description: When Method is Random, the horizontal axis is divided between the materials to choose from. At the center of a horizontal segment corresponding to a certain material, the height of the ramp is the percentage chance of that material being chosen. Set the Interpolation to Constant. For example, given three materials, to give the second material a 50% chance of being assigned, add a point at position 0.25, with a value of 0.5, set the last point's position to 0.75 with a value of 1. If the probabilities don't add up to exactly 100% the values are normalized. This ramp might be useful to interactively play with material probabilities, however if you want to assign specific probabilities to specific materials, it's much easier to use Method > Weighted Random.
parameters.heading: Method: Random

parameters.label: Method
parameters.description: Whether to specify the time at which to measure the prim positions in frames or by seconds.
parameters.heading: Reference Frame

parameters.label: Frame
parameters.description: Measure the positions of the prims at this frame number.
parameters.heading: Reference Frame

parameters.label: Integer Frames
parameters.description: Rounds the given frame number to the nearest integer frame, avoiding fractional frame cooking.
parameters.heading: Reference Frame

parameters.label: Time
parameters.description: Measure the positions of the prims at this number of seconds along the timeline.
parameters.heading: Reference Frame

parameters.label: Frequency
parameters.description: Controls the size of the Voronoi cells. A higher frequency will generate smaller cells.
parameters.heading: Cells

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.description: Moves the noise through 3D.
parameters.heading: Cells

parameters.label: Jitter
parameters.description: Lower values give more even cells, higher values give more variation between large cells and small cells.
parameters.heading: Cells

parameters.label: Frequency
parameters.description: The frequency of anti-aliased noise used to jitter primitive positions.
parameters.heading: Position Jitter

parameters.label: Amplitude
parameters.description: Scales anti-aliased noise used to jitter primitive positions.
parameters.heading: Position Jitter

parameters.label: Roughness
parameters.description: Coarseness of the noise used to jitter primitive positions.
parameters.heading: Position Jitter

parameters.label: Max Octaves
parameters.description: Maximum number of iterations of noise to apply when jittering primitive positions.
parameters.heading: Position Jitter

parameters.label: Auto-fill Materials
parameters.description: Creates multi-parm instances for each material selected in the Materials field. If you change the Materials pattern and want to re-do this, click Clear in the multi-parm, then click this button again.
parameters.heading: Method: Weighted Random

parameters.label: Enable
parameters.description: For each material, whether to assign it a weight.
parameters.heading: Method: Weighted Random

parameters.label: Material Path
parameters.description: Scene graph path to the material prim. If this material doesn't exist, or isn't listed in Materials, the node ignores it.
parameters.heading: Method: Weighted Random

parameters.label: Weight
parameters.description: A weighting factor to assign to the material. Materials with higher weights are more likely to be chosen. The node normalizes the weights, so they are all relative to each other. Note that materials listed in Materials but not in the multi-parm are considered to have a weight of 1.
parameters.heading: Method: Weighted Random

entries.label: Volume
entries.summary: References volume data on disk into a volume prim containing field prims.

parameters.label: Sampling Behavior
parameters.description: Cooking this node can generate many USD time samples, rather than just a single time sample at the current time. This can be equivalent to having a Cache LOP following this node, but it will evaluate much faster, and does not cache data from any other nodes. This allows animated data to be authored to USD without introducing a node time dependency which would then cause all following nodes to also be time dependent. This can vastly improve playback performance of some LOP Networks. In all sampling modes, if a parameter on this node does not vary with time, and does not rely on other time sampled data from the stage, only a single default value will be generated in USD for the corresponding attribute. USD time samples are only generated for parameters that may vary over time. Sample Current Frame: A single time sample will be generated for the current time. Sample Frame Range If Input Is Not Time Dependent: If the input to this node is time dependent, this node behaves as if it is in Sample Current Frame mode. Otherwise it behaves as if it is in Sample Frame Range mode. Sample Frame Range: The Start/End/Inc parameter is used to generate multiple times at which this node's parameters are evaluated, and a USD time sample is created for each attribute at each one of these times.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Start/End/Inc
parameters.description: When the Sampling behavior is Sample Frame Range, this parameter controls the number and spacing of base time samples to be generated by this node. The default values of this parameter are @fstart, @fend, and @finc. These values correspond to the start, end, and step size of the global Houdini animation settings when interacting with Houdini. When using a ROP node to generate a range of frames, these values correspond to the start, end, and increment values specified on the ROP node being executed. This default ensures that a USD file written to disk will contain time samples for exactly the frame range requested by the ROP (regardless of the Houdini animation settings).
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Subframe Sampling
parameters.description: For each primary sample generated by this node, these parameters can cause additional samples to be generated around that primary sample time. This is most often used to ensure that accurate data exists at exactly the camera shutter open and close times, as well as at the primary sample time.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Shutter
parameters.description: Controls the method used to specify the shutter open and close times relative to the primary sample times. Specify Manually: The Shutter Open/Close parameter values provide exact offset values relative to the primary sample time. Use Camera Prim: The Camera Prim parameter provides the scene graph path of a camera primitive from which the shutter open and close times are extracted to provide the offset values relative to the primary time sample.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Shutter Open/Close
parameters.description: When Shutter is set to Specify Manually, these two offset values are added to the primary sample time to indicate the shutter open and close times. The open time should be less than or equal to zero, and the close time should be greater than or equal to zero.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Camera Prim
parameters.description: When Shutter is set to Use Camera Prim, this is the scene graph path of a camera prim on the input node's stage. The shutter open and close attribute values are read from this primitive.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Samples
parameters.description: The number of subframe samples to create for each primary sample. These samples are evenly distributed between the shutter open and close times. Note that such an even distribution may or may not create a sample at exactly the primary sample time.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Always Include Frame Sample
parameters.description: When turned on, forces a sample to be created at exactly the primary sample time. If the Samples value, together with the shutter open and close times, already place a sample at the primary sample time, turning on this option has no effect. Otherwise, this option causes an addition sample to be added. This means that the actual number of samples per primary sample may in fact be one more than the number specified in the Samples parameter.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.description: Create the main volume primitive at this scene graph path.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Primitive Kind
parameters.description: Set this as the new volume prim's kind. The default is None.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Parent Primitive Type
parameters.description: If any parents of the path in Primitive Path do not exist, this node will automatically create them. In this case, it will create parent nodes of this type.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Primitive Specifier
parameters.description: Determines the USD specifier set on the volume primitive and any ancestor primitives created by this LOP.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Generate Errors For Missing Files
parameters.description: If any volume files cannot be found or cannot be loaded, this node will generate an error, causing all downstream nodes to also error. Turn off this option to generate warnings instead. This is only recommended in the early stages of a project where the integrity of the output does not need to be validated.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Files
parameters.description: This node can reference multiple files as fields of a single volume. Set this to the number of fields to read, or click the plus and minus buttons to add or remove field file references.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: File Path
parameters.description: The location of the volume file on disk. USD is not capable of representing volumes currently. It can only point to volumes stored as separate files on disk. These files can be BGEO _or_ VDB when working _within_ Houdini and using a Houdini render delegate. If you want to use the volume data with non-Houdini processes, then you'll need to save the volume data as VDB files.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Fields
parameters.description: A space separated list of field names (as they appear in the file) to read. You can use patterns to match multiple names. Field Customizations: This multi-parm is nested under each file reference instance. It lets you rename fields in the file. Source Name: The name of the field as it appears in the file. Destination Name: The name of the USD field prim to create from the field.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Shutter Open/Close
parameters.description: When Shutter is set to Specify Manually, these two offset values are added to the primary sample time to indicate the shutter open and close times. The open time should be less than or equal to zero, and the close time should be greater than or equal to zero.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Camera Prim
parameters.description: When Shutter is set to Use Camera Prim, this is the scene graph path of a camera prim on the input node's stage. The shutter open and close attribute values are read from this primitive.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Samples
parameters.description: The number of subframe samples to create for each primary sample. These samples are evenly distributed between the shutter open and close times. Note that such an even distribution may or may not create a sample at exactly the primary sample time.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Always Include Frame Sample
parameters.description: When turned on, forces a sample to be created at exactly the primary sample time. If the Samples value, together with the shutter open and close times, already place a sample at the primary sample time, turning on this option has no effect. Otherwise, this option causes an addition sample to be added. This means that the actual number of samples per primary sample may in fact be one more than the number specified in the Samples parameter.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.description: The primitive(s) the node should operate on. You can drag primitives from the scene graph tree pane into this textbox to add their paths, or click the Smallicon:BUTTONS/reselect Reselect button beside the text box to select the primitives in the viewer, or ((Ctrl))-click the Reselect button to choose prims from a pop-up tree window. You can also use primitive patterns for advanced matching, including matching all prims in a collection (using /path/to/prim.collection:<<name>>). You can drag and drop a specific (or multiple specific) USD prim(s) from the Scene Graph Tree into the window to run validation on only these USD primitives. NOTE: This parameter needs to be exposed in order for the transform handles to be context-aware. Without it, the handles may not be positioned properly.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Transform Description
parameters.description: Because all USD edits are non-destructive, editing transforms is accomplished adding a xformOp:transform attribute. Each attribute name has a descriptive suffix. For example, if you set this to foo, it authors an attribute named xformOp:transform:foo. The resulting full attribute name must be unique among attributes on the same prim (Houdini will automatically alter the name by adding a number if it's not unique). The default ($OS) uses the node name as the descriptive suffix.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Apply Transform in World Space
parameters.description: (Default on) Apply the given transform as if it was in world space. When this is off, the transform is local. Technically, transform operations are always local, but this can be confusing (for example, a parent prim may have a rotation around Z, which will make a local move along X axis actually move the primitive along world Y). So this option exists to let you specify the transform more intuitively in world space, and have the node create a local transform that achieves the same effect.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Set Absolute Transform
parameters.description: When Apply Transform in World Space is off and this is on, make this transform _the only active_ xformOp:transform attribute on the prim. This works by setting the xformOpOrder list to only contain the new transform attribute. (So any previously existing transform attributes are still on the prim, but aren't used because they're not listed in xformOpOrder.)
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Use XformCommonAPI
parameters.description: The transform specified in the remaining transform parameters will be expressed using a Houdini-defined extension of the USD XformCommonAPI specification.
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Transform Order
parameters.description: The order in which Houdini applies translates, rotates, and scales, and the order in which it applies rotation.

parameters.label: Translate
parameters.description: Movement amount along XYZ axes.

parameters.label: Rotate

parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Scale

parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Shear

parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes

parameters.label: Uniform Scale

For large filter sizes (1000's), this technique is orders of magnitude faster than the mathematically accurate blurs.

parameters.label: Plane Scope

parameters.label: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Frame Range

parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Frame Dropoff
parameters.description: For Inside/Outside Range, this parameter specifies certain number of frames before and after to slowly ramp up to scoped. parameters.label: Non-scoped Effect

parameters.label: Color

parameters.heading: Color

parameters.label: Component 4
parameters.description: The value of the 4th component, in the case where the plane is a 4 element vector.
parameters.heading: Color

parameters.label: Scalar
parameters.description: The value of Luminance, Depth and Single channel Mask planes.
parameters.heading: Color

parameters.label: Effect Amount
parameters.description: If no mask is present, this multiplies the output by a constant amount (0 = black, 1 = all output). If a mask is present, this amount multiplies the mask.
parameters.heading: Color

parameters.label: Mask Plane
parameters.description: A mask can be a component of a plane or an entire plane. If a vector plane is supplied as a mask, its components are multiplied by the images' components. Scalar Mask ('A', 'C.r'): {{{ C.r = I.r * M C.g = I.g * M C.b = I.b * M }}} Vector Mask ('C'): {{{ C.r = I.r * M.r C.g = I.g * M.g C.b = I.b * M.b }}}
parameters.heading: Color

parameters.label: Invert Mask
parameters.description: Inverts the mask so that all fully 'masked' portions become unmasked. This saves you from inserting an Invert COP after the node with the mask.
parameters.heading: Color

parameters.label: Override Size
parameters.description: If off, the resolution of the image is defined by the resolution in the Composite Project settings. If on, any resolution can be specified.
parameters.heading: Color

parameters.label: Pixel Aspect Ratio
parameters.description: If off, the pixel aspect ratio of the image is defined by the pixel aspect ratio in the Composite Project settings. If on, any pixel aspect ratio can be specified. The pixel aspect ratio determines the shape of the pixel; it represents the width of the pixel compared to the height. A pixel with an aspect ratio of '2' is twice as wide as it is high (2:1). Pixel aspect ratios less than 1 are taller than they are wide. The image viewer attempts to show the image as it would appear by horizontally scaling the image by the pixel aspect ratio. This can result in slight artifacts for non-integer ratios (ie, 0.9:1, 1.442:1). Turn off 'Fast Pixel Aspect' in the Display Options to suppress these artifacts. Many effect filters that have parameters that represent width and height will have the width scaled appropriately (such as Blur, Defocus, Expand).
parameters.heading: Color

parameters.label: Image Planes
parameters.description: Specifies the plane(s) to generate. Color and Alpha will always be present, but the generator does not always have to write to them. The list of planes is all the ones Houdini recognizes as special. Other planes can be added with the 'Custom Planes' parameter. C, A (C:rgb A): Color and Alpha C, A (C:rgb A:rgb): Color and 3-channel Alpha C (rgb): Color only A: Alpha only A (rgb): 3-channel Alpha only M: Mask plane M (rgb): 3-channel Mask plane Z: Z Depth plane L: Luminance plane B (uv): Bump plane P (xyz): Point plane N (xyz): Normal plane V (xyz): Velocity plane None: No planes generated.
parameters.heading: Color

parameters.label: Add Plane
parameters.description: When a generator is connected to an input, it generates a Mask plane by default. This parameter determines which planes are generated in this case. The list of planes to generate are the same as 'Image Planes'. In addition, if the plane already exists in the input sequence, one of the following operations will be performed to combine the new plane. Replace: Input plane replaced by the generated plane. (G) Rename: Generated plane renamed. Add: Input plane added to the generated plane. (I+G) Screen: Input plane photographically added to the generated plane. (I+G-I*G) Subtract: Generated plane subtracted from the input plane. (I-G). Multiply: Input plane multiplied by the generated plane. (IxG) Min: Minimum pixel value of input and generated planes. (min{I,G}) Max: Maximum pixel value of input and generated planes. (max{I,G}) Average: Average pixel value of the input and generated planes. (I+G)/2
parameters.heading: Color

parameters.label: Custom Planes
parameters.description: This string parameter allows you to create your own plane formats. The syntax is
parameters.heading: Color

parameters.label: Raster Depth
parameters.description: The byte format of the image. Higher bit depths provide better color resolution and range at the expense of memory. 8 Bit Integer: Lowest bit depth. Banding can occasionally be seen. Suitable for video. 16 Bit Integer: Intermediate bit depth. No banding can be seen, though clipping can still occur below and above the black and white points. 32 Bit Integer: Generally not used for color, 32bit integer values are used to store object IDs, counts, and other integer values with a large range. 16 Bit Floating Point: High bit depth. No banding can be seen, and no clipping occurs at white and black. Uses less memory than 32 bit float, however processing time for this format is slightly higher as it is not a native CPU data format. This format supports values in the range -65504 to +65504. 32 Bit Floating Point: High bit depth. No banding can be seen, and no clipping occurs at white and black. Uses 4x as much memory as 8bit, which is this format's main drawback. Default Depth: Use the raster depth specified in the Composite Project options.
parameters.heading: Color

parameters.label: Black/White Points
parameters.description: The integer formats (8, 16 and 32 bit) can specify the raw values that the black and white points occur at. The white point must always be higher than the black point. The minimum and maximum values for the black and white points for each format are td>> td>> td>>
parameters.heading: Color

parameters.label: Interlacing
parameters.description: Controls the ability to generate images that are compatible with interlaced images. If you are manipulating the generated output with a filter that uses neighboring pixels (like Blur or Expand), it is recommended that you do not use Black Interlaced, as the filter will use the black scanlines as well. The second menu determines which scanlines are in which fields (odd,even) None: No interlacing. Half Res Interlaced: The image is half the height of a normal frame, with the scanlines on every line. Black Interlaced: The image is the same height as a normal frame, with the inactive scanlines filled with black. Line Doubled: The image is the same height as a normal frame, with the inactive scanlines filled with their active neighbor. Odd Dominant: Odd-numbered scanline fields come before even-numbered scanline fields. Even Dominant: Even-numbered scanline fields come before odd-numbered scanline fields. Odd Frames Only: Only odd-numbered scanline fields are produced. Even Frames Only: Only even-numbered scanline fields are produced.
parameters.heading: Color

parameters.label: Override Global Range
parameters.description: If off, the global animation range is used as the frame range. If on, the frame range of the sequence can be specified in the following parameters.

parameters.label: Still Image
parameters.description: A still image is time-invariant. It exists at every frame. If off, the Start Frame and Length are used to determine the frame range.

Hold N Frames: Hold the first frame for a certain number of frames; before that, show black frames.

parameters.description: Color value in the middle of the wheel.

parameters.description: Color value at the edge of the wheel.
parameters.heading: Color Wheel

parameters.label: Effect Amount
parameters.description: If no mask is present, this multiplies the output by a constant amount (0 = black, 1 = all output). If a mask is present, this amount multiplies the mask.
parameters.heading: Color Wheel

parameters.label: Mask Plane
parameters.description: A mask can be a component of a plane or an entire plane. If a vector plane is supplied as a mask, its components are multiplied by the images' components. Scalar Mask ('A', 'C.r'): {{{ C.r = I.r * M C.g = I.g * M C.b = I.b * M }}} Vector Mask ('C'): {{{ C.r = I.r * M.r C.g = I.g * M.g C.b = I.b * M.b }}}

parameters.label: Invert Mask
parameters.description: Inverts the mask so that all fully 'masked' portions become unmasked. This saves you from inserting an Invert COP after the node with the mask.

parameters.label: Override Size
parameters.description: If off, the resolution of the image is defined by the resolution in the Composite Project settings. If on, any resolution can be specified.
parameters.heading: Color Wheel

parameters.label: Pixel Aspect Ratio
parameters.description: If off, the pixel aspect ratio of the image is defined by the pixel aspect ratio in the Composite Project settings. If on, any pixel aspect ratio can be specified. The pixel aspect ratio determines the shape of the pixel; it represents the width of the pixel compared to the height. A pixel with an aspect ratio of '2' is twice as wide as it is high (2:1). Pixel aspect ratios less than 1 are taller than they are wide. The image viewer attempts to show the image as it would appear by horizontally scaling the image by the pixel aspect ratio. This can result in slight artifacts for non-integer ratios (ie, 0.9:1, 1.442:1). Turn off 'Fast Pixel Aspect' in the Display Options to suppress these artifacts. Many effect filters that have parameters that represent width and height will have the width scaled appropriately (such as Blur, Defocus, Expand).
parameters.heading: Color Wheel

parameters.label: Image Planes
parameters.description: Specifies the plane(s) to generate. Color and Alpha will always be present, but the generator does not always have to write to them. The list of planes is all the ones Houdini recognizes as special. Other planes can be added with the 'Custom Planes' parameter. C, A (C:rgb A): Color and Alpha C, A (C:rgb A:rgb): Color and 3-channel Alpha C (rgb): Color only A: Alpha only A (rgb): 3-channel Alpha only M: Mask plane M (rgb): 3-channel Mask plane Z: Z Depth plane L: Luminance plane B (uv): Bump plane P (xyz): Point plane N (xyz): Normal plane V (xyz): Velocity plane None: No planes generated.
parameters.heading: Color Wheel

parameters.label: Add Plane
parameters.description: When a generator is connected to an input, it generates a Mask plane by default. This parameter determines which planes are generated in this case. The list of planes to generate are the same as 'Image Planes'. In addition, if the plane already exists in the input sequence, one of the following operations will be performed to combine the new plane. Replace: Input plane replaced by the generated plane. (G) Rename: Generated plane renamed. Add: Input plane added to the generated plane. (I+G) Screen: Input plane photographically added to the generated plane. (I+G-I*G) Subtract: Generated plane subtracted from the input plane. (I-G). Multiply: Input plane multiplied by the generated plane. (IxG) Min: Minimum pixel value of input and generated planes. (min{I,G}) Max: Maximum pixel value of input and generated planes. (max{I,G}) Average: Average pixel value of the input and generated planes. (I+G)/2
parameters.heading: Color Wheel

parameters.label: Custom Planes
parameters.description: This string parameter allows you to create your own plane formats. The syntax is
parameters.heading: Color Wheel

parameters.label: Raster Depth
parameters.description: The byte format of the image. Higher bit depths provide better color resolution and range at the expense of memory. 8 Bit Integer: Lowest bit depth. Banding can occasionally be seen. Suitable for video. 16 Bit Integer: Intermediate bit depth. No banding can be seen, though clipping can still occur below and above the black and white points. 32 Bit Integer: Generally not used for color, 32bit integer values are used to store object IDs, counts, and other integer values with a large range. 16 Bit Floating Point: High bit depth. No banding can be seen, and no clipping occurs at white and black. Uses less memory than 32 bit float, however processing time for this format is slightly higher as it is not a native CPU data format. This format supports values in the range -65504 to +65504. 32 Bit Floating Point: High bit depth. No banding can be seen, and no clipping occurs at white and black. Uses 4x as much memory as 8bit, which is this format's main drawback. Default Depth: Use the raster depth specified in the Composite Project options.
parameters.heading: Color Wheel

parameters.label: Black/White Points
parameters.description: The integer formats (8, 16 and 32 bit) can specify the raw values that the black and white points occur at. The white point must always be higher than the black point. The minimum and maximum values for the black and white points for each format are td>> td>> td>>
parameters.heading: Color Wheel

parameters.label: Interlacing
parameters.description: Controls the ability to generate images that are compatible with interlaced images. If you are manipulating the generated output with a filter that uses neighboring pixels (like Blur or Expand), it is recommended that you do not use Black Interlaced, as the filter will use the black scanlines as well. The second menu determines which scanlines are in which fields (odd,even) None: No interlacing. Half Res Interlaced: The image is half the height of a normal frame, with the scanlines on every line. Black Interlaced: The image is the same height as a normal frame, with the inactive scanlines filled with black. Line Doubled: The image is the same height as a normal frame, with the inactive scanlines filled with their active neighbor. Odd Dominant: Odd-numbered scanline fields come before even-numbered scanline fields. Even Dominant: Even-numbered scanline fields come before odd-numbered scanline fields. Odd Frames Only: Only odd-numbered scanline fields are produced. Even Frames Only: Only even-numbered scanline fields are produced.
parameters.heading: Color Wheel

entries.summary: Does a composite (over, under, inside, add, etc) between two images.

parameters.label: Operation
parameters.description: Specifies the compositing operation Over: Places the foreground over the background. Under: Places the foreground under the background's alpha. Atop: Places the foreground over the background only where the background alpha exists. Inside: Places the foreground inside the background's alpha. Outside: Places the foreground outside the background's alpha. Screen: Acts as a saturating add, much like photographic addition. Add: Adds the foreground to the background. Subtract: Subtracts the foreground from the background. Diff: Takes the absolute difference between the foreground and the background. Multiply: Multiplies the background by the foreground. Minimum: Takes the minimum of the foreground and background. Maximum: Takes the maximum of the foreground and background. Average: Takes the average of the foreground and background. Xor: Takes the exclusive or of the two alpha planes, so that alpha areas that overlap are removed.

entries.summary: Increases or decreases the contrast of an image.

parameters.label: Range / Scale
parameters.description: Two different methods to apply contrast. The two methods attempt to be consistent with one another, however, the Range method can represent a wider variety of color transformations once the range moves outside 0 to 1. In this case, switching back to Scale may change the results. Each method provides a global setting and a component setting. The global contrast is applied first, and then the component contrast. parameters.label: Point Distance
parameters.description: Determines how the distance from a point is calculated. Radial: Straight line distance; produces a radial interpolation. Block: Horizontal + Vertical distance; produces more linear interpolation
parameters.heading: CornerRamp

parameters.label: Correct for Aspect Ratio
parameters.description: When on, the aspect ratio of the image is compensated for, so that Radial Distance computations produce circular falloffs, regardless of the shape of the image.

parameters.label: Point num
parameters.description: The (u,v) location of this ramp point.

parameters.label: Color
parameters.description: The color of this ramp point.
parameters.heading: Ramp Points

parameters.label: Weight
parameters.description: The weight of a point determines how much it contributes to the ramp. The point weight is relative to all other points' weights (so if all the weights are 2, the ramp would appear the same as if they were all 1). Increasing a point's weight makes a larger area of effect in the ramp. Setting the weight to zero removes the point from the ramp altogether.
parameters.heading: Ramp Points

parameters.label: Effect Amount
parameters.description: If no mask is present, this multiplies the output by a constant amount (0 = black, 1 = all output). If a mask is present, this amount multiplies the mask.
parameters.heading: Ramp Points

parameters.label: Mask Plane
parameters.description: A mask can be a component of a plane or an entire plane. If a vector plane is supplied as a mask, its components are multiplied by the images' components. Scalar Mask ('A', 'C.r'): {{{ C.r = I.r * M C.g = I.g * M C.b = I.b * M }}} Vector Mask ('C'): {{{ C.r = I.r * M.r C.g = I.g * M.g C.b = I.b * M.b }}}

parameters.label: Invert Mask
parameters.description: Inverts the mask so that all fully 'masked' portions become unmasked. This saves you from inserting an Invert COP after the node with the mask.

parameters.description: If off, the resolution of the image is defined by the resolution in the Composite Project settings. If on, any resolution can be specified.
parameters.heading: Ramp Points

parameters.label: Pixel Aspect Ratio
parameters.description: If off, the pixel aspect ratio of the image is defined by the pixel aspect ratio in the Composite Project settings. If on, any pixel aspect ratio can be specified. The pixel aspect ratio determines the shape of the pixel; it represents the width of the pixel compared to the height. A pixel with an aspect ratio of '2' is twice as wide as it is high (2:1). Pixel aspect ratios less than 1 are taller than they are wide. The image viewer attempts to show the image as it would appear by horizontally scaling the image by the pixel aspect ratio. This can result in slight artifacts for non-integer ratios (ie, 0.9:1, 1.442:1). Turn off 'Fast Pixel Aspect' in the Display Options to suppress these artifacts. Many effect filters that have parameters that represent width and height will have the width scaled appropriately (such as Blur, Defocus, Expand).

C, A (C:rgb A): Color and Alpha C, A (C:rgb A:rgb): Color and 3-channel Alpha C (rgb): Color only A: Alpha only A (rgb): 3-channel Alpha only M: Mask plane M (rgb): 3-channel Mask plane Z: Z Depth plane L: Luminance plane B (uv): Bump plane P (xyz): Point plane N (xyz): Normal plane V (xyz): Velocity plane None: No planes generated.
parameters.heading: Ramp Points

parameters.label: Add Plane
parameters.description: When a generator is connected to an input, it generates a Mask plane by default. This parameter determines which planes are generated in this case. The list of planes to generate are the same as 'Image Planes'. In addition, if the plane already exists in the input sequence, one of the following operations will be performed to combine the new plane. Replace: Input plane replaced by the generated plane. (G) Rename: Generated plane renamed. Add: Input plane added to the generated plane. (I+G) Screen: Input plane photographically added to the generated plane. (I+G-I*G) Subtract: Generated plane subtracted from the input plane. (I-G). Multiply: Input plane multiplied by the generated plane. (IxG) Min: Minimum pixel value of input and generated planes. (min{I,G}) Max: Maximum pixel value of input and generated planes. (max{I,G}) Average: Average pixel value of the input and generated planes. (I+G)/2
parameters.heading: Ramp Points

parameters.label: Custom Planes
parameters.description: This string parameter allows you to create your own plane formats. The syntax is
parameters.heading: Ramp Points

parameters.label: Raster Depth
parameters.description: The byte format of the image. Higher bit depths provide better color resolution and range at the expense of memory. 8 Bit Integer: Lowest bit depth. Banding can occasionally be seen. Suitable for video. 16 Bit Integer: Intermediate bit depth. No banding can be seen, though clipping can still occur below and above the black and white points. 32 Bit Integer: Generally not used for color, 32bit integer values are used to store object IDs, counts, and other integer values with a large range. 16 Bit Floating Point: High bit depth. No banding can be seen, and no clipping occurs at white and black. Uses less memory than 32 bit float, however processing time for this format is slightly higher as it is not a native CPU data format. This format supports values in the range -65504 to +65504. 32 Bit Floating Point: High bit depth. No banding can be seen, and no clipping occurs at white and black. Uses 4x as much memory as 8bit, which is this format's main drawback. Default Depth: Use the raster depth specified in the Composite Project options.
parameters.heading: Ramp Points

parameters.label: Black/White Points
parameters.description: The integer formats (8, 16 and 32 bit) can specify the raw values that the black and white points occur at. The white point must always be higher than the black point. The minimum and maximum values for the black and white points for each format are td>> td>> td>>
parameters.heading: Ramp Points

parameters.label: Interlacing
parameters.description: Controls the ability to generate images that are compatible with interlaced images. If you are manipulating the generated output with a filter that uses neighboring pixels (like Blur or Expand), it is recommended that you do not use Black Interlaced, as the filter will use the black scanlines as well. The second menu determines which scanlines are in which fields (odd,even) None: No interlacing. Half Res Interlaced: The image is half the height of a normal frame, with the scanlines on every line. Black Interlaced: The image is the same height as a normal frame, with the inactive scanlines filled with black. Line Doubled: The image is the same height as a normal frame, with the inactive scanlines filled with their active neighbor. Odd Dominant: Odd-numbered scanline fields come before even-numbered scanline fields. Even Dominant: Even-numbered scanline fields come before odd-numbered scanline fields. Odd Frames Only: Only odd-numbered scanline fields are produced. Even Frames Only: Only even-numbered scanline fields are produced.
parameters.heading: Ramp Points

parameters.label: Override Global Range
parameters.description: If off, the global animation range is used as the frame range. If on, the frame range of the sequence can be specified in the following parameters.
parameters.heading: Ramp Points

parameters.label: Still Image
parameters.description: A still image is time-invariant. It exists at every frame. If off, the Start Frame and Length are used to determine the frame range.

parameters.description: The starting frame of the sequence.

parameters.label: Pre Extend
parameters.description: For sequences with a frame range, this determines how to show frames before the start frame. Black Frames: Display black. Cycle: Cycle the sequence, always playing it forward. Mirror: Cycle the sequence, reversing the direction every cycle. Hold: Hold the first frame indefinitely. Hold N Frames: Hold the first frame for a certain number of frames; before that, show black frames.
parameters.heading: Ramp Points

parameters.label: Pre Hold
parameters.description: The number of frames to hold the first frame for, if 'Hold N Frames' is selected.
parameters.heading: Ramp Points

parameters.label: Post Extend
