entries.summary: Defocuses an image similar to a real camera defocus.

parameters.label: Defocus
parameters.description: The amount of defocusing to apply (in pixels). This is the diameter of the defocus circle (or poly).

parameters.label: Defocus Y
parameters.description: If you would like to specify a different defocus size for the vertical direction, toggle on this parameter (useful for getting a motion blur defocus effect).

parameters.label: Defocus Shape
parameters.description: The shape of the lens's circle of confusion.

parameters.label: Polygon Edges
parameters.description: If the defocus shape is a polygon, this is the number of edges that the regular polygon has.

parameters.label: Lens Rotation
parameters.description: If the defocus shape is a polygon, you can rotate the polygon shape to any orientation.

parameters.label: Per Pixel Defocus
parameters.description: This option is enabled when a mask is used (Mask tab). It allows you to vary the amount of defocus applied based on the mask brightness. There is also a tolerance value which quantizes the defocus sizes. This can speed up the per-pixel defocus, especially when the mask is at a high bit depth (like floating point). It is expressed in defocus size; so a tolerance of 0.01 would have 500 distinct defocus levels between 0 and a defocus size of 5 (0, 0.01, 0.02, ... 4.99, 5). Higher tolerances produce faster composites, at the expense of image quality. Artifacts generally become noticeable around 0.1.

parameters.label: Add Edge Ring
parameters.description: Adds a brighter ring area around the defocused area, to mimic a real lens.

parameters.label: Ring Size
parameters.description: The portion of the defocused area that will be visible as a bright ring (its proportional thickness). 0 is none, 1 is the entire area. Normally the ring is only a small portion of the defocused area (around 5%, or 0.05).

parameters.label: Ring Intensity
parameters.description: The extra brightness of the ring (0 is none).

parameters.label: Ring Offset
parameters.description: The ring can be biased more to one side of the bloom; a negative value shifts the bloom ring left or down, while a positive value shift the bloom ring right or up.

parameters.label: Boost Intensity of Bright Spots
parameters.description: If on, values about a certain threshold are brightened to produce visible circles.

parameters.label: Boost Threshold
parameters.description: All luminances above this value will be boosted.

parameters.label: Boost Factor
parameters.description: Multiplies the luminance above the threshold to produce the boost. Produces a more gradual boost.

parameters.label: Boost Level
parameters.description: Boosts the luminance above the threshold amount by this value (by adding it to the luminance). Produces more abrupt changes in color, making the defocus shape stand out more from the image.

entries.label: Denoise TVD
entries.summary: Removes white noise from an image.

parameters.label: Iterations
parameters.description: Governs the number of rounds of denoising that will be performed on the image. Running time is proportional to the number of rounds. Additional iterations will increase the removal of noise at the expense of losing more fine detail.
parameters.heading: Denoise

parameters.label: Diffuse
parameters.description: A scale factor for the amount of diffusion to apply in each round of iteration. The total amount of diffusion will thus be this times the Iterations. However, if this is made too large, the process can become unstable and not converge to a good result.
parameters.heading: Denoise

parameters.label: Full Sequence
parameters.description: Instead of operating on a single frame, perform the denoise calculation across the entire sequence. This requires the entire sequence be loaded into memory and processed at once, so may be infeasible for large images or long sequences. This will result in greater frame-to-frame coherency of the resulting denoising. An internal cache is generated for each image plane (such as C or A) denoised. To save out the result in a file ROP it is recommended to only save one plane at a time so the cache can be used.
parameters.heading: Denoise

parameters.label: Pixel Size
parameters.description: Acts as the conversion factor from pixel space into the three dimensional coordinates in which the denoising will occur. The relative magnitude of the pixel size is important, not the absolute values. This is primarily used for the Full Sequence mode to determine how far in Z one frame should be. Making the Z steps smaller or larger will affect the relative importance of temporal coherence versus spatial coherence.
parameters.heading: Denoise

entries.label: Depth Darken
entries.summary: Darkens depth boundaries in an image.

parameters.label: Depth Scale
parameters.description: Differences in depth have to be converted into differences in intensity. As the size of scenes can vary, the correct ratio will vary depending on the size of the scene. The Depth Scale allows one to compensate for the ratio of the scene.

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: The diameter of the depth darkening effect. Pixels up to this radius from the depth boundary can be affected.

parameters.label: Maximum Darken
parameters.description: The final darkening effect is clamped against the maximum darken value. A solid black halo can be too aggressive, so smaller values are useful to modulate the extent of the effect.

parameters.label: Use Logarithmic
parameters.description: Unlike traditional color values which have a fixed range, z-depth values can vary considerably over the image. Working with linear z-values may cause far away depth discontinuities to be exaggerated because their absolute difference is large, despite their relative difference being the same. By working in logarithmic space, a depth boundary that doubles the distance to the camera will have a fixed level of effect.

entries.label: Diff
entries.summary: Computes the difference between the foreground image and the background image.

parameters.label: Image Units
parameters.description: Selects pixels or UV units for the transform.
parameters.heading: Composite

parameters.label: Translate, Rotate, Scale, Pivot
parameters.description: Transforms the foreground in X,Y relative to the background.
parameters.heading: Composite

parameters.label: Image Filter
parameters.description: Specifies the filter to use when transforming.
parameters.heading: Composite

parameters.label: Image Wrap
parameters.description: Specifies the foreground image's wrapping style.
parameters.heading: Composite

parameters.label: Motion Blur
parameters.description: Toggles on motion blur, and specifies the time range around the current frame to blur.
parameters.heading: Composite

parameters.label: Motion Frame Bias
parameters.description: Shifts the time range for the blur.
parameters.heading: Composite

parameters.label: Motion Blur Segments
parameters.description: Number of samples to blur together in the specified time range.
parameters.heading: Composite

parameters.label: Motion Blur Method
parameters.description: Velocity: Only uses the current frame and the transform to compute past and future positions. Deformation: Cooks the images at all time samples.
parameters.heading: Composite

parameters.description: Amount to blur the shadow. Defaults to pixels.

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.description: The amount to offset the shadow to give the effect of directional lighting.

parameters.label: Units
parameters.description: The distance based parameters may either be specified in pixels or in uv coordinates. This switches between the two specifications.

entries.label: Equalize
entries.summary: Equalizes colors by stretching or shifting the image histogram.

parameters.label: Operation
parameters.description: The equalization operation to perform Stretch Range to Black/White: The minimum and maximum values found in the image are mapped to black and white, which may result in a contrast adjustment and a luminance shift. Move Minimum Value to Black: The values are transformed so that the minimum value maps to black. Move Maximum Value to White: The values are transformed so that the maximum value maps to white. Shift Average Luminance: The global luminance is computed and all values are transformed so that the global luminance matches the specified value. Equalize Luminance Across Frames: The global luminance is computed for several frames around the current frame. The current frame's global luminance is transformed to match the average global luminance, effectively removing frame flicker.
parameters.heading: Equalize

parameters.label: Fit Method
parameters.description: The transformation, either a bright scale or shift.
parameters.heading: Equalize

parameters.label: Luminance
parameters.description: The method for computing luminance.
parameters.heading: Equalize

parameters.label: Black
parameters.description: What value 'black' is defined to be, normally zero. (black & white are independent of black/white points)
parameters.heading: Equalize

parameters.label: White
parameters.description: What value 'white' is defined to be, normally one.
parameters.heading: Equalize

parameters.label: Average Luminance
parameters.description: The luminance to move the average luminance to.
parameters.heading: Equalize

parameters.label: Frames Before
parameters.description: Number of frames before the current frame to analyze (for Equalize Luminance only).
parameters.heading: Equalize

parameters.label: Frames After
parameters.description: Number of frames after the current frame to analyze.
parameters.heading: Equalize

parameters.label: Effect
parameters.description: The amount of effect equalize has on the image (0 is none, 1 is full effect).
parameters.heading: Equalize

parameters.description: Selects whether to extract a full plane or a channel of a plane.
parameters.heading: Mask

parameters.label: Plane
parameters.description: Selects which plane to extract when Extract is Plane.
parameters.heading: Mask

parameters.label: Channel
parameters.description: Selects a channel to extract from a plane when Extract is Single Channel.
parameters.heading: Mask

parameters.label: Rename Plane
parameters.description: Name of the new plane. When Extract is Plane, this can be left blank and no rename will be done (the original plane name is preserved). It is required in Single Channel mode.
parameters.heading: Mask

entries.label: Extrapolate Boundaries
entries.summary: Fills "empty" areas of an image using the colors at the edges the non-empty areas.

parameters.label: Blend Method
parameters.description: How to expand the edges of the masked areas. Image:/images/nodes/cop2/extrapolateboundaries_before.jpg Fill Average: Fill the boundaries with the average color of the image. Image:/images/nodes/cop2/extrapolateboundaries_average.jpg Flood Fill: Fill the boundaries with black. Only perform border expansion. Image:/images/nodes/cop2/extrapolateboundaries_flood.jpg Diffuse Fill: Smooth out the transition between the boundaries. Image:/images/nodes/cop2/extrapolateboundaries_diffuse.jpg
parameters.heading: Extrapolate Boundaries

parameters.label: Edge Padding
parameters.description: The number of pixels to pad the boundaries with.
parameters.heading: Extrapolate Boundaries

parameters.label: Use Alpha as Mask
parameters.description: Use the input image's alpha channel as the boundary mask if the second input has not been provided.
parameters.heading: Extrapolate Boundaries

parameters.label: Unpremultiply
parameters.description: Unpremultiply the input image with the provided mask or alpha channel before processing.
parameters.heading: Extrapolate Boundaries

parameters.label: Mask Threshold
parameters.description: When using non-binary masks, this value sets the minimum pixel intensity that will be considered as part of the boundary.
parameters.heading: Extrapolate Boundaries

parameters.label: Invert Mask
parameters.description: Invert the mask.
parameters.heading: Extrapolate Boundaries

parameters.label: Visualize Fill Region
parameters.description: Overlay the input image with the fill region.
parameters.heading: Extrapolate Boundaries

parameters.label: Color
parameters.description: The color of the overlaid fill region.
parameters.heading: Extrapolate Boundaries

parameters.label: Opacity
parameters.description: The opacity of the overlaid fill region.
parameters.heading: Extrapolate Boundaries

parameters.label: Effect Amount
parameters.description: If no mask is present, this blends the output with the input by a constant amount (0 = all input, 1 = all output). If a mask is present, this amount multiplies the mask.
parameters.heading: Mask

parameters.label: Operation Mask
parameters.description: Selects the mask plane to use as a mask from the mask input. The mask can be selected from First Input: Useful for masking the operation to the image's own alpha plane. Mask Input: Selects the mask from the side mask input. Off: Turns off masking, without requiring disconnection of the mask input (useful for temporarily disabling the mask).
parameters.heading: Mask

parameters.label: Resize Mask to Fit Image
parameters.description: If the mask image is a different resolution than the output image, turning on this parameter will scale the mask to the output image's resolution. If this node is changing constantly, and the mask is not, it is somewhat faster to put a Scale COP down to do the resize for the mask image. Otherwise, the scale will occur every time this node cooks.
parameters.heading: Mask

parameters.label: Invert Mask
parameters.description: Inverts the mask so that all fully 'masked' portions become unmasked. This saves you from inserting an Invert COP after the node with the mask.
parameters.heading: Mask

parameters.label: Plane Scope
parameters.description: Specifies the scope for both the RGB components of Color, Alpha, and other planes. The (C)RGBA mask only affects Color components and Alpha. 'C' will toggle all the RGB components. For planes other than Color and Alpha, the plane name (plus component, if applicable) should be specified in the string field. The pulldown menu can be used to select planes or components present in this node. A plane is specified by its name. A component is specified by both its plane and component name. The '*' wildcard may be used to scope all extra planes. Any number of planes or components can be specified, separated by spaces. Examples
parameters.heading: Scope

parameters.label: Frame Scope
parameters.description: Allows scoping of specific frames in the frame range. This is in addition to the plane scope (so a plane at a certain frame must be both plane scoped and frame scoped to be modified). All Frames: All frames are scoped. Inside Range: All frames inside a subrange are scoped. Outside Range: All frames outside a subrange are scoped. Even Frames: Even numbered frames are scoped. Odd Frames: Odd numbered frames are scoped. Specific Frames: A user-defined list of frames are scoped.
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Frame Range
parameters.description: For Inside/Outside range, this parameter specifies the subrange of the sequence to scope (or unscope). This can be edited in Timeline viewer mode (((Ctrl + 2)) in viewer).
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Frame Dropoff
parameters.description: For Inside/Outside Range, this parameter specifies certain number of frames before and after to slowly ramp up to scoped. The operation will be blended with its input to 'ease in' or 'ease out' the scoping effect over a number of frames. This can be edited in Timeline viewer mode (((Ctrl + 2)) in viewer).
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Non-scoped Effect
parameters.description: For unscoped frames, this sets the blend factor between the input and modified images. Normally this is zero (use the input image). By setting this to a non-zero value, you can make unscoped frames be 'slightly' unscoped. The value can vary between 0 (unscoped) and 1 (scoped).
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Frame List
parameters.description: The frame list for 'Specific Frames'. Frame numbers should be separated by spaces.
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Automatically Adjust for Length Changes
parameters.description: If the sequence range changes, enabling this parameter will adjust the subrange and frame dropoff lengths to fit the new range.
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

entries.label: Fetch
entries.summary: Fetches a sequence of images from another COP, even in another network.

parameters.label: COP
parameters.description: The path to the COP to fetch.

entries.label: Field Merge
entries.summary: Merges two fields into one Interlaced Frame.

parameters.label: Detect Field Type from Input
parameters.description: If on, the type of the sequence will be read from the sequence information of the input. Field Split and the generator Interlace parameters set this information. It is not automatically detected from loaded files.

parameters.label: Others
parameters.description: The next two parameters are for manually specifying the field type.

parameters.label: Field Dominance
parameters.description: The field dominance of the input sequence. Odd Dominant (Field 1): The odd scanlines (1,3,5...) appear in the first field of the video pair. Even Dominant (Field 2): The even scanlines (2,4,6...) appear in the first field of the video pair.

entries.label: Field Split
entries.summary: Splits an interlaced frame into two fields per frame (odd and even fields).

parameters.label: Split
parameters.description: The split operation. Frame to 2 Fields: Splits each frame into 2 fields. The sequence will be twice as long. Odd Fields: Extracts the odd scanlines from each frame. The sequence length remains unaffected. Even Fields: Extracts the even scanlines from each frame. The sequence length remains unaffected.

parameters.label: Field Dominance
parameters.description: The field dominance of the new sequence. Odd Dominant (Field 1): The odd scanlines (1,3,5...) appear in the first field of the video pair. Even Dominant (Field 2): The even scanlines (2,4,6...) appear in the first field of the video pair.

entries.label: File
entries.summary: Loads image files into Houdini.

parameters.label: Detect Subframes
parameters.description: The character "." is treated as a decimal, and sequences of images with fractional frame numbers are loaded. Each fractional frame is placed at the next available integer frame in the sequence (1,2,3...), rather than at subframes (1, 1.25, 1.5...). File Size: Specifies the size of the file to load, either by at the natural resolution or a custom size. Image Filter: When the file size is overridden, this specifies the image filter to use when scaling. Pixel Aspect Ratio: Specifies the pixel aspect ratio of the image. Flip Image: Flips the image vertically if on. File Raster Depth: Selects how the raster depth is determined. Natural Depth: The image file's depth is used. Project Depth: The depth specified in the Composite Project settings is used, overriding the file's natural depth. Specific Depth: The following Depth parameter selects the raster depth, overriding the file's natural depth.
parameters.heading: File

parameters.label: Linearize Non-linear Images
parameters.description: When enabled, planes with non-linear colorspaces will be converted to linear colorspace. If the colorspace is unknown, only 8b images will be assumed to be sRGB. 8b non-linear planes will always be upconverted to at least 16b float, unless the File Raster Depth explicity sets a different format.
parameters.heading: File

parameters.label: Image Color Space
parameters.description: When Linearize is enabled, the image color space is determined by looking at the image file itself. In some cases, the file may contain an image in a colorspace that is different that the one the format specifies (ie, an sRGB image in an OpenEXR file, which the format dictates should be linear). This parameter allows you to explicitly state the color space of the loaded image, which may affect if the image is linearized (sRGB) or not (Linear). This parameter is not used if Linearize Non-linear Images is off. Autodetect from File: Use the image format or image file to determine the colorspace. Linear: Assume the image is in linear space, ignoring the file or format's colorspace. The image will not be linearized. sRGB: Assume the image is in sRGB space, ignoring the file or format's colorspace. The image will be run through a inverse sRGB transform. Use OpenColorIO: Use OpenColorIO to specify the image color space. OCIO Color Space: When the Image Color Space is set to use OpenColorIO, this parameter specifies how the OCIO color space is determined. The first option is to parse the color space from the filename. This uses the OCIO file parsing semantics to determine the color space. In OCIO 2.0, this uses the file_rules defined in the config file. Other choices are the list of color spaces defined by OCIO. Depth: If the File Raster Depth parameter is set to Specific, this parameter sets the raster depth used for the files. Override Frame Range: If off, the frame range is automatically determined by the lowest and highest frame numbers found in the file pattern. Otherwise the File Range Start, File Range Length, and Shift to Start at Frame parameters set the range. Detect Frame Range: If Override Frame Range is on, you can do a one-time frame range detect of the sequence by pressing this button. It will put the range values into the following parameters. Still Image: When checked, only the first image in the file range will be read and a still image will be created instead of a sequence. Shift to Start at Frame: Specifies the frame where the sequence should start. If this number is different from the file range start, the sequence will be shifted appropriately. File Range Start: Specifies the number of the first file where the sequence should start. For example, if the file name is file$F.tiff and the file range start is 15, the first file in the sequence will be file15.tiff. By default, this number is determined from the first file found matching the file name pattern, but it can be changed to create a sequence of a subset of the files. File Range Length: Specifies the length of the sequence. By default, this number is the number of files matching the pattern. It can be changed to create a sequence of a subset of the files. Missing Frames: If a frame is missing in the sequence, this parameter specifies how to handle it. Missing Frames: For bad or missing frames, the File COP can either use a black frame or a neighboring frame. Use Closest Frame: Searches forward and backward in the frames to find a substitution. The closest frame is used; in the event of a tie, the previous frame is taken. Use Previous Frame: Searches backward from the missing frame to find a replacement. Use Next Frame: Searches forward from the missing frame to find a replacement. Use Black Frame: Bad and missing frames are replaced with a black frame. Report Error: The File node errors when a bad or missing frame is found. Print Warning for Missing Frames: If on, a message is printed to the shell when a missing or bad frame is encountered (ie, /img/img1/file1: Missing frame 1).
parameters.heading: File

parameters.label: Enable Proxy Files
parameters.description: Enables the use of proxies, which are smaller versions of the full sized images. A proxy sequence should be identical to the original sequence, except for the resolution. When cooking the file COP at other resolutions than the proxy resolutions, the closest larger proxy sequence is used.
parameters.heading: Proxy

parameters.label: 1/2, 1/4, 1/8 Res Proxy
parameters.description: Specifies the proxy sequence to use for 1/2, 1/4 and 1/8 of the full resolution.
parameters.heading: Proxy

parameters.label: Custom Proxy
parameters.description: Allows you to specify other proxy resolutions and their proxy sequences.
parameters.heading: Proxy

parameters.label: Effect Amount
parameters.description: If no mask is present, this blends the output with the input by a constant amount (0 = all input, 1 = all output). If a mask is present, this amount multiplies the mask.
parameters.heading: Mask

parameters.label: Operation Mask
parameters.description: Selects the mask plane to use as a mask from the mask input. A mask can be a component of a plane or an entire plane. If a vector plane is supplied as a mask, its components are multiplied by the images' components. *Scalar Mask ('A', 'C.r')* {{{ C.r = I.r * M C.g = I.g * M C.b = I.b * M }}} *Vector Mask ('C')* {{{ C.r = I.r * M.r C.g = I.g * M.g C.b = I.b * M.b }}}
parameters.heading: Mask

If this node is changing constantly, and the mask is not, it is somewhat faster to put a Scale COP down to do the resize for the mask image. Otherwise, the scale will occur every time this node cooks.

parameters.label: Invert Mask
parameters.description: Inverts the mask so that all fully 'masked' portions become unmasked. This saves you from inserting an Invert COP after the node with the mask.
parameters.heading: Mask

parameters.label: Pre Extend
parameters.description: For sequences with a frame range, this determines how to show frames before the start frame. Black Frames: Display black. Cycle: Cycle the sequence, always playing it forward. Mirror: Cycle the sequence, reversing the direction every cycle. Hold: Hold the first frame indefinitely. Hold N Frames: Hold the first frame for a certain number of frames; before that, show black frames.
parameters.heading: Sequence

parameters.label: Pre Hold
parameters.description: The number of frames to hold the first frame for, if Hold N Frames is selected.
parameters.heading: Sequence

parameters.label: Post Extend
parameters.description: For sequences with a frame range, this determines how to show frames after the last frame. Black Frames: Display black. Cycle: Cycle the sequence, always playing it forward. Mirror: Cycle the sequence, reversing the direction every cycle. Hold: Hold the last frame indefinitely. Hold N Frames: Hold the last frame for a certain number of frames; after that, show black frames.
parameters.heading: Sequence

parameters.label: Post Hold
parameters.description: The number of frames to hold the last frame for, if Hold N Frames is selected.
parameters.heading: Sequence

entries.label: Fog
entries.summary: Adds a variety of atmospheric effects to an image, including fog, haze and heat waves.

parameters.label: Fog Type
parameters.description: The atmospheric effect to be applied. Normal Fog: As distance increases, the pixel color changes to the fog color. Additive Fog: The fog color is added to the pixel color. Looks more "cloudy". Haze: As distance increases, the pixel's saturation decreases, so distant pixels appear more gray. Heat Waves: Adds a shimmering heat wave effect to distant pixels.
parameters.heading: Fog

parameters.label: Fog Density
parameters.description: The density of the atmospheric effect. For each depth unit, this amount is applied.
parameters.heading: Fog

parameters.label: Fog Color
parameters.description: The color of the fog for fog effects (Normal and Additive fog only).
parameters.heading: Fog

parameters.label: Distance Offset
parameters.description: A constant value added to the per-pixel distance.
parameters.heading: Fog

parameters.label: Fog Direction
parameters.description: The direction the distance is computed in, either X,Y,Z or camera depth.
parameters.heading: Fog

parameters.label: Smooth Edges
parameters.description: Enabling this option attempts to blend the fog on edges with sharp changes in depth. Because only 1 depth value is stored per-pixel, and they aren't normally blended, some edges can have sections look fogged and some that aren't at all, depending on the sampling. This option detects edges and corrects these artifacts.
parameters.heading: Fog

parameters.label: Smooth Edge Threshold
parameters.description: Edges are blended if the edge transition is greater than this threshold, from the current edge pixel to a neighboring pixel. If all the neighboring pixels are within this distance of the current pixel, it is not considered an edge and smoothing is not applied.
parameters.heading: Fog

parameters.label: Smoothness
parameters.description: The number of samples taken from the image. '1' produces a grainy effect, while higher values produce a blurry effect.
parameters.heading: Heat (only applicable for Heat Waves):

parameters.label: Horizontal Scale
parameters.description: How much horizontal deviation the heat waves cause.
parameters.heading: Heat (only applicable for Heat Waves):

parameters.label: Vertical Scale
parameters.description: How much vertical deviation the heat waves cause.
parameters.heading: Heat (only applicable for Heat Waves):

parameters.label: Time Scale
parameters.description: How quickly the heat waves change.
parameters.heading: Heat (only applicable for Heat Waves):

parameters.label: Noise Offset
parameters.description: The 3D noise offset for the heat waves. Animate the 'Y' parameter with $F to see rising heat waves.
parameters.heading: Heat (only applicable for Heat Waves):

parameters.label: Layered
parameters.description: Turns layered fog on, with the fog appearing in the specified area. The most common type of layered fog is 'Y Layered Below' (for ground hugging fog) and 'Y Layered Above' (for clouds).
parameters.heading: Layer

parameters.label: Layer Edge
parameters.description: Where the fog begins to falloff to zero. If Layered is set to 'Y Layered Below', all values with a Y value lower than the layer edge value will be fogged.
parameters.heading: Layer

parameters.label: Layer Falloff
parameters.description: The size of the falloff region, which produces a gradual decrease in the fog once the Layer Edge has been reached.
parameters.heading: Layer

parameters.label: Falloff Function
parameters.description: The shape of the falloff region.
parameters.heading: Layer

parameters.label: Use Fog Noise
parameters.description: If on, the fog is not uniform and has 3D noise variations in it.
parameters.heading: Noise

parameters.label: Noise Amplitude
parameters.description: The amount of noise variation to add to the constant fog.
parameters.heading: Noise

parameters.label: Noise Frequency
parameters.description: How quickly the noise changes in each of the 3 axis. Lower values produce very smooth, gradually changing noise, while high values produce very static noise.
parameters.heading: Noise

parameters.label: Noise Offset
parameters.description: By changing the noise offset, you can animate the fog noise itself, which makes it flow as if wind were blowing it.
parameters.heading: Noise

parameters.label: Turbulence
parameters.description: Adds more harmonics to the noise, given it more 'depth'. It will have more high frequency components in it.
parameters.heading: Noise

parameters.label: Roughness
parameters.description: For each level of turbulence, this multiplies the noise harmonics. It controls the amount of high frequency noise present in the generated noise. So, for a turbulence of 3 a roughness of 0.5, the low frequency noise will be multiplied by 1, then next higher frequency by 0.5, and the highest frequency (level 2) by 0.25.
parameters.heading: Noise

parameters.label: Noise Step
parameters.description: How often the noise is sampled along the way to the final point. If you have points that are extremely distant (>100), consider increasing this parameter, otherwise a tremendous amount of noise sampling will be done and the operation will slow down.
parameters.heading: Noise

entries.label: Font
entries.summary: Renders anti-aliased text.

parameters.label: Font
parameters.description: The font to use for drawing the text. By default the menu lists all known system fonts. You can browse for a specific font file, if it is not listed.
parameters.heading: Font

parameters.label: Use Text File
parameters.description: If on, the text is read from an ASCII file instead of the 'Text' parameter.
parameters.heading: Font

parameters.label: Text
parameters.description: The text to render.
parameters.heading: Font

parameters.label: Text File
parameters.description: The name of the text file(s).
parameters.heading: Font

parameters.label: Text Line
parameters.description: When reading from a text file, this specifies the first line to start rendering.
parameters.heading: Font

parameters.label: Limit Num Lines
parameters.description: If on, this limits the number of lines rendered.
parameters.heading: Font

parameters.label: Text Size
parameters.description: The size of the text.
parameters.heading: Font

parameters.label: Tracking
parameters.description: Increases or decreases the horizontal and vertical spacing between characters and lines.
parameters.heading: Font

parameters.label: Oblique
parameters.description: Amount of slant to apply to the text, in degrees.
parameters.heading: Font

parameters.label: Antialias
parameters.description: The render antialias level from 1x1 (none) to 8x8 (highest).
parameters.heading: Font

parameters.label: Font Detail
parameters.description: The level of detail to use when converting the font to polygons to be rendered.
parameters.heading: Font

parameters.label: Alignment
parameters.description: How to orient the text around the text position.
parameters.heading: Layout

parameters.label: Include Descender in Vertical Alignment
parameters.description: If enabled, then the alignment baseline is set to the descender of the font, rather than the font's baseline. A descender is the portion of a letter that extends below the baseline of the font - for example the stem of a lower case letter p.
parameters.heading: Layout

parameters.label: Automatic Kerning
parameters.description: Automatically apply kerning pairs from the font to adjust spacing between letters for a more visually pleasing results.
parameters.heading: Layout

parameters.label: Units
parameters.description: Specifies the units that the Translate and Pivot parameters are in (0-1 UVs, or 0-XRES pixels).
parameters.heading: Layout

parameters.label: Translate
parameters.description: Translation of the text.
parameters.heading: Layout

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: Scale of the text.
parameters.heading: Layout

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.description: Rotation of the text.
parameters.heading: Layout

parameters.label: Pivot
parameters.description: Pivot location for Scale and Rotate.
parameters.heading: Layout

parameters.label: Color
parameters.description: The color of the text.
parameters.heading: Layout

parameters.label: Effect Amount
parameters.description: If no mask is present, this multiplies the output by a constant amount (0 = black, 1 = all output). If a mask is present, this amount multiplies the mask.
parameters.heading: Layout

parameters.label: Mask Plane
parameters.description: A mask can be a component of a plane or an entire plane. If a vector plane is supplied as a mask, its components are multiplied by the images' components. Scalar Mask ('A', 'C.r'): {{{ C.r = I.r * M C.g = I.g * M C.b = I.b * M }}} Vector Mask ('C'): {{{ C.r = I.r * M.r C.g = I.g * M.g C.b = I.b * M.b }}}
parameters.heading: Layout

parameters.label: Invert Mask
parameters.description: Inverts the mask so that all fully 'masked' portions become unmasked. This saves you from inserting an Invert COP after the node with the mask.
parameters.heading: Layout

parameters.label: Override Size
parameters.description: If off, the resolution of the image is defined by the resolution in the Composite Project settings. If on, any resolution can be specified.
parameters.heading: Layout

parameters.label: Pixel Aspect Ratio
parameters.description: If off, the pixel aspect ratio of the image is defined by the pixel aspect ratio in the Composite Project settings. If on, any pixel aspect ratio can be specified. The pixel aspect ratio determines the shape of the pixel; it represents the width of the pixel compared to the height. A pixel with an aspect ratio of '2' is twice as wide as it is high (2:1). Pixel aspect ratios less than 1 are taller than they are wide. The image viewer attempts to show the image as it would appear by horizontally scaling the image by the pixel aspect ratio. This can result in slight artifacts for non-integer ratios (ie, 0.9:1, 1.442:1). Turn off 'Fast Pixel Aspect' in the Display Options to suppress these artifacts. Many effect filters that have parameters that represent width and height will have the width scaled appropriately (such as Blur, Defocus, Expand).
parameters.heading: Layout

parameters.label: Image Planes
parameters.description: Specifies the plane(s) to generate. Color and Alpha will always be present, but the generator does not always have to write to them. The list of planes is all the ones Houdini recognizes as special. Other planes can be added with the 'Custom Planes' parameter. C, A (C:rgb A): Color and Alpha C, A (C:rgb A:rgb): Color and 3-channel Alpha C (rgb): Color only A: Alpha only A (rgb): 3-channel Alpha only M: Mask plane M (rgb): 3-channel Mask plane Z: Z Depth plane L: Luminance plane B (uv): Bump plane P (xyz): Point plane N (xyz): Normal plane V (xyz): Velocity plane None: No planes generated.
parameters.heading: Layout

parameters.label: Add Plane
parameters.description: When a generator is connected to an input, it generates a Mask plane by default. This parameter determines which planes are generated in this case. The list of planes to generate are the same as 'Image Planes'. In addition, if the plane already exists in the input sequence, one of the following operations will be performed to combine the new plane. Replace: Input plane replaced by the generated plane. (G) Rename: Generated plane renamed. Add: Input plane added to the generated plane. (I+G) Screen: Input plane photographically added to the generated plane. (I+G-I*G) Subtract: Generated plane subtracted from the input plane. (I-G). Multiply: Input plane multiplied by the generated plane. (IxG) Min: Minimum pixel value of input and generated planes. (min{I,G}) Max: Maximum pixel value of input and generated planes. (max{I,G}) Average: Average pixel value of the input and generated planes. (I+G)/2
parameters.heading: Layout

parameters.label: Custom Planes
parameters.description: This string parameter allows you to create your own plane formats. The syntax is
parameters.heading: Layout

parameters.label: Raster Depth
parameters.description: The byte format of the image. Higher bit depths provide better color resolution and range at the expense of memory. 8 Bit Integer: Lowest bit depth. Banding can occasionally be seen. Suitable for video. 16 Bit Integer: Intermediate bit depth. No banding can be seen, though clipping can still occur below and above the black and white points. 32 Bit Integer: Generally not used for color, 32bit integer values are used to store object IDs, counts, and other integer values with a large range. 16 Bit Floating Point: High bit depth. No banding can be seen, and no clipping occurs at white and black. Uses less memory than 32 bit float, however processing time for this format is slightly higher as it is not a native CPU data format. This format supports values in the range -65504 to +65504. 32 Bit Floating Point: High bit depth. No banding can be seen, and no clipping occurs at white and black. Uses 4x as much memory as 8bit, which is this format's main drawback. Default Depth: Use the raster depth specified in the Composite Project options.
parameters.heading: Layout

parameters.label: Black/White Points
parameters.description: The integer formats (8, 16 and 32 bit) can specify the raw values that the black and white points occur at. The white point must always be higher than the black point. The minimum and maximum values for the black and white points for each format are td>> td>> td>>
parameters.heading: Layout

parameters.label: Interlacing
parameters.description: Controls the ability to generate images that are compatible with interlaced images. If you are manipulating the generated output with a filter that uses neighboring pixels (like Blur or Expand), it is recommended that you do not use Black Interlaced, as the filter will use the black scanlines as well. The second menu determines which scanlines are in which fields (odd,even) None: No interlacing. Half Res Interlaced: The image is half the height of a normal frame, with the scanlines on every line. Black Interlaced: The image is the same height as a normal frame, with the inactive scanlines filled with black. Line Doubled: The image is the same height as a normal frame, with the inactive scanlines filled with their active neighbor. Odd Dominant: Odd-numbered scanline fields come before even-numbered scanline fields. Even Dominant: Even-numbered scanline fields come before odd-numbered scanline fields. Odd Frames Only: Only odd-numbered scanline fields are produced. Even Frames Only: Only even-numbered scanline fields are produced.
parameters.heading: Layout

parameters.label: Override Global Range
parameters.description: If off, the global animation range is used as the frame range. If on, the frame range of the sequence can be specified in the following parameters.
parameters.heading: Layout

parameters.label: Still Image
parameters.description: A still image is time-invariant. It exists at every frame. If off, the Start Frame and Length are used to determine the frame range.
parameters.heading: Layout

parameters.label: Start Frame
parameters.description: The starting frame of the sequence.
parameters.heading: Layout

parameters.label: Length
parameters.description: The length of the sequence (number of frames in the sequence).
parameters.heading: Layout

parameters.label: Frame Rate
parameters.description: If on, the frame rate of the sequence can be overridden.
parameters.heading: Layout

parameters.label: Pre Extend
parameters.description: For sequences with a frame range, this determines how to show frames before the start frame. Black Frames: Display black. Cycle: Cycle the sequence, always playing it forward. Mirror: Cycle the sequence, reversing the direction every cycle. Hold: Hold the first frame indefinitely. Hold N Frames: Hold the first frame for a certain number of frames; before that, show black frames.
parameters.heading: Layout

parameters.label: Pre Hold
parameters.description: The number of frames to hold the first frame for, if 'Hold N Frames' is selected.
parameters.heading: Layout

parameters.label: Post Extend
parameters.description: For sequences with a frame range, this determines how to show frames after the last frame. Black Frames: Display black. Cycle: Cycle the sequence, always playing it forward. Mirror: Cycle the sequence, reversing the direction every cycle. Hold: Hold the last frame indefinitely. Hold N Frames: Hold the last frame for a certain number of frames; after that, show black frames.
parameters.heading: Layout

parameters.label: Post Hold
parameters.description: The number of frames to hold the last frame for, if 'Hold N Frames' is selected.
parameters.heading: Layout

entries.label: Front Face
entries.summary: Cleans up flipped normals by making them face the camera.

parameters.label: Align
parameters.description: The direction the normals should be facing. Toward Camera: Towards the camera or viewer, the most common orientation. Away From Camera: Away from the camera or viewer. Toward Direction: Towards an arbitrary direction, defined by a direction vector.
parameters.heading: Front Face

parameters.label: Direction
parameters.description: Specifies the direction vector for 'Toward Direction' alignment.
parameters.heading: Front Face

parameters.label: Max Angle Difference
parameters.description: The normal flipping threshold. If the angle that the normal makes with the camera or direction vector is less than this amount, the normal will not be flipped. Otherwise, the normal is flipped.
parameters.heading: Front Face

parameters.label: Override Normal Name
parameters.description: If on, you can specify a different plane for the normals. By default the normal plane is "N".
parameters.heading: Front Face

parameters.label: Normal Name
parameters.description: The name of the plane containing normals.
parameters.heading: Front Face

parameters.label: Effect Amount
parameters.description: If no mask is present, this blends the output with the input by a constant amount (0 = all input, 1 = all output). If a mask is present, this amount multiplies the mask.
parameters.heading: Mask

parameters.label: Operation Mask
parameters.description: Selects the mask plane to use as a mask from the mask input. The mask can be selected from First Input: Useful for masking the operation to the image's own alpha plane. Mask Input: Selects the mask from the side mask input. Off: Turns off masking, without requiring disconnection of the mask input (useful for temporarily disabling the mask).
parameters.heading: Mask

parameters.label: Resize Mask to Fit Image
parameters.description: If the mask image is a different resolution than the output image, turning on this parameter will scale the mask to the output image's resolution. If this node is changing constantly, and the mask is not, it is somewhat faster to put a Scale COP down to do the resize for the mask image. Otherwise, the scale will occur every time this node cooks.
parameters.heading: Mask

parameters.label: Invert Mask
parameters.description: Inverts the mask so that all fully 'masked' portions become unmasked. This saves you from inserting an Invert COP after the node with the mask.
parameters.heading: Mask

parameters.label: Plane Scope
parameters.description: Specifies the scope for both the RGB components of Color, Alpha, and other planes. The (C)RGBA mask only affects Color components and Alpha. 'C' will toggle all the RGB components. For planes other than Color and Alpha, the plane name (plus component, if applicable) should be specified in the string field. The pulldown menu can be used to select planes or components present in this node. A plane is specified by its name. A component is specified by both its plane and component name. The '*' wildcard may be used to scope all extra planes. Any number of planes or components can be specified, separated by spaces. Examples
parameters.heading: Scope

parameters.label: Frame Scope
parameters.description: Allows scoping of specific frames in the frame range. This is in addition to the plane scope (so a plane at a certain frame must be both plane scoped and frame scoped to be modified). All Frames: All frames are scoped. Inside Range: All frames inside a subrange are scoped. Outside Range: All frames outside a subrange are scoped. Even Frames: Even numbered frames are scoped. Odd Frames: Odd numbered frames are scoped. Specific Frames: A user-defined list of frames are scoped.
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Frame Range
parameters.description: For Inside/Outside range, this parameter specifies the subrange of the sequence to scope (or unscope). This can be edited in Timeline viewer mode (((Ctrl + 2)) in viewer).
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Frame Dropoff
parameters.description: For Inside/Outside Range, this parameter specifies certain number of frames before and after to slowly ramp up to scoped. The operation will be blended with its input to 'ease in' or 'ease out' the scoping effect over a number of frames. This can be edited in Timeline viewer mode (((Ctrl + 2)) in viewer).
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Non-scoped Effect
parameters.description: For unscoped frames, this sets the blend factor between the input and modified images. Normally this is zero (use the input image). By setting this to a non-zero value, you can make unscoped frames be 'slightly' unscoped. The value can vary between 0 (unscoped) and 1 (scoped).
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Frame List
parameters.description: The frame list for 'Specific Frames'. Frame numbers should be separated by spaces.
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Automatically Adjust for Length Changes
parameters.description: If the sequence range changes, enabling this parameter will adjust the subrange and frame dropoff lengths to fit the new range.
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

Scalar Mask ('A', 'C.r'): {{{ C.r = I.r * M C.g = I.g * M C.b = I.b * M }}} Vector Mask ('C'): {{{ C.r = I.r * M.r C.g = I.g * M.g C.b = I.b * M.b }}}
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Invert Mask
parameters.description: Inverts the mask so that all fully 'masked' portions become unmasked. This saves you from inserting an Invert COP after the node with the mask.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Override Size
parameters.description: If off, the resolution of the image is defined by the resolution in the Composite Project settings. If on, any resolution can be specified.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Pixel Aspect Ratio
parameters.description: If off, the pixel aspect ratio of the image is defined by the pixel aspect ratio in the Composite Project settings. If on, any pixel aspect ratio can be specified. The pixel aspect ratio determines the shape of the pixel; it represents the width of the pixel compared to the height. A pixel with an aspect ratio of '2' is twice as wide as it is high (2:1). Pixel aspect ratios less than 1 are taller than they are wide. The image viewer attempts to show the image as it would appear by horizontally scaling the image by the pixel aspect ratio. This can result in slight artifacts for non-integer ratios (ie, 0.9:1, 1.442:1). Turn off 'Fast Pixel Aspect' in the Display Options to suppress these artifacts. Many effect filters that have parameters that represent width and height will have the width scaled appropriately (such as Blur, Defocus, Expand).
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Image Planes
parameters.description: Specifies the plane(s) to generate. Color and Alpha will always be present, but the generator does not always have to write to them. The list of planes is all the ones Houdini recognizes as special. Other planes can be added with the 'Custom Planes' parameter. C, A (C:rgb A): Color and Alpha C, A (C:rgb A:rgb): Color and 3-channel Alpha C (rgb): Color only A: Alpha only A (rgb): 3-channel Alpha only M: Mask plane M (rgb): 3-channel Mask plane Z: Z Depth plane L: Luminance plane B (uv): Bump plane P (xyz): Point plane N (xyz): Normal plane V (xyz): Velocity plane None: No planes generated.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Add Plane
parameters.description: When a generator is connected to an input, it generates a Mask plane by default. This parameter determines which planes are generated in this case. The list of planes to generate are the same as 'Image Planes'. In addition, if the plane already exists in the input sequence, one of the following operations will be performed to combine the new plane. Replace: Input plane replaced by the generated plane. (G) Rename: Generated plane renamed. Add: Input plane added to the generated plane. (I+G) Screen: Input plane photographically added to the generated plane. (I+G-I*G) Subtract: Generated plane subtracted from the input plane. (I-G). Multiply: Input plane multiplied by the generated plane. (IxG) Min: Minimum pixel value of input and generated planes. (min{I,G}) Max: Maximum pixel value of input and generated planes. (max{I,G}) Average: Average pixel value of the input and generated planes. (I+G)/2
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Custom Planes
parameters.description: This string parameter allows you to create your own plane formats. The syntax is
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Raster Depth
parameters.description: The byte format of the image. Higher bit depths provide better color resolution and range at the expense of memory. 8 Bit Integer: Lowest bit depth. Banding can occasionally be seen. Suitable for video. 16 Bit Integer: Intermediate bit depth. No banding can be seen, though clipping can still occur below and above the black and white points. 32 Bit Integer: Generally not used for color, 32bit integer values are used to store object IDs, counts, and other integer values with a large range. 16 Bit Floating Point: High bit depth. No banding can be seen, and no clipping occurs at white and black. Uses less memory than 32 bit float, however processing time for this format is slightly higher as it is not a native CPU data format. This format supports values in the range -65504 to +65504. 32 Bit Floating Point: High bit depth. No banding can be seen, and no clipping occurs at white and black. Uses 4x as much memory as 8bit, which is this format's main drawback. Default Depth: Use the raster depth specified in the Composite Project options.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Black/White Points
parameters.description: The integer formats (8, 16 and 32 bit) can specify the raw values that the black and white points occur at. The white point must always be higher than the black point. The minimum and maximum values for the black and white points for each format are td>> td>> td>>
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Interlacing
parameters.description: Controls the ability to generate images that are compatible with interlaced images. If you are manipulating the generated output with a filter that uses neighboring pixels (like Blur or Expand), it is recommended that you do not use Black Interlaced, as the filter will use the black scanlines as well. The second menu determines which scanlines are in which fields (odd,even) None: No interlacing. Half Res Interlaced: The image is half the height of a normal frame, with the scanlines on every line. Black Interlaced: The image is the same height as a normal frame, with the inactive scanlines filled with black. Line Doubled: The image is the same height as a normal frame, with the inactive scanlines filled with their active neighbor. Odd Dominant: Odd-numbered scanline fields come before even-numbered scanline fields. Even Dominant: Even-numbered scanline fields come before odd-numbered scanline fields. Odd Frames Only: Only odd-numbered scanline fields are produced. Even Frames Only: Only even-numbered scanline fields are produced.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Override Global Range
parameters.description: If off, the global animation range is used as the frame range. If on, the frame range of the sequence can be specified in the following parameters.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Still Image
parameters.description: A still image is time-invariant. It exists at every frame. If off, the Start Frame and Length are used to determine the frame range.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Start Frame
parameters.description: The starting frame of the sequence.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Length
parameters.description: The length of the sequence (number of frames in the sequence).

parameters.label: Frame Rate

parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Pre Extend
parameters.description: For sequences with a frame range, this determines how to show frames before the start frame. Black Frames: Display black. Cycle: Cycle the sequence, always playing it forward. Mirror: Cycle the sequence, reversing the direction every cycle. Hold: Hold the first frame indefinitely. Hold N Frames: Hold the first frame for a certain number of frames; before that, show black frames.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Pre Hold
parameters.description: The number of frames to hold the first frame for, if 'Hold N Frames' is selected.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Post Extend
parameters.description: For sequences with a frame range, this determines how to show frames after the last frame. Black Frames: Display black. Cycle: Cycle the sequence, always playing it forward. Mirror: Cycle the sequence, reversing the direction every cycle. Hold: Hold the last frame indefinitely. Hold N Frames: Hold the last frame for a certain number of frames; after that, show black frames.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Post Hold
parameters.description: The number of frames to hold the last frame for, if 'Hold N Frames' is selected.
parameters.heading: Transform

entries.label: Gradient
entries.summary: Computes the gradient of an image.

parameters.label: Gradient Type
parameters.description: The channel used to compute the gradient. Normal Map can also use Displacement to convert XYZ displacements to normals. Displacement does not work for the other output modes and luminance will be used instead.

parameters.label: Output
parameters.description: The type of output produced UV Gradient: Computes the UV gradient of the image, which is a 2D vector which points in the direction of greatest luminance increase. The magnitude of the vector is the increase amount. Similar to the results produced by the Bump COP. Normal Map: Computes a normal map from the gradient. The normal and the gradient are similar: the normal is a normalized 3D vector with the Z component set to 1 and X & Y set to the U & V values of the gradient. Gradient Magnitude: Computes the gradient magnitude, which appears as a luminance edge-detected image. Thresholded Magnitude: Computes the gradient magnitude and only accepts values between the low and high threshold values. If normalize is on, the values are mapped from low to high to 0 to 1. Sum of Neighbor Gradient Magnitudes: Compute the gradients between the current pixel and its 4 immediate neighbors and sum the magnitudes of each.

parameters.label: Low/High Threshold
parameters.description: The low and high thresholds for thresholded magnitude output.

parameters.label: Normalize
parameters.description: If UV Gradient output is used, this normalizes the gradient's magnitudes to 1. If Thresholded Magnitude is used, this maps the low to high range to 0 - 1.

parameters.label: Effect Amount
parameters.description: If no mask is present, this blends the output with the input by a constant amount (0 = all input, 1 = all output). If a mask is present, this amount multiplies the mask.
parameters.heading: Mask

parameters.label: Operation Mask
parameters.description: Selects the mask plane to use as a mask from the mask input. The mask can be selected from First Input: Useful for masking the operation to the image's own alpha plane. Mask Input: Selects the mask from the side mask input. Off: Turns off masking, without requiring disconnection of the mask input (useful for temporarily disabling the mask).
parameters.heading: Mask

parameters.label: Resize Mask to Fit Image
parameters.description: If the mask image is a different resolution than the output image, turning on this parameter will scale the mask to the output image's resolution. If this node is changing constantly, and the mask is not, it is somewhat faster to put a Scale COP down to do the resize for the mask image. Otherwise, the scale will occur every time this node cooks.
parameters.heading: Mask

parameters.label: Invert Mask
parameters.description: Inverts the mask so that all fully 'masked' portions become unmasked. This saves you from inserting an Invert COP after the node with the mask.
parameters.heading: Mask

parameters.label: Plane Scope
parameters.description: Specifies the scope for both the RGB components of Color, Alpha, and other planes. The (C)RGBA mask only affects Color components and Alpha. 'C' will toggle all the RGB components. For planes other than Color and Alpha, the plane name (plus component, if applicable) should be specified in the string field. The pulldown menu can be used to select planes or components present in this node. A plane is specified by its name. A component is specified by both its plane and component name. The '*' wildcard may be used to scope all extra planes. Any number of planes or components can be specified, separated by spaces. Examples
parameters.heading: Scope

parameters.label: Frame Scope
parameters.description: Allows scoping of specific frames in the frame range. This is in addition to the plane scope (so a plane at a certain frame must be both plane scoped and frame scoped to be modified). All Frames: All frames are scoped. Inside Range: All frames inside a subrange are scoped. Outside Range: All frames outside a subrange are scoped. Even Frames: Even numbered frames are scoped. Odd Frames: Odd numbered frames are scoped. Specific Frames: A user-defined list of frames are scoped.
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Frame Range
parameters.description: For Inside/Outside range, this parameter specifies the subrange of the sequence to scope (or unscope). This can be edited in Timeline viewer mode (((Ctrl + 2)) in viewer).
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Frame Dropoff
parameters.description: For Inside/Outside Range, this parameter specifies certain number of frames before and after to slowly ramp up to scoped. The operation will be blended with its input to 'ease in' or 'ease out' the scoping effect over a number of frames. This can be edited in Timeline viewer mode (((Ctrl + 2)) in viewer).
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Non-scoped Effect
parameters.description: For unscoped frames, this sets the blend factor between the input and modified images. Normally this is zero (use the input image). By setting this to a non-zero value, you can make unscoped frames be 'slightly' unscoped. The value can vary between 0 (unscoped) and 1 (scoped).
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Frame List
parameters.description: The frame list for 'Specific Frames'. Frame numbers should be separated by spaces.
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Automatically Adjust for Length Changes
parameters.description: If the sequence range changes, enabling this parameter will adjust the subrange and frame dropoff lengths to fit the new range.
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

entries.label: Illegal Pixel
entries.summary: Detects illegal pixels, like NAN and INF, in images.

parameters.label: Illegal Pixels
parameters.description: Illegal pixels can be flagged or fixed. Often, flagging is used to debug the shader, while fixing is used to attempt to continue with the image as-is. "Fix by Blending Surrounding Pixels": For small numbers or isolated pixels, this method will work well to fix the image. "Fix by Zeroing": This method clears the NANs so that downstream compositing operations behave, but doesn't do much in the way of visually correcting the image. "Show by Highlighting": Shows bad pixels by highlighting them super-red (20,0,0). "Show by Isolating": Shows bad pixels by highlighting them and clearing all correct pixels.
parameters.heading: Illegal Pixel

parameters.label: Notification
parameters.description: If a bad pixel is found, this operation can raise a warning or an error. "None": The node is not flagged with an error or warning, though the number of bad pixels is still reported in the node info. "Warning": A warning flag is posted with the number of bad pixels in the node info. "Error": An error is raised. The number of bad pixels is printed in the node info, but it may not be entirely accurate because this will terminate the cook, and no more tiles will be processed. "Error if Over Limit": An error is raised if the number of bad pixels in a single plane is greater than the limit specified. Otherwise, a warning is raised.
parameters.heading: Illegal Pixel

parameters.label: "Illegal Pixel Limit"
parameters.description: The number of acceptable bad pixels. If more than this number are in the image, the cook will halt.
parameters.heading: Illegal Pixel

parameters.label: Effect Amount
parameters.description: If no mask is present, this blends the output with the input by a constant amount (0 = all input, 1 = all output). If a mask is present, this amount multiplies the mask.
parameters.heading: Mask

parameters.label: Operation Mask
parameters.description: Selects the mask plane to use as a mask from the mask input. The mask can be selected from First Input: Useful for masking the operation to the image's own alpha plane. Mask Input: Selects the mask from the side mask input. Off: Turns off masking, without requiring disconnection of the mask input (useful for temporarily disabling the mask).
parameters.heading: Mask

parameters.label: Resize Mask to Fit Image
parameters.description: If the mask image is a different resolution than the output image, turning on this parameter will scale the mask to the output image's resolution. If this node is changing constantly, and the mask is not, it is somewhat faster to put a Scale COP down to do the resize for the mask image. Otherwise, the scale will occur every time this node cooks.
parameters.heading: Mask

parameters.label: Invert Mask
parameters.description: Inverts the mask so that all fully 'masked' portions become unmasked. This saves you from inserting an Invert COP after the node with the mask.
parameters.heading: Mask

parameters.label: Plane Scope
parameters.description: Specifies the scope for both the RGB components of Color, Alpha, and other planes. The (C)RGBA mask only affects Color components and Alpha. 'C' will toggle all the RGB components. For planes other than Color and Alpha, the plane name (plus component, if applicable) should be specified in the string field. The pulldown menu can be used to select planes or components present in this node. A plane is specified by its name. A component is specified by both its plane and component name. The '*' wildcard may be used to scope all extra planes. Any number of planes or components can be specified, separated by spaces. Examples
parameters.heading: Scope

parameters.label: Frame Scope
parameters.description: Allows scoping of specific frames in the frame range. This is in addition to the plane scope (so a plane at a certain frame must be both plane scoped and frame scoped to be modified). All Frames: All frames are scoped. Inside Range: All frames inside a subrange are scoped. Outside Range: All frames outside a subrange are scoped. Even Frames: Even numbered frames are scoped. Odd Frames: Odd numbered frames are scoped. Specific Frames: A user-defined list of frames are scoped.
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Frame Range
parameters.description: For Inside/Outside range, this parameter specifies the subrange of the sequence to scope (or unscope). This can be edited in Timeline viewer mode (((Ctrl + 2)) in viewer).
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Frame Dropoff
parameters.description: For Inside/Outside Range, this parameter specifies certain number of frames before and after to slowly ramp up to scoped. The operation will be blended with its input to 'ease in' or 'ease out' the scoping effect over a number of frames. This can be edited in Timeline viewer mode (((Ctrl + 2)) in viewer).
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Non-scoped Effect
parameters.description: For unscoped frames, this sets the blend factor between the input and modified images. Normally this is zero (use the input image). By setting this to a non-zero value, you can make unscoped frames be 'slightly' unscoped. The value can vary between 0 (unscoped) and 1 (scoped).
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Frame List
parameters.description: The frame list for 'Specific Frames'. Frame numbers should be separated by spaces.
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Automatically Adjust for Length Changes
parameters.description: If the sequence range changes, enabling this parameter will adjust the subrange and frame dropoff lengths to fit the new range.
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

entries.label: Layer
entries.summary: Layers a series of inputs together by compositing them one by one on the background image (input 1).

parameters.label: Operation
parameters.description: Specifies the global compositing operation Over: Places the foreground over the background. Under: Places the foreground under the background's alpha. Atop: Places the foreground over the background only where the background alpha exists. Inside: Places the foreground inside the background's alpha. Outside: Places the foreground outside the background's alpha. Screen: Acts as a saturating add, much like photographic addition. Add: Adds the foreground to the background. Subtract: Subtracts the foreground from the background. Diff: Takes the absolute difference between the foreground and the background. Multiply: Multiplies the background by the foreground. Minimum: Takes the minimum of the foreground and background. Maximum: Takes the maximum of the foreground and background. Average: Takes the average of the foreground and background. Xor: Takes the exclusive or of the two alpha planes, so that alpha areas that overlap are removed.
parameters.heading: Composite

parameters.label: Alpha Operation
parameters.description: Specifies the compositing operation for the alpha plane, which is normally the same as the global compositing operations (see above).

entries.summary: Generates continuous noise patterns.

parameters.label: Noise Type
parameters.description: Specifies the noise type. Hermite Interpolation: Fast, somewhat uniform. Sparse Convolution: Slower, more random. Improved Hermite: Fast, better randomness than Hermite Interpolation. Alligator: Slow, cell-like noise. Random (white): Random numbers per pixel.
parameters.heading: Noise

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.description: Random seed for the noise.
parameters.heading: Noise

parameters.label: Noise Per Component
parameters.description: If on, different noise values are generated per component, otherwise, all components share the same pixel values.
parameters.heading: Noise

parameters.label: Turbulence
parameters.description: The number of noise generations to use.
parameters.heading: Noise

parameters.label: Roughness
parameters.description: The amplitude reduction of higher frequency noise contributions.
parameters.heading: Noise

parameters.label: Exponent
parameters.description: Raises the noise to the given exponent.
parameters.heading: Noise

parameters.label: Spatial Frequency
parameters.description: The scale of the noise; decreasing frequency increases feature size.
parameters.heading: Noise

parameters.label: Spatial Offset
parameters.description: Allows you to pan around in the noise.
parameters.heading: Noise

parameters.label: Frame Frequency
parameters.description: How quickly the noise changes over time.
parameters.heading: Noise

parameters.label: Frame Offset
parameters.description: Allows you to shift noise frames through time.
parameters.heading: Noise

parameters.label: Amplitude
parameters.description: Amplitude of the final noise intensity.
parameters.heading: Noise

parameters.label: Shift
parameters.description: Constant value added to all noise results.
parameters.heading: Noise

parameters.label: Adjust for Aspect Ratio
parameters.description: If on, the noise is vertically stretched or squashed by the aspect ratio of the image (width/height) so that the noise isn't distorted.
parameters.heading: Noise

parameters.label: Effect Amount
parameters.description: If no mask is present, this multiplies the output by a constant amount (0 = black, 1 = all output). If a mask is present, this amount multiplies the mask.
parameters.heading: Noise

parameters.label: Mask Plane
parameters.description: A mask can be a component of a plane or an entire plane. If a vector plane is supplied as a mask, its components are multiplied by the images' components. Scalar Mask ('A', 'C.r'): {{{ C.r = I.r * M C.g = I.g * M C.b = I.b * M }}} Vector Mask ('C'): {{{ C.r = I.r * M.r C.g = I.g * M.g C.b = I.b * M.b }}}
parameters.heading: Noise

parameters.label: Invert Mask
parameters.description: Inverts the mask so that all fully 'masked' portions become unmasked. This saves you from inserting an Invert COP after the node with the mask.
parameters.heading: Noise

parameters.label: Override Size
parameters.description: If off, the resolution of the image is defined by the resolution in the Composite Project settings. If on, any resolution can be specified.
parameters.heading: Noise

parameters.label: Pixel Aspect Ratio
parameters.description: If off, the pixel aspect ratio of the image is defined by the pixel aspect ratio in the Composite Project settings. If on, any pixel aspect ratio can be specified. The pixel aspect ratio determines the shape of the pixel; it represents the width of the pixel compared to the height. A pixel with an aspect ratio of '2' is twice as wide as it is high (2:1). Pixel aspect ratios less than 1 are taller than they are wide. The image viewer attempts to show the image as it would appear by horizontally scaling the image by the pixel aspect ratio. This can result in slight artifacts for non-integer ratios (ie, 0.9:1, 1.442:1). Turn off 'Fast Pixel Aspect' in the Display Options to suppress these artifacts. Many effect filters that have parameters that represent width and height will have the width scaled appropriately (such as Blur, Defocus, Expand).
parameters.heading: Noise

parameters.label: Image Planes
parameters.description: Specifies the plane(s) to generate. Color and Alpha will always be present, but the generator does not always have to write to them. The list of planes is all the ones Houdini recognizes as special. Other planes can be added with the 'Custom Planes' parameter. C, A (C:rgb A): Color and Alpha C, A (C:rgb A:rgb): Color and 3-channel Alpha C (rgb): Color only A: Alpha only A (rgb): 3-channel Alpha only M: Mask plane M (rgb): 3-channel Mask plane Z: Z Depth plane L: Luminance plane B (uv): Bump plane P (xyz): Point plane N (xyz): Normal plane V (xyz): Velocity plane None: No planes generated.
parameters.heading: Noise

parameters.label: Add Plane
parameters.description: When a generator is connected to an input, it generates a Mask plane by default. This parameter determines which planes are generated in this case. The list of planes to generate are the same as 'Image Planes'. In addition, if the plane already exists in the input sequence, one of the following operations will be performed to combine the new plane. Replace: Input plane replaced by the generated plane. (G) Rename: Generated plane renamed. Add: Input plane added to the generated plane. (I+G) Screen: Input plane photographically added to the generated plane. (I+G-I*G) Subtract: Generated plane subtracted from the input plane. (I-G). Multiply: Input plane multiplied by the generated plane. (IxG) Min: Minimum pixel value of input and generated planes. (min{I,G}) Max: Maximum pixel value of input and generated planes. (max{I,G}) Average: Average pixel value of the input and generated planes. (I+G)/2
parameters.heading: Noise

parameters.label: Custom Planes
parameters.description: This string parameter allows you to create your own plane formats. The syntax is
parameters.heading: Noise

parameters.label: Raster Depth
parameters.description: The byte format of the image. Higher bit depths provide better color resolution and range at the expense of memory. 8 Bit Integer: Lowest bit depth. Banding can occasionally be seen. Suitable for video. 16 Bit Integer: Intermediate bit depth. No banding can be seen, though clipping can still occur below and above the black and white points. 32 Bit Integer: Generally not used for color, 32bit integer values are used to store object IDs, counts, and other integer values with a large range. 16 Bit Floating Point: High bit depth. No banding can be seen, and no clipping occurs at white and black. Uses less memory than 32 bit float, however processing time for this format is slightly higher as it is not a native CPU data format. This format supports values in the range -65504 to +65504. 32 Bit Floating Point: High bit depth. No banding can be seen, and no clipping occurs at white and black. Uses 4x as much memory as 8bit, which is this format's main drawback. Default Depth: Use the raster depth specified in the Composite Project options.
parameters.heading: Noise

parameters.label: Black/White Points
parameters.description: The integer formats (8, 16 and 32 bit) can specify the raw values that the black and white points occur at. The white point must always be higher than the black point. The minimum and maximum values for the black and white points for each format are td>> td>> td>>
parameters.heading: Noise

parameters.label: Interlacing
parameters.description: Controls the ability to generate images that are compatible with interlaced images. If you are manipulating the generated output with a filter that uses neighboring pixels (like Blur or Expand), it is recommended that you do not use Black Interlaced, as the filter will use the black scanlines as well. The second menu determines which scanlines are in which fields (odd,even) None: No interlacing. Half Res Interlaced: The image is half the height of a normal frame, with the scanlines on every line. Black Interlaced: The image is the same height as a normal frame, with the inactive scanlines filled with black. Line Doubled: The image is the same height as a normal frame, with the inactive scanlines filled with their active neighbor. Odd Dominant: Odd-numbered scanline fields come before even-numbered scanline fields. Even Dominant: Even-numbered scanline fields come before odd-numbered scanline fields. Odd Frames Only: Only odd-numbered scanline fields are produced. Even Frames Only: Only even-numbered scanline fields are produced.
parameters.heading: Noise

parameters.label: Override Global Range
parameters.description: If off, the global animation range is used as the frame range. If on, the frame range of the sequence can be specified in the following parameters.
parameters.heading: Noise

parameters.label: Still Image
parameters.description: A still image is time-invariant. It exists at every frame. If off, the Start Frame and Length are used to determine the frame range.

parameters.heading: Noise

parameters.label: Pre Extend
parameters.description: For sequences with a frame range, this determines how to show frames before the start frame. Black Frames: Display black. Cycle: Cycle the sequence, always playing it forward. Hold N Frames: Hold the first frame for a certain number of frames; before that, show black frames.

parameters.label: Ramp
parameters.description: The type of ramp to generate. Horizontal: Ramp is linear type with points horizontally. Vertical: Ramp is linear type with points vertically. Radial: Ramp is circular with points extending radially. Concentric: Ramp is circular with points at varying distances from the center.
parameters.heading: Ramp

parameters.label: Global Interpolation
parameters.description: The interpolation between ramp point which is used by default. Individual points may override this interpolation. Step: The segment is constant valued, immediately changing to the next color. Hold: The segment is constant valued, holding the current color until the next point. Linear: The segment is linearly interpolated between the two point colors. Ease In: The segment drops off quickly from the first value and eases into the second. Ease Out: The segment eases out of the first value and drops quickly to the second. Ease In Ease Out: The segment eases into both values.
parameters.heading: Ramp

parameters.label: Rotation
