parameters.heading: Ramp

parameters.label: Center
parameters.description: Specifies the center of the ramp for radial and concentric ramps.
parameters.heading: Ramp

parameters.label: Wrap First To Last
parameters.description: If on, an implicit segment is created between the last and first points. Otherwise, the value of the first and last ramp points is held before or after the ramp point range.
parameters.heading: Ramp

parameters.label: Repeat Ramp
parameters.description: For a concentric ramp, this will repeat the ramp continually if on. Otherwise, only 1 cycle is used.
parameters.heading: Ramp

parameters.label: Point N
parameters.description: The U coordinate of this ramp point (0-1).
parameters.heading: Points

parameters.label: Color
parameters.description: The color of the ramp point. Values may be less than zero or greater than 1.
parameters.heading: Points

parameters.label: Segment N Interpolation
parameters.description: By default, the global interpolation is used. This can override the interpolation to give a segment a specific interpolation.
parameters.heading: Points

parameters.label: Effect Amount
parameters.description: If no mask is present, this multiplies the output by a constant amount (0 = black, 1 = all output). If a mask is present, this amount multiplies the mask.
parameters.heading: Points

parameters.description: A mask can be a component of a plane or an entire plane. If a vector plane is supplied as a mask, its components are multiplied by the images' components. Scalar Mask ('A', 'C.r'): {{{ C.r = I.r * M C.g = I.g * M C.b = I.b * M }}} Vector Mask ('C'): {{{ C.r = I.r * M.r C.g = I.g * M.g C.b = I.b * M.b }}}
parameters.heading: Points

parameters.label: Invert Mask
parameters.description: Inverts the mask so that all fully 'masked' portions become unmasked. This saves you from inserting an Invert COP after the node with the mask.
parameters.heading: Points

parameters.label: Override Size
parameters.description: If off, the resolution of the image is defined by the resolution in the Composite Project settings. If on, any resolution can be specified.
parameters.heading: Points

parameters.label: Pixel Aspect Ratio
parameters.description: If off, the pixel aspect ratio of the image is defined by the pixel aspect ratio in the Composite Project settings. If on, any pixel aspect ratio can be specified. The pixel aspect ratio determines the shape of the pixel; it represents the width of the pixel compared to the height. A pixel with an aspect ratio of '2' is twice as wide as it is high (2:1). Pixel aspect ratios less than 1 are taller than they are wide. The image viewer attempts to show the image as it would appear by horizontally scaling the image by the pixel aspect ratio. This can result in slight artifacts for non-integer ratios (ie, 0.9:1, 1.442:1). Turn off 'Fast Pixel Aspect' in the Display Options to suppress these artifacts. Many effect filters that have parameters that represent width and height will have the width scaled appropriately (such as Blur, Defocus, Expand).

In addition, if the plane already exists in the input sequence, one of the following operations will be performed to combine the new plane. Replace: Input plane replaced by the generated plane. (G) Rename: Generated plane renamed. Add: Input plane added to the generated plane. (I+G) Screen: Input plane photographically added to the generated plane. (I+G-I*G) Subtract: Generated plane subtracted from the input plane. (I-G). Multiply: Input plane multiplied by the generated plane. (IxG) Min: Minimum pixel value of input and generated planes. (min{I,G}) Max: Maximum pixel value of input and generated planes. (max{I,G}) Average: Average pixel value of the input and generated planes. (I+G)/2
parameters.heading: Points

parameters.label: Custom Planes
parameters.description: This string parameter allows you to create your own plane formats. The syntax is
parameters.heading: Points

parameters.label: Raster Depth
parameters.description: The byte format of the image. Higher bit depths provide better color resolution and range at the expense of memory. 8 Bit Integer: Lowest bit depth. Banding can occasionally be seen. Suitable for video. 16 Bit Integer: Intermediate bit depth. No banding can be seen, though clipping can still occur below and above the black and white points. 32 Bit Integer: Generally not used for color, 32bit integer values are used to store object IDs, counts, and other integer values with a large range. 16 Bit Floating Point: High bit depth. No banding can be seen, and no clipping occurs at white and black. Uses less memory than 32 bit float, however processing time for this format is slightly higher as it is not a native CPU data format. This format supports values in the range -65504 to +65504. 32 Bit Floating Point: High bit depth. No banding can be seen, and no clipping occurs at white and black. Uses 4x as much memory as 8bit, which is this format's main drawback. Default Depth: Use the raster depth specified in the Composite Project options.
parameters.heading: Points

parameters.label: Black/White Points
parameters.description: The integer formats (8, 16 and 32 bit) can specify the raw values that the black and white points occur at. The white point must always be higher than the black point. The minimum and maximum values for the black and white points for each format are td>> td>> td>>
parameters.heading: Points

parameters.label: Interlacing
parameters.description: Controls the ability to generate images that are compatible with interlaced images. If you are manipulating the generated output with a filter that uses neighboring pixels (like Blur or Expand), it is recommended that you do not use Black Interlaced, as the filter will use the black scanlines as well. The second menu determines which scanlines are in which fields (odd,even) None: No interlacing. Half Res Interlaced: The image is half the height of a normal frame, with the scanlines on every line. Black Interlaced: The image is the same height as a normal frame, with the inactive scanlines filled with black. Line Doubled: The image is the same height as a normal frame, with the inactive scanlines filled with their active neighbor. Odd Dominant: Odd-numbered scanline fields come before even-numbered scanline fields. Even Dominant: Even-numbered scanline fields come before odd-numbered scanline fields. Odd Frames Only: Only odd-numbered scanline fields are produced. Even Frames Only: Only even-numbered scanline fields are produced.
parameters.heading: Points

parameters.label: Override Global Range

parameters.label: Still Image

parameters.description: The starting frame of the sequence.
parameters.heading: Points

parameters.label: Length
parameters.description: The length of the sequence (number of frames in the sequence).
parameters.heading: Points

parameters.label: Frame Rate
parameters.description: If on, the frame rate of the sequence can be overridden.
parameters.heading: Points

parameters.label: Pre Extend
parameters.description: For sequences with a frame range, this determines how to show frames before the start frame. Black Frames: Display black. Cycle: Cycle the sequence, always playing it forward. Hold N Frames: Hold the first frame for a certain number of frames; before that, show black frames.

parameters.label: Post Extend

parameters.description: The level of antialiasing, both horizontally and vertically. This can vary from 1 to 8. Higher levels of antialiasing will produce more levels of gray on edges, but increase rendering time. The product of the horizontal and vertical antialias setting cannot exceed 64 (8x8).

entries.label: Scale
entries.summary: Changes the resolution of the image.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: Specifies the scaling method To Resolution: Scales to the specified number of pixels. To Fraction: Scales to a fraction (e.g. 0.5 = 50%) To Aspect Ratio: Scales to a given Pixel Aspect ratio. To Second Input's Resolution: Scales to match the resolution of the second input. To a Fraction of the Second Input: Scales to match the resolution of the second input scaled by a fraction (e.g. 0.5 = 50%). To Second Input's Aspect Ratio: Scales to match the second input's aspect ratio.

parameters.label: Image Size
parameters.description: Specify the size the image should be scaled to (in Pixels).

parameters.label: Image Fraction
parameters.description: Specify the size you'd like to scale the image as a fraction (e.g. 0.5 = 50%).

parameters.label: Pixel Aspect
parameters.description: Pixel Aspect is the ratio of the width to the height. Specify the pixel aspect ratio to scale the image by here.

parameters.label: Preserve Aspect Ratio
parameters.description: When enabled, it preserves the ratio of the image width to height when scaling.

parameters.label: Image Filter
parameters.description: Specifies the type of filter to use when scaling. The Box filter is the fastest; for almost all uses, the Gaussian is the best choice; use Catmull when you need something a bit sharper than Gaussian.

entries.label: Screen
entries.summary: Adds two images together, saturating at white like photographic addition.

parameters.label: Image Units
parameters.description: Selects pixels or UV units for the transform.
parameters.heading: Composite

parameters.label: Translate, Rotate, Scale, Pivot
parameters.description: Transforms the foreground in X,Y relative to the background.
parameters.heading: Composite

parameters.label: Image Filter
parameters.description: Specifies the filter to use when transforming.
parameters.heading: Composite

parameters.label: Image Wrap
parameters.description: Specifies the foreground image's wrapping style.
parameters.heading: Composite

parameters.label: Motion Blur
parameters.description: Toggles on motion blur, and specifies the time range around the current frame to blur.
parameters.heading: Composite

parameters.label: Motion Frame Bias
parameters.description: Shifts the time range for the blur.
parameters.heading: Composite

parameters.label: Motion Blur Segments
parameters.description: Number of samples to blur together in the specified time range.
parameters.heading: Composite

parameters.label: Motion Blur Method
parameters.description: Velocity: Only uses the current frame and the transform to compute past and future positions. Deformation: Cooks the images at all time samples.
parameters.heading: Composite

parameters.label: Overview
parameters.description: These parameters specify how to build the output sequence when there are differences between the input sequences.
parameters.heading: Merge

parameters.label: Plane Merge
parameters.description: If the planes in the inputs differ, this specifies what the output planes should be.
parameters.heading: Merge

parameters.label: Raster Depth
parameters.description: If the raster depth for a given plane differs between inputs, this specifies what the output raster depth for the plane should be.
parameters.heading: Merge

parameters.label: Frame Range
parameters.description: If the frame ranges of the inputs differ, this determines what the output range should be.
parameters.heading: Merge

parameters.label: Frame Rate
parameters.description: If the frame rates of the inputs differ, this determines what the output frame rate should be.
parameters.heading: Merge

parameters.label: Frame Match
parameters.description: If the frame rates of the inputs differ, this determines which input frame to pick when the cook time doesn't reside on a frame boundary.
parameters.heading: Merge

parameters.label: Effect Amount
parameters.description: If no mask is present, this blends the output with the input by a constant amount (0 = all input, 1 = all output). If a mask is present, this amount multiplies the mask.
parameters.heading: Mask

parameters.label: Operation Mask
parameters.description: Selects the mask plane to use as a mask from the mask input. The mask can be selected from First Input: Useful for masking the operation to the image's own alpha plane. Mask Input: Selects the mask from the side mask input. Off: Turns off masking, without requiring disconnection of the mask input (useful for temporarily disabling the mask).
parameters.heading: Mask

parameters.label: Resize Mask to Fit Image
parameters.description: If the mask image is a different resolution than the output image, turning on this parameter will scale the mask to the output image's resolution. If this node is changing constantly, and the mask is not, it is somewhat faster to put a Scale COP down to do the resize for the mask image. Otherwise, the scale will occur every time this node cooks.
parameters.heading: Mask

parameters.label: Invert Mask
parameters.description: Inverts the mask so that all fully 'masked' portions become unmasked. This saves you from inserting an Invert COP after the node with the mask.
parameters.heading: Mask

parameters.label: Plane Scope
parameters.description: Specifies the scope for both the RGB components of Color, Alpha, and other planes. The (C)RGBA mask only affects Color components and Alpha. 'C' will toggle all the RGB components. For planes other than Color and Alpha, the plane name (plus component, if applicable) should be specified in the string field. The pulldown menu can be used to select planes or components present in this node. A plane is specified by its name. A component is specified by both its plane and component name. The '*' wildcard may be used to scope all extra planes. Any number of planes or components can be specified, separated by spaces. Examples
parameters.heading: Scope

parameters.label: Frame Scope
parameters.description: Allows scoping of specific frames in the frame range. This is in addition to the plane scope (so a plane at a certain frame must be both plane scoped and frame scoped to be modified). All Frames: All frames are scoped. Inside Range: All frames inside a subrange are scoped. Outside Range: All frames outside a subrange are scoped. Even Frames: Even numbered frames are scoped. Odd Frames: Odd numbered frames are scoped. Specific Frames: A user-defined list of frames are scoped.
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Frame Range
parameters.description: For Inside/Outside range, this parameter specifies the subrange of the sequence to scope (or unscope). This can be edited in Timeline viewer mode (((Ctrl + 2)) in viewer).
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Frame Dropoff
parameters.description: For Inside/Outside Range, this parameter specifies certain number of frames before and after to slowly ramp up to scoped. The operation will be blended with its input to 'ease in' or 'ease out' the scoping effect over a number of frames. This can be edited in Timeline viewer mode (((Ctrl + 2)) in viewer).
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Non-scoped Effect
parameters.description: For unscoped frames, this sets the blend factor between the input and modified images. Normally this is zero (use the input image). By setting this to a non-zero value, you can make unscoped frames be 'slightly' unscoped. The value can vary between 0 (unscoped) and 1 (scoped).
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Frame List
parameters.description: The frame list for 'Specific Frames'. Frame numbers should be separated by spaces.
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Automatically Adjust for Length Changes
parameters.description: If the sequence range changes, enabling this parameter will adjust the subrange and frame dropoff lengths to fit the new range.
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

entries.summary: Generates simple shapes, such as circles, stars and regular N-sided polygons.

parameters.label: Shape Type
parameters.description: Selects the shape. Regular N-sided: Regular polygons, like triangles, pentagons and octagons. Star: N-pointed stars. Circle: A perfect circle. Ring: A circular ring. Equilateral Triangle: A triangle with all sides equal. Isosceles Triangle: A triangle with two sides equal. Rectangle: A rectangle. Parallelogram: A slanted rectangle.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Number of Sides
parameters.description: The number of sides in a Regular N-sided shape.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Number of Points
parameters.description: The number of points in a star.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Inner Radius
parameters.description: The inner radius of a star and a ring.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Corner Angle
parameters.description: The slant angle of a parallelogram.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Use Sweep Angles
parameters.description: If on, the start and end sweep angles of circles and rings.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Preserve Aspect Ratio
parameters.description: If on, the 1:1 aspect ratio of the shape is kept even if the image resolution is not 1:1.
parameters.heading: Shape

parameters.label: Fill
parameters.description: The render mode, Solid (filled) or Hollow (outlined).
parameters.heading: Fill

parameters.label: Antialias
parameters.description: The amount of antialiasing to perform on edges. Higher numbers produce more edge levels. The product of the two fields must not exceed 64 (8x8).
parameters.heading: Fill

parameters.label: Level of Detail
parameters.description: The level of detail used when converting circles and rings to polygons before rendering.
parameters.heading: Fill

parameters.label: Fill Outside
parameters.description: If on, the 'outside' region is filled instead of the interior (for hollow shapes, the outside region is the region not included by the line thickness).
parameters.heading: Fill

parameters.label: Thickness
parameters.description: For hollow shapes, the thickness of the lines to use, in UV space.
parameters.heading: Fill

parameters.label: Color
parameters.description: The color to render the shape.
parameters.heading: Fill

parameters.label: Overview
parameters.description: A 2D animated transform can be applied to the spline. All units are in UV space.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Effect Amount
parameters.description: If no mask is present, this multiplies the output by a constant amount (0 = black, 1 = all output). If a mask is present, this amount multiplies the mask.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Mask Plane
parameters.description: A mask can be a component of a plane or an entire plane. If a vector plane is supplied as a mask, its components are multiplied by the images' components. Scalar Mask ('A', 'C.r'): {{{ C.r = I.r * M C.g = I.g * M C.b = I.b * M }}} Vector Mask ('C'): {{{ C.r = I.r * M.r C.g = I.g * M.g C.b = I.b * M.b }}}
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Invert Mask
parameters.description: Inverts the mask so that all fully 'masked' portions become unmasked. This saves you from inserting an Invert COP after the node with the mask.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Override Size
parameters.description: If off, the resolution of the image is defined by the resolution in the Composite Project settings. If on, any resolution can be specified.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Pixel Aspect Ratio
parameters.description: If off, the pixel aspect ratio of the image is defined by the pixel aspect ratio in the Composite Project settings. If on, any pixel aspect ratio can be specified. The pixel aspect ratio determines the shape of the pixel; it represents the width of the pixel compared to the height. A pixel with an aspect ratio of '2' is twice as wide as it is high (2:1). Pixel aspect ratios less than 1 are taller than they are wide. The image viewer attempts to show the image as it would appear by horizontally scaling the image by the pixel aspect ratio. This can result in slight artifacts for non-integer ratios (ie, 0.9:1, 1.442:1). Turn off 'Fast Pixel Aspect' in the Display Options to suppress these artifacts. Many effect filters that have parameters that represent width and height will have the width scaled appropriately (such as Blur, Defocus, Expand).
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Image Planes
parameters.description: Specifies the plane(s) to generate. Color and Alpha will always be present, but the generator does not always have to write to them. The list of planes is all the ones Houdini recognizes as special. Other planes can be added with the 'Custom Planes' parameter. C, A (C:rgb A): Color and Alpha C, A (C:rgb A:rgb): Color and 3-channel Alpha C (rgb): Color only A: Alpha only A (rgb): 3-channel Alpha only M: Mask plane M (rgb): 3-channel Mask plane Z: Z Depth plane L: Luminance plane B (uv): Bump plane P (xyz): Point plane N (xyz): Normal plane V (xyz): Velocity plane None: No planes generated.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Add Plane
parameters.description: When a generator is connected to an input, it generates a Mask plane by default. This parameter determines which planes are generated in this case. The list of planes to generate are the same as 'Image Planes'. In addition, if the plane already exists in the input sequence, one of the following operations will be performed to combine the new plane. Replace: Input plane replaced by the generated plane. (G) Rename: Generated plane renamed. Add: Input plane added to the generated plane. (I+G) Screen: Input plane photographically added to the generated plane. (I+G-I*G) Subtract: Generated plane subtracted from the input plane. (I-G). Multiply: Input plane multiplied by the generated plane. (IxG) Min: Minimum pixel value of input and generated planes. (min{I,G}) Max: Maximum pixel value of input and generated planes. (max{I,G}) Average: Average pixel value of the input and generated planes. (I+G)/2
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Custom Planes
parameters.description: This string parameter allows you to create your own plane formats. The syntax is
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Raster Depth
parameters.description: The byte format of the image. Higher bit depths provide better color resolution and range at the expense of memory. 8 Bit Integer: Lowest bit depth. Banding can occasionally be seen. Suitable for video. 16 Bit Integer: Intermediate bit depth. No banding can be seen, though clipping can still occur below and above the black and white points. 32 Bit Integer: Generally not used for color, 32bit integer values are used to store object IDs, counts, and other integer values with a large range. 16 Bit Floating Point: High bit depth. No banding can be seen, and no clipping occurs at white and black. Uses less memory than 32 bit float, however processing time for this format is slightly higher as it is not a native CPU data format. This format supports values in the range -65504 to +65504. 32 Bit Floating Point: High bit depth. No banding can be seen, and no clipping occurs at white and black. Uses 4x as much memory as 8bit, which is this format's main drawback. Default Depth: Use the raster depth specified in the Composite Project options.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Black/White Points
parameters.description: The integer formats (8, 16 and 32 bit) can specify the raw values that the black and white points occur at. The white point must always be higher than the black point. The minimum and maximum values for the black and white points for each format are td>> td>> td>>
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Interlacing
parameters.description: Controls the ability to generate images that are compatible with interlaced images. If you are manipulating the generated output with a filter that uses neighboring pixels (like Blur or Expand), it is recommended that you do not use Black Interlaced, as the filter will use the black scanlines as well. The second menu determines which scanlines are in which fields (odd,even) None: No interlacing. Half Res Interlaced: The image is half the height of a normal frame, with the scanlines on every line. Black Interlaced: The image is the same height as a normal frame, with the inactive scanlines filled with black. Line Doubled: The image is the same height as a normal frame, with the inactive scanlines filled with their active neighbor. Odd Dominant: Odd-numbered scanline fields come before even-numbered scanline fields. Even Dominant: Even-numbered scanline fields come before odd-numbered scanline fields. Odd Frames Only: Only odd-numbered scanline fields are produced. Even Frames Only: Only even-numbered scanline fields are produced.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Override Global Range
parameters.description: If off, the global animation range is used as the frame range. If on, the frame range of the sequence can be specified in the following parameters.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Still Image
parameters.description: A still image is time-invariant. It exists at every frame. If off, the Start Frame and Length are used to determine the frame range.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Start Frame
parameters.description: The starting frame of the sequence.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Length
parameters.description: The length of the sequence (number of frames in the sequence).
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Frame Rate
parameters.description: If on, the frame rate of the sequence can be overridden.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Pre Extend
parameters.description: For sequences with a frame range, this determines how to show frames before the start frame. Black Frames: Display black. Cycle: Cycle the sequence, always playing it forward. Mirror: Cycle the sequence, reversing the direction every cycle. Hold: Hold the first frame indefinitely. Hold N Frames: Hold the first frame for a certain number of frames; before that, show black frames.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Pre Hold
parameters.description: The number of frames to hold the first frame for, if 'Hold N Frames' is selected.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Post Extend
parameters.description: For sequences with a frame range, this determines how to show frames after the last frame. Black Frames: Display black. Cycle: Cycle the sequence, always playing it forward. Mirror: Cycle the sequence, reversing the direction every cycle. Hold: Hold the last frame indefinitely. Hold N Frames: Hold the last frame for a certain number of frames; after that, show black frames.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Post Hold
parameters.description: The number of frames to hold the last frame for, if 'Hold N Frames' is selected.
parameters.heading: Transform

entries.label: Sharpen
entries.summary: Sharpens an image by enhancing the contrast of edges.

parameters.label: Size
parameters.description: Increases the size of the areas over which it performs the sharpen (in pixels). Larger values will enhance larger features.
parameters.heading: Sharpen

parameters.label: Units
parameters.description: The units that the Size parameter is expressed in, either pixels or UV coords.
parameters.heading: Sharpen

parameters.label: Effect
parameters.description: Intensity of the sharpen effect.
parameters.heading: Sharpen

parameters.label: Noise Suppress
parameters.description: If on, image noise is not sharpened. Noise is any edge that has a smaller magnitude than the Noise Suppress value. This produces clearer images. Image variances less than the suppress value are not sharpened (as if the effect was zero). If a blend region is used, variances just above the suppress cutoff are sharpened somewhat, depending on their position within the blend region. {{{ | No Sharpening | Diminished Sharpening | Full Sharpening effect: | 0% | 25% 50% 75% | 100% ----> | | suppress blend | variance: 0 (Suppress) (Suppress + Blend) }}}
parameters.heading: Sharpen

parameters.label: Suppress Function
parameters.description: Determines how noise in the Suppress Blend range is sharpened Sharp Cutoff: No blend region is used. Linear: Sharpening is uniformly reduced. Ease In: Sharpening is gradually reduced. Ease Out: Sharpening is quickly reduced. Ease In Ease Out: Similar to linear but using a smoother function. Gaussian: Similar to Ease In Ease Out, with a quicker dropoff.
parameters.heading: Sharpen

parameters.label: Suppress Blend
parameters.description: The size of the blend region between full sharpening and no sharpening of the variances just above the noise threshold. This prevents "patches" of sharp areas in the image by blending the patches in.
parameters.heading: Sharpen

parameters.label: Show Edges
parameters.description: Sharpens all the edges, while removing non-edge components.
parameters.heading: Sharpen

parameters.label: Effect Amount
parameters.description: If no mask is present, this blends the output with the input by a constant amount (0 = all input, 1 = all output). If a mask is present, this amount multiplies the mask.
parameters.heading: Mask

parameters.label: Operation Mask
parameters.description: Selects the mask plane to use as a mask from the mask input. The mask can be selected from First Input: Useful for masking the operation to the image's own alpha plane. Mask Input: Selects the mask from the side mask input. Off: Turns off masking, without requiring disconnection of the mask input (useful for temporarily disabling the mask).
parameters.heading: Mask

parameters.label: Resize Mask to Fit Image
parameters.description: If the mask image is a different resolution than the output image, turning on this parameter will scale the mask to the output image's resolution. If this node is changing constantly, and the mask is not, it is somewhat faster to put a Scale COP down to do the resize for the mask image. Otherwise, the scale will occur every time this node cooks.
parameters.heading: Mask

parameters.label: Invert Mask
parameters.description: Inverts the mask so that all fully 'masked' portions become unmasked. This saves you from inserting an Invert COP after the node with the mask.
parameters.heading: Mask

parameters.label: Plane Scope
parameters.description: Specifies the scope for both the RGB components of Color, Alpha, and other planes. The (C)RGBA mask only affects Color components and Alpha. 'C' will toggle all the RGB components. For planes other than Color and Alpha, the plane name (plus component, if applicable) should be specified in the string field. The pulldown menu can be used to select planes or components present in this node. A plane is specified by its name. A component is specified by both its plane and component name. The '*' wildcard may be used to scope all extra planes. Any number of planes or components can be specified, separated by spaces. Examples
parameters.heading: Scope

parameters.label: Frame Scope
parameters.description: Allows scoping of specific frames in the frame range. This is in addition to the plane scope (so a plane at a certain frame must be both plane scoped and frame scoped to be modified). All Frames: All frames are scoped. Inside Range: All frames inside a subrange are scoped. Outside Range: All frames outside a subrange are scoped. Even Frames: Even numbered frames are scoped. Odd Frames: Odd numbered frames are scoped. Specific Frames: A user-defined list of frames are scoped.
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Frame Range
parameters.description: For Inside/Outside range, this parameter specifies the subrange of the sequence to scope (or unscope). This can be edited in Timeline viewer mode (((Ctrl + 2)) in viewer).
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Frame Dropoff
parameters.description: For Inside/Outside Range, this parameter specifies certain number of frames before and after to slowly ramp up to scoped. The operation will be blended with its input to 'ease in' or 'ease out' the scoping effect over a number of frames. This can be edited in Timeline viewer mode (((Ctrl + 2)) in viewer).
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Non-scoped Effect
parameters.description: For unscoped frames, this sets the blend factor between the input and modified images. Normally this is zero (use the input image). By setting this to a non-zero value, you can make unscoped frames be 'slightly' unscoped. The value can vary between 0 (unscoped) and 1 (scoped).
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Frame List
parameters.description: The frame list for 'Specific Frames'. Frame numbers should be separated by spaces.
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Automatically Adjust for Length Changes
parameters.description: If the sequence range changes, enabling this parameter will adjust the subrange and frame dropoff lengths to fit the new range.
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

entries.label: Shift
entries.summary: Shifts an image sequence in time.

parameters.label: Shift Method
parameters.description: Sequences can be shifted in several ways if no reference input is connected. Relative Shift: Shifts the amount specified by the Shift Value. Shift Start to Shift Value: Starts at the point specified by Shift Value. Shift End to Shift Value: Shifts the image sequence such that it ends at the point specified by the Shift Value.

parameters.label: Input Shift
parameters.description: If a reference input is connected, several different ways of linking the two sequences together can be used. The sequence will always follow any changes in the reference sequence's start or end time. Align Start with 2nd Input's Start: Make the output sequence start at the same time as the sequence attached to input #2. Align End with 2nd Input's End: Make the output sequence end at the same time as the sequence attached to input #2. Shift To Precede 2nd Input: Output sequence will end on the frame just before the second input starts. Shift To Follow 2nd Input: Output sequence will start on the frame after 2nd input ends.

parameters.label: Shift Value
parameters.description: The amount to shift by, in either frames or seconds.

parameters.label: Units
parameters.description: The shift units, either Frames or Seconds.

entries.label: Shuffle
entries.summary: Shuffle frames around to do out-of-order editing.

parameters.label: Shuffle Frames
parameters.description: A string specifying how the frames are to be moved about. The format is as follows A-B: Move frame A to frame B, moving all frames in between by 1.

entries.label: Sky Environment Map
entries.summary: Creates sky and ground images for use as environment maps.

parameters.label: Use
parameters.description: Controls which of the following parameters are available to set the position of the sun in the image.
parameters.heading: Sun

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.description: The Euler rotation angles to align -Z axis vector towards the sun.
parameters.heading: Sun

parameters.label: Direction Vector
parameters.description: The explicit vector that points towards the sun.
parameters.heading: Sun

parameters.label: Azimuth
parameters.description: Azimuth of the sun in the image. Note that the default plane (C) shows the _right_ view, so 90 will put the sun straight ahead in that view.
parameters.heading: Sun

parameters.label: Elevation
parameters.description: Elevation of the sun in the image.
parameters.heading: Sun

parameters.label: Latitude
parameters.description: Latitude of the observer, used to compute the position of the sun based on the date when Use is not Angle and elevation.
parameters.heading: Sun

parameters.label: Longitude
parameters.description: Longitude of the observer, used to compute the position of the sun based on the date when Use is not Angle and elevation.
parameters.heading: Sun

parameters.label: Date
parameters.description: Date of observation, used to compute the position of the sun when Use is Location, date, and time.
parameters.heading: Sun

parameters.label: Time
parameters.description: Time of observation, used to compute the position of the sun when Use is Location, date, and time.
parameters.heading: Sun

parameters.label: Day of Year
parameters.description: A (fractional) day of the year (for example, 0.5 would be noon on January 1), used to compute the position of the sun when Use is Location, date, and time.
parameters.heading: Sun

parameters.label: Use
parameters.description: Controls whether the sun is rendered using a physically realistic simulation or using an artistically controllable color ramp. The Realistic option is especially useful when animating the time of day, since it automatically produces realistic colors for sunrise, sunset, high noon, and so on. The Ramp option gives you artistic control of the colors, but does not simulate atmospheric effects, for example along the horizon.
parameters.heading: Sky

parameters.label: Haziness
parameters.description: Controls how sunlight scatters in the air, used when Use is Realistic.
parameters.heading: Sky

parameters.label: Brightness
parameters.description: Controls the brightness of the sky, used when Use is Realistic.
parameters.heading: Sky

parameters.label: Color ramp
parameters.description: Manually sets a color ramp from the sun to the surrounding sky, used when Use is Ramp.
parameters.heading: Sky

parameters.label: Albedo
parameters.description: Sets the albedo of the ground.
parameters.heading: Ground

parameters.label: Normal
parameters.description: Sets the orientation of the ground plane. Only used when Use is Ramp.
parameters.heading: Ground

parameters.label: Horizon elevation
parameters.description: Sets the horizontal elevation of the viewer. Only used when Use is Ramp.
parameters.heading: Ground

entries.label: Snip
entries.summary: Either removes frames from a sequence or allows you to order them in a user-defined order.

parameters.label: Frame Operation
parameters.description: "Snip Scoped Frames" removes the specified frames; "Keep Scoped Frames" keeps only the specified frames; "User Defined Order" re-orders the frames in the order defined in the "Frame Order" parameter.

parameters.label: Frames
parameters.description: The frames to either Snip or Keep.

parameters.label: Frame Order
parameters.description: The new order of the frames in the sequence.

parameters.label: Automatically Adjust for Length Changes
parameters.description: If on, all the frame numbers will be adjusted when the length of the input sequence changes.

entries.label: SOP Import
entries.summary: Imports a 2d Volume from SOPs as planes into a composite network.

parameters.label: SOP Path
parameters.description: The SOP Node to cook. It should consist of a number of named, two-dimensional, volumes.

parameters.label: Import
parameters.description: Volume names to import. Wildcards are accepted, as well as a whitespace separated list of names. Only volumes whose names match the list will be imported. Volumes without names will only be imported if the mask is '*' or empty.

parameters.label: Set Resolution from SOPs
parameters.description: Turns on the Override Resolution and sets it to the current resolution of the first volume in the pointed to network. If no SOP or no volume is found, this does nothing.

parameters.label: Set Planes from SOPs
parameters.description: Turns off the built-in list of plane generations and builds a custom plane list to import each named primitive in the source SOP. If no SOP is found, does nothing.

parameters.label: Remap Range
parameters.description: When on, the layers imported will be scaled and shifted to fit inside this range.

entries.label: Streak Blur
entries.summary: Streaks an image, adding a motion blur effect.

parameters.label: Size
parameters.description: The length of the streaks, in pixels.
parameters.heading: Streak Blur

parameters.label: Rotation
parameters.description: Specifies the streak direction (0 is horizontal, 90 vertical).
parameters.heading: Streak Blur

parameters.label: Streak Bias
parameters.description: Determines how the streak is centered on the pixel creating the streak. To center the streak around the pixel, use 0. To make the streak end at the pixel, use -1 (the streak comes before the pixel that generates it). To make the streak begin at the pixel, use 1.
parameters.heading: Streak Blur

parameters.label: Falloff
parameters.description: The intensity falloff of the streak from the pixel that generated it. None: No falloff; the streak has constant intensity. Linear: The intensity falls off linearly. Gaussian: The intensity drops off gradually.
parameters.heading: Streak Blur

parameters.label: Falloff Amount
parameters.description: The amount of the streak that has a falloff. By default, this is the entire streak (1). This parameter can be adjusted so that only the ends of the streak fall off (ie. 0.1-0.3).
parameters.heading: Streak Blur

'C' will toggle all the RGB components. For planes other than Color and Alpha, the plane name (plus component, if applicable) should be specified in the string field. The pulldown menu can be used to select planes or components present in this node. A plane is specified by its name. A component is specified by both its plane and component name. The '*' wildcard may be used to scope all extra planes. Any number of planes or components can be specified, separated by spaces. Examples
parameters.heading: Scope

parameters.label: Frame Scope
parameters.description: Allows scoping of specific frames in the frame range. This is in addition to the plane scope (so a plane at a certain frame must be both plane scoped and frame scoped to be modified). All Frames: All frames are scoped. Inside Range: All frames inside a subrange are scoped. Outside Range: All frames outside a subrange are scoped. Even Frames: Even numbered frames are scoped. Odd Frames: Odd numbered frames are scoped. Specific Frames: A user-defined list of frames are scoped.
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Frame Range
parameters.description: For Inside/Outside range, this parameter specifies the subrange of the sequence to scope (or unscope). This can be edited in Timeline viewer mode (((Ctrl + 2)) in viewer).
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Frame Dropoff
parameters.description: For Inside/Outside Range, this parameter specifies certain number of frames before and after to slowly ramp up to scoped. The operation will be blended with its input to 'ease in' or 'ease out' the scoping effect over a number of frames. This can be edited in Timeline viewer mode (((Ctrl + 2)) in viewer).
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Non-scoped Effect
parameters.description: For unscoped frames, this sets the blend factor between the input and modified images. Normally this is zero (use the input image). By setting this to a non-zero value, you can make unscoped frames be 'slightly' unscoped. The value can vary between 0 (unscoped) and 1 (scoped).
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Frame List
parameters.description: The frame list for 'Specific Frames'. Frame numbers should be separated by spaces.
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Automatically Adjust for Length Changes
parameters.description: If the sequence range changes, enabling this parameter will adjust the subrange and frame dropoff lengths to fit the new range.
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

entries.label: Switch
entries.summary: Passes the input of one of its connected inputs through, acting like an exclusive switch.

parameters.label: Input Index
parameters.description: The index of the input to pass through.

entries.label: Switch Alpha
entries.summary: Replaces input 1's alpha with input 2's alpha.

parameters.label: Redo Premultiply
parameters.description: If on, the image will first be divided by the original alpha, and then multiplied by the new alpha.

parameters.label: Apply Premultiplies To
parameters.description: Only redo the Premultiplication on these planes (normally color).

entries.label: Tile
entries.summary: Tiles the image sequence with multiple copies of the input image.

parameters.label: Tiling
parameters.description: Specify the number of copies of the input image to tile here, both horizontally and vertically.

parameters.label: Tile Offset
parameters.description: Allows you to set the origin of the tiling (uses UV 0-1 ranges). This will translate the tiles.

parameters.label: Tile Method
parameters.description: Allows you to mirror the copies that you are tiling independently for X and Y. Normal: Don't do any mirroring. Mirror: Flip every other tile, starting with the second tile. Mirror First: Flip every other tile, starting at the first tile.

entries.label: Time Machine
entries.summary: Uses a second input to time warp the first input on a per pixel basis.

parameters.label: Black Pixel Frame
parameters.description: The frame value that a black pixel represents.
parameters.heading: Time Machine

parameters.label: White Pixel Frame
parameters.description: The frame value that a white pixel represents. Pixels between the black and white will have frame values that are linearly interpolated between the Black Pixel Frame and the White Pixel Frame. Values above white or below black will be extrapolated.
parameters.heading: Time Machine

parameters.label: Relative to Current Frame
parameters.description: If on, the frame value is added to the current frame, making the frame value an offset from the current frame. If off, the frame values represent actual frame numbers.
parameters.heading: Time Machine

parameters.label: Blend Frames
parameters.description: If on, fractional frames are computed and pixels from the two nearest frames are linearly blended together to produce the output frame's pixel.
parameters.heading: Time Machine

parameters.label: Before Start
parameters.description: If a filtered frame is before the beginning of the sequence, this determines what frame to use. Black: A black frame. Cycle: Cycle back into the sequence from the end (so 2 frames before the start will use frame 'end-2'). Mirror: Mirror back into the sequence (so 2 frames before will use frame 'start+2'). Hold: Use the first frame.
parameters.heading: Time Machine

parameters.label: After End
parameters.description: Similar to 'Before Start', except this parameter determines what frame to use if filtering goes past the last frame of the sequence.
parameters.heading: Time Machine

entries.label: Time Filter
entries.summary: Blurs a pixel through several frames.

parameters.label: Filter Width
parameters.description: The size of the filter, in frames.
parameters.heading: Time Filter

parameters.label: Blur Effect
parameters.description: The amount of blur to apply (0 = none, 1 = full effect)
parameters.heading: Time Filter

parameters.label: Filter Type
parameters.description: The type of blur filter to apply - box, hanning (triangle) or Gaussian. Box: All frames are weighted equally, which produces an averaging effect. Hanning: Frames in the middle of the filter are weighted more than frames at the edge, by using a tent-like filter. Gaussian: Frames in the middle of the filter are weighted more than frames at the edge, by using a gaussian filter, which is smoother than the Hanning filter.
parameters.heading: Time Filter

parameters.label: Filter Range
parameters.description: What frames are filtered. Before Current: The frames from 'current' to 'current-filterwidth' are filtered. Centered About Current: The frames from 'current-filterwidth/2' to 'current-filterwidth/2 + filterwidth' After Current: The frames from 'current' to 'current + filterwidth'
parameters.heading: Time Filter

parameters.label: Before Start
parameters.description: If a filtered frame is before the beginning of the sequence, this determines what frame to use. Black: A black frame. Cycle: Cycle back into the sequence from the end (so 2 frames before the start will use frame 'end-2'). Mirror: Mirror back into the sequence (so 2 frames before will use frame 'start+2'). Hold: Use the first frame.
parameters.heading: Time Filter

parameters.label: After End
parameters.description: Similar to 'Before Start', except this parameter determines what frame to use if filtering goes past the last frame of the sequence.
parameters.heading: Time Filter

parameters.label: Effect Amount
parameters.description: If no mask is present, this blends the output with the input by a constant amount (0 = all input, 1 = all output). If a mask is present, this amount multiplies the mask.
parameters.heading: Mask

parameters.label: Operation Mask
parameters.description: Selects the mask plane to use as a mask from the mask input. The mask can be selected from First Input: Useful for masking the operation to the image's own alpha plane. Mask Input: Selects the mask from the side mask input. Off: Turns off masking, without requiring disconnection of the mask input (useful for temporarily disabling the mask).
parameters.heading: Mask

parameters.label: Resize Mask to Fit Image
parameters.description: If the mask image is a different resolution than the output image, turning on this parameter will scale the mask to the output image's resolution. If this node is changing constantly, and the mask is not, it is somewhat faster to put a Scale COP down to do the resize for the mask image. Otherwise, the scale will occur every time this node cooks.
parameters.heading: Mask

parameters.label: Invert Mask
parameters.description: Inverts the mask so that all fully 'masked' portions become unmasked. This saves you from inserting an Invert COP after the node with the mask.

entries.label: TimeScale
entries.summary: Stretches or compresses a sequence in time.

parameters.label: Scale Method
parameters.description: Select a method for changing the timing. Modify Sequence Length Only: Changes the length of the sequence without changing the frame rate; the sequence will be longer or shorter in time. Modify Sequence Length, Same Time Span: Changes the length of the sequence Time Span and adjusts the frame rate so the sequence is the same time length. Modify Frame Rate Only: Only changes the frame rate. The sequence becomes longer or shorter, but the number of frames stays the same. Modify Frame Rate, Same Time Span: Changes the frame rate and increases Span or decreases the number of frames to keep the sequence the same time length.

parameters.label: Interpolation
parameters.description: When increasing or decreasing the number of frames in the sequence, this parameter determines the frame(s) to use for the output frames. Previous Frame: Uses the input frame exactly at or before the time of the output frame. Closest Frame: Uses the input frame exactly at or closest to the time of the output frame. Next Frame: Uses the input frame exactly at or after the time of the output frame. Blend Nearest Frames: Picks the 2 closest frames and linearly blends them together, weighting them with how close each input frames' time is to the output frame.

parameters.label: Frame Rate
parameters.description: The frame rate, for methods that require it.

parameters.label: Length Method
parameters.description: Specifies how to change the length of the sequence, for Scale Methods that require it (see below).

parameters.label: Length Scale
parameters.description: Changes the length of the sequence by a scale factor. Scales greater than 1 increase the length, scales less than 1 decrease it.

parameters.label: Sequence Length
parameters.description: Specifies the new length of the sequence, in frames.

parameters.label: Length Difference
parameters.description: Specifies how many frames to add or subtract from the input sequence length.

entries.label: Trim
entries.summary: Trims an input sequence in time by adjusting the beginning or the end of the sequence.

parameters.label: Trim
parameters.description: Specify whether the trim should be Relative to Current Start/End: Trim values represent start/end offsets. Absolute Start/End Values: Trim values are start/end frames. Single Image: Trim a single image out of the sequence by specifying the frame. Single Image Relative to Start: Trim a single image out of the sequence by an offset from the start. Single Image Relative to End: Trim a single image out of the sequence by an offset from the end.

parameters.label: Units
parameters.description: Specify Frames or Seconds.

parameters.label: Start
parameters.description: The start frame or offset to begin the trim at.

parameters.label: End
parameters.description: The start frame or offset to end the trim at.

entries.label: Under
entries.summary: Composites the first input (Foreground) under the second (background).

parameters.label: Image Units
parameters.description: Selects pixels or UV units for the transform.
parameters.heading: Composite

parameters.label: Translate, Rotate, Scale, Pivot
parameters.description: Transforms the foreground in X,Y relative to the background.
parameters.heading: Composite

parameters.label: Image Filter
parameters.description: Specifies the filter to use when transforming.
parameters.heading: Composite

parameters.label: Image Wrap
parameters.description: Specifies the foreground image's wrapping style.
parameters.heading: Composite

parameters.label: Motion Blur
parameters.description: Toggles on motion blur, and specifies the time range around the current frame to blur.
parameters.heading: Composite

parameters.label: Motion Frame Bias
parameters.description: Shifts the time range for the blur.
parameters.heading: Composite

parameters.label: Motion Blur Segments
parameters.description: Number of samples to blur together in the specified time range.
parameters.heading: Composite

parameters.label: Motion Blur Method
parameters.description: Velocity: Only uses the current frame and the transform to compute past and future positions. Deformation: Cooks the images at all time samples.
parameters.heading: Composite

parameters.description: These parameters specify how to build the output sequence when there are differences between the input sequences.
parameters.heading: Merge

parameters.label: Plane Merge
parameters.description: If the planes in the inputs differ, this specifies what the output planes should be.
parameters.heading: Merge

parameters.label: Raster Depth
parameters.description: If the raster depth for a given plane differs between inputs, this specifies what the output raster depth for the plane should be.
parameters.heading: Merge

parameters.label: Frame Range
parameters.description: If the frame ranges of the inputs differ, this determines what the output range should be.
parameters.heading: Merge

parameters.label: Frame Rate
parameters.description: If the frame rates of the inputs differ, this determines what the output frame rate should be.
parameters.heading: Merge

parameters.label: Frame Match
parameters.description: If the frame rates of the inputs differ, this determines which input frame to pick when the cook time doesn't reside on a frame boundary.
parameters.heading: Merge

parameters.description: Specifies the units of the point coordinates.

parameters.label_norm: bottom left, bottom right, top left, top right
parameters.description: The four corner points of the input area.

parameters.label: Filter

entries.label: UV Map
entries.summary: Creates a UV map.

parameters.description: If on, the U values are reversed (1 to 0).
parameters.heading: UV Map

parameters.label: U Clamp
parameters.description: How U values below 0 or above 1 are dealt with. Off: No clamping occurs; U values may be less than 0 or greater than 1. Clamp: U values are clamped at 0 and 1. parameters.label: U Cycles
parameters.description: Values higher than 1 produce more U cycles across the image.

entries.label: Velocity Blur
entries.summary: Blurs an image by using pixel velocity to produce a motion blur effect.

parameters.label: Quality
parameters.description: Affects the smoothness of the blur. Higher qualities take more samples per pixel to blur (which is also slower to compute).
parameters.heading: Velocity Blur

parameters.label: Velocity Scale
parameters.description: Uniformly scales velocity to change the amount of blur.
parameters.heading: Velocity Blur

parameters.label: Per Pixel Velocity
parameters.description: If on, the velocity plane is used to determine the blur on a per-pixel basis. If off, a global velocity vector is used.
parameters.heading: Velocity Blur

parameters.label: Velocity Plane
parameters.description: The name of the velocity plane.
parameters.heading: Velocity Blur

parameters.label: Accurate Velocity Lookups
parameters.description: If on, the velocity is "followed" by sampling the velocity at each point, resulting potentially curved blur streaks. If off, only the initial velocity is used and the blur streaks are straight.
parameters.heading: Velocity Blur

parameters.label: Velocity Vector
parameters.description: If Per Pixel Velocity if off, this is the global velocity vector that is used to produce a streaking blur.
parameters.heading: Velocity Blur

parameters.label: Start Blur Scale
parameters.description: The start blur factor. The first blurred pixel is multiplied by this value.
parameters.heading: Velocity Blur

parameters.label: End Blur Scale
parameters.description: The end blur factor. The last blurred pixel is multiplied by this value.
parameters.heading: Velocity Blur

parameters.label: Blur Dropoff
parameters.description: The interpolation function for pixel samples in between the start and end pixels.
parameters.heading: Velocity Blur

parameters.label: Filtering
parameters.description: The pixel sampling filter. None: Quick, low quality filter. Bilinear: Medium quality filter. Full Filtered: Slow, high quality filter.
parameters.heading: Velocity Blur

parameters.label: Correct for Image Aspect
parameters.description: If on, the blur is adjusted so it appears circular if the image aspect ratio isn't square.
parameters.heading: Velocity Blur

parameters.label: Outside Bounds
parameters.description: Specifies the sampling method for pixels outside the image.
parameters.heading: Velocity Blur

parameters.label: Effect Amount
parameters.description: If no mask is present, this blends the output with the input by a constant amount (0 = all input, 1 = all output). If a mask is present, this amount multiplies the mask.
parameters.heading: Mask

parameters.label: Operation Mask
parameters.description: Selects the mask plane to use as a mask from the mask input. The mask can be selected from First Input: Useful for masking the operation to the image's own alpha plane. Mask Input: Selects the mask from the side mask input. Off: Turns off masking, without requiring disconnection of the mask input (useful for temporarily disabling the mask).
parameters.heading: Mask

parameters.label: Resize Mask to Fit Image
parameters.description: If the mask image is a different resolution than the output image, turning on this parameter will scale the mask to the output image's resolution. If this node is changing constantly, and the mask is not, it is somewhat faster to put a Scale COP down to do the resize for the mask image. Otherwise, the scale will occur every time this node cooks.
parameters.heading: Mask

parameters.label: Invert Mask
parameters.description: Inverts the mask so that all fully 'masked' portions become unmasked. This saves you from inserting an Invert COP after the node with the mask.
parameters.heading: Mask

parameters.label: Plane Scope
parameters.description: Specifies the scope for both the RGB components of Color, Alpha, and other planes. The (C)RGBA mask only affects Color components and Alpha. 'C' will toggle all the RGB components. For planes other than Color and Alpha, the plane name (plus component, if applicable) should be specified in the string field. The pulldown menu can be used to select planes or components present in this node. A plane is specified by its name. A component is specified by both its plane and component name. The '*' wildcard may be used to scope all extra planes. Any number of planes or components can be specified, separated by spaces. Examples
parameters.heading: Scope

parameters.label: Frame Scope
parameters.description: Allows scoping of specific frames in the frame range. This is in addition to the plane scope (so a plane at a certain frame must be both plane scoped and frame scoped to be modified). All Frames: All frames are scoped. Inside Range: All frames inside a subrange are scoped. Outside Range: All frames outside a subrange are scoped. Even Frames: Even numbered frames are scoped. Odd Frames: Odd numbered frames are scoped. Specific Frames: A user-defined list of frames are scoped.
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Frame Range
parameters.description: For Inside/Outside range, this parameter specifies the subrange of the sequence to scope (or unscope). This can be edited in Timeline viewer mode (((Ctrl + 2)) in viewer).
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Frame Dropoff
parameters.description: For Inside/Outside Range, this parameter specifies certain number of frames before and after to slowly ramp up to scoped. The operation will be blended with its input to 'ease in' or 'ease out' the scoping effect over a number of frames. This can be edited in Timeline viewer mode (((Ctrl + 2)) in viewer).
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Non-scoped Effect
parameters.description: For unscoped frames, this sets the blend factor between the input and modified images. Normally this is zero (use the input image). By setting this to a non-zero value, you can make unscoped frames be 'slightly' unscoped. The value can vary between 0 (unscoped) and 1 (scoped).
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Frame List
parameters.description: The frame list for 'Specific Frames'. Frame numbers should be separated by spaces.
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Automatically Adjust for Length Changes
parameters.description: If the sequence range changes, enabling this parameter will adjust the subrange and frame dropoff lengths to fit the new range.
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

entries.summary: Runs a VEX script on the planes it generates.

parameters.label: VEX Function
parameters.description: The VEX script to run, with any parameter arguments you wish to override.
parameters.heading: VEX Generate

parameters.label: Reload VEX Functions
parameters.description: Reloads the VEX script. Useful if the script has been modified and re-compiled.
parameters.heading: VEX Generate

parameters.label: Effect Amount
parameters.description: If no mask is present, this multiplies the output by a constant amount (0 = black, 1 = all output). If a mask is present, this amount multiplies the mask.
parameters.heading: VEX Generate

parameters.label: Mask Plane
parameters.description: A mask can be a component of a plane or an entire plane. If a vector plane is supplied as a mask, its components are multiplied by the images' components. Scalar Mask ('A', 'C.r'): {{{ C.r = I.r * M C.g = I.g * M C.b = I.b * M }}} Vector Mask ('C'): {{{ C.r = I.r * M.r C.g = I.g * M.g C.b = I.b * M.b }}}
parameters.heading: VEX Generate

parameters.label: Invert Mask
parameters.description: Inverts the mask so that all fully 'masked' portions become unmasked. This saves you from inserting an Invert COP after the node with the mask.
parameters.heading: VEX Generate

parameters.label: Override Size
parameters.description: If off, the resolution of the image is defined by the resolution in the Composite Project settings. If on, any resolution can be specified.
parameters.heading: VEX Generate

parameters.label: Pixel Aspect Ratio
parameters.description: If off, the pixel aspect ratio of the image is defined by the pixel aspect ratio in the Composite Project settings. If on, any pixel aspect ratio can be specified. The pixel aspect ratio determines the shape of the pixel; it represents the width of the pixel compared to the height. A pixel with an aspect ratio of '2' is twice as wide as it is high (2:1). Pixel aspect ratios less than 1 are taller than they are wide. The image viewer attempts to show the image as it would appear by horizontally scaling the image by the pixel aspect ratio. This can result in slight artifacts for non-integer ratios (ie, 0.9:1, 1.442:1). Turn off 'Fast Pixel Aspect' in the Display Options to suppress these artifacts. Many effect filters that have parameters that represent width and height will have the width scaled appropriately (such as Blur, Defocus, Expand).
parameters.heading: VEX Generate

parameters.label: Image Planes
parameters.description: Specifies the plane(s) to generate. Color and Alpha will always be present, but the generator does not always have to write to them. The list of planes is all the ones Houdini recognizes as special. Other planes can be added with the 'Custom Planes' parameter. C, A (C:rgb A): Color and Alpha C, A (C:rgb A:rgb): Color and 3-channel Alpha C (rgb): Color only A: Alpha only A (rgb): 3-channel Alpha only M: Mask plane M (rgb): 3-channel Mask plane Z: Z Depth plane L: Luminance plane B (uv): Bump plane P (xyz): Point plane N (xyz): Normal plane V (xyz): Velocity plane None: No planes generated.
parameters.heading: VEX Generate

parameters.label: Add Plane
parameters.description: When a generator is connected to an input, it generates a Mask plane by default. This parameter determines which planes are generated in this case. The list of planes to generate are the same as 'Image Planes'. In addition, if the plane already exists in the input sequence, one of the following operations will be performed to combine the new plane. Replace: Input plane replaced by the generated plane. (G) Rename: Generated plane renamed. Add: Input plane added to the generated plane. (I+G) Screen: Input plane photographically added to the generated plane. (I+G-I*G) Subtract: Generated plane subtracted from the input plane. (I-G). Multiply: Input plane multiplied by the generated plane. (IxG) Min: Minimum pixel value of input and generated planes. (min{I,G}) Max: Maximum pixel value of input and generated planes. (max{I,G}) Average: Average pixel value of the input and generated planes. (I+G)/2
parameters.heading: VEX Generate

parameters.label: Custom Planes
parameters.description: This string parameter allows you to create your own plane formats. The syntax is
parameters.heading: VEX Generate

parameters.label: Raster Depth
parameters.description: The byte format of the image. Higher bit depths provide better color resolution and range at the expense of memory. 8 Bit Integer: Lowest bit depth. Banding can occasionally be seen. Suitable for video. 16 Bit Integer: Intermediate bit depth. No banding can be seen, though clipping can still occur below and above the black and white points. 32 Bit Integer: Generally not used for color, 32bit integer values are used to store object IDs, counts, and other integer values with a large range. 16 Bit Floating Point: High bit depth. No banding can be seen, and no clipping occurs at white and black. Uses less memory than 32 bit float, however processing time for this format is slightly higher as it is not a native CPU data format. This format supports values in the range -65504 to +65504. 32 Bit Floating Point: High bit depth. No banding can be seen, and no clipping occurs at white and black. Uses 4x as much memory as 8bit, which is this format's main drawback. Default Depth: Use the raster depth specified in the Composite Project options.
parameters.heading: VEX Generate

parameters.label: Black/White Points
parameters.description: The integer formats (8, 16 and 32 bit) can specify the raw values that the black and white points occur at. The white point must always be higher than the black point. The minimum and maximum values for the black and white points for each format are td>> td>> td>>
parameters.heading: VEX Generate

parameters.label: Interlacing
parameters.description: Controls the ability to generate images that are compatible with interlaced images. If you are manipulating the generated output with a filter that uses neighboring pixels (like Blur or Expand), it is recommended that you do not use Black Interlaced, as the filter will use the black scanlines as well. The second menu determines which scanlines are in which fields (odd,even) None: No interlacing. Half Res Interlaced: The image is half the height of a normal frame, with the scanlines on every line. Black Interlaced: The image is the same height as a normal frame, with the inactive scanlines filled with black. Line Doubled: The image is the same height as a normal frame, with the inactive scanlines filled with their active neighbor. Odd Dominant: Odd-numbered scanline fields come before even-numbered scanline fields. Even Dominant: Even-numbered scanline fields come before odd-numbered scanline fields. Odd Frames Only: Only odd-numbered scanline fields are produced. Even Frames Only: Only even-numbered scanline fields are produced.
parameters.heading: VEX Generate

parameters.label: Override Global Range
parameters.description: If off, the global animation range is used as the frame range. If on, the frame range of the sequence can be specified in the following parameters.
parameters.heading: VEX Generate

parameters.label: Still Image
parameters.description: A still image is time-invariant. It exists at every frame. If off, the Start Frame and Length are used to determine the frame range.
parameters.heading: VEX Generate

parameters.label: Start Frame
parameters.description: The starting frame of the sequence.
parameters.heading: VEX Generate

parameters.label: Length
parameters.description: The length of the sequence (number of frames in the sequence).
parameters.heading: VEX Generate

parameters.label: Frame Rate
parameters.description: If on, the frame rate of the sequence can be overridden.
parameters.heading: VEX Generate

parameters.label: Pre Extend
parameters.description: For sequences with a frame range, this determines how to show frames before the start frame. Black Frames: Display black. Cycle: Cycle the sequence, always playing it forward. Mirror: Cycle the sequence, reversing the direction every cycle. Hold: Hold the first frame indefinitely. Hold N Frames: Hold the first frame for a certain number of frames; before that, show black frames.
parameters.heading: VEX Generate

parameters.label: Pre Hold
parameters.description: The number of frames to hold the first frame for, if 'Hold N Frames' is selected.
parameters.heading: VEX Generate

parameters.label: Post Extend
parameters.description: For sequences with a frame range, this determines how to show frames after the last frame. Black Frames: Display black. Cycle: Cycle the sequence, always playing it forward. Mirror: Cycle the sequence, reversing the direction every cycle. Hold: Hold the last frame indefinitely. Hold N Frames: Hold the last frame for a certain number of frames; after that, show black frames.
parameters.heading: VEX Generate

parameters.label: Post Hold
parameters.description: The number of frames to hold the last frame for, if 'Hold N Frames' is selected.
parameters.heading: VEX Generate

entries.summary: Cuts a small window out of a larger image.

parameters.description: The window area can either be represented by 2 opposite points of a rectangle, or the rectangles lower left corner and its width and height.

parameters.description: Specifies the units to crop in, either pixels or UV.

parameters.label: Horizontal Area
parameters.description: The left/right bounds of the window area. This parameter cannot be animated; use the Offset parameter to pan the image through the window.

parameters.label: Vertical Area
parameters.description: The bottom/top bounds of the window area. This parameter cannot be animated; use the Offset parameter to pan the image through the window.

parameters.description: An animatable image offset, so the image may be panned through the area.

parameters.label: Hold Edges Outside Image Bounds
parameters.description: This determines the behavior of the crop when the crop window goes outside the normal image bounds. If on, the edge pixels will be streaked outward to fill the outside area. If off, black pixels will be used.

Horizontal Wipe: Cuts the images vertically and fits them together, so that one image is to the left of the other. 4 Corner Shrink: Cut out a rectangular region in the middle of the second input for the first input. Circular Shrink: Bring out the second input from a circle (or ellipse) in the center of the first input. AA Circular Shrink: Same as above, but the edges of the circle are antialiased.

entries.label: Transform
entries.summary: Translates, rotates and/or scales the input image without changing the image resolution.

parameters.label: Units
parameters.description: Selects pixels or UV units for the transforms.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Translate
parameters.description: The UV translation, in pixels or UV units.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.description: The rotation to apply to the image.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: The scale to apply to the image.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Pivot
parameters.description: The pivot offset from the newly translated image origin, around which the image is rotated and scaled.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: X/Y Filters
parameters.description: The filter(s) to use when transforming.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Filter Size
parameters.description: The size of the filter (normally 1). Larger values produce a more blurred transform, while smaller values do less anti-aliasing.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Image Wrap
parameters.description: How to wrap the image when outside its bounds (repeat, clamp, decal, mirror)
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Motion Blur
parameters.description: Toggles on motion blur, and specifies the time range around the current frame to blur.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Motion Frame Bias
parameters.description: Shifts the time range for the blur.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Motion Blur Segments
parameters.description: Number of samples to blur together in the specified time range.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Motion Blur Method
parameters.description: Velocity: Only uses the current frame and the transform to compute past and future positions. Deformation: Cooks the images at all time samples.
parameters.heading: Transform

parameters.label: Effect Amount
parameters.description: If no mask is present, this blends the output with the input by a constant amount (0 = all input, 1 = all output). If a mask is present, this amount multiplies the mask.
parameters.heading: Mask

parameters.label: Operation Mask
parameters.description: Selects the mask plane to use as a mask from the mask input. The mask can be selected from First Input: Useful for masking the operation to the image's own alpha plane. Mask Input: Selects the mask from the side mask input. Off: Turns off masking, without requiring disconnection of the mask input (useful for temporarily disabling the mask).
parameters.heading: Mask

parameters.label: Resize Mask to Fit Image
parameters.description: If the mask image is a different resolution than the output image, turning on this parameter will scale the mask to the output image's resolution. If this node is changing constantly, and the mask is not, it is somewhat faster to put a Scale COP down to do the resize for the mask image. Otherwise, the scale will occur every time this node cooks.
parameters.heading: Mask

parameters.label: Invert Mask
parameters.description: Inverts the mask so that all fully 'masked' portions become unmasked. This saves you from inserting an Invert COP after the node with the mask.
parameters.heading: Mask

parameters.label: Plane Scope
parameters.description: Specifies the scope for both the RGB components of Color, Alpha, and other planes. The (C)RGBA mask only affects Color components and Alpha. 'C' will toggle all the RGB components. For planes other than Color and Alpha, the plane name (plus component, if applicable) should be specified in the string field. The pulldown menu can be used to select planes or components present in this node. A plane is specified by its name. A component is specified by both its plane and component name. The '*' wildcard may be used to scope all extra planes. Any number of planes or components can be specified, separated by spaces. Examples
parameters.heading: Scope

parameters.label: Frame Scope
parameters.description: Allows scoping of specific frames in the frame range. This is in addition to the plane scope (so a plane at a certain frame must be both plane scoped and frame scoped to be modified). All Frames: All frames are scoped. Inside Range: All frames inside a subrange are scoped. Outside Range: All frames outside a subrange are scoped. Even Frames: Even numbered frames are scoped. Odd Frames: Odd numbered frames are scoped. Specific Frames: A user-defined list of frames are scoped.
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Frame Range
parameters.description: For Inside/Outside range, this parameter specifies the subrange of the sequence to scope (or unscope). This can be edited in Timeline viewer mode (((Ctrl + 2)) in viewer).
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Frame Dropoff
parameters.description: For Inside/Outside Range, this parameter specifies certain number of frames before and after to slowly ramp up to scoped. The operation will be blended with its input to 'ease in' or 'ease out' the scoping effect over a number of frames. This can be edited in Timeline viewer mode (((Ctrl + 2)) in viewer).
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Non-scoped Effect
parameters.description: For unscoped frames, this sets the blend factor between the input and modified images. Normally this is zero (use the input image). By setting this to a non-zero value, you can make unscoped frames be 'slightly' unscoped. The value can vary between 0 (unscoped) and 1 (scoped).
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Frame List
parameters.description: The frame list for 'Specific Frames'. Frame numbers should be separated by spaces.
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Automatically Adjust for Length Changes
parameters.description: If the sequence range changes, enabling this parameter will adjust the subrange and frame dropoff lengths to fit the new range.
parameters.heading: Frame Scope

entries.label: Xor
entries.summary: Makes two elements mutually exclusive; if their alpha mattes overlap, the overlap is removed.

parameters.label: Image Units

parameters.heading: Composite

parameters.label: Image Wrap

parameters.label: Overview
parameters.description: These parameters specify how to build the output sequence when there are differences between the input sequences.
parameters.heading: Merge

parameters.label: Plane Merge
parameters.description: If the planes in the inputs differ, this specifies what the output planes should be.
parameters.heading: Merge

parameters.label: Raster Depth
parameters.description: If the raster depth for a given plane differs between inputs, this specifies what the output raster depth for the plane should be.
parameters.heading: Merge

parameters.label: Frame Range
parameters.description: If the frame ranges of the inputs differ, this determines what the output range should be.
parameters.heading: Merge

parameters.label: Frame Rate
parameters.description: If the frame rates of the inputs differ, this determines what the output frame rate should be.
parameters.heading: Merge

parameters.label: Frame Match
parameters.description: If the frame rates of the inputs differ, this determines which input frame to pick when the cook time doesn't reside on a frame boundary.
parameters.heading: Merge

entries.label: Z Composite
entries.summary: Does a Z composite of two images.

parameters.label: Foreground Offset
parameters.description: Allows you to specify an offset Z-depth, as well as an XY offset for the foreground image (X,Y,Z)
parameters.heading: Z Composite

parameters.label: Use Depth Plane For Background
parameters.description: The background will use a depth or point plane if on. If off, specify the global depth of the image with the Background Depth parameter.
parameters.heading: Z Composite

parameters.label: Background Depth
parameters.description: The global background depth.
parameters.heading: Z Composite

parameters.label: Use Depth Plane For Foreground
parameters.description: The foreground will use a depth or point plane if on. If off, specify the global depth of the image with the Foreground Depth parameter.
parameters.heading: Z Composite

parameters.label: Foreground Depth
parameters.description: The global foreground depth.
parameters.heading: Z Composite

parameters.label: Supersample
parameters.description: The amount of aliasing to do. '2' means 2x2.
parameters.heading: Z Composite

parameters.label: Focal Length, Aperature
parameters.description: If the foreground is translated in X or Y, the Focal Length and Aperature parameters are used to recompute the X and Y values from the new Z value..
parameters.heading: Z Composite
